declarations.name: Module.characterModule_pureInjective
declarations.doc:
The character module `Hom_ℤ(M, ℚ/ℤ)` of any module `M` over a commutative ring is pure
injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem characterModule_pureInjective (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] :
    Module.PureInjective A (CharacterModule M)
declarations.comment: character_module_pure_injective

declarations.name: Module.pureInjective_iff_evalₗ_splits
declarations.doc:
A module is pure injective if and only if evaluation into its double character
module has a linear retraction.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pureInjective_iff_evalₗ_splits (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Type v) [AddCommGroup I] [Module A I] :
    Module.PureInjective A I ↔
      ∃ r : CharacterModule (CharacterModule I) →ₗ[A] I,
        r.comp (CharacterModule.evalₗ A I) = LinearMap.id
declarations.comment: pure_injective_iff_double_dual_splits

declarations.name: Module.exists_pureInjective_universallyExact_extension
declarations.doc:
Every module embeds universally injectively into a pure injective module, with a
surjective cokernel map making the resulting sequence exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pureInjective_universallyExact_extension
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] :
    ∃ (I N : Type v)
      (_ : AddCommGroup I) (_ : Module A I)
      (_ : AddCommGroup N) (_ : Module A N)
      (f : M →ₗ[A] I) (g : I →ₗ[A] N),
      Function.Injective f ∧
        Function.Surjective g ∧
          LinearMap.range f = LinearMap.ker g ∧
            UniversallyInjective f ∧ Module.PureInjective A I
declarations.comment: exists_pure_injective_universally_exact_extension

declarations.name: Module.universallyInjective_range_subtype
declarations.doc:
If `L → M → N` is exact and remains exact after every tensor product, then the
inclusion of the image of `M → N` in `N` is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyInjective_range_subtype
    {L M N : Type v} [AddCommGroup L] [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
    [Module A L] [Module A M] [Module A N]
    (f : L →ₗ[A] M) (g : M →ₗ[A] N)
    (hexact : Function.Exact f g)
    (h : ∀ (Q : Type v) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q],
      Function.Exact (f.rTensor Q) (g.rTensor Q)) :
    UniversallyInjective (LinearMap.range g).subtype
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Module.kernel_universallyExact
declarations.doc:
The kernel-to-term-to-next-kernel sequences of a universally exact complex are
universally exact short exact sequences.
declarations.statement:
theorem kernel_universallyExact
    {M : ℤ → Type u} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module A (M i)]
    (d : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[A] M (i + 1)) (h : UniversallyExactComplex M d) (i : ℤ) :
    UniversallyExact (LinearMap.ker (d i)).subtype (toNextKernel d h i)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Module.PureInjectiveResolution.IsPureInjectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
An augmentation `M ⟶ I⁰` of a cochain complex is a *pure injective resolution* if
`0 ⟶ M ⟶ I⁰ ⟶ I¹ ⟶ ⋯` is universally exact and every `Iⁱ` is pure injective.
declarations.statement:
public structure IsPureInjectiveResolution
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} A) ℕ) (augmentation : M →ₗ[A] I.X 0) : Prop
declarations.comment: pure_injective_resolution

declarations.name: Module.PureProjectiveResolution.IsPureProjectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
An augmentation `P₀ ⟶ M` of a chain complex is a *pure projective resolution* if
`⋯ ⟶ P₁ ⟶ P₀ ⟶ M ⟶ 0` is universally exact and every `Pᵢ` is pure projective.
declarations.statement:
public structure IsPureProjectiveResolution
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (P : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{w} A) ℕ) (augmentation : P.X 0 →ₗ[A] M) : Prop
declarations.comment: pure_projective_resolution

declarations.name: Module.PureProjectiveResolution.exists_comparison_map
declarations.doc:
A module map extends from a pure projective resolution to any universally
exact resolution.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_comparison_map
    {M N : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (f : M →ₗ[A] N)
    (P C : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} A) ℕ)
    (aP : P.X 0 →ₗ[A] M) (aC : C.X 0 →ₗ[A] N)
    (hP : Module.PureProjectiveResolution.IsPureProjectiveResolution P aP)
    (hC : IsUniversallyExactResolution C aC) :
    ∃ F : P ⟶ C, aC.comp (F.f 0).hom = f.comp aP
declarations.comment: comparison_map

declarations.name: Module.PureProjectiveResolution.homotopy_of_same_augmentation
declarations.doc: Two maps of resolutions inducing the same map of resolved modules are homotopic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopy_of_same_augmentation
    {M N : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (P C : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} A) ℕ)
    (augmentationP : P.X 0 →ₗ[A] M) (augmentationC : C.X 0 →ₗ[A] N)
    (hP : Module.PureProjectiveResolution.IsPureProjectiveResolution P augmentationP)
    (hC : Module.PureProjectiveResolution.IsUniversallyExactResolution C augmentationC)
    (f : M →ₗ[A] N) (α β : P ⟶ C)
    (hα : augmentationC.comp (α.f 0).hom = f.comp augmentationP)
    (hβ : augmentationC.comp (β.f 0).hom = f.comp augmentationP) :
    Nonempty (Homotopy α β)
declarations.comment: homotopy_uniqueness

declarations.name: Module.PureProjectiveResolution.exists_isPureProjectiveResolution
declarations.doc: Every module admits a pure projective resolution.
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: Module.PureInjectiveResolution.exists_comparison_map
declarations.doc:
A map `M → N` extends to a map from any universally exact resolution of `M`
to any pure injective resolution of `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_comparison_map
    {M N : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (f : M →ₗ[A] N)
    (C I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} A) ℕ)
    (aC : M →ₗ[A] C.X 0) (aI : N →ₗ[A] I.X 0)
    (hC : IsUniversallyExactResolution C aC)
    (hI : Module.PureInjectiveResolution.IsPureInjectiveResolution I aI) :
    ∃ F : C ⟶ I, (F.f 0).hom.comp aC = aI.comp f
declarations.comment: comparison_map

declarations.name: Module.PureInjectiveResolution.homotopy_of_same_augmentation
declarations.doc: Comparison maps extending the same map between resolved modules are homotopic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopy_of_same_augmentation
    {M N : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (C I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} A) ℕ)
    (augmentationC : M →ₗ[A] C.X 0) (augmentationI : N →ₗ[A] I.X 0)
    (hC : Module.PureInjectiveResolution.IsUniversallyExactResolution C augmentationC)
    (hI : Module.PureInjectiveResolution.IsPureInjectiveResolution I augmentationI)
    (f : M →ₗ[A] N) (α β : C ⟶ I)
    (hα : (α.f 0).hom.comp augmentationC = augmentationI.comp f)
    (hβ : (β.f 0).hom.comp augmentationC = augmentationI.comp f) :
    Nonempty (Homotopy α β)
declarations.comment: comparison_homotopy

declarations.name: Module.PureInjectiveResolution.exists_pureInjectiveResolution
declarations.doc: Every module admits an augmented, universally exact cochain complex of pure injectives.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_pureInjectiveResolution
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] :
    ∃ (I : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} A) ℕ) (augmentation : M →ₗ[A] I.X 0),
      Module.PureInjectiveResolution.IsPureInjectiveResolution I augmentation
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: Module.pureExt
declarations.doc: The `i`th pure extension module of `M` by `N`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def pureExt (M N : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] (i : ℕ) : ModuleCat.{v} A

declarations.name: Module.pureExt_isZero_of_pureInjective
declarations.doc: Positive-degree pure extensions into a pure injective module vanish.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pureExt_isZero_of_pureInjective
    (M N : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (hN : Module.PureInjective A N)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (Module.pureExt (A := A) M N i)
declarations.comment: pure_injective_vanishing

declarations.name: Module.pureExt_isZero_of_pureProjective
declarations.doc: Positive-degree pure extensions out of a pure projective module vanish.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pureExt_isZero_of_pureProjective
    (M N : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (hM : Module.PureProjective A M)
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (Module.pureExt (A := A) M N i)
declarations.comment: pure_projective_vanishing

declarations.name: Module.pureExt_isZero_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc: Positive-degree pure extensions out of a module of finite presentation vanish.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pureExt_isZero_of_finitePresentation
    (M N : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.FinitePresentation A M]
    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (Module.pureExt (A := A) M N i)
declarations.comment: finite_presentation_vanishing

declarations.name: Module.pureExtIsoHomologyOfPureProjectiveResolution
declarations.doc:
**Pure extensions are computed by a pure projective resolution of the first variable**:
`Pext^i_A(M, N)` is the `i`th cohomology module of `Hom_A(Pᐧ, N)` for every pure projective
resolution `Pᐧ ⟶ M`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def pureExtIsoHomologyOfPureProjectiveResolution
    (M N : Type (max u v)) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    {P : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) ℕ} {ε : P.X 0 →ₗ[A] M}
    (hP : Module.PureProjectiveResolution.IsPureProjectiveResolution P ε) (i : ℕ) :
    Module.pureExt (A := A) M N i ≅ (Module.homComplexOfChain P N).homology i
declarations.comment: pure_projective_resolution

declarations.name: AdequateFunctor.injective_iff_moduleExtension_pureInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0708.** An adequate module-valued functor is injective exactly when it
is naturally isomorphic to the extension of a pure injective module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_iff_moduleExtension_pureInjective {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (F : (adequate.{u, v, max u v w} A).FullSubcategory) :
    Injective F ↔ ∃ I : ModuleCat.{max u v w} A, Module.PureInjective A I ∧
      Nonempty (F.obj ≅ moduleExtension.{max u v w, v} A I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.pureExtToExt_bijective_and_natural
declarations.doc:
Let `U = Spec A` be affine and `M`, `N` be `A`-modules. For every `i`, the canonical arrow
`Pext^i_A(M, N) ⟶ Ext^i_{Mod(𝒪)}(M^a, N^a)` of `pureExtToExt` is bijective, and it is functorial in
`M` and in `N`: precomposition with `g : M' ⟶ M` on `Pext` corresponds to composition with the
class of `g^a`, and the action of `g : N ⟶ N'`, through any map of the chosen pure injective
resolutions lying over `g`, to composition with the class of `g^a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem pureExtToExt_bijective_and_natural :
    letI := adequate_isClosedUnderKernels.{u, u} B
    letI := adequate_isClosedUnderCokernels.{u, u} B
    letI := adequate_isClosedUnderFiniteProducts.{u, u} B
    letI : Abelian (adequate.{u, u} B).FullSubcategory := abelian_adequate B
    letI : PreservesFiniteLimits (adequate.{u, u} B).ι := (exact_ι_adequate B).1
    letI : PreservesFiniteColimits (adequate.{u, u} B).ι := (exact_ι_adequate B).2
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (adequate.{u, u} B).FullSubcategory :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasExt.{u + 1} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) :=
      hasExt_of_hasDerivedCategory _
    letI : HasExt.{u + 1} (adequate.{u, u} B).FullSubcategory :=
      hasExt_of_hasDerivedCategory _
    (∀ (M N : ModuleCat.{u} A) (n : ℕ), Function.Bijective (pureExtToExt B M N n)) ∧
    (∀ {M M' : ModuleCat.{u} A} (N : ModuleCat.{u} A) (g : M' ⟶ M) (n : ℕ)
      (x : Module.pureExt (A := A) M N n),
      pureExtToExt B M' N n
          ((HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
            (Module.homComplexPrecomp g.hom (Module.pureExtResolution (A := A) N)) n).hom x) =
        (Ext.mk₀ ((associatedTilde B).map g)).comp (pureExtToExt B M N n x) (zero_add n)) ∧
    (∀ (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) {N N' : ModuleCat.{u} A} (g : N ⟶ N')
      (F : Module.pureExtResolution (A := A) N ⟶ Module.pureExtResolution (A := A) N')
      (_ : (F.f 0).hom.comp (Module.pureExtAugmentation N) =
        (Module.pureExtAugmentation N').comp g.hom)
      (n : ℕ) (x : Module.pureExt (A := A) M N n),
      pureExtToExt B M N' n
          ((HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (Module.homComplexPostcomp M F) n).hom x) =
        (pureExtToExt B M N n x).comp (Ext.mk₀ ((associatedTilde B).map g)) (add_zero n))
declarations.comment: every degree i: the canonical arrow is bijective and natural in M and N

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.bijective_pureExtToExt_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0709] in degree `1`.** For `U = Spec A` affine and `A`-modules `M`, `N`, the
canonical arrow `Pext¹_A(M, N) ⟶ Ext¹_{Mod((Sch/U)_τ, 𝒪)}(M^a, N^a)` is bijective, with no
hypothesis. It is the isomorphism `Pext¹_A(M, N) ≅ Ext¹_{Adeq(𝒪)}(M^a, N^a)` of
`Stacks.Adequate.pureExtAddEquivExtAdequate` followed by the comparison of Tag 06ZW, which is
bijective in degree `1` because the adequate modules are closed under extensions
(`Stacks.Adequate.bijective_mapExtAddHom_ι_adequate_one`). The arrow is natural in `M` and `N`
by `Stacks.Adequate.pureExtToExt_naturality_left` and `_naturality_right`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijective_pureExtToExt_one (M N : ModuleCat.{u} A) :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasExt.{u + 1} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) :=
      hasExt_of_hasDerivedCategory _
    Function.Bijective (pureExtToExt B M N 1)
declarations.comment: degree 1: the canonical arrow pureExtToExt, natural in M and N by pureExtToExt_naturality_left/_right, is bijective in degree 1; every degree is pureExtToExt_bijective_and_natural in HigherExtsAdequate/AdequateExtComparisonAll

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.pureExtZeroAddEquivExtZero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0709] in degree `0`.** For `U = Spec A` affine and `A`-modules `M`, `N`, the
canonical arrow

`Pext⁰_A(M, N) ⟶ Ext⁰_{Mod((Sch/U)_τ, 𝒪)}(M^a, N^a)`

is an isomorphism, with no hypothesis. It is the composite of two identifications:
`Pext⁰_A(M, N) = Hom_A(M, N)`, because the degree-`0` cohomology of `Hom_A(M, Iᐧ)` is the kernel
of its first differential and that kernel is the image of the augmentation
(`Module.pureExtZeroIsoHom`); and `Hom_A(M, N) = Ext⁰_{Mod(𝒪)}(M^a, N^a)`, because `M ↦ M^a` is
fully faithful (`Stacks.Adequate.homAddEquivExtZero`). Neither Tag 06ZW nor Tag 06ZG enters: in
degree `0` the comparison is a map on `Hom`, so no derived functor and no injective resolution
in a category of functors is needed.

Functoriality in `M` and `N` is the naturality of the two halves, which is
`Stacks.Adequate.homAddEquivExtZero_naturality_left` and `_naturality_right` for the `Ext` half
and `Module.homComplexZeroHom_naturality_left` and `Module.homComplexZeroHom_naturality_right`
for the `Pext` half; see the module documentation for why the latter two are stated at the Hom
complex that computes `Module.pureExt` rather than at `Module.pureExt` itself.

The `letI` preamble is not a list of hypotheses: both entries are the standard derived-category
and `Ext` choices for the sheaves of modules on the site, spelled out rather than registered
because declaring them as `instance`s in this chapter changes instance selection for files that
do not import this one. It matches the preamble of
`Stacks.Adequate.bijective_mapExtAddHom_ι_adequate_zero`, the degree-`0` registration of
Tag 06ZW, so the two share one spelling of each object.
declarations.statement:
public def pureExtZeroAddEquivExtZero (M N : ModuleCat.{u} A) :
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    letI : HasExt.{u + 1} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf) :=
      hasExt_of_hasDerivedCategory _
    Module.pureExt (A := A) M N 0 ≃+
      Ext ((associatedTilde B).obj M) ((associatedTilde B).obj N) 0
declarations.comment: degree 0, where the canonical arrow is the action of M ↦ M^a on Hom composed with the computation of Pext in degree 0, and neither Tag 06ZW nor Tag 06ZG is needed; functorial in M and N by homAddEquivExtZero_naturality_left/_right together with Module.homComplexZeroHom_naturality_left/_right. Every degree is pureExtToExt_bijective_and_natural in HigherExtsAdequate/AdequateExtComparisonAll

declarations.name: Ab.exact_lim_map_of_isMittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B → C → D` be an exact sequence of inverse systems of abelian groups indexed by
`ℕ`. If `A` satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, then the induced sequence on inverse limits
`lim B → lim C → lim D` is exact at `lim C`.

The proof is the source's: `ψ` factors through `K = Ker(χ)` by an epimorphism `ψ'`, whose kernel
is a quotient of `A`, hence Mittag-Leffler (02N1); so `lim B → lim K` is onto (02N1), and
`lim K = Ker(lim χ)` because `lim` preserves kernels.
declarations.statement:
theorem Ab.exact_lim_map_of_isMittagLeffler {A B C D : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u}} (φ : A ⟶ B) (ψ : B ⟶ C)
    (χ : C ⟶ D)
    (hφψ : φ ≫ ψ = 0) (hψχ : ψ ≫ χ = 0)
    (hAB : (ShortComplex.mk φ ψ hφψ).Exact) (hBC : (ShortComplex.mk ψ χ hψχ).Exact)
    (hML : (A ⋙ forget Ab).IsMittagLeffler) :
    (ShortComplex.mk (lim.map ψ) (lim.map χ)
      (by rw [← lim.map_comp, hψχ, Functor.map_zero])).Exact

declarations.name: ModuleCat.exact_lim_map_of_isMittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070B for towers of modules.** Let `A → B → C → D` be an exact sequence of inverse
systems of `R`-modules indexed by `ℕ`. If `A` satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, then the
induced sequence on inverse limits `lim B → lim C → lim D` is exact at `lim C`.

This is the same argument as `Ab.exact_lim_map_of_isMittagLeffler`, run with the two inputs for
towers of modules: `ψ` factors through `K = Ker(χ)` by an epimorphism `ψ'`, whose kernel is a
quotient of `A`, hence Mittag-Leffler; so `lim B → lim K` is onto, and `lim K = Ker(lim χ)`
because `lim` preserves kernels.
declarations.statement:
theorem ModuleCat.exact_lim_map_of_isMittagLeffler {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    {A B C D : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{v} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) (ψ : B ⟶ C) (χ : C ⟶ D)
    (hφψ : φ ≫ ψ = 0) (hψχ : ψ ≫ χ = 0)
    (hAB : (ShortComplex.mk φ ψ hφψ).Exact) (hBC : (ShortComplex.mk ψ χ hψχ).Exact)
    (hML : (A ⋙ forget (ModuleCat.{v} R)).IsMittagLeffler) :
    (ShortComplex.mk (lim.map ψ) (lim.map χ)
      (by rw [← lim.map_comp, hψχ, Functor.map_zero])).Exact
declarations.comment: for towers of modules

declarations.name: essentially_constant_iff_direct_sum_decomposition
declarations.doc:
For a directed preorder `ι` and an inverse system `F : ιᵒᵖ ⥤ 𝓐` in an
abelian category with a limit cone `c`, the system is essentially constant if
and only if there is an index `i₀` admitting a compatible direct-sum
decomposition with eventually-vanishing `Z`-summand.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentially_constant_iff_direct_sum_decomposition
    [IsDirected ι (· ≤ ·)]
    (F : ιᵒᵖ ⥤ 𝓐) (c : Cone F) (_hc : IsLimit c) :
    (∃ (i : ιᵒᵖ) (s : F.obj i ⟶ c.pt),
        EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantWith F c i s) ↔
      HasDirectSumDecomposition F c

declarations.name: isMittagLeffler_forget_iff_of_isEssentiallyConstantPro
declarations.doc:
Let `0 → (A_i) → (B_i) → (C_i) → 0` be a short exact sequence of inverse
systems of abelian groups indexed by a cofiltered category `J`. If `(C_i)` is
essentially constant, then `(A_i)` has the Mittag-Leffler property iff
`(B_i)` does.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLeffler_forget_iff_of_isEssentiallyConstantPro
    {J : Type*} [Category J] [IsCofiltered J]
    (S : ShortComplex (J ⥤ Ab))
    (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hC : EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantPro S.X₃) :
    (S.X₁ ⋙ forget Ab).IsMittagLeffler ↔ (S.X₂ ⋙ forget Ab).IsMittagLeffler

declarations.name: isIso_comparisonHomologyLimit_of_isMittagLeffler
declarations.doc:
For a countable inverse system of 4-term complexes of abelian groups, if
`(A^{-2}_i)` and `(A^{-1}_i)` are Mittag-Leffler and
`(H^{-1}_i)` is essentially constant, then the comparison morphism from the
`0`-cohomology of the limit complex to the limit of the `0`-cohomologies is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_comparisonHomologyLimit_of_isMittagLeffler
    (A_neg2 A_neg1 A_0 A_1 : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{v})
    (d_neg2 : A_neg2 ⟶ A_neg1) (d_neg1 : A_neg1 ⟶ A_0) (d_0 : A_0 ⟶ A_1)
    (h_neg1 : ∀ i, d_neg2.app i ≫ d_neg1.app i = 0)
    (h_0 : ∀ i, d_neg1.app i ≫ d_0.app i = 0)
    (hML_neg2 : (A_neg2 ⋙ forget Ab).IsMittagLeffler)
    (hML_neg1 : (A_neg1 ⋙ forget Ab).IsMittagLeffler)
    (hEC : EssentiallyConstantPro.IsEssentiallyConstantPro
      (homologyInvSystem d_neg2 d_neg1 h_neg1)) :
    IsIso (comparisonHomologyLimit d_neg1 d_0 h_0)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_sequence_quasiIso_truncGE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070F.** Let `A` be an abelian category and let `P` be a class of objects of `A`
which contains a zero object, is closed under finite products, and is such that every object of
`A` is a subobject of an object satisfying `P`. Let `K` be a cochain complex. Then there are
complexes `I n`, quasi-isomorphisms `f n : τ_{≥ -n} K ⟶ I n` and morphisms
`g n : I (n + 1) ⟶ I n` forming a commutative ladder under the canonical truncations of `K`,
such that (1) each `f n` is degreewise monomorphic, (2) each `I n` is bounded below with all
terms satisfying `P`, and (3) each `g n` is degreewise a split surjection whose kernel satisfies
`P`. This is the dual of Stacks 06XX.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_sequence_quasiIso_truncGE (P : ObjectProperty A) [P.ContainsZero]
    (hprod : ∀ X Y : A, P X → P Y → P (X ⊞ Y))
    (hP : ∀ X : A, ∃ (Y : A) (_ : P Y) (i : X ⟶ Y), Mono i) (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) :
    ∃ (I : ℕ → CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : ∀ n : ℕ, K.truncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ⟶ I n)
      (g : ∀ n : ℕ, I (n + 1) ⟶ I n),
      (∀ n, QuasiIso (f n)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), Mono ((f n).f i)) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, (I n).IsStrictlyGE (-(n : ℤ))) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), P ((I n).X i)) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), ∃ (C : A) (_ : P C) (e : (I (n + 1)).X i ≅ (I n).X i ⊞ C),
          e.inv ≫ (g n).f i = biprod.fst) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, K.πTruncGE (-((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) ≫ f (n + 1) ≫ g n
          = K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ≫ f n)

registrations.name: CochainComplex.IsKInjective
registrations.comment: definition: every chain map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic

registrations.name: CochainComplex.isKInjective_iff_rightOrthogonal
registrations.comment: Hom_{K(A)}(M, I) = 0 for every acyclic M

declarations.name: CochainComplex.isKInjective_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070I.** Let `A` be an abelian category and `I` a cochain complex in `A`. The
following are equivalent: (1) `I` is K-injective; (2) for every quasi-isomorphism `M ⟶ N` in
`K(A)`, precomposition `Hom_{K(A)}(N, I) → Hom_{K(A)}(M, I)` is bijective; (3) for every `N` in
`K(A)`, the localization map `Hom_{K(A)}(N, I) → Hom_{D(A)}(N, I)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isKInjective_tfae {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] (I : CochainComplex A ℤ) :
    List.TFAE
      [I.IsKInjective,
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).isLocal
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I),
        ∀ N : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ),
          Function.Bijective (DerivedCategory.Qh.map :
            (N ⟶ (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I) → _)]

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isRightDerivable_and_computesRightDerived_of_exists_quasiIso_isKInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070K.** Let `A` be an abelian category such that every complex admits a
quasi-isomorphism towards a K-injective complex, and let `F : K(A) ⥤ D'` be a functor on the
homotopy category of `ℤ`-indexed cochain complexes, `Qis(A)` its class of quasi-isomorphisms.
Then `F` has a right derived functor `RF : D(A) ⥤ D'` and `RF(I) = F(I)` for K-injective `I`:

* `F` is right derivable with respect to `Qis(A)`, i.e. `RF` is everywhere defined in the sense of
  Tag 05SV: for every object `X` of `K(A)` the ind-object `X/Qis(A) ⥤ D'`,
  `(s : X ⟶ X') ↦ F(X')`, is essentially constant (`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsRightDerivable`);
* every K-injective complex `I` computes `RF` in the sense of Tag 05SX: `RF` is defined at `I` and
  the canonical map `F(I) ⟶ RF(I)` is an isomorphism
  (`CategoryTheory.Functor.ComputesRightDerived`);
* in Mathlib's terms, `F` has a pointwise right derived functor with respect to `Qis(A)` — a
  pointwise left Kan extension `RF : D(A) ⥤ D'` of `F` along the localization `K(A) ⥤ D(A)` —
  and for any localization functor `L` for `Qis(A)` and any right derived functor `RF` of `F`
  with unit `α : F ⟶ L ⋙ RF`, the component `α.app I : F(I) ⟶ RF(I)` at a K-injective `I` is an
  isomorphism.

The source assumes `F` exact between triangulated categories; none of the conclusions uses this,
so the statement is for an arbitrary functor.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRightDerivable_and_computesRightDerived_of_exists_quasiIso_isKInjective
    {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] {H : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} H]
    (F : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤ H)
    (hA : ∀ K : CochainComplex A ℤ, ∃ (I : CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : K ⟶ I),
      I.IsKInjective ∧ QuasiIso f) :
    F.IsRightDerivable (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      (∀ I : CochainComplex A ℤ, I.IsKInjective →
        F.ComputesRightDerived (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)) ∧
      F.HasPointwiseRightDerivedFunctor (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
      ∀ {D : Type u₃} [Category.{v₃} D] (L : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤ D)
        [L.IsLocalization (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
        (RF : D ⥤ H) (α : F ⟶ L ⋙ RF)
        [RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor α (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
        (I : CochainComplex A ℤ), I.IsKInjective →
          IsIso (α.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I))

declarations.name: isKInjective_limit_of_inverseSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 070L (Lemma 13.31.8).** Let `A` be an abelian category and let
`F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ` be an inverse system of complexes (transition maps
go from larger to smaller index). Assume:
1. each complex `F.obj (op n)` is K-injective;
2. each transition map `F_{n+1} ⟶ F_n` is a split surjection in every degree `m`;
3. the limit complex `limit F` exists (the degreewise limits exist in `A`).
Then the limit complex `limit F` is K-injective.

The proof reduces (via `exists_cylinder_extension_limit`, then
`exists_compatible_homotopy_family`) to the Mittag–Leffler construction of a compatible
family of null-homotopies; the final step postcomposes the canonical cylinder homotopy
`cylinder.ι₀ ≃ cylinder.ι₁` with the assembled extension.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_limit_of_inverseSystem
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ) [HasLimit F]
    (hKInj : ∀ n : ℕ, (F.obj (op n)).IsKInjective)
    (hSplit : ∀ (n : ℕ) (m : ℤ),
      IsSplitEpi ((F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).f m)) :
    (limit F).IsKInjective

declarations.name: CochainComplex.isKInjective_limit_and_isDerivedLimit_of_isSplitEpi
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be an abelian category with countable products and let
`𝓘 : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ` be an inverse system of K-injective complexes whose transition maps
are degreewise split epimorphisms. Then the limit `I = lim 𝓘` exists, it is K-injective, and it
represents the derived limit `R lim 𝓘ₙ`. Moreover, for every cochain complex `K` of `A` equipped
with quasi-isomorphisms `f n : τ_{≥ -n} K ⟶ 𝓘ₙ` making the ladder over the canonical maps
`K.πTruncGE (-n) : K ⟶ τ_{≥ -n} K` commute — the system produced by Stacks 070F, for which
`R lim 𝓘ₙ` is `R lim τ_{≥ -n} K`, as the `f n` become isomorphisms in `D(A)` — the unique map
`γ : K ⟶ I` compatible with the maps `K ⟶ τ_{≥ -n} K ⟶ 𝓘ₙ` is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if
every map `K ⟶ R lim τ_{≥ -n} K` compatible with the projections, as in Stacks 0H72, is an
isomorphism in `D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isKInjective_limit_and_isDerivedLimit_of_isSplitEpi
    (𝓘 : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ) (h𝓘 : ∀ n : ℕ, (𝓘.obj ⟨n⟩).IsKInjective)
    (hsplit : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), IsSplitEpi ((𝓘.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).f i)) :
    ∃ (_ : HasLimit 𝓘) (_ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => (𝓘 ⋙ Q).obj ⟨n⟩),
      (limit 𝓘).IsKInjective ∧ IsDerivedLimit (𝓘 ⋙ Q) (Q.obj (limit 𝓘)) ∧
        ∀ (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : ∀ n : ℕ, K.truncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ⟶ 𝓘.obj ⟨n⟩),
          (∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (f n)) →
          (∀ n : ℕ, K.πTruncGE (-((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) ≫ f (n + 1) ≫
              𝓘.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op = K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ≫ f n) →
          ∃ γ : K ⟶ limit 𝓘, (∀ n : ℕ, γ ≫ limit.π 𝓘 ⟨n⟩ = K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ≫ f n) ∧
            (QuasiIso γ ↔ ∀ (L : DerivedCategory A) (c : Q.obj K ⟶ L)
              (p : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => (𝓘 ⋙ Q).obj ⟨n⟩)
              (δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => (𝓘 ⋙ Q).obj ⟨n⟩) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
              Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ =>
                  Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (𝓘 ⋙ Q).obj ⟨n⟩) n -
                    Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (𝓘 ⋙ Q).obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫
                      (𝓘 ⋙ Q).map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
                distTriang (DerivedCategory A) →
              (∀ n : ℕ, c ≫ p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => (𝓘 ⋙ Q).obj ⟨n⟩) n =
                Q.map (K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ≫ f n)) → IsIso c)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.toLimitOfTruncGEResolutions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 070P**, the displayed arrow `ℱ• → ℐ•`. Given an inverse system `𝓘` of
cochain complexes and maps `f n : τ_{≥ -n} K ⟶ 𝓘ₙ` commuting with the canonical truncation maps
of `K`, this is the induced map `K ⟶ lim 𝓘`. For the tower of Stacks 070F the target is the
candidate K-injective complex of Stacks 070L.
declarations.statement:
def toLimitOfTruncGEResolutions (𝓘 : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ) [HasLimit 𝓘]
    (K : CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : ∀ n : ℕ, K.truncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ⟶ 𝓘.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hladder : ∀ n : ℕ, K.πTruncGE (-((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) ≫ f (n + 1) ≫
      𝓘.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op = K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ≫ f n) :
    K ⟶ limit 𝓘

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.quasiIso_to_limit_of_truncGE_resolutions
declarations.doc:
Let `O` be a sheaf of rings on a site, let `K` be a cochain complex of `O`-modules, and let
`𝓘` be an inverse system of K-injective complexes with degreewise split-epimorphic transition
maps resolving the truncations `τ_{≥ -n} K` compatibly with the canonical maps
`K ⟶ τ_{≥ -n} K`. If a subset `B` of the objects of the site covers every object and
`H^p(V, H^q(K)) = 0` for every `V ∈ B`, every `p > d` and every `q < 0`, then the canonical map
`γ : K ⟶ lim 𝓘` is a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_to_limit_of_truncGE_resolutions {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} (O : Sheaf J RingCat.{u})
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [EnoughInjectives (SheafOfModules.{u} O)]
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ℤ)
    (𝓘 : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ℤ)
    (f : ∀ n : ℕ, K.truncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ⟶ 𝓘.obj ⟨n⟩)
    (hf : ∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (f n))
    (hcompat : ∀ n : ℕ,
      K.πTruncGE (-((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)) ≫ f (n + 1) ≫ 𝓘.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op =
        K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ≫ f n)
    (h𝓘 : ∀ n : ℕ, (𝓘.obj ⟨n⟩).IsKInjective)
    (hsplit : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), IsSplitEpi ((𝓘.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).f i))
    [HasLimit 𝓘] (γ : K ⟶ limit 𝓘)
    (hγ : ∀ n : ℕ, γ ≫ limit.π 𝓘 ⟨n⟩ = K.πTruncGE (-(n : ℤ)) ≫ f n)
    (B : Set C) (d : ℕ)
    (hB : ∀ U : C, ∃ 𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u} U, 𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i, B (𝒰.X i))
    (hvan : ∀ V : C, B V → ∀ p : ℕ, d < p → ∀ q : ℤ, q < 0 →
      IsZero (moduleCohomology O V p
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u} O) q).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)))) :
    QuasiIso γ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.toZariskiRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R.** The morphism of ringed sites
`id_{small, étale, Zar} : (S_étale, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)`: the continuous inclusion of the small
Zariski site of `S` into the small étale site of `S`, with structure map the identification of
the sections of `𝒪_S` over an open with the functions on it.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def toZariskiRingedToposHom :
    RingedToposSiteHom (ringedTopos B S hS) S.zariskiRingedTopos
declarations.comment:
the morphism of ringed sites `id_{small, étale, Zar} : (S_étale, 𝒪) → (S_Zar,
  𝒪_S)`, item (26) of the list of Topologies, Section 03FE at `f = id`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseStructureComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, part (1): the structure-sheaf map `f_big^♯ : 𝒪_Y ⟶ f_{big, *}𝒪_X`**, in each
of the five topologies.  Its component at an object `T/Y` is the map on global functions induced
by the projection `X ×_Y T ⟶ T`, that is, the map `𝒪(T/Y) ⟶ 𝒪(X ×_Y T/X)` of the source.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.structureComparison` read at the `τ`-localized
topologies: the same map of presheaves of rings, the topology entering only through the sheaf
conditions and the continuity instance.
declarations.comment: part (1): `f_big^♯` for the big fppf, syntomic, smooth, étale and Zariski sites, at the structure sheaves over which modules are taken

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseChange
declarations.doc:
The continuous functor giving the morphism of big fppf sites
`f_big : (Sch/X)_fppf → (Sch/Y)_fppf`: base change along `f`, sending `T / Y` to `X ×_Y T / X`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def baseChange : BigFppfOver B Y hY ⥤ BigFppfOver B X hX
declarations.comment: part (1): the functor underlying the morphism of big fppf sites `f_big`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isMorphismOfSites_baseChange
declarations.doc:
Base change along `f` defines a morphism of big fppf sites
`f_big : (Sch/X)_fppf → (Sch/Y)_fppf` in the sense of Stacks 00X1: it is continuous, and the
pushforward it induces on sheaves of sets has a left exact left adjoint.

That left adjoint is the inverse image of `f_big`, which is restriction along postcomposition:
the pushforward along the cocontinuous functor `CategoryTheory.Over.map` agrees with the
pushforward along its continuous right adjoint `CategoryTheory.Over.pullback`, and restriction
along postcomposition is left exact.
declarations.statement:
public instance isMorphismOfSites_baseChange :
    IsMorphismOfSites.{u + 1} (baseChange B hX hY f) (topology B Y hY) (topology B X hX)
declarations.comment: part (1): base change is a morphism of sites, so `f_big` is one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.structureComparison
declarations.doc:
The map of structure sheaves `f_big^♯ : 𝒪_Y → f_{big, *} 𝒪_X` which, together with the
morphism of sites `f_big`, makes `f_big` a morphism of ringed sites
`((Sch/X)_fppf, 𝒪_X) ⟶ ((Sch/Y)_fppf, 𝒪_Y)` as in Stacks Definition 03AD.

Its component at an object `T / Y` is the map on global functions induced by the projection
`X ×_Y T → T`, that is, the map `𝒪(T / Y) → 𝒪(X ×_Y T / X)` of the source.
declarations.comment: part (1): the structure-sheaf map `f_big^♯` of the morphism of ringed sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, part (2).** The morphism of ringed sites
`(f_small, f_small^♯) : (X_étale, 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Y_étale, 𝒪_Y)` attached to a morphism of schemes
`a : X ⟶ Y`: the underlying morphism of sites is base change of étale `Y`-schemes along `a`, and
the structure map pulls a global function on an étale `V / Y` back along the projection
`X ×_Y V ⟶ V`.
declarations.comment: part (2): the morphism of ringed sites of the small étale sites of schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
The morphism of small étale *ringed topoi* `(a_small, a_small^♯) : (X_étale, 𝒪_X) ⟶
(Y_étale, 𝒪_Y)` of a morphism of schemes `a : X ⟶ Y`.
declarations.comment: part (2), read in the 2-category of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isMorphismOfSites_bigSiteBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, part (1): `f_big` is a morphism of sites**, at the universe of the sections
of the structure sheaves, which is the universe at which a morphism of ringed sites reads its
site condition.

A localized big site is essentially small at the universe of its morphisms
(`AlgebraicGeometry.essentiallySmall_overBase`) and base change is continuous and flat, so this
is `isMorphismOfSites_of_essentiallySmall`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMorphismOfSites_bigSiteBaseChange :
    IsMorphismOfSites.{u} (Over.pullback f) (overTopology τ B S hS) (overTopology τ B T hT)
declarations.comment: part (1): `f_big` is a morphism of sites, in each of the five topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSiteStructureSharp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, part (1): the structure map `f_big^♯ : 𝒪_S ⟶ f_{big, *}𝒪_T`**, in each of
the five topologies.  On an object `S'/S` it is the map on global functions induced by the
projection `T ×_S S' ⟶ S'`, that is, the usual `pr_{S'}^♯`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSiteStructureSharp :
    commStructureSheaf S (overTopology τ B S hS) (bigSiteToOver B S hS)
        (bigSite_structure_isSheaf B S hS) ⟶
      ((Over.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{u} (overTopology τ B S hS)
        (overTopology τ B T hT)).obj
      (commStructureSheaf T (overTopology τ B T hT) (bigSiteToOver B T hT)
        (bigSite_structure_isSheaf B T hT))
declarations.comment: part (1): `f_big^♯`, in each of the five topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.bigSiteRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, part (1), in all five topologies at once.**  A morphism of schemes of a big
`τ`-site makes the morphism of big sites `f_big : (\Sch/T)_τ ⟶ (\Sch/S)_τ` a morphism of ringed
sites

```
  (f_big, f_big^♯) : ((\Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) ⟶ ((\Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪_S)
```

in the sense of Stacks 03AD, for `τ` the fppf, syntomic, smooth, étale or Zariski topology.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigSiteRingedSiteHom :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (bigSiteRingedSite B T hT) (bigSiteRingedSite B S hS)
declarations.comment: part (1): `(f_big, f_big^♯)` for the big fppf, syntomic, smooth, étale and Zariski sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiPiRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
The projection `π_S : (\Sch/S)_{Zar} ⟶ S_{Zar}` of Topologies, Lemma 020Z, as a morphism of
ringed sites

```
  (π_S, π_S^♯) : ((\Sch/S)_{Zar}, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_{Zar}, 𝒪).
```

Its structure map is the identity, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiPiStructureSharp_eq_id`.
declarations.comment: `π_S` on the Zariski sites, as a morphism of ringed sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiPiStructureSharp_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**The structure map of `π_S` is the identity.**  Both structure sheaves are global functions
on the underlying scheme, and the inclusion of the small site into the big one is compatible
with the two underlying-scheme functors on the nose, so no comparison map intervenes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallZariskiPiStructureSharp_eq_id :
    (smallZariskiPiRingedSiteHom B (S := S)).fsharp = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: `π_S^♯` is the identity on the Zariski sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiToBig_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**`i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` for the Zariski sites.**  Restricting the structure sheaf of the big
Zariski site over `S` along the functor `V/T ↦ V/S` which presents the morphism of topoi
`i_f : \mathrm{Sh}(T_{Zar}) ⟶ \mathrm{Sh}((\Sch/S)_{Zar})` of Topologies, Lemma 020Y returns the
structure sheaf of the small Zariski site of `T`.

By the inverse-image formula of that lemma the inverse image of `i_f` is that restriction, so
this is the identity `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` which the remark gives as the reason `i_f` becomes a
morphism of ringed topoi.
declarations.comment: the identity `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` for the big and small Zariski sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePiRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
The projection `π_S : (\Sch/S)_\etale ⟶ S_\etale` of Topologies, Lemma 021G, as a morphism
of ringed sites

```
  (π_S, π_S^♯) : ((\Sch/S)_\etale, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_\etale, 𝒪).
```

Its structure map is the identity, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePiStructureSharp_eq_id`.
declarations.comment: `π_S` on the étale sites, as a morphism of ringed sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtalePiStructureSharp_eq_id
declarations.doc:
**The structure map of `π_S` is the identity**, for the same reason as on the Zariski
sites.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallEtalePiStructureSharp_eq_id :
    (smallEtalePiRingedSiteHom B (S := S)).fsharp = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: `π_S^♯` is the identity on the étale sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleToBig_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**`i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` for the étale sites.**  Restricting the structure sheaf of the big étale
site over `S` along the functor `V/T ↦ V/S` which presents the morphism of topoi
`i_f : \mathrm{Sh}(T_\etale) ⟶ \mathrm{Sh}((\Sch/S)_\etale)` of Topologies, Lemma 021F returns
the structure sheaf of the small étale site of `T`.
declarations.comment: the identity `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` for the big and small étale sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiToBigZariski_inverseImageStructureIso
declarations.doc:
**`i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` for the Zariski sites**, as an isomorphism of sheaves of commutative
rings.  The inverse image of `i_f` is restriction, and restricting the structure sheaf of the
big Zariski site over `S` along `V/T ↦ V/S` returns the structure sheaf of the small Zariski
site of `T` — which is `AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiToBig_structureSheaf`, an equality by
`rfl`.  The comparison is the identity on sections.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallZariskiToBigZariski_inverseImageStructureIso :
    (inverseImageCommRingFunctor (smallZariskiToBigZariskiToposHom B f)).obj
        (bigSiteRingedSite (τ := .zariski) B S.1 S.property).O ≅
      (smallZariskiRingedSite B T.1 T.property).O
declarations.comment: `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` for the Zariski sites, as an isomorphism of ring sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiToBigZariskiRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R for `i_f` on the Zariski sites.**  The morphism of topoi
`i_f : \mathrm{Sh}(T_{Zar}) ⟶ \mathrm{Sh}((\Sch/S)_{Zar})` of Topologies, Lemma 020Y, as a
morphism of ringed topoi

```
  (i_f, i_f^♯) : (\mathrm{Sh}(T_{Zar}), 𝒪) ⟶ (\mathrm{Sh}((\Sch/S)_{Zar}), 𝒪),
```

in the sense of Stacks 01D3.  Its structure map is the one determined by `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪`.
declarations.comment: `i_f` on the Zariski sites, as a morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_smallZariskiToBigZariskiRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**The formal content of "because `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪`":** the structure map of `i_f` in
inverse-image form is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public instance isIso_smallZariskiToBigZariskiRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImage :
    IsIso (smallZariskiToBigZariskiRingedToposHom B f).fSharpInverseImage
declarations.comment: `i_f` is a morphism of ringed topoi because `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪`, Zariski case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleToBigEtale_inverseImageStructureIso
declarations.doc:
**`i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` for the étale sites**, as an isomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings.
The underlying equality of ring sheaves is
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleToBig_structureSheaf`, which holds by `rfl`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtaleToBigEtale_inverseImageStructureIso :
    (inverseImageCommRingFunctor (smallEtaleToBigEtaleToposHom B f)).obj
        (bigSiteRingedSite (τ := .etale) B S.obj S.property).O ≅
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B T.obj T.property).O
declarations.comment: `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪` for the étale sites, as an isomorphism of ring sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleToBigEtaleRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R for `i_f` on the étale sites.**  The morphism of topoi
`i_f : \mathrm{Sh}(T_\etale) ⟶ \mathrm{Sh}((\Sch/S)_\etale)` of Topologies, Lemma 021F, as a
morphism of ringed topoi, in the sense of Stacks 01D3.
declarations.comment: `i_f` on the étale sites, as a morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_smallEtaleToBigEtaleRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**The formal content of "because `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪`":** the structure map of `i_f` in
inverse-image form is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public instance isIso_smallEtaleToBigEtaleRingedToposHom_fSharpInverseImage :
    IsIso (smallEtaleToBigEtaleRingedToposHom B f).fSharpInverseImage
declarations.comment: `i_f` is a morphism of ringed topoi because `i_f^{-1}𝒪 = 𝒪`, étale case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiStructureSharp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, part (2): the structure map `f_small^♯ : 𝒪_S ⟶ f_{small, *}𝒪_T`** on the
small Zariski sites.  On an open `V/S` it is the map on global functions induced by the
projection `T ×_S V ⟶ V`, through the identification of small Zariski base change with the
fibre product.
declarations.comment: part (2): `f_small^♯` for the small Zariski sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, part (2), for the small Zariski site.**  A morphism of schemes `f : T ⟶ S` of
a big Zariski site makes the morphism of small sites `f_small : T_{Zar} ⟶ S_{Zar}` a morphism of
ringed sites

```
  (f_small, f_small^♯) : (T_{Zar}, 𝒪_T) ⟶ (S_{Zar}, 𝒪_S)
```

in the sense of Stacks 03AD.  This is the "similarly for the small Zariski site" of part (2),
and item (27) of the change-of-topologies list of Topologies, Section 03FE.
declarations.comment: part (2): `(f_small, f_small^♯)` for the small Zariski sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.isMorphismOfSites_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, the generator `id_{τ, τ'}` of the 03FE list: it is a morphism of sites**, at
the universe of the sections of the structure sheaves.

The identity functor is representably flat, and a localized big site is essentially small at the
universe of its morphisms, so this is `isMorphismOfSites_of_essentiallySmall`.
declarations.comment: `id_{τ, τ'}` is a morphism of sites, at the universe of the structure rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.idRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R for the generator `id_{τ, τ'}`.**  The identity
`id_{τ, τ'} : (\Sch/S)_τ ⟶ (\Sch/S)_{τ'}`, for `τ` finer than `τ'`, as a morphism of ringed
sites

```
  (id_{τ, τ'}, id_{τ, τ'}^♯) : ((\Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) ⟶ ((\Sch/S)_{τ'}, 𝒪).
```

Its structure map is the identity, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.idRingedSiteHom_fsharp`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def idRingedSiteHom (h : τ.IsFiner τ') :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (B.carriedOverRingedSite S hS τ) (B.carriedOverRingedSite S hS τ')
declarations.comment: `id_{τ, τ'}` as a morphism of ringed sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.idRingedSiteHom_fsharp
declarations.doc:
**`id_{τ, τ'}^♯` is the identity.**  The two sites are presented by the one functor to the
schemes over `S`, so their structure presheaves are literally the same presheaf and no
comparison map intervenes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem idRingedSiteHom_fsharp (h : τ.IsFiner τ') :
    (B.idRingedSiteHom S hS h).fsharp = 𝟙 _
declarations.comment: `id_{τ, τ'}^♯` is the identity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.bigBaseChangeRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, part (1) on the sites carried by `B`.**  `f_big` as a morphism of ringed
sites, for each of the five topologies.
declarations.comment: part (1): `f_big` on the five big sites carried by one big fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.bigRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R for every big-site entry of the change-of-topologies list.**  For a morphism of
schemes `f : T ⟶ S` of a chosen big fppf site and `τ` finer than `τ'`, the morphism of sites
`f_{sites} : (\Sch/T)_τ ⟶ (\Sch/S)_{τ'}` of Topologies, Section 03FE is a morphism of ringed
sites

```
  (f_{sites}, f_{sites}^♯) : ((\Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) ⟶ ((\Sch/S)_{τ'}, 𝒪_S).
```

This is entries (1)–(15) of that list: `f_{sites}` is `id_{τ, τ'} ∘ f_{big}`, and the
composition of morphisms of ringed sites is Stacks 03AD, part (3).
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigRingedSiteHom (h : τ.IsFiner τ') (f : B.obj hT ⟶ B.obj hS) :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (B.carriedOverRingedSite T hT τ) (B.carriedOverRingedSite S hS τ')
declarations.comment: entries (1)-(15) of the 03FE list: `(Sch/T)_τ ⟶ (Sch/S)_τ'` for τ finer than τ'

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.bigToSmallEtaleRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, entries (16)–(19) of the change-of-topologies list.**  For `τ` finer than the
étale topology, the morphism of sites `f_{sites} : (\Sch/T)_τ ⟶ S_\etale` is a morphism of
ringed sites.  It is `π_S ∘ f_{sites}`, with `f_{sites} : (\Sch/T)_τ ⟶ (\Sch/S)_\etale` the
big-site entry and `π_S : (\Sch/S)_\etale ⟶ S_\etale` the projection of Topologies,
Lemma 021G.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigToSmallEtaleRingedSiteHom (h : τ.IsFiner .etale)
    (f : B.obj hT ⟶ B.obj hS) :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (B.carriedOverRingedSite T hT τ)
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B.toBigEtaleSite S hS)
declarations.comment: entries (16)-(19) of the 03FE list: `(Sch/T)_τ ⟶ S_étale`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.bigToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, entries (20)–(24) of the change-of-topologies list.**  For every one of the
five topologies, the morphism of sites `f_{sites} : (\Sch/T)_τ ⟶ S_{Zar}` is a morphism of
ringed sites.  It is `π_S ∘ f_{sites}`, with `π_S : (\Sch/S)_{Zar} ⟶ S_{Zar}` the projection of
Topologies, Lemma 020Z.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def bigToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom (h : τ.IsFiner .zariski)
    (f : B.obj hT ⟶ B.obj hS) :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (B.carriedOverRingedSite T hT τ)
      (smallZariskiRingedSite B.toBigZariskiSite S hS)
declarations.comment: entries (20)-(24) of the 03FE list: `(Sch/T)_τ ⟶ S_Zar`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallEtaleToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R, entry (26) of the change-of-topologies list.**  The morphism of sites
`T_\etale ⟶ S_{Zar}` is a morphism of ringed sites: it is
`id_{small, \etale, Zar} ∘ f_{small}`, with `f_{small} : T_\etale ⟶ S_\etale` the morphism of
ringed small étale sites of Stacks 070R part (2) and `id_{small, \etale, Zar}` the inclusion of
the small Zariski site of `S` into its small étale site.

The target is the opens model of the small Zariski site of `S`, which is the model in which
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.toZariskiRingedSiteHom` is stated; see the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallEtaleToSmallZariskiRingedSiteHom (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    {X Y : B.Scheme} (a : X ⟶ Y) :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (smallEtaleRingedSite B X.obj X.property)
      Y.obj.zariskiRingedSite
declarations.comment: entry (26) of the 03FE list: `T_étale ⟶ S_Zar`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ChangeOfSites.structureSharp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R.**  The structure-sheaf homomorphism `f_sites^♯ : 𝒪 ⟶ f_{sites, *}𝒪` of a
change-of-topologies morphism of sites.

Here `F` is the continuous functor representing `f_sites`, in the direction opposite to it, and
`p` is the family of projections `T ×_S S' ⟶ S'` of underlying schemes, natural in the object
`S'` of the target site.  The homomorphism is pullback of global functions along `p`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def structureSharp [F.IsContinuous J K]
    (p : F ⋙ toOver' ⋙ Over.forget T ⟶ toOver ⋙ Over.forget S)
    (hJ : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf S toOver))
    (hK : Presheaf.IsSheaf K (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf T toOver')) :
    commStructureSheaf S J toOver hJ ⟶
      (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{u} J K).obj
        (commStructureSheaf T K toOver' hK)
declarations.comment: the structure-sheaf homomorphism `f_sites^♯` of a change-of-topologies morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ChangeOfSites.structureSharpOfBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R.**  The structure-sheaf homomorphism of a change-of-topologies morphism of
sites whose continuous functor is exhibited as scheme-theoretic base change along
`f : T ⟶ S`: on an object `S'/S` it is the usual map
`pr_{S'}^♯ : 𝒪(S') ⟶ 𝒪(T ×_S S')`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def structureSharpOfBaseChange [F.IsContinuous J K] (f : T ⟶ S)
    (bc : F ⋙ toOver' ≅ toOver ⋙ Over.pullback f)
    (hJ : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf S toOver))
    (hK : Presheaf.IsSheaf K (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf T toOver')) :
    commStructureSheaf S J toOver hJ ⟶
      (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous CommRingCat.{u} J K).obj
        (commStructureSheaf T K toOver' hK)
declarations.comment: `f_sites^♯` for a functor exhibited as base change along `f : T ⟶ S`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ChangeOfSites.ringedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R.**  A change-of-topologies morphism of sites, together with its
structure-sheaf homomorphism, is a morphism of ringed sites

```
  (f_sites, f_sites^♯) : ((Sch/T)_τ, 𝒪_T) ⟶ ((Sch/S)_{τ'}, 𝒪_S)
```

in the sense of Stacks 03AD.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def ringedSiteHom (hF : IsMorphismOfSites.{u} F J K)
    (p : F ⋙ toOver' ⋙ Over.forget T ⟶ toOver ⋙ Over.forget S)
    (hJ : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf S toOver))
    (hK : Presheaf.IsSheaf K (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf T toOver')) :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (ringedSite T K toOver' hK) (ringedSite S J toOver hJ)
declarations.comment: a change-of-topologies morphism of sites is one of ringed sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ChangeOfSites.ringedSiteHomOfBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070R.**  The same, for a continuous functor exhibited as scheme-theoretic base
change along `f : T ⟶ S`, which is the form every morphism of the change-of-topologies list
takes.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def ringedSiteHomOfBaseChange (hF : IsMorphismOfSites.{u} F J K)
    (f : T ⟶ S) (bc : F ⋙ toOver' ≅ toOver ⋙ Over.pullback f)
    (hJ : Presheaf.IsSheaf J (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf S toOver))
    (hK : Presheaf.IsSheaf K (Stacks.Sites.structurePresheaf T toOver')) :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (ringedSite T K toOver' hK) (ringedSite S J toOver hJ)
declarations.comment: the morphism of ringed sites of a base-change morphism of sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleIsoPullbackSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070S (2).**  Let `F` be an arbitrary sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules.  The pullback of `F`
along the morphism of ringed sites `id_{small,étale,Zar} : (S_étale, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` is the
étale sheafification of the presheaf `(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f^*F)` on `S_étale`.

The pullback is `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModule`, presented by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleSheafificationIso` as the sheafification of the
pullback of presheaves of modules, and the identification is the sheafification of the
comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.pullbackSectionsComparison`, an isomorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.isIso_sheafification_map_pullbackSectionsComparison`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleIsoPullbackSections (F : S.Modules) :
    (associatedModule B S hS).obj F ≅
      (PresheafOfModules.sheafification.{u} (𝟙 (structureSheaf B S hS).obj)).obj
        (pullbackSectionsPresheaf B S hS F)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleIsoSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070S for the small étale site of `S`.** The associated module `𝓕^a` of a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_S`-module `𝓕` is the étale sheafification of the pullback-sections presheaf
`(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f⁺𝓕)` of Stacks 03DS.

`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.associatedModuleSheafificationIso` presents `𝓕^a` as the
sheafification of the presheaf-level pullback along the structure map, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.sectionsComparisonSheafifiesToIso` — Stacks 070S (2), with no
hypothesis — says the comparison of that pullback with the pullback-sections presheaf becomes an
isomorphism after sheafification.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def associatedModuleIsoSections (F : S.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (associatedModule B S hS).obj F ≅
      (PresheafOfModules.sheafification.{u} (𝟙 (structureSheaf B S hS).obj)).obj
        (sectionsPresheafOfModules B S hS F)
declarations.comment: part (2), in the shape of part (1): 𝓕^a is the étale sheafification of the pullback-sections presheaf of Stacks 03DS

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.sectionsComparisonSheafifiesToIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070S part (2) for `S_étale`**: the hypothesis
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.SectionsComparisonSheafifiesToIso` holds.
declarations.statement:
public theorem sectionsComparisonSheafifiesToIso :
    SectionsComparisonSheafifiesToIso B S hS
declarations.comment: part (2), small site at τ = étale

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseSmallEtalePullbackIsoSectionsSheafification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070S part (3).**  For an *arbitrary* sheaf of `𝒪`-modules `𝓖` on the small étale
site `S_étale`, the inverse image `(id_{τ,étale})^*𝓖` along the morphism of ringed sites
`id_{τ,étale} : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_étale, 𝒪)` is the `τ`-sheafification of the étale sheaf
`(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f_small^*𝓖)` on `(Sch/S)_τ`, where `f_small : T_étale ⟶ S_étale` is the
morphism of ringed small étale sites of Stacks 070R (2).

Here `(id_{τ,étale})^*` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.smallEtaleToBaseModulePullback`, the sections rule is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.smallEtaleSectionsPresheafOfModules`, and the identification is
`CategoryTheory.SheafOfModules.pullbackIso` — which presents `(id_{τ,étale})^*𝓖` as the
`τ`-sheafification of the presheaf-level inverse image — followed by the `τ`-sheafification of
the comparison `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.smallEtaleSectionsGamma`, which is locally
bijective by `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isIso_baseSheafification_map_smallEtaleSectionsGamma`.

The topology `τ` is one refining the étale topology: that is the range `τ ∈ {étale, smooth,
syntomic, fppf}` over which the source states this clause, the Zariski topology being excluded
there.  By
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isContinuous_smallEtaleToFppf_of_etaleTopology_le` that single
hypothesis also supplies the continuity of the inclusion of the small étale site, i.e. the
existence of `id_{τ,étale}`, so the instance argument below is never an extra assumption: it is
discharged at each of the four `τ`, and nothing discharges it at `τ = Zariski`, which is exactly
why the source excludes that one.  `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseSmallEtaleIsoSectionsEtale`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseSmallEtaleIsoSectionsFppf` are the hypothesis-free
instances at `τ = étale` and `τ = fppf`; `.baseSmallEtaleIsoSectionsSmooth` and
`.baseSmallEtaleIsoSectionsSyntomic`, in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Descent/AssociatedModulePullbackBigToSmallEtale.lean`, are the
other two.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def baseSmallEtalePullbackIsoSectionsSheafification
    (hτ : B.etaleTopology ≤ B.baseTopology τ) :
    (smallEtaleToBaseModulePullback B S hS τ).obj 𝓖 ≅
      (PresheafOfModules.sheafification.{u}
          (𝟙 (FibredSite.baseRingStructureSheaf B S hS τ).obj)).obj
        (smallEtaleSectionsPresheafOfModules B S hS τ 𝓖)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoPullbackSections
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070S (1).**  Let `F` be an arbitrary sheaf of `𝒪_S`-modules.  For each of the five
topologies `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, the pullback of `F` along the
morphism of ringed sites `id_{τ,Zar} : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` is the
`τ`-sheafification of the presheaf `(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f^*F)` on `(Sch/S)_τ`.

The pullback is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModule`, presented by
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleSheafificationIso` as the
`τ`-sheafification of the pullback of presheaves of modules; the presheaf of sections is
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.pullbackSectionsPresheaf`; and the identification is the
`τ`-sheafification of the comparison
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.pullbackSectionsComparison`, which is locally surjective and
locally injective for every `τ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isLocallySurjective_pullbackSectionsComparison` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.isLocallyInjective_pullbackSectionsComparison`).
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleIsoSections
declarations.doc:
For each of the five topologies `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, the
associated module of a quasi-coherent module `F` on `S` — the pullback along the morphism of
ringed sites `id_{τ,Zar} : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) → (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` — is the `τ`-sheafification of the
pullback-sections presheaf `(f : T → S) ↦ Γ(T, f⁺F)` of Stacks 03DS.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseAssociatedModuleSheafificationIso` at `F`, which
presents the associated module as the `τ`-sheafification of the presheaf-level pullback, followed
by the `τ`-sheafification of `AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.sectionsComparison`.
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseToZariskiRingedSiteHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070U**: the morphism of ringed sites `f : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` in the
sense of Stacks 03AD, for each `τ ∈ {Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf}`, at independent
object universes: the continuous inclusion of the small Zariski site of `S` into the big
`τ`-site, which defines a morphism of sites at the universe of the structure rings, together
with the identification of the sections of `𝒪_S` over an open with the functions on it.

This is the same geometric datum and the same structure map as
`AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.baseToZariskiRingedToposHom`, which records only continuity;
what is added is the site condition, and with it the morphism of topoi.
declarations.statement:
public def baseToZariskiRingedSiteHom (τ : SiteKind) :
    RingedSite.HomGeneral (baseRingedSite B S hS τ) S.zariskiRingedSite
declarations.comment: the morphism of ringed sites of 070R, for each of the five topologies, at independent object universes

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.Coarsening.derivedAdequateCoarseningEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070V].** Let `S` be a scheme and let `τ` and `τ'` be two of the five
topologies `Zar`, `étale`, `smooth`, `syntomic`, `fppf`, with `τ` stronger than `τ'`, and denote
`𝒪_τ` and `𝒪_τ'` the structure sheaf `𝒪` viewed as a sheaf on the big `τ`-site, resp. the big
`τ'`-site, over `S`. Then `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ)` and `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ')` are canonically equivalent.

The equivalence is [Stacks, Tag 07A8] for the category of the site, the class of adequate
`𝒪_τ`-modules and the affine objects of the site
(`Stacks.Cohomology.CompareTopologies.derivedEquivalenceImageOfLEOfEssentiallySmall`). Its
assumption (1) is `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.Coarsening.adequateIsFineSheaf`, (2) is
`Stacks.Adequate.adequate_isWeakSerreClass`, (3) is
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.Coarsening.affineCoarseCovering` and (4) is
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isZero_rightDerived_sections_of_isAdequate`, [Stacks, Tag 06VM] (3).
Assumption (1) also identifies the image class of the adequate `𝒪_τ`-modules with the adequate
`𝒪_τ'`-modules (`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.Coarsening.adequate_site_eq_imageOfLE`).
declarations.statement:
def derivedAdequateCoarseningEquivalence
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (SheafOfModules.{u} c.site.structureSheaf)] :
    (BigSite.derivedAdequate.{u, u, d} B).FullSubcategory ≌
      (BigSite.derivedAdequate.{u, u, d'} c.site).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment:
the canonical equivalence of `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ)` and `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ')`, for a coarsening
of a chosen big site, at any models of the two derived categories

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.derivedAdequateTopologyEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070V].** Let `S` be a scheme and let `τ, τ'` be two of the five topologies
`Zar`, `étale`, `smooth`, `syntomic`, `fppf`, and denote `𝒪_τ`, resp. `𝒪_τ'`, the structure sheaf
`𝒪` viewed as a sheaf on the big site `(Sch/S)_τ`, resp. `(Sch/S)_τ'`, the two big sites being
built on the same category of schemes over `S` (their cutoffs agree). Then `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ)` and
`D_Adeq(𝒪_τ')` are canonically equivalent.

The five topologies are linearly ordered, `Zar ≺ étale ≺ smooth ≺ syntomic ≺ fppf`; if `τ` is
finer than `τ'` this is `Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.derivedAdequateEquivalenceOfIsFiner`, and
otherwise `τ'` is finer than `τ` and it is the inverse of that equivalence with the roles of the
two sites exchanged. Both derived categories are taken at arbitrary models.
declarations.statement:
def BigSite.derivedAdequateTopologyEquivalence (B : BigSite τ S) (B' : BigSite τ' S)
    (hcut : B'.cutoff = B.cutoff)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d'} (SheafOfModules.{u} B'.structureSheaf)] :
    (BigSite.derivedAdequate.{u, u, d} B).FullSubcategory ≌
      (BigSite.derivedAdequate.{u, u, d'} B').FullSubcategory
declarations.comment:
`D_Adeq(𝒪_τ) ≌ D_Adeq(𝒪_τ')` for any two of the five topologies, for big sites
built on the same category of schemes over `S`, at any models of the two derived categories

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.Coarsening.derivedAdequateEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070V].** Let `S` be a scheme and let `τ` and `τ'` be two of the five
topologies `Zar`, `étale`, `smooth`, `syntomic`, `fppf`, with `τ` stronger than `τ'`, and
denote `𝒪_τ` and `𝒪_τ'` the structure sheaf `𝒪` viewed as a sheaf on the big `τ`-site, resp.
the big `τ'`-site, over `S`. Then `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ)` and `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ')` are canonically isomorphic.

The equivalence is the second conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 07A8] applied to the class of adequate
`𝒪_τ`-modules and to the collection of affine objects of the site. Its assumption (2) is
`Stacks.Adequate.adequate_isWeakSerreClass` and its assumption (4) is
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isZero_rightDerived_sections_of_isAdequate`, which is
[Stacks, Tag 06VM] (3) and carries no hypothesis; assumptions (1) and (3) are `hfine` and
`hcover`.
That the two sides are the derived categories of the *adequate* modules for each topology,
rather than of the adequate modules for `τ` and their image under `ε_*`, is
`Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.Coarsening.adequate_site_eq_imageOfLE`.

The inputs this declaration takes are: `comparison`, the second conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 07A8]
in the generality of its source, which this library does not prove; `AdequateIsFineSheaf` and
`AffineCoarseCovering`, assumptions (1) and (3) of 07A8 for the adequate modules and the affine
objects. Assumption (2) is discharged outright by [Stacks, Tag 06VQ], and assumption (4) by
[Stacks, Tag 06VM] (3). The modules have values in the universe of the site, the universe at
which [Stacks, Tag 06VQ] is available.
declarations.statement:
public def derivedAdequateEquivalence
    [HasSheafify c.topology AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [c.topology.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{u} B.structureSheaf)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{u} c.site.structureSheaf)]
    (comparison : ∀ {C : Type (u + 1)} [Category.{u} C] {J J' : GrothendieckTopology C}
      (h : J' ≤ J) (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u})
      [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
      [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
      [HasSheafify J' AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
      [J'.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
      [EnoughInjectives (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
      [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{u} R)]
      [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (SheafOfModules.{u} (R.ofLE h))]
      (A : ObjectProperty (SheafOfModules.{u} R)) (ℬ : Set C), A.IsWeakSerreClass →
        (∀ U : C, ∃ 𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} U, 𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ J' U ∧ ∀ i, ℬ (𝒰.X i)) →
        (∀ U ∈ ℬ, ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → ∀ F, A F →
          IsZero ((((sheafSections J AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (op U)).rightDerived p).obj
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf R).obj F))) →
        ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB A).FullSubcategory ≌
          (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
            (Stacks.Cohomology.CompareTopologies.imageOfLE.{u + 1, u, u, u} h R
              A)).FullSubcategory))
    (hfine : AdequateIsFineSheaf.{u, u} c) (hcover : AffineCoarseCovering.{u} c) :
    (BigSite.derivedAdequate.{u, u, d} B).FullSubcategory ≌
      (BigSite.derivedAdequate.{u, u, d} c.site).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment:
the canonical isomorphism of `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ)` and `D_Adeq(𝒪_τ')` as an equivalence
of categories, for a coarsening of a chosen big site; the inputs it takes, and the one proved
here, are listed in the docstring

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.derivedRestrictAdequate
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070W], the pushforward landing in the source's own form `Rf_* = f_*`.**
Restriction to the small Zariski site of `S` along the morphism of [Stacks, Tag 070U], assumed
right exact, induces a functor `D_Adeq(𝒪) ⥤ D_QCoh(S)` on the chosen big fppf site over `S`;
on modules it lands in the quasi-coherent sheaves by [Stacks, Tag 06VM] (1).
declarations.statement:
public def BigSite.derivedRestrictAdequate :
    (BigSite.derivedAdequate.{u, u, d} (BigSite.ofBigFppfSite B S hS)).FullSubcategory ⥤
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment:
the assertion that Rf_* carries D_Adeq(𝒪) into D_QCoh(S), in the source's own form
Rf_* = f_* for the Zariski restriction of the morphism of Tag 070U, with right exactness of that
restriction an instance argument. Lf^*, adjointness and Rf_* Lf^* ≅ id are covered elsewhere

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.derivedAdequateAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070W], the adjointness assertion.** Given the ambient derived adjunction
`Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` on all `𝒪`-modules and the two landing assertions, the restricted functors
`Lf^* : D_QCoh(S) ⥤ D_Adeq(𝒪)` and `Rf_* : D_Adeq(𝒪) ⥤ D_QCoh(S)` are adjoint.

The inputs are the ambient derived adjunction `adj : L ⊣ R` on all modules and both landing
assertions — `hL`, that `Lf^*` carries `D_QCoh(S)` into `D_Adeq(𝒪)`, and `hR`, that `Rf_*`
carries `D_Adeq(𝒪)` into `D_QCoh(S)`. Each carries its own content and none is proved here: the
ambient adjunction of [Stacks, Tag 07A6] is not available for the morphism of [Stacks, Tag 070U]
at the universes in which that morphism is stated. The isomorphism `Rf_* Lf^* ≅ id` is a
separate declaration.
declarations.comment: the adjointness assertion only, for the subcategories D_Adeq(O) and D_QCoh(S); the ambient adjunction and the two landing assertions are inputs, listed in the docstring

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.derivedQuasicoherentAdequateAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070W], the adjunction.** The morphism `f` of [Stacks, Tag 070U] induces
adjoint functors `Lf^* : D_QCoh(S) ⥤ D_Adeq(𝒪)` and `Rf_* : D_Adeq(𝒪) ⥤ D_QCoh(S)`: the total
derived functors of [Stacks, Tag 07A6] preserve the two subcategories, and their adjunction
restricts.
declarations.statement:
def BigSite.derivedQuasicoherentAdequateAdjunction :
    B.derivedQuasicoherentPullback ⊣ B.derivedAdequateDirectImage
declarations.comment:
the adjunction Lf^* ⊣ Rf_* between D_QCoh(S) and D_Adeq(O), for the derived
functors of the morphism of Tag 070U on a chosen big site, with no hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.derivedAdequateDirectImagePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070W], `Rf_* Lf^* ≅ id_{D_QCoh(S)}`.** The unit of the derived adjunction
is invertible at every complex with quasi-coherent cohomology.
declarations.statement:
def BigSite.derivedAdequateDirectImagePullbackIso :
    B.derivedQuasicoherentPullback ⋙ B.derivedAdequateDirectImage ≅ 𝟭 _
declarations.comment:
Rf_* Lf^* ≅ id on D_QCoh(S), for the derived functors of the morphism of
Tag 070U on a chosen big site

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.isLocalization_trW_derivedParasitic_derivedAdequateDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070X].** Let `S` be a scheme and `f : ((Sch/S)_τ, 𝒪) ⟶ (S_Zar, 𝒪_S)` the
morphism of [Stacks, Tag 070U], for a chosen big site and any of the five topologies. The derived
direct image `Rf_* : D_Adeq(𝒪) ⥤ D_QCoh(S)` is the Verdier quotient of `D_Adeq(𝒪)` by
`D_𝒞(𝒪)`, the complexes whose cohomology modules are parasitic adequate: it is a localization
functor for the morphisms whose cone lies in `D_𝒞(𝒪)`, so that it induces an equivalence
`D_Adeq(𝒪)/D_𝒞(𝒪) ⟶ D_QCoh(S)`.
declarations.comment:
the equivalence D_Adeq(O)/D_C(O) -> D_QCoh(S) induced by Rf_*, with the quotient
the Verdier quotient by the complexes with parasitic adequate cohomology, for the derived functors
of the morphism of Tag 070U on a chosen big site and each of the five topologies

declarations.name: Stacks.Adequate.BigSite.derivedAdequateParasiticQuotientEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 070X], the equivalence `D_Adeq(𝒪)/D_𝒞(𝒪) ≌ D_QCoh(S)`.** The Verdier
quotient of `D_Adeq(𝒪)` by the complexes with parasitic adequate cohomology is equivalent to
`D_QCoh(S)`, by the functor induced by `Rf_*`.
declarations.comment:
the equivalence of categories D_Adeq(O)/D_C(O) ≌ D_QCoh(S) itself, for the
derived functors of the morphism of Tag 070U on a chosen big site and each of the five
topologies

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.exists_isRightDerivedValueAt_and_isIso_of_isKInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 070Y.** Let `A` be an abelian category and `F : K(A) ⥤ H` a functor on the homotopy
category of `ℤ`-indexed cochain complexes. Let `I` be a K-injective complex. Then:

* `I` computes the right derived functor `RF` relative to the quasi-isomorphisms of `K(A)`: the
  ind-object `I/Qis(A) ⥤ H`, `(s : I ⟶ N) ↦ F(N)`, is essentially constant, and the canonical
  map `F(I) ⟶ RF(I)`, i.e. the coprojection of its value cocone at the index `𝟙 I`, is an
  isomorphism;
* `RF` is defined at every object `X` of `K(A)` that is quasi-isomorphic to `I`, i.e. admits a
  quasi-isomorphism to or from `I` in `K(A)`.

The source assumes `F` exact between triangulated categories; neither conclusion uses this.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isRightDerivedValueAt_and_isIso_of_isKInjective
    {A : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} A] [Abelian A] {H : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} H]
    (F : HomotopyCategory A (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⥤ H)
    (I : CochainComplex A ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    (∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ))
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).obj I) c ∧
        IsIso (c.ι.app (MorphismProperty.Under.mk ⊤
          (𝟙 ((HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).obj I))
          (MorphismProperty.id_mem _ _)))) ∧
      ∀ X : HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ),
        ((∃ s : X ⟶ (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).obj I,
            HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ) s) ∨
          (∃ s : (HomotopyCategory.quotient A (.up ℤ)).obj I ⟶ X,
            HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ) s)) →
        ∃ c, F.IsRightDerivedValueAt (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ)) X c

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.stalkExtensionByZeroIso
declarations.doc:
The stalk of extension by zero from `C/U` is the direct sum of the stalks
at the points of `C/U` above the given point.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def stalkExtensionByZeroIso
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) (p : GrothendieckTopology.Point.{u, u, u} X.J)
    (U : X.C) (G : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))
    [HasWeakSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}] :
    (p.presheafFiber.obj (((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
      (F := Over.forget U)
        (𝟙 ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))).obj G).val.presheaf)) ≅
      ∐ fun x : p.fiber.obj U => (p.over x).presheafFiber.obj G.val.presheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.ExtensionByZero.OfEssentiallySmall.stalkExtensionByZeroIso
declarations.doc:
The stalk of extension by zero from `C/U` is the direct sum of the stalks

noncomputable def stalkExtensionByZeroIso

    (p : GrothendieckTopology.Point.{u, u, c} X.J)
    (U : X.C) (G : SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))

    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}] :
    (p.presheafFiber.obj (((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
      (F := Over.forget U) (𝟙 ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))).obj
        G).val.presheaf)) ≅
      ∐ fun x : p.fiber.obj U => (p.over x).presheafFiber.obj G.val.presheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.KInjective.quasiIso_canonicalMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 071B.** Let `F` be a complex of `𝒪_X`-modules on a ringed space, with candidate
K-injective resolution `F ⟶ lim_n I_n` as in Tag 071A, and write `ℋ^q = H^q(F)` for its
cohomology sheaves. If a set `B` of opens of `X` covers every open of `X` and `H^p(U, ℋ^q) = 0`
for every `U ∈ B`, every `p > d` and every `q < 0`, then that canonical map is a
quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_canonicalMap (O : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) RingCat.{u})
    (F : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ℤ)
    (R : CandidateKInjectiveResolution O F) (B : Set (Opens X)) (d : ℕ)
    (hB : ∀ V : Opens X, ∃ 𝒰 : Set (Opens X), 𝒰 ⊆ B ∧ (V : Set X) = ⋃ U ∈ 𝒰, (U : Set X))
    (hvan : ∀ U ∈ B, ∀ p : ℕ, d < p → ∀ q : ℤ, q < 0 →
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} O (Opposite.op U)).rightDerived p).obj
        (F.homology q))) :
    QuasiIso R.canonicalMap

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CompositeRightDerived.cohomology
declarations.doc:
The `p`-th cohomology functor over an object,
`H^p(U, -) = R^p \Gamma(U, -) : Sheaf J Ab \to Ab`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cohomology (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (U : C) (p : ℕ) :

**Cohomology of a sheaf of modules over an object of a ringed site (Stacks 071G).**  The
`p`-th cohomology `Hᵖ(U, F)` is the `p`-th right derived functor of the sections functor
`Γ(U, -) = SheafOfModules.evaluation O (op U)`, evaluated at `F`; it is a module over the ring

    [EnoughInjectives (SheafOfModules.{wModule} O)]
    (U : C) (p : ℕ) (F : SheafOfModules.{wModule} O) :
    ModuleCat.{wModule} (O.obj.obj (op U))
