declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family of smooth 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` with
`|𝒳| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒵 j|)`, and let `F` be a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_étale`. If every inverse
image `f j^{-1} F` is locally quasi-coherent, then so is `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
    {J : Type v} {𝒵 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hsmooth : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)) F.presheaf)
    (hlqc : ∀ j, IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f j).hom ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS (f j).hom)
      ((stackModulePresheafPullback.{u, w, u} B S hS (f j)).obj F)) :
    IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasicoherent_stackModuleHigherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and
`ℱ` a locally quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-module on `𝒳_étale`. Then every higher direct image `Rⁱf_*ℱ`,
computed in the étale topology, is locally quasi-coherent on `𝒴_étale`.

Modules have sections in the universe `u` of the schemes, the universe of the structure sheaf
`𝒪_𝒳`, and `Rⁱf_*` is the right derived functor of the direct image right adjoint to the inverse
image (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.stackModuleHigherDirectImage`). The small étale sites `U_étale` in
the definition of local quasi-coherence (**Stacks 06WJ**) are those of the big étale site `E`
whose underlying category is that of the big fppf site `B` (`E.cutoff = B.cutoff`), which is the
convention of the source: `Sch_étale` is the big étale site on the underlying category `Sch_α`
of `Sch_fppf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasicoherent_stackModuleHigherDirectImage
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (F : StackModules B S hS .etale 𝒳)
    (hF : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids F.val)
    (i : ℕ) :
    IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS 𝒴.val.val.p 𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
      ((stackModuleHigherDirectImage B S hS f .etale i).obj F).val
declarations.comment: the whole statement, for every degree i, with the source's hypotheses: f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, ℱ a locally quasi-coherent 𝒪_𝒳-module on 𝒳_étale; modules have sections in the universe of the structure sheaf, and Sch_étale is the big étale site E on the underlying category of Sch_fppf (E.cutoff = B.cutoff), as in the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictSheafModulesPullbackComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0761.** The comparison map
`c_φ : f_{small}^*(F|_{U'_ét}) ⟶ F|_{U_ét}` of Equation (103.7.0.1) for an étale sheaf `F` of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules, below an arrow `φ : x ⟶ y` of `𝒳` lying over a morphism of schemes
`f : U ⟶ U'`. Here `f_{small}^*` is the pullback of modules along the morphism of ringed topoi
`(Sh(U_ét), 𝒪_U) ⟶ (Sh(U'_ét), 𝒪_{U'})`, that is `SheafOfModules.pullback` along the morphism
of ringed sites `ε_f` of **Stacks 070R (2)**, whose ring map is the map `f_{small}^♯` of
**Stacks 06WC**; it includes sheafification.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictSheafPullbackComparison` (the adjunct, across
sheafification on `U_ét`, of the presheaf map
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictModulePullbackComparison` of Sheaves on Stacks, Equation
(96.9.4.1)) read through the identification
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.sheafifiedPullbackComparisonIso` of the sheafified presheaf pullback
with `SheafOfModules.pullback`.

This is also **Stacks 06WC**, the comparison map
`c_φ : a_{small}^*(F|_{V_ét}) ⟶ F|_{U_ét}` of `𝒪_{U_ét}`-modules of Sheaves on Stacks,
Equation (96.9.4.1), for an étale sheaf `F` of modules on `𝒳`: there too `a_{small}^*` is the
pullback of sheaves of modules along `ε_a`, the map `a_{small}^♯` being the one of Stacks 070R,
and `F|_{V_ét}`, `F|_{U_ét}` are the restrictions of Stacks 06WJ.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictSheafModulesPullbackComparison
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B))) :
    (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (SmallEtale.smallEtaleStructureMapRing E
        (smallEtaleBaseMorphism B E h S hS p φ))).obj
        ((restrictSheafToSmallEtale.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp y).obj F) ⟶
      (restrictSheafToSmallEtale.{u, v, w, u} B E h S hS p hp x).obj F
declarations.comment: with `f_{small}^*` the pullback of sheaves of modules along the morphism of ringed topoi of the small étale sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0762.** An étale sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules *has the flat base change property* when the
comparison map `c_φ` of **Stacks 0761**, taken with `a_{small}^*` the inverse image of sheaves of
modules as the source takes it, is an isomorphism for every arrow `φ` of `𝒳` lying over a flat
morphism of schemes. The source calls the name nonstandard.

This is the property read in the source's ambient category `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`. The source
takes `𝒳` an algebraic stack; here `𝒳` is any category fibred in groupoids over
`(Sch/S)_{fppf}`. The module sections live in any universe `m` with `UnivLE.{u, m}`; the source's
case is `m = u`, where `UnivLE.{u, u}` always holds, so this is no extra hypothesis. At `m = u`
the comparison map is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.restrictSheafModulesPullbackComparison`, whose
domain is `SheafOfModules.pullback`, up to the isomorphism of
`hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE_iff_isIso_restrictSheafModulesPullbackComparison`.
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasFlatBaseChangeProperty` is the same definition with the inverse image
of presheaves of modules, which on an étale sheaf is strictly the stronger demand; the
implementation notes of this file say why.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE
    (F : SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B))) : Prop
declarations.comment: for an étale sheaf of modules on a category fibred in groupoids, with `f_{small}^*` the pullback of sheaves of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (4), for presheaves of modules.** The colimit of a diagram of presheaves
of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules each having the flat base change property of **Stacks 0762** again has the flat
base change property, and the colimit is the colimit of presheaves of modules.

For an arrow `φ` of `𝒳` lying over a flat morphism of schemes, the comparison map `c_φ` is the
component of a natural transformation from `F ↦ a_{small}^*(F|_{V_ét})` to `F ↦ F|_{U_ét}`. Both
functors preserve colimits — the first because `a_{small}^*` is a left adjoint, the second
because restriction to the small étale site is restriction along a functor followed by a change
of scalars — and the component at a colimit of a natural transformation of colimit-preserving
functors is an isomorphism as soon as every component on the diagram is.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_colimit
    (K : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj)
    (hK : ∀ i, HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp τ hτ (K.obj i)) :
    HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp τ hτ (colimit K)
declarations.comment: part (4), with the ambient category the presheaves of modules rather than the étale sheaves of modules: a colimit of presheaves of modules with the flat base change property has the flat base change property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (4), for presheaves of modules**, in the form for an arbitrary colimit
cocone: the vertex of a colimit cocone on a diagram of presheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules with the flat
base change property has the flat base change property.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_colimit` transported along the
canonical isomorphism of the vertex with the chosen colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_of_isColimit
    {K : J ⥤ PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj}
    {c : Cocone K} (hc : IsColimit c)
    (hK : ∀ i, HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp τ hτ (K.obj i)) :
    HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp τ hτ c.pt
declarations.comment: part (4), with the ambient category the presheaves of modules rather than the étale sheaves of modules: the vertex of a colimit cocone on a diagram of presheaves of modules with the flat base change property has the flat base change property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_flatBaseChangeModulePresheaves
declarations.doc:
The presheaves of modules with the flat base change property are closed under colimits of
shape `J`, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_of_isColimit`.

This is **Stacks 0764, part (4), for presheaves of modules**: through Mathlib's instances
`CategoryTheory.Limits.hasColimitsOfShape_of_closedUnderColimits` and
`CategoryTheory.preservesColimitOfShape_of_createsColimitsOfShape_and_hasColimitsOfShape`, the
subcategory has colimits of shape `J` and its inclusion preserves them.
declarations.statement:
instance isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_flatBaseChangeModulePresheaves :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape
      (flatBaseChangeModulePresheaves.{u, v, w} B E h S hS p hp τ hτ) J
declarations.comment: part (4), with the ambient category the presheaves of modules rather than the étale sheaves of modules: the modules with the flat base change property have colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_flatBaseChangeModulePresheaves
declarations.doc:
The presheaves of modules with the flat base change property are closed under colimits of
shape `J`, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_of_isColimit`.

This is **Stacks 0764, part (4), for presheaves of modules**: through Mathlib's instances
`CategoryTheory.Limits.hasColimitsOfShape_of_closedUnderColimits` and
`CategoryTheory.preservesColimitOfShape_of_createsColimitsOfShape_and_hasColimitsOfShape`, the
subcategory has colimits of shape `J` and its inclusion preserves them.
declarations.statement:
instance isClosedUnderColimitsOfShape_flatBaseChangeModulePresheaves :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape
      (flatBaseChangeModulePresheaves.{u, v, w} B E h S hS p hp τ hτ) J
declarations.comment: part (4), with the ambient category the presheaves of modules rather than the étale sheaves of modules: those colimits agree with the colimits of all modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (2), for presheaves of modules.** The cokernel of a morphism of
presheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules with the flat base change property of **Stacks 0762** has the flat
base change property. This is the closure under cokernels asked for by **Stacks 0754**.

A cokernel is a colimit indexed by the walking parallel pair, whose two values are the source
and the target of the morphism, so this is a case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_colimit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_cokernel
    {F G : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj} (α : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp τ hτ F)
    (hG : HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp τ hτ G) :
    HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp τ hτ (cokernel α)
declarations.comment: part (2), with the ambient category the presheaves of modules rather than the étale sheaves of modules: the closure under cokernels asked for by Stacks 0754

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_initial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (2), for presheaves of modules.** An initial presheaf of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules — equivalently, a zero object — has the flat base change property of
**Stacks 0762**. This is the containment of a zero object asked for by **Stacks 0754**.

An initial object is the colimit of the empty diagram, so this is the case of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_of_isColimit` in which the hypothesis on the
diagram is vacuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangeProperty_initial
    {F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp τ hτ).obj}
    (hF : IsInitial F) :
    HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp τ hτ F
declarations.comment: part (2), with the ambient category the presheaves of modules rather than the étale sheaves of modules: the zero object asked for by Stacks 0754

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (4), as the source states it.** The colimit of a diagram of étale sheaves
of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules each having the flat base change property of **Stacks 0762** again has the flat
base change property, the colimit being the colimit of `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`.

For an arrow `φ` of `𝒳` lying over a flat morphism of schemes, `c_φ^{sh}` is the component of a
natural transformation from `F ↦ a_{small}^*(F|_{V_ét})` to `F ↦ F|_{U_ét}`. Both functors
preserve colimits — the first because the inverse image of sheaves of modules is a left adjoint,
by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.sheafifiedPullbackComparisonAdjunction`, the second by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesColimitsOfShape_restrictSheafToSmallEtale` — and the component
at a colimit of a natural transformation of colimit-preserving functors is an isomorphism as
soon as every component on the diagram is.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_colimit
    (K : J ⥤ SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B))) [HasColimit K]
    (hK : ∀ i, HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp (K.obj i)) :
    HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp (colimit K)
declarations.comment: part (4), with the ambient category the étale sheaves of modules, as the source states it -- and so with a_small^* the inverse image of sheaves of modules, not the inverse image of presheaves of modules used by the part (4) registrations of FlatBaseChangeColimits: a colimit of étale sheaves of modules with the flat base change property has the flat base change property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_of_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (4), as the source states it**, in the form for an arbitrary colimit
cocone: the vertex of a colimit cocone on a diagram of étale sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules with the
flat base change property has the flat base change property.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_colimit` transported along the
canonical isomorphism of the vertex with the chosen colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_of_isColimit
    {K : J ⥤ SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B))} {c : Cocone K} (hc : IsColimit c)
    (hK : ∀ i, HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp (K.obj i)) :
    HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp c.pt
declarations.comment: part (4), with the ambient category the étale sheaves of modules, as the source states it -- and so with a_small^* the inverse image of sheaves of modules, not the inverse image of presheaves of modules used by the part (4) registrations of FlatBaseChangeColimits: the vertex of a colimit cocone on a diagram of étale sheaves of modules with the flat base change property has the flat base change property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasColimitsOfShape_flatBaseChangeEtaleModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (4), as the source states it**: the category of étale sheaves of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules with the flat base change property has the colimits that `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`
has; those colimits exist, the étale sheafification of abelian presheaves on `𝒳` being
available unconditionally.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasColimitsOfShape_flatBaseChangeEtaleModules :
    HasColimitsOfShape J (flatBaseChangeEtaleModules.{u, v, w} B E h S hS p hp).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: part (4), in the source's ambient category Mod(X_etale, O_X): the full subcategory of etale sheaves of modules with the flat base change property has colimits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesColimitsOfShape_flatBaseChangeEtaleModules_ι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (4), as the source states it**: the colimits of étale sheaves of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules with the flat base change property agree with the colimits of
`Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`, the inclusion preserving them.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_flatBaseChangeEtaleModules_ι :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape J (flatBaseChangeEtaleModules.{u, v, w} B E h S hS p hp).ι
declarations.comment: part (4), in the source's ambient category Mod(X_etale, O_X): the colimits of the subcategory agree with the colimits in Mod(X_etale, O_X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_etaleInternalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (6).** Let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_{fppf}` be a category fibred in groupoids and
let `F`, `G` be étale sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules, with `F` of finite presentation on `𝒳_étale`
(Stacks 03DL) and `G` with the flat base change property of Stacks 0762. Then the internal Hom
`𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(F, G)` of `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)` has the flat base change property.

Let `φ : x ⟶ y` lie over a flat morphism, and let `{e_j : y_j ⟶ y}` be an étale covering on
whose members `F` has a finite presentation. At every arrow into some `y_j` lying over a flat
morphism the comparison map of `𝓗om(F, G)` is invertible by the presented case proved above, and
that suffices for `c_φ` by the étale-local criterion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_restrictSheafPullbackComparison_of_etaleCover`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_etaleInternalHom
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
    (hfp : F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite)
    (hG : HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp G) :
    HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp (etaleInternalHom B S hS p hp F G)
declarations.comment: part (6): for F, G in Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳) with F of finite presentation and G with the flat base change property, the internal Hom 𝓗om_{𝒪_𝒳}(F, G) of Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳) has the flat base change property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (1), in the source's ambient category.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a
1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of `S`, and let `F` be an
étale sheaf of `𝒪_𝒴`-modules with the flat base change property of **Stacks 0762** (comparison
maps taken with the inverse image of sheaves of modules on the small étale sites). Then the
inverse image `f^*F` of sheaves of modules has the flat base change property.

An arrow `φ` of `𝒳` lies over the same morphism of schemes as `f φ`, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_restrictSheafPullbackComparison_modulePullback_iff` at each arrow
lying over a flat morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_modulePullback
    (F : SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS q hq (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
    (hF : HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS q hq F) :
    HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp
      ((modulePullback B S hS p q hp hq f hf (etaleTopology B)
        (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (1), the whole part, in the source's ambient category of étale sheaves of modules (a_small^* the inverse image of sheaves of modules), for any 1-morphism f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴 of categories fibred in groupoids over (Sch/S)_fppf, in particular any morphism of algebraic stacks: the inverse image f^*F of a module F with the flat base change property has the flat base change property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (3), in the source's ambient category.** Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family
of smooth 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` with `|𝒳| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒵 j|)`, and let `F` be
an étale sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules. If every inverse image `f j^* F` of sheaves of modules has the
flat base change property of **Stacks 0762**, then so does `F`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_etaleCovering_family_fibre_lift` covers the scheme below any
object of `𝒳` by étale morphisms over which the object lifts through some `f j`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_of_etaleLocal` concludes.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective [UnivLE.{u, m}]
    {J : Type v} {𝒵 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hsmooth : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : SheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
    (hF : ∀ j, HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f j).hom ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS (f j).hom)
      ((modulePullback B S hS (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f j).hom ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p)
        𝒳.val.val.p (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS (f j).hom)
        𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f j).hom) rfl
        (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj F)) :
    HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids F
declarations.comment: part (3), the whole part, in the source's ambient category of étale sheaves of modules (a_small^* the inverse image of sheaves of modules): for a family of smooth 1-morphisms f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳 of algebraic stacks with |𝒳| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒵 j|), if each inverse image f j^* F has the flat base change property then so does F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_tensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (5).** The tensor product, in `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`, of two étale sheaves of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules with the flat base change property of **Stacks 0762** has the flat base change
property.

The tensor product is the canonical one, `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor` at the
structure sheaf of the associated étale site; it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.etaleTensorSheaf` by `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.etaleTensorSheaf_eq`. The
sheafification instances it is formed with hold for every `𝒳`, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSheafify_etaleAssociatedTopology` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.wEqualsLocallyBijective_etaleAssociatedTopology`, and are supplied here.

At an arrow over a flat morphism of schemes this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_restrictSheafPullbackComparison_etaleTensorSheaf`: the
restrictions commute with tensor products, the pullback commutes with tensor products by
**Stacks 03EL**, and under these identifications the comparison map of the tensor product is the
tensor product of the comparison maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_tensor
    (F G : SheafOfModules.{u}
      (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
    (hF : HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp F)
    (hG : HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp G) :
    letI := hasSheafify_etaleAssociatedTopology B S hS p hp
    letI := wEqualsLocallyBijective_etaleAssociatedTopology B S hS p hp
    HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE B E h S hS p hp
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{_, _, _, u, u}
        (structureSheaf B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
          (etaleTopology_le_topology B))).obj F).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (5), with the ambient category the étale sheaves of modules, as the source states it -- and so with a_small^* the inverse image of sheaves of modules: the tensor product in Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳) of two modules with the flat base change property has the flat base change property

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isWeakSerreClass_flatBaseChangeEtaleModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0764, part (2), as the source states it.** The étale sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules with
the flat base change property of **Stacks 0762** form a weak Serre subcategory of
`Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`, in the form **Stacks 0754** gives: a strictly full subcategory containing a
zero object and closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions.

Strict fullness is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_flatBaseChangeEtaleModules`, the zero object
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_initial`, the cokernels are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_cokernel`, the extensions are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_of_shortExact`, and the kernels are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_kernel`, the last with the left exactness
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesFiniteLimits_sheafifiedPullbackComparison`: this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isWeakSerreClass_flatBaseChangeEtaleModules_of_preservesFiniteLimits`
at section universe `u`.

The abelian structure on `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)` is the one coming from étale sheafification of
abelian presheaves on `𝒳`, whose two instances are supplied in the statement by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSheafify_etaleAssociatedTopology` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.wEqualsLocallyBijective_etaleAssociatedTopology`; they are not
hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakSerreClass_flatBaseChangeEtaleModules :
    letI := hasSheafify_etaleAssociatedTopology B S hS p hp
    letI := wEqualsLocallyBijective_etaleAssociatedTopology B S hS p hp
    letI : Abelian (SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B))) :=
      SheafOfModules.instAbelian (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
        (etaleTopology_le_topology B))
    (flatBaseChangeEtaleModules.{u, v, w} B E h S hS p hp).IsWeakSerreClass
declarations.comment: part (2): the étale sheaves of O_X-modules with the flat base change property form a weak Serre subcategory of Mod(X_etale, O_X), in the form of Stacks 0754 -- strictly full, with a zero object, and closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions. The whole of part (2), in the source's ambient category, with a_small^* the inverse image of sheaves of modules, and with no hypothesis beyond the source's

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_moduleSheafHigherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact (Stacks 050U) and quasi-separated
(Stacks 04YW) 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, and let `ℱ` be an étale sheaf of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules which is locally quasi-coherent (Stacks 06WJ) and has the flat base change property
(Stacks 0762). Then every higher direct image `Rⁱf_*ℱ`, computed in the étale topology, has the
flat base change property.

The flat base change property is the source's, read on sheaves
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE`); the sheaves of modules have their
sections in `Type (u + 1)`, where the higher direct images of Stacks 06WE live, and the source
`𝒳` is presented strictly, its structure functor written as the functor of `f` followed by that
of `𝒴`.

This is the registered form of **Stacks 0765**: the whole lemma, in every degree, with the
source's hypotheses and nothing more. The proof is the source's: the criterion of
**Stacks 076Z** (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smoothLocalHigherDirectImageCriterion_unconditional`)
at the rule `LQCoh^fbc`, whose four conditions are discharged in this file and its imports
(**Stacks 06WM**, **Stacks 06WL**, **Stacks 075Y** with **Stacks 0764**, and the affine case).
The presheaf-reading statement
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasFlatBaseChangePropertyUnivLE_moduleSheafHigherDirectImage` is untagged.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFlatBaseChangePropertySheaf_moduleSheafHigherDirectImage
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
    (hlqc : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) F.val)
    (hfbc : HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE.{u, u + 1, u, u + 1} B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) F)
    (i : ℕ) :
    letI := hasSheafify_associatedTopology_of_category_succ B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
    letI := wEqualsLocallyBijective_associatedTopology_of_category_succ B S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p)
    letI := hasSheafify_associatedTopology_of_category_succ B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
    letI := wEqualsLocallyBijective_associatedTopology_of_category_succ B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
    HasFlatBaseChangePropertySheafUnivLE.{u, u + 1, u, u + 1} B E h S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
      𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
      ((moduleSheafHigherDirectImage.{u, u + 1, u, u + 1, u} B S hS
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom ⋙ 𝒴.val.val.p) 𝒴.val.val.p
        (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS f.hom) 𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor f.hom) rfl (etaleTopology B)
        (etaleTopology_le_topology B) i).obj F)
declarations.comment: the whole lemma, in every degree, with the source's hypotheses: f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, F an étale O_X-module that is locally quasi-coherent with the flat base change property (read on sheaves, as in the source); then every R^i f_* F, computed in the étale topology, has the flat base change property. Proved by the criterion of Stacks 076Z applied to LQCoh^fbc, all four of its conditions discharged

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoYonedaPresheaf
declarations.doc:
The contravariant functor `F : 𝒞 ⥤ Groupoids` with `F(U) = Mor_{Cat/𝒞}(𝒞/U, 𝒮)` and
`F(f) : F(V) ⥤ F(U)` given by precomposition with the functor `𝒞/U ⥤ 𝒞/V` induced by
`f : U ⟶ V`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Functor.twoYonedaPresheaf (p : 𝒮 ⥤ 𝒞) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    𝒞ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grpd.{max u₁ v₁ v₂, max u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂}

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoYonedaComparison
declarations.doc: The functor `G : 𝒮' ⥤ 𝒮` sending the pair `(U, x)` to `x(id_U)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def twoYonedaComparison (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    ∫ᶜ (p.twoYonedaPresheaf hp ⋙ Grpd.forgetToCat).toPseudofunctor' ⥤
      (BasedCategory.ofFunctor p).obj

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoYonedaComparison_comp
declarations.doc:
The functor `G` is a functor over `𝒞`: its composite with `p` is the projection of the
category `𝒮'` attached to `F`.
declarations.statement:
lemma twoYonedaComparison_comp (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    p.twoYonedaComparison hp ⋙ p = (presheafOfGroupoids (p.twoYonedaPresheaf hp)).p

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.twoYonedaComparison_isEquivalenceOver
declarations.doc:
The functor `G` is an equivalence in the 2-category of categories fibred in groupoids over
`𝒞`: it admits a quasi-inverse which is again a functor over `𝒞`, and the unit and counit have
all their components lying over identity morphisms of `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
theorem twoYonedaComparison_isEquivalenceOver (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    ∃ (H : 𝒮 ⥤ (presheafOfGroupoids (p.twoYonedaPresheaf hp)).obj)
      (_ : H ⋙ (presheafOfGroupoids (p.twoYonedaPresheaf hp)).p = p)
      (η : p.twoYonedaComparison hp ⋙ H ≅ 𝟭 _)
      (ε : H ⋙ p.twoYonedaComparison hp ≅ 𝟭 _),
      (∀ a, (presheafOfGroupoids (p.twoYonedaPresheaf hp)).p.IsHomLift
          (𝟙 ((presheafOfGroupoids (p.twoYonedaPresheaf hp)).p.obj a)) (η.hom.app a)) ∧
      (∀ z, p.IsHomLift (𝟙 (p.obj z)) (ε.hom.app z))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isSheaf_etale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 076M.** A presheaf of sets on the big fppf category over `S` which is a sheaf for
the chosen étale topology, whose diagonal is representable and which admits a surjective étale
atlas by a scheme is an algebraic space over `S`.

Only the fppf sheaf condition is at issue, and it comes from a comparison with the fppf
quotient sheaf `U/R` of the étale equivalence relation `R = U ×_F U`: the atlas and the
quotient map are both locally surjective for the étale topology and have the same kernel pair,
so `F` and `U/R` are the same coequalizer of `h_R ⇉ h_U` in étale sheaves, and `F` inherits the
fppf sheaf condition from `U/R`. The comparison is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAlgebraicSpace_of_isSheaf_etale_of_isLocallySurjective_quotientMap`;
the étale-local surjectivity of the quotient map is Stacks 02WW.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicSpace_of_isSheaf_etale (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf ((etaleTopology B).over (B.obj hS)) F)
    (hdiag : yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (diag F))
    (hatlas : ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f ∧
      (MorphismProperty.inverseImage (@Etale.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf f) :
    IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comparisonAlgebraicSpaces
declarations.doc:
The comparison map

```
c_φ : a_small⁻¹(g⁻¹ℱ|_{V_étale}) ⟶ f⁻¹ℱ|_{U_étale}
```

of a 2-commutative triangle `φ : a ⋙ g ≅ f` of 1-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids
over `(Sch/S)_{fppf}` whose two source categories `𝒰`, `𝒱` are representable by algebraic spaces
`U`, `V`, for a sheaf `ℱ` on the inherited étale site of `𝒳`.

Here `a_small` is the morphism of small étale topoi attached to the morphism `aSpace : U ⟶ V`
of algebraic spaces corresponding to `a`, and `c_φ` is the adjoint, under
`a_small⁻¹ ⊣ a_{small,*}`, of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comparisonPushforwardHom`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def comparisonAlgebraicSpaces
    (ℱ : Sheaf (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS r .etale) (Type u)) :
    (smallToposMorphismTypeU B S hS aSpace).inverseImage.obj
        (etaleRestrictedInverseImage B S hS q r hq eV g hg ℱ) ⟶
      etaleRestrictedInverseImage B S hS p r hp eU f hf ℱ
declarations.comment: the comparison map of a 2-commutative triangle, on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.comparisonAlgebraicSpacesModules
declarations.doc:
The comparison map

```
c_φ : a_small^*(g^*ℱ|_{V_étale}) ⟶ f^*ℱ|_{U_étale}
```

of a 2-commutative triangle `φ : a ⋙ g ≅ f` of 1-morphisms of categories fibred in groupoids
over `(Sch/S)_{fppf}` whose two source categories `𝒰`, `𝒱` are representable by algebraic
spaces `U`, `V`, for an `𝒪_𝒳`-module `ℱ` on the inherited étale site of `𝒳`.

Here `a_small^*` is the inverse image of modules (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullback`)
for the morphism `aSpace : U ⟶ V` of algebraic spaces corresponding to `a`, and `c_φ` is the
adjoint, under `a_small^* ⊣ a_{small,*}`, of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.moduleComparisonPushforwardHom`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def comparisonAlgebraicSpacesModules
    (ℱ : inheritedEtaleModules B S hS r hr) :
    (modulePullback B S hS aSpace).obj
        (etaleRestrictedModuleInverseImage B S hS q r hq hr eV g hg ℱ) ⟶
      etaleRestrictedModuleInverseImage B S hS p r hp hr eU f hf ℱ
declarations.comment: the comparison map of a 2-commutative triangle, on modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.quotientStackObjectRestrictionMap_injective_and_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 076S.**  Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over `S` whose source
and target are flat and locally of finite presentation, let `𝒳 = [U/R]` be the quotient stack and
`x` the object of `𝒳` over `U` (the canonical projection of Stacks 044R).  Let `ℱ` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_𝒳`-module and `ℋ` any `𝒪_𝒳`-module.  Then the map
`Hom_{𝒪_𝒳}(ℱ, ℋ) ⟶ Hom_{𝒪_U}(x^*ℱ|_{U_étale}, x^*ℋ|_{U_étale})`, `ψ ↦ x^*ψ|_{U_étale}`, is
injective, and its image consists of exactly those `φ` which give rise to a commutative diagram
of modules on `R_étale`: there is a morphism `χ : (x ∘ s)^*ℱ|_{R_étale} ⟶ (x ∘ s)^*ℋ|_{R_étale}`
with `c_s(ℱ) ≫ χ = s_small^*φ ≫ c_s(ℋ)` and `c_t(ℱ) ≫ χ = t_small^*φ ≫ c_t(ℋ)`, where `c_s` and
`c_t` are the comparison maps of equation 076R of the triangles through the source and through
the target, the latter carried by the 2-morphism of Stacks 044S which identifies
`(x ∘ t)^*ℱ|_{R_étale}` with `(x ∘ s)^*ℱ|_{R_étale}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quotientStackObjectRestrictionMap_injective_and_range
    (_hsflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.source.hom) (_htflat : Space.IsFlat C S hS G.target.hom)
    (_hslfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.source.hom)
    (_htlfp : Space.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation C S hS G.target.hom)
    (F : FibredSite.quasicoherentModules.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u} C S hS (quotientStack G).p
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_quotientStack G))
    (H : QuotientStackModules G) :
    Function.Injective (fun ψ : F.obj ⟶ H => quotientStackObjectRestrictionMap G ψ) ∧
      ∀ φ : quotientStackObjectRestriction G F.obj ⟶ quotientStackObjectRestriction G H,
        (∃ ψ : F.obj ⟶ H, quotientStackObjectRestrictionMap G ψ = φ) ↔
          ∃ χ, quotientStackSourceComparison G F.obj ≫ χ =
              (Space.modulePullback C S hS G.source).map φ ≫ quotientStackSourceComparison G H ∧
            quotientStackTargetComparison G F.obj ≫ χ =
              (Space.modulePullback C S hS G.target).map φ ≫ quotientStackTargetComparison G H

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_fppf_of_isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_flatBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 076T.** Let `F` be a presheaf of modules over the structure sheaf of a category
fibred in groupoids over the big fppf category of schemes over `S`. If `F` is locally
quasi-coherent (**Stacks 06WJ**) and the comparison map `c_φ` of **Stacks 06WC** is an
isomorphism for every arrow of `𝒳` lying over a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally of
finite presentation, then `F` is a sheaf for the fppf topology of **Stacks 06TP**.

The sheaf condition is tested, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_of_isSheafFor_flatLfp`, on the families of arrows lying over an
fppf covering of schemes; along such a family hypothesis (b) applies to every member, and the
sheaf condition for it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheafForLiftedFppfFamily_of_isFiberedInGroupoids`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_fppf_of_isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_flatBaseChange
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj)
    (hlqc : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp F)
    (hbc : HasFlatLfpBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS p hp (etaleTopology B)
      (etaleTopology_le_topology B) F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p B.topology) F.presheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_fppf_of_isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_isLocallyBijective_flatLfp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 076T**, with the pullback of sheaves of Stacks 06WC. Let `F` be a presheaf of
modules over the structure sheaf of a category fibred in groupoids over `(Sch/S)_{fppf}`. If `F`
is locally quasi-coherent (Stacks 06WJ) and the comparison map
`c_φ : f_{small}^*(F|_{V_ét}) ⟶ F|_{U_ét}` is an isomorphism of sheaves (it is locally injective
and locally surjective for the étale topology of the small site of `U`) for every arrow `φ` of
`𝒳` lying over a morphism of schemes which is flat and locally of finite presentation, then `F`
is a sheaf for the fppf topology of Stacks 06TP.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_fppf_of_isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_isLocallyBijective_flatLfp
    (hlqc : IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS p hp F)
    (hbc : ∀ {x y : 𝒳} (φ : x ⟶ y), Flat (B.inclusion.map (p.map φ).left) →
      LocallyOfFinitePresentation (B.inclusion.map (p.map φ).left) →
        IsLocallyBijectiveRestrictModulePullbackComparisonUnivLE B E h S hS p hp
          (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B) φ F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p B.topology) F.presheaf
declarations.comment: with the pullback of sheaves of Stacks 06WC in hypothesis (b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isAlgebraicStack_of_isStackInGroupoids_etale_of_smoothAtlas
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 076V.** Let `S` be a scheme of a big fppf site and let `𝒳` be a category over the
common underlying category of the big fppf and big étale sites of `S` such that

1. `𝒳` is a stack in groupoids for the étale topology,
2. the diagonal `Δ : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳 × 𝒳` is representable by algebraic spaces, and
3. there are a scheme `U` over `S` and a 1-morphism `(Sch/U) ⟶ 𝒳` which is representable by
   algebraic spaces, surjective and smooth.

Then `𝒳` is an algebraic stack over `S` in the sense of Stacks 026O.

Conditions (2) and (3) are stated exactly as the corresponding clauses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsAlgebraicStack`, which, as the source's proof notes, are independent of
the topology; condition (1) is Stacks 02ZI for the étale topology localised at `S`, at the index
universe of the families of the site. The fppf stack clause is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isStack_of_isStack_etale_of_smoothAtlas`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAlgebraicStack_of_isStackInGroupoids_etale_of_smoothAtlas
    (𝒳 : BasedCategory.{u, u + 1} (BigFppfOver B S hS))
    (hstack : 𝒳.p.IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1} ((etaleTopology B).over (B.obj hS)))
    (hdiag : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS
      (diagonalBasedFunctor B S hS (CatFiberedInGroupoids.mk 𝒳 hstack.isFiberedInGroupoids)))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (f : (schemeFibredCategory B S hS U).val ⥤ᵇ 𝒳)
    (hfrep : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces B S hS f)
    (hfprop : ∀ (V : BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (y : BigFppfOver B V.left.1 V.left.2 ⥤ 𝒳.obj)
        (_hy : y ⋙ 𝒳.p = Over.map V.hom)
        (F : (BigFppfOver B V.left.1 V.left.2)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
        (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B V.left.1 V.left.2 F),
        Nonempty (StacksRepresentableCFG.EquivalenceOver
          (TwoFibreProductOver.fst (Over.map V.hom)
            (schemeFibredCategory B S hS U).val.p 𝒳.p y f.toFunctor)
          (presheafOfCategories (F ⋙ typeToCat)).p) →
        (let g := (algebraicSpaceMap B S hS V
          ((spacesOverSmallerBaseFunctor B V.left.1 S V.left.2 hS V.hom).obj ⟨F, hF⟩)).hom
         Space.IsSurjective B S hS g ∧ Space.IsSmooth B S hS g)) :
    IsAlgebraicStack.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: the criterion, with hypotheses (2) and (3) in the topology-independent form of the corresponding clauses of Stacks 026O

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.exactFunctor_quasicoherentPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 076X.** If `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is a flat morphism of algebraic stacks, then
`f^* : QCoh(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is an exact functor: it preserves finite colimits, as it does for
every `f`, and finite limits, because kernels of quasi-coherent modules are computed on flat
objects (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentKernelsOnFlatObjects`) and `f`
carries flat objects to flat objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem exactFunctor_quasicoherentPullback (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f) :
    exactFunctor (quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒴) (quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳)
      (quasicoherentPullback B S hS f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.preservesFiniteColimits_quasicoherentPullback
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of quasi-coherent modules along a 1-morphism of categories fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf category of `S`, `f^* : QCoh(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)`, is right exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteColimits_quasicoherentPullback :
    PreservesFiniteColimits (quasicoherentPullback B S hS p q hp hq f hF)
declarations.comment: right exactness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smoothLocalHigherDirectImageCriterion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 076Z.** Let `M` be a rule assigning to a category fibred in groupoids over `S` a
predicate on the modules on its étale site. If `M` cuts out a weak Serre subcategory everywhere,
is stable under inverse image along a smooth 1-morphism, is local for every jointly surjective
family of smooth 1-morphisms indexed in `Type (max u s)`, and is preserved by the higher direct
images between algebraic stacks representable by affine schemes, then the higher direct images
carry the rule into the rule along every quasi-compact (**Stacks 050U**) quasi-separated
(**Stacks 04YW**) 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, in every degree.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smoothLocalHigherDirectImageCriterion_unconditional`.
Hypothesis (3) is the source's, read for the families indexed in `Type (max u s)`: the source asks
it of every jointly surjective family whatever its index set, so its hypothesis implies this one
and this statement implies the source's.
declarations.statement: alias smoothLocalHigherDirectImageCriterion
declarations.comment: the whole statement: every rule satisfying the source's four hypotheses, every quasi-compact quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and every degree; hypothesis (3) is read for the families indexed in a universe containing u, which the source's hypothesis implies, so the statement is no weaker than the source's

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smoothLocalHigherDirectImageCriterion_unconditional
declarations.doc:
Let `M` be a rule on the modules on the étale sites of the algebraic stacks over `S` such that
(1) it cuts out a weak Serre subcategory on every algebraic stack, (2) it is preserved by inverse
image along every smooth 1-morphism, (3) membership in it is local for every jointly surjective
family of smooth 1-morphisms indexed in `Type (max u s)`, and (4) the higher direct images along
every 1-morphism between algebraic stacks representable by affine schemes carry it into itself.
Then the higher direct images along every quasi-compact quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks carry `M` into `M`, in every degree.

Hypothesis (3) is the source's, read for the families indexed in `Type (max u s)`: the source asks
it of every jointly surjective family whatever its index set, so its hypothesis implies this one
and this statement implies the source's (see the module documentation).
declarations.statement:
theorem smoothLocalHigherDirectImageCriterion_unconditional :
    SmoothLocalHigherDirectImageCriterion.{u, t, max u s} B S hS
declarations.comment: the whole statement: every rule satisfying the source's four hypotheses, every quasi-compact quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and every degree; hypothesis (3) is read for the families indexed in a universe containing u, which the source's hypothesis implies, so the statement is no weaker than the source's

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.higherDirectImage_mem_of_quasiCompact_quasiSeparated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0770.** Let `M` be a rule which associates to every algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` a
subcategory `M_𝒳` of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, the modules on the fppf site of `𝒳`, such that

1. `M_𝒳` is a weak Serre subcategory of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` for every algebraic stack `𝒳`;
2. for a smooth 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` the inverse image `f^*` maps `M_𝒴` into `M_𝒳`;
3. `M` is smooth-local on the target; and
4. for a 1-morphism of stacks representable by affine schemes, `Rⁱf_*` maps `M` into `M`.

Then for every quasi-compact and quasi-separated 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks and
every `F` in `M_𝒳`, the higher direct image `Rⁱf_* F`, computed in the fppf topology, lies in
`M_𝒴`.

The proof is the source's: the first move
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.higherDirectImagesMapInto_of_smoothAffineCover`)
transports the question along a smooth presentation of `𝒴` by affine-representable stacks, using
clauses (1), (2), (3) and the base-change isomorphisms; the second
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.higherDirectImagesMapInto_of_abutsTo`) settles each
base-changed 1-morphism, whose target is affine-representable and which is again quasi-compact
and quasi-separated, from clauses (1), (2), (4) and the Čech spectral sequence.

Two prerequisites beyond the four clauses are hypothesised, `hpres` and `hcech`: the base-change
isomorphisms of **Stacks 075H** and the Čech spectral sequence of **Stacks 072G** part (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem higherDirectImage_mem_of_quasiCompact_quasiSeparated (M : ModuleRule.{u, w} B S hS)
    (hSerre : ∀ 𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS, (M 𝒳).IsWeakSerreClass)
    (hSmooth : IsSmoothPullbackStable B S hS M) (hLocal : IsSmoothLocal B S hS M)
    (hAffine : AffineHigherDirectImagesMapInto B S hS M)
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqc : Stack.IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f)
    (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (hpres : HasSmoothAffineBaseChange B S hS f)
    (hcech : ∀ {𝒳' 𝒴' : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} (f' : 𝒳' ⟶ 𝒴'),
      Stack.IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f' →
      AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f' → IsAffineRepresentable B S hS 𝒴' →
      HasFppfCechPresentation B S hS f')
    (i : ℕ) (F : fppfModules B S hS 𝒳) (hF : M 𝒳 F) :
    M 𝒴 ((fppfHigherDirectImage B S hS f i).obj F)
declarations.comment:
the reduction of the quasi-compact quasi-separated case to the affine case,
  which is the source's own clause (4), from clauses (1) to (4) together with two hypothesised
  prerequisites, the base-change isomorphisms of Stacks 075H and the fppf relative Cech
  pushforward spectral sequence of Stacks 072G part (2)(b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.StackModuleRule.preservesHigherDirectImages_fppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0770.** Let `M` be a rule which associates to every algebraic stack `𝒳` over `S` a
property `M_𝒳` of the sheaves of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on the fppf site of `𝒳` such that

1. `M_𝒳` is a weak Serre subcategory of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` for all algebraic stacks `𝒳`;
2. for a smooth 1-morphism `f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳` the inverse image `f^*` maps `M_𝒳` into `M_𝒵`;
3. if `fᵢ : 𝒳ᵢ ⟶ 𝒳` is a family of smooth 1-morphisms with `|𝒳| = ⋃ᵢ |fᵢ|(|𝒳ᵢ|)`, then a module
   `ℱ` lies in `M_𝒳` if and only if every `fᵢ^*ℱ` lies in `M_{𝒳ᵢ}`; and
4. if `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` is a 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and `𝒳` and `𝒴` are representable by
   affine schemes, then `Rⁱf_*` maps `M_𝒳` into `M_𝒴`.

Then for every quasi-compact and quasi-separated 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks,
`Rⁱf_*` maps `M_𝒳` into `M_𝒴` in every degree, the higher direct images being computed in the
fppf topology.

Clause (1) is read as "`M_𝒳` is a weak Serre subcategory": the source prints "`𝒪_𝒳` is a weak
Serre subcategory", a typo, as the identical clause (1) of **Stacks 076Z** shows. Clause (3) is
asked only for families indexed by a type in the universe of the schemes, which makes the
hypothesis weaker and the theorem stronger. "Representable by an affine scheme" in clause (4) is
equivalence over the site with the big site of an affine scheme
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.IsAffineRepresentable`). Modules have sections in the
universe of the schemes, and the higher direct images are the right derived functors of the
direct image right adjoint to the inverse image.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesHigherDirectImages_fppf (M : StackModuleRule.{u, t} B S hS .fppf)
    (h1 : IsWeakSerre .fppf M) (h2 : IsStableUnderSmoothPullback .fppf M)
    (h3 : IsSmoothLocal.{u, t, u} .fppf M)
    (h4 : PreservesHigherDirectImagesOfAffine (stackModuleDirectImageData.{u, t} B S hS .fppf) M) :
    PreservesHigherDirectImages (stackModuleDirectImageData.{u, t} B S hS .fppf) M
declarations.comment: the whole statement: every rule satisfying (1)-(4), every quasi-compact quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and every degree, higher direct images in the fppf topology; (1) read as M_X weak Serre (the source's O_X is a typo), (3) asked for families indexed by Type u only

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_fppf_of_isLocallyQuasicoherentWithSheafFlatBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (1).** A presheaf of modules over the structure sheaf of a category
fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site which lies in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` — locally
quasi-coherent (**Stacks 06WJ**) with the flat base change property of **Stacks 0762** — is a
sheaf for the fppf topology of **Stacks 06TP**.

This is **Stacks 076T**,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_fppf_of_isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_sheafFlatLfpBaseChange`, whose
hypothesis (b) asks the flat base change property of fewer arrows. The module sections are in the
universe of the schemes; the statement holds for every category fibred in groupoids, which
generalizes the source's algebraic stack.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_fppf_of_isLocallyQuasicoherentWithSheafFlatBaseChange
    (hF : IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithSheafFlatBaseChange B E h S hS p hp F) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS p B.topology) F.presheaf
declarations.comment: part (1): a member of LQCoh^fbc (with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves) is a sheaf for the fppf topology; for every category fibred in groupoids

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fppfModuleOfLqcohSheafFbc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (1)**, the clause "it is an object of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`": a member of
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) ⊆ Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)` on an algebraic stack is a module on the fppf site, with the
same underlying presheaf of modules, and it lies in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) ⊆ Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fppfModuleOfLqcohSheafFbc (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
    (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)))
    (hG : lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 G) :
    (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: part (1), the clause `i.e. it is an object of Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`: a member of LQCoh^fbc on the étale site of an algebraic stack, as an object of LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) ⊆ Mod(𝒪_𝒳) with the same underlying presheaf of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_fppfModulesHigherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (4)(b)**, in `Mod(𝒪_𝒴)`. Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and `F` an object of `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`. Then each
higher direct image `Rⁱf_*F`, computed in the fppf topology, is an object of `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴)`.

Modules have sections in the universe `u` of the schemes; local quasi-coherence is read against
an auxiliary big étale site `E` with `E.cutoff = B.cutoff`, and the flat base change property is
the sheaf-level one of **Stacks 0762**.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_fppfModulesHigherDirectImage
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (F : StackModules B S hS .fppf 𝒳) (hF : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, t, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F)
    (i : ℕ) :
    lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, t, u} B E h S hS 𝒴
      ((fppfModulesHigherDirectImage B S hS f i).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (4)(b), in Mod(𝒪_𝒴): for f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, each R^i f_*F computed in the fppf topology lies in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴), with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; modules at the module universe u of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_etaleComparison_fppfModulesHigherDirectImage_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (4)(a)**, for the higher direct images. Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and `F` an object of
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`. Then `Rⁱf_*F` is the same whether computed in the étale or in the fppf
topology: `ε_*(Rⁱf_{fppf,*}F) ≅ Rⁱf_{ét,*}(ε_*F)`, where `ε_*` reads an fppf module on the étale
site.

Modules have sections in the universe `u` of the schemes. The assertion of the source about the
total direct image `Rf_*` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcTotalDirectImageIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_etaleComparison_fppfModulesHigherDirectImage_iso
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (F : StackModules B S hS .fppf 𝒳) (hF : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, t, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F)
    (i : ℕ) :
    Nonempty ((stackModulesEtaleComparison B S hS 𝒴).obj
        ((fppfModulesHigherDirectImage B S hS f i).obj F) ≅
      (stackModuleHigherDirectImage B S hS f .etale i).obj
        ((stackModulesEtaleComparison B S hS 𝒳).obj F))
declarations.comment: part (4)(a), for the higher direct images: ε_*(R^i f_{fppf,*}F) ≅ R^i f_{ét,*}(ε_*F) for f quasi-compact and quasi-separated and F in LQCoh^fbc, modules at the module universe u of the schemes; the total direct image Rf_* is lqcohSheafFbcTotalDirectImageIso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcModuleRule_stackModuleHigherDirectImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (4)(b), in the étale topology.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated 1-morphism of algebraic stacks and `F` an object of `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`, a module on
`𝒳_étale` which is locally quasi-coherent with the flat base change property. Then each higher
direct image `Rⁱf_*F`, computed in the étale topology, is an object of `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴)`.

Modules have sections in the universe `u` of the schemes, local quasi-coherence is read against an
auxiliary big étale site `E` with `E.cutoff = B.cutoff`, and the flat base change property is the
sheaf-level one of **Stacks 0762** (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.HasSheafFlatBaseChangeProperty`).
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcModuleRule_stackModuleHigherDirectImage
    {𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, t} B S hS} (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f) (hqs : AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f)
    (F : StackModules B S hS .etale 𝒳)
    (hF : IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithSheafFlatBaseChange B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids F.val) (i : ℕ) :
    IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithSheafFlatBaseChange B E h S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
      𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids ((stackModuleHigherDirectImage B S hS f .etale i).obj F).val
declarations.comment: part (4)(b), étale topology: for f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, each R^i f_*F computed in the étale topology lies in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴), with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; modules at the module universe u of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules_stackModuleInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (3)**, on `Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)`: the inverse image along a 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks of the étale sites carries `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴)` into `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules_stackModuleInverseImage (F : StackModules B S hS .etale 𝒴)
    (hF : lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒴 F) :
    lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳
      ((stackModuleInverseImage B S hS .etale f).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (3), on Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳): f^* carries LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴) into LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) for every 1-morphism f of algebraic stacks, with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; the module sections in the universe of the schemes. The induced functor is lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModulesPullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_fppfModulesPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (3)**, on `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`: the inverse image along a 1-morphism of algebraic
stacks of the fppf sites carries `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴)` into `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_fppfModulesPullback (F : fppfModules B S hS 𝒴)
    (hF : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒴 F) :
    lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 ((fppfModulesPullback B S hS f).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (3), on Mod(𝒪_𝒳): f^* carries LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒴) into LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) for every 1-morphism f of algebraic stacks, with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; the module sections in the universe of the schemes. The induced functor is lqcohSheafFbcFppfModulesPullback

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcTotalDirectImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (4)(a), for the total direct image.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of
algebraic stacks and `F` an object of `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) ⊆ Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`. The total direct image of `F`
computed in the étale topology is the one computed in the fppf topology, read on the étale site:
`Rf_{ét,*}(ε_*F) ≅ Rε_*(Rf_{fppf,*}F)` in `D⁺(Mod(𝒴_ét, 𝒪_𝒴))`.

Here `ε_* : Mod(𝒪_𝒴) ⥤ Mod(𝒴_ét, 𝒪_𝒴)` is only left exact, so the fppf result is compared through
its right derived functor `Rε_*`. The isomorphism is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.totalDirectImageEtaleComparisonIso` together with `Rε_*F ≅ ε_*F`, which
is **Stacks 075R** (1),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isZero_rightDerived_etaleComparisonPushforward_of_lqcohSheafFbc`.
No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of `f` is needed for this form. When `f` is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, part (4)(b) and **Stacks 075R** (1) make the cohomology
sheaves `Rⁱf_{fppf,*}F` of `Rf_{fppf,*}F` themselves `ε_*`-acyclic, so that `Rε_*` there is
`ε_*` applied to the cohomology sheaves: that is the form of part (4)(a) for the higher direct
images, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_etaleComparison_fppfModulesHigherDirectImage_iso`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.nonempty_homology_etaleComparison_totalDirectImage_iso` below.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lqcohSheafFbcTotalDirectImageIso (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (F : StackModules B S hS .fppf 𝒳)
    (hF : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, t, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F) :
    (stackModuleDirectImage B S hS f .etale).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
          ((stackModulesEtaleComparison B S hS 𝒳).obj F)) ≅
      (stackModulesEtaleComparison B S hS 𝒴).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
        ((stackModuleDirectImage B S hS f .fppf).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))
declarations.comment: part (4)(a), total direct image Rf_*: Rf_{ét,*}(ε_*F) ≅ Rε_*(Rf_{fppf,*}F) in D⁺(𝒴_ét), for F in LQCoh^fbc (flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves) and every 1-morphism f, so the source's quasi-compact and quasi-separated f is a special case; modules at the module universe u of the schemes. The higher direct images R^i f_* are nonempty_etaleComparison_fppfModulesHigherDirectImage_iso

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbc_hasColimits_and_agree
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (5).**  The category `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` has colimits, and they agree with
colimits in `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)` as well as in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`.

In order: `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`, read inside `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`, has small colimits and its inclusion
preserves them; read inside `Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)` the same holds; and restricting a colimit
cocone in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` of objects of `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` to the étale site gives a colimit cocone in
`Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳)`, so the two readings compute the same colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbc_hasColimits_and_agree :
    HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).FullSubcategory ∧
      PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).ι ∧
      (HasColimitsOfSize.{u, u}
          (lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).FullSubcategory ∧
        PreservesColimitsOfSize.{u, u} (lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).ι) ∧
      ∀ {K : Type u} [Category.{u} K] {D : K ⥤ fppfModules B S hS 𝒳},
        (∀ k, lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 (D.obj k)) →
          ∀ {c : Cocone D}, IsColimit c →
            Nonempty (IsColimit ((fppfToEtaleModules B S hS 𝒳).mapCocone c))
declarations.comment: part (5): LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) has u-small colimits, preserved by its inclusions into Mod(𝒪_𝒳) and into Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳), and a colimit in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) of members restricts to a colimit in Mod(𝒳_étale, 𝒪_𝒳); flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_fppfInternalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (7).** For `F` an `𝒪_𝒳`-module of finite presentation and `G` in
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` on an algebraic stack, the internal Hom `SheafHom_{𝒪_𝒳}(F, G)` of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`
is in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.

`G` is cartesian along the flat arrows between objects over affine schemes (step R2 of
Stacks 0779), hence so is `SheafHom_{𝒪_𝒳}(F, G)`, `F` being of finite presentation; a module
cartesian along those arrows is locally quasi-coherent and has the flat base change property.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_fppfInternalHom (F G : fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    [F.IsFinitePresentationOnSite]
    (hG : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 G) :
    lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳
      (AlgebraicStacks.fppfInternalHom B S hS 𝒳 F G)
declarations.comment: part (7): SheafHom(F, G) of Mod(𝒪_𝒳) lies in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) for F of finite presentation in Mod(𝒪_𝒳) and G in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳), with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; modules at the module universe u of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_sheafTensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (6).** For `F` and `G` in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` on an algebraic stack, the
tensor product `F ⊗_{𝒪_𝒳} G` computed in `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` is again in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.

Both factors are cartesian along the flat arrows between objects over affine schemes (step R2 of
Stacks 0779), hence so is their tensor product, whose sections over an affine object are the tensor
product of the sections; a module cartesian along those arrows is locally quasi-coherent and has
the flat base change property.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_sheafTensor (F G : fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (hF : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F)
    (hG : lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 G) :
    lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳
      (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
        (FlatFppf.fppfRingedTopos B S hS 𝒳).O).obj
        F).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (6): F ⊗_{𝒪_𝒳} G of Mod(𝒪_𝒳) lies in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) for F and G in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳), with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; modules at the module universe u of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isWeakSerreClass_lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (2), the étale half: `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` is a weak Serre subcategory of
`Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳)`**, for an algebraic stack `𝒳`, at module universe `u`, with the abelian
structure coming from the sheafification of abelian presheaves on the associated étale site
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.hasSheafify_etaleAssociatedTopology`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakSerreClass_lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules (𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS) :
    letI := hasSheafify_etaleAssociatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
    letI := wEqualsLocallyBijective_etaleAssociatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
    (lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).IsWeakSerreClass
declarations.comment: part (2), the étale half: LQCoh^fbc is a weak Serre subcategory of Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳), with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; modules at the module universe u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isWeakSerreClass_lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0771, part (2), the fppf half: `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)` is a weak Serre subcategory of
`Mod(𝒪_𝒳)`**, for an algebraic stack `𝒳`, at module universe `u`, with the abelian structure
coming from the sheafification of abelian presheaves on the fppf site
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.hasSheafify_fppf_addCommGrpCat`): it contains `0` and is
closed under isomorphisms, kernels, cokernels and extensions (**Stacks 0754**).
declarations.statement:
instance isWeakSerreClass_lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules :
    (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).IsWeakSerreClass
declarations.comment: part (2), fppf half: LQCoh^fbc is a weak Serre subcategory of Mod(𝒪_𝒳), with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; modules at the module universe u

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsParasitic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0773.** A presheaf of modules over the structure sheaf of one of the sites
associated with an algebraic stack `𝒳` is *parasitic* when its module of sections at every flat
object of `𝒳` vanishes — an object being flat, as in **Stacks 0787**, when the 1-morphism it
names out of the scheme it lies over is flat.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsParasitic
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{t}
      (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
        𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids τ).obj) : Prop
declarations.comment: parasitic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_of_isFlat_isLfp_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0774** (4). Let `f j : 𝒳 j ⟶ 𝒴` be a jointly surjective family of flat, locally
finitely presented 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`, and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of
`𝒪_𝒴`-modules on the fppf site of `𝒴`. If every inverse image `(f j)^*ℱ` is parasitic, then `ℱ`
is parasitic.

At a flat object `y` of `𝒴` the covering of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fppfCovering_family_flatObject_lift` supplies an fppf covering
family of `y` by objects `f (a i)(x_i)` with `x_i` a *flat* object of `𝒳 (a i)`; the sections of
`ℱ` there are the sections of `(f (a i))^*ℱ` at `x_i`, which vanish, and a sheaf is
separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isParasitic_of_isFlat_isLfp_jointlySurjective {J : Type v}
    {𝒳 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒳 j ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hflat : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (f j))
    (hlfp : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒴)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : SheafOfModules.{t}
      (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
        𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids SiteKind.fppf))
    (hF : ∀ j, IsParasitic B S hS (𝒳 j) SiteKind.fppf
      ((modulePresheafPullbackOfHom.{u, w, t} B S hS (f j) SiteKind.fppf).obj F.val)) :
    IsParasitic B S hS 𝒴 SiteKind.fppf F.val
declarations.comment:
part (4): an fppf sheaf of modules whose inverse images along a jointly surjective
family of flat, locally finitely presented 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks are all parasitic is
parasitic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_modulePresheafPullbackOfHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0774** (1). If `F` is a parasitic presheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules and `g : 𝒴 ⟶ 𝒳` is a
flat 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, then the inverse image `g^*F` is a parasitic presheaf of
`𝒪_𝒴`-modules.

Let `y` be an object of `𝒴` lying over a scheme `V` for which `y : V → 𝒴` is flat. Then
`g y : V → 𝒴 → 𝒳` is flat, being a composite of flat 1-morphisms (**Stacks 06PX**), so `F`
vanishes at `g y` by hypothesis. The sections of `g^*F` at `y` are the sections of `F` at
`g y`, whence the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isParasitic_modulePresheafPullbackOfHom
    (hg : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS g)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{t}
      (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
        𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids τ).obj)
    (hF : IsParasitic B S hS 𝒳 τ F) :
    IsParasitic B S hS 𝒴 τ
      ((modulePresheafPullbackOfHom.{u, w, t} B S hS g τ).obj F)
declarations.comment:
part (1): the inverse image of a parasitic presheaf of modules along a flat
1-morphism of algebraic stacks is parasitic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0774** (2)(b), the closure under submodules. A submodule of a parasitic module on
one of the sites associated with an algebraic stack is parasitic.

It is immediate from the definition, as the source says: a monomorphism of sheaves of modules is
injective on sections, so at a flat object the sections of the submodule inject into the
vanishing sections of the ambient module.
declarations.comment:
part (2)(b), the closure under submodules: a submodule of a parasitic module is
parasitic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_X₂_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0774** (2)(b), the closure under extensions. Given a short exact sequence
`0 → F₁ → F₂ → F₃ → 0` of modules on one of the sites associated with an algebraic stack, with
`F₁` and `F₃` parasitic, the module `F₂` is parasitic.

This is the source's "evaluate on `x` lying over a scheme flat over `𝒳`": at a flat object the
sections of `F₁` and of `F₃` vanish, and taking sections is left exact, so the sections of `F₂`
vanish too.
declarations.statement:
theorem isParasitic_X₂_of_shortExact
    {Sq : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{t}
      (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
        𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids τ))}
    (hSq : Sq.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : IsParasitic B S hS 𝒳 τ Sq.X₁.val) (h₃ : IsParasitic B S hS 𝒳 τ Sq.X₃.val) :
    IsParasitic B S hS 𝒳 τ Sq.X₂.val
declarations.comment:
part (2)(b), the closure under extensions: the middle term of a short exact
sequence of modules whose outer terms are parasitic is parasitic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_of_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0774** (2)(b), the closure under quotients. If `p : F ⟶ G` is an epimorphism of
modules on one of the sites associated with an algebraic stack and `F` is parasitic, then `G` is
parasitic.

An epimorphism of sheaves of modules is locally surjective, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_of_isLocallySurjective`: at a flat object every section of
`G` comes from a section of `F` on a covering, and that covering may be refined by one whose
sources are again flat objects, where `F` vanishes.
declarations.comment:
part (2)(b), the closure under quotients: a quotient of a parasitic module is
parasitic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSerreClass_parasiticModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0774** (2)(b). The full subcategory of `Mod(𝒳_τ, 𝒪_𝒳)` consisting of the parasitic
modules is a Serre subcategory: it contains a zero object and is closed under submodules, under
quotients and under extensions, which are the four instances above.
declarations.statement:
instance isSerreClass_parasiticModules :
    (parasiticModules.{u, w, t} B S hS 𝒳 τ).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: part (2)(b): the parasitic modules are a Serre subcategory of Mod(𝒳_τ, 𝒪_𝒳)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_sheafification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0774** (2)(a). The `τ`-sheafification of a parasitic presheaf of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules is parasitic, for each of the five topologies `τ` of **Stacks 06TP**.

The map from a presheaf of modules to its sheafification is locally surjective, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_of_isLocallySurjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isParasitic_sheafification
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{t}
      (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
        𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids τ).obj)
    (hF : IsParasitic B S hS 𝒳 τ F) :
    IsParasitic B S hS 𝒳 τ
      ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification.{t}
        (𝟙 (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
          𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids τ).obj)).obj F).val
declarations.comment:
part (2)(a): the τ-sheafification of a parasitic presheaf of modules is
parasitic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0774** (3). Let `f j : 𝒳 j ⟶ 𝒴` be a jointly surjective family of smooth
1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S`, and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒴`-modules on the étale
site of `𝒴`. If every inverse image `(f j)^*ℱ` is parasitic, then `ℱ` is parasitic.

At a flat object `y` of `𝒴`, every point of the scheme `y` lies over is hit by a smooth morphism
`m` of the site carrying a lift of `y` to some `𝒳 j` which is a *flat* object there
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_flatObject_lift_of_isSmooth_at_point`), so the sections of `ℱ`
restrict to zero along the comparison morphism. Refining `m` by an étale morphism factoring
through it (**Stacks 055U**) and taking a cartesian lift of the comparison morphism gives an
*étale* covering family of `y` along every member of which the sections of `ℱ` restrict to zero;
`ℱ` is an étale sheaf, hence separated, so they vanish.
declarations.statement:
theorem isParasitic_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective {J : Type v}
    {𝒳 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒳 j ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hsmooth : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒴)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : SheafOfModules.{t}
      (FibredSite.ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p
        𝒴.val.isFiberedInGroupoids SiteKind.etale))
    (hF : ∀ j, IsParasitic B S hS (𝒳 j) SiteKind.etale
      ((modulePresheafPullbackOfHom.{u, w, t} B S hS (f j) SiteKind.etale).obj F.val)) :
    IsParasitic B S hS 𝒴 SiteKind.etale F.val
declarations.comment:
part (3): an étale sheaf of modules whose inverse images along a jointly surjective
family of smooth 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks are all parasitic is parasitic

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isZero_fppfModuleCohomology_of_isParasitic_atSchemeUniverse
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0775** part (1), for the fppf topology, at the module universe `u` of the schemes.
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and `ℱ` a parasitic sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules (**Stacks 0773**).
Then `H^i(𝒳, ℱ) = 0` for every `i`, where `H^i(𝒳, -)` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.fppfModuleCohomology`, `Ext^i` out of the structure sheaf, in
any universe `t` of `Ext`-groups.
