declarations.doc:
The Grothendieck topology of the lisse-étale site: the one generated by the inherited étale
covering families between smooth objects.
declarations.statement: abbrev topology : GrothendieckTopology (LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: the lisse-etale site: its Grothendieck topology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smoothObject_schemeStack_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0787.** An object of the algebraic stack of a scheme `U` over `S` — that is, a scheme
`x` over `U` in the big fppf category — is a *smooth object* exactly when the morphism of schemes
underlying its structure morphism is smooth.
declarations.statement:
theorem smoothObject_schemeStack_iff (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (x : Over U) :
    smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS U) x ↔
      Smooth ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map x.hom)
declarations.comment: lisse_etale_site: smooth objects of the stack of a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isContinuous_inclusion'
declarations.doc:
**Continuity of the inclusion of the flat-fppf site (Stacks 0788 (2)).** This is the fppf case
of Stacks 07AK, whose closure hypothesis is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.closedUnderFlatMorphisms`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_inclusion' :
    (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.IsContinuous (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
declarations.comment: the inclusion of the flat-fppf site is continuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isCocontinuous_inclusion'
declarations.doc: **Cocontinuity of the inclusion of the flat-fppf site (Stacks 0788 (2)).**
declarations.statement:
theorem isCocontinuous_inclusion' :
    (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.IsCocontinuous (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
declarations.comment: the inclusion of the flat-fppf site is cocontinuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isContinuous_inclusion_topology
declarations.doc:
**Continuity of the inclusion of the flat-fppf site, for the chosen-family topology
(Stacks 0788 (2)).** The same assertion at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.topology` rather than at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.inclusionTopology`.

Continuity passes from a topology to any smaller one, because a sheaf for the larger topology is a
sheaf for the smaller, so this follows from
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isContinuous_inclusion'` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.topology_le_inclusionTopology`. Cocontinuity does *not* pass in
that direction, which is why the two are recorded differently here.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_inclusion_topology :
    (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.IsContinuous (topology B S hS 𝒳)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
declarations.comment: continuity of the inclusion, read at the topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isCocontinuous_inclusion_topology
declarations.doc:
**Cocontinuity of the inclusion of the flat-fppf site, for the chosen-family topology
(Stacks 0788 (2)).** The same assertion at `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.topology` rather than
at `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.inclusionTopology`.

Unlike continuity, cocontinuity does not transfer from a topology to a smaller one, so this needs
the equality `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.inclusionTopology_eq_topology` and not merely
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.topology_le_inclusionTopology`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCocontinuous_inclusion_topology :
    (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.IsCocontinuous (topology B S hS 𝒳)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
declarations.comment: cocontinuity of the inclusion, read at the topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.toposMorphism
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of topoi `g` of Stacks 0788 (2)(a)**:
`g : Sh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_{fppf})`, with inverse image restriction along the inclusion of
the flat objects, pushforward its cocontinuous right adjoint, and left exactness of the inverse
image automatic.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toposMorphism :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi induced by the inclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.toposMorphismTopology
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of topoi `g` of Stacks 0788 (2)(a), for the chosen-family topology**: the same
morphism of topoi as `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.toposMorphism`, transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.inclusionTopology_eq_topology`, so that its source is the topos
of sheaves for `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.topology`. No second construction is involved:
the two topologies are equal, and this is the one morphism of topoi read at the other
description.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toposMorphismTopology :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (topology B S hS 𝒳) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: that morphism of topoi, read at the topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.setsShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788 (2)(b).** The inverse image of the morphism of topoi `g` of Stacks 0788 (2)(a)
has a left adjoint on sheaves of sets, namely `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.setsShriek`.

This is `CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafAdjunctionLowerShriek` (**Stacks 00XR** (2)) at the inclusion
of the flat objects, whose continuity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isContinuous_inclusion_topology`. The right-hand side is the
inverse image of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.toposMorphismTopology`, restriction along the
inclusion.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev setsShriekAdjunction :
    setsShriek B S hS 𝒳 ⊣
      (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (topology B S hS 𝒳) (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
declarations.comment: the lower-shriek adjunction on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_setsShriekAdjunction_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788 (2)(c), the half about `g_!`.** The canonical map `F ⟶ g⁻¹g_!F` on sheaves of
sets — the unit of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.setsShriekAdjunction` — is an isomorphism.

This is **Stacks 00XT** for a fully faithful, continuous and cocontinuous functor of sites, all
three of which hold for the inclusion of the flat objects at this topology.
declarations.statement: instance isIso_setsShriekAdjunction_unit : IsIso (setsShriekAdjunction B S hS 𝒳).unit
declarations.comment: the unit of the sets lower-shriek adjunction is invertible

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.abelianShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788 (2)(d).** Restriction of abelian sheaves along the inclusion of the flat
objects has a left adjoint, namely `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.abelianShriek`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev abelianShriekAdjunction :
    abelianShriek.{u, w, v} B S hS 𝒳 ⊣
      (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.sheafPushforwardContinuous Ab.{max u v}
        (topology B S hS 𝒳) (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
declarations.comment: the lower-shriek adjunction on abelian sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_abelianShriekAdjunction_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788 (2)(e)**: the canonical map `F ⟶ g⁻¹g_!F` on abelian sheaves — the unit of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.abelianShriekAdjunction` — is an isomorphism. This is
**Stacks 00XT** again, now at abelian coefficients.
declarations.statement:
instance isIso_abelianShriekAdjunction_unit :
    IsIso (abelianShriekAdjunction.{u, w, v} B S hS 𝒳).unit
declarations.comment: the unit of the abelian lower-shriek adjunction is invertible

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788**, `flat_ringed`. The structure sheaf of the flat-fppf site of an algebraic
stack: the restriction, along the inclusion of the flat objects, of the structure sheaf of its
fppf site. The rings of sections are unchanged — they are those of the fppf structure sheaf at
the flat objects.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def structureSheaf : Sheaf (topology B S hS 𝒳) CommRingCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the structure sheaf of the flat-fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.structureSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788**, `flat_ringed`: `g⁻¹𝒪_𝒳 ≅ 𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}}`. The inverse image of the fppf
structure sheaf along the morphism of topoi of **Stacks 0788** (2)(a) is the structure sheaf of
the flat-fppf site.

The inverse image of `g` on sheaves of sets *is* restriction along the inclusion of the flat
objects, so this is the comparison of the transported commutative ring operations with those of
the restricted sheaf, and that comparison is the identity on sections
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.structureSheafIso_apply`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureSheafIso :
    (inverseImageCommRingFunctor (toposMorphismOnRings B S hS 𝒳)).obj
        (fppfRingedTopos B S hS 𝒳).O ≅ (ringedTopos B S hS 𝒳).O
declarations.comment: the structure sheaf is the restriction of the big one

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.structureSheafIso_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788**, `flat_ringed`. The identification `g⁻¹𝒪_𝒳 ≅ 𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}}` is the
identity on sections over a flat object. This pins it: it is not an arbitrary automorphism of the
restricted structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem structureSheafIso_apply (U : (FlatFppf B S hS 𝒳)ᵒᵖ)
    (a : ((inverseImageCommRingFunctor (toposMorphismOnRings B S hS 𝒳)).obj
      (fppfRingedTopos B S hS 𝒳).O).obj.obj U) :
    (structureSheafIso B S hS 𝒳).hom.hom.app U a = a
declarations.comment: that identification, on sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.ringedToposMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788**, `flat_ringed`. The morphism of ringed topoi
`(g, g♯) : (Sh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}), 𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}}) ⟶ (Sh(𝒳_{fppf}), 𝒪_𝒳)` of **Stacks 01D3**
part (2), whose structure map is the adjoint of the identification
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.structureSheafIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ringedToposMorphism :
    RingedToposHom (ringedTopos B S hS 𝒳) (fppfRingedTopos B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: the induced morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.ringedToposMorphism_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788**, `flat_ringed`. The flat-fppf morphism of ringed topoi is flat, in the sense
of **Stacks 04JB**: its inverse-image structure map is an isomorphism, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.ringedToposMorphism_fSharpInverseImage`, and an isomorphism of
sheaves of commutative rings is a flat morphism.
declarations.statement: theorem ringedToposMorphism_isFlat : (ringedToposMorphism B S hS 𝒳).IsFlat
declarations.comment: that morphism of ringed topoi is flat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788**, `flat_ringed`. Restriction of sheaves of modules along the inclusion of the
flat objects, over the fppf structure sheaf and its restriction. The scalar comparison is the
identity, because the structure sheaf of the flat-fppf site is the restriction of the fppf one
with its original rings of sections.

This is the functor that the third assertion of **Stacks 0788** (2)(f) identifies pullback of
modules along `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.ringedToposMorphism` with; the identification is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.modulePullbackIso`, in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Stacks.FlatFppfRingedModules`.
declarations.comment: restriction of modules along it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.modulePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
Pullback of sheaves of modules along the flat-fppf morphism of ringed topoi is restriction of
sheaves of modules along the inclusion of the flat objects, over the fppf structure sheaf and its
restriction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackIso :
    Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules.{u, u, u, u + 1, u, u + 1}
        (ringedToposModulesHom B S hS 𝒳) ≅
      moduleRestriction B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: pullback of modules along it, as an identification

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.modulePullbackIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1)(f), third assertion**: `g^{-1} = g^*`. Pullback of sheaves of modules
along the lisse-étale morphism of ringed topoi
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.ringedToposMorphism'` *is* restriction of sheaves of modules
along the inclusion of the smooth objects, over the étale structure sheaf of **Stacks 06TV** and
its restriction. No hypothesis is carried: this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.subsiteModulePullbackIso` at `P = AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.smoothObject`
and the étale topology, where the two locality hypotheses hold for every algebraic stack.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def modulePullbackIso :
    Stacks.Sheaves.RingedToposModules.RingedToposHom.pullbackModules.{u, u, u, u + 1, u, u + 1}
        (subsiteRingedToposModulesHom B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
          (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B) (smoothObject.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳)) ≅
      subsiteRingedToposModuleRestriction B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
        (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B) (smoothObject.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: part (1)(f): pullback of modules along it is restriction of modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isContinuous_inclusion'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1): continuity of the inclusion of the lisse-étale site.** The étale case
of Stacks 07AK at the chosen étale precoverage of **Stacks 03FF**, with the closure condition of
07AK (1) discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_inclusion' :
    (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι.IsContinuous (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
declarations.comment: the inclusion of the lisse-etale site is continuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isCocontinuous_inclusion'
declarations.doc: **Stacks 0788, part (1): cocontinuity of the inclusion of the lisse-étale site.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isCocontinuous_inclusion' :
    (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι.IsCocontinuous (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
declarations.comment: the inclusion of the lisse-etale site is cocontinuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isContinuous_inclusion_topology'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1): continuity of the inclusion of the lisse-étale site, for the
chosen-family topology.** The same assertion at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.topology`, which is the description Stacks 0787 is recorded
at.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_inclusion_topology' :
    (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι.IsContinuous (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
declarations.comment: continuity of that inclusion, read at the topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isCocontinuous_inclusion_topology'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1): cocontinuity of the inclusion of the lisse-étale site, for the
chosen-family topology.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isCocontinuous_inclusion_topology' :
    (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι.IsCocontinuous (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
declarations.comment: cocontinuity of that inclusion, read at the topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.toposMorphism'
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of topoi of Stacks 0788 (1)(a)**:
`g : Sh(𝒳_{lisse,étale}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_étale)`, with inverse image restriction along the inclusion of
the smooth objects. This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.toposMorphism` with its hypothesis
discharged.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toposMorphism' :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi induced by the lisse-etale inclusion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.toposMorphismTopology'
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of topoi of Stacks 0788 (1)(a), for the chosen-family topology**: the same
morphism of topoi read at `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.topology`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toposMorphismTopology' :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (Type (u + 1)))
      (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the lisse-etale morphism of topoi, read at the topologies

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.setsShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1)(b).** The inverse image of the morphism of topoi `g` of
Stacks 0788 (1)(a) has a left adjoint on sheaves of sets, namely
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.setsShriek`.

This is `CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafAdjunctionLowerShriek` (**Stacks 00XR** (2)) at the inclusion
of the smooth objects, whose continuity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isContinuous_inclusion_topology'`. The right-hand side is the
inverse image of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.toposMorphismTopology'`, restriction along
the inclusion.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev setsShriekAdjunction :
    setsShriek.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ⊣
      (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).ι.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
        (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
declarations.comment: part (1)(b): the lower-shriek adjunction on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isIso_setsShriekAdjunction_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1)(c), the half about `g_!^{Sh}`.** The canonical map `F ⟶ g⁻¹g_!F` on
sheaves of sets — the unit of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.setsShriekAdjunction` — is an
isomorphism.

This is **Stacks 00XT** for a fully faithful, continuous and cocontinuous functor of sites, all
three of which hold for the inclusion of the smooth objects at this topology.
declarations.statement: instance isIso_setsShriekAdjunction_unit : IsIso (setsShriekAdjunction.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).unit
declarations.comment: part (1)(c): the unit of the sets lower-shriek adjunction is invertible

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.abelianLowerShriekAdjunction'
declarations.doc:
**The adjunction `g_! ⊣ g⁻¹` of Stacks 0788 (1)(d) on abelian sheaves**, with no hypothesis:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.abelianLowerShriekAdjunction` with its closure property
discharged.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev abelianLowerShriekAdjunction' :
    abelianLowerShriek.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms B S hS 𝒳) ⊣
      abelianInverseImage.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: part (1)(d): the lower-shriek adjunction on abelian sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isIso_abelianLowerShriek_unit'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1)(e)**, with no hypothesis: the canonical map `F ⟶ g⁻¹(g_!F)` on abelian
sheaves — the unit of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.abelianLowerShriekAdjunction'` — is an
isomorphism. This is **Stacks 077I**, whose three hypotheses on the inclusion of the smooth
objects are full faithfulness, `isContinuous_inclusion'` and `isCocontinuous_inclusion'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_abelianLowerShriek_unit'
    (F : Sheaf (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) AbCat.{u, u + 1}) :
    IsIso ((abelianLowerShriekAdjunction'.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).unit.app F)
declarations.comment: part (1)(e): the unit of the abelian lower-shriek adjunction is invertible

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.structureSheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1)(f), first assertion**:
`g⁻¹𝒪_𝒳 = 𝒪_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}}`. The inverse image of the étale structure sheaf of **Stacks 06TV**
along the morphism of topoi of Stacks 0788 (1)(a) is the structure sheaf of the lisse-étale site.

The inverse image of `g` on sheaves of sets *is* restriction along the inclusion of the smooth
objects, so this is the comparison of the transported commutative ring operations with those of
the restricted sheaf, and that comparison is the identity on sections
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.structureSheafIso_apply`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureSheafIso :
    (inverseImageCommRingFunctor (toposMorphismOnRings.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)).obj
        (etaleRingedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).O ≅ (ringedTopos'.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).O
declarations.comment: part (1)(f): the inverse image of the structure sheaf is the lisse-etale structure sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.structureSheafIso_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1)(f).** The identification `g⁻¹𝒪_𝒳 ≅ 𝒪_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}}` is the
identity on sections over a smooth object. This pins it: it is not an arbitrary automorphism of
the restricted structure sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem structureSheafIso_apply (U : (LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)ᵒᵖ)
    (a : ((inverseImageCommRingFunctor (toposMorphismOnRings.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)).obj
      (etaleRingedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).O).obj.obj U) :
    (structureSheafIso.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).hom.hom.app U a = a
declarations.comment: part (1)(f): that identification, on sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.ringedToposMorphism'
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of ringed topoi of Stacks 0788 (1)(f)**, with no hypothesis:
`(g, g♯) : (Sh(𝒳_{lisse,étale}), 𝒪_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}}) ⟶ (Sh(𝒳_étale), 𝒪_𝒳)`, whose structure map
is the adjoint of `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.structureSheafIso`. This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.ringedToposMorphism` with its closure property
discharged.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ringedToposMorphism' :
    RingedToposHom (ringedTopos'.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (etaleRingedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: part (1)(f): the induced morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isFlat_ringedToposMorphism'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0788, part (1)(f), second assertion**, with no hypothesis: the lisse-étale morphism
of ringed topoi is flat in the sense of **Stacks 04JB**, its inverse-image structure map being the
isomorphism `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.structureSheafIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_ringedToposMorphism' :
    RingedToposHom.IsFlat
      (X := ringedTopos'.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (Y := etaleRingedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
      (ringedToposMorphism'.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: part (1)(f): that morphism of ringed topoi is flat

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isIso_sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous_counit
declarations.doc:
If `u : C ⥤ D` is cocontinuous, continuous and fully faithful, the counit
`g^{-1}g_*F ⟶ F` of `g^{-1} ⊣ g_*` is an isomorphism; equivalently `g_*` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public instance isIso_sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous_counit
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (u : C ⥤ D)
    (A : Type w) [Category.{w'} A]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [u.IsCocontinuous J K] [u.IsContinuous J K] [u.Full] [u.Faithful]
    [∀ F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A, u.op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] :
    IsIso (u.sheafAdjunctionCocontinuous A J K).counit
declarations.comment: (1)(c) and (2)(c): the counit of the cocontinuous sheaf adjunction is invertible

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isRightAdjoint_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0789**, part (2), first assertion: pullback of sheaves of modules along the
flat-fppf morphism of ringed topoi `g` admits a left adjoint `g_!`.

Registered as an instance, because the functor `g_!` and its adjunction are then the canonical
choices it supplies.
declarations.comment: flat_module_shriek

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.moduleLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**The functor `g_!` of Stacks 0789 (1) on sheaves of modules**: the left adjoint of the
pullback `g^*` along the lisse-étale morphism of ringed topoi.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev moduleLowerShriek
declarations.comment: part (1), existence of the functor `g_!` on sheaves of modules for the lisse-étale site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.moduleLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc: **The adjunction `g_! ⊣ g^*` of Stacks 0789 (1) on sheaves of modules.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev moduleLowerShriekAdjunction :
    moduleLowerShriek.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳 ⊣ modulePullback.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (1), left adjointness of `g_!` to `g^*` on sheaves of modules for the lisse-étale site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isIso_moduleLowerShriekAdjunction_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0789 (1), `g^*g_! = id`**: the unit of the adjunction `g_! ⊣ g^*` on sheaves of
modules for the lisse-étale site is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_moduleLowerShriekAdjunction_unit :
    IsIso (moduleLowerShriekAdjunction.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳).unit
declarations.comment: part (1), `g^*g_! = id` on sheaves of modules for the lisse-étale site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**The functor `g_!` of Stacks 0789 (2) on sheaves of modules**: the left adjoint of the
pullback `g^*` along the flat-fppf morphism of ringed topoi.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev moduleLowerShriek
declarations.comment: part (2), existence of the functor `g_!` on sheaves of modules for the flat-fppf site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc: **The adjunction `g_! ⊣ g^*` of Stacks 0789 (2) on sheaves of modules.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev moduleLowerShriekAdjunction :
    moduleLowerShriek B S hS 𝒳 ⊣ modulePullback B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (2), left adjointness of `g_!` to `g^*` on sheaves of modules for the flat-fppf site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_moduleLowerShriekAdjunction_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0789 (2), `g^*g_! = id`**: the unit of the adjunction `g_! ⊣ g^*` on sheaves of
modules for the flat-fppf site is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_moduleLowerShriekAdjunction_unit :
    IsIso (moduleLowerShriekAdjunction B S hS 𝒳).unit
declarations.comment: part (2), `g^*g_! = id` on sheaves of modules for the flat-fppf site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.moduleLowerShriekForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0789 (1), `g_!` on modules agrees with `g_!` on abelian sheaves.** For the lisse-étale
site of an arbitrary algebraic stack `𝒳`, the underlying abelian sheaf of `g_!M`, for `g_!` the
lower shriek `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.moduleLowerShriek` on sheaves of modules, is the
lower shriek of the underlying abelian sheaf of `M`, for `g_!` the left adjoint of restriction of
abelian sheaves along the inclusion of the smooth objects (**Stacks 0788** (1)(d)); naturally in
`M`. The abelian sheaves are taken at the universe of the module sections, which is where the
underlying abelian sheaves of the modules live.

The isomorphism is the canonical comparison of **Stacks 0798**
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekForgetComparison`), which is invertible here because the
structure sheaf of each slice `𝒳_étale/x` is the left Kan extension of its restriction to
`𝒳_{lisse,étale}/x` (**Stacks 07AJ** on the slice; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.bijective_whiskerLeft_overPost_structureSheaf`).
declarations.comment: part (1), `g_!` on sheaves of modules agrees with `g_!` on abelian sheaves, for the lisse-étale site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.moduleLowerShriek_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0789 (1)**, the whole part, for the lisse-étale site of an arbitrary algebraic stack
`𝒳`: the pullback `g^*` of sheaves of modules has a left adjoint `g_!`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.moduleLowerShriek`, with adjunction
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.moduleLowerShriekAdjunction`); `g_!` agrees with the functor
`g_!` on abelian sheaves, i.e. forgetting the module structure commutes with it
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.moduleLowerShriekForgetIso`); and `g^*g_! = id`, the unit of
the adjunction being an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleLowerShriek_spec :
    (modulePullback.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳).IsRightAdjoint ∧
      Nonempty (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _ ⋙
          (smoothObject.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳).ι.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u}
            (inclusionTopology.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳)
            (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)) ≅
        moduleLowerShriek.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳 ⋙ SheafOfModules.toSheaf _) ∧
      IsIso (moduleLowerShriekAdjunction.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳).unit
declarations.comment: part (1), all four assertions, for the lisse-étale site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleLowerShriekForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0789 (2), `g_!` on modules agrees with `g_!` on abelian sheaves.** For the flat-fppf
site of an arbitrary algebraic stack `𝒳`, the underlying abelian sheaf of `g_!M`, for `g_!` the
lower shriek `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleLowerShriek` on sheaves of modules, is the
lower shriek of the underlying abelian sheaf of `M`, for `g_!` the left adjoint of restriction of
abelian sheaves along the inclusion of the flat objects (**Stacks 0788** (2)(d)); naturally in
`M`. The abelian sheaves are taken at the universe of the module sections.

The isomorphism is the canonical comparison of **Stacks 0798**, invertible because the structure
sheaf of each slice `𝒳_fppf/x` is the left Kan extension of its restriction to
`𝒳_{flat,fppf}/x` (**Stacks 07AJ** on the slice): the affine line and plane over a flat object are
flat objects.
declarations.comment: part (2), `g_!` on sheaves of modules agrees with `g_!` on abelian sheaves, for the flat-fppf site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleLowerShriek_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0789 (2)**, the whole part, for the flat-fppf site of an arbitrary algebraic stack
`𝒳`: the pullback `g^*` of sheaves of modules has a left adjoint `g_!`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleLowerShriek`, with adjunction
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleLowerShriekAdjunction`); `g_!` agrees with the functor
`g_!` on abelian sheaves, i.e. forgetting the module structure commutes with it
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.moduleLowerShriekForgetIso`); and `g^*g_! = id`, the unit of
the adjunction being an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleLowerShriek_spec :
    (modulePullback B S hS 𝒳).IsRightAdjoint ∧
      Nonempty (SheafOfModules.toSheaf _ ⋙
          (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{u}
            (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology) ≅
        moduleLowerShriek B S hS 𝒳 ⋙ SheafOfModules.toSheaf _) ∧
      IsIso (moduleLowerShriekAdjunction B S hS 𝒳).unit
declarations.comment: part (2), all four assertions, for the flat-fppf site of an arbitrary algebraic stack

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isIso_unitLowerShriekMap_algebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 078A (1)**: `g_!O_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}} = O_𝒳` for every algebraic stack `𝒳`. The
canonical map from the lower shriek, along the morphism of ringed topoi
`g : (Sh(𝒳_{lisse,étale}), O_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}}) ⟶ (Sh(𝒳_étale), O_𝒳)` of **Stacks 0788**, of
the structure sheaf of the lisse-étale site to the structure sheaf of `𝒳` — the transpose under
the adjunction `g_! ⊣ g^*` of **Stacks 0789** (1) of the identification
`O_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}} = g^{-1}O_𝒳` — is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_unitLowerShriekMap_algebraicStack : IsIso (unitLowerShriekMap.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: part (1): `g_!O_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}} = O_𝒳` for every algebraic stack `𝒳`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_unitLowerShriekMap_algebraicStack
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 078A (2)**: `g_!O_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}} = O_𝒳` for every algebraic stack `𝒳`. The
canonical map from the lower shriek, along the morphism of ringed topoi
`g : (Sh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}), O_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}}) ⟶ (Sh(𝒳_fppf), O_𝒳)` of **Stacks 0788**, of the
structure sheaf of the flat-fppf site to the structure sheaf of `𝒳` — the transpose under the
adjunction `g_! ⊣ g^*` of **Stacks 0789** (2) of the identification
`O_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}} = g^{-1}O_𝒳` — is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_unitLowerShriekMap_algebraicStack : IsIso (unitLowerShriekMap B S hS 𝒳)
declarations.comment: part (2): `g_!O_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}} = O_𝒳` for every algebraic stack `𝒳`

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.QcohPushforward.exists_quasiCompact_not_quasiSeparated_pushforward_not_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 078D (non-quasi-separated case).** A quasi-compact morphism need not
be quasi-separated, and may send its quasi-coherent structure sheaf to a module which is not
quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiCompact_not_quasiSeparated_pushforward_not_isQuasicoherent :
    ∃ (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Y),
      QuasiCompact f ∧
      ¬ QuasiSeparated f ∧
      (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      ¬ ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: non_quasi_separated

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.QcohPushforward.exists_isSeparated_not_quasiCompact_pushforward_not_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 078D (non-quasi-compact case).** Over `Spec ℤ`, a separated,
non-quasi-compact morphism can push a quasi-coherent structure sheaf to a sheaf which is not
quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isSeparated_not_quasiCompact_pushforward_not_isQuasicoherent :
    ∃ (X : Scheme) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of ℤ)),
      IsSeparated f ∧ ¬ QuasiCompact f ∧
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf).IsQuasicoherent ∧
          ¬ ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: non_quasi_compact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveLinePow.exists_fpqc_sheaf_not_isAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 078F.** There is a functor `F : Sch^{opp} ⥤ Sets` which satisfies the sheaf
condition for the fpqc topology, has representable diagonal `F ⟶ F × F`, and receives a
surjective, flat, universally open, quasi-compact morphism `U ⟶ F` from a scheme `U`, but which
is not an algebraic space: for every big fppf site `B`, its restriction to the big fppf site of
`Spec ℤ` in `B` is not an algebraic space over `Spec ℤ`.

The functor is `(ℙ¹)^∞`, sending a scheme `T` to the set of sequences of morphisms `T ⟶ ℙ¹`.
Its sheaf property and representable diagonal are
`AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_fpqc_projectiveLinePow` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.relativelyRepresentable_diag_projectiveLinePow`. The morphism `U ⟶ F` is
`projectiveLinePowFlatCover`, from the product of countably many copies of the disjoint union of
the two standard charts of `ℙ¹`, an affine scheme. That `F` is not an algebraic space is
`not_isAlgebraicSpace_siteRestrict_projectiveLinePow`. A morphism from a scheme to `F` is
surjective, flat, universally open or quasi-compact when every base change of it along a morphism
from a scheme is, in the sense of `CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.presheaf`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fpqc_sheaf_not_isAlgebraicSpace :
    ∃ F : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u,
      Presheaf.IsSheaf Scheme.fpqcTopology.{u} F ∧
      yoneda.relativelyRepresentable (diag F) ∧
      (∃ (U : Scheme.{u}) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F),
        MorphismProperty.presheaf (C := Scheme.{u}) @Surjective p ∧
        MorphismProperty.presheaf (C := Scheme.{u}) @Flat p ∧
        MorphismProperty.presheaf (C := Scheme.{u}) @UniversallyOpen p ∧
        MorphismProperty.presheaf (C := Scheme.{u}) @QuasiCompact p) ∧
      ∀ B : BigFppfSite.{u}, ¬ IsAlgebraicSpace B (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
        B.contains_spec_ulift_int (siteRestrict B B.contains_spec_ulift_int F)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.app_fibers_inv_comp_unitInv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0791: the fibre identification of `j_!j^{-1}G` is evaluation of the shriek counit.**
Write `E` for the equivalence of `sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda` and
`T = E(j^{-1}G)` for the object of `Sh(C)/F` whose source is `j_!j^{-1}G`. The equivalence
identifies the fibre sheaf of `T` with `j^{-1}G`: on underlying presheaves the fibre sheaf of `T`
is `(U, s) ↦ {t ∈ T.left(U) | T.hom(t) = s}` by the `fibers` field, and `E.inverse (E T) ≅ T` by
the unit. This says that the identification sends a section `t` of `j_!j^{-1}G` over `U` lying in
the fibre over `s ∈ F(U)` to its image under the counit of `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}`, a section of `G` over
`U`.

This is the statement connecting the package's two descriptions of `E`. A comparison built from
the *fibre* field — such as Stacks 04J4's identification of the inverse image of a relocalization
with a base change — and one built from the *counit* of `j_!` — such as Stacks 04IE's
identification of the inverse image of a localization with a product — are otherwise assertions
about data that nothing relates, even though both come from the same `E`. Both sides here are
morphisms out of the fibre presheaf of `T`, so comparing them needs no further transport.
declarations.statement:
theorem Presheaf.IsSheaf.app_fibers_inv_comp_unitInv {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf J F)
    [(CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).IsContinuous
      ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) J]
    (G : Sheaf J (Type v)) (X : CostructuredArrow yoneda F)
    (p : OverArrows (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.equivalence.functor.obj
        (((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type v)
          ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) J).obj G)).hom.hom X.hom) :
    (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.fibers.inv.app
          (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.equivalence.functor.obj
            (((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type v)
              ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) J).obj G)) ≫
        (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.equivalence.unitInv.app
            (((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type v)
              ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) J).obj G)).hom).app
        (op X) p =
      (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.shriek.counit.app G).hom.app (op X.left)
        p.val
declarations.comment: the fibre identification of `j_!j^{-1}G` is evaluation of the counit of `j_!`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.app_fibers_inv_comp_homEquiv_shriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0791: transposing across `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}` is evaluation on fibres.** Let `T` be an
object of `Sh(C)/F` and `β : T.left ⟶ G` a morphism of sheaves on `C`. Reading `β` as a morphism
out of `j_!` of the fibre sheaf of `T` — which is what precomposing with the counit of the
equivalence does — and transposing it across `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}` gives a morphism from the fibre sheaf
of `T` to `j^{-1}G`. This says that that morphism sends a section `t` of `T.left` over `U` lying
in the fibre over `s ∈ F(U)` to `β(t)`.

This is the general form of `app_fibers_inv_comp_unitInv`, which is the case
`T = E(j^{-1}G)`, `β` the counit; it is what a comparison built from the `fibers` field has to be
fed through in order to be compared with one built from the counit of `j_!`, since the underlying
sheaf `T.left` of an object in the image of `E` has no description other than by its fibres.
Everything in `j_!`'s adjunction cancels against the equivalence, so the content is exactly the
fibre hom bijection of the source's proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem Presheaf.IsSheaf.app_fibers_inv_comp_homEquiv_shriek {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf J F)
    [(CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).IsContinuous
      ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) J]
    (T : Over (⟨F, hF⟩ : Sheaf J (Type v))) (G : Sheaf J (Type v)) (β : T.left ⟶ G)
    (X : CostructuredArrow yoneda F) (p : OverArrows T.hom.hom X.hom) :
    (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.fibers.inv.app T ≫
        (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.shriek.homEquiv
            (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.equivalence.inverse.obj T) G
            ((Over.forget (⟨F, hF⟩ : Sheaf J (Type v))).map
              (hF.sheafEquivalenceCostructuredArrowYoneda.equivalence.counit.app T) ≫
                β)).hom).app
        (op X) p =
      β.hom.app (op X.left) p.val
declarations.comment: transposing across `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}` is evaluation on fibres

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Presheaf.IsSheaf.exists_sheafEquivalence_costructuredArrow_yoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0791.** Let `(C, J)` be a site and let `F` be a sheaf of sets on `C`. Let
`C/F = CostructuredArrow yoneda F` be the category of pairs `(U, s)` with `s ∈ F(U)`, with its
projection `j = CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F` to `C`, and declare a family
`{(U_i, s_i) ⟶ (U, s)}` to be a covering when `{U_i ⟶ U}` is a covering of `C`, i.e. give `C/F`
the topology `j.restrictedTopology J` generated by those families. Then:

1. `C/F` is a site with exactly those coverings: a sieve of `(U, s)` is covering for
   `j.restrictedTopology J` if and only if its image under `j` is a covering sieve of `U`;
2. the canonical equivalence `Over F ≌ PSh(C/F)` of `overEquivPresheafCostructuredArrow` matches
   sheaves with sheaves: for an object `φ : G ⟶ F` of `PSh(C)/F`, the presheaf
   `(U, s) ↦ {t ∈ G(U) | φ(t) = s}` on `C/F` is a sheaf if and only if `G` is a sheaf on `C`;
3. `j` is continuous and cocontinuous, so that it induces a morphism of topoi
   `j : Sh(C/F) ⟶ Sh(C)` with `j^{-1}` restriction (Stacks 00XR); and
4. there is an equivalence `E : Sh(C/F) ≌ Sh(C)/F`, namely the restriction of that canonical
   equivalence — `E.inverse` is `(G, φ) ↦ ((U, s) ↦ {t ∈ G(U) | φ(t) = s})` on underlying
   presheaves — for which `E.functor` followed by `Over.forget` is left adjoint to `j^{-1}`, that
   is, is `j_!`. Since `Over.forget` is the `j_{F!}` of Stacks 04GZ, this is the assertion that
   `E` turns `j` into the localization morphism `j_F`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Presheaf.IsSheaf.exists_sheafEquivalence_costructuredArrow_yoneda {C : Type u}
    [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf J F) :
    (∀ (X : CostructuredArrow yoneda F) (S : Sieve X),
        S ∈ (CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J X ↔
          Sieve.functorPushforward (CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F) S ∈ J X.left) ∧
      (∀ T : Over F,
        Presheaf.IsSheaf ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J)
            ((overEquivPresheafCostructuredArrow F).functor.obj T) ↔
          Presheaf.IsSheaf J T.left) ∧
      ∃ (_ :
        (CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).IsContinuous
          ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) J)
        (_ :
        (CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).IsCocontinuous
          ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) J)
        (E :
        Sheaf ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) (Type v) ≌
          Over (⟨F, hF⟩ : Sheaf J (Type v))),
        Nonempty
            (E.inverse ⋙
                sheafToPresheaf ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) (Type v) ≅
              Over.post (X := (⟨F, hF⟩ : Sheaf J (Type v))) (sheafToPresheaf J (Type v)) ⋙
                (overEquivPresheafCostructuredArrow F).functor) ∧
          Nonempty
            (E.functor ⋙ Over.forget (⟨F, hF⟩ : Sheaf J (Type v)) ⊣
              (CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type v)
                ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda F).restrictedTopology J) J)
declarations.comment:
Sheaves on the site `C/F` of pairs `(U, s)` with `s ∈ F(U)`, whose coverings are
  those of `C`: `C/F` is a site, `j` is continuous and cocontinuous, the canonical equivalence
  `PSh(C)/F ≌ PSh(C/F)` matches sheaves with sheaves, and it restricts to an equivalence
  `Sh(C/F) ≌ Sh(C)/F` carrying `j_!` to `Over.forget`, i.e. turning `j` into `j_F`.

declarations.name: isRightAdjoint_of_partialAdjointData
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒜` and `𝓑` be abelian categories, `u : 𝒜 ⥤ 𝓑` a functor, and suppose
there is `S ⊆ Ob(𝓑)` such that every object of `𝓑` is a quotient of some
object of `S` and, for every `P ∈ S`, the functor `A ↦ Hom_𝓑(P, u A)` is
corepresentable. Then `u` admits a left adjoint.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRightAdjoint_of_partialAdjointData
    {A B : Type*} [Category A] [Category B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B]
    (u : A ⥤ B) (S : Set B)
    (h1 : QuotientOfFamily S)
    (h2 : PartialAdjointData u S) :
    u.IsRightAdjoint

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isLeftDerivable_of_acyclic_mapHomologicalComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0794.** Let `F : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ` be a right exact functor of abelian categories and let `P`
be a class of objects of `𝒜`. Assume

1. `P` contains a zero object, is closed under finite direct sums, and every object of `𝒜` is a
   quotient of an object satisfying `P`,
2. `F` turns every bounded above acyclic complex with all terms satisfying `P` into an acyclic
   complex,
3. `𝒜` and `ℬ` have colimits of systems indexed by `ℕ`,
4. those colimits are exact in both `𝒜` and `ℬ`, and
5. `F` commutes with them.

Then `LF` is defined on all of `D(𝒜)`: the functor `K(𝒜) ⥤ D(ℬ)`, `K ↦ F(K)`, is left
derivable with respect to the quasi-isomorphisms (Tag 05SV), i.e. for every complex `K` the
pro-object `(s : K' ⟶ K) ↦ F(K')` over quasi-isomorphisms `s` is essentially constant (Tag 05S9).

The proof is the source's: every object of `K(𝒜)` receives a quasi-isomorphism from a
`P`-cellular complex (the colimit of the ladder of Tag 06XX), `F` sends quasi-isomorphisms
between `P`-cellular complexes to quasi-isomorphisms (the claim of the source's proof,
`StacksDraft.UnboundedLeftDerivedFunctor.derives_cellularLocalizerMorphism`), and Tag 06XN(2)
then makes `LF` everywhere defined.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLeftDerivable_of_acyclic_mapHomologicalComplex
    (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    (P : ObjectProperty A) [P.ContainsZero]
    (hsum : ∀ X Y : A, P X → P Y → P (X ⊞ Y))
    (hP : ∀ X : A, ∃ (Y : A) (_ : P Y) (p : Y ⟶ X), Epi p)
    (hFP : ∀ (a : ℤ) (L : CochainComplex A ℤ), L.IsStrictlyLE a → (∀ n, P (L.X n)) →
      L.Acyclic → ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj L).Acyclic)
    [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ A] [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ B]
    [HasExactColimitsOfShape ℕ A] [HasExactColimitsOfShape ℕ B]
    [PreservesColimitsOfShape ℕ F] :
    (F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).IsLeftDerivable
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (ComplexShape.up ℤ))

declarations.name: CochainComplex.KFlat.tensor
declarations.doc:
(Stacks tag 0795, Lemma 15.60.4) If `K` and `L` are K-flat complexes of
`R`-modules, then `Tot(K ⊗_R L)` (i.e. the monoidal tensor product `K ⊗ L`) is
K-flat.

For acyclic `M`, K-flatness of `K` makes `M ⊗ K` acyclic, then K-flatness of `L`
makes `(M ⊗ K) ⊗ L` acyclic, and acyclicity transfers to `M ⊗ (K ⊗ L)` across the
associator.
declarations.statement:
theorem CochainComplex.KFlat.tensor (K L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
    (hK : K.KFlat) (hL : L.KFlat) : (K ⊗ L).KFlat

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriek

associated with a continuous and cocontinuous functor of sites, where `O_C = g^{-1} O_D`: a
sheaf of `O_C`-modules is pushed forward as a presheaf of modules and the result is sheafified.
declarations.statement:
def lowerShriek [u.IsCocontinuous J K] :

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekForgetComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical natural transformation from lower shriek applied to the underlying abelian
sheaf to the underlying abelian sheaf of lower shriek on modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lowerShriekForgetComparison :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} S ⋙
        F.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{w} J K ⟶
      _root_.SheafOfModules.pullback.{w} phi ⋙ _root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} R
declarations.comment: comparison_transformation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekForgetComparison_homEquiv
declarations.doc:
The comparison map is adjoint to the forgotten unit of the module lower-shriek
adjunction.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerShriekForgetComparison_homEquiv (M : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} S) :
    (F.sheafAdjunctionContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{w} J K).homEquiv
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} S).obj M)
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} R).obj
          ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullback.{w} phi).obj M))
        ((lowerShriekForgetComparison F phi).app M) =
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} S).map
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{w} phi).unit.app M)
declarations.comment: comparison_transformation

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekForget_not_isomorphic
declarations.doc:
The lower shriek of modules may differ, even as an abelian sheaf, from lower
shriek of the underlying abelian sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerShriekForget_not_isomorphic :
    ∃ (J : GrothendieckTopology PUnit) (K : GrothendieckTopology Bool)
      (F : PUnit ⥤ Bool) (R : Sheaf K RingCat.{0})
      (hF : F.IsContinuous J K) (_hFc : F.IsCocontinuous J K),
      letI : F.IsContinuous J K := hF
      let S : Sheaf J RingCat.{0} :=
        (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{0} J K).obj R
      let φ : S ⟶ (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous RingCat.{0} J K).obj R := 𝟙 S
      ∃ (hAb : (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{0} J K).IsRightAdjoint)
        (hMod : (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{0} φ).IsRightAdjoint),
      letI : (F.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{0} J K).IsRightAdjoint := hAb
      letI : (SheafOfModules.pushforward.{0} φ).IsRightAdjoint := hMod
      ∃ M : SheafOfModules.{0} S,
        ¬ Nonempty
          (((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{0} S ⋙
              F.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{0} J K).obj M) ≅
            ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{0} φ ⋙
              SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{0} R).obj M))
declarations.comment: noncommutativity

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_lowerShriekForgetComparison_iff
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison between lower shriek on sheaves of modules and lower shriek on the
underlying abelian sheaves is an isomorphism if and only if it is an isomorphism at the extension
by zero `j_{U!} O_U` of the structure sheaf for every object `U` of the source site.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lowerShriekForgetComparison_iff :
    IsIso (lowerShriekForgetComparison F phi) ↔
      ∀ U : C, IsIso ((lowerShriekForgetComparison F phi).app
        (extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, u, max u₂ v₂ t} S U))
declarations.comment: the criterion: agreement iff the comparison is invertible at every j_{U!} O_U

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_lowerShriekForgetComparison_iff_of_isos
declarations.doc:
If a family `G` of sheaves of modules is isomorphic, object by object, to the extensions by
zero of the structure sheaf, then the comparison is an isomorphism exactly when it is an
isomorphism at every `G U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lowerShriekForgetComparison_iff_of_isos
    (G : C → _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u₁ v₁ u₂ v₂ u t} S)
    (e : ∀ U : C, extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, u, max u₂ v₂ t} S U ≅ G U) :
    IsIso (lowerShriekForgetComparison F phi) ↔
      ∀ U : C, IsIso ((lowerShriekForgetComparison F phi).app (G U))
declarations.comment: the criterion, at any family isomorphic to the extensions by zero of the structure sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_lowerShriekForgetComparison_iff_extensionByZeroUnit
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison between lower shriek on sheaves of modules and lower shriek on the
underlying abelian sheaves is an isomorphism if and only if, for every object `U` of the source
site, the canonical map

`g_!^{Ab} j_{U!} O_U ⟶ j_{u(U)!} O_{u(U)}`

is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lowerShriekForgetComparison_iff_extensionByZeroUnit :
    IsIso (lowerShriekForgetComparison u (structureMap J K u O)) ↔
      ∀ V : C, IsIso ((lowerShriekForgetComparison u (structureMap J K u O)).app
            (extensionByZeroUnit (inverseImageRing J K u O) V) ≫
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf O).map
            (pullbackExtensionByZeroUnitIso.{t, u₁, u₂, v₁, v₂} J K u O V).hom)
declarations.comment: the criterion in the source's form: the comparison is an isomorphism iff `g_!^{Ab} j_{U!} O_U ⟶ j_{u(U)!} O_{u(U)}` is one for every `U`, the target being identified by Stacks 07AC

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekForgetComparison_app_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
The lower-shriek forget comparison carries the forgotten counit of the module lower-shriek
adjunction to the counit of the abelian one: both sides are maps from the abelian lower shriek of
the direct image of `N` to the abelian sheaf underlying `N`, the left one going through the module
lower shriek of the direct image.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerShriekForgetComparison_app_comp_counit (N : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} R) :
    (lowerShriekForgetComparison F phi).app
          ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pushforward.{w} phi).obj N) ≫
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} R).map
          ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{w} phi).counit.app N) =
      (F.sheafAdjunctionContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{w} J K).counit.app
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} R).obj N)
declarations.comment: the comparison on counits

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.abelianShriekOverIso
declarations.doc:
Lower shriek of abelian sheaves commutes with localization: with `V = u(U)` and
`g' : Sh(C/U) ⟶ Sh(D/V)` the morphism of topoi induced by the localized functor `u' = Over.post u`
of Stacks 03EG,

`g_!^{Ab} ∘ j_{U!} ≅ j_{V!} ∘ (g')^{Ab}_!`.
declarations.comment: `g_!^{Ab} j_{U!} = j_{u(U)!} (g')^{Ab}_!`, the consequence of the localized square of Stacks 03EG that the remark uses

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.homEquiv_comp_lowerShriekForgetComparison
declarations.doc:
The composition law for the comparison transformation of Stacks 0798. For a composite
`a ⋙ b` of continuous functors of sites, with the structure sheaves the successive restrictions
of a sheaf of rings on the target, the composite

`b_!^{Ab} (c^a) ≫ c^b`

of the two comparison transformations is the adjoint transpose, under the composite of the two
lower-shriek adjunctions for abelian sheaves, of the forgotten unit of the composite of the two
lower-shriek adjunctions for modules, written with the two units separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem homEquiv_comp_lowerShriekForgetComparison
    (M : _root_.SheafOfModules.{w} (inverseImageRing JA JB a (inverseImageRing JB JE b O))) :
    ((a.sheafAdjunctionContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{w} JA JB).comp
        (b.sheafAdjunctionContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{w} JB JE)).homEquiv _ _
      ((b.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{w} JB JE).map
          ((lowerShriekForgetComparison a
            (structureMap JA JB a (inverseImageRing JB JE b O))).app M) ≫
        (lowerShriekForgetComparison b (structureMap JB JE b O)).app
          ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullback.{w}
            (structureMap JA JB a (inverseImageRing JB JE b O))).obj M)) =
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w}
            (inverseImageRing JA JB a (inverseImageRing JB JE b O))).map
          ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{w}
            (structureMap JA JB a (inverseImageRing JB JE b O))).unit.app M) ≫
        (a.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{w} JA JB).map
          ((_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} (inverseImageRing JB JE b O)).map
            ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction.{w}
              (structureMap JB JE b O)).unit.app
              ((_root_.SheafOfModules.pullback.{w}
                (structureMap JA JB a (inverseImageRing JB JE b O))).obj M)))
declarations.comment: the composition law for the comparison transformation `g_!^{Ab} ∘ forget ⟶ forget ∘ g_!`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.localizedStructureSheafComparison
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `(g')_!^{Ab} O_U ⟶ O_{u(U)}` of Stacks 0798: lower shriek of abelian
sheaves applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of the structure sheaf of the localized source
site, mapping to the underlying abelian sheaf of the structure sheaf of the localized target
site. It is the comparison transformation of Stacks 0798 for the localized functor, evaluated at
the structure sheaf, followed by the canonical map `g'_! O_U ⟶ O_{u(U)}` of sheaves of
modules.
declarations.statement:
def localizedStructureSheafComparison :
    ((Over.post (X := V) u).sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat.{w} (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V))).obj
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} (inverseImageRing (J.over V) (K.over (u.obj V))
            (Over.post (X := V) u) (O.over (u.obj V)))).obj
          (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit _)) ⟶
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{w} (O.over (u.obj V))).obj
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit (O.over (u.obj V)))
declarations.comment: the canonical map of equation 0799, `κ_U : (g')_!^{Ab} O_U ⟶ O_{u(U)}`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isIso_lowerShriekForgetComparison_of_localizedStructureSheafComparison
declarations.doc:
Lower shriek on sheaves of modules agrees with lower shriek on the underlying abelian
sheaves, that is, the comparison transformation `Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekForgetComparison`
is an isomorphism, as soon as, for every object `U` of the source site, the canonical map

`(g')_!^{Ab} O_U ⟶ O_{u(U)}`

of `Stacks.SheafOfModules.localizedStructureSheafComparison` is an isomorphism, `g'` being the
morphism of topoi induced by the localized functor `u' = Over.post u : C/U ⥤ D/u(U)` of Stacks
03EG.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lowerShriekForgetComparison_of_localizedStructureSheafComparison
    (h : ∀ V : C, IsIso (localizedStructureSheafComparison J K u O V)) :
    IsIso (lowerShriekForgetComparison u (structureMap J K u O))
declarations.comment: the criterion: `g_! = g_!^{Ab}` if the canonical map of equation 0799 is an isomorphism for every object `U`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_etaleLowerShriekForgetComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0798** for postcomposition along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces: the
comparison from extension by zero of the underlying abelian sheaf to the underlying abelian
sheaf of extension by zero of modules is an isomorphism, because every slice functor of
postcomposition is an equivalence and the structure morphism of rings is the identity.
declarations.statement:
instance isIso_etaleLowerShriekForgetComparison (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsEtale B S hS f.hom) :
    IsIso (Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriekForgetComparison.{u, u}
      (smallEtalePostcomp B S hS f hf)
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.structureMap (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.1)
        (SmallEtale.topology B S hS Y.1) (smallEtalePostcomp B S hS f hf)
        (etaleRingSheaf B S hS Y)))
declarations.comment: postcomposition along an étale morphism of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleModuleShriekForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Tag 0798 for an étale morphism of algebraic spaces.**  The abelian sheaf underlying the
extension by zero of a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules is the extension by zero of the abelian sheaf
underlying it.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleModuleShriekForgetIsoRaw` repackaged: the two isomorphisms
have the same components, and only the spelling of the functors differs.  The repackaging is
what makes the structure sheaf of rings of `X` appear as
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleRingSheaf` rather than as the restriction along postcomposition of
that of `Y`, and the module categories appear as `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Modules`; without it
every rewrite below is rejected for being type-incorrect at the transparency rewriting uses.
declarations.statement:
def etaleModuleShriekForgetIso :
    SheafOfModules.toSheaf (etaleRingSheaf B S hS X) ⋙
        abelianEtaleExtensionByZero B S hS f hf ≅
      etaleModuleLowerShriek B S hS f hf ⋙
        SheafOfModules.toSheaf (etaleRingSheaf B S hS Y)
declarations.comment: extension by zero of modules and of abelian sheaves, for an étale morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.etaleModuleShriekForgetIso_hom_app_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of Tag 0798 carries the forgotten counit of the module extension-by-zero
adjunction to the counit of the abelian one.**
declarations.statement:
theorem etaleModuleShriekForgetIso_hom_app_comp_counit
    (N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2) :
    (etaleModuleShriekForgetIso B S hS f hf).hom.app
          ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS f hf).obj N) ≫
        (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (etaleRingSheaf B S hS Y)).map
          ((etaleModuleLowerShriekAdjunction B S hS f hf).counit.app N) =
      (abelianEtaleExtensionByZeroAdjunction B S hS f hf).counit.app
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (etaleRingSheaf B S hS Y)).obj N)
declarations.comment: the comparison on counits, for an étale morphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.IsGenerator
declarations.doc:
An object `U` of `C` is a *generator* if for every `N ⊂ M` with `N ≠ M` there is a morphism
`U ⟶ M` which does not factor through `N`. A subobject `N ⊂ M` is given by a monomorphism
`i : N ⟶ M`, and `N ≠ M` says that `i` is not an isomorphism.

Mathlib has no name for this condition; it uses `CategoryTheory.IsSeparator` instead, with which
this agrees by `Stacks.Injectives.isGenerator_iff_isSeparator`.
declarations.statement: def IsGenerator (U : C) : Prop
declarations.comment: generator

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isGenerator_iff_subobject
declarations.doc:
The definition of a generator, phrased with subobjects: `U` is a generator if and only if for
every object `M` and every subobject `N` of `M` other than `M` itself there is a morphism `U ⟶ M`
which does not factor through `N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGenerator_iff_subobject (U : C) :
    IsGenerator U ↔ ∀ (M : C) (N : Subobject M), N ≠ ⊤ →
      ∃ u : U ⟶ M, ∀ v : U ⟶ (N : C), v ≫ N.arrow ≠ u
declarations.comment: generator as a subobject condition

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isGenerator_iff_isSeparator
declarations.doc:
A generator in the sense of the Stacks project is the same thing as a separator in the sense of
Mathlib: morphisms out of `U` see every proper subobject if and only if they distinguish parallel
morphisms.

From left to right: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is killed by every morphism `U ⟶ X` then every such morphism
factors through `ker f`, which therefore cannot be a proper subobject of `X`, so `f = 0`. From
right to left: if `i : N ⟶ M` is a monomorphism through which every morphism `U ⟶ M` factors, then
every morphism `U ⟶ M` is killed by `coker i ≠ 0`, so `i` is an epimorphism and hence, `C` being
balanced, an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: theorem isGenerator_iff_isSeparator (U : C) : IsGenerator U ↔ IsSeparator U
declarations.comment: generator is separator

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isGrothendieckAbelian_iff_ab5_and_exists_isGenerator
declarations.doc:
An abelian category is a *Grothendieck abelian category* if it has AB5 and a generator. Both
sides are expressed with Mathlib's vocabulary: AB5 at size `v` is
`CategoryTheory.AB5OfSize.{v, v}`, and `CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v}` is Mathlib's
class.

The equivalence is stated at `w = v`, for `v` the hom universe of `C`, because Mathlib's class
carries the further requirement `LocallySmall.{w} C`, which has no counterpart in the Stacks
definition and is vacuous exactly for that choice of `w`. The hypothesis that filtered colimits of
size `v` exist is part of AB5 as the Stacks project states it, AB5 being AB3 together with
exactness of filtered colimits; in Mathlib it is the instance argument of
`CategoryTheory.AB5OfSize`, so it has to be assumed on both sides at once.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGrothendieckAbelian_iff_ab5_and_exists_isGenerator
    [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{v, v} C] :
    CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} C ↔
      (CategoryTheory.AB5OfSize.{v, v} C ∧ ∃ U : C, IsGenerator U)
declarations.comment: Grothendieck abelian category

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.AB3
declarations.doc: **AB3**: `C` has direct sums, i.e. coproducts indexed by every type in `Type w`.
declarations.statement: def AB3 : Prop
declarations.comment: AB3

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.AB4
declarations.doc: **AB4**: `C` has AB3 and direct sums are exact.
declarations.statement: def AB4 : Prop
declarations.comment: AB4

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.AB5
declarations.doc:
**AB5**: `C` has AB3 and filtered colimits are exact. Filtered colimits exist as soon as AB3
holds, `C` having coequalizers
(`CategoryTheory.Limits.has_colimits_of_hasCoequalizers_and_coproducts`, [Stacks, Tag 002P]);
exactness is `CategoryTheory.AB5OfSize`.
declarations.statement: def AB5 : Prop
declarations.comment: AB5

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.AB3Star
declarations.doc: **AB3\***: `C` has products, indexed by every type in `Type w`.
declarations.statement: def AB3Star : Prop
declarations.comment: AB3*

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.AB4Star
declarations.doc: **AB4\***: `C` has AB3\* and products are exact.
declarations.statement: def AB4Star : Prop
declarations.comment: AB4*

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.AB5Star
declarations.doc:
**AB5\***: `C` has AB3\* and cofiltered limits are exact. Cofiltered limits exist as soon as
AB3\* holds, `C` having equalizers
(`CategoryTheory.Limits.has_limits_of_hasEqualizers_and_products`, [Stacks, Tag 002N]);
exactness is `CategoryTheory.AB5StarOfSize`.
declarations.statement: def AB5Star : Prop
declarations.comment: AB5*

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.ab3_iff_hasColimitsOfSize
declarations.doc: AB3 is the existence of all colimits of size `w` ([Stacks, Tag 002P]).
declarations.statement: theorem ab3_iff_hasColimitsOfSize : AB3.{w} C ↔ HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} C
declarations.comment: AB3 gives all colimits

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.ab3Star_iff_hasLimitsOfSize
declarations.doc: AB3\* is the existence of all limits of size `w` ([Stacks, Tag 002N]).
declarations.statement: theorem ab3Star_iff_hasLimitsOfSize : AB3Star.{w} C ↔ HasLimitsOfSize.{w, w} C
declarations.comment: AB3* gives all limits

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.ab4_iff_ab4OfSize
declarations.doc: On a category with direct sums, AB4 is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.AB4OfSize`.
declarations.statement: theorem ab4_iff_ab4OfSize [HasCoproducts.{w} C] : AB4.{w} C ↔ CategoryTheory.AB4OfSize.{w} C
declarations.comment: AB4 in Mathlib's terms

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.ab5_iff
declarations.doc: AB5 is AB3 together with Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.AB5OfSize`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ab5_iff [HasFilteredColimitsOfSize.{w, w} C] :
    AB5.{w} C ↔ HasCoproducts.{w} C ∧ CategoryTheory.AB5OfSize.{w, w} C
declarations.comment: AB5 in Mathlib's terms

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.ab4Star_iff_ab4StarOfSize
declarations.doc: On a category with products, AB4\* is Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.AB4StarOfSize`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ab4Star_iff_ab4StarOfSize [HasProducts.{w} C] :
    AB4Star.{w} C ↔ CategoryTheory.AB4StarOfSize.{w} C
declarations.comment: AB4* in Mathlib's terms

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.ab5Star_iff
declarations.doc: AB5\* is AB3\* together with Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.AB5StarOfSize`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ab5Star_iff [HasCofilteredLimitsOfSize.{w, w} C] :
    AB5Star.{w} C ↔ HasProducts.{w} C ∧ CategoryTheory.AB5StarOfSize.{w, w} C
declarations.comment: AB5* in Mathlib's terms

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.IsGrothendieckAbelianCategory
declarations.doc:
**Grothendieck abelian category**: `C` has AB5 and a generator. The direct sums and filtered
colimits of AB5 are indexed by sets in the hom universe `v` of `C`, the size at which the
Stacks project's (locally small) categories live.
declarations.statement: def IsGrothendieckAbelianCategory : Prop
declarations.comment: Grothendieck abelian category, Stacks definition

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isGrothendieckAbelianCategory_iff
declarations.doc:
A category is a Grothendieck abelian category in the sense of the Stacks project, that is it
has AB5 and a generator, if and only if it is one in the sense of Mathlib,
`CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v}` (locally small, exact filtered colimits of size `v`,
a separator), with no further hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isGrothendieckAbelianCategory_iff :
    IsGrothendieckAbelianCategory C ↔ CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} C
declarations.comment: Grothendieck abelian category, agreement with Mathlib

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.Size.size
declarations.doc:
The *size* of an object `M` of an abelian category: the cardinality of the set of
subobjects of `M`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def size {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C] (M : C) : Cardinal

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.Size.size_X₁_le_size_X₂
declarations.doc:
For a short exact sequence `0 → M' → M → M'' → 0` in a Grothendieck abelian
category, the size of `M'` is at most the size of `M`: there is an injection from the
subobjects of `M'` into the subobjects of `M`, hence `|M'| ≤ |M|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem size_X₁_le_size_X₂ {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian C]
    (S : ShortComplex C) (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    size S.X₁ ≤ size S.X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.Size.size_X₃_le_size_X₂
declarations.doc:
For a short exact sequence `0 → M' → M → M'' → 0`, the size of `M''` is at most the
size of `M`: there is an injection from the subobjects of `M''` into the subobjects of
`M`, hence `|M''| ≤ |M|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem size_X₃_le_size_X₂ {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian C]
    (S : ShortComplex C) (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    size S.X₃ ≤ size S.X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exists_epi_coproduct_of_subobject_cardinality_le
declarations.doc:
If the cardinality of the set of subobjects of `M` is at most `κ`, then `M` is a
quotient of a coproduct, indexed by a type of cardinality at most `κ`, of copies of the
generator `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_coproduct_of_subobject_cardinality_le (U M : C) (hU : IsSeparator U)
    (κ : Cardinal.{w})
    (hM : Cardinal.lift.{w} (Cardinal.mk (Subobject M)) ≤
      Cardinal.lift.{max u v} κ) :
    ∃ (ι : Type w), Cardinal.mk ι ≤ κ ∧
      ∃ (f : (∐ fun (_ : ι) => U) ⟶ M), Epi f
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.essentiallySmall_subobject_cardinality_le
declarations.doc:
For every cardinal `κ`, the objects whose sets of subobjects have cardinality at most
`κ` have only a set of isomorphism classes.
declarations.statement:
theorem essentiallySmall_subobject_cardinality_le (κ : Cardinal.{w}) :
    ObjectProperty.EssentiallySmall.{w}
      (fun M : C => Cardinal.lift.{w} (Cardinal.mk (Subobject M)) ≤
        Cardinal.lift.{max u v} κ)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isSmallWithRespectTo_monomorphisms_of_hasCardinalLT_subobject_cof
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 079F.** Let `A` be a Grothendieck abelian category, let `M` be an object of `A`
and let `κ = |M|` be the cardinality of the set of subobjects of `M`. If `α` is an ordinal
whose cofinality is bigger than `κ`, then `M` is `α`-small with respect to injections: for
every system `(B_β)_{β ∈ α}` in `A` with monomorphic transition maps the canonical map
`colim_β Hom(M, B_β) ⟶ Hom(M, colim_β B_β)` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSmallWithRespectTo_monomorphisms_of_hasCardinalLT_subobject_cof
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C]
    (M : C) (α : Ordinal.{w}) (hM : HasCardinalLT (Subobject M) α.cof) :
    IsSmallWithRespectTo M (MorphismProperty.monomorphisms C) α

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.injective_iff_exists_extension_of_subobject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 079G.** An object `I` of a Grothendieck abelian category is injective if and
only if, for every subobject `M` of a separator `G`, every morphism `M ⟶ I` extends along
`M.arrow` to a morphism `G ⟶ I`.

The forward implication is injectivity applied to the monomorphism `M.arrow`; the converse is
the statement that the inclusions of the subobjects of a separator have the same right lifting
property as all monomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_iff_exists_extension_of_subobject [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C]
    {G : C} (hG : IsSeparator G) (I : C) :
    Injective I ↔
      ∀ (M : Subobject G) (f : (M : C) ⟶ I), ∃ g : G ⟶ I, M.arrow ≫ g = f

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.exists_monomorphisms_injective_iff
declarations.doc:
**Tag 079G in set-indexed form.** A Grothendieck abelian category has a set `T` and, for
each `t : T`, a monomorphism `N t ⟶ N' t` such that an object `I` is injective precisely when
every morphism `N t ⟶ I` extends to `N' t`.

The family is the one of `injective_iff_exists_extension_of_subobject`: the inclusions of the
subobjects of `CategoryTheory.separator C`, whose collection is `w`-small because a
Grothendieck abelian category is well-powered. This is the shape in which Tags 0FSN and 0FSS
consume Tag 079G.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_monomorphisms_injective_iff (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C] :
    ∃ (T : Type w) (N N' : T → C) (i : ∀ t, N t ⟶ N' t),
      (∀ t, Mono (i t)) ∧
        ∀ I : C, Injective I ↔ ∀ (t : T) (f : N t ⟶ I), ∃ g : N' t ⟶ I, i t ≫ g = f
declarations.comment: set-indexed form

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.FunctorialEmbedding.hasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 079H.** A Grothendieck abelian category has functorial injective
embeddings in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 0139].
declarations.statement: theorem hasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings : HasFunctorialInjectiveEmbeddings C
declarations.comment: functorial form; Mathlib's enoughInjectives has the non-functorial half

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.SmallSubobjectEpi.exists_subobject_epi_smallSize_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 079J.** Let `C` be a Grothendieck abelian category with a generator `U`, and let
`c(κ) = |⨁_{α ∈ κ} U|` (`smallCardFn U κ`). For every epimorphism `π : M ⟶ N` there is a
subobject `M' ⊆ M` such that `M' ⟶ M ⟶ N` is an epimorphism and `|M'| ≤ c(|N|)`, sizes being
cardinalities of sets of subobjects (`smallSize`, see `lift_smallSize`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_subobject_epi_smallSize_le {U : C} (hU : IsSeparator U) {M N : C} (π : M ⟶ N)
    [Epi π] :
    ∃ M' : Subobject M, Epi (M'.arrow ≫ π) ∧
      smallSize (M' : C) ≤ smallCardFn U (smallSize N)
declarations.comment:
Mathlib's setting `IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} C` for `Category.{v} C`; sizes in
`Cardinal.{v}`, the generator `U` arbitrary

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.acyclicComplexSizeBound
declarations.doc:
A cardinal which uniformly bounds the sizes of the terms of the small bounded-above acyclic
complexes: the supremum over `n` of the `(n + 1)`-st iterate of `κ ↦ #(Subobject (∐_κ U))` at
`#(Subobject U)`, where `U` is the separator of `C`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def acyclicComplexSizeBound (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C] : Cardinal.{w}
declarations.comment: the cardinal

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exists_small_boundedAbove_acyclic_subcomplex
declarations.doc:
Every nonzero acyclic complex contains a nonzero bounded-above acyclic subcomplex
whose terms have uniformly bounded size.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_boundedAbove_acyclic_subcomplex
    (M : CochainComplex C ℤ) (hM : M.Acyclic) (hM₀ : ¬ IsZero M) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : N ⟶ M),
      Mono f ∧
      ¬ IsZero N ∧
      N.Acyclic ∧
      (∃ a : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, a < n → IsZero (N.X n)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, Cardinal.mk (Shrink.{w} (Subobject (N.X n))) ≤
        acyclicComplexSizeBound (C := C)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.exists_epi_coproduct_small_boundedAbove_acyclic
declarations.doc:
Every acyclic complex is an epimorphic image of a coproduct of bounded-above
acyclic complexes whose terms have uniformly bounded size.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_coproduct_small_boundedAbove_acyclic
    (M : CochainComplex C ℤ) (hM : M.Acyclic) :
    ∃ (I : Type w) (N : I → CochainComplex C ℤ)
      (f : (∐ fun i ↦ N i) ⟶ M),
      Epi f ∧
      ∀ i : I,
        (N i).Acyclic ∧
        (∃ a : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, a < n → IsZero ((N i).X n)) ∧
        ∀ n : ℤ,
          Cardinal.mk (Shrink.{w} (Subobject ((N i).X n))) ≤
            acyclicComplexSizeBound (C := C)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isKInjective_of_small_boundedAbove_acyclic
declarations.doc:
A complex of injective objects is K-injective provided that all maps to it from
bounded-above acyclic complexes within the uniform size bound are null-homotopic.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_of_small_boundedAbove_acyclic (I : CochainComplex C ℤ)
    (hI : ∀ n : ℤ, Injective (I.X n))
    (hvanish : ∀ (M : CochainComplex C ℤ), M.Acyclic →
      (∃ a : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, a < n → IsZero (M.X n)) →
      (∀ n : ℤ, Cardinal.mk (Shrink.{w} (Subobject (M.X n))) ≤
        acyclicComplexSizeBound (C := C)) →
      ∀ f : M ⟶ I, Nonempty (Homotopy f 0)) :
    I.IsKInjective

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isKInjective_of_injective_of_small_boundedAbove_acyclic
declarations.doc:
A complex of injective objects in a Grothendieck abelian category is K-injective if every
map to it in the homotopy category from a uniformly small bounded-above acyclic complex is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_of_injective_of_small_boundedAbove_acyclic
    (I : CochainComplex C ℤ) [∀ n : ℤ, Injective (I.X n)]
    (hI : ∀ (M : CochainComplex C ℤ), M.Acyclic →
      (∃ a : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, a < n → IsZero (M.X n)) →
      (∀ n : ℤ, Cardinal.mk (Shrink.{w} (Subobject (M.X n))) ≤
        acyclicComplexSizeBound (C := C)) →
      ∀ f : (HomotopyCategory.quotient C (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M ⟶
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient C (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I, f = 0) :
    I.IsKInjective

declarations.doc:
