declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.weilRestriction_representableBy_closedImmersion_of_affineTests
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07AI.** The Weil restriction `f_* Y` of a closed subscheme `Y` of `X`
along a morphism `f : X ⟶ S` which is of finite presentation, flat and pure is represented by a
closed immersion `Z ⟶ S`.

By the equivalence
`Stacks.Flatness.WeilRestriction.isIsomorphismAfterBaseChange_iff_isIso_closedSubschemeBaseChange`
the functor is the isomorphism functor of the surjection `u : 𝒪_X ⟶ 𝒪_X/I` cutting out `Y`, whose
hypotheses in Tag 05PF are exactly the ones assumed here: `𝒪_X` is of finite type and of finite
presentation over itself, it is flat over `S` because `f` is flat, and it is pure relative to `S`
because `X` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem weilRestriction_representableBy_closedImmersion_of_affineTests
    (i : Y ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [Flat f]
    (hpure : AlgebraicGeometry.IsSchemePureRelative f) :
    ∃ W : Over S, IsClosedImmersion W.hom ∧
      Nonempty ((weilRestrictionFunctor i f).RepresentableBy W)
declarations.comment: representability by a closed immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.Flatness.finitePresentation_hom_of_representableBy_weilRestrictionFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07AI.** If the closed subscheme `Y` is of finite presentation over `S`,
every closed immersion representing the Weil restriction `f_* Y` is of finite presentation.

The quotient `𝒪_X/I` is then of finite presentation, by Tag 01TV and
`Stacks.Flatness.WeilRestriction.isFinitePresentation_pushforwardUnit`, which is the hypothesis
Tag 05PF's second assertion needs; the assertion itself is
`Stacks.Flatness.finitePresentation_hom_of_representableBy_isomorphismFunctor`, and needs no
flattening ideal.  Unlike the first assertion this one constructs no representative: it applies
to any representing closed immersion, and such a one exists by the first assertion.
declarations.statement:
theorem finitePresentation_hom_of_representableBy_weilRestrictionFunctor
    (i : Y ⟶ X) (f : X ⟶ S) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (hY : AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation (i ≫ f))
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (p : Z ⟶ S) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion p]
    (e : (weilRestrictionFunctor i f).RepresentableBy (Over.mk p)) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.FinitePresentation p
declarations.comment: finite presentation of the representing closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_lowerShriekStructureSheafHom_of_isClosedUnderAffineLine
declarations.doc:
Let `C₁ ⊆ C₂` be full subcategories of the big fppf category over a scheme `X`, let `C₁`
contain the base object `X/X` and the affine line over each of its objects, and let
`g : Sh(C₁) ⟶ Sh(C₂)` be the morphism of topoi of the inclusion. Then the canonical map
`g_!O₁ ⟶ O₂` from the lower shriek of the restricted structure sheaf to the structure sheaf is an
isomorphism.

The sheaf condition on the structure presheaf of `C₂` and the existence of `g_!`, a left adjoint
of the pushforward along the inclusion, are taken as hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lowerShriekStructureSheafHom_of_isClosedUnderAffineLine
    {P₁ P₂ : ObjectProperty (BigFppfOver B X hX)} (h₁₂ : P₁ ≤ P₂)
    (J₁ : GrothendieckTopology P₁.FullSubcategory)
    (J₂ : GrothendieckTopology P₂.FullSubcategory)
    (hsh : Presheaf.IsSheaf J₂ (P₂.ι.op ⋙ bigOverPresheafAb B X hX))
    [(ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h₁₂).IsContinuous J₁ J₂]
    [((ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h₁₂).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      AddCommGrpCat.{t} J₁ J₂).IsRightAdjoint]
    (hbase : P₁ (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hX)))) (hline : IsClosedUnderAffineLine P₁) :
    IsIso (lowerShriekStructureSheafHom h₁₂ J₁ J₂ hsh)
declarations.comment: part (b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.fullyFaithful_isContinuous_isCocontinuous_ιOfLE_baseOverTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AJ (a).** Let `τ` be any of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf
topologies, and let `C₁ ⊆ C₂` be full subcategories of the big category over `X`, each with the
topology it inherits from the big `τ`-site over `X`, both satisfying the closure condition (1)(a)
of the source. Then the inclusion `C₁ ⊆ C₂` is fully faithful, continuous and cocontinuous.

Full faithfulness holds for any inclusion of full subcategories; continuity and cocontinuity are
`AlgebraicGeometry.isContinuous_ιOfLE_baseOverTopology` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.isCocontinuous_ιOfLE_baseOverTopology`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fullyFaithful_isContinuous_isCocontinuous_ιOfLE_baseOverTopology (τ : CoveringTopology)
    {P₁ P₂ : ObjectProperty (BigFppfOver B X hX)} (h₁₂ : P₁ ≤ P₂)
    (hcov₁ : IsClosedUnderCoverings τ P₁) (hcov₂ : IsClosedUnderCoverings τ P₂) :
    (ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h₁₂).Full ∧ (ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h₁₂).Faithful ∧
      (ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h₁₂).IsContinuous
        (P₁.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B X hX τ.toSiteKind))
        (P₂.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B X hX τ.toSiteKind)) ∧
      (ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h₁₂).IsCocontinuous
        (P₁.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B X hX τ.toSiteKind))
        (P₂.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B X hX τ.toSiteKind))
declarations.comment: part (a), at the inherited topologies, for every τ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_lowerShriekStructureSheafHom_baseOverTopology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AJ (b).** Let `τ` be any of the Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic and fppf
topologies, and let `C₁ ⊆ C₂` be full subcategories of the big category over a scheme `X`, each
with the topology it inherits from the big `τ`-site over `X`, both satisfying the closure
condition (1)(a) of the source, and let `C₁` contain the base object `X/X` and the affine line
over each of its objects — conditions (2) and (1)(b). Writing `g : Sh(C₁) ⟶ Sh(C₂)` for the
morphism of topoi of the inclusion, the canonical map `g_!O₁ ⟶ O₂` from the lower shriek of the
restriction of the structure sheaf to the structure sheaf is an isomorphism.

The continuity of the inclusion that `g` and `g_!` refer to is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isContinuous_ιOfLE_baseOverTopology`; the existence of `g_!` is instance
search on the essential smallness of the two sites; the descent witness for the structure
presheaf of `C₂` is `AlgebraicGeometry.isSheaf_inheritedTopology_bigOverPresheafAb`. With those
three supplied, the assertion is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_lowerShriekStructureSheafHom_of_isClosedUnderAffineLine` read at the
inherited topologies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_lowerShriekStructureSheafHom_baseOverTopology (τ : CoveringTopology)
    {P₁ P₂ : ObjectProperty (BigFppfOver B X hX)} (h₁₂ : P₁ ≤ P₂)
    (hcov₁ : IsClosedUnderCoverings τ P₁) (hcov₂ : IsClosedUnderCoverings τ P₂)
    (hbase : P₁ (Over.mk (𝟙 (B.obj hX)))) (hline : IsClosedUnderAffineLine P₁) :
    letI : (ObjectProperty.ιOfLE h₁₂).IsContinuous
        (P₁.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B X hX τ.toSiteKind))
        (P₂.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B X hX τ.toSiteKind)) :=
      isContinuous_ιOfLE_baseOverTopology τ h₁₂ hcov₁
    IsIso (lowerShriekStructureSheafHom h₁₂
      (P₁.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B X hX τ.toSiteKind))
      (P₂.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.baseOverTopology B X hX τ.toSiteKind))
      (isSheaf_inheritedTopology_bigOverPresheafAb τ hcov₂))
declarations.comment: part (b), at the inherited topologies, for every τ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inclusionToposMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AK, the morphism of topoi.** Cocontinuity of the inclusion gives the adjoint pair
`g^{-1} ⊣ g_*` between the topos of the subcategory site and that of the ambient site, with
`g^{-1}` left exact: the morphism of topoi `g : Sh(𝒳'_τ) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_τ)` of the source.

The sheaves take values in `Type max v w`, which is the universe in which the sheaves of sets on
either site live.
declarations.statement:
def inclusionToposMorphism (τ : SiteKind) (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hclose : IsClosedUnderSitePullback B S hS p P τ) :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (P.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS p τ))
        (Type max v w))
      (Sheaf (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS p τ) (Type max v w))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi `g : Sh(𝒳'_τ) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_τ)` defined by the inclusion, whose inverse image is restriction to `𝒳'`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.subsite_cohomology_comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AK.** Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack over `S`, let `τ` be the étale or the fppf
topology, and let `𝒳' ⊆ 𝒳` be a full subcategory such that

1. if `x ⟶ x'` is a morphism of `𝒳` lying over a smooth (respectively flat and locally finitely
   presented) morphism of schemes and `x'` is in `𝒳'`, then `x` is in `𝒳'` — this is
   `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.IsClosedUnderSitePullback`, which also pins `τ` down to one of the two
   admissible topologies; and
2. there is an object `x` of `𝒳'` lying over a scheme `U` whose associated 1-morphism
   `x : (Sch/U)_fppf ⟶ 𝒳` is smooth and surjective.

Give `𝒳'` the topology whose coverings are the families of `𝒳'` that are coverings of `𝒳_τ`. Then
the inclusion `𝒳' ⟶ 𝒳_τ` is fully faithful, continuous and cocontinuous, so it defines a morphism
of topoi `g : Sh(𝒳'_τ) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_τ)` — `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.inclusionToposMorphism`, whose inverse
image is restriction to `𝒳'` — and `H^p(𝒳'_τ, g⁻¹ℱ) ≅ H^p(𝒳_τ, ℱ)` for all `p ≥ 0` and all abelian
sheaves `ℱ` on `𝒳_τ`, where on abelian sheaves `g⁻¹` is again restriction to `𝒳'`.

The isomorphism of cohomology groups is the natural isomorphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.subsiteCohomologyIsoOfAtlas`.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsite_cohomology_comparison :
    P.ι.Full ∧ P.ι.Faithful ∧
      P.ι.IsContinuous (P.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS
        𝒳.val.val.p τ)) (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p τ) ∧
      P.ι.IsCocontinuous (P.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS
        𝒳.val.val.p τ)) (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p τ) ∧
      (haveI := isContinuous_ι_associatedTopology_of_isClosedUnderSitePullback B S hS
          𝒳.val.val.p P τ 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids hcl;
        Nonempty ((inclusionToposMorphism B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p P τ 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
          hcl).inverseImage ≅ P.ι.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
            (P.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p τ))
            (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p τ))) ∧
      ∀ q : ℕ,
        haveI := isContinuous_ι_associatedTopology_of_isClosedUnderSitePullback B S hS
          𝒳.val.val.p P τ 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids hcl;
        Nonempty (P.ι.sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
            (P.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p τ))
            (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p τ) ⋙
          Sheaf.functorH.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u + 1}
            (P.ι.inheritedTopology (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p τ)) q ≅
          Sheaf.functorH.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u + 1}
            (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p τ) q)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fppfCovering_family_fibre_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AN.** Let `f j : 𝒳 j ⟶ 𝒴`, `j ∈ J`, be a family of 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks
over `S` which are each flat and locally of finite presentation and which are jointly surjective,
that is `|𝒴| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒳 j|)`. Then for every object `U` of the big fppf site of `S` and every
object `y` of the fibre of `𝒴` over `U` there are an fppf covering `{U i → U}_{i ∈ I}` of `U`, a
map `a : I → J` and, for every `i`, an object of `𝒳 (a i)` over `U i` whose image is isomorphic to
the restriction of `y` to `U i`.

The covering is given as a family of morphisms `m i : W i ⟶ U.left` of the underlying category of
the site which are flat, locally of finite presentation and jointly surjective on the underlying
schemes — which is what an fppf covering of `U` is. The isomorphism over a member is rendered as a
morphism from the image of the object to `y` lying over that member, which in a category fibred in
groupoids is exactly an isomorphism in the fibre.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fppfCovering_family_fibre_lift {J : Type v}
    {𝒳 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒳 j ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hflat : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (f j))
    (hlfp : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒴)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : 𝒴.val.val.p.Fiber U) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (W : I → B.Schemes) (m : ∀ i, W i ⟶ U.left) (a : I → J),
      (∀ i, Flat (B.inclusion.map (m i))) ∧
        (∀ i, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (B.inclusion.map (m i))) ∧
          (∀ x : (B.inclusion.obj U.left), ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (B.inclusion.map (m i))) ∧
            ∀ i, ∃ (x : (𝒳 (a i)).val.val.obj)
              (α : (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f (a i)).hom).obj x ⟶ y.1),
              𝒴.val.val.p.IsHomLift
                (Over.homMk (m i) rfl :
                  (Over.mk (m i ≫ U.hom) : BigFppfOver B S hS) ⟶ U) α
declarations.comment: the covering family and the index map

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fppfCovering_fibre_lift_of_family
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AN, with the covering as a covering sieve.** Under the hypotheses of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fppfCovering_family_fibre_lift` there is a covering sieve of `U`
for the big fppf topology of `S` such that over every arrow of it the object `y` is isomorphic to
the image of an object of `𝒳 j` for some `j`.

The index `j` is produced per arrow of the sieve rather than by a map out of the index set of a
covering family, since a sieve carries no family; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fppfCovering_family_fibre_lift` for the family form.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fppfCovering_fibre_lift_of_family {J : Type v}
    {𝒳 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒳 j ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hflat : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (f j))
    (hlfp : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒴)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (y : 𝒴.val.val.p.Fiber U) :
    ∃ R ∈ BigFppfOver.topology B S hS U,
      ∀ ⦃V : BigFppfOver B S hS⦄ ⦃k : V ⟶ U⦄, R.arrows k →
        ∃ (j : J) (x : (𝒳 j).val.val.obj)
          (α : (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f j).hom).obj x ⟶ y.1),
          𝒴.val.val.p.IsHomLift k α
declarations.comment: the covering sieve form

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.exists_fppfCovering_isQuasicoherentOnSite_restrictModuleToSmallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AP, its fppf-local half.** Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family of flat, locally
finitely presented 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` with `|𝒳| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒵 j|)`, let
`F` be a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_étale` and suppose every inverse image `f j^{-1} F` is
locally quasi-coherent. Then every object `x` of `𝒳` admits a family of arrows `φ i : y i ⟶ x`
lying over flat, locally finitely presented and jointly surjective morphisms of schemes, at every
member of which the restriction of `F` to the small étale site is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fppfCovering_isQuasicoherentOnSite_restrictModuleToSmallEtale {J : Type v}
    {𝒵 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hflat : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (f j))
    (hlfp : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{m} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)) F.presheaf)
    (hlqc : ∀ j, IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f j).hom ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS (f j).hom)
      ((stackModulePresheafPullback.{u, w, m} B S hS (f j)).obj F))
    (x : 𝒳.val.val.obj) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (y : I → 𝒳.val.val.obj) (φ : ∀ i, y i ⟶ x),
      (∀ i, Flat (B.inclusion.map (𝒳.val.val.p.map (φ i)).left)) ∧
        (∀ i, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (B.inclusion.map (𝒳.val.val.p.map (φ i)).left)) ∧
          (∀ t : B.inclusion.obj (𝒳.val.val.p.obj x).left,
            ∃ i, t ∈ Set.range (B.inclusion.map (𝒳.val.val.p.map (φ i)).left)) ∧
            ∀ i, (⟨restrictModuleToSmallEtale B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
                  𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (y i) (etaleTopology B)
                  (etaleTopology_le_topology B) F,
                restrictModuleToSmallEtale_isSheaf B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
                  𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (y i) F hF⟩ :
              SheafOfModules.{m} (SmallEtale.structureSheaf E
                (𝒳.val.val.p.obj (y i)).left.1
                (contains_base B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (y i)))).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: the fppf-local half: every object acquires a jointly surjective family of flat, locally finitely presented arrows at whose sources the small étale restriction of the module is quasi-coherent, via the fppf-local factorisation of Stacks 07AN

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_isFlat_isLfp_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AP.** Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family of flat (**Stacks 06PW**) and locally
finitely presented (**Stacks 06Q2**) 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` with
`|𝒳| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒵 j|)` (**Stacks 04XG**), and let `F` be a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on
`𝒳_fppf`. If every inverse image `f j^{-1} F` is locally quasi-coherent (**Stacks 06WJ**), then
so is `F`.

The étale sheaf condition follows from the fppf one. At an object `x` lying over `U`, the
restriction `x^*F|_{U_étale}` is quasi-coherent because it is cartesian between affine objects
(Descent, Proposition 03DX), which through the index functor of **Stacks 06W1** is the cartesian
condition for `F` along arrows lying over étale morphisms of affine schemes, proved by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isIso_restrictionBaseChange_of_isFlat_isLfp_jointlySurjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasicoherent_of_isFlat_isLfp_jointlySurjective {J : Type v}
    {𝒵 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hflat : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (f j))
    (hlfp : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology) F.presheaf)
    (hlqc : ∀ j, IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f j).hom ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS (f j).hom)
      ((stackModulePresheafPullback.{u, w, u} B S hS (f j)).obj F)) :
    IsLocallyQuasicoherent B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isLocallyQuasicoherentWithFlatBaseChange_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AQ, part (1), the local quasi-coherence half.** Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family
of smooth 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks over `S` with `|𝒳| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒵 j|)`, and let `F`
be a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_étale`. If every inverse image `f j^{-1} F` lies in
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_{𝒵 j})` and `F` has the flat base change property, then `F` lies in
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.

Local quasi-coherence of `F` is **Stacks 075Y**, applied to the local quasi-coherence of the
inverse images. The flat base change property of `F` is the hypothesis `hfbc`: the source deduces
it from **Stacks 0764** part (3), whose argument is not available for the presheaf-level inverse
image that the flat base change property is formulated with here; see the implementation notes of
this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasicoherentWithFlatBaseChange_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
    {J : Type v} {𝒵 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳)
    (hsmooth : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B)).obj)
    (hF : Presheaf.IsSheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)) F.presheaf)
    (hfbc : HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
      (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B) F)
    (hlqc : ∀ j, IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithFlatBaseChange B E h S hS
      (CatFiberedInGroupoids.homFunctor (f j).hom ⋙ 𝒳.val.val.p)
      (isFiberedInGroupoids_homFunctor_comp B S hS (f j).hom)
      ((stackModulePresheafPullback.{u, w, u} B S hS (f j)).obj F)) :
    IsLocallyQuasicoherentWithFlatBaseChange B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
      F
declarations.comment: part (1), the local quasi-coherence half: the criterion along a jointly surjective family of smooth morphisms, with the flat base change property of the source assumed (Stacks 0764 part (3))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AQ**, part (1). Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family of smooth 1-morphisms of
algebraic stacks with `|𝒳| = ⋃ |f j|(|𝒵 j|)`, and `F` a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_ét`. If
every `f j^{-1} F` is in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_{𝒵 j})`, then `F` is in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.

The source's hypothesis reads `LQCoh^{fpc}`, a misprint for `LQCoh^{fbc}`. `LQCoh^fbc` is the
sheaf-level one (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules`), with the flat base change
property of **Stacks 0762**; the module sections are in the universe of the schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
    {J : Type v} {𝒵 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳) (hsmooth : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : StackModules B S hS .etale 𝒳)
    (hF : ∀ j, lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS (𝒵 j)
      ((stackModuleInverseImage B S hS .etale (f j)).obj F)) :
    lqcohSheafFbcEtaleModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F
declarations.comment: part (1), on Mod(𝒳_ét, 𝒪_𝒳), with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; the module sections in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_of_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AQ**, part (2). Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family of flat and locally finitely
presented 1-morphisms of algebraic stacks with `|𝒳| = ⋃ |f j|(|𝒵 j|)`, and `F` a sheaf of
`𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_fppf`. If every `f j^{-1} F` is in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_{𝒵 j})`, then `F` is in
`LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`.

`LQCoh^fbc` is the sheaf-level one (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules`), with the
flat base change property of **Stacks 0762**; the module sections are in the universe of the
schemes. The proof is the source's ("analogous to the proof of 07AP"), carried out for a general
module rule in
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.mem_of_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_jointlySurjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules_of_isFlat_isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_jointlySurjective
    {J : Type v} {𝒵 : J → AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS} {𝒳 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS}
    (f : ∀ j, 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳) (hflat : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (f j))
    (hlfp : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (F : fppfModules B S hS 𝒳)
    (hF : ∀ j, lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS (𝒵 j)
      ((fppfModulesPullback B S hS (f j)).obj F)) :
    lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳 F
declarations.comment: part (2), on Mod(𝒪_𝒳) (fppf), with the flat base change property of 0762 read on sheaves; the module sections in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isParasitic_iff_isZero_pullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AR** (1). A sheaf of modules on the étale site of an algebraic stack which has the
flat base change property of **Stacks 0762** is parasitic exactly when its pullback along the
lisse-étale morphism of ringed topoi of **Stacks 0788** (1) vanishes.

The pullback is restriction to the smooth objects
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.modulePullbackIso`), so the right-hand side says that the
sections of `F` vanish at every smooth object. A smooth object is flat, which gives one
implication with no hypothesis; the converse is where the flat base change property is used, to
carry the vanishing along a flat arrow out of an object covering a given flat object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isParasitic_iff_isZero_pullbackModules
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u + 1, u, u}
      (etaleRingedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).O))
    (hfbc : HasFlatBaseChangeProperty B E h S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids
      (etaleTopology B) (etaleTopology_le_topology B) F.val) :
    IsParasitic.{u, w, u} B S hS 𝒳 .etale F.val ↔
      IsZero ((RingedToposHom.pullbackModules.{u, u, u, u + 1, u, u + 1}
        (ringedToposModulesHom.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (1), the lisse-étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isParasitic_iff_isZero_pullbackModules_lisseEtale_and_flatFppf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AR, the whole statement.** For an algebraic stack `𝒳`:

* (1) a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules `F` on `𝒳_étale` with the flat base change property of
  **Stacks 0762** is parasitic exactly when `g^*F = 0` for the lisse-étale morphism of ringed
  topoi of **Stacks 0788** (1); and
* (2) a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules `G` on `𝒳_fppf` is parasitic exactly when `g^*G = 0` for the
  flat-fppf morphism of ringed topoi of **Stacks 0788** (2), with no hypothesis.

The two conjuncts are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isParasitic_iff_isZero_pullbackModules` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isParasitic_iff_isZero_pullbackModules`.
declarations.comment: the whole statement: parts (1) and (2) conjoined

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isParasitic_iff_isZero_pullbackModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AR** (2). A sheaf of modules on the fppf site of an algebraic stack is parasitic
exactly when its pullback along the flat-fppf morphism of ringed topoi of **Stacks 0788** (2)
vanishes.

The flat-fppf site has the flat objects of `𝒳` for its objects, and the pullback along `g` is
restriction to them (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.modulePullbackIso`), so the two conditions
are the same condition read on the two sites.
declarations.comment: part (2), the flat-fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.abelianLowerShriek_derived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AS (1)**, all three assertions, for every algebraic stack and with NO hypothesis.
For `g : Sh(𝒳_{lisse,étale}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_{étale})` the comparison morphism of topoi of
**Stacks 0788** (1):

* the functor `g_! : Ab(𝒳_{lisse,étale}) ⥤ Ab(𝒳_{étale})` has a left derived functor
  `Lg_! : D(𝒳_{lisse,étale}) ⟶ D(𝒳_{étale})` — degreewise `g_!` followed by the localization of
  the homotopy category of `Ab(𝒳_{étale})` has a pointwise left derived functor along the
  localization of the homotopy category of `Ab(𝒳_{lisse,étale})`, and `Lg_!` is that total left
  derived functor;
* `Lg_!` is left adjoint to `g⁻¹`, by an adjunction whose unit is an isomorphism;
* `g⁻¹ ∘ Lg_! = id`.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianLowerShriek_derived :
    haveI := isContinuous_inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    haveI := isCocontinuous_inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    haveI := abelianLowerShriek_additive.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
    ((abelianLowerShriek.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳
        (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh).HasPointwiseLeftDerivedFunctor
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
        (Sheaf (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) AbCat.{u, u + 1}) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
    (∃ adj : derivedAbelianLowerShriek.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ⊣
        derivedAbelianRestriction.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳, IsIso adj.unit) ∧
    Nonempty (derivedAbelianLowerShriek.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ⋙
        derivedAbelianRestriction.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ≅
      𝟭 (DerivedCategory (Sheaf (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) AbCat.{u, u + 1})))
declarations.comment: part (1), the whole of it: existence of the unbounded left derived functor `Lg_!` of `g_!` on abelian sheaves for the lisse-étale site, its adjunction `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹` (with invertible unit), and `g⁻¹ ∘ Lg_! = id`, for every algebraic stack, with no hypothesis. The acyclicity statement of Tag 07AC is proved, as `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.abelianLowerShriekAcyclic`, and the invertibility of the ordinary unit is Tag 077I

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.abelianLowerShriek_derived

**Stacks 0788** (2):

* the functor `g_! : Ab(𝒳_{flat,fppf}) ⥤ Ab(𝒳_{fppf})` has a left derived functor
  `Lg_! : D(𝒳_{flat,fppf}) ⟶ D(𝒳_{fppf})` — degreewise `g_!` followed by the localization of the
  homotopy category of `Ab(𝒳_{fppf})` has a pointwise left derived functor along the localization
  of the homotopy category of `Ab(𝒳_{flat,fppf})`, and `Lg_!` is that total left derived functor;
* `Lg_!` is left adjoint to `g⁻¹`, by an adjunction whose unit is an isomorphism;

    haveI := isContinuous_inclusion B S hS 𝒳 flatClosure

        DerivedCategory.Qh).HasPointwiseLeftDerivedFunctor
      (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
        (Sheaf (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) AbCat.{u, u + 1}) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ∧
    (∃ adj : derivedAbelianLowerShriekFunctor B S hS 𝒳 ⊣ derivedAbelianRestriction B S hS 𝒳,
      IsIso adj.unit) ∧
    Nonempty (derivedAbelianLowerShriekFunctor B S hS 𝒳 ⋙ derivedAbelianRestriction B S hS 𝒳 ≅
      𝟭 (DerivedCategory (Sheaf (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) AbCat.{u, u + 1})))
declarations.comment: part (3), the whole of it: existence of the unbounded left derived functor `Lg_!` of `g_!` on abelian sheaves for the flat-fppf site, its adjunction `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹` (with invertible unit), and `g⁻¹ ∘ Lg_! = id`, for every algebraic stack, with no hypothesis. declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.lowerShriekModules_derived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AS (4)**, all three assertions, for every algebraic stack and with NO
hypothesis.  For `g : Sh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}) ⟶ Sh(𝒳_τ)` the morphism of ringed topoi of
**Stacks 0788**:

* the functor `g_! : Mod(𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}}) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` has a left derived functor
  `Lg_! : D(𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}}) ⟶ D(𝒪_𝒳)` — degreewise `g_!` followed by the localization of the
  homotopy category of `Mod(𝒪_𝒳)` has a pointwise left derived functor along the localization of
  the homotopy category of `Mod(𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}})`, and `Lg_!` is that total left derived functor;
* `Lg_!` is left adjoint to `g^*`, by an adjunction whose unit is an isomorphism;
* `g^* ∘ Lg_! = id`.

The structure sheaf is the one of **Stacks 06TV**, with sections in `Type u`, and the modules
have their sections in `Type (u+1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem lowerShriekModules_derived :
    (FreeRingUniverse.lowerShriekOnHomotopy.{u + 1} (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
        (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology) (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι
        (moduleRing B S hS 𝒳) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Qh).HasPointwiseLeftDerivedFunctor
        (FreeRingUniverse.sourceQuasiIso.{u + 1} (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
        (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology) (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳).ι
        (moduleRing B S hS 𝒳)) ∧
    (∃ adj : derivedLowerShriekModules B S hS 𝒳 ⊣ derivedRestrictionModules B S hS 𝒳,
      IsIso adj.unit) ∧
    Nonempty (derivedLowerShriekModules B S hS 𝒳 ⋙ derivedRestrictionModules B S hS 𝒳 ≅
      𝟭 (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (subsiteModuleRingFlat B S hS 𝒳))))
declarations.comment: part (4), the whole of it: existence of the unbounded left derived functor `Lg_!` of `g_!` on sheaves of modules for the flat-fppf site, its adjunction `Lg_! ⊣ g^*` (with invertible unit), and `g^* ∘ Lg_! = id`, for every algebraic stack, with no hypothesis. The structure sheaf is the one of Tag 06TV; the acyclicity statement of Tag 07AC is proved, as `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.subsiteLowerShriekModulesAcyclic`, and the invertibility of the ordinary unit is Tag 077I

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.siteFunctor
declarations.doc:
The restriction of a flat 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks over `S` to a functor
between the flat-fppf sites, specified by the property that its composite with the inclusion of
the flat objects of `𝒴` is the inclusion of those of `𝒳` followed by the underlying functor of
`f`.
declarations.comment: the functor of flat-fppf sites along a flat 1-morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.siteFunctor_isContinuous
declarations.doc: The restriction of a flat 1-morphism to the flat-fppf sites is continuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem siteFunctor_isContinuous (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f) :
    (siteFunctor B S hS f hf).1.IsContinuous
      (topology B S hS 𝒳) (topology B S hS 𝒴)
declarations.comment: that functor is continuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.siteFunctor_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc: The restriction of a flat 1-morphism to the flat-fppf sites is cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
theorem siteFunctor_isCocontinuous (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f) :
    (siteFunctor B S hS f hf).1.IsCocontinuous
      (topology B S hS 𝒳) (topology B S hS 𝒴)
declarations.comment: that functor is cocontinuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.siteFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (1), the site functor. A smooth 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks
over `S` restricts to a functor between the lisse-étale sites, specified by the property that its
composite with the inclusion of the smooth objects of `𝒴` is the inclusion of those of `𝒳`
followed by the underlying functor of `f`.

The restriction exists because `f` carries smooth objects to smooth objects
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.smoothObject_map`), and that equality of composites is what
says its action on objects and arrows is the action of `f`.
declarations.comment: the functor of lisse-etale sites along a smooth 1-morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.siteFunctor_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (1), continuity. The restriction of a smooth 1-morphism to the lisse-étale
sites is continuous: its composite with the inclusion of `𝒴` is, and continuity descends along
that inclusion, which is fully faithful and cocontinuous by **Stacks 0788** (1).
declarations.statement:
theorem siteFunctor_isContinuous (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    (siteFunctor.{u, w} B S hS f hf).1.IsContinuous
      (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)
declarations.comment: that functor is continuous, in the smooth case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.siteFunctor_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (1), cocontinuity. The same descent, with the roles of continuity and
cocontinuity of the inclusion exchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem siteFunctor_isCocontinuous (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    (siteFunctor.{u, w} B S hS f hf).1.IsCocontinuous
      (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)
declarations.comment: that functor is cocontinuous, in the smooth case

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.primedPushforwardAmbientEquiv'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT (2), the identity `f'_*(g')^{-1} = g^{-1}f_*`, at one flat object of `𝒴` and
for a sheaf of sets, with no further hypothesis.** For a flat 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic
stacks, a flat object `y` of `𝒴` and a sheaf `ℱ` of sets on the fppf site of `𝒳`, the value at
`y` of the pushforward along the restriction `f'` of `f` to the flat-fppf sites of the restriction
of `ℱ` to the flat-fppf site of `𝒳` is the value at `y` of the pushforward of `ℱ` along `f`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.primedPushforwardAmbientEquiv` at the topology of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ambientTwoFibreProductTopology`, whose three remaining inputs are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_comp_ambientProjection`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.hasLocalFactorizations_primedInclusion` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.hasLocallyConnectedFactorizations_primedInclusion`.
declarations.statement:
def primedPushforwardAmbientEquiv' (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS f)
    (y : FlatFppf B S hS 𝒴) (ℱ : (𝒳.val.val.obj)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1))
    (hℱ : Presieve.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p .fppf) ℱ) :
    ((primedSiteFunctor B S hS f hf).op.ran.obj ((inclusion B S hS 𝒳).op ⋙ ℱ)).obj (op y) ≃
      (f.hom.hom.toFunctor.op.ran.obj ℱ).obj (op y.obj)
declarations.comment: part (2), the identity `f'_*(g')^{-1} = g^{-1}f_*` for the flat-fppf site, at one flat object `y` of `𝒴` and for a sheaf of sets, with NO hypothesis beyond the sheaf condition on `ℱ`: the topology on the 2-fibre product `V ×_{y, 𝒴} 𝒳` that `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.primedPushforwardAmbientEquiv` takes as `J` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ambientTwoFibreProductTopology`, and its arguments `hℱ`, `hfac` and `hconn` are the theorems `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_comp_ambientProjection`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.hasLocalFactorizations_primedInclusion` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.hasLocallyConnectedFactorizations_primedInclusion`, each proved for every algebraic stack. The site functor itself and its continuity and cocontinuity, which are the first assertion of the tag, are registered in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/FlatFppfSiteFunctor.lean`. Three pieces of the tag are not covered here: naturality of the bijection in `y`, so that it becomes an equality of sheaves on `𝒴_{flat,fppf}` rather than a family of bijections; the same identity at abelian rather than set coefficients; and the second identity `g'_!(f')^{-1} = f^{-1}g_!`. The first and the third are registered in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/SubsiteSheafPushforwardBaseChange.lean`; the abelian form is claimed nowhere in the tree, and the tag does not ask for it -- the source's `ℱ` is a sheaf of sets, which is what the functors of a morphism of topoi act on

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.primedPushforwardAmbientEquiv'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT (1), the identity `f'_*(g')^{-1} = g^{-1}f_*`, at one smooth object of `𝒴` and
for a sheaf of sets, with no further hypothesis.** For a smooth 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of
algebraic stacks, a smooth object `y` of `𝒴` and a sheaf `ℱ` of sets on the étale site of `𝒳`,
the value at `y` of the pushforward along the restriction `f'` of `f` to the lisse-étale sites of
the restriction of `ℱ` to the lisse-étale site of `𝒳` is the value at `y` of the pushforward of
`ℱ` along `f`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.primedPushforwardAmbientEquiv` at the topology of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ambientTwoFibreProductTopology`, whose three remaining inputs are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_comp_ambientProjection`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.hasLocalFactorizations_primedInclusion` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.hasLocallyConnectedFactorizations_primedInclusion`.
declarations.statement:
def primedPushforwardAmbientEquiv' (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f)
    (y : LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴) (ℱ : (𝒳.val.val.obj)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1))
    (hℱ : Presieve.IsSheaf (BigFppfOver.associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p .etale) ℱ) :
    ((primedSiteFunctor.{u, w} B S hS f hf).op.ran.obj
        ((inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳).op ⋙ ℱ)).obj (op y) ≃

declarations.comment: part (1), the identity `f'_*(g')^{-1} = g^{-1}f_*` for the lisse-étale site, at one smooth object `y` of `𝒴` and for a sheaf of sets, with NO hypothesis beyond the sheaf condition on `ℱ`: the topology on the 2-fibre product `V ×_{y, 𝒴} 𝒳` that `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.primedPushforwardAmbientEquiv` takes as `J` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ambientTwoFibreProductTopology`, and its arguments `hℱ`, `hfac` and `hconn` are the theorems `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isSheaf_comp_ambientProjection`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.hasLocalFactorizations_primedInclusion` and `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.hasLocallyConnectedFactorizations_primedInclusion`, each proved for every algebraic stack. The site functor itself and its continuity and cocontinuity, which are the first assertion of the tag, are registered in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/LisseEtaleSiteFunctor.lean`. Three pieces of the tag are not covered here: naturality of the bijection in `y`, so that it becomes an equality of sheaves on `𝒴_{lisse,étale}` rather than a family of bijections; the same identity at abelian rather than set coefficients; and the second identity `g'_!(f')^{-1} = f^{-1}g_!`. The first and the third are registered in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/SubsiteSheafPushforwardBaseChange.lean`; the abelian form is claimed nowhere in the tree, and the tag does not ask for it -- the source's `ℱ` is a sheaf of sets, which is what the functors of a morphism of topoi act on

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.siteFunctorRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (1), clause (d). **The restriction `f'` of a smooth 1-morphism to the
lisse-étale sites is a morphism of ringed topoi.** Its inverse image is restriction along the site
functor, and its structure map is the canonical identification of the two lisse-étale structure
sheaves: both are restrictions of the structure sheaf of **Stacks 06TV** of the base, along the
two composites of the square, which agree on the nose.
declarations.statement:
def siteFunctorRingedToposHom (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    RingedToposHom
      (ringedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳))
      (ringedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴))
declarations.comment: part (1), clause (d): the restriction `f'` of a smooth 1-morphism to the lisse-étale sites is a morphism of ringed topoi, at the universe in which the structure sheaf of Stacks 06TV takes its sections. Its structure map is the canonical identification of the two restricted structure sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isIso_fSharpInverseImage_siteFunctorRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (1), clause (d). The structure map of `f'` is an isomorphism: it is the
canonical identification of the two restricted structure sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_fSharpInverseImage_siteFunctorRingedToposHom (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴)
    (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    IsIso (siteFunctorRingedToposHom.{u, w} B S hS f hf).fSharpInverseImage
declarations.comment: part (1), clause (d): the structure map of `f'` on the lisse-étale sites is an isomorphism, so `f'` is a flat morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.ringedSquareTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (1), clause (e). **The square of ringed topoi 2-commutes**: the composite
`g' ∘ f'` and the composite `f ∘ g` are 2-isomorphic as morphisms of ringed topoi
`(Sh(𝒳_{lisse,étale}), O) ⟶ (Sh(𝒴_{étale}), O)`.

The 2-isomorphism is the adjoint mate of the canonical morphism of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.ringedSquare_inverseImage_eq`: the two ways around the square
restrict along the same functor of sites, so their inverse images are *equal*, and every structure
map in sight is the restriction comparison followed by an equality of structure sheaves, hence a
transport. Compatibility of the mate with the structure maps is then automatic, both sides of it
being transports between the same two objects.
declarations.statement:
def ringedSquareTwoIso (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴) (hf : AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    RingedToposHom.TwoIso
      (A := ringedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳))
      (B := etaleRingedTopos.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)
      (ringedSquareDownAcross.{u, w} B S hS f)
      (ringedSquareAcrossDown.{u, w} B S hS f hf)
declarations.comment: part (1), clause (e): the square of ringed topoi formed by `f`, its restriction `f'` to the lisse-étale sites and the two inclusions `g`, `g'` of Stacks 0788 2-commutes. The invertible 2-morphism is the adjoint mate of the canonical morphism of the equality of the two inverse images

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.siteFunctorRingedToposHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (2), clause (d). **The restriction `f'` of a flat 1-morphism to the flat-fppf
sites is a morphism of ringed topoi.** Its inverse image is restriction along the site functor,
and its structure map is the canonical identification of the two flat-fppf structure sheaves.

declarations.comment: part (2), clause (d): the restriction `f'` of a flat 1-morphism to the flat-fppf sites is a morphism of ringed topoi, at the universe in which the structure sheaf of Stacks 06TV takes its sections. Its structure map is the canonical identification of the two restricted structure sheaves

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_fSharpInverseImage_siteFunctorRingedToposHom
declarations.doc: **Stacks 07AT** (2), clause (d). The structure map of `f'` is an isomorphism.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.ringedSquareTwoIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (2), clause (e). **The square of ringed topoi 2-commutes**: `g' ∘ f'` and

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isIso_sheafBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (1), the identity `f'_*(g')^{-1} = g^{-1}f_*`. For a smooth 1-morphism
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks, the canonical map of Sites, Section 06UM from the restriction
along the inclusion `g` of the lisse-étale site of `𝒴` of the pushforward along `f`, to the
pushforward along the restriction `f'` of the restriction along the inclusion `g'` of the
lisse-étale site of `𝒳`, is an isomorphism of functors on sheaves of sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafBaseChange :
    IsIso (SubsitePushforward.subsiteSheafBaseChange.{_, _, _, _, u + 1} f.hom.hom.toFunctor
      (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (smoothObject_map.{u, w} B S hS f hf)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
      (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)
      (isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_homFunctor_associatedTopology B S hS f
        (etaleTopology B)).2
      (isCocontinuous_subsiteFunctor_topology.{u, w} B S hS f hf)
      (isContinuous_inclusion_topology'.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
      (isContinuous_inclusion_topology'.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴))
declarations.comment: part (1), the identity `f'_*(g')^{-1} = g^{-1}f_*` for the lisse-étale site, on sheaves of sets and natural in the object of the lisse-étale site of `𝒴`: the canonical map of Sites, Section 06UM, which is `CategoryTheory.SubsitePushforward.subsiteRanBaseChange` at the square of `f`, its restriction `f'` and the two inclusions, is invertible. The site functor and its continuity and cocontinuity are registered in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/LisseEtaleSiteFunctor.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.shriekBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (1), the identity `g'_!(f')^{-1} = f^{-1}g_!`. It is the conjugate of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isIso_sheafBaseChange` along the adjointness of `f^{-1}` and
`f_*`, of `g_!` and `g^{-1}`, and of their primed versions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def shriekBaseChangeIso :
    letI := (isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_homFunctor_associatedTopology B S hS f
      (etaleTopology B)).1
    letI := (isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_homFunctor_associatedTopology B S hS f
      (etaleTopology B)).2
    letI := isContinuous_subsiteFunctor_topology.{u, w} B S hS f hf
    letI := isCocontinuous_subsiteFunctor_topology.{u, w} B S hS f hf
    (SubsitePushforward.subsiteFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
          (smoothObject_map.{u, w} B S hS f hf)).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
          (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴) ⋙
        setsShriek B S hS 𝒳 ≅
      setsShriek B S hS 𝒴 ⋙ f.hom.hom.toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
        (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
declarations.comment: part (1), the identity `g'_!(f')^{-1} = f^{-1}g_!` for the lisse-étale site, on sheaves of sets: the conjugate of the first identity along the four adjunctions, exactly as the source derives it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_sheafBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (2), the identity `f'_*(g')^{-1} = g^{-1}f_*`. For a flat 1-morphism
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks, the canonical map of Sites, Section 06UM from the restriction
along the inclusion `g` of the flat-fppf site of `𝒴` of the pushforward along `f`, to the
pushforward along the restriction `f'` of the restriction along the inclusion `g'` of the
flat-fppf site of `𝒳`, is an isomorphism of functors on sheaves of sets.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sheafBaseChange :
    IsIso (SubsitePushforward.subsiteSheafBaseChange.{_, _, _, _, u + 1} f.hom.hom.toFunctor
      (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳) (flatObject_map B S hS f hf)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
      (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p B.topology)
      (topology B S hS 𝒳) (topology B S hS 𝒴)
      (isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_homFunctor_associatedTopology B S hS f B.topology).2
      (isCocontinuous_subsiteFunctor_topology B S hS f hf)
      (isContinuous_inclusion_topology B S hS 𝒳)
      (isContinuous_inclusion_topology B S hS 𝒴))
declarations.comment: part (2), the identity `f'_*(g')^{-1} = g^{-1}f_*` for the flat-fppf site, on sheaves of sets and natural in the object of the flat-fppf site of `𝒴`: the canonical map of Sites, Section 06UM, which is `CategoryTheory.SubsitePushforward.subsiteRanBaseChange` at the square of `f`, its restriction `f'` and the two inclusions, is invertible. The site functor and its continuity and cocontinuity are registered in `StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Stacks/FlatFppfSiteFunctor.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.shriekBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AT** (2), the identity `g'_!(f')^{-1} = f^{-1}g_!`. It is the conjugate of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_sheafBaseChange` along the adjointness of `f^{-1}` and
`f_*`, of `g_!` and `g^{-1}`, and of their primed versions. The two lower-shriek adjunctions are
the ones of **Stacks 0788** already in the tree.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def shriekBaseChangeIso :
    letI := (isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_homFunctor_associatedTopology B S hS f
      B.topology).1
    letI := (isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_homFunctor_associatedTopology B S hS f
      B.topology).2

    letI := isCocontinuous_subsiteFunctor_topology B S hS f hf

          (flatObject_map B S hS f hf)).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
          (topology B S hS 𝒳) (topology B S hS 𝒴) ⋙
        setsShriek B S hS 𝒳 ≅
      setsShriek B S hS 𝒴 ⋙ f.hom.hom.toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))

        (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p B.topology)
declarations.comment: part (2), the identity `g'_!(f')^{-1} = f^{-1}g_!` for the flat-fppf site, on sheaves of sets: the conjugate of the first identity along the four adjunctions, exactly as the source derives it

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SubsitePushforward.subsitePushforwardSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AU**, equation 103.15.1.1. Let `f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴` be a 1-morphism of categories over a
base `𝒞` with `𝒴` fibred in groupoids, and let `𝒳' ⊆ 𝒳` and `𝒴' ⊆ 𝒴` be full subcategories such
that `f` carries `𝒳'` into `𝒴'`, so that it restricts to `f' : 𝒳' ⥤ 𝒴'`. Then for a presheaf
`ℋ` on `𝒳'` and an object `y` of `𝒴'` lying over `V : 𝒞`,

`f'_*ℋ(y) = Γ((V ×_{y, 𝒴} 𝒳)', (pr')^{-1}ℋ)`,

where `f'_*` is the right Kan extension along `f'.op`, the primed 2-fibre product is the full
subcategory of `V ×_{y, 𝒴} 𝒳` whose objects have their `𝒳`-component in `𝒳'`, and `(pr')^{-1}`
is restriction along the projection `pr'` to `𝒳'`.

This is the source's equation for the lisse-étale and the flat-fppf site: no property of the
subcategories beyond fullness is used, and neither the topologies nor their closure conditions
enter the identification.
declarations.statement:
def subsitePushforwardSectionsEquiv (p𝒳 : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞) (p𝒴 : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒞) (f : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒴) (P : ObjectProperty 𝒳)
    {Q : ObjectProperty 𝒴} (hPQ : ∀ x : P.FullSubcategory, Q (f.obj x.obj))
    (h𝒴 : p𝒴.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hf : f ⋙ p𝒴 = p𝒳) (c : p𝒴.ChoiceOfPullbacks)
    (y : Q.FullSubcategory) (ℋ : (P.FullSubcategory)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
    [∀ G : (P.FullSubcategory)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w,
      (subsiteFunctor f P hPQ).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G]
    [∀ G : (P.FullSubcategory)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w, (P.ι ⋙ f).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension G] :
    ((subsiteFunctor f P hPQ).op.ran.obj ℋ).obj (op y) ≃
      Presheaf.globalSections ((primedProjection p𝒳 p𝒴 f P c y).op ⋙ ℋ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.sheafPrimedPushforwardSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AU, the flat-fppf case**, equation 103.15.1.1. Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a flat
1-morphism of algebraic stacks, let `ℋ` be a sheaf of sets on the flat-fppf site of `𝒳` and let
`y` be a flat object of `𝒴` lying over the scheme `V`. The direct image of `ℋ` along the morphism
of flat-fppf topoi induced by `f` has

`f'_*ℋ(y) = Γ((V ×_{y, 𝒴} 𝒳)', (pr')^{-1}ℋ)`,

the global sections of `ℋ` restricted along the projection `pr'` of the primed 2-fibre product.
The direct image is `CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous` along the site functor
of **Stacks 07AT**, whose cocontinuity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.siteFunctor_isCocontinuous`.
declarations.statement:
def sheafPrimedPushforwardSectionsEquiv (y : FlatFppf B S hS 𝒴)
    (ℋ : Sheaf (topology B S hS 𝒳) (Type a))
    [∀ F : (FlatFppf B S hS 𝒳)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type a,
      (primedSiteFunctor B S hS f hf).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    [∀ F : (FlatFppf B S hS 𝒳)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type a,
      (inclusion B S hS 𝒳 ⋙ f.hom.hom.toFunctor).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] :
    letI : (primedSiteFunctor B S hS f hf).IsCocontinuous
        (topology B S hS 𝒳) (topology B S hS 𝒴) :=
      siteFunctor_isCocontinuous B S hS f hf
    ((((primedSiteFunctor B S hS f hf).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type a)
        (topology B S hS 𝒳) (topology B S hS 𝒴)).obj ℋ).obj.obj (op y)) ≃
      Presheaf.globalSections ((primedProjection B S hS f y).op ⋙ ℋ.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.sheafPrimedPushforwardSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AU, the lisse-étale case**, equation 103.15.1.1. Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a smooth
1-morphism of algebraic stacks, let `ℋ` be a sheaf of sets on the lisse-étale site of `𝒳` and let
`y` be a smooth object of `𝒴` lying over the scheme `V`. The direct image of `ℋ` along the
morphism of lisse-étale topoi induced by `f` has

`f'_*ℋ(y) = Γ((V ×_{y, 𝒴} 𝒳)', (pr')^{-1}ℋ)`,

the global sections of `ℋ` restricted along the projection `pr'` of the primed 2-fibre product.
The direct image is `CategoryTheory.Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous` along the site functor
of **Stacks 07AT**, whose cocontinuity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.siteFunctor_isCocontinuous`.
declarations.statement:
def sheafPrimedPushforwardSectionsEquiv (y : LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)
    (ℋ : Sheaf (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (Type a))
    [∀ F : (LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type a,
      (primedSiteFunctor.{u, w} B S hS f hf).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F]
    [∀ F : (LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type a,
      (inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 ⋙ f.hom.hom.toFunctor).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F] :
    letI : (primedSiteFunctor.{u, w} B S hS f hf).IsCocontinuous
        (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴) :=
      siteFunctor_isCocontinuous.{u, w} B S hS f hf
    ((((primedSiteFunctor.{u, w} B S hS f hf).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type a)
        (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) (topology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)).obj ℋ).obj.obj (op y)) ≃
      Presheaf.globalSections ((primedProjection B S hS f y).op ⋙ ℋ.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedRestrictionBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AV, first identity, for abelian sheaves on the flat-fppf sites:
`g⁻¹ ∘ Rf_* = Rf'_* ∘ (g')⁻¹`.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a flat 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, `Rf_*`
and `Rf'_*` total right derived functors of the direct images along `f` and along its restriction
`f'` to the flat-fppf sites, and `g⁻¹`, `(g')⁻¹` restriction of abelian sheaves to the
flat-fppf sites of `𝒴` and `𝒳`. Then, on the unbounded derived categories,

`(g')⁻¹ ⋙ Rf'_* ≅ Rf_* ⋙ g⁻¹`.

No hypothesis is made beyond the right derived functor properties of `Rf_*` and `Rf'_*` (a right
derived functor being determined only up to unique isomorphism). The isomorphism is
`Stacks.Cohomology.UnboundedComplexes.derivedBaseChangeIsoOfUnit` at the degree-zero
identification `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_abelianSheafBaseChange` and at
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isIso_derivedPushforwardUnit_restriction`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedRestrictionBaseChangeIso
    (Rf : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p B.topology)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
    (Rf' : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒴) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
    (αf : haveI := (isContinuous_and_isCocontinuous_homFunctor B S hS f).2
      haveI : (f.hom.hom.toFunctor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p B.topology)).Additive :=
        Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous_additive.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u, u + 1} _ _ _
      (f.hom.hom.toFunctor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology)
          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p B.topology)).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rf)
    (αf' : haveI := isCocontinuous_subsiteFunctor B S hS f hf
      haveI : ((SubsitePushforward.subsiteFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor
          (flatObject B S hS 𝒳.val)
          (flatObject_map B S hS f hf)).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
        (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒴)).Additive :=
        Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous_additive.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u, u + 1} _ _ _
      ((SubsitePushforward.subsiteFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor (flatObject B S hS 𝒳.val)
          (flatObject_map B S hS f hf)).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳)
        (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒴)).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rf')
    [hRf : Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor αf (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
      (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [hRf' : Rf'.IsRightDerivedFunctor αf' (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
      (Sheaf (inclusionTopology B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    haveI := isContinuous_inclusion B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderFlatMorphisms B S hS 𝒳)
    haveI := isContinuous_inclusion B S hS 𝒴 (closedUnderFlatMorphisms B S hS 𝒴)
    haveI := additive_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒳
    haveI := additive_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒴
    haveI := preservesFiniteLimits_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒳
    haveI := preservesFiniteLimits_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒴
    haveI := preservesFiniteColimits_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒳
    haveI := preservesFiniteColimits_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒴
    (subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p B.topology
        (flatObject B S hS 𝒳.val)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ Rf' ≅
      Rf ⋙ (subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p B.topology
        (flatObject B S hS 𝒴.val)).mapDerivedCategory
declarations.comment: the flat-fppf case for abelian sheaves, first identity: g⁻¹ ∘ Rf_* = Rf'_* ∘ (g')⁻¹ on the unbounded derived categories, as an isomorphism (g')⁻¹ ⋙ Rf'_* ≅ Rf_* ⋙ g⁻¹ for every pair of total right derived functors Rf_*, Rf'_* of the two direct images, the canonical ones included, with nothing assumed. The degree-zero square of Stacks 07AT (2) and the fact that restricted K-injective complexes compute Rf'_* (Stacks 07AK at the 2-fibre products V ×_y 𝒳, the content of Stacks 0GR3) are proved, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedLowerShriekBaseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AV, second identity, for abelian sheaves on the flat-fppf sites:
`L(g')_! ∘ (f')⁻¹ = f⁻¹ ∘ Lg_!`.** For a flat 1-morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks, with
`Lg_!` and `L(g')_!` the derived lower shrieks of **Stacks 07AS** (1) for `𝒴` and `𝒳`, and `f⁻¹`,
`(f')⁻¹` the inverse images along `f` and along its restriction `f'` to the flat-fppf sites,

`Lg_! ⋙ f⁻¹ ≅ (f')⁻¹ ⋙ L(g')_!`

on the unbounded derived categories of abelian sheaves. All four functors are the canonical ones
and no hypothesis is made. The isomorphism is the conjugate, under the composites of the derived
adjunctions `Lg_! ⊣ g⁻¹`, `L(g')_! ⊣ (g')⁻¹` of Stacks 07AS (3) and `f⁻¹ ⊣ Rf_*`,
`(f')⁻¹ ⊣ Rf'_*` (exact left adjoints), of the first identity
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedRestrictionBaseChangeIso`.
declarations.comment: the flat-fppf case for abelian sheaves, second identity: L(g')_! ∘ (f')⁻¹ = f⁻¹ ∘ Lg_! on the unbounded derived categories, as an isomorphism Lg_! ⋙ f⁻¹ ≅ (f')⁻¹ ⋙ L(g')_! of the canonical functors, with nothing assumed: the derived lower shrieks are those of Stacks 07AS (3), and the four derived adjunctions are constructed

`g⁻¹ ∘ Rf_* = Rf'_* ∘ (g')⁻¹`.** Let `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` be a smooth 1-morphism of algebraic stacks, `Rf_*`
and `Rf'_*` total right derived functors of the direct images along `f` and along its restriction

lisse-étale sites of `𝒴` and `𝒳`. Then, on the unbounded derived categories,

def derivedRestrictionBaseChangeIso
    (Rf : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))

      DerivedCategory (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))
    (Rf' : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}))

        (etaleTopology B)).2

          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))).Additive :=
        Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous_additive.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u, u + 1} _ _ _

          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))
          (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p (etaleTopology B))).mapHomotopyCategory
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rf)
    (αf' : haveI := isCocontinuous_subsiteFunctor.{u, w} B S hS f hf
      haveI : ((SubsitePushforward.subsiteFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor
          (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
          (smoothObject_map.{u, w} B S hS f hf)).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
        (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)).Additive :=
        Functor.sheafPushforwardCocontinuous_additive.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u, u + 1} _ _ _
      ((SubsitePushforward.subsiteFunctor f.hom.hom.toFunctor (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
          (smoothObject_map.{u, w} B S hS f hf)).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
        (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Qh ⟶ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ Rf')
    [hRf : Rf.IsRightDerivedFunctor αf (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
      (Sheaf (associatedTopology B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (ComplexShape.up ℤ))]
    [hRf' : Rf'.IsRightDerivedFunctor αf' (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso
      (Sheaf (inclusionTopology.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))] :
    haveI := isContinuous_inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)
    haveI := isContinuous_inclusion.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴 (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)
    haveI := additive_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒳
    haveI := additive_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒴
    haveI := preservesFiniteLimits_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒳
    haveI := preservesFiniteLimits_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒴
    haveI := preservesFiniteColimits_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒳
    haveI := preservesFiniteColimits_subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒴
    (subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)
        (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒳)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ Rf' ≅
      Rf ⋙ (subsiteRestriction B S hS 𝒴.val.val.p (etaleTopology B)
        (smoothObject.{u, w} B S hS 𝒴)).mapDerivedCategory

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AZ, part (1).**  Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family of smooth 1-morphisms of
algebraic stacks over `S` which is jointly surjective, that is `|𝒳| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒵 j|)` for the
points of **Stacks 04XG**, and let `M` be a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on `𝒳_étale`.  If every
inverse image `f j^{-1} M` is quasi-coherent, then so is `M`.

Joint surjectivity turns every object of `𝒳` into one covered, étale-locally, by images of
objects of the members of the family; quasi-coherence of the inverse images presents `M` globally
on a covering of each of those images, and quasi-coherence is local.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isSmooth_jointlySurjective
    (hsmooth : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsSmooth B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids (B.baseTopology .etale)
      (B.baseTopology_le_topology .etale)))
    (hM : ∀ j, ((familyModulePullback B S hS 𝒵 f (B.baseTopology .etale)
      (B.baseTopology_le_topology .etale) j).obj M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (1): the smooth family on the étale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isFlat_isLfp_jointlySurjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07AZ, part (2).**  Let `f j : 𝒵 j ⟶ 𝒳` be a family of 1-morphisms of algebraic
stacks over `S` which are each flat and locally of finite presentation and which is jointly
surjective, that is `|𝒳| = ⋃ j, |f j|(|𝒵 j|)`, and let `M` be a sheaf of `𝒪_𝒳`-modules on
`𝒳_fppf`.  If every inverse image `f j^{-1} M` is quasi-coherent, then so is `M`.

This is the argument of part (1) with "smooth" replaced by "flat and locally of finite
presentation" and the étale covering of **Stacks 06XH** by the fppf covering of
**Stacks 07AN**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isFlat_isLfp_jointlySurjective
    (hflat : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsFlat B S hS (f j))
    (hlfp : ∀ j, AlgebraicStacks.IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS (f j))
    (hjs : (Set.univ : Set (AlgebraicStacks.points B S hS 𝒳)) =
      ⋃ j, Set.range (AlgebraicStacks.pointsMap B S hS (f j)))
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringStructureSheafCore B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p
      𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl))
    (hM : ∀ j, ((familyModulePullback B S hS 𝒵 f B.topology le_rfl j).obj
      M).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (2): the flat, locally finitely presented family on the fppf site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.isQuasicoherentClause_fppf_moduleLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and let `H` be a quasi-coherent
`O_{𝒳_{lisse,étale}}`-module on the lisse-étale site of `𝒳`. Then `g_!H` is a quasi-coherent
module on `𝒳`, where `g_!` is the lower shriek on sheaves of modules of **Stacks 0789** (1).

A quasi-coherent module on `𝒳` is one in the sense of **Stacks 06WG**: a sheaf for the fppf
topology which is quasi-coherent on `(𝒳_fppf, O_𝒳)`. The conclusion is this property of the
underlying presheaf of modules of the sheaf `g_!H` on `𝒳_étale`, in the form of
`AlgebraicGeometry.FibredSite.IsQuasicoherentClause` at `.fppf` (**Stacks 0EM8**).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentClause_fppf_moduleLowerShriek
    (H : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedTopos.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳
      (closedUnderSmoothMorphisms.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳)).O))
    (hH : H.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    FibredSite.IsQuasicoherentClause B S hS 𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids .fppf
      ((moduleLowerShriek.{u, t} B S hS 𝒳).obj H).val
declarations.comment: part (1): for every quasi-coherent module `H` on the lisse-étale site of an algebraic stack `𝒳`, `g_!H` is a quasi-coherent module on `𝒳`: an fppf sheaf which is quasi-coherent on `(𝒳_fppf, O_𝒳)`, the 06WG notion, stated as the fppf clause of 0EM8

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.isQuasicoherentOnSite_moduleLowerShriek_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒳` be an algebraic stack and let `H` be a quasi-coherent
`O_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}}`-module on the flat-fppf site of `𝒳`. Then `g_!H` is a quasi-coherent module
on `𝒳`, where `g_!` is the lower shriek on sheaves of modules of **Stacks 0789** (2): it is
quasi-coherent on `(𝒳_fppf, O_𝒳)`, the ambient site being `𝒳_fppf` itself, which is
quasi-coherence of a module on `𝒳` in the sense of **Stacks 06WG**.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_moduleLowerShriek_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (H : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (subsiteRingedTopos B S hS
      𝒳.val.val.p 𝒳.val.isFiberedInGroupoids B.topology le_rfl (objectProperty B S hS 𝒳)).O))
    (hH : H.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((moduleLowerShriek B S hS 𝒳).obj H).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: part (2): for every quasi-coherent module `H` on the flat-fppf site of an algebraic stack `𝒳`, `g_!H` is a quasi-coherent module on `𝒳`, that is, quasi-coherent on `(𝒳_fppf, O_𝒳)` in the sense of 06WG

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.quasicoherentEquivalence
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic stack `𝒳`, the functors `g^{-1}` and `g_!` are mutually inverse equivalences
between `QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` and `QCoh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}, 𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}})`. The functor of the equivalence
is `g^{-1}` and its inverse is `g_!`, both on the nose (`quasicoherentEquivalence_functor_comp_ι`,
`quasicoherentEquivalence_inverse_comp_ι`); the unit is the inverse of the counit
`g_!g^{-1}𝓖 ⟶ 𝓖` of `g_! ⊣ g^{-1}`, an isomorphism on quasi-coherent modules, and the counit is
the inverse of its unit `ℋ ⟶ g^{-1}g_!ℋ`.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentEquivalence :
    AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentModules B S hS 𝒳 ≌ quasicoherentSubsiteModules B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (2)(a): g^{-1} and g_! are mutually inverse functors between QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) and QCoh(𝒳_{flat,fppf}, 𝒪_{𝒳_{flat,fppf}})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.coheratorIsoLowerShriekModulePullback
declarations.doc:
For `𝓕` in `LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳)`, `Q(𝓕) = g_!g^{-1}𝓕`, naturally in `𝓕`, where
`Q : LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳) ⥤ QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)` is the coherator of **Stacks 0778**
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.AlgebraicStacks.lqcohFbcCoherator`). The isomorphism at `𝓕` is
`g_!g^{-1}` of the adjunction map `Q(𝓕) ⟶ 𝓕`, preceded by the inverse of the counit
`g_!g^{-1}Q(𝓕) ⟶ Q(𝓕)`.
declarations.statement:
def coheratorIsoLowerShriekModulePullback :
    AlgebraicStacks.lqcohFbcCoherator B E h S hS 𝒳 ⋙
        AlgebraicStacks.quasicoherentInclusion B S hS 𝒳 ≅
      (lqcohSheafFbcFppfModules.{u, w, u} B E h S hS 𝒳).ι ⋙ modulePullback B S hS 𝒳 ⋙
        moduleLowerShriek B S hS 𝒳
declarations.comment: part (2)(c): Q(F) = g_! g^{-1} F for F in LQCoh^fbc(𝒪_𝒳), Q the coherator of 0778
