declarations.comment: the third assertion: for f quasi-compact and quasi-separated, Hom_D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳)(Lf^*_QCoh A, B) = Hom_D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒴)(A, Rf_QCoh,* B) for A in D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒴) and B in D⁺_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳), at module universe u + 1, for the class of Stacks 0762 read with the pullback of sheaves, at the standard models of the derived categories

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSuccHomEquiv_naturality_left
declarations.doc: Naturality of the adjointness of Stacks 07BE in `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSuccHomEquiv_naturality_left
    {A A' : (DerivedCategoryB.serreQuotientW (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒴)
      (parasiticSheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒴)).Localization} (e : A' ⟶ A)
    (Bq : (DerivedCategoryB.serreQuotientWPlus (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)
      (parasiticSheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)).Localization)
    (g : (derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSucc B E h S hS f).obj A ⟶
      (DerivedCategoryB.serreQuotientPlusToSerreQuotient
        (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)
        (parasiticSheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)).obj Bq) :
    derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSuccHomEquiv B E h S hS f hqc hqs A' Bq
        ((derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSucc B E h S hS f).map e ≫ g) =
      e ≫ derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSuccHomEquiv B E h S hS f hqc hqs A Bq g
declarations.comment: the third assertion: naturality of the adjointness in A

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.FlatFppf.derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSuccHomEquiv_naturality_right
declarations.doc: Naturality of the adjointness of Stacks 07BE in `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSuccHomEquiv_naturality_right
    (A : (DerivedCategoryB.serreQuotientW (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒴)
      (parasiticSheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒴)).Localization)
    {Bq Bq' : (DerivedCategoryB.serreQuotientWPlus (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)
      (parasiticSheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)).Localization} (k : Bq ⟶ Bq')
    (g : (derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSucc B E h S hS f).obj A ⟶
      (DerivedCategoryB.serreQuotientPlusToSerreQuotient
        (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)
        (parasiticSheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)).obj Bq) :
    derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSuccHomEquiv B E h S hS f hqc hqs A Bq'
        (g ≫ (DerivedCategoryB.serreQuotientPlusToSerreQuotient
          (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)
          (parasiticSheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒳)).map k) =
      derivedQuasicoherentPullbackSuccHomEquiv B E h S hS f hqc hqs A Bq g ≫
        (DerivedCategoryB.serreQuotientPlusToSerreQuotient
          (sheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒴)
          (parasiticSheafFlatBaseChangeModulesSucc B E h S hS 𝒴)).map
          ((derivedPushforwardQuasicoherentPlusSucc B E h S hS f hqc hqs).map k)
declarations.comment: the third assertion: naturality of the adjointness in B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.LisseEtale.exists_not_isMorphismOfSites_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07BG.** *The lisse-étale site is not functorial, even for morphisms of schemes.*

There is a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of schemes over `S` in a big fppf site for which the base-change
functor `Y_{lisse,étale} ⥤ X_{lisse,étale}` — identified here by a natural isomorphism after
forgetting smoothness, so that no particular choice of fibre products is asserted — is
continuous, and yet does not define a morphism of sites: its pushforward on sheaves has no left
exact left adjoint.

See the module documentation for the counterexample.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_isMorphismOfSites_pullback :
    ∃ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
      (X Y : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : X ⟶ Y)
      (F : LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Y) ⥤
        LisseEtale.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS X)),
      Nonempty (F ⋙ inclusion.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS X) ≅
        inclusion.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Y) ⋙ Over.pullback f) ∧
      F.IsContinuous (topology.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Y))
        (topology.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS X)) ∧
      ¬ IsMorphismOfSites.{u + 1} F
        (topology.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS Y))
        (topology.{u, w} B S hS (schemeStack.{u, w} B S hS X))

registrations.name: IsLocalHom
registrations.comment:
A local homomorphism of local rings: `φ(𝔪_R) ⊆ 𝔪_S`. Mathlib states the
  equivalent reflects-units condition, which needs no `IsLocalRing` instance; the equivalence
  is `IsLocalRing.local_hom_TFAE` (tag 07BJ).

registrations.name: IsLocalRing
registrations.comment:
A local ring is a ring with exactly one maximal ideal. Mathlib defines this
  by the equivalent condition that the ring is nontrivial and `a` or `b` is a unit whenever
  `a + b = 1`; see `IsLocalRing.maximal_ideal_unique` for the Stacks wording.

registrations.name: IsLocalRing.maximal_ideal_unique
registrations.comment:
`∃! I, I.IsMaximal` — the Stacks project's own phrasing of the definition
  of a local ring, which Mathlib derives from its `a + b = 1` formulation.

registrations.name: IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal
registrations.comment:
The maximal ideal `𝔪_R` of a local ring `R`, realised as the ideal of
  nonunits.

registrations.name: IsLocalRing.ResidueField
registrations.comment: The residue field `κ = R/𝔪_R` of a local ring.

registrations.name: IsLocalRing.residue
registrations.comment: The quotient map `R → R/𝔪_R = κ` onto the residue field.

sga.comment: Ω when K is a field

registrations.name: Algebra.Generators.self
registrations.comment: the canonical surjection R[S] → S, [s] ↦ s: the generators of S indexed by S itself, whose map MvPolynomial S R → S is aeval id

declarations.name: Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**The naive cotangent complex** (Stacks 07BN): for a ring map `R → S`, the two-term chain
complex of `S`-modules
```
NL_{S/R} = (I/I² ⟶ Ω_{R[S]/R} ⊗_{R[S]} S)
```
where `I` is the kernel of the canonical surjection `R[S] → S`, `[s] ↦ s`, with `I/I²` in
homological degree `1`, `Ω_{R[S]/R} ⊗_{R[S]} S` in homological degree `0`, and the canonical
map of Stacks 07BM, sending the class of `f ∈ I` to `df ⊗ 1`, as its differential. It is zero
in all other degrees. Its degree-`0` homology is `Ω_{S/R}` and its degree-`1` homology is
`H₁(L_{S/R}) = Algebra.H1Cotangent R S`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def Algebra.naiveCotangentComplex (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] : ChainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} S) ℕ
declarations.comment:
The complex itself; Mathlib has its differential
(`Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex` at `Algebra.Generators.self R S`) and its degree-`1`
homology (`Algebra.H1Cotangent`), but not the two-term complex. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: h1Cotangent_equiv_cotangent_of_surjective
declarations.doc:
For a surjective ring map `A → B` with kernel `I := RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B)`, the
`A`-linear isomorphism `Algebra.H1Cotangent A B ≃ₗ[A] I.Cotangent`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def h1Cotangent_equiv_cotangent_of_surjective
    (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A B)) :
    Algebra.H1Cotangent A B ≃ₗ[A] (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A B)).Cotangent

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.nlToConormalOfSurjective_isHomotopyEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07BP.** Let `A → B` be a surjective ring map with kernel `I`. Then the naive
cotangent complex `NL_{B/A}` is homotopy equivalent to the chain complex `(I/I² → 0)` with
`I/I²` in degree `1`, via `nlToConormalOfSurjective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nlToConormalOfSurjective_isHomotopyEquiv (h : Function.Surjective (algebraMap A B)) :
    IsHomotopyEquiv (nlToConormalOfSurjective h)
declarations.comment:
the homotopy equivalence `NL_{B/A} ≃ (I/I^2 → 0)`; the consequence
`H_1(L_{B/A}) = I/I^2` is `h1Cotangent_equiv_cotangent_of_surjective`

declarations.name: RingMapSystemUnbundled.isIso_colim_NL
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 07BQ, Lemma 10.134.9 (packaged).**
The canonical comparison morphism `colim_λ NL_{S_λ/R_λ} → NL_{S/R}` is an
isomorphism of two-term complexes: it is a bijection in each homological degree
(degree 1 and degree 0) and the two degreewise comparison maps commute with the
differentials (the colimit differential `colimDifferential` and the differential
`NL_{S/R}.cotangentComplex`).  This bundles the three theorems above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colim_NL [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty Λ] :
    Function.Bijective sys.comparisonCotangent ∧
    Function.Bijective sys.comparisonCotangentSpace ∧
    (∀ x : sys.colimCotangent,
      sys.comparisonCotangentSpace (sys.colimDifferential x)
        = sys.NLinf.cotangentComplex (sys.comparisonCotangent x))

declarations.name: kaehlerDifferential_subsingleton_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
`H₀(NL_{S⁻¹A/A}) = Ω_{S⁻¹A/A} = 0`: the module of Kähler differentials of a
localization `S⁻¹A` over `A` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem kaehlerDifferential_subsingleton_of_isLocalization
    [IsLocalization S B] :
    Subsingleton (Ω[B⁄A])

declarations.name: h1Cotangent_subsingleton_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
`H₁(NL_{S⁻¹A/A}) = 0`: the first naive cotangent homology of a localization `S⁻¹A`
over `A` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem h1Cotangent_subsingleton_of_isLocalization
    [IsLocalization S B] :
    Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent A B)

declarations.name: naiveCotangentComplex_localization_base_homotopyEquiv
declarations.doc:
With `Aₘ` a localization of `A` at the multiplicative subset `M` and a ring map `Aₘ → B`, the
canonical chain map `φ = (φ₁, φ₀) : NL_{B/A} → NL_{B/Aₘ}`, given by
`Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map h` and `Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map h` for the morphism
of extensions `h` induced by the tower `A → Aₘ → B`, is a homotopy equivalence of the two term
naive cotangent complexes of `B`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem naiveCotangentComplex_localization_base_homotopyEquiv
    (A : Type*) (Aₘ : Type*) (B : Type*)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing Aₘ] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A Aₘ] [Algebra A B] [Algebra Aₘ B]
    [IsScalarTower A Aₘ B]
    (M : Submonoid A) [IsLocalization M Aₘ] :
    let P := (Generators.self A B).toExtension
    let Q := (Generators.self Aₘ B).toExtension
    let h : P.Hom Q :=
      ((Generators.self A B).defaultHom (Generators.self Aₘ B)).toExtensionHom
    let φ₁ := Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map h
    let φ₀ := Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map h
    ∃ (ψ₁ : Q.Cotangent →ₗ[B] P.Cotangent)
      (ψ₀ : Q.CotangentSpace →ₗ[B] P.CotangentSpace)
      (s : P.CotangentSpace →ₗ[B] P.Cotangent)
      (t : Q.CotangentSpace →ₗ[B] Q.Cotangent),
      Q.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ φ₁ = φ₀ ∘ₗ P.cotangentComplex ∧
      P.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ ψ₁ = ψ₀ ∘ₗ Q.cotangentComplex ∧
      ψ₁ ∘ₗ φ₁ - LinearMap.id = s ∘ₗ P.cotangentComplex ∧
      ψ₀ ∘ₗ φ₀ - LinearMap.id = P.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ s ∧
      φ₁ ∘ₗ ψ₁ - LinearMap.id = t ∘ₗ Q.cotangentComplex ∧
      φ₀ ∘ₗ ψ₀ - LinearMap.id = Q.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ t

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.isQuasiIso_nlExtensionOverMap_of_isLocalization
declarations.doc:
**Localizing the base**: for a localization `R' = N⁻¹R` of `R` at a multiplicative subset
`N ⊆ R` and a ring map `R' → T`, the canonical map of two-term complexes `NL_{T/R} ⟶ NL_{T/R'}`
is bijective in both degrees, hence a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiIso_nlExtensionOverMap_of_isLocalization (N : Submonoid R) [IsLocalization N R'] :
    IsQuasiIso (nlExtensionOverMap
      ((Generators.self R T).defaultHom (Generators.self R' T)).toExtensionHom)
declarations.comment:
the canonical map `NL_{T/R} ⟶ NL_{T/R'}` is bijective in both degrees, hence a
quasi-isomorphism; the homotopy equivalence itself is
`naiveCotangentComplex_localization_base_homotopyEquiv`.

declarations.name: Algebra.Generators.finite_and_projective_tensor_cotangent_of_syntomic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07BT.** Let `S = R[x_1, …, x_n]/I` and let `g ∈ S` be such that `S_g` is syntomic
over `R`. Then `(I/I²)_g` is a finite projective `S_g`-module.
declarations.comment:
The presentation `R[x_1, …, x_n] → S` is `Algebra.Generators R S (Fin n)`,
`I/I²` is its cotangent module `P.toExtension.Cotangent`, and `(I/I²)_g` is the base change
`T ⊗_S I/I²` to a localization `T` of `S` away from `g`. The source's hypothesis that `I` is
finitely generated is not needed.

declarations.name: Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae_h1Cotangent_and_kaehlerDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness at a prime is the vanishing of `H_1` together with freeness of `Ω`**
(Stacks 07BU). Let `R → S` be of finite presentation, let `q` be a prime of `S` and let `Sq` be a
model of `S_q`. The following are equivalent: (1) `R → S` is smooth at `q`, that is `R → S_g` is
smooth for some `g ∉ q`; (2) `H_1(L_{S/R})_q = 0` and `Ω_{S/R, q}` is a finite free
`S_q`-module; (3) `H_1(L_{S/R})_q = 0` and `Ω_{S/R, q}` is projective; (4) `H_1(L_{S/R})_q = 0`
and `Ω_{S/R, q}` is flat; (5) `S_q` is formally smooth over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isSmoothAt_tfae_h1Cotangent_and_kaehlerDifferential
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S]
    (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq]
    [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] [Algebra R Sq] [IsScalarTower R S Sq] :
    List.TFAE
      [∃ g ∉ q, Algebra.Smooth R (Localization.Away g),
       Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent R Sq) ∧
         Module.Finite Sq Ω[Sq⁄R] ∧ Module.Free Sq Ω[Sq⁄R],
       Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent R Sq) ∧ Module.Projective Sq Ω[Sq⁄R],
       Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent R Sq) ∧ Module.Flat Sq Ω[Sq⁄R],
       Algebra.IsSmoothAt R q]
declarations.comment:
The localizations `H_1(L_{S/R})_q` and `Ω_{S/R, q}` are read on an arbitrary model
`Sq` of `S_q` as `Algebra.H1Cotangent R Sq` and `Ω[Sq⁄R]`, which is Lemma 00S7 and is witnessed by
the instances `Algebra.H1Cotangent.isLocalizedModule` and
`KaehlerDifferential.isLocalizedModule_map`; vanishing is `Subsingleton` and `finite free` is
`Module.Finite` and `Module.Free`. Item (1) is Definition 00TB verbatim, and Mathlib's
`Algebra.IsSmoothAt` is added as item (5). See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Subalgebra.directedOn_isGlobalCompleteIntersectionOver_and_exists_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07BV, first part.** Every field extension `K/k` is a filtered colimit of global
complete intersection algebras over `k`: the `k`-subalgebras of `K` that are global complete
intersections over `k` form a directed family whose union is `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Subalgebra.directedOn_isGlobalCompleteIntersectionOver_and_exists_mem
    (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] :
    DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) {A : Subalgebra k K | IsGlobalCompleteIntersectionOver k A} ∧
      ∀ x : K, ∃ A ∈ {A : Subalgebra k K | IsGlobalCompleteIntersectionOver k A}, x ∈ A
declarations.comment:
First part. The filtered colimit is the directed union of the global complete
intersection `k`-subalgebras of `K`; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: Subalgebra.directedOn_smooth_and_exists_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07BV, second part.** A separable field extension `K/k` is a filtered colimit of
smooth `k`-algebras: the smooth `k`-subalgebras of `K` form a directed family whose union
is `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Subalgebra.directedOn_smooth_and_exists_mem
    (k K : Type*) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K] :
    DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) {A : Subalgebra k K | Algebra.Smooth k A} ∧
      ∀ x : K, ∃ A ∈ {A : Subalgebra k K | Algebra.Smooth k A}, x ∈ A
declarations.comment:
Second part. The filtered colimit is the directed union of the smooth
`k`-subalgebras of `K`; see the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularRingHom
declarations.doc:
A ring homomorphism is *regular* if it is flat and, over every prime of its source, its
residue-field fibre is Noetherian and geometrically regular over that residue field.
declarations.statement:
public def IsRegularRingHom {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) : Prop

declarations.name: isRegularRingHom_tfae_localizations
declarations.doc:
A ring homomorphism with Noetherian target is regular if and only if all its induced maps on
local rings at corresponding prime ideals are regular, and if and only if this holds for
maximal ideals of the target and their contractions.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRingHom_tfae_localizations
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) [IsNoetherianRing S] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsRegularRingHom f,
      ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] (h : p = q.comap f),
        IsRegularRingHom (Localization.localRingHom p q f h),
      ∀ (m : Ideal R) [m.IsPrime] (m' : Ideal S) [m'.IsMaximal]
        (h : m = m'.comap f),
        IsRegularRingHom (Localization.localRingHom m m' f h)]

declarations.name: isRegularRingHom_baseChange
declarations.doc: A finite-type base change of a regular ring homomorphism is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRingHom_baseChange
    {R : Type u} {Λ : Type v} {R' : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R Λ] [Algebra R R']
    [Algebra.FiniteType R R']
    (h : IsRegularRingHom (algebraMap R Λ)) :
    IsRegularRingHom
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R) (A := Λ) (B := R')).toRingHom

declarations.name: CommRingCat.ind_under_iff_exists_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Criterion for being a filtered colimit of algebras of a given family.** Let `R → Λ` be a
ring map and let `E` be a family of `R`-algebras of finite presentation over `R`. Then `Λ` is a
filtered colimit of members of `E` if and only if every `R`-algebra map `A → Λ` with `A` of
finite presentation over `R` factors as `A → B → Λ` with `B` in `E`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ind_under_iff_exists_factorization {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (Λ : Under R)
    {E : ObjectProperty (Under R)} (hE : E ≤ fun B : Under R ↦ B.hom.hom.FinitePresentation) :
    ObjectProperty.ind.{u} E Λ ↔
      ∀ A : Under R, A.hom.hom.FinitePresentation → ∀ f : A ⟶ Λ,
        ∃ (B : Under R) (g : A ⟶ B) (h : B ⟶ Λ), g ≫ h = f ∧ E B
declarations.comment:
The family `𝓔` is an `E : ObjectProperty (Under R)` on the category `Under R` of
`R`-algebras, and "`Λ` is a filtered colimit of members of `𝓔`" is Mathlib's
`ObjectProperty.ind.{u} E Λ`. `E` is not assumed small; the source's set-theoretic hypothesis is
only a smallness device. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.singularIdeal
declarations.doc:
The *singular ideal* `H_{A/R}` of `A` over `R`: the vanishing ideal of the set of primes of
`A` at which `R → A` is not smooth.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def singularIdeal : Ideal A
declarations.comment: the singular ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.singularIdeal_isRadical
declarations.doc: The singular ideal is radical.
declarations.statement: theorem singularIdeal_isRadical : (singularIdeal R A).IsRadical
declarations.comment: radicality

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.zeroLocus_singularIdeal
declarations.doc:
The vanishing locus of the singular ideal is exactly the locus of primes at which `R → A` is
not smooth.
declarations.comment: vanishing locus

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.eq_singularIdeal_iff_of_isRadical
declarations.doc:
A radical ideal is the singular ideal exactly when its vanishing locus is the non-smooth
locus; this is the uniqueness in the definition of the singular ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem eq_singularIdeal_iff_of_isRadical {I : Ideal A} (hI : I.IsRadical) :
    I = singularIdeal R A ↔
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) =
        {q : PrimeSpectrum A | ¬ Algebra.SmoothAt R A q.asIdeal}
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_notMem_eq_mul_jacobianMinorOn_of_smoothAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07C6.** If a finite polynomial presentation of `A` over `R` is smooth at a prime `q`
(Definition 00TB), then some element `a ∈ A` outside `q` is a multiple of a `c × c` Jacobian minor
`det(∂f_j/∂x_i)_{j ∈ V, i ∈ U}` on sets `U`, `V` of `c` variables and `c` relations, and, modulo
the square of the full relation ideal, every lift of `a` carries every relation into the ideal
generated by the relations indexed by `V`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_notMem_eq_mul_jacobianMinorOn_of_smoothAt
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {A : Type v} [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    (P : _root_.Presentation R A) (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : Algebra.SmoothAt R A q) :
    ∃ (a : A), a ∉ q ∧
      ∃ (c : ℕ) (U : Finset (Fin P.n)) (V : Finset (Fin P.m))
        (_hcn : c ≤ P.n) (_hcm : c ≤ P.m) (hU : U.card = c) (hV : V.card = c),
        ∃ a' : A,
          a = a' * P.lift (P.jacobianMinorOn c U V hU hV) ∧
          (∀ (ℓ : Fin P.m) (ã : MvPolynomial (Fin P.n) R), P.IsLift a ã →
            ã * P.f ℓ ∈ P.selectedRelIdeal V + P.relIdeal ^ 2)

declarations.name: IsElementaryStandard
declarations.doc:
An element `a ∈ A` is *elementary standard in `A` over `R`* if there exists a presentation
of `A` over `R` and an integer `c` with `0 ≤ c ≤ min(n, m)` realizing `a` as elementary
standard.
declarations.statement: def IsElementaryStandard (a : A) : Prop
declarations.comment: the first of the two notions the definition introduces: `a` is elementary standard in `A` over `R`, i.e. some presentation `A = R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m)` and some `0 ≤ c ≤ min(n, m)` satisfy 16.2.3.1 and 16.2.3.2. The two conditions themselves are `Presentation.IsElementaryStandardFor`

declarations.name: IsStrictlyStandard
declarations.doc:
An element `a ∈ A` is *strictly standard in `A` over `R`* if there exists a presentation of
`A` over `R` and an integer `c` with `0 ≤ c ≤ min(n, m)` realizing `a` as strictly standard.
declarations.statement: def IsStrictlyStandard (a : A) : Prop
declarations.comment: the second of the two notions the definition introduces: `a` is strictly standard in `A` over `R`, i.e. some presentation `A = R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m)` and some `0 ≤ c ≤ min(n, m)` satisfy 16.2.3.3 and 16.2.3.4. The two conditions themselves are `Presentation.IsStrictlyStandardFor`

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.singularIdeal_eq_radical_span_isElementaryStandard
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07CA.** The singular ideal is the radical of the ideal generated by the elementary
standard elements of `A` over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem singularIdeal_eq_radical_span_isElementaryStandard (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A] :
    singularIdeal R A = (Ideal.span {a : A | IsElementaryStandard (R := R) a}).radical
declarations.comment: elementary standard elements

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.singularIdeal_eq_radical_span_isStrictlyStandard
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07CA.** The singular ideal is the radical of the ideal generated by the strictly
standard elements of `A` over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem singularIdeal_eq_radical_span_isStrictlyStandard (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (A : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A] :
    singularIdeal R A = (Ideal.span {a : A | IsStrictlyStandard (R := R) a}).radical
declarations.comment: strictly standard elements

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.NotQuasiCompact.finitePresentation
declarations.doc: The ring map `R → A = R/(x)` is of finite presentation.
declarations.statement: theorem finitePresentation : Algebra.FinitePresentation (baseRing k) (quotientRing k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.NotQuasiCompact.smoothLocus_eq_iUnion
declarations.doc: The smooth locus of `R → A` is the union of the standard opens `D(y_i)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smoothLocus_eq_iUnion :
    Algebra.smoothLocus (baseRing k) (quotientRing k) =
      ⋃ i : ℕ, (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (y k i) : Set (PrimeSpectrum (quotientRing k)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.NotQuasiCompact.smoothLocus_not_compact
declarations.doc: The smooth locus of the finitely presented ring map `R → A` is not quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem smoothLocus_not_compact :
    ¬ IsCompact (Algebra.smoothLocus (baseRing k) (quotientRing k))

declarations.name: isElementaryStandard_basechange
declarations.doc:
Let `R → A` be a ring map of finite presentation and `R → R'` a ring map. If `a ∈ A` is
elementary standard in `A` over `R`, then `a ⊗ 1 ∈ A ⊗_R R'` is elementary standard in
`A ⊗_R R'` over `R'`. Here `A ⊗_R R'` is modelled as `R' ⊗[R] A` and `a ⊗ 1` as `1 ⊗ a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isElementaryStandard_basechange (a : A) (ha : IsElementaryStandard (R := R) a) :
    IsElementaryStandard (R := R')
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight a : R' ⊗[R] A)

declarations.name: isStrictlyStandard_basechange
declarations.doc:
Let `R → A` be a ring map of finite presentation and `R → R'` a ring map. If `a ∈ A` is
strictly standard in `A` over `R`, then `a ⊗ 1 ∈ A ⊗_R R'` is strictly standard in `A ⊗_R R'`
over `R'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrictlyStandard_basechange (a : A) (ha : IsStrictlyStandard (R := R) a) :
    IsStrictlyStandard (R := R')
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight a : R' ⊗[R] A)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_finiteType_retraction_improving_presentation
declarations.doc:
A finitely presented algebra admits one finite-type retract satisfying both local
improvements of its presentation. The retract is the symmetric algebra of the finite conormal
module of a polynomial presentation, and the retraction is its augmentation. This conormal module
is projective when the algebra is a local complete intersection over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteType_retraction_improving_presentation
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A] :
    ∃ (C : Type v) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra R C) (_ : Algebra A C)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R A C) (_ : Algebra.FiniteType A C) (g : C →ₐ[R] A)
      (n : ℕ) (P : Algebra.Generators R A (Fin n))
      (e : C ≃ₐ[A] SymmetricAlgebra A P.toExtension.Cotangent),
      Module.Finite A P.toExtension.Cotangent ∧
        (RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap R A) →
          Module.Projective A P.toExtension.Cotangent) ∧
        (∀ c : C, g c = SymmetricAlgebra.algebraMapInv (e c)) ∧
        g.comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R A C) = AlgHom.id R A ∧
        (∀ a : A,
          RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap R (Localization.Away a)) →
          (letI : Algebra (Localization.Away a)
                (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a)) :=
              (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap A C) a).toAlgebra;
            Algebra.Smooth (Localization.Away a)
                (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a)) ∧
              HasFreeConormalPresentation R (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a)))) ∧
        (∀ a : A, Algebra.Smooth R (Localization.Away a) →
          Module.Free (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a))
            (KaehlerDifferential R (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a))))

declarations.name: Algebra.exists_presentation_basis_cotangent_of_free_cotangent
declarations.doc:
A finitely presented `R`-algebra `S` admitting a presentation `S = R[x₁, …, xₙ]/I` with
`I/I²` free over `S` admits a presentation `S = R[y₁, …, y_m]/(f₁, …, f_c)` whose conormal
module is free with basis the classes of `f₁, …, f_c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_presentation_basis_cotangent_of_free_cotangent [FinitePresentation R S]
    (h : ∃ (ι : Type) (_ : Finite ι) (P : Generators R S ι),
      Module.Free S P.toExtension.Cotangent) :
    ∃ (ι σ : Type) (_ : Finite ι) (_ : Finite σ) (P : Presentation R S ι σ)
      (b : Module.Basis σ S P.toExtension.Cotangent),
      ∀ r, b r = Extension.Cotangent.mk ⟨P.relation r, P.relation_mem_ker r⟩

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_smooth_retract_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07CG.** A syntomic `R`-algebra `A` admits a smooth `A`-algebra `C` with a retraction
`C → A`, flat over `R` and a relative global complete intersection over `R`: so `C` is cut out of
a polynomial ring by `c` equations, flat over `R`, with all fibres of dimension `n - c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_retract_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [Algebra.Syntomic R A] :
    ∃ (C : Type v) (hC : CommRing C) (hRC : Algebra R C) (hAC : Algebra A C)
      (hTower : IsScalarTower R A C),
      let : CommRing C := hC
      let : Algebra R C := hRC
      let : Algebra A C := hAC
      let : IsScalarTower R A C := hTower
      Algebra.Smooth A C ∧
        Module.Flat R C ∧
          ∃ ρ : C →+* A,
          ρ.comp (algebraMap A C) = RingHom.id A ∧
            Algebra.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection R C

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_smooth_retract_isStandardSmooth_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**A smooth algebra has a standard smooth retract.** For a smooth ring map `R → A` there is a
smooth `R`-algebra map `A → B` with a retraction such that `B` is standard smooth over `R`, that
is, `B ≅ R[x_1, …, x_n]/(f_1, …, f_c)` with `det(∂f_j/∂x_i)_{i, j = 1, …, c}` invertible in `B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_retract_isStandardSmooth_of_smooth :
    Algebra.Smooth R A →
      ∃ (B : Type v) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : Algebra R B),
        IsScalarTower R A B ∧ Algebra.Smooth A B ∧
          Algebra.IsStandardSmooth R B ∧
          ∃ (r : B →+* A),
            r.comp (algebraMap A B) = RingHom.id A
declarations.comment:
`B` is produced as a type in the universe of `A`, carrying compatible `Algebra A B`
and `Algebra R B` instances with `IsScalarTower R A B`; "`B` is standard smooth over `R`" is
Mathlib's `Algebra.IsStandardSmooth`, whose submersive presentation is exactly the displayed
presentation with invertible `c × c` Jacobian minor. The retraction is a `RingHom`, which is
automatically an `R`-algebra map. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_smooth_isStandardSmooth_retraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07CH.** Let `R → A` be a smooth ring map. Then there is a smooth `A`-algebra `B`
which is standard smooth over `R` and such that `A → B` has an `A`-algebra retraction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_isStandardSmooth_retraction (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.Smooth R A] :
    ∃ (B : Type v) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : Algebra R B)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R A B),
      Algebra.Smooth A B ∧ Algebra.IsStandardSmooth R B ∧
        ∃ r : B →+* A, r.comp (algebraMap A B) = RingHom.id A

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.ind_isStandardSmooth_of_ind_smooth
declarations.doc:
**A filtered colimit of smooth algebras is a filtered colimit of standard smooth algebras.**
Let `R → Λ` be a ring map. If `Λ` is a filtered colimit of smooth `R`-algebras, then `Λ` is a
filtered colimit of standard smooth `R`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem ind_isStandardSmooth_of_ind_smooth {R Λ : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ]
    (f : R →+* Λ)
    (h : ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
      (fun B : Under (CommRingCat.of R) ↦ B.hom.hom.Smooth)
      (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom f))) :
    ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
      (fun B : Under (CommRingCat.of R) ↦ B.hom.hom.IsStandardSmooth)
      (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom f))
declarations.comment:
"`Λ` is a filtered colimit of smooth (resp. standard smooth) `R`-algebras" is
`ObjectProperty.ind.{u}` of `RingHom.Smooth` (resp. `RingHom.IsStandardSmooth`) on the category
`Under (CommRingCat.of R)` of `R`-algebras, as in Lemma `07C3`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_smooth_quotient_factorization
declarations.doc:
**The lifting problem.** Let `R → Λ` be a ring map and `I ⊂ R` an ideal with `I² = 0` such
that `Λ/IΛ` is a filtered colimit of smooth `R/I`-algebras. Then every `R`-algebra map
`φ : A → Λ` with `A` of finite presentation over `R` factors as `A → B/J → Λ` with `B` a smooth
`R`-algebra and `J ⊂ IB` a finitely generated ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_quotient_factorization
    {R Λ A : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra R Λ] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (hΛ : ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
      (fun B : Under (CommRingCat.of (R ⧸ I)) ↦ B.hom.hom.Smooth)
      (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (R ⧸ I) (Λ ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Λ))))))
    (φ : A →ₐ[R] Λ) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (alg : Algebra R B),
      letI := alg
      Algebra.Smooth R B ∧
        ∃ J : Ideal B, J ≤ I.map (algebraMap R B) ∧ J.FG ∧
          ∃ (α : A →ₐ[R] B ⧸ J) (β : (B ⧸ J) →ₐ[R] Λ), β.comp α = φ

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_smooth_factorization_of_fg_le_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07CL.** Let `I ⊂ R` be an ideal with `I² = 0` such that `Λ/IΛ` is a
filtered colimit of smooth `R/I`-algebras, and let `Λ` be flat over `R`. Then an `R`-algebra map
`φ : B → Λ` with `B` smooth over `R` factors as `B → B' → Λ` with `B'` smooth over `R` and with
`B → B'` killing any prescribed finitely generated ideal `J ⊆ IB` that `φ` annihilates.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_factorization_of_fg_le_map
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (hΛ : ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
      (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of (R ⧸ I)) ↦ C.hom.hom.Smooth)
      (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (R ⧸ I) (Λ ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Λ))))))
    [Module.Flat R Λ] {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra.Smooth R B]
    (φ : B →ₐ[R] Λ) (J : Ideal B) (hJI : J ≤ I.map (algebraMap R B)) (hJfg : J.FG)
    (hφJ : ∀ x ∈ J, φ x = 0) :
    ∃ (B' : Type u) (_ : CommRing B') (alg : Algebra R B'),
      letI := alg
      Algebra.Smooth R B' ∧
        ∃ (α : B →ₐ[R] B') (β : B' →ₐ[R] Λ), (∀ x ∈ J, α x = 0) ∧ β.comp α = φ

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.ind_smooth_of_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07CM: ind-smoothness of an algebra is stable under infinitesimal
deformations.** Let `R → Λ` be a ring map and `I ⊂ R` a nilpotent ideal. If `Λ/IΛ` is a filtered
colimit of smooth `R/I`-algebras and `R → Λ` is flat, then `Λ` is a filtered colimit of smooth
`R`-algebras.

Here "filtered colimit of smooth algebras" is `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.ind` of
`RingHom.Smooth` on `Under (CommRingCat.of R)`, the spelling of `07C3`, `07CK` and `07CL`;
nilpotence is `IsNilpotent I`, that is `I ^ n = ⊥` for some `n`; and flatness is
`Module.Flat R Λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ind_smooth_of_isNilpotent (I : Ideal R) (hI : IsNilpotent I)
    (hΛ : ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
      (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of (R ⧸ I)) ↦ C.hom.hom.Smooth)
      (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (R ⧸ I) (Λ ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R Λ))))))
    [Module.Flat R Λ] :
    ObjectProperty.ind.{u} (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of R) ↦ C.hom.hom.Smooth)
      (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R Λ)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_finitePresentation_lift_smoothAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07CP.** A finitely presented algebra modulo `π²`
admits a lift modulo `π` with the asserted smoothness properties.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finitePresentation_lift_smoothAt
    (R : Type u) (Λ : Type v) (C : Type w)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ] [CommRing C] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Algebra R Λ] (π : R)
    (hR : ∀ r : R, r * π = 0 ↔ r * π ^ 2 = 0)
    (hΛ : ∀ x : Λ,
      x * algebraMap R Λ π = 0 ↔ x * (algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2 = 0)
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) C]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) C]
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2})
      (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2})]
    (hquot : ∀ x : R, algebraMap (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2})
      (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2})
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap R Λ x))
    (f : C →ₐ[R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}]
      Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2}) :
    ∃ (D : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing D) (_ : Algebra R D)
      (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation R D) (g : D →ₐ[R] Λ)
      (c : C →+* D ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap R D π})
      (reduceΛ : (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2}) →+*
        Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap R Λ π})
      (reduceD : (D ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap R D π}) →+*
        Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap R Λ π})
      (_ : Algebra (C ⧸ Ideal.span {
        algebraMap (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) C
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) π)})
        (D ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap R D π})),
      (∀ x : Λ, reduceΛ (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x) ∧
      (∀ x : D, reduceD (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x) =
        Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (g x)) ∧
      (∀ x : C, reduceD (c x) = reduceΛ (f x)) ∧
      (∀ x : R, c (algebraMap (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) C
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x)) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap R D x)) ∧
      (∀ x : C, algebraMap
          (C ⧸ Ideal.span {
            algebraMap (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) C
              (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) π)})
          (D ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap R D π}) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ x) = c x) ∧
      (∀ (q : Ideal D) [q.IsPrime], algebraMap R D π ∉ q →
        Algebra.IsSmoothAt R q) ∧
      (∀ (q : Ideal D) [q.IsPrime], algebraMap R D π ∈ q →
        (∃ (p : Ideal C) (_ : p.IsPrime),
          Algebra.IsSmoothAt (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) p ∧
          p = Ideal.comap c (Ideal.map
            (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {algebraMap R D π})) q)) →
        Algebra.IsSmoothAt R q) ∧
      ∀ (q : Ideal (D ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap R D π})) [q.IsPrime],
        (∃ (p : Ideal C) (_ : p.IsPrime),
          Algebra.IsSmoothAt (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) p ∧
          p = Ideal.comap c q) →
        Algebra.IsSmoothAt
          (C ⧸ Ideal.span {
            algebraMap (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) C
              (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {π ^ 2}) π)}) q

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_finitePresentation_factorization_singularIdeal
declarations.doc:
**The desingularization lemma.** Let `R` be Noetherian, let `Λ` be an `R`-algebra in which
the annihilators of `π` and of `π²` agree, and let `A` be an `R`-algebra of finite presentation
with an `R`-algebra map `f : A → Λ`. If the image of `π` in `A` is strictly standard over `R`,
and if there is a retraction `ρ : A/π⁴A → R/π⁴R` compatible with the maps to `Λ/π⁴Λ`, then `f`
factors through an `R`-algebra `B` of finite presentation with `𝔞 B ⊆ H_{B/R}`, where
`𝔞 = Ann_R (Ann_R (π²) / Ann_R (π))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_factorization_singularIdeal
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) (Λ : Type w) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing Λ]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R Λ] [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A]
    (π : R) (f : A →ₐ[R] Λ)
    (hAnn : (Submodule.span Λ {algebraMap R Λ π}).annihilator =
      (Submodule.span Λ {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (hstandard : IsStrictlyStandard (R := R) (algebraMap R A π))
    (ρ : (A ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R A π) ^ 4}) →ₐ[R] (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 4}))
    (hρ : ∀ (x : A) (r : R),
      ρ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R A π) ^ 4}) x) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {π ^ 4}) r →
        Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 4}) (f x) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 4}) (algebraMap R Λ r)) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra R B) (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation R B)
      (g : A →ₐ[R] B) (h : B →ₐ[R] Λ),
      h.comp g = f ∧
        Ideal.map (algebraMap R B) (annihilatorDefectIdeal R π) ≤ singularIdeal R B

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_finitePresentation_factorization_singularIdeal_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07CT.** A strictly standard element and a factorization modulo its fourth power
yield a common finitely presented factorization `A → B ← D` over `Λ` with
`H_{D/R} B ⊆ H_{B/D}` and `H_{D/R} B ⊆ H_{B/R}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_factorization_singularIdeal_le
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) (D : Type w) (Λ : Type x)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing D] [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra R D] [Algebra R Λ]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R D] (π : R)
    (hR : (Submodule.span R {π}).annihilator = (Submodule.span R {π ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (hΛ : (Submodule.span Λ {algebraMap R Λ π}).annihilator =
      (Submodule.span Λ {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (fA : A →ₐ[R] Λ) (fD : D →ₐ[R] Λ)
    (hπ : IsStrictlyStandard (R := R) (A := A) (algebraMap R A π))
    (bar : (A ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R A π) ^ 4}) →ₐ[R]
      D ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R D π) ^ 4})
    (hbar : ∀ (a : A) (y : D),
      bar (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R A π) ^ 4}) a) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R D π) ^ 4}) y →
        Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 4}) (fA a) =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 4}) (fD y)) :
    ∃ (B : Type w) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra D B) (_ : Algebra R B)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R D B) (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation R B)
      (a : A →ₐ[R] B) (g : B →ₐ[R] Λ),
      g.comp a = fA ∧ g.comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom R D B) = fD ∧
        (singularIdeal R D).map (algebraMap D B) ≤ singularIdeal D B ∧
        (singularIdeal R D).map (algebraMap D B) ≤ singularIdeal R B

declarations.name: Ideal.IsRegular
declarations.doc:
An ideal is regular if, at every prime containing it, some principal localization away from
the prime is generated by a regular sequence.
declarations.statement: public def IsRegular {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) : Prop

declarations.name: Ideal.IsKoszulRegular
declarations.doc:
An ideal is Koszul-regular if, at every prime containing it, some principal localization away
from the prime is generated by a Koszul-regular sequence.
declarations.statement: public def IsKoszulRegular {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) : Prop

declarations.name: Ideal.IsH1Regular
declarations.doc:
An ideal is `H₁`-regular if, at every prime containing it, some principal localization away
from the prime is generated by an `H₁`-regular sequence.
declarations.statement: public def IsH1Regular {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) : Prop

declarations.name: Quasiregular.isQuasiregularIdeal_fg
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07CW**.
A quasi-regular ideal is finitely generated.
declarations.statement: theorem isQuasiregularIdeal_fg {I : Ideal R} (hI : IsQuasiregularIdeal' I) : I.FG

declarations.name: Ideal.inf_sq_eq_mul_of_quotient_isH1RegularIdeal
declarations.doc: If `I ⊆ J` and `J / I` is an H₁-regular ideal of `A / I`, then `I ∩ J² = I J`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem inf_sq_eq_mul_of_quotient_isH1RegularIdeal
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (I J : Ideal A) (hIJ : I ≤ J)
    (hreg : IsH1Regular (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) J)) :
    I ⊓ J ^ 2 = I * J

declarations.name: RingHom.isKoszulRegularIdeal_ker_of_surjective_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
The kernel of every finite polynomial presentation is a Koszul-regular ideal if the kernel
of one such presentation is Koszul-regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isKoszulRegularIdeal_ker_of_surjective_mvPolynomial
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    {ι : Type w} [_root_.Finite ι] {κ : Type x} [_root_.Finite κ]
    (α : MvPolynomial ι A →ₐ[A] B) (hα : Function.Surjective α)
    (hI : Ideal.IsKoszulRegular (RingHom.ker α.toRingHom))
    (β : MvPolynomial κ A →ₐ[A] B) (hβ : Function.Surjective β) :
    Ideal.IsKoszulRegular (RingHom.ker β.toRingHom)

declarations.name: RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
A ring homomorphism is a local complete intersection if it is of finite type and some finite
polynomial presentation has Koszul-regular kernel.
declarations.statement:
public def IsLocalCompleteIntersection {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) : Prop

declarations.name: RingHom.isLocalCompleteIntersection_of_localization_away
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07D1.** If finitely many elements `g j` generate the unit ideal of `S` and every
composite from `R` to the localization `S_{g j}` is a local complete intersection, then the
original ring homomorphism `R → S` is a local complete intersection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocalCompleteIntersection_of_localization_away
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S)
    {m : ℕ} (g : Fin m → S) (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
    (hlocal : ∀ j, RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection
      ((algebraMap S (Localization.Away (g j))).comp f)) :
    RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection f

declarations.name: RingHom.isKoszulRegular_relation_of_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
The relations in a polynomial presentation of a relative global complete intersection form a
Koszul-regular sequence in the polynomial ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isKoszulRegular_relation_of_isRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    {ι : Type w} [_root_.Finite ι] {c : ℕ} (P : Algebra.Presentation R S ι (Fin c))
    (hP : P.IsRelativeGlobalCompleteIntersection) :
    Koszul.IsKoszulRegular P.relation

declarations.name: RingHom.syntomic_iff_flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07D3.** A ring homomorphism is syntomic if and only if it is flat and a local
complete intersection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem syntomic_iff_flat_and_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) :
    letI := f.toAlgebra
    Algebra.Syntomic R S ↔ f.Flat ∧ RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection f

declarations.name: RingHom.cotangentMap_toComp_injective_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B → C` be ring maps, let `α : A[x_s] → B` and
`β : B[y₁, ..., yₘ] → C` be presentations, and write `K` for the kernel of the induced
presentation `β.comp α : A[x_s, y_t] → C`. If `B → C` is a local complete intersection, then
the canonical map `C ⊗_B (I / I²) → K / K²` is injective. Together with the canonical exact
conormal/differential diagram and the Jacobi--Zariski exactness lemmas, this gives the exact
sequence
`0 → H₁(NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C) → H₁(L_{C/A}) → H₁(L_{C/B}) →
C ⊗_B Ω[B⁄A] → Ω[C⁄A] → Ω[C⁄B] → 0`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cotangentMap_toComp_injective_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    {C : Type u₃} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Algebra B C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    {S : Type w} {m : ℕ} (α : Generators A B S) (β : Generators B C (Fin m))
    (h : RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap B C)) :
    Function.Injective
      ((Extension.Cotangent.map (β.toComp α).toExtensionHom).liftBaseChange C)
declarations.comment: the injectivity of C ⊗_B I/I² → K/K²

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariski_exact_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07D4.** Let `A → B → C` be ring maps with `B → C` a local complete intersection,
let `α : A[x_s] → B` be a presentation with kernel `I`, let `β : B[y₁, …, yₘ] → C` be a
presentation with kernel `J`, and let `γ = β.comp α : A[x_s, y_t] → C` be the induced
presentation, with kernel `K`. Then the canonical diagram, whose vertical maps are the
differentials of `NL(α) ⊗_B C`, `NL(γ)` and `NL(β)`, commutes, and both of its rows
```
0 ⟶ C ⊗_B Ω_{A[x]/A} ⟶ Ω_{A[x,y]/A} ⊗ C ⟶ Ω_{B[y]/B} ⊗ C ⟶ 0
0 ⟶   C ⊗_B I/I²     ⟶       K/K²        ⟶      J/J²      ⟶ 0
```
are exact. In particular the six-term sequence of Stacks 00S2 can be completed with a zero on
the left: the sequence
```
0 → H₁(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₁(NL(γ)) → H₁(NL(β)) --δ--> H₀(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₀(NL(γ)) → H₀(NL(β)) → 0
```
is exact, that is
`0 → H₁(NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C) → H₁(L_{C/A}) → H₁(L_{C/B}) → Ω_{B/A} ⊗_B C → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0`,
with `δ` the connecting map `NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariskiConnecting`.
declarations.statement:
theorem jacobiZariski_exact_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection {S : Type w} {m : ℕ}
    (α : Generators A B S) (β : Generators B C (Fin m))
    (h : RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap B C)) :
    -- the two squares of the canonical diagram commute
    ((NL (β.comp α)).d ∘ₗ (nlToComp β α).f₁ = (nlToComp β α).f₀ ∘ₗ (nlBaseChange C α).d ∧
      (NL β).d ∘ₗ (nlOfComp β α).f₁ = (nlOfComp β α).f₀ ∘ₗ (NL (β.comp α)).d) ∧
    -- the row of Kähler differentials is exact
    (Injective (nlToComp β α).f₀ ∧ Exact (nlToComp β α).f₀ (nlOfComp β α).f₀ ∧
      Surjective (nlOfComp β α).f₀) ∧
    -- the row of conormal modules is exact
    (Injective (nlToComp β α).f₁ ∧ Exact (nlToComp β α).f₁ (nlOfComp β α).f₁ ∧
      Surjective (nlOfComp β α).f₁) ∧
    -- the six-term sequence of Stacks 00S2, completed with a zero on the left, is exact
    (Injective (nlToComp β α).onH₁ ∧
      Exact (nlToComp β α).onH₁ (nlOfComp β α).onH₁ ∧
      Exact (nlOfComp β α).onH₁ (jacobiZariskiConnecting β α) ∧
      Exact (jacobiZariskiConnecting β α) (nlToComp β α).onH₀ ∧
      Exact (nlToComp β α).onH₀ (nlOfComp β α).onH₀ ∧
      Surjective (nlOfComp β α).onH₀)

declarations.name: NaiveCotangent.injective_onH₁_nlExtensionBaseChangeMap_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07D4, read on `H₁` over the canonical presentations.**  For ring maps `A → B → C`
with `B → C` a local complete intersection homomorphism, the canonical map

`NL_{B/A} ⊗_B C ⟶ NL_{C/A}`

of two-term complexes of `C`-modules is injective on `H₁`.  Together with the six-term exact
sequence of Stacks 00S2 this puts a zero at the left of that sequence.

The statement holds for every morphism of extensions inducing the comparison, any two being
homotopic.  Stacks 07D4 gives injectivity of the whole degree-`1` component for the presentation
`β.comp α` induced by the canonical presentation `α` of `B` over `A` and a finite presentation
`β` of `C` over `B`; the comparison of that presentation with the canonical presentation of `C`
over `A` is a quasi-isomorphism by Stacks 00S1 (4), and injectivity on `H₁` is inherited.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_onH₁_nlExtensionBaseChangeMap_of_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    (h : RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (algebraMap B C))
    (hom : (Generators.self A B).toExtension.Hom (Generators.self A C).toExtension) :
    Function.Injective (nlExtensionBaseChangeMap (T := C) hom).onH₁
declarations.comment: the zero on the left of the 00S2 sequence, over the canonical presentations

declarations.name: RingHom.cotangentMap_toComp_injective_of_isFilteredColimit_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B → C` be ring maps and suppose that `B → C` is exhibited as a filtered
colimit of local complete intersection homomorphisms, with `eB`, `eC`, and `hcomm` identifying
the directed system's colimit map with `B → C`. For presentations `α : A[x_s] → B`
and `β : B[y_t] → C`, the canonical map
`C ⊗_B (I / I²) → K / K²` from the conormal module of `α` to that of the induced
presentation `β.comp α` is injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem cotangentMap_toComp_injective_of_isFilteredColimit_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    {C : Type u₃} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Algebra B C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    {S : Type w} {T : Type w'} (α : Generators A B S) (β : Generators B C T)
    {J : Type u₄} [Preorder J] [IsDirectedOrder J] [Nonempty J]
    (sys : RingMapSystemUnbundled.{u₅} J)
    (eB : sys.Rinf ≃+* B) (eC : sys.Sinf ≃+* C)
    (hcomm : eC.toRingHom.comp sys.gInf = (algebraMap B C).comp eB.toRingHom)
    (h : ∀ i : J, RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (sys.g i)) :
    Function.Injective
      ((Extension.Cotangent.map (β.toComp α).toExtensionHom).liftBaseChange C)
declarations.comment:
The conormal form: injectivity of `C ⊗_B I/I² → K/K²`, the one assertion of the
source beyond Stacks 00S2. The complete statement, both exact rows and the seven-term sequence, is
`RingHom.jacobiZariski_exact_of_isFilteredColimit_isLocalCompleteIntersection`.

declarations.name: RingHom.jacobiZariski_exact_of_isFilteredColimit_isLocalCompleteIntersection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07D5.** Let `A → B → C` be ring maps and suppose that `B → C` is a filtered
colimit of local complete intersection homomorphisms, exhibited by a directed system `sys` of
ring maps each of which is a local complete intersection, together with `eB`, `eC` and `hcomm`
identifying the system's colimit map with `B → C`. Let `α : A[x_s] → B` and `β : B[y_t] → C` be
presentations and `γ = β.comp α` the induced presentation of `C` over `A`. Then the conclusion
of Stacks 07D4 holds:

* the degree-`0` row `0 → C ⊗_B Ω_{A[x]/A} → Ω_{A[x,y]/A} ⊗ C → Ω_{B[y]/B} ⊗ C → 0` and the
  degree-`1` row `0 → C ⊗_B I/I² → K/K² → J/J² → 0` of the canonical diagram are exact;
* the sequence
  `0 → H₁(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₁(NL(γ)) → H₁(NL(β)) → H₀(NL(α) ⊗_B C) → H₀(NL(γ)) → H₀(NL(β)) → 0`
  is exact, its connecting map being `NaiveCotangent.jacobiZariskiConnecting β α`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem jacobiZariski_exact_of_isFilteredColimit_isLocalCompleteIntersection
    {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    {C : Type u₃} [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] [Algebra B C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    {S : Type w} {T : Type w'} (α : Generators A B S) (β : Generators B C T)
    {J : Type u₄} [Preorder J] [IsDirectedOrder J] [Nonempty J]
    (sys : RingMapSystemUnbundled.{u₅} J)
    (eB : sys.Rinf ≃+* B) (eC : sys.Sinf ≃+* C)
    (hcomm : eC.toRingHom.comp sys.gInf = (algebraMap B C).comp eB.toRingHom)
    (h : ∀ i : J, RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection (sys.g i)) :
    (Injective (nlToComp β α).f₀ ∧ Exact (nlToComp β α).f₀ (nlOfComp β α).f₀ ∧
        Surjective (nlOfComp β α).f₀) ∧
      (Injective (nlToComp β α).f₁ ∧ Exact (nlToComp β α).f₁ (nlOfComp β α).f₁ ∧
        Surjective (nlOfComp β α).f₁) ∧
      Injective (nlToComp β α).onH₁ ∧
      Exact (nlToComp β α).onH₁ (nlOfComp β α).onH₁ ∧
      Exact (nlOfComp β α).onH₁ (jacobiZariskiConnecting β α) ∧
      Exact (jacobiZariskiConnecting β α) (nlToComp β α).onH₀ ∧
      Exact (nlToComp β α).onH₀ (nlOfComp β α).onH₀ ∧
      Surjective (nlOfComp β α).onH₀
declarations.comment:
The complete conclusion of 07D4 for a filtered colimit of lci maps: both exact
rows of the conormal/differential diagram and the seven-term Jacobi-Zariski sequence with a zero
on the left, for the naive cotangent complexes of the three presentations.

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isRepresentable_iff_preservesLimits
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Grothendieck abelian category and `F : Aᵒᵖ ⥤ Set` a functor. Then `F` is
representable if and only if it commutes with colimits, that is, `F (colim_i N_i) = lim_i F (N_i)`
for every diagram `I ⥤ A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRepresentable_iff_preservesLimits [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C]
    (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w) : F.IsRepresentable ↔ PreservesLimitsOfSize.{w, w} F

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.hasProducts_of_isGrothendieckAbelian
declarations.doc:
A Grothendieck abelian category has AB3\*, that is, it has products. Mathlib's name for AB3\*
is `CategoryTheory.Limits.HasProducts`, so there is nothing left to define here.

The Stacks project deduces this from its criterion for representability of a functor on a
Grothendieck abelian category: for a family `M_i` of objects the functor `F = ∏ h_{M_i}` commutes
with colimits, so it is representable, and the representing object is the product of the family.
Here we instead invoke `CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.hasLimits`, which gives all limits of
size `w` at once.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasProducts_of_isGrothendieckAbelian [CategoryTheory.IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} C] :
    HasProducts.{w} C

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.isLimit_productFanInDerivedCategory
declarations.doc:
The termwise product of K-injective representatives represents their product in the
unbounded derived category.
declarations.comment: termwise products of K-injective complexes

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.derivedCategoryQ_preservesCoproducts
declarations.doc:
The localization functor from complexes to the unbounded derived category preserves direct
sums; thus the image of the termwise direct sum of any family of complexes is its direct sum in
the derived category.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedCategoryQ_preservesCoproducts [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A] (I : Type w) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) (DerivedCategory.Q (C := A))
declarations.comment: direct_sums_termwise

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.hasCoproducts_derivedCategory
declarations.doc: The unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category has direct sums.
declarations.statement:
instance hasCoproducts_derivedCategory (A : Type u) [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{z} A] :
    HasCoproducts.{w} (DerivedCategory A)
declarations.comment: direct_sums_exist

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.hasProducts_derivedCategory
declarations.doc:
The unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category has arbitrary
products.
declarations.statement:
instance hasProducts_derivedCategory (𝒜 : Type u) [Category.{v} 𝒜] [Abelian 𝒜]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} 𝒜] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} 𝒜] :
    HasProducts.{w} (DerivedCategory 𝒜)
declarations.comment: products_exist

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_iff_appTop
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07DB.** A morphism of affine schemes is a local complete intersection morphism
exactly when the induced homomorphism of the rings of global sections is a local complete
intersection homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_iff_appTop {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X]
    [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f ↔ f.appTop.hom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.UnboundedDerivedPushforward.not_forall_derivedPushforward_mem_derivedLocallyQuasicoherentFlatBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07DD.** A quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic stacks
need not send `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` into `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒴)` under the unbounded derived direct
image `Rf_*`, read at module universe `u + 1`. The counterexample is the discussion of
**Stacks 07DC** with `p = 2`: `k = 𝔽₂`, `S = Spec k[x]`, `f : B(ℤ/2)_S ⟶ S` the structure
morphism and `E = ∏_{m ≥ 0} 𝒪_𝒳[m]`. The object `E` lies in `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)`
(`shiftedStructureSheafProduct_mem`), `Rf_*𝒪_𝒳` is computed by the cochain complex of `ℤ/2` with
coefficients `𝒪_S`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ClassifyingZModTwo.derivedPushforwardStructureModuleIso` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ClassifyingZModTwo.cechCosimplicialIso`), and then `H⁰(Rf_*E)` is a
countable product of copies of `𝒪_S`, which is not locally quasi-coherent
(`not_mem_derivedPushforward_of_iso`).
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_derivedPushforward_mem_derivedLocallyQuasicoherentFlatBaseChange :
    ¬ ∀ (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (E : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (h : E.cutoff = B.cutoff) (S : Scheme.{u})
        (hS : B.Contains S) (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} B S hS)
        [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} (fppfModulesUnivLE.{u, w, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳)]
        [HasDerivedCategory.{u + 2} (fppfModulesUnivLE.{u, w, u + 1} B S hS 𝒴)] (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴),
        IsQuasiCompactMorphism B S hS f → AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f →
        ∀ K, derivedLocallyQuasicoherentFlatBaseChangeUnivLE.{u, w, u + 1} B E h S hS 𝒳 K →
          derivedLocallyQuasicoherentFlatBaseChangeUnivLE.{u, w, u + 1} B E h S hS 𝒴
            ((fppfDerivedPushforwardOfStacks B S hS f).obj K)
declarations.comment: D_QCoh is read through the subcategory D_LQCoh^fbc of D(O) whose Verdier quotient it is (Tag 07B6), and Rf_* is the unbounded total derived direct image; the witness is the counterexample of Tag 07DC with p = 2

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.UnboundedDerivedPushforward.exists_not_derivedCategoryB_lqcFbcFppf_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07DD**, for the source's own example. Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p > 0`,
`S = Spec k[x]`, and let `𝒞` be any big fppf site containing `S`. The classifying stack
`𝒳 = [S/(ℤ/pℤ)]` and `S` itself are algebraic stacks over `S`, the structure morphism
`f : 𝒳 ⟶ S` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and for every choice of derived categories
the object `E = ⊕_{m ≥ 0} 𝒪_𝒳[m]` lies in `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` while `Rf_*E` does not lie in
`D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_S)`. So `Rf_*` does not carry `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` into `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_S)`
and does not induce a functor `D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_S)` on the Verdier quotients of
**Stacks 07B6** (`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.derivedCategoryQuasicoherentSheaf`, whose subcategory
`LQCoh^fbc` is `AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.lqcFbcFppf`).

`Rf_*` is the total right derived functor of the direct image of **Stacks 06WE** on the
unbounded derived categories of fppf modules
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.fppfModulesDerivedPushforward`).
The proof is the discussion of **Stacks 07DC**: see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_not_derivedCategoryB_lqcFbcFppf_derivedPushforward (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [CharP k p] (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u})
    (hS : 𝒞.Contains (Spec (.of (Polynomial k)))) :
    ∃ (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} 𝒞 (Spec (.of (Polynomial k))) hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴),
      IsQuasiCompactMorphism 𝒞 _ hS f ∧ AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated 𝒞 _ hS f ∧
      ∀ [HasDerivedCategory.{t} (fppfModules 𝒞 _ hS 𝒳)]
        [HasDerivedCategory.{t} (fppfModules 𝒞 _ hS 𝒴)],
        ∃ E : DerivedCategory (fppfModules 𝒞 _ hS 𝒳),
          DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (lqcFbcFppf 𝒞 _ hS 𝒳) E ∧
            ¬ DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (lqcFbcFppf 𝒞 _ hS 𝒴)
              ((fppfModulesDerivedPushforward 𝒞 _ hS f).obj E)
declarations.comment: for the source's example: f : [Spec k[x]/(Z/pZ)] -> Spec k[x] with char k = p, over any big fppf site containing Spec k[x], E = sum of O_X[m] in D_LQCoh^fbc(O_X) and Rf_*E not in D_LQCoh^fbc(O_S), with LQCoh^fbc the class of the Verdier quotient D_QCoh of 07B6 and Rf_* the unbounded total derived direct image

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.UnboundedDerivedPushforward.exists_isQuasiCompact_isQuasiSeparated_not_derivedCategoryB_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07DD.** A quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` of algebraic
stacks need not induce a functor `Rf_* : D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒳) ⟶ D_QCoh(𝒪_𝒴)`: there are a big fppf site
`𝒞`, a scheme `S` in it, algebraic stacks `𝒳`, `𝒴` over `S` and a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated `f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴` such that, for every choice of derived categories, some object `E` of
`D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒳)` has `Rf_*E` outside `D_{LQCoh^fbc}(𝒪_𝒴)`. The witness is the source's, with
`p = 2`: `exists_not_derivedCategoryB_lqcFbcFppf_derivedPushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isQuasiCompact_isQuasiSeparated_not_derivedCategoryB_derivedPushforward :
    ∃ (𝒞 : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : 𝒞.Contains S)
      (𝒳 𝒴 : AlgebraicStacks.{u, w} 𝒞 S hS) (f : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒴),
      IsQuasiCompactMorphism 𝒞 S hS f ∧ AlgebraicStacks.IsQuasiSeparated 𝒞 S hS f ∧
      ∀ [HasDerivedCategory.{t} (fppfModules 𝒞 S hS 𝒳)]
        [HasDerivedCategory.{t} (fppfModules 𝒞 S hS 𝒴)],
        ∃ E : DerivedCategory (fppfModules 𝒞 S hS 𝒳),
          DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (lqcFbcFppf 𝒞 S hS 𝒳) E ∧
            ¬ DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (lqcFbcFppf 𝒞 S hS 𝒴)
              ((fppfModulesDerivedPushforward 𝒞 S hS f).obj E)
declarations.comment: Rf_* does not carry D_LQCoh^fbc(O_X) into D_LQCoh^fbc(O_Y) for some qcqs f of algebraic stacks, so it does not induce D_QCoh(O_X) -> D_QCoh(O_Y) on the Verdier quotients of 07B6; Rf_* is the unbounded total derived direct image

declarations.name: Matrix.exists_mul_eq_smul_one_of_mem_minorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07DQ (1)**: every element of the ideal of maximal minors of `A` is realised as a
scalar left inverse of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mul_eq_smul_one_of_mem_minorIdeal {A : Matrix n m R} {f : R}
    (hf : f ∈ A.minorIdeal) : ∃ B : Matrix m n R, B * A = f • 1

declarations.name: Matrix.pow_card_mem_minorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07DQ (2)**: a scalar left inverse of `A` lies in the ideal of maximal minors of `A`
after raising it to the number of columns of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pow_card_mem_minorIdeal {A : Matrix n m R} {B : Matrix m n R} {f : R}
    (h : B * A = f • 1) : f ^ Fintype.card m ∈ A.minorIdeal

declarations.name: Matrix.mem_radical_minorIdeal_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07DQ**, both parts at once: the radical of the ideal of maximal minors of `A` is
exactly the set of scalars some power of which admits a left inverse against `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_radical_minorIdeal_iff {A : Matrix n m R} {f : R} :
    f ∈ A.minorIdeal.radical ↔ ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ B : Matrix m n R, B * A = (f ^ k) • 1

declarations.name: exists_matrix_of_mem_minorIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.** For any `f` in the ideal `J` generated by the `m × m`
minors of `A`, there is an `m × n` matrix `B` with `B * A = f • 1` (the `m × m`
matrix `f · I_m`).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_matrix_of_mem_minorIdeal (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) R)
    (f : R) (hf : f ∈ maximalMinorsIdeal A) :
    ∃ B : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) R, B * A = f • (1 : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) R)

declarations.name: pow_mem_minorIdeal_of_matrix
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2.** If `B * A = f • 1` for some `m × n` matrix `B`, then
`f ^ m` lies in the ideal `J` generated by the `m × m` minors of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pow_mem_minorIdeal_of_matrix (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin m) R)
    (f : R) (B : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) R)
    (hB : B * A = f • (1 : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) R)) :
    f ^ m ∈ maximalMinorsIdeal A

declarations.name: essFiniteType_comp
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.** The class of ring maps essentially of finite type is
preserved under composition (Stacks Tag 07DS, first assertion).

declarations.name: essFinitePresentation_comp
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2.** The class of ring maps essentially of finite presentation
is preserved under composition (Stacks Tag 07DS, second assertion).

The proof combines Stacks tag 053N, transitivity of finite presentation,
localization-of-localization, and a universe re-presentation:

1. Unpack `hf`: f.p. `R`-algebra `A`, with `S = M⁻¹A` (`IsLocalization M S`).
   Unpack `hg`: f.p. `S`-algebra `B`, with `T = N₂⁻¹B` (`IsLocalization N₂ T`).
2. `A` acts on `B` through `S` (`IsScalarTower A S B`).
3. `essFP_descent M B`: descend `B` to a f.p. `A`-algebra `B₀` with
   `B = N⁻¹B₀` (`IsLocalization N B`).
4. `Algebra.FinitePresentation.trans R A B₀`: since `A` is f.p./R and `B₀` is
   f.p./A, `B₀` is f.p./R.
5. localization-of-localization: `B = N⁻¹B₀` and `T = N₂⁻¹B`, so
   `T = U⁻¹B₀` for `U := localizationLocalizationSubmodule N N₂`
   (`IsLocalization.localization_localization_isLocalization`).
6. `essFP_reuniverse`: re-present the f.p. `R`-algebra `B₀ : Type (max u v w)`
   (with its localization `IsLocalization U T`) by a f.p. `R`-algebra
   `A' : Type (max u w)` carrying `IsLocalization U' T`, matching the universe
   demanded by `RingHom.EssentiallyOfFinitePresentation` for `g.comp f : R →+* T`.

declarations.name: finite_iff_residue_finite
declarations.doc: `f : R → S` is finite if and only if the composite `π ∘ f : R → S/m` is finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_iff_residue_finite (f : R →+* S) :
    f.Finite ↔ ((IsLocalRing.residue S).comp f).Finite

declarations.name: finiteType_iff_residue_finiteType
declarations.doc:
`f : R → S` is of finite type if and only if the composite `π ∘ f : R → S/m`
is of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteType_iff_residue_finiteType (f : R →+* S) :
    f.FiniteType ↔ ((IsLocalRing.residue S).comp f).FiniteType

declarations.name: essFiniteType_iff_residue_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
`f : R → S` is essentially of finite type if and only if the composite
`π ∘ f : R → S/m` is essentially of finite type.
declarations.statement:
theorem essFiniteType_iff_residue_essFiniteType (f : R →+* S) :
    f.EssFiniteType ↔ ((IsLocalRing.residue S).comp f).EssFiniteType

declarations.name: IsIdealOfDefinition
declarations.doc:
An ideal `I` of a Noetherian local ring `(R, m)` is an *ideal of definition* if its
radical is the maximal ideal, i.e. `√I = m`.
declarations.statement:
def IsIdealOfDefinition {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (I : Ideal R) : Prop

declarations.name: RingTheory.Sequence.isRegular_zipWith_pow_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07DV.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `M` be an `R`-module, let
`rs = [f₁, …, f_r]` be a list of elements of `R` and let `es = [e₁, …, e_r]` be a list of
positive integers of the same length. Then `f₁ ^ e₁, …, f_r ^ e_r` is an `M`-regular sequence
if and only if `f₁, …, f_r` is an `M`-regular sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem RingTheory.Sequence.isRegular_zipWith_pow_iff {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {rs : List R} {es : List ℕ}
    (hlen : rs.length = es.length) (hes : ∀ e ∈ es, 0 < e) :
    IsRegular M (rs.zipWith (· ^ ·) es) ↔ IsRegular M rs

declarations.name: tfae_isRegular_perm_sublist_polySeq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 07DW (Lemma 10.68.10).** For `fs = [f_1, …, f_r] : List R` whose entries
do not generate the unit ideal (`Ideal.span {x | x ∈ fs} ≠ ⊤`, i.e. `(f_1, …, f_r) ≠ R`),
the three conditions are equivalent. The proof is the 3-cycle `1 → 2 → 3 → 1`:
`1 → 2` extends a sublist to a permutation; `2 → 3` is `sg_two_to_three` (Stacks 07DV);
`3 → 1` is `sg_three_to_one` (variable-permutation automorphism + descent).
declarations.statement:
theorem tfae_isRegular_perm_sublist_polySeq (fs : List R) (hfs : Ideal.span {x | x ∈ fs} ≠ ⊤) :
    List.TFAE
      [ ∀ l' : List R, l'.Perm fs → IsRegular R l',
        ∀ l' : List R, l' <+ fs → IsRegular R l',
        IsRegular (MvPolynomial (Fin fs.length) R) (polySeq fs) ]

declarations.name: CommRingCat.isRegularLocalRing_pt_of_forall_isRegularLocalRing_of_forall_isLocalHom
declarations.doc:
Let `F : J ⥤ CommRingCat` be a directed system `(R i, φ i i')` of commutative rings over a
nonempty, `u`-small directed preorder `J`, and let `c` be a colimit cocone on `F`, so that `c.pt`
is `colim_i R i`. If every `R i` is a regular local ring, every transition map is a local ring map,
and the colimit is Noetherian, then the colimit is a regular local ring — in particular it is
local, its maximal ideal being the colimit of the maximal ideals of the `R i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularLocalRing_pt_of_forall_isRegularLocalRing_of_forall_isLocalHom
    {J : Type w} [Preorder J] [IsDirectedOrder J] [Nonempty J] [Small.{u} J]
    {F : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}}
    (hreg : ∀ j : J, IsRegularLocalRing (F.obj j))
    (hloc : ∀ ⦃i j : J⦄ (u : i ⟶ j), IsLocalHom (F.map u).hom)
    {c : Cocone F} (hc : IsColimit c) [IsNoetherianRing c.pt] :
    IsRegularLocalRing c.pt
declarations.comment:
The directed system is a functor on a nonempty `u`-small directed preorder together
  with an arbitrary colimit cocone, as in 0AS7; locality of a transition map is `IsLocalHom` of
  the underlying ring homomorphism; `IsRegularLocalRing` of the colimit includes the assertion
  that it is local. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Module.Flat.of_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_of_isWeaklyRegular_map
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a regular local ring, let `xs = x₁, …, x_d` be a regular system of parameters of
`R`, that is, a list generating `𝔪_R` whose length is the minimal number of generators of `𝔪_R`,
let `S` be a Noetherian local ring receiving a local homomorphism from `R` and let `M` be a
finite `S`-module. If the images of `x₁, …, x_d` in `S` form a weakly `M`-regular sequence, then
`M` is flat over `R`. Taking `M = S` shows that `R → S` is flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Module.Flat.of_ofList_eq_maximalIdeal_of_isWeaklyRegular_map
    {R : Type*} (S : Type*) (M : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] [CommRing S]
    [IsLocalRing S] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R S)]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module.Finite S M]
    (xs : List R) (hxs : Ideal.ofList xs = maximalIdeal R)
    (hmin : xs.length = (maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank)
    (hreg : IsWeaklyRegular M (xs.map (algebraMap R S))) :
    Module.Flat R M
declarations.comment:
Stated for a finite `S`-module `M` in place of `S` itself, the source's statement
being the case `M = S`; a regular system of parameters is a list generating the maximal ideal
whose length is its minimal number of generators; and the source's regular sequence is weakened
to `RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular`, its nonvanishing clause being replaced by
`IsLocalHom`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IntermediateField.finrank_adjoin_eq_pow_of_linearIndependent_D
declarations.doc:
**Adjoining `p`-th roots of elements with independent differentials.** Let `k` be a field of
characteristic `p > 0` and let `a : ι → k` be a finite family such that the differentials `d aᵢ`
are linearly independent in `Ω[k⁄𝔽_p]`. If `b : ι → K` is a family of `p`-th roots of the `aᵢ` in
an extension field `K/k`, then the field extension `k(a_1^{1/p}, …, a_n^{1/p}) = k(bᵢ : i)` has
degree `p ^ #ι` over `k`.
declarations.comment:
The source's `Ω_{k/𝔽_p}` is `Ω[k⁄ZMod p]`, characteristic `p > 0` is
`[Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (ZMod p) k]`, and `k(a_1^{1/p}, …, a_n^{1/p})` is
`IntermediateField.adjoin k (Set.range b)` for a family `b` of `p`-th roots in an ambient extension
`K/k`, which is unique since Frobenius is injective. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: trdeg_eq_finrank_kaehlerDifferential_sub_finrank_h1Cotangent
declarations.doc:
**Cartier's equality.** For a finitely generated extension of fields `K/k`, the module of
Kähler differentials and the first homology of the naive cotangent complex are
finite-dimensional, and their dimensions differ by the transcendence degree.
declarations.statement:
public theorem trdeg_eq_finrank_kaehlerDifferential_sub_finrank_h1Cotangent
    (k : Type u) (K : Type v) [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType k K] :
    FiniteDimensional K Ω[K⁄k] ∧
      FiniteDimensional K (Algebra.H1Cotangent k K) ∧
        (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg k K) : ℤ) =
          (Module.finrank K Ω[K⁄k] : ℤ) - Module.finrank K (Algebra.H1Cotangent k K)

declarations.name: jacobiZariski_exact_of_fieldExtensions
declarations.doc:
Let `M/L/K` be a tower of field extensions. Then the canonical Jacobi--Zariski sequence

`0 → H₁(L_{L/K}) ⊗[L] M → H₁(L_{M/K}) → H₁(L_{M/L}) →`
`M ⊗[L] Ω[L⁄K] → Ω[M⁄K] → Ω[M⁄L] → 0`

is exact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem jacobiZariski_exact_of_fieldExtensions
    (K : Type u₁) (L : Type u₂) (M : Type u₃)
    [Field K] [Field L] [Field M]
    [Algebra K L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra K M] [IsScalarTower K L M] :
    let i := (Algebra.H1Cotangent.map K K L M).liftBaseChange M
    let p := Algebra.H1Cotangent.map K L M M
    let δ := Algebra.H1Cotangent.δ K L M
    let d := KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange K L M
    let q := KaehlerDifferential.map K L M M
    Function.Injective i ∧
      Function.Exact i p ∧
      Function.Exact p δ ∧
      Function.Exact δ d ∧
      Function.Exact d q ∧
      Function.Surjective q

declarations.name: finrank_ker_sub_finrank_coker_kaehlerDifferential_map_sub_h1Cotangent_map_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
Given a commutative square of fields
```
K  → K'
↑    ↑
k  → k'
```
whose horizontal extensions `k'/k` and `K'/K` are finitely generated field extensions (possibly
transcendental), the kernels and cokernels of the canonical maps
`α : K' ⊗[K] Ω[K⁄k] → Ω[K'⁄k']` and `β : K' ⊗[K] H₁(L_{K/k}) → H₁(L_{K'/k'})` are
finite-dimensional. The alternating sum of their dimensions is the difference of the
transcendence degrees of the horizontal extensions.

A finitely generated field extension is expressed by `Algebra.EssFiniteType`, following Mathlib;
it is equivalent to `(⊤ : IntermediateField k k').FG` by `IntermediateField.fg_top_iff`. Both
transcendence degrees are finite, so they are written as `Cardinal.toNat` of `Algebra.trdeg`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    finrank_ker_sub_finrank_coker_kaehlerDifferential_map_sub_h1Cotangent_map_of_essFiniteType
    (k : Type u₁) (K : Type u₂) (k' : Type u₃) (K' : Type u₄)
    [Field k] [Field K] [Field k'] [Field K']
    [Algebra k K] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra K K'] [Algebra k' K'] [Algebra k K']
    [IsScalarTower k K K'] [IsScalarTower k k' K']
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType k k'] [Algebra.EssFiniteType K K'] :
    let α := (KaehlerDifferential.map k k' K K').liftBaseChange K'
    let β := (Algebra.H1Cotangent.map k k' K K').liftBaseChange K'
    FiniteDimensional K' (LinearMap.ker α) ∧
      FiniteDimensional K' (Ω[K'⁄k'] ⧸ LinearMap.range α) ∧
      FiniteDimensional K' (LinearMap.ker β) ∧
      FiniteDimensional K' (Algebra.H1Cotangent k' K' ⧸ LinearMap.range β) ∧
      (Module.finrank K' (LinearMap.ker α) : ℤ) -
          Module.finrank K' (Ω[K'⁄k'] ⧸ LinearMap.range α) -
          Module.finrank K' (LinearMap.ker β) +
          Module.finrank K' (Algebra.H1Cotangent k' K' ⧸ LinearMap.range β) =
      (Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg k k') : ℤ) -
          Cardinal.toNat (Algebra.trdeg K K')

declarations.name: geometricallyRegular_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem geometricallyRegular_tfae
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) (A : Type v)
    [Field k] [CharP k p] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    letI : Algebra (ZMod p) k := ZMod.algebra k p
    letI : Algebra (ZMod p) A :=
      ((algebraMap k A).comp (algebraMap (ZMod p) k)).toAlgebra
    letI : IsScalarTower (ZMod p) k A := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
    letI : Algebra k (PerfectClosure k p) := (PerfectClosure.of k p).toAlgebra
    List.TFAE [
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k A,
      (∀ (k' : IntermediateField k (PerfectClosure k p)),
        FiniteDimensional k k' →
        (∀ x : k', (x : PerfectClosure k p) ^ p ∈
          Set.range (algebraMap k (PerfectClosure k p))) →
        IsRegularRing (A ⊗[k] k')),
      IsRegularLocalRing A ∧
        Function.Injective
          (Algebra.H1Cotangent.map k A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
            (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)),
      IsRegularLocalRing A ∧
        Function.Injective
          ((KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange (ZMod p) k A).baseChange
            (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A))]

declarations.name: flat_localization_and_regular_quotient_of_basis_kaehlerDifferential
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a Noetherian local algebra over a field `k` of positive characteristic, and assume
that `A` is geometrically regular over `k`. Let `F` be a finitely generated intermediate field of
the residue field of `A`. If `yᵢ ∈ F` have differentials forming a basis of `Ω[F⁄k]`, and a
map `k[X₁, …, Xₘ] → A` lifts the `yᵢ`, then `A` is flat over its localization at the inverse
image of the maximal ideal, and the quotient of `A` by the extended prime is regular local.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_localization_and_regular_quotient_of_basis_kaehlerDifferential
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) (A : Type v)
