    [Field k] [CharP k p] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k A] (m : ℕ)
    (F : IntermediateField k (ResidueField A)) [Algebra.EssFiniteType k F]
    (y : Fin m → F) (b : Module.Basis (Fin m) F Ω[F⁄k])
    (hb : ∀ i, b i = KaehlerDifferential.D k F (y i))
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] A)
    (hφ : ∀ i, residue A (φ (MvPolynomial.X i)) = algebraMap F (ResidueField A) (y i)) :
    letI : Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) A := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    ∀ (A₀ : Type w) [CommRing A₀] [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) A₀]
      [IsLocalization.AtPrime A₀ ((maximalIdeal A).comap φ)] [Algebra A₀ A]
      [IsScalarTower (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) A₀ A],
      Module.Flat A₀ A ∧
        IsRegularLocalRing (A ⧸ Ideal.map φ ((maximalIdeal A).comap φ))

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.IsIdealOfDefinition
declarations.doc: An ideal of definition is open and its powers are cofinal among the neighborhoods of zero.
declarations.statement:
public def IsIdealOfDefinition {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    (I : Ideal R) : Prop

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.IsPreAdmissible
declarations.doc: A topological ring is pre-admissible if it has an ideal of definition.
declarations.statement: public def IsPreAdmissible (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] : Prop

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.IsAdmissible
declarations.doc: A topological ring is admissible if it is pre-admissible and complete.
declarations.statement:
public def IsAdmissible (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.IsPreAdic
declarations.doc:
A topological ring is pre-adic if an ideal of definition defines its topology through its
powers.
declarations.statement: public def IsPreAdic (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] : Prop

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.IsAdic
declarations.doc: A topological ring is adic if it is pre-adic and complete.
declarations.statement:
public def IsAdic (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: TopologicalRing.preAdic_and_adic_iff_admissible_and_open_powers
declarations.doc:
A (pre-)adic topological ring is equivalently a (pre-)admissible topological ring possessing
an ideal of definition all of whose positive powers are open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preAdic_and_adic_iff_admissible_and_open_powers
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R]
    [IsTopologicalRing R] [IsLinearTopology R R] :
    (IsPreAdic R ↔ IsPreAdmissible R ∧
      ∃ I : Ideal R, IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → IsOpen ((I ^ n : Ideal R) : Set R)) ∧
    (IsAdic R ↔ IsAdmissible R ∧
      ∃ I : Ideal R, IsIdealOfDefinition I ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → IsOpen ((I ^ n : Ideal R) : Set R))
declarations.comment: equivalent characterization

declarations.name: RingHom.continuous_adic_iff
declarations.doc:
A ring homomorphism `φ : R → S` between commutative rings is continuous with respect to the
`I`-adic topology on `R` and the `J`-adic topology on `S` if and only if there exists `n ≥ 1` with
`φ(I ^ n) ⊆ J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.continuous_adic_iff {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (φ : R →+* S) (I : Ideal R) (J : Ideal S) :
    @Continuous R S I.adicTopology J.adicTopology φ ↔
      ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧ ∀ x ∈ I ^ n, φ x ∈ J

declarations.name: IsFormallySmooth
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism between linearly topologized rings is formally smooth if it
is continuous and every compatible square-zero lifting problem with a discrete
target ring has a continuous lift.
declarations.statement:
def IsFormallySmooth.{u, v, w} {R : Type v} {S : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R] [IsLinearTopology R R]
    [CommRing S] [TopologicalSpace S] [IsTopologicalRing S] [IsLinearTopology S S]
    (φ : R →+* S) : Prop

declarations.name: RingHom.FormallySmoothTop.of_formallySmooth_of_isAdic
declarations.doc: Algebraic formal smoothness implies topological formal smoothness for an adic target.
declarations.statement:
theorem of_formallySmooth_of_isAdic.{u, v, w}
    {R : Type v} {S : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R]
    [TopologicalSpace S] [IsTopologicalRing S]
    (phi : R →+* S) (n : Ideal S) (hn : IsAdic n)
    (hphi : @Algebra.FormallySmooth R S _ _ phi.toAlgebra) :
    RingHom.FormallySmoothTop.{u, v, w} phi

declarations.name: isFormallySmooth_of_formallySmooth_and_isAdic_and_iff_discrete
declarations.doc:
Algebraic formal smoothness implies formal smoothness for any continuous
map from a linearly topologized ring to a pre-adic ring. Moreover, for ideals
`m ⊆ R` and `n ⊆ S`, a continuous map for the adic topologies is formally
smooth if and only if it is formally smooth with the discrete topology on
`R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFormallySmooth_of_formallySmooth_and_isAdic_and_iff_discrete.{u, v, w}
    {R : Type v} {S : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) :
    (∀ (tR : TopologicalSpace R) (tS : TopologicalSpace S),
      letI := tR
      letI := tS
      ∀ [IsTopologicalRing R] [IsLinearTopology R R]
        [IsTopologicalRing S] [IsLinearTopology S S],
        (∃ n : Ideal S, IsAdic n) →
          @Algebra.FormallySmooth R S _ _ φ.toAlgebra → Continuous φ →
            IsFormallySmooth.{u} φ) ∧
      ∀ (m : Ideal R) (n : Ideal S),
        (letI := m.adicTopology
         letI : IsTopologicalRing R := m.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
         letI := n.adicTopology
         letI : IsTopologicalRing S := n.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
         @Continuous R S m.adicTopology n.adicTopology φ) →
          ((letI := m.adicTopology
            letI : IsTopologicalRing R := m.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
            letI : IsLinearTopology R R := m.isLinearTopology
            letI := n.adicTopology
            letI : IsTopologicalRing S := n.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
            letI : IsLinearTopology S S := n.isLinearTopology
            IsFormallySmooth.{u} φ) ↔
           (letI : TopologicalSpace R := ⊥
            letI : DiscreteTopology R := ⟨rfl⟩
            letI := n.adicTopology
            letI : IsTopologicalRing S := n.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
            letI : IsLinearTopology S S := n.isLinearTopology
            IsFormallySmooth.{u} φ))

declarations.name: isFormallySmooth_iff_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
Formal smoothness of a continuous homomorphism of adic rings is unchanged
by completing the target, or by completing both source and target.

The hypotheses are exactly those of Stacks 07ED: rings `R` and `S` with
finitely generated ideals `m` and `n`, endowed with the `m`-adic and `n`-adic
topologies, and a continuous ring homomorphism `f : R →+* S`. The completions
carry the adic topologies of the extended ideals `m R^∧` and `n S^∧`; since `m`
and `n` are finitely generated, these are the `m`-adic and `n`-adic topologies
of the completions (Stacks 05GG).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFormallySmooth_iff_adicCompletion.{u, v, w}
    {R : Type v} {S : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (m : Ideal R) (n : Ideal S) (hm : m.FG) (hn : n.FG) (f : R →+* S)
    (hf : @Continuous R S m.adicTopology n.adicTopology f) :
    letI : WithIdeal R := ⟨m⟩
    letI : WithIdeal S := ⟨n⟩
    let mhat : Ideal (Completion R) := m.map Completion.coeRingHom
    let nhat : Ideal (Completion S) := n.map Completion.coeRingHom
    let fhat : Completion R →+* Completion S := Completion.mapRingHom f hf
    let toShat : R →+* Completion S := Completion.coeRingHom.comp f
    letI : TopologicalSpace (Completion R) := mhat.adicTopology
    letI : IsTopologicalRing (Completion R) := mhat.nonarchimedean.toIsTopologicalRing
    letI : IsLinearTopology (Completion R) (Completion R) := mhat.isLinearTopology
    letI : TopologicalSpace (Completion S) := nhat.adicTopology
    letI : IsTopologicalRing (Completion S) := nhat.nonarchimedean.toIsTopologicalRing
    letI : IsLinearTopology (Completion S) (Completion S) := nhat.isLinearTopology
    (IsFormallySmooth.{u} f ↔ IsFormallySmooth.{u} toShat) ∧
      (IsFormallySmooth.{u} toShat ↔ IsFormallySmooth.{u} fhat)

declarations.name: RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.mono
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 07EE, Lemma 15.38.6: if `n ≤ n'` are ideals of `S` and `φ : R → S`
is formally smooth for the `n`-adic topology, then it is formally smooth for the
`n'`-adic topology. Usable as `h.mono hnn'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormallySmoothNAdic.mono {R : Type v} {S : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    {φ : R →+* S} {n n' : Ideal S} (h : FormallySmoothNAdic.{u, v, w} φ n) (hnn' : n ≤ n') :
    FormallySmoothNAdic.{u, v, w} φ n'

declarations.name: RingHom.FormallySmoothTop.comp
declarations.doc:
Stacks Lemma 15.38.7 (Tag 07EF). A composition of formally smooth continuous
ring homomorphisms of topological rings is formally smooth: if `φ : R →+* S` and
`ψ : S →+* T` are formally smooth and `ψ` is continuous, then `ψ.comp φ` is
formally smooth. Usable as `hsφ.comp hsψ hψ`. Continuity of `ψ.comp φ` is not
part of the conclusion; it follows from `Continuous.comp` given that `φ` is
continuous.

declarations.name: RingHom.formallySmoothTop_iff_formallySmoothNAdic
declarations.doc:
For a discrete source and an adic target, topological formal smoothness is equivalent to
formal smoothness for the adic topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmoothTop_iff_formallySmoothNAdic.{u, v, w}
    {R : Type v} {S : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R] [DiscreteTopology R]
    [TopologicalSpace S] [IsTopologicalRing S]
    (phi : R →+* S) (n : Ideal S) (hn : IsAdic n) :
    FormallySmoothTop.{u, v, w} phi ↔ FormallySmoothNAdic.{u, v, w} phi n

declarations.name: RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.baseChange
declarations.doc:
Formal smoothness for the `n`-adic topology is preserved by arbitrary base change from
`R` to `R'`; on `S ⊗[R] R'`, the adic ideal is the extension of `n`.

declarations.name: isFormallySmooth_adic_of_split_baseChange
declarations.doc:
If `R → R'` admits an `R`-linear retraction and the base change
`R' → S ⊗[R] R'` is formally smooth for the topology defined by the
extension of `n`, then `R → S` is formally smooth for the `n`-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFormallySmooth_adic_of_split_baseChange.{u, v, w, z}
    {R : Type v} {S : Type w} {R' : Type z}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R R']
    (n : Ideal S)
    (hsplit : ∃ p : R' →ₗ[R] R,
      p.comp (Algebra.linearMap R R') = LinearMap.id)
    (hsmooth :
      letI : Algebra R' (S ⊗[R] R') :=
        Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra (R := R) (A := S) (B := R')
      let n' : Ideal (S ⊗[R] R') :=
        Ideal.map (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft : S →ₐ[R] S ⊗[R] R') n
      letI : TopologicalSpace R' := ⊥
      letI : DiscreteTopology R' := ⟨rfl⟩
      letI : TopologicalSpace (S ⊗[R] R') := n'.adicTopology
      letI : IsTopologicalRing (S ⊗[R] R') := n'.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
      letI : IsLinearTopology (S ⊗[R] R') (S ⊗[R] R') := n'.isLinearTopology
      IsFormallySmooth.{max u z} (algebraMap R' (S ⊗[R] R'))) :
    letI : TopologicalSpace R := ⊥
    letI : DiscreteTopology R := ⟨rfl⟩
    letI : TopologicalSpace S := n.adicTopology
    letI : IsTopologicalRing S := n.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
    letI : IsLinearTopology S S := n.isLinearTopology
    IsFormallySmooth.{u} (algebraMap R S)

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_of_isFormallySmooth_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian local algebra over a field that is formally smooth for its
maximal-ideal adic topology is a regular local ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_isFormallySmooth_maximalIdeal.{v, w}
    {k : Type v} {A : Type w} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (h : FormallySmoothDiscreteMaximalIdeal.{max v w, v, w} (algebraMap k A)) :
    IsRegularLocalRing A

declarations.name: RingHom.FormallySmoothTop.isRegularLocalRing_of_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian local algebra over a field is regular if its structure map
is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal adic topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularLocalRing_of_maximalIdeal.{v, w}
    {k : Type v} {A : Type w} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (h :
      let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
      let : TopologicalSpace k := ⊥
      let : DiscreteTopology k := ⟨rfl⟩
      let : TopologicalSpace A := m.adicTopology
      let : IsTopologicalRing A := m.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
      let : IsLinearTopology A A := m.isLinearTopology
      RingHom.FormallySmoothTop.{max v w} (algebraMap k A)) :
    IsRegularLocalRing A

declarations.name: isFormallySmooth_maximalIdeal_of_isRegularLocalRing
declarations.doc:
A regular local algebra over a field whose residue field is separable over
the base field is formally smooth for its maximal-ideal adic topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFormallySmooth_maximalIdeal_of_isRegularLocalRing.{u, v, w}
    {k : Type v} {A : Type w} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [IsRegularLocalRing A]
    (hsep : Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)) :
    FormallySmoothDiscreteMaximalIdeal.{u, v, w} (algebraMap k A)

declarations.name: formalSmoothness_maximalIdeal_characterizations
declarations.statement:
public theorem formalSmoothness_maximalIdeal_characterizations
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    (let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
     letI : TopologicalSpace k := ⊥
     letI : DiscreteTopology k := ⟨rfl⟩
     letI : TopologicalSpace A := m.adicTopology
     letI : IsTopologicalRing A := m.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
     letI : IsLinearTopology A A := m.isLinearTopology
     ∀ [CharZero k],
       IsRegularLocalRing A ↔
         IsFormallySmooth.{max u v} (algebraMap k A)) ∧
    (∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p],
      letI : Algebra (ZMod p) k := ZMod.algebra k p
      letI : Algebra (ZMod p) A :=
        ((algebraMap k A).comp (algebraMap (ZMod p) k)).toAlgebra
      letI : IsScalarTower (ZMod p) k A := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
      letI : Algebra k (PerfectClosure k p) := (PerfectClosure.of k p).toAlgebra
      let m := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
      letI : TopologicalSpace k := ⊥
      letI : DiscreteTopology k := ⟨rfl⟩
      letI : TopologicalSpace A := m.adicTopology
      letI : IsTopologicalRing A := m.ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
      letI : IsLinearTopology A A := m.isLinearTopology
      List.TFAE [
        Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k A,
        IsFormallySmooth.{max u v} (algebraMap k A),
        (∀ (k' : IntermediateField k (PerfectClosure k p)),
          FiniteDimensional k k' →
          (∀ x : k', (x : PerfectClosure k p) ^ p ∈
            Set.range (algebraMap k (PerfectClosure k p))) →
          IsRegularRing (A ⊗[k] k')),
        IsRegularLocalRing A ∧
          Function.Injective
            (Algebra.H1Cotangent.map k A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
              (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)),
        IsRegularLocalRing A ∧
          Function.Injective
            ((KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange (ZMod p) k A).baseChange
              (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A))])

declarations.name: formallySmooth_adic_examples_with_inseparable_residueField
declarations.doc:
In characteristic `p`, the local ring
`k[x, y]_(x, y ^ p - a) / (y ^ p - a - x)` is geometrically regular over `k`, formally
smooth both algebraically and for its maximal-ideal-adic topology, and has purely inseparable
residue field. Closely relatedly, if `K` is the perfect closure of `𝔽ₚ(t)`, there is a map
`𝔽ₚ(s) → K[[x]]` sending `s` to `t + x` which is formally smooth for the `(x)`-adic topology.
For the latter map, `ds` and `dx` are the indicated bases of the Kähler differentials and the
map on differentials sends `ds` to `dx`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem formallySmooth_adic_examples_with_inseparable_residueField
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    (∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p] (a : k),
      a ∉ Set.range (fun b : k => b ^ p) →
      let P := MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k
      let m : Ideal P := Ideal.span
        {MvPolynomial.X 0, MvPolynomial.X 1 ^ p - MvPolynomial.C a}
      let g : P := MvPolynomial.X 1 ^ p - MvPolynomial.C a - MvPolynomial.X 0
      ∃ hm : m.IsPrime,
        letI : m.IsPrime := hm
        let B := Localization.AtPrime m
        let A := B ⧸ Ideal.span {algebraMap P B g}
        ∃ hlocal : IsLocalRing A,
          letI : IsLocalRing A := hlocal
          IsNoetherianRing A ∧
          Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k A ∧
          IsPurelyInseparable k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) ∧
          Algebra.FormallySmooth k A ∧
          let n := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
          @IsAdicallyFormallySmooth k A _ _ n (algebraMap k A)) ∧
    (let k := RatFunc (ZMod p)
     let K := PerfectClosure k p
     letI : Algebra k K := (PerfectClosure.of k p).toAlgebra
     let A := PowerSeries K
     ∃ f : k →+* A,
       f RatFunc.X =
          PowerSeries.C (algebraMap k K RatFunc.X) + PowerSeries.X ∧
       letI : Algebra k A := f.toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra (ZMod p) A :=
         (f.comp (algebraMap (ZMod p) k)).toAlgebra
       letI : IsScalarTower (ZMod p) k A :=
         IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' rfl
       (∃ b : Module.Basis Unit k (KaehlerDifferential (ZMod p) k),
          b () = KaehlerDifferential.D (ZMod p) k RatFunc.X) ∧
       (∃ b : Module.Basis Unit A (KaehlerDifferential (ZMod p) A),
          b () = KaehlerDifferential.D (ZMod p) A PowerSeries.X) ∧
       KaehlerDifferential.map (ZMod p) (ZMod p) k A
           (KaehlerDifferential.D (ZMod p) k RatFunc.X) =
         KaehlerDifferential.D (ZMod p) A PowerSeries.X ∧
       let x : Ideal A := Ideal.span {PowerSeries.X}
       @IsAdicallyFormallySmooth k A _ _ x f)

declarations.doc: **Stacks 07EN.** A local complete intersection homomorphism is perfect.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalCompleteIntersection.perfect {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] {f : A →+* B} (h : IsLocalCompleteIntersection f) : f.Perfect

declarations.name: isRegularRingHom_of_filteredColimit_smooth
declarations.doc:
The colimit of a small nonempty directed system of smooth `R`-algebras, computed on
underlying sets, whose residue-field fibres are Noetherian is regular over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRingHom_of_filteredColimit_smooth
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {J : Type w} [Preorder J] [IsDirectedOrder J] [Nonempty J] [Small.{max u v} J]
    (F : J ⥤ CommAlgCat.{v} R) (c : Cocone F) (hc : IsColimit c)
    [PreservesColimit (F ⋙ forget₂ (CommAlgCat.{v} R) CommRingCat.{v})
      (forget CommRingCat.{v})]
    (hsm : ∀ j, Algebra.Smooth R (F.obj j))
    (hnoeth : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], IsNoetherianRing (p.Fiber c.pt)) :
    IsRegularRingHom (algebraMap R c.pt)

declarations.name: isRegularRingHom_iff_isSeparableExtension
declarations.doc: A field extension is a regular ring map if and only if it is separable.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_comp_eq_lsmul_of_eq_sum_jacobianMinor
declarations.doc:
A strictly standard equation supplies a left inverse to its Jacobian map. Only the equation
16.2.3.3 is used; the relation-ideal condition 16.2.3.4 is not needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_comp_eq_lsmul_of_eq_sum_jacobianMinor
    (P : Presentation R A) (a : A) (c : ℕ) (hcm : c ≤ P.m)
    (ha : ∃ aI : Finset (Fin P.n) → A,
      a = ∑ s ∈ Finset.powersetCard c (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin P.n)),
        aI s * P.lift (if h : s.card = c then P.jacobianMinor c hcm s h else 0)) :
    ∃ ψ : (Fin P.n → A) →ₗ[A] (Fin c → A),
      ψ.comp (Matrix.toLin' (jacobianMatrix P c hcm)) =
        LinearMap.lsmul A (Fin c → A) a
declarations.comment: the forward half: the equation of 07ER implies that there is an `A`-linear `ψ : ⊕_{i = 1,…,n} A dx_i → A^{⊕c}` whose composition with `A^{⊕c} →^{(f_1,…,f_c)} I/I² →^{f ↦ df} ⊕_{i = 1,…,n} A dx_i` is multiplication by `a`. The two-step composite is the Jacobian map `jacobianMatrix`, whose `j`-th column is `d f_j`. Only 07ER is hypothesised, as in the source; the condition of 07ES is not assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_pow_eq_sum_jacobianMinor_of_comp_eq_lsmul
declarations.doc:
A left inverse to the Jacobian expresses the corresponding power as a sum of Jacobian minors
(the equation of Stacks 07ER). This also holds for `c = 0`, when the empty minor is `1`; the
relation-ideal condition of Stacks 07ES is a separate requirement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pow_eq_sum_jacobianMinor_of_comp_eq_lsmul
    (P : Presentation R A) (a : A) (c : ℕ) (hcm : c ≤ P.m)
    (ψ : (Fin P.n → A) →ₗ[A] (Fin c → A))
    (hψ : ψ.comp (Matrix.toLin' (jacobianMatrix P c hcm)) =
      LinearMap.lsmul A (Fin c → A) a) :
    ∃ aI : Finset (Fin P.n) → A,
      a ^ c = ∑ s ∈ Finset.powersetCard c (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin P.n)),
        aI s * P.lift (if h : s.card = c then P.jacobianMinor c hcm s h else 0)
declarations.comment: the converse half: if such a `ψ` exists — that is, if some `A`-linear `ψ : ⊕_{i = 1,…,n} A dx_i → A^{⊕c}` composed with `A^{⊕c} →^{(f_1,…,f_c)} I/I² →^{f ↦ df} ⊕_{i = 1,…,n} A dx_i` is multiplication by `a` — then `a ^ c` satisfies the equation of 07ER. As in the source the conclusion is only that equation, not the condition of 07ES

declarations.name: exists_smooth_factorization_of_singularIdeal_map_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Given ring maps `R → A → Λ` with `A` of finite presentation over `R`, if the image of the
singular ideal `H_{A/R}` generates the unit ideal of `Λ`, then `A → Λ` factors as
`A → B → Λ` with `B` smooth over `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_factorization_of_singularIdeal_map_eq_top
    (R : Type u) (A : Type v) (Λ : Type w) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing Λ]
    [Algebra R A] [Algebra A Λ] [Algebra R Λ] [IsScalarTower R A Λ]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A]
    (h : Ideal.map (algebraMap A Λ) (singularIdeal R A) = ⊤) :
    ∃ (B : Type (max v w)) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra R B) (_ : Algebra A B)
      (_ : Algebra B Λ),
      IsScalarTower R A B ∧ IsScalarTower A B Λ ∧ IsScalarTower R B Λ ∧ Algebra.Smooth R B

declarations.name: cotangentComplex_of_isSymmetricAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07EV, corrected.** Let `0 → K → Aᵐ → M → 0` be exact and let `C` be the symmetric
algebra on `M`. For the induced polynomial presentation of `C`, there is a canonical surjection
`C ⊗[A] K → P.Cotangent` compatible with the map into `Cᵐ`, and `Ω[C⁄A]` is canonically
`C ⊗[A] M`. The last three conditions pin down the canonical maps: polynomial differentials go to
the standard basis, `1 ⊗ₜ k` goes to the conormal class of its linear relation, and the
differential of a symmetric-algebra generator goes to `1 ⊗ₜ x`.

Stacks states that `NL(α) = (K ⊗_A C → ⊕ C dy_j)`, i.e. that this surjection is an isomorphism.
That is false: `not_forall_cotangentEquiv_of_isSymmetricAlgebra` gives `A = ℤ`, `K = ℤ²`,
`i = 2`, `M = (ℤ/2)²`, where `y₂ ⊗ e₁ - y₁ ⊗ e₂` is a nonzero element of the kernel. What is true in
general is the statement here: the conormal module is a quotient of `K ⊗_A C` compatibly with the
maps to `⊕ C dy_j`, so `Ω_{C/A} = M ⊗_A C`. (When `M` is projective, `K → Aᵐ` splits and the map
is an isomorphism.)
declarations.statement:
theorem cotangentComplex_of_isSymmetricAlgebra
    {A : Type uA} {K : Type uK} {M : Type uM} [CommRing A]
    [AddCommGroup K] [Module A K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    (m : ℕ) (i : K →ₗ[A] (Fin m → A)) (p : (Fin m → A) →ₗ[A] M)
    (_hi : Function.Injective i) (hip : Function.Exact i p) (hp : Function.Surjective p)
    (C : Type uC) [CommRing C] [Algebra A C]
    (ι : M →ₗ[A] C) (hC : IsSymmetricAlgebra ι)
    (α : MvPolynomial (Fin m) A →ₐ[A] C) (hα : Function.Surjective α)
    (hαX : ∀ j, α (MvPolynomial.X j) = ι (p ((Pi.basisFun A (Fin m)) j))) :
    let P := Algebra.Extension.ofSurjective α hα
    ∃ (eK : C ⊗[A] K →ₗ[C] P.Cotangent)
      (eF : P.CotangentSpace ≃ₗ[C] (Fin m → C))
      (eΩ : KaehlerDifferential A C ≃ₗ[C] C ⊗[A] M),
      Function.Surjective eK ∧
        eF.toLinearMap ∘ₗ P.cotangentComplex ∘ₗ eK =
          (TensorProduct.piScalarRight A C C (Fin m)).toLinearMap ∘ₗ i.baseChange C ∧
        (∀ j, eF (1 ⊗ₜ[P.Ring]
          KaehlerDifferential.D A P.Ring (MvPolynomial.X j)) = Pi.single j 1) ∧
        (∀ k, ∃ hk : (∑ j, MvPolynomial.C (i k j) * MvPolynomial.X j) ∈ P.ker,
          eK (1 ⊗ₜ k) = Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.mk
            ⟨∑ j, MvPolynomial.C (i k j) * MvPolynomial.X j, hk⟩) ∧
        ∀ x, eΩ (KaehlerDifferential.D A C (ι x)) = 1 ⊗ₜ x
declarations.comment: corrected: K ⊗_A C → J/J² is a canonical surjection, compatible with the maps to ⊕ C dy_j, and Ω_{C/A} = M ⊗_A C; the isomorphism K ⊗_A C ≅ J/J² claimed by Stacks fails

declarations.name: not_forall_cotangentEquiv_of_isSymmetricAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07EV is false as printed.** The lemma asserts that for an exact sequence
`0 → K → Aᵐ → M → 0` and `C = Sym_A(M)` presented by `α : A[y_1, …, y_m] → C`, the conormal
module `J/J²` of `α` is `K ⊗_A C`, with `1 ⊗ k` corresponding to the class of the linear relation
`∑ i(k)_j y_j`. This fails for `A = ℤ`, `K = ℤ²`, `i = 2`, `M = (ℤ/2)²`: the element
`y₂ ⊗ e₁ - y₁ ⊗ e₂` of `C ⊗ K` is nonzero but goes to the class of `y₂ · 2y₁ - y₁ · 2y₂ = 0`.
So no `C`-linear isomorphism `C ⊗[A] K ≃ P.Cotangent` sends `1 ⊗ₜ k` to that class. The correct
statement is `cotangentComplex_of_isSymmetricAlgebra`, where the canonical map is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_forall_cotangentEquiv_of_isSymmetricAlgebra :
    ¬ ∀ (A K M : Type) [CommRing A] [AddCommGroup K] [Module A K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
      (m : ℕ) (i : K →ₗ[A] (Fin m → A)) (p : (Fin m → A) →ₗ[A] M),
      Function.Injective i → Function.Exact i p → Function.Surjective p →
      ∀ (C : Type) [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] (ι : M →ₗ[A] C), IsSymmetricAlgebra ι →
      ∀ (α : MvPolynomial (Fin m) A →ₐ[A] C) (hα : Function.Surjective α),
      (∀ j, α (MvPolynomial.X j) = ι (p ((Pi.basisFun A (Fin m)) j))) →
      let P := Algebra.Extension.ofSurjective α hα
      ∃ eK : C ⊗[A] K ≃ₗ[C] P.Cotangent,
        ∀ k : K, ∃ hk : (∑ j : Fin m, MvPolynomial.C (σ := Fin m) (i k j) *
            MvPolynomial.X (R := A) j) ∈ P.ker,
          eK (1 ⊗ₜ k) = Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.mk
            ⟨∑ j, MvPolynomial.C (i k j) * MvPolynomial.X j, hk⟩
declarations.comment: counterexample: for A = ℤ, K = ℤ², i = 2, M = (ℤ/2)², the canonical map K ⊗_A C → J/J² has nonzero kernel, so J/J² is not K ⊗_A C as claimed

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.localizedConormalEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical description of the conormal module of the genuine localization presentation.
The first factor is generated by the newly adjoined relation `P.σ(a) X - 1`; the second is the
localized old conormal module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizedConormalEquiv
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra A S] [IsScalarTower R A S]
    {I : Type uι} (P : Algebra.Generators R A I) (a : A)
    [IsLocalization.Away a S] :
    ((Algebra.Generators.localizationAway S a).comp P).toExtension.Cotangent ≃ₗ[S]
      S × (S ⊗[A] P.toExtension.Cotangent)
declarations.comment: the two localized conormal-module identifications

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.localizedConormalEquiv_freeGenerator
declarations.doc:
The direct-sum identification sends the class of the new relation `P.σ(a) X - 1` to the free
generator.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedConormalEquiv_freeGenerator
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra A S] [IsScalarTower R A S]
    {I : Type uι} (P : Algebra.Generators R A I) (a : A)
    [IsLocalization.Away a S] :
    (localizedConormalEquiv (S := S) P a)
        (localizationRelationCotangent (S := S) P a) = (1, 0)
declarations.comment: the free generator in the localized identifications

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.localizedConormalEquiv_symm_comp_inr
declarations.doc:
On the localized old conormal summand, the inverse direct-sum identification is the canonical
base-changed conormal map.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedConormalEquiv_symm_comp_inr
    {S : Type*} [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra A S] [IsScalarTower R A S]
    {I : Type uι} (P : Algebra.Generators R A I) (a : A)
    [IsLocalization.Away a S] :
    (localizedConormalEquiv (S := S) P a).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ
        LinearMap.inr S S (S ⊗[A] P.toExtension.Cotangent) =
      (Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map
        ((Algebra.Generators.localizationAway S a).toComp P).toExtensionHom).liftBaseChange S
declarations.comment: compatibility of the localized identifications

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.localizedConormalSequence_exact
declarations.doc: Exactness at `C_a ⊕ (J/J²)_a` in the localized conormal sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedConormalSequence_exact
    (a : A) [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap A C a) L]
    {K : Type uK} [AddCommGroup K] [Module A K]
    (eK : (L ⊗[C] Q.toExtension.Cotangent) ≃ₗ[L] (L ⊗[A] K)) :
    Function.Exact (localizedConormalIncoming P Q)
      (localizedConormalOutgoing P Q eK)
declarations.comment: exactness at the middle term

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.localizedConormalSequence_surjective
declarations.doc: The final arrow is surjective, so the localized conormal sequence ends in zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizedConormalSequence_surjective
    (a : A) [IsLocalization.Away (algebraMap A C a) L]
    {K : Type uK} [AddCommGroup K] [Module A K]
    (eK : (L ⊗[C] Q.toExtension.Cotangent) ≃ₗ[L] (L ⊗[A] K)) :
    Function.Surjective (localizedConormalOutgoing P Q eK)
declarations.comment: surjectivity onto the final term

declarations.name: standardSmooth_presentation_with_prescribed_generators
declarations.statement:
theorem standardSmooth_presentation_with_prescribed_generators
    (R A : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    (hA : IsStandardSmoothRingMap R A) (E : Finset A) (n : ℕ) (hn : E.card = n) :
    ∃ (m c : ℕ) (_ : n ≤ c) (hcnm : c ≤ n + m)
      (f : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R)
      (π : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + m)) R →ₐ[R] A),
      -- (1) Presentation: `π` is surjective with kernel `(f_1, ..., f_c)`.
      (Function.Surjective π ∧
        RingHom.ker π.toRingHom = Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ∧
      -- (2) Standard smooth Jacobian condition: the image of the Jacobian
      -- determinant is invertible in `A`.
      IsUnit (π (jacobianDet hcnm f)) ∧
      -- (3) Generators include `E`: `E` equals the set of images of the first `n`
      -- variables `x_1, ..., x_n`.
      (E : Set A) = Set.range (fun i : Fin n => π (X (Fin.castAdd m i)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_eventually_isStrictlyStandard_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 16.3.7 (e).** Let `R → A` be of finite presentation and `a ∈ A`. If `A_a` is
smooth over `R` and `Ω_{A_a/R}` is stably free, then `a ^ e` is strictly standard in `A` over
`R` for every sufficiently large `e`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eventually_isStrictlyStandard_pow (S : SixStandardnessConditions.{u, v})
    (hS : Algebra.Smooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a) ∧
      Module.IsStablyFree (Localization.Away S.a)
        (KaehlerDifferential S.R (Localization.Away S.a))) :
    ∃ e₀ : ℕ, ∀ e : ℕ, e₀ ≤ e → IsStrictlyStandard (R := S.R) (S.a ^ e)
declarations.comment: clause (e), the implication (2) ⇒ `a ^ e` is strictly standard in `A` over `R` for all `e ≥ e_0`: the conclusion is `∃ e₀, ∀ e, e₀ ≤ e → ...`, the source's all sufficiently large powers, and not merely that some power is strictly standard

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.standardSmooth_localization_isSmooth_and_free
declarations.doc:
Standard smoothness of `A_a` implies condition (3): `A_a` is smooth over `R` and its module
of relative differentials is free.
declarations.statement:
theorem standardSmooth_localization_isSmooth_and_free
    (S : SixStandardnessConditions)
    (h : Algebra.IsStandardSmooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a)) :
      Algebra.Smooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a) ∧
      Module.Free (Localization.Away S.a)
        (KaehlerDifferential S.R (Localization.Away S.a))
declarations.comment: clause (a), the implication (4) ⇒ (3): if `A_a` is standard smooth over `R` then `A_a` is smooth over `R` and `Ω_{A_a/R}` is free

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.free_of_differentials_implies_stably_free
declarations.doc: Condition (3) implies condition (2): a free module of differentials is stably free.
declarations.statement:
theorem free_of_differentials_implies_stably_free
    (S : SixStandardnessConditions)
    (h : Algebra.Smooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a) ∧
      Module.Free (Localization.Away S.a)
        (KaehlerDifferential S.R (Localization.Away S.a))) :
    Algebra.Smooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a) ∧
      Module.IsStablyFree (Localization.Away S.a)
        (KaehlerDifferential S.R (Localization.Away S.a))
declarations.comment: clause (a), the implication (3) ⇒ (2): if `A_a` is smooth over `R` and `Ω_{A_a/R}` is free then it is stably free

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.smooth_of_smooth_and_stablyFree_differentials
declarations.doc: Condition (2) implies condition (1): smoothness of `A_a` over `R`.
declarations.statement:
lemma smooth_of_smooth_and_stablyFree_differentials (S : SixStandardnessConditions)
    (h : Algebra.Smooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a) ∧
      Module.IsStablyFree (Localization.Away S.a)
        (KaehlerDifferential S.R (Localization.Away S.a))) :
    Algebra.Smooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a)
declarations.comment: clause (a), the implication (2) ⇒ (1): if `A_a` is smooth over `R` and `Ω_{A_a/R}` is stably free then `A_a` is smooth over `R`

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.elementaryStandard_implies_strictlyStandard
declarations.doc:
Condition (6) implies condition (5): an elementary standard element is strictly standard.
The single principal minor is the minor indexed by the first `c` variables.
declarations.statement:
theorem elementaryStandard_implies_strictlyStandard
    (S : SixStandardnessConditions)
    (h : IsElementaryStandard (R := S.R) (A := S.A) S.a) :
    IsStrictlyStandard (R := S.R) (A := S.A) S.a
declarations.comment: clause (b), the implication (6) ⇒ (5): an elementary standard element is strictly standard, the single principal minor being the one on the first `c` variables

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.isStandardSmooth_localizationAway_of_isElementaryStandard
declarations.doc:
Condition (6) implies condition (4): an elementary standard element has a standard smooth
localization.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStandardSmooth_localizationAway_of_isElementaryStandard
    (S : SixStandardnessConditions)
    (ha : IsElementaryStandard (R := S.R) S.a) :
    Algebra.IsStandardSmooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a)
declarations.comment: clause (c), the implication (6) ⇒ (4): if `a` is elementary standard in `A` over `R` then `A_a` is *standard smooth* over `R` — condition (4), not merely smooth after some further localization

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.smooth_and_isStablyFree_kaehlerDifferential_of_isStrictlyStandard
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 16.3.7, (5) ⇒ (2).** If the distinguished element is strictly standard,
then its localization is smooth and its module of differentials is stably free.
declarations.statement:
theorem smooth_and_isStablyFree_kaehlerDifferential_of_isStrictlyStandard
    (S : SixStandardnessConditions)
    (h : IsStrictlyStandard (R := S.R) S.a) :
    Algebra.Smooth S.R (Localization.Away S.a) ∧
      Module.IsStablyFree (Localization.Away S.a)
        (KaehlerDifferential S.R (Localization.Away S.a))
declarations.comment: clause (d), the implication (5) ⇒ (2): if `a` is strictly standard in `A` over `R` then `A_a` is smooth over `R` and `Ω_{A_a/R}` is stably free. Both conjuncts of (2) are concluded; the smoothness one is the implication (5) ⇒ (1) of 07CA

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_finitePresentation_factorization_smoothAway_singularIdeal_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07F0.** Let `R` be Noetherian, let `Λ` be an `R`-algebra and let `π ∈ R` be an
element with `Ann_R(π) = Ann_R(π²)` and `Ann_Λ(π) = Ann_Λ(π²)`. Let `A → Λ` be an `R`-algebra
map with `A` of finite presentation and with the image of `π` strictly standard in `A` over `R`,
and let `A/π⁸A → C̄ → Λ/π⁸Λ` be a factorization of the induced map with `C̄` of finite
presentation over `R/π⁸R`. Then `A → Λ` factors as `A → B → Λ` with `B` of finite presentation
such that `R_π → B_π` is smooth and
`H_{C̄/(R/π⁸R)} · Λ/π⁸Λ ⊆ √(H_{B/R}Λ) mod π⁸Λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_factorization_smoothAway_singularIdeal_le
    (R : Type u) (Λ : Type v) (A : Type w) (C : Type x)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ] [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Algebra R Λ] [Algebra R A] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R A] (π : R)
    (hR : (Submodule.span R {π}).annihilator = (Submodule.span R {π ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (hΛ : (Submodule.span Λ {algebraMap R Λ π}).annihilator =
      (Submodule.span Λ {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (fA : A →ₐ[R] Λ) (hπ : IsStrictlyStandard (R := R) (A := A) (algebraMap R A π))
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 8}) C]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 8}) C]
    [Algebra (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 8}) (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 8})]
    (hquot : ∀ r : R, algebraMap (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 8})
        (Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 8}) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ r) =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap R Λ r))
    (toC : (A ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R A π) ^ 8}) →+* C)
    (htoC : ∀ r : R, toC (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (algebraMap R A r)) =
      algebraMap (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 8}) C (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ r))
    (fC : C →ₐ[R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 8}] Λ ⧸ Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 8})
    (hfC : ∀ a : A, fC (toC (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ a)) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (fA a)) :
    ∃ (B : Type (max u v x)) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra R B)
      (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation R B) (a : A →ₐ[R] B) (g : B →ₐ[R] Λ),
      g.comp a = fA ∧
      (letI : Algebra (Localization.Away π) (Localization.Away (algebraMap R B π)) :=
        (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap R B) π).toAlgebra
       Algebra.Smooth (Localization.Away π) (Localization.Away (algebraMap R B π))) ∧
      Ideal.map fC.toRingHom (singularIdeal (R ⧸ Ideal.span {π ^ 8}) C) ≤
        Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {(algebraMap R Λ π) ^ 8}))
          (Ideal.map g.toRingHom (singularIdeal R B)).radical

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.RegularRingMapSituation
declarations.doc: The standing data of Stacks 16.8.1: a regular ring map between Noetherian rings.
declarations.statement: structure RegularRingMapSituation

declarations.name: pt_product
declarations.doc:
Let `R_i → Λ_i` (`i = 1, 2`) be ring maps of Noetherian rings. If PT holds for `R_1 → Λ_1`
and for `R_2 → Λ_2`, then PT holds for the product ring map `R_1 × R_2 → Λ_1 × Λ_2` (with the
componentwise algebra structure).
declarations.statement:
theorem pt_product
    (R₁ R₂ Λ₁ Λ₂ : Type)
    [CommRing R₁] [CommRing R₂] [CommRing Λ₁] [CommRing Λ₂]
    [Algebra R₁ Λ₁] [Algebra R₂ Λ₂]
    [IsNoetherianRing R₁] [IsNoetherianRing Λ₁]
    [IsNoetherianRing R₂] [IsNoetherianRing Λ₂]
    (hPT₁ : PT R₁ Λ₁) (hPT₂ : PT R₂ Λ₂) :
    letI : Algebra (R₁ × R₂) (Λ₁ × Λ₂) :=
      ((algebraMap R₁ Λ₁).prodMap (algebraMap R₂ Λ₂)).toAlgebra
    PT (R₁ × R₂) (Λ₁ × Λ₂)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_factorization_isElementaryStandard
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07F4.** Let `R → A → Λ` be ring maps with `A` of finite presentation over `R` and
let `S ⊆ R` be a multiplicative set. Given a factorization `S⁻¹A → B' → S⁻¹Λ` with `B'` smooth
over `S⁻¹R`, there is a factorization `A → B → Λ` of `A → Λ` by `R`-algebras in which some
`s ∈ S` maps to an elementary standard element of `B` over `R`.

Step 1 of the source proof, the reduction to a standard smooth `B'`, is Stacks 07CH; it is
supplied by `Stacks.Smoothing.exists_smooth_isStandardSmooth_retraction`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_isElementaryStandard
    (S : Submonoid R)
    [Algebra (Localization S) (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R A)))]
    [IsScalarTower R (Localization S) (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R A)))]
    [Algebra (Localization S) (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R Λ)))]
    [Algebra (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R A)))
      (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R Λ)))]
    [Algebra A (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R Λ)))]
    [IsScalarTower A Λ (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R Λ)))]
    (h : ∃ (B' : Type u') (_ : CommRing B')
      (_ : Algebra (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R A))) B')
      (_ : Algebra (Localization S) B')
      (_ : Algebra B' (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R Λ))))
      (_ : Algebra A B')
      (_ : IsScalarTower A (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R A))) B')
      (_ : IsScalarTower (Localization S)
        (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R A))) B')
      (_ : IsScalarTower (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R A))) B'
        (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R Λ))))
      (_ : IsScalarTower A B' (Localization (S.map (algebraMap R Λ)))),
      Algebra.Smooth (Localization S) B') :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B) (_ : Algebra B Λ)
      (_ : Algebra R B),
      IsScalarTower R A B ∧ IsScalarTower A B Λ ∧ IsScalarTower R B Λ ∧
        ∃ s : S, IsElementaryStandard (R := R) (algebraMap R B s)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.indSmooth_of_indSmooth_of_field_base
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07F5.** If property PT — that `Λ` is a filtered colimit of smooth `R`-algebras —
holds for every regular ring map `R → Λ` of Noetherian rings whose source is a field, then it
holds for every regular ring map of Noetherian rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem indSmooth_of_indSmooth_of_field_base
    (hfield : ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
      [IsNoetherianRing Λ], IsRegularRingMap k Λ → IndSmooth k Λ)
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [Algebra R Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (hregular : IsRegularRingMap R Λ) :
    IndSmooth R Λ
declarations.comment:
Situation 07F2 is `IsRegularRingMap` plus the Noetherian hypotheses, and PT is
`IndSmooth`, the `ObjectProperty.ind` spelling of Lemma 07C3.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolved_of_quotient_eighthPowerIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07F8.** Let `R → A → Λ ⊃ q` be a local smoothing situation, let `r ≥ 1` and let
`π₁, …, π_r ∈ R` map into `q`. Assume that for `i = 1, …, r` the annihilator of `π_i` equals
the annihilator of `π_i²` in `R/(π₁⁸, …, π_{i-1}⁸)R` and likewise in
`Λ/(π₁⁸, …, π_{i-1}⁸)Λ`, and that `π_i` maps to a strictly standard element of `A` over `R`.
If the chain `R/(π₁⁸, …, π_r⁸)R → A/(π₁⁸, …, π_r⁸)A → Λ/(π₁⁸, …, π_r⁸)Λ`
can be resolved at `q/(π₁⁸, …, π_r⁸)Λ`, then `R → A → Λ ⊃ q` can be resolved.
declarations.statement:
theorem canBeResolved_of_quotient_eighthPowerIdeal
    (S : LocalSmoothingSituation.{u, v, w})
    {r : ℕ} (hr : 1 ≤ r) (π : Fin r → S.R)
    (hπq : ∀ i, algebraMap S.R S.Λ (π i) ∈ S.q)
    (hannR : ∀ i,
      let I := eighthPowerPrefixIdeal π i
      (Submodule.span (S.R ⧸ I) {Ideal.Quotient.mk I (π i)}).annihilator =
        (Submodule.span (S.R ⧸ I) {(Ideal.Quotient.mk I (π i)) ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (hannΛ : ∀ i,
      let I := Ideal.map (algebraMap S.R S.Λ) (eighthPowerPrefixIdeal π i)
      (Submodule.span (S.Λ ⧸ I)
          {Ideal.Quotient.mk I (algebraMap S.R S.Λ (π i))}).annihilator =
        (Submodule.span (S.Λ ⧸ I)
          {(Ideal.Quotient.mk I (algebraMap S.R S.Λ (π i))) ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (hstandard : ∀ i,
      IsStrictlyStandard (R := S.R) (A := S.A) (algebraMap S.R S.A (π i)))
    (hresolve :
      let I := eighthPowerIdeal π
      let IA := Ideal.map (algebraMap S.R S.A) I
      let IΛ := Ideal.map (algebraMap S.A S.Λ) IA
      letI : Algebra (S.R ⧸ I) (S.Λ ⧸ IΛ) :=
        ((algebraMap (S.A ⧸ IA) (S.Λ ⧸ IΛ)).comp
          (algebraMap (S.R ⧸ I) (S.A ⧸ IA))).toAlgebra
      letI : IsScalarTower (S.R ⧸ I) (S.A ⧸ IA) (S.Λ ⧸ IΛ) :=
        IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
      CanBeResolved
        (S.R ⧸ I) (S.A ⧸ IA) (S.Λ ⧸ IΛ)
        (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk IΛ) S.q)) :
    S.CanBeResolved

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_finitePresentation_factorization_singularIdeal_not_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07F9.** Let `R → A → Λ ⊃ q` be a local smoothing situation, `p = R ∩ q`. If `q` is
minimal over `𝔥_A` and the localized chain `R_p → A_p → Λ_q ⊃ q Λ_q` can be resolved, then there
is a factorization `A → C → Λ` with `C` of finite presentation over `R` and
`H_{C/R} Λ ⊄ q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finitePresentation_factorization_singularIdeal_not_le
    (S : LocalSmoothingSituation.{u, v, w})
    (_hq : S.q ∈ S.radicalSingularIdealExtension.minimalPrimes)
    (hresolve : S.IsResolvableAfterLocalizing) :
    ∃ (Cr : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing Cr) (_ : Algebra S.R Cr) (_ : Algebra S.A Cr)
        (_ : Algebra Cr S.Λ),
      IsScalarTower S.R S.A Cr ∧ IsScalarTower S.A Cr S.Λ ∧ IsScalarTower S.R Cr S.Λ ∧
        Algebra.FinitePresentation S.R Cr ∧
        ¬ Ideal.map (algebraMap Cr S.Λ) (singularIdeal S.R Cr) ≤ S.q

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolved_of_localization_dim_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FA.** Let `R → A → Λ ⊃ q` be a local smoothing situation with `q` minimal over
`𝔥_A = √(H_{A/R} Λ)`. If the localized chain `R_p → A_p → Λ_q ⊃ q Λ_q` can be resolved and `Λ_q`
has Krull dimension zero, then `R → A → Λ ⊃ q` can be resolved.
declarations.statement:
theorem canBeResolved_of_localization_dim_zero (S : LocalSmoothingSituation.{u, v, w})
    (hq : S.q ∈ S.radicalSingularIdealExtension.minimalPrimes)
    (hresolve : S.IsResolvableAfterLocalizing)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime S.q) = 0) : S.CanBeResolved

declarations.name: ogoma_ker_eq_of_localization
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 07FC (Ogoma's lemma). Over a Noetherian ring `A`, for a finite
`A`-module `M`, a multiplicative subset `S` and `π : A`, if multiplication by `π`
and `π²` have the same kernel on the localization `S⁻¹M`, then there is a single
`s ∈ S` such that for all `n > 0`, multiplication by `sⁿπ` and `(sⁿπ)²` have the
same kernel on `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ogoma_ker_eq_of_localization {A M : Type*} [CommRing A] [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [Module.Finite A M] (S : Submonoid A) (π : A)
    (h : LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul A (LocalizedModule S M) π)
      = LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul A (LocalizedModule S M) (π ^ 2))) :
    ∃ s ∈ S, ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n →
      LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul A M (s ^ n * π))
        = LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.lsmul A M ((s ^ n * π) ^ 2))

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_parameters_pow_mem_and_annihilator_sq_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FD.** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, let `I` and `q` be ideals of `Λ` with `q`
prime, and let `n`, `e` be positive integers. Assume that the extension of `q ^ n` to `Λ_q` is
contained in the extension of `I`, and that `Λ_q` is a regular local ring of dimension `d`.
Then there are `π₁, …, π_d ∈ Λ` such that `(π₁, …, π_d) Λ_q = q Λ_q`, such that `π_i ^ n ∈ I`
for every `i`, and such that for every `i` the annihilator of `π_i` in
`Λ ⧸ (π₁ ^ e, …, π_{i-1} ^ e)` is the annihilator of `π_i ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_parameters_pow_mem_and_annihilator_sq_eq
    (Λ : Type*) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (I q : Ideal Λ) [q.IsPrime]
    (n e d : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (he : 0 < e)
    (hqI : Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) (q ^ n) ≤
      Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) I)
    [IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    (hd : ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q) = d) :
    ∃ π : Fin d → Λ,
      Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) (Ideal.span (Set.range π)) =
          Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) q ∧
      (∀ i : Fin d, π i ^ n ∈ I) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin d, ∀ x : Λ ⧸ Ideal.span
          (Set.range fun j : Fin i.1 => π (j.castLE (Nat.le_of_lt i.2)) ^ e),
        x * Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (π i) = 0 ↔ x * Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (π i ^ 2) = 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolved_of_isRegularLocalRing_of_isSeparableExtension
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FE.** Let `k → A → Λ ⊃ q` be a local smoothing situation over a field `k`
with `Λ` Noetherian, `q` minimal over `𝔥_A = √(H_{A/k} Λ)`, `Λ_q` a regular local ring and the
residue field extension `κ(q)/k` separable. Then the chain can be resolved at `q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canBeResolved_of_isRegularLocalRing_of_isSeparableExtension
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) (Lambda : Type w)
    [Field k] [CommRing A] [CommRing Lambda]
    [Algebra k A] [Algebra k Lambda] [Algebra A Lambda]
    [IsScalarTower k A Lambda] [Algebra.FinitePresentation k A]
    [IsNoetherianRing Lambda] (q : Ideal Lambda) [q.IsPrime]
    (hq : (Ideal.map (algebraMap A Lambda)
      (Stacks.Smoothing.singularIdeal k A)).radical.IsMinimalPrime q)
    [IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    [Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k q.ResidueField] :
    CanBeResolved k A Lambda q

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.nonempty_coefficientSectionData_of_finite_h1Cotangent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FG**, the central claim of its proof: the data of `CoefficientSectionData` exists
for every Artinian local algebra over a field of characteristic `p > 0` whose residue field
extension has `dim_K H₁(L_{K/k}) < ∞`.

No finiteness is assumed of the residue field extension itself; the transcendence degree of `K`
over `k` may be infinite.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_coefficientSectionData_of_finite_h1Cotangent {k Λ : Type*} [Field k]
    [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [IsArtinianRing Λ] [IsLocalRing Λ] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    [CharP k p] [Module.Finite (ResidueField Λ) (Algebra.H1Cotangent k (ResidueField Λ))] :
    Nonempty (CoefficientSectionData k Λ)
declarations.comment:
The central claim of the source's proof, the only place where char k = p and
dim H₁(L_{K/k}) < ∞ are used: there exist a ring-theoretic section σ : K → Λ of the residue map,
generators λ₁, …, λ_d of 𝔪, and a finitely generated k ⊆ F₀ ⊆ K with the image of k in Λ
contained in Ψ_σ(F₀[λ₁, …, λ_d]). The source's induction on the nilpotency order of 𝔪 is
followed, including the correction of σ by a derivation K → 𝔪^{n-1} read off the Jacobi-Zariski
sequence. NOT covered: the conclusion of the lemma, which is proved from this claim in
`exists_directedOn_flat_essFiniteType`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_directedOn_flat_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FG**. Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p > 0` and let `(Λ, 𝔪, K)` be an
Artinian local `k`-algebra with `dim_K H₁(L_{K/k}) < ∞`. Then there is a directed family `𝒜` of
`k`-subalgebras of `Λ` which covers `Λ` — so that `Λ` is the filtered colimit of `𝒜` — each
member `A` of which is Artinian local, is essentially of finite type over `k`, has `Λ` flat over
it, and satisfies `𝔪_A Λ = 𝔪`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_directedOn_flat_essFiniteType {k Λ : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing Λ]
    [Algebra k Λ] [IsArtinianRing Λ] [IsLocalRing Λ] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    [Module.Finite (ResidueField Λ) (Algebra.H1Cotangent k (ResidueField Λ))] :
    ∃ 𝒜 : Set (Subalgebra k Λ), DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) 𝒜 ∧ (∀ y : Λ, ∃ A ∈ 𝒜, y ∈ A) ∧
      ∀ A ∈ 𝒜, ∃ (_ : IsArtinianRing A) (_ : IsLocalRing A),
        Module.Flat A Λ ∧ Algebra.EssFiniteType k A ∧
        Ideal.map A.val.toRingHom (maximalIdeal A) = maximalIdeal Λ
declarations.comment:
The lemma, under the source's own hypotheses and nothing else: char k = p > 0, Λ
an Artinian local k-algebra, and dim H₁(L_{K/k}) < ∞, with no finiteness assumed of K/k. The
conclusion is read in the directed-union form in which the source itself reads it (flatness of
A → Λ out of a local ring makes it injective, as the source's first line observes): the
approximating subalgebras are the stages Ψ_σ(F[λ]) for finitely generated F₀ ≤ F ≤ K, and they
are Artinian local k-subalgebras of Λ, essentially of finite type over k, with Λ flat (indeed
free) over each and with 𝔪_A Λ = 𝔪, and they are directed and cover Λ. The section σ and the
finitely generated F₀ are produced by the source's induction on the nilpotency order of 𝔪 in
`nonempty_coefficientSectionData_of_finite_h1Cotangent`, the only place where char k = p and
dim H₁(L_{K/k}) < ∞ are used; the properties of the stages are
`exists_directedOn_flat_essFiniteType_of_coefficientSectionData`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_directedOn_flat_essFiniteType_of_charP
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FG**, under the name used for it in the documentation of the Stacks 07FH material
in the second half of this file. The statement is that of
`exists_directedOn_flat_essFiniteType`.
declarations.statement: alias exists_directedOn_flat_essFiniteType_of_charP
declarations.comment:
The lemma, under the source's own hypotheses: the statement of
`exists_directedOn_flat_essFiniteType`, to which this reduces, under the name used for it in the
documentation of the Stacks 07FH material in the second half of this file.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_coefficientStage_basis_kaehlerDifferential_primePowerQuotient
declarations.doc:
**The λ-choice of Stacks 07FH, in the setting of that lemma.** Let `k` be a field of
characteristic `p > 0`, let `Λ` be a Noetherian `k`-algebra, let `𝔮` be a prime of `Λ`, let
`n ≥ 1` and assume `dim_K H₁(L_{K/k}) < ∞` for the residue field `K = κ(𝔮)` of
`Λ̄ = Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮`. Then for every finite subset `S` of `Λ` there are a ring-theoretic section
`σ : K → Λ̄` of the residue map, generators `λ₁, …, λ_d` of the maximal ideal of `Λ̄`, a finite
`S ⊆ Y ⊆ Λ` and elements `μ₁, …, μ_t` of `Y` such that the stage
`A = Ψ_σ(F[λ₁, …, λ_d])` of the coefficient field `F = k(ȳ : y ∈ Y)` contains the image of `k`
and the images of all elements of `Y`, has residue image exactly `F`, and has
`dμ̄₁, …, dμ̄_t` a basis of `Ω_{F/k}`.

The hypothesis of `exists_coefficientStage_basis_kaehlerDifferential` on the map `Λ → Λ̄` is
automatic here: `κ(𝔮)` is the fraction field of `Λ/𝔮`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coefficientStage_basis_kaehlerDifferential_primePowerQuotient {k Λ : Type*}
    [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (𝔮 : Ideal Λ) [𝔮.IsPrime] {n : ℕ}
    [IsLocalRing (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    [Module.Finite (ResidueField (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n))
      (Algebra.H1Cotangent k (ResidueField (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)))] (S : Finset Λ) :
    ∃ (Y : Finset Λ) (σ : ResidueField (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) →+* primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)
      (d : ℕ) (x : Fin d → primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)
      (F : IntermediateField k (ResidueField (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n))) (t : ℕ) (lam : Fin t → Λ)
      (hlam : ∀ j, residue (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)
        (algebraMap Λ (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) (lam j)) ∈ F),
      S ⊆ Y ∧ (∀ j, lam j ∈ Y) ∧ (∀ c, residue (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) (σ c) = c) ∧
      Ideal.span (Set.range x) = maximalIdeal (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) ∧
      F = IntermediateField.adjoin k ((fun y => residue (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)
        (algebraMap Λ (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) y)) '' (Y : Set Λ)) ∧ F.FG ∧
      (∀ a : k, algebraMap k (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) a ∈ coefficientStage σ F x) ∧
      (∀ y ∈ Y, algebraMap Λ (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) y ∈ coefficientStage σ F x) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ coefficientStage σ F x, residue (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) z ∈ F) ∧
      ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin t) F (Ω[F⁄k]), ∀ j, b j = KaehlerDifferential.D k F
        ⟨residue (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) (algebraMap Λ (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) (lam j)),
          hlam j⟩
declarations.comment:
A strengthening of the central claim of the source's proof, needed by Stacks 07FH
and not proved there. 07FH picks λ₁, …, λ_t ∈ Λ whose images lie in the approximating subalgebra
A ⊆ Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮 of 07FG and whose differentials form a basis of Ω_{F/k} for F = A/𝔪_A; no
argument is given, A is never enlarged afterwards, and for a general member of the directed
family the residues of elements of Λ lying in F do not generate F. With Λ/𝔮 = k[x, y], so
K = k(x, y), and F = k(x/y) one has F ∩ k[x, y] = k, because a nonconstant element of k(x/y) is
homogeneous of degree 0, so the differentials of the residues of Λ lying in F span 0 ≠ Ω_{F/k};
and by exists_subalgebra_residueField_image_eq_of_charP every finitely generated subfield of K
above a bound does occur as A/𝔪_A. What is added here is that the section σ and
the generators λ of 𝔪 may be chosen so that the coefficient field is generated by residues of
elements of Λ — it is k(Ȳ) for a finite Y ⊆ Λ containing any prescribed finite set, with the
images of all elements of Y inside the stage — whence a basis of Ω_{k(Ȳ)/k} among the
differentials of residues of elements of Λ whose images lie in the stage. NOT covered: flatness
of Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮 over this particular stage, which exists_stage supplies only for coefficient
fields large enough to contain the b-coordinates of the generators of 𝔪.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_mvPolynomial_factorization_isEssentiallySmooth_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FH, clause (2)**, in the generality of the tag. Let `k` be a field, let `Λ` be a
Noetherian geometrically regular `k`-algebra, let `𝔮` be a prime of `Λ` and let `n ≥ 1`. Then
there are `m ≥ 0` and a `k`-algebra map `φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → Λ` such that, with
`𝔭 = φ^{-1}(𝔮)`, one has `𝔭 Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮 Λ_𝔮` with `g : k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮` flat, and the map
`k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭/𝔭^n → Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮` induced by `g` factors through a local Artinian subring `D`
of `Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮` by an essentially smooth map followed by the inclusion of `D`, which is flat.

"Essentially smooth" is `RingHom.IsEssentiallySmooth`: essentially of finite presentation
(Tag 00QM (2)) and formally smooth. The Stacks Project never defines the term; see
`StacksFrontier/RingTheory/Smoothing/EssentiallySmooth.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mvPolynomial_factorization_isEssentiallySmooth_flat
    {k Λ : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    [Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ] (𝔮 : Ideal Λ) [𝔮.IsPrime]
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
      (g : Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) →+* Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)
      (u : primePowerQuotient (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) n →+* primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)
      (D : Subring (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n))
      (a : primePowerQuotient (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) n →+* D),
      Ideal.map ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)).comp φ.toRingHom)
          (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)
        = Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) 𝔮 ∧
      (∀ f, g (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
            (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)) f)
          = algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) (φ f)) ∧
      g.Flat ∧
      (∀ y, u (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
              (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)))
              (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮 ^ n)) y)
          = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) (𝔮 ^ n))
            (g y)) ∧
      (∀ z, (a z : primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) = u z) ∧
      ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing D) (_ : IsArtinianRing D),
        a.IsEssentiallySmooth ∧ D.subtype.Flat
declarations.comment:
clause (2), UNCONDITIONALLY: no hypothesis on `κ(𝔮)` beyond the tag's own (`Λ`
Noetherian and geometrically regular over `k`); the characteristic hypothesis is not needed
either. `essentially smooth` is `RingHom.IsEssentiallySmooth` (essentially of finite
presentation, Tag 00QM (2), plus formally smooth); the Stacks Project uses the term here and in
the two following lemmas without ever defining it, and this repository supplies the definition
those proofs need, in `StacksFrontier.RingTheory.Smoothing.EssentiallySmooth`. WHAT IS PROVED: `m`
and `φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → Λ` with `𝔭 = φ^{-1}(𝔮)`, the ideal identity `𝔭Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮Λ_𝔮`, flatness
of `g : k[y]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮`, a local Artinian subring `D` of `Λ̄ = Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮` and a factorization of
the induced map `u : k[y]_𝔭/𝔭^n → Λ̄` as an essentially smooth map into `D` followed by the
inclusion `D → Λ̄`, which is flat. HOW: clause (2) on its own needs no approximating subring at
either end. Clause (1), `exists_mvPolynomial_flat_localization`, is unconditional and supplies
`φ` with `𝔭Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮Λ_𝔮` and `k[y]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮` flat; hence `𝔭^n Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮^n Λ_𝔮`, so `u` is the base
change of a flat map along `k[y]_𝔭 → k[y]_𝔭/𝔭^n` and is flat, and `u` is a local homomorphism of
local rings, hence faithfully flat (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom`), hence
INJECTIVE. So `D = range u` is a local Artinian subring of `Λ̄`, `u` restricts to an isomorphism
onto it — essentially smooth, a bijective ring map being so — and `D → Λ̄` is flat because `u`
is. The source instead draws `D` from the directed family of Stacks 07FG, because it proves
clause (3) at the same time: the approximating subring is needed for `E ⊆ D`, and that is where
the source's unjustified λ-choice sits. WHAT REMAINS: clause (2) alone places no element inside
`D`, so it is Stacks 07FT's joint use of clauses (2) AND (3) that carries the difficulty; see
`exists_mvPolynomial_factorization_mem_isEssentiallySmooth_flat`, which is still conditional.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_mvPolynomial_flat_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FH, clause (1).** Let `k` be a field, let `Λ` be a Noetherian `k`-algebra which is
geometrically regular over `k` and let `𝔮` be a prime of `Λ`. Then there are `m ≥ 0` and a
`k`-algebra map `φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → Λ` such that, with `𝔭 = φ^{-1}(𝔮)`, one has
`𝔭 Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮 Λ_𝔮` and the induced local map `k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mvPolynomial_flat_localization {k Λ : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ] (𝔮 : Ideal Λ) [𝔮.IsPrime] :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
      (g : Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) →+* Localization.AtPrime 𝔮),
      Ideal.map ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)).comp φ.toRingHom)
          (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)
        = Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) 𝔮 ∧
      (∀ f, g (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
            (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)) f)
          = algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) (φ f)) ∧
      g.Flat
declarations.comment:
clause (1), unconditionally. The source's choice of `λ_1, …, λ_t ∈ Λ` whose
differentials form a basis of `Ω_{F/k}` for the residue field `F` of an approximating subalgebra
`A ⊆ Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮` of Stacks 07FG is not justified by the source's TEXT, which fixes `A` by 07FG
and only afterwards asks for the `λ`, never enlarging `A` again: for SOME members of the directed
family no such `λ` exist, the residues of those elements of `Λ` which land in `F` need not
generate `F` (see the module docstring for the counterexample `Λ/𝔮 = k[x, y]`, `F = k(x/y)`).
That is all the counterexample shows. It says nothing against the source's ROUTE, since `A` may
be chosen for the purpose rather than taken as given, and
`exists_coefficientStage_basis_kaehlerDifferential` chooses it so. The choice is not needed for
clause (1) in any case: the clause is the
source's own construction specialized to `F = k`, where `t = 0`, the fibre of `Λ_𝔮` over `k` is
`Λ_𝔮` itself, and `λ_1, …, λ_m` is a regular system of parameters of `Λ_𝔮` lifted to `𝔮`. What
the λ-choice is needed for is the essential smoothness in clause (2); only regularity of `Λ_𝔮`,
not geometric regularity, is used here. `𝔭 Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮 Λ_𝔮` is the stated equality of extended
ideals and the flat arrow is the unique `g` with `g ∘ (k[y] → k[y]_𝔭) = (k[y] → Λ → Λ_𝔮)`,
flatness being `RingHom.Flat`. The source proves this from Lemma 07E6 and More on Algebra
15.36.2; the route here is miracle flatness, Lemma 00R4.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_mvPolynomial_factorization_mem_isEssentiallySmooth_flat_of_charP
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FH, all three clauses, in the generality of the tag.** Let `k` be a field of
characteristic `p > 0`, let `Λ` be a Noetherian geometrically regular `k`-algebra, let `𝔮` be a
prime of `Λ`, let `n ≥ 1` and let `E` be a finite subset of `Λ̄ = Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮`. Then there are
`m ≥ 0` and a `k`-algebra map `φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → Λ` such that, with `𝔭 = φ^{-1}(𝔮)`:

* `𝔭 Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮 Λ_𝔮` and the induced local map `g : k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮` is flat — clause (1);
* the map `u : k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭/𝔭^n → Λ̄` induced by `g` factors through a local Artinian
  subring `D` of `Λ̄` as an essentially smooth map `a` followed by the inclusion of `D`, which is
  flat — clause (2);
* `E ⊆ D` — clause (3).

No hypothesis is placed on `κ(𝔮)`. **The proof of clause (3) is Brian Nugent's**: see
`exists_global_stage_primePowerQuotient` for his repair of the λ-choice, which the source's text
leaves unjustified and which is false for a general member of the directed family of Stacks 07FG
(two counterexamples are recorded in the implementation notes, the second of them his). The two
ingredients are that the generating family of `𝔪_Λ̄` used to build the approximating subalgebra
`D` is kept GLOBAL — chosen in `𝔮 ⊆ Λ` once and for all, so that `exists_stage` still grants
freeness and the fibre's regular parameters can be extracted from it as a subfamily by Nakayama —
and that the coefficient field is pushed up to one generated by residues of global elements
`s^P`, `a·s^{P-1}` whose images lie in `σ(F)`, where `σ(f) = q(a)/q(s)` is an exact relation in
`Λ̄` and `P` is a `p`-power at least `n`. The pair `s^P`, `a·s^{P-1}` generates what neither
member does: their residues are `α^P` and `f·α^P`, of ratio `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mvPolynomial_factorization_mem_isEssentiallySmooth_flat_of_charP
    {k Λ : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    [Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ] (𝔮 : Ideal Λ) [𝔮.IsPrime] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime]
    [CharP k p] {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (E : Finset (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
      (g : Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) →+* Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)
      (u : primePowerQuotient (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) n →+* primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)
      (D : Subring (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n))
      (a : primePowerQuotient (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) n →+* D),
      Ideal.map ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)).comp φ.toRingHom)
          (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)
        = Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) 𝔮 ∧
      (∀ f, g (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
            (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)) f)
          = algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) (φ f)) ∧
      g.Flat ∧
      (∀ y, u (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
              (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)))
              (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮 ^ n)) y)
          = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) (𝔮 ^ n))
            (g y)) ∧
      (∀ z, (a z : primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) = u z) ∧
      (∀ x ∈ E, x ∈ D) ∧
      ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing D) (_ : IsArtinianRing D),
        a.IsEssentiallySmooth ∧ D.subtype.Flat
declarations.comment:
All three clauses, in the generality of the tag: no hypothesis on κ(𝔮) beyond the
tag's own (Λ Noetherian and geometrically regular over a field k of characteristic p, 𝔮 a prime,
n ≥ 1, E a finite subset of Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮). Clause (1) is the ideal identity 𝔭Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮Λ_𝔮 together
with flatness of k[y]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮; clause (2) is the factorization of k[y]_𝔭/𝔭^n → Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮
through a local Artinian subring D by an essentially smooth map followed by a flat one; clause
(3) is E ⊆ D. `Essentially smooth' is RingHom.IsEssentiallySmooth: essentially of finite
presentation (Tag 00QM (2)) and formally smooth; the Stacks Project never defines the term. The
λ-choice of the source's proof is not justified by its text and is false for a general member of
the directed family of 07FG; the repair implemented here is due to Brian Nugent and is described
in the module docstring and in `exists_global_stage_primePowerQuotient`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_essentiallySmooth_enlargement_containing_pow_of_factorization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FI.** Let `k` be a field of characteristic `p > 0`, let `Λ` be a Noetherian
geometrically regular `k`-algebra, let `𝔮 ⊆ Λ` be a prime and let `n ≥ 1`. Let
`φ : k[y₁, …, y_m] → Λ` be a `k`-algebra map, `𝔭 = φ⁻¹(𝔮)`, and suppose, as in Lemma 07FH,

1. `𝔭Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮Λ_𝔮` and `g : k[y₁, …, y_m]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮` is flat;
2. the induced map `u : k[y₁, …, y_m]_𝔭/𝔭ⁿ → Λ_𝔮/𝔮ⁿΛ_𝔮` factors as `b ∘ a` through a local
   Artinian ring `D`, with `a` essentially smooth and `b` flat;
3. a finite subset `E ⊆ Λ_𝔮/𝔮ⁿΛ_𝔮` is contained in `D`.

Then for every `λ ∈ Λ ∖ 𝔮` there are an integer `q > 0` and a factorization
`k[y₁, …, y_m]_𝔭/𝔭ⁿ → D → D' → Λ_𝔮/𝔮ⁿΛ_𝔮` of `u`, with `D'` local Artinian, `c : D → D'` an
essentially smooth local homomorphism, `b' : D' → Λ_𝔮/𝔮ⁿΛ_𝔮` flat, local and injective (so
that `D'` is a subring of `Λ_𝔮/𝔮ⁿΛ_𝔮`), `b' ∘ c = b`, and `λ^q ∈ D'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_essentiallySmooth_enlargement_containing_pow_of_factorization
    {k Λ : Type u} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ]
    (𝔮 : Ideal Λ) [𝔮.IsPrime] {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    {m : ℕ} (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
    (g : Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) →+* Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)
    (_hmap : Ideal.map ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)).comp φ.toRingHom)
        (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) = Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) 𝔮)
    (_hg : ∀ f, g (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
        (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)) f)
          = algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) (φ f))
    (_hgflat : g.Flat)
    (u : primePowerQuotient (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) n →+* primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)
    (_hu : ∀ y, u (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
          (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮))) (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮 ^ n)) y)
        = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) (𝔮 ^ n)) (g y))
    {D : Type u} [CommRing D] [IsLocalRing D] [IsArtinianRing D]
    (a : primePowerQuotient (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) n →+* D)
    (b : D →+* primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)
    (_ha : a.IsEssentiallySmooth) (hb : b.Flat) (hab : b.comp a = u)
    (E : Finset (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)) (_hE : ∀ x ∈ E, x ∈ b.range)
    (lam : Λ) (_hlam : lam ∉ 𝔮) :
    ∃ (q : ℕ) (D' : Type u) (_ : CommRing D') (_ : IsLocalRing D') (_ : IsArtinianRing D')
      (c : D →+* D') (b' : D' →+* primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) (_ : IsLocalHom c)
      (_ : IsLocalHom b'),
      0 < q ∧ c.IsEssentiallySmooth ∧ b'.Flat ∧ b'.comp c = b ∧ (b'.comp c).comp a = u ∧
        Function.Injective b' ∧
        algebraMap Λ (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n) (lam ^ q) ∈ b'.range
declarations.comment: in the full setup of Lemma 07FH: `Λ` Noetherian and geometrically regular over `k` of characteristic `p > 0`, `n ≥ 1`, `φ : k[y₁,…,y_m] → Λ` with clause (1) (`𝔭Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮Λ_𝔮`, `k[y]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮` flat), the factorization `k[y]_𝔭/𝔭ⁿ → D → Λ_𝔮/𝔮ⁿΛ_𝔮` of clause (2) through a local Artinian `D` (first arrow essentially smooth, second flat) and the finite `E ⊆ D` of clause (3), and `λ ∉ 𝔮`. `D'` is a ring with an injective flat local map to `Λ_𝔮/𝔮ⁿΛ_𝔮`, and `λ^q ∈ D'` means the image of `λ^q` lies in its range. Essentially smooth is `RingHom.IsEssentiallySmooth` (essentially of finite presentation, Tag 00QM (2), and formally smooth)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolvedInPositiveCharacteristic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FJ.** Let `k → A → Λ ⊃ 𝔮` be as in Situation 07F7 with `k` of characteristic
`p > 0`, `A` of finite presentation over `k`, `Λ` Noetherian and geometrically regular over `k`,
and `𝔮` minimal over `𝔥_A`. Then the chain can be resolved at `𝔮`.

This is `Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolvedInPositiveCharacteristic_of_locallyResolvable` with both
of its hypotheses discharged: item (9), Stacks 07FT, by
`Stacks.Smoothing.hasArtinianApproximationData`, and items (22)–(26) by
`Stacks.Smoothing.twistedQuotientLocallyResolvable` above. Every one of the twenty-six items of
the source's proof is therefore proved.
declarations.statement: theorem canBeResolvedInPositiveCharacteristic : CanBeResolvedInPositiveCharacteristic.{u}
declarations.comment: the lemma in full generality, with NO carried hypotheses: the whole of Situation 07F7 over a field of characteristic `p > 0`, with `𝔮` minimal over `𝔥_A`, and the conclusion `CanBeResolved k A Λ 𝔮`. Its two inputs are both proved in this library. The first is item (9), Stacks 07FT, `hasArtinianApproximationData`; the second is items (22)-(26), Stacks 07G6-07GA, `twistedQuotientLocallyResolvable`. The λ-choice in the source's proof of Stacks 07FH, on which 07FT turns, is not justified by the source's text and is false for a general member of the directed family of 07FG; the repair is due to BRIAN NUGENT, and is implemented in `exists_global_stage_primePowerQuotient`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.LocalSmoothingSituation.exists_pos_map_pow_le_map_singularIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FK.** In a local smoothing situation with `Λ` Noetherian and `q` minimal over
`𝔥_A = √(H_{A/R} Λ)`, some positive power of `q` extends into `H_{A/R} Λ_q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pos_map_pow_le_map_singularIdeal [IsNoetherianRing S.Λ]
    (hq : S.q ∈ S.radicalSingularIdealExtension.minimalPrimes) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧
      Ideal.map (algebraMap S.Λ (Localization.AtPrime S.q)) (S.q ^ N) ≤
        Ideal.map (algebraMap S.Λ (Localization.AtPrime S.q))
          (Ideal.map (algebraMap S.A S.Λ) (singularIdeal S.R S.A))

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.LocalSmoothingSituation.exists_fin_span_range_eq_singularIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FL.** The singular ideal `H_{A/R}` of a local smoothing situation is generated by
finitely many elements of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fin_span_range_eq_singularIdeal :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (a : Fin t → S.A), Ideal.span (Set.range a) = singularIdeal S.R S.A

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.LocalSmoothingSituation.exists_nat_eq_ringKrullDim_localization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FM.** The Krull dimension of the localization `Λ_q` of a local smoothing situation
with `Λ` Noetherian is a natural number.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_nat_eq_ringKrullDim_localization [IsNoetherianRing S.Λ] :
    ∃ d : ℕ, ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime S.q) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.parameterPowerIdeal
declarations.doc:
The ideal `(x_i^{2N} - Σ_j z_{ij} a_j : i = 1, …, d)` of the polynomial ring
`A[x_1, …, x_d, z_{ij}]`, whose variables are indexed by `Fin d ⊕ Fin d × Fin t` so that
`x_i = X (Sum.inl i)` and `z_{ij} = X (Sum.inr (i, j))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def parameterPowerIdeal {A : Type v} [CommRing A] (d : ℕ) {t : ℕ} (N : ℕ)
    (a : Fin t → A) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin d ⊕ Fin d × Fin t) A)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.parameterPowerAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The algebra `B = A[x_1, …, x_d, z_{ij}]/(x_i^{2N} - Σ_j z_{ij} a_j)`: the algebra `A` with
`d` generic elements `x_i` adjoined whose `2N`-th powers lie in the ideal generated by
`a_1, …, a_t`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev parameterPowerAlgebra (A : Type v) [CommRing A] (d : ℕ) {t : ℕ} (N : ℕ)
    (a : Fin t → A) : Type v

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_retraction_parameterPowerAlgebra
declarations.doc:
Let `B = A[x_i, z_{ij}]/(x_i^{2N} - Σ_j z_{ij} a_j)`, viewed as a `k[x_1, …, x_d]`-algebra.
There is a finite-type `B`-algebra `C`, of finite presentation over `k[x_1, …, x_d]`, with a
`k[x_1, …, x_d]`-algebra retraction `C → B`, such that for each `b ∈ B`: if `B_b` is a local
complete intersection over `k[x_1, …, x_d]`, then `C_b` is smooth over `B_b` and has a
presentation over `k[x_1, …, x_d]` with free conormal module; and if `B_b` is smooth over
`k[x_1, …, x_d]`, then the module of differentials of `C_b` over `k[x_1, …, x_d]` is free.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_retraction_parameterPowerAlgebra (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] (d : ℕ) {t : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (a : Fin t → A) :
    ∃ (C : Type v) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) C)
      (_ : Algebra (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C)
      (_ : IsScalarTower (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C)
      (_ : Algebra.FiniteType (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C)
      (_ : Algebra.FinitePresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) C)
      (g : C →ₐ[MvPolynomial (Fin d) k] parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a),
      g.comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
          (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C) =
        AlgHom.id (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) ∧
      (∀ b : parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a,
        RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection
            (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (Localization.Away b)) →
          (letI : Algebra (Localization.Away b)
              (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b)) :=
            (Localization.awayMap
              (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C) b).toAlgebra;
          Algebra.Smooth (Localization.Away b)
              (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b)) ∧
            HasFreeConormalPresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
              (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b)))) ∧
      (∀ b : parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a,
        Algebra.Smooth (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (Localization.Away b) →
          Module.Free (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b))
            (KaehlerDifferential (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
              (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_pos_isStrictlyStandard_X_pow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FQ.** Let `A` be of finite type over a field `k`, let `a_1, …, a_t` generate the
singular ideal `H_{A/k}`, and let `C` be an algebra over `B = A[x_i, z_{ij}]/(x_i^{2N} - Σ_j
z_{ij} a_j)` with the two localization properties that Stacks 07FP supplies. Then some positive
power `x_i^c`, one `c` for all `i`, is strictly standard in `C` over `k[x_1, …, x_d]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pos_isStrictlyStandard_X_pow (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A]
    [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] (d N : ℕ) {t : ℕ} (a : Fin t → A)
    (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = singularIdeal k A) (C : Type v) [CommRing C]
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) C] [Algebra (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C]
    [IsScalarTower (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) C]
    (hC₁ : ∀ b : parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a,
      RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection
          (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (Localization.Away b)) →
        (letI : Algebra (Localization.Away b)
            (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b)) :=
          (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C) b).toAlgebra
