        Algebra.Smooth (Localization.Away b)
            (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b)) ∧
          HasFreeConormalPresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
            (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b))))
    (hC₂ : ∀ b : parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a,
      Algebra.Smooth (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (Localization.Away b) →
        Module.Free (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b))
          (KaehlerDifferential (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
            (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b)))) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ i : Fin d, IsStrictlyStandard (R := MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
      (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) C (MvPolynomial.X i) ^ c)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.resolutionTruncationOrder
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FR.** The order `n = N + dc` to which the local ring `Λ_q` is truncated in the
proof of Stacks 07FJ.
declarations.statement: def resolutionTruncationOrder (N d c : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.resolutionPowerExponent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FR.** The exponent `e = 8c` used in the proof of Stacks 07FJ: it is eight times
the exponent `c` making `x_i^c` strictly standard, so that `γ_i^e = (γ_i^c)^8` is the eighth
power required by Stacks 07F8.
declarations.statement: def resolutionPowerExponent (c : ℕ) : ℕ

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_finset_primePowerQuotient_eq_image_generators
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FS.** Let `A` be a `k`-algebra of finite type mapping to a ring `Λ` with a prime
`𝔮`, and let `n` be an exponent. Then `A` has a finite `k`-algebra generating family whose image
in `Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮` is a finite subset of that ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finset_primePowerQuotient_eq_image_generators (k : Type u) (A : Type v)
    (Λ : Type w) [CommRing k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] [CommRing Λ]
    [Algebra A Λ] (𝔮 : Ideal Λ) [𝔮.IsPrime] (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ (s : Finset A) (E : Finset (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)),
      Algebra.adjoin k (s : Set A) = ⊤ ∧
      (E : Set (primePowerQuotient 𝔮 n)) =
        toPrimePowerQuotient 𝔮 n '' (algebraMap A Λ '' (s : Set A))
declarations.comment:
Item 8 of the proof of Stacks 07FJ. `E` is produced as a `Finset` of
`Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮`, which is the shape in which clause (3) of Stacks 07FH consumes it; the generating
family of `A` is a `Finset` because `A` is of finite type over `k`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.hasArtinianApproximationData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FT in full generality**, the predicate
`Stacks.Smoothing.HasArtinianApproximationData` proved: for every field `k` of characteristic
`p > 0`, every Noetherian geometrically regular `k`-algebra `Λ`, every prime `𝔮` of `Λ`, every
`n ≥ 1` and every finite subset `E` of `Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮`, the Artinian approximation data exist.

This was item (9) of the proof of Stacks 07FJ, carried as a hypothesis there and in
`Stacks.Smoothing.TwistedQuotientResolution`. The λ-choice of Stacks 07FH, on which it turns, is
not justified by the source's text; **the repair implemented here is due to Brian Nugent**.

This is the only declaration carrying `@[stacks 07FT]`: the special case
`Stacks.Smoothing.exists_mvPolynomial_localArtinianFactorization_mem`, which assumes in addition
that the residue field `κ(𝔮)` is essentially of finite type over `k`, is untagged.
declarations.statement: theorem hasArtinianApproximationData : HasArtinianApproximationData.{u}
declarations.comment:
The lemma in full generality: for every field k of characteristic p > 0, every
Noetherian geometrically regular k-algebra Λ, every prime 𝔮 of Λ, every n ≥ 1 and every finite
subset E of Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮, there are m and a k-algebra map φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → Λ such that, with
𝔭 = φ⁻¹(𝔮), the induced local map k[y]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮 is flat with 𝔭Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮Λ_𝔮, and the induced map
k[y]_𝔭/𝔭^n → Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮 factors through a local Artinian subring D containing E by an
essentially smooth map followed by a flat one. The three clauses of Stacks 07FH that this
consumes are proved in
`Stacks.Smoothing.exists_mvPolynomial_factorization_mem_isEssentiallySmooth_flat_of_charP`; the
λ-choice of the source's proof of 07FH is not justified by its text and is false for a general
member of the directed family of 07FG, and the repair is due to Brian Nugent.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_fin_mem_span_eq_maximalIdeal_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FU.** Let `𝔮` be a prime of a Noetherian ring `Λ`, let `𝔭` be the contraction of
`𝔮` along a `k`-algebra map `φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → Λ` and suppose the induced map
`g : k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭 → Λ_𝔮` is flat with `𝔭Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮Λ_𝔮`. If `d = dim Λ_𝔮`, then
`dim k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭 = d` and there are `π_1, …, π_d ∈ 𝔭` whose images generate the maximal
ideal of `k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭`, that is, form a regular system of parameters of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_fin_mem_span_eq_maximalIdeal_of_flat {k : Type u} [Field k] {Λ : Type v}
    [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (𝔮 : Ideal Λ) [𝔮.IsPrime] {m : ℕ}
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ)
    (g : Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) →+* Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)
    (hmap : Ideal.map ((algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)).comp φ.toRingHom)
          (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)
        = Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮)) 𝔮)
    (hg : ∀ f, g (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
          (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)) f)
        = algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) (φ f))
    (hgflat : g.Flat) {d : ℕ}
    (hd : ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime 𝔮) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) :
    ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧
      ∃ π : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin m) k, (∀ i, π i ∈ Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮) ∧
        Ideal.span (Set.range fun i => algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)
            (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮)) (π i))
          = maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.comap φ.toRingHom 𝔮))
declarations.comment:
Item 10 of the proof of Stacks 07FJ. `d` is `dim Λ_𝔮` of item 07FM, and the first
thing proved is that it is also `dim k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭`: `𝔭Λ_𝔮 = 𝔮Λ_𝔮` makes the fibre of `g`
over the closed point a field, and `g` is flat, hence satisfies going down, so Stacks 00ON gives
`height 𝔮Λ_𝔮 = height 𝔭k[y]_𝔭 + 0`. A polynomial ring over a field is regular, so `k[y]_𝔭` is a
regular local ring and its maximal ideal is generated by `dim k[y]_𝔭` elements; each may be taken
to be the image of an element of `𝔭`, because an element of the maximal ideal of a localization is
a unit multiple of such an image. `d` elements of `𝔭` whose images generate the maximal ideal of
the `d`-dimensional regular local ring `k[y]_𝔭` is exactly a regular system of parameters of
`k[y]_𝔭`, and the dimension equality is part of the conclusion so that this reading is pinned
down. The hypotheses are the part of item 07FT that the step uses: `φ`, the flat `g` compatible
with `φ`, and the ideal identity.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.parameterScalingRing
declarations.doc:
The polynomial ring `R = k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_d]`, with `y_j = X (Sum.inl j)` the
variables of the polynomial ring of Stacks 07FT and `t_i = X (Sum.inr i)` one new variable for
each member of the regular system of parameters of Stacks 07FU.
declarations.statement: abbrev parameterScalingRing (k : Type u) [CommRing k] (m d : ℕ) : Type u
declarations.comment:
Item 11 of the proof of Stacks 07FJ, with one correction: the source writes
`R = k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_m]`, but the `t`-block has `d` members, not `m`. Every later use of
`R` in the proof writes `k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_d]` — items 07FZ, 07G3 and 07G9, and repeatedly
in the justifications — and `γ_i = π_i t_i` is defined only for `i = 1, …, d`, the `π_i` being the
`d` elements supplied by item 07FU, with `I = (γ_1^e, …, γ_d^e)` in item 07G1. `R` is
`MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k` with `y_j = X (Sum.inl j)` and `t_i = X (Sum.inr i)`; the
`k`-algebra map `k[y_1, …, y_m] → R` of the source is `MvPolynomial.rename Sum.inl`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.parameterScalingGen
declarations.doc:
The element `γ_i = π_i t_i` of `R = k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_d]`: the `i`-th member of a
family `π_1, …, π_d` in `k[y_1, …, y_m]`, scaled by the new variable `t_i`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def parameterScalingGen {k : Type u} [CommRing k] {m d : ℕ}
    (π : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (i : Fin d) : parameterScalingRing k m d
declarations.comment:
Item 11 of the proof of Stacks 07FJ; see `parameterScalingRing` for the correction
to the source's `R`. `γ_i` is defined for `i = 1, …, d`, matching the `d` elements `π_i` of item
07FU.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_annihilator_scaledVariable_sq_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FW.** Let `P` be a Noetherian ring, let `p ⊂ P` be a prime such that `P_p` is a
regular local ring of dimension `d`, and let `π₁, …, π_d ∈ P` map to a regular system of
parameters of `P_p`. For every `e > 0` the `π_i` may be rescaled by elements of `P \ p`, which
leaves them a regular system of parameters, so that in `R ⧸ (γ₁ ^ e, …, γ_{i-1} ^ e)` the
annihilator of `γ_i` is the annihilator of `γ_i ^ 2`, where `R = P[t₁, …, t_d]` and
`γ_i = π_i t_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_annihilator_scaledVariable_sq_eq {P : Type u} [CommRing P] [IsNoetherianRing P]
    (p : Ideal P) [p.IsPrime] [IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)] {d : ℕ}
    (hd : ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p) = d) (π : Fin d → P)
    (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range fun i => algebraMap P (Localization.AtPrime p) (π i)) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
    {e : ℕ} (he : 0 < e) :
    ∃ π' : Fin d → P, (∀ i, ∃ s ∈ p.primeCompl, π' i = s * π i) ∧
      Ideal.span (Set.range fun i => algebraMap P (Localization.AtPrime p) (π' i)) =
        IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin d, ∀ x : MvPolynomial (Fin d) P ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range fun j : Fin i.1 =>
          scaledVariable π' (j.castLE (Nat.le_of_lt i.2)) ^ e),
        x * Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (scaledVariable π' i) = 0 ↔
          x * Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (scaledVariable π' i ^ 2) = 0
declarations.comment: the source's `R = k[y_1, …, y_m]` is an arbitrary Noetherian ring `P`, and the data of (07FU) — the lifts of a regular system of parameters of `P_p` — are the hypotheses on `π`; `γ_i = π_i t_i` is `scaledVariable π i`

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_essentiallySmooth_enlargement_annihilator_sq_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FX.** In the situation of Stacks 07FJ, with `N ≤ n`, `q ^ N Λ_q ⊆ (a_1, …, a_r)Λ_q`
and `π_1, …, π_d ∈ q` lifting a regular system of parameters of `Λ_q`, suppose the `a_j` and the
`π_i` reduce in `Λ_q/q^nΛ_q` into the image of an Artinian local ring `D` mapping to
`Λ_q/q^nΛ_q` by a flat local homomorphism. Then there are `δ_1, …, δ_d ∈ Λ \ q` and a
factorization `D → D' → Λ_q/q^nΛ_q` with `D'` Artinian local, `D → D'` essentially smooth and
`D' → Λ_q/q^nΛ_q` flat and local, such that, writing `π'_i = δ_i π_i`:
`(π'_i)^{2N} = Σ_j a_j λ_{ij}` in `Λ` with every `λ_{ij}` reducing into the image of `D'`; the
annihilator of `π'_i` in `Λ ⧸ ((π'_1)^e, …, (π'_{i-1})^e)` is the annihilator of `(π'_i)^2`; and
every `δ_i` reduces into the image of `D'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_essentiallySmooth_enlargement_annihilator_sq_eq
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    (q : Ideal Λ) [q.IsPrime] [IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime q)]
    {d r N n e : ℕ} (hd : ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q) = d)
    (hN : 0 < N) (hn : N ≤ n) (he : 0 < e)
    [IsLocalRing (truncatedLocalization Λ q n)] [IsArtinianRing (truncatedLocalization Λ q n)]
    (a : Fin r → Λ)
    (hqN : Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) (q ^ N) ≤
      Ideal.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q)) (Ideal.span (Set.range a)))
    (π : Fin d → Λ) (hπq : ∀ i, π i ∈ q)
    (hπspan : Ideal.span (Set.range fun i => algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (π i)) =
      IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
    {D : Type u} [CommRing D] [IsLocalRing D] [IsArtinianRing D]
    (b : D →+* truncatedLocalization Λ q n) [IsLocalHom b] (hb : RingHom.Flat b)
    (haD : ∀ j, ∃ w : D, b w = algebraMap Λ (truncatedLocalization Λ q n) (a j))
    (hπD : ∀ i, ∃ w : D, b w = algebraMap Λ (truncatedLocalization Λ q n) (π i)) :
    ∃ (δ : Fin d → Λ) (lam : Fin d → Fin r → Λ) (D' : Type u) (_ : CommRing D')
      (_ : IsLocalRing D') (_ : IsArtinianRing D') (c : D →+* D')
      (b' : D' →+* truncatedLocalization Λ q n) (_ : IsLocalHom c) (_ : IsLocalHom b'),
      c.IsEssentiallySmooth ∧ RingHom.Flat b' ∧ b'.comp c = b ∧
      (∀ i, δ i ∈ q.primeCompl) ∧
      (∀ i, (δ i * π i) ^ (2 * N) = ∑ j, a j * lam i j) ∧
      (∀ i j, ∃ w : D', b' w = algebraMap Λ (truncatedLocalization Λ q n) (lam i j)) ∧
      (∀ i, ∃ w : D', b' w = algebraMap Λ (truncatedLocalization Λ q n) (δ i)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin d, ∀ x : Λ ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range fun j : Fin i.1 =>
          (δ (j.castLE (Nat.le_of_lt i.2)) * π (j.castLE (Nat.le_of_lt i.2))) ^ e),
        x * Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (δ i * π i) = 0 ↔
          x * Ideal.Quotient.mk _ ((δ i * π i) ^ 2) = 0)
declarations.comment: the data of (07FT) — the Artinian local `D`, the flat local `D → Λ_q/q^nΛ_q`, and the memberships of the generators of `A` — are hypotheses, as are the lifts of (07FU); `H_{A/k}Λ` is the ideal generated by the images `a_1, …, a_r` and `(a)` is stated as the relation in `Λ` together with the reduction of each `λ_{ij}` into the image of `D'`

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.parameterPowerAlgebraToTarget
declarations.doc:
The `A`-algebra map `B = A[x_i, z_{ij}]/(x_i^{2N} - Σ_j z_{ij} a_j) → Λ` sending `x_i` to
`π'_i` and `z_{ij}` to `λ_{ij}`, where `(π'_i)^{2N} = Σ_j a_j λ_{ij}` in `Λ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def parameterPowerAlgebraToTarget {A : Type v} {Λ : Type w} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing Λ] [Algebra A Λ] {d t : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (a : Fin t → A) (π' : Fin d → Λ)
    (lam : Fin d → Fin t → Λ)
    (hπ' : ∀ i, π' i ^ (2 * N) = ∑ j, algebraMap A Λ (a j) * lam i j) :
    parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a →ₐ[A] Λ

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.improvedAlgebraToTarget
declarations.doc:
The ring map `C → Λ` obtained by composing the `k[x_1, …, x_d]`-algebra retraction `g : C → B`
of Stacks 07FP with the map `B → Λ` of `Stacks.Smoothing.parameterPowerAlgebraToTarget`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.twistedBaseToTarget
declarations.doc:
The `k`-algebra map `R = k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_d] → Λ` which is a given
`φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → Λ` on the variables `y_j` and sends `t_i` to `δ_i ∈ Λ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def twistedBaseToTarget {k : Type u} {Λ : Type w} [CommRing k] [CommRing Λ]
    [Algebra k Λ] {m d : ℕ} (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ) (δ : Fin d → Λ) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k →ₐ[k] Λ

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.twistedBaseHom
declarations.doc:
The `k`-algebra map `k[x_1, …, x_d] → R = k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_d]` sending `x_i` to the
twisted parameter `γ_i = π_i t_i`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolved_of_canBeResolved_twistedBase_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07G0.** Let `k` be a field, `A` a finite type `k`-algebra with
`H_{A/k} = (a_1, …, a_t)`, `A → Λ` a `k`-algebra map and `q ⊂ Λ`. Let
`B = A[x_1, …, x_d, z_{ij}]/(x_i^{2N} - Σ_j z_{ij} a_j)` and let `B → C` be as in Stacks 07CE
(07FP), with `k[x_1, …, x_d]`-algebra retraction `g : C → B`. Let `φ : k[y_1, …, y_m] → Λ`,
`π_1, …, π_d ∈ k[y_1, …, y_m]`, `δ_1, …, δ_d ∈ Λ` and `λ_{ij} ∈ Λ` with
`(π'_i)^{2N} = Σ_j a_j λ_{ij}` for `π'_i = δ_i π_i`; map `B → Λ` by `x_i ↦ π'_i`,
`z_{ij} ↦ λ_{ij}` and `C → Λ` through `g` (step (14)); let `R = k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_d]`
map to `Λ` by `φ` and `t_i ↦ δ_i`, and `k[x_1, …, x_d] → R` by `x_i ↦ γ_i = π_i t_i` (step
(15)). Then it suffices to resolve `R → C ⊗_{k[x_1, …, x_d]} R → Λ ⊃ q`, where
`C ⊗_{k[x_1, …, x_d]} R → Λ` is induced by the two maps `C → Λ` and `R → Λ`.

The base change is written `R ⊗_{k[x_1, …, x_d]} C`, the same ring with its two factors swapped,
for which the `R`-algebra structure is Mathlib's canonical one. The structure maps
`k[x_1, …, x_d] → R`, `R → Λ` and `R ⊗_{k[x_1, …, x_d]} C → Λ` are arbitrary instances pinned
down by `hR`, `hRΛ` and `hTΛ` to the maps of steps (14)–(15). The further properties of the `π_i`
and `δ_i` chosen in steps (10)–(13) are not needed for this step.
declarations.statement:
theorem canBeResolved_of_canBeResolved_twistedBase_tensorProduct {k : Type u} {A : Type u}
    {Λ : Type w} {C : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [CommRing Λ] [CommRing C] [Algebra k A]
    [Algebra k Λ] [Algebra A Λ] [IsScalarTower k A Λ] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] {t d N m : ℕ}
    (a : Fin t → A) (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = singularIdeal k A)
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) C] [Algebra (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C]
    [IsScalarTower (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) C]
    (g : C →ₐ[MvPolynomial (Fin d) k] parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a)
    (hg : g.comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
        (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C) =
      AlgHom.id (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a))
    (hC : ∀ b : parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a,
      RingHom.IsLocalCompleteIntersection
          (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (Localization.Away b)) →
      (letI : Algebra (Localization.Away b)
          (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b)) :=
        (Localization.awayMap (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C) b).toAlgebra
      Algebra.Smooth (Localization.Away b)
        (Localization.Away (algebraMap (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) C b))))
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ) (π : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (δ : Fin d → Λ)
    (lam : Fin d → Fin t → Λ)
    (hrel : ∀ i, (δ i * φ (π i)) ^ (2 * N) = ∑ j, algebraMap A Λ (a j) * lam i j)
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k)]
    (hR : algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k) =
      (twistedBaseHom π).toRingHom)
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k) Λ]
    (hRΛ : algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k) Λ = (twistedBaseToTarget φ δ).toRingHom)
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k ⊗[MvPolynomial (Fin d) k] C) Λ]
    [IsScalarTower (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k)
      (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k ⊗[MvPolynomial (Fin d) k] C) Λ]
    (hTΛ : ∀ (r : MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k) (c : C),
      algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k ⊗[MvPolynomial (Fin d) k] C) Λ (r ⊗ₜ c) =
        twistedBaseToTarget φ δ r *
          improvedAlgebraToTarget N a (fun i => δ i * φ (π i)) lam hrel g c)
    (q : Ideal Λ)
    (h : CanBeResolved (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k)
      (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k ⊗[MvPolynomial (Fin d) k] C) Λ q) :
    CanBeResolved k A Λ q

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.twistedParameterPowerIdeal
declarations.doc:
The ideal `I = (γ_1^e, …, γ_d^e)` of `R = k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_d]` generated by the `e`-th
powers of the twisted parameters.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def twistedParameterPowerIdeal {k : Type u} [CommRing k] {m d : ℕ}
    (π : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (e : ℕ) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolved_of_quotient_span_pow
declarations.doc:
Let `R → D → Λ ⊃ q` be a chain with `R` Noetherian and `D` of finite presentation over `R`, let
`γ_1, …, γ_d ∈ R` with `d ≥ 1`, and let `I = (γ_1^{8c}, …, γ_d^{8c})`. Assume each `γ_i^c` maps
into `q`, is strictly standard in `D` over `R`, and has the annihilator condition of Stacks 07FW
and 07FX in `R` and in `Λ` modulo the eighth powers of `γ_1^c, …, γ_{i-1}^c`. Then resolving
`R/I → D/ID → Λ/IΛ` resolves `R → D → Λ ⊃ q`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canBeResolved_of_quotient_span_pow {R : Type u} {D : Type v} {Λ : Type w} [CommRing R]
    [CommRing D] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra R D] [Algebra D Λ] [Algebra R Λ] [IsScalarTower R D Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R D] (q : Ideal Λ) [q.IsPrime] {d : ℕ}
    (hd : 1 ≤ d) (γ : Fin d → R) (c : ℕ) (I : Ideal R)
    (hI : I = Ideal.span (Set.range fun i => γ i ^ (8 * c)))
    (hγq : ∀ i, algebraMap R Λ (γ i ^ c) ∈ q)
    (hannR : ∀ i,
      let K := eighthPowerPrefixIdeal (fun i => γ i ^ c) i
      (Submodule.span (R ⧸ K) {Ideal.Quotient.mk K (γ i ^ c)}).annihilator =
        (Submodule.span (R ⧸ K) {(Ideal.Quotient.mk K (γ i ^ c)) ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (hannΛ : ∀ i,
      let K := Ideal.map (algebraMap R Λ) (eighthPowerPrefixIdeal (fun i => γ i ^ c) i)
      (Submodule.span (Λ ⧸ K)
          {Ideal.Quotient.mk K (algebraMap R Λ (γ i ^ c))}).annihilator =
        (Submodule.span (Λ ⧸ K)
          {(Ideal.Quotient.mk K (algebraMap R Λ (γ i ^ c))) ^ 2}).annihilator)
    (hstd : ∀ i, IsStrictlyStandard (R := R) (A := D) (algebraMap R D (γ i ^ c)))
    (hresolve :
      let ID := Ideal.map (algebraMap R D) I
      let IΛ := Ideal.map (algebraMap D Λ) ID
      letI : Algebra (R ⧸ I) (Λ ⧸ IΛ) :=
        ((algebraMap (D ⧸ ID) (Λ ⧸ IΛ)).comp (algebraMap (R ⧸ I) (D ⧸ ID))).toAlgebra
      letI : IsScalarTower (R ⧸ I) (D ⧸ ID) (Λ ⧸ IΛ) :=
        IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (fun _ => rfl)
      CanBeResolved (R ⧸ I) (D ⧸ ID) (Λ ⧸ IΛ) (Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk IΛ) q)) :
    CanBeResolved R D Λ q
declarations.comment: for arbitrary γ_1, …, γ_d ∈ R, d ≥ 1

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.twistedBasePrime
declarations.doc:
The prime `r ⊂ R = k[y_1, …, y_m, t_1, …, t_d]` which is the inverse image of `q ⊂ Λ` under the
map of `Stacks.Smoothing.twistedBaseToTarget`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def twistedBasePrime {k : Type u} {Λ : Type w} [CommRing k] [CommRing Λ]
    [Algebra k Λ] {m d : ℕ} (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) k →ₐ[k] Λ) (δ : Fin d → Λ) (q : Ideal Λ) :
    Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m ⊕ Fin d) k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.LocalSmoothingSituation.canBeResolved_of_nilpotent_generators
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FJ, step 20** (tag 07G4). It suffices to resolve the localized chain
`(R/I)_𝔯 → C ⊗ (R/I)_𝔯 → Λ_𝔮/IΛ_𝔮`: a chain `R → A → Λ ⊃ 𝔮` whose prime is minimal over
`𝔥_A`, whose localized chain can be resolved, and in whose localization `Λ_𝔮` the maximal ideal
is generated by finitely many nilpotent elements, can be resolved. The last condition is the
one supplied by the step: the images of the parameters `π_1, …, π_d` generate the maximal ideal
and their `e`-th powers already lie in the ideal `I` divided out.
declarations.statement:
theorem LocalSmoothingSituation.canBeResolved_of_nilpotent_generators
    (S : LocalSmoothingSituation.{u, v, w}) {d : ℕ} (π : Fin d → Localization.AtPrime S.q)
    (hgen : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime S.q) = Ideal.span (Set.range π))
    (hnil : ∀ i, IsNilpotent (π i))
    (hq : S.q ∈ S.radicalSingularIdealExtension.minimalPrimes)
    (hres : S.IsResolvableAfterLocalizing) : S.CanBeResolved
declarations.comment: for a chain whose localized target has maximal ideal generated by finitely many nilpotents, which is the form taken by the quotient by (γ_1^e, …, γ_d^e)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.baseParameterPowerIdeal
declarations.doc: The ideal `J = (π_1^e, …, π_d^e)` of `k[y_1, …, y_m]`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def baseParameterPowerIdeal {k : Type u} [CommRing k] {m d : ℕ}
    (π : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin m) k) (e : ℕ) : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin m) k)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolved_of_canBeResolved_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FJ, step 22** (tag 07G6). It suffices to resolve the chain over `(R/JR)_𝔭`: a
solution there, localized at `𝔯`, solves the chain of step (20) over `(R/I)_𝔯`. Over a local
Artinian target resolvability is the existence of a smooth factorization, and a smooth
factorization is carried along any base change of the chain.
declarations.statement:
theorem canBeResolved_of_canBeResolved_baseChange [IsLocalRing L₁]
    [Algebra.IsPushout R₁ A₁ R₂ A₂] {q : Ideal L₂} (hq : q ≠ ⊤)
    (h : CanBeResolved R₁ A₁ L₁ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal L₁)) : CanBeResolved R₂ A₂ L₂ q
declarations.comment: for an arbitrary base change R₁ → R₂ of the chain in place of the passage from (R/JR)_𝔭 to its localization (R/I)_𝔯, the base-changed target receiving the original target

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.span_range_pow_le_span_range_pow_of_le
declarations.doc:
**The bound of Stacks 07FJ, step 23, corrected.** If `𝔭 = (π_1, …, π_d)` and
`J = (π_1^e, …, π_d^e)` then `𝔭^n ⊆ J` as soon as `d(e - 1) < n`, and this is sharp: a monomial
of degree `n` in the `π_i` is forced into `J` only when one of its exponents reaches `e`. The
bound `d·e < n` of `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealPowerSections.span_range_pow_le_span_range_pow`
is the same statement with a weaker hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem span_range_pow_le_span_range_pow_of_le {d : ℕ} (π : Fin d → Y) {e n : ℕ} (he : 1 ≤ e)
    (hn : d * (e - 1) + 1 ≤ n) :
    Ideal.span (Set.range π) ^ n ≤ Ideal.span (Set.range fun i => π i ^ e)
declarations.comment: with the hypothesis d*(e-1)+1 ≤ n in place of the source's n = N + dc, which does not give 𝔭^n ⊆ J: a degree-n monomial in the regular system of parameters π_1, …, π_d lies in (π_1^e, …, π_d^e) only if some exponent reaches e, so the containment needs d*(e-1) < n, whereas N is fixed in step (1) before c and hence before e = 8c

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolved_quotient_of_canBeResolved
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FJ, step 23** (tag 07G7). It suffices to resolve the chain before dividing by the
ideal: dividing a solution of `R → A → Λ` by an ideal `I` of the base gives a solution of
`R/I → A/IA → Λ/IΛ`, because `A/IA` is the base change of `A` along `R → R/I`. In step (23) the
base is `(R/𝔭^nR)_𝔭`, the ideal is `J = (π_1^e, …, π_d^e)`, and
`span_range_pow_le_span_range_pow_of_le` is what makes `(R/JR)_𝔭` that quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem canBeResolved_quotient_of_canBeResolved [IsLocalRing L] (I : Ideal R)
    (h : CanBeResolved R A L (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal L)) :
    let IA := Ideal.map (algebraMap R A) I
    let IL := Ideal.map (algebraMap A L) IA
    letI : Algebra (R ⧸ I) (L ⧸ IL) :=
      ((algebraMap (A ⧸ IA) (L ⧸ IL)).comp (algebraMap (R ⧸ I) (A ⧸ IA))).toAlgebra
    letI : IsScalarTower (R ⧸ I) (A ⧸ IA) (L ⧸ IL) := IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
    ∀ q : Ideal (L ⧸ IL), q ≠ ⊤ → CanBeResolved (R ⧸ I) (A ⧸ IA) (L ⧸ IL) q
declarations.comment: the reduction half of the step: the solution of the chain over (R/p^nR)_p is divided by J, which is a base change of the chain; the numeric input p^n ⊆ J is span_range_pow_le_span_range_pow_of_le, stated with the corrected bound

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.hasSmoothFactorization_of_algHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FJ, step 24** (tag 07G8). It suffices to resolve the chain with `B` in place of
`C`: an `R`-algebra section `C → B` compatible with the maps to the target carries a smooth
factorization of `B → Λ` to one of `C → Λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSmoothFactorization_of_algHom {C₀ : Type u} [CommRing C₀] [Algebra R₀ C₀]
    [Algebra C₀ L] [IsScalarTower R₀ C₀ L] (σ : C₀ →ₐ[R₀] A₀)
    (hσ : ∀ c, algebraMap A₀ L (σ c) = algebraMap C₀ L c)
    (h : HasSmoothFactorization R₀ A₀ L) : HasSmoothFactorization R₀ C₀ L

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.canBeResolved_of_factorization_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FJ, step 25** (tag 07G9). It suffices to find a factorization
`B ⊗_{k[x_1, …, x_d]} (R/𝔭^nR)_𝔭 → D'[t_1, …, t_d] → Λ_𝔮/𝔮^nΛ_𝔮`: the ring
`R_𝔭/𝔭^nR_𝔭` is the polynomial ring `Λ₀[t_1, …, t_d]` over
`Λ₀ = k[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭/𝔭^nk[y_1, …, y_m]_𝔭`, the algebra `D'` is essentially smooth over `Λ₀`,
hence `D'[t_1, …, t_d]` is a filtered colimit of smooth `Λ₀[t_1, …, t_d]`-algebras and the
finitely presented middle term factors through one of them.
declarations.statement:
theorem canBeResolved_of_factorization_mvPolynomial {Λ₀ B₀ D A L : Type u} [CommRing Λ₀]
    [CommRing B₀] [CommRing D] [CommRing A] [CommRing L] [Algebra Λ₀ B₀] [Algebra B₀ D]
    [Algebra Λ₀ D] [IsScalarTower Λ₀ B₀ D] [Algebra.FinitePresentation Λ₀ B₀] (M : Submonoid B₀)
    [IsLocalization M D] (hD : Algebra.FormallySmooth Λ₀ D) {d : ℕ}
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin d) Λ₀) A] [Algebra A L] [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin d) Λ₀) L]
    [IsScalarTower (MvPolynomial (Fin d) Λ₀) A L]
    [Algebra.FinitePresentation (MvPolynomial (Fin d) Λ₀) A]
    (g : A →ₐ[MvPolynomial (Fin d) Λ₀] MvPolynomial (Fin d) D)
    (k : MvPolynomial (Fin d) D →ₐ[MvPolynomial (Fin d) Λ₀] L)
    (hgk : k.comp g = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom (MvPolynomial (Fin d) Λ₀) A L)
    {q : Ideal L} (hq : q ≠ ⊤) :
    CanBeResolved (MvPolynomial (Fin d) Λ₀) A L q
declarations.comment: for a chain whose middle term is an arbitrary algebra of finite presentation over Λ₀[t_1, …, t_d] in place of B ⊗_{k[x_1, …, x_d]} (R/p^nR)_p, with essential smoothness of Λ₀ → D' spelled out as: D' is a localization of a Λ₀-algebra of finite presentation and is formally smooth over Λ₀

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_algHom_parameterPowerAlgebra_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07FJ, step 26** (tag 07GA). The factorization required by step (25) exists. Its
twist is that `B = A[x_i, z_{ij}]/(x_i^{2N} - Σ_j z_{ij}a_j)` must send `x_i` to `π_i t_i`, not
to `π'_i = δ_i π_i`, for the square over `k[x_1, …, x_d] → R_𝔭/𝔭^nR_𝔭` to commute; the defining
relation then forces `z_{ij} ↦ λ_{ij} t_i^{2N}/δ_i^{2N}`, which lies in `D'[t_1, …, t_d]`
because `δ_i` is a unit of the local ring `D'`. The map is produced as a
`k[x_1, …, x_d]`-algebra map for the structure `x_i ↦ π_i t_i` on `D'[t_1, …, t_d]`, which is
exactly the commutation of the square in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_algHom_parameterPowerAlgebra_mvPolynomial (k : Type u) {A D : Type u} [CommRing k]
    [CommRing A] [CommRing D] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k D] {d r N : ℕ} (a : Fin r → A)
    (φ : A →ₐ[k] D) (π δ : Fin d → D) (lam : Fin d → Fin r → D) (hδ : ∀ i, IsUnit (δ i))
    (hrel : ∀ i, (δ i * π i) ^ (2 * N) = ∑ j, φ (a j) * lam i j) :
    letI : Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) (MvPolynomial (Fin d) D) :=
      (MvPolynomial.aeval (R := k) fun i => C (π i) * X i).toRingHom.toAlgebra
    ∃ ψ : parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a →ₐ[MvPolynomial (Fin d) k] MvPolynomial (Fin d) D,
      (∀ x : A, ψ (algebraMap A (parameterPowerAlgebra A d N a) x) = C (φ x)) ∧
      (∀ i, ψ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (parameterPowerIdeal d N a) (X (Sum.inl i))) = C (π i) * X i) ∧
      ∀ i j, ψ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (parameterPowerIdeal d N a) (X (Sum.inr (i, j)))) =
        C (lam i j * (↑(hδ i).unit⁻¹ : D) ^ (2 * N)) * X i ^ (2 * N)
declarations.comment: the choices of (07FT), (07FU) and (07FX) are hypotheses: the map A → D' whose existence is the condition E ⊆ D of (07FT), the images π_i, δ_i, λ_{ij} in D' of (07FU) and (07FX), the invertibility of δ_i in the local ring D', and clause (a) of (07FX) read in D'. The target D'[t_1, …, t_d] is MvPolynomial (Fin d) D'

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.indSmooth_of_isRegularRingMap
declarations.doc:
**Popescu's theorem.** A regular ring map of Noetherian rings makes its target a filtered
colimit of smooth algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem indSmooth_of_isRegularRingMap
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (Λ : Type u) [CommRing Λ] [Algebra R Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (hregular : IsRegularRingMap R Λ) :
    IndSmooth R Λ
declarations.comment: Popescu's theorem with NO carried hypotheses: every regular ring map of Noetherian rings is a filtered colimit of smooth ring maps. Regularity is `IsRegularRingMap` (Situation 07F2) and the conclusion is `IndSmooth`, the `ObjectProperty.ind` spelling of Lemma 07C3. Every step of the source's argument is proved: the reduction to a field base (07F5), the Noetherian induction on `𝔥_A`, the case `𝔥_A = Λ` (07EU), the characteristic-zero resolution (07FE), and the characteristic-`p` resolution (07FJ, `canBeResolvedInPositiveCharacteristic`), whose own λ-choice repair is due to Brian Nugent. Nothing is assumed.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Precoverage.chaotic
declarations.doc:
The chaotic (indiscrete) precoverage on an arbitrary category `C`: the covering presieves
of `U` are the singletons `{φ}` with `φ : V ⟶ U` an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: def chaotic : Precoverage C
declarations.comment:
the iso-singleton coverings, for an arbitrary category (Mathlib's
  `Pretopology.trivial` needs `HasPullbacks C`)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Precoverage.toGrothendieck_chaotic
declarations.doc:
The Grothendieck topology generated by the chaotic precoverage is `⊥`, the topology in which
only the maximal sieve covers.
declarations.statement: theorem toGrothendieck_chaotic : (chaotic C).toGrothendieck = ⊥
declarations.comment:
the iso-singleton coverings of an arbitrary category generate the bottom
  topology

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Precoverage.sheafChaoticEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Sheaves on the chaotic site of an arbitrary category `C`, with values in a category `A`,
are the presheaves on `C`: the forgetful functor is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
def sheafChaoticEquivalence (A : Type*) [Category* A] :
    Sheaf (chaotic C).toGrothendieck A ≌ Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A
declarations.comment: sheaves on the chaotic site of an arbitrary category are the presheaves

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretopology.toGrothendieck_bot
registrations.comment:
the chaotic pretopology generates the bottom topology, in which only the
  maximal sieve covers

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.sheafBotEquivalence
registrations.comment:
sheaves on the chaotic site are the presheaves: the forgetful functor from
  sheaves for the bottom topology to presheaves is an equivalence of categories

declarations.name: IsGRing
declarations.doc:
A commutative ring is a G-ring if it is Noetherian and, for every prime ideal `p`, the
canonical map from its local ring at `p` to the completion of that local ring is regular.
declarations.statement: public def IsGRing (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: DividedPowers.instSubsingletonDividedPowers
declarations.doc: A divided power structure on an ideal in a ring torsion-free as a `ℤ`-module is unique.
declarations.statement:
public instance instSubsingletonDividedPowers {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [Module.IsTorsionFree ℤ A] (I : Ideal A) : Subsingleton (_root_.DividedPowers I)
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: DividedPowers.exists_dividedPowers_iff_factorial_mul_eq_pow
declarations.doc:
Over a torsion-free commutative ring, maps on an ideal are divided power operations if and
only if their products with the corresponding factorials are the corresponding powers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dividedPowers_iff_factorial_mul_eq_pow
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [Module.IsTorsionFree ℤ A] (I : Ideal A)
    (γ : ℕ → I → I) :
    (∃ dp : _root_.DividedPowers I,
        ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : I), 0 < n → dp.dpow n (x : A) = (γ n x : A)) ↔
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (x : I), 0 < n →
        (n.factorial : A) * (γ n x : A) = (x : A) ^ n
declarations.comment: factorial_criterion

declarations.name: DividedPowers.nonempty_dividedPowers_iff_exists_generators_pow_mem_factorial_mul
declarations.doc:
Let `I` be an ideal in a torsion-free commutative ring. Then `I` admits a divided power
structure if and only if it has a set of ideal generators `s` such that, for every `x ∈ s` and
every positive `n`, the power `x ^ n` belongs to `(n!) I`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma nonempty_dividedPowers_iff_exists_generators_pow_mem_factorial_mul
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] [HasUniqueDiv A] (I : Ideal A) :
    Nonempty (_root_.DividedPowers I) ↔
      ∃ s : Set A, (Ideal.span s = I ∧
        ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ n : ℕ, (1 ≤ n →
          x ^ n ∈ Ideal.span {(n.factorial : A)} * I))
declarations.comment: generator_criterion

declarations.name: DividedPowers.exists_dividedPowers_span_natCast
declarations.doc:
If `A` is a `ℤ_(p)`-algebra, the ideal generated by `p` has the divided power structure
given by
`γₙ(p * a) = (p ^ n / n!) * a ^ n`.

The function `q` in the conclusion consists of the coefficients `p ^ n / n!` in `ℤ_(p)`;
the first two properties say that these quotients exist and lie in `pℤ_(p)` in positive
degrees.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dividedPowers_span_natCast
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (IntegersAtPrime p) A] :
    ∃ (q : ℕ → IntegersAtPrime p) (γ : DividedPowers (Ideal.span {(p : A)})),
      (∀ n : ℕ, (n.factorial : IntegersAtPrime p) * q n = (p : IntegersAtPrime p) ^ n) ∧
        (∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → q n ∈ Ideal.span {(p : IntegersAtPrime p)}) ∧
          ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : A),
            γ.dpow n ((p : A) * a) = algebraMap (IntegersAtPrime p) A (q n) * a ^ n

declarations.name: DividedPowers.exists_dividedPowers_of_axioms_on_generators
declarations.doc:
The product and iteration axioms for divided powers need only be checked on a set of
generators of the ideal, provided the other divided power axioms hold everywhere.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dividedPowers_of_axioms_on_generators
    {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (dpow : ℕ → A → A) (S : Set A)
    (hS : I = Ideal.span S)
    (dpow_zero : ∀ {x : A}, x ∈ I → dpow 0 x = 1)
    (dpow_one : ∀ {x : A}, x ∈ I → dpow 1 x = x)
    (dpow_mem : ∀ {n : ℕ} {x : A}, n ≠ 0 → x ∈ I → dpow n x ∈ I)
    (dpow_add : ∀ {n : ℕ} {x y : A}, x ∈ I → y ∈ I →
      dpow n (x + y) = (antidiagonal n).sum fun k ↦ dpow k.1 x * dpow k.2 y)
    (dpow_mul : ∀ {n : ℕ} {a x : A}, x ∈ I →
      dpow n (a * x) = a ^ n * dpow n x)
    (mul_dpow_on_generators : ∀ {m n : ℕ} {x : A}, x ∈ S →
      dpow m x * dpow n x = (choose (m + n) m : A) * dpow (m + n) x)
    (dpow_comp_on_generators : ∀ {m n : ℕ} {x : A}, n ≠ 0 → x ∈ S →
      dpow m (dpow n x) = (uniformBell m n : A) * dpow (m * n) x) :
    ∃ hI : _root_.DividedPowers I, ∀ (n : ℕ) {x : A}, x ∈ I → hI.dpow n x = dpow n x

declarations.name: DividedPowers.existsUnique_on_ideal_add
declarations.doc:
Divided power structures which agree on the intersection of their ideals extend uniquely
to the sum of the ideals.
declarations.statement:
public lemma existsUnique_on_ideal_add {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {I J : Ideal A}
    (γ : _root_.DividedPowers I)
    (δ : _root_.DividedPowers J)
    (h : ∀ (n : ℕ) {x : A}, x ∈ I ⊓ J → γ.dpow n x = δ.dpow n x) :
    ∃! ε : _root_.DividedPowers (I + J),
      (∀ (n : ℕ) {x : A}, x ∈ I → ε.dpow n x = γ.dpow n x) ∧
        (∀ (n : ℕ) {x : A}, x ∈ J → ε.dpow n x = δ.dpow n x)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.locallyNilpotent_iff_isNilpotent_natCast
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime number, let `γ` be a divided power structure on an ideal `I` of a
commutative ring `A`, and assume `p` is nilpotent in `A ⧸ I`. Then `I` is locally nilpotent,
i.e. every element of `I` is nilpotent, if and only if `p` is nilpotent in `A`.

declarations.name: DividedPowers.eq_iff_dpow_prime_eq
declarations.doc: Over a `ℤ_(p)`-algebra, a divided power structure is determined by its `p`th operation.
declarations.statement:
public lemma eq_iff_dpow_prime_eq {A : Type*} [CommRing A] {I : Ideal A} (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) (hA : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬p ∣ n → IsUnit (n : A))
    (γ γ' : _root_.DividedPowers I) :
    γ = γ' ↔ ∀ x : I, γ.dpow p x = γ'.dpow p x
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: DividedPowers.existsUnique_of_prime_operation
declarations.doc:
A map satisfying the factorial, homogeneity, and addition identities for a `p`th divided
power operation extends uniquely to a divided power structure.
declarations.statement:
public lemma existsUnique_of_prime_operation {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p.Prime) (hA : ∀ n : ℕ, ¬p ∣ n → IsUnit (n : A)) (δ : I → I)
    (factorial_mul : ∀ x : I, (p.factorial : A) * (δ x : A) = (x : A) ^ p)
    (smul : ∀ (a : A) (x : I), δ (a • x) = a ^ p • δ x)
    (add : ∀ x y : I,
      (δ (x + y) : A) = (δ x : A) +
        ∑ ij ∈ (antidiagonal p).filter (fun ij ↦ ij.1 ≠ 0 ∧ ij.2 ≠ 0),
          factorialInverse p hp hA ij.1 * factorialInverse p hp hA ij.2 *
            (x : A) ^ ij.1 * (y : A) ^ ij.2 +
        (δ y : A)) :
    ∃! γ : _root_.DividedPowers I, ∀ x : I, γ.dpow p x = δ x
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: DividedPowerRing
declarations.doc:
A divided power ring is a commutative ring equipped with an ideal and a divided power
structure on that ideal.
declarations.statement: public structure DividedPowerRing
declarations.comment: divided power rings

declarations.name: DividedPowerRing.hasLimits
declarations.doc: The category of divided power rings has all small limits.
declarations.statement: public instance hasLimits : HasLimits DividedPowerRing.{u}
declarations.comment: existence of limits

declarations.name: DividedPowerRing.forgetPreservesLimits
declarations.doc: Limits of divided power rings are computed on their underlying commutative rings.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance forgetPreservesLimits :
    PreservesLimits DividedPowerRing.forget.{u}
declarations.comment: agreement with limits of rings

declarations.name: DividedPowerRing.isCorepresentable_of_cardinal_solutionSet
declarations.doc:
A limit-preserving functor on divided power rings is corepresentable when every one of its
elements is obtained from an element over a divided power ring whose underlying type has
uniformly bounded cardinality.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCorepresentable_of_cardinal_solutionSet
    (F : DividedPowerRing.{u} ⥤ Type u)
    [PreservesLimitsOfSize.{u, u} F]
    (hF : ∃ κ : Cardinal.{u}, ∀ (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (f : F.obj A),
      ∃ (A' : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (f' : F.obj A') (g : A' ⟶ A),
        F.map g f' = f ∧ Cardinal.mk A' ≤ κ) :
    F.IsCorepresentable

declarations.name: DividedPowerRing.instHasColimits
declarations.doc: The category of divided power rings has all colimits.
declarations.statement: public instance instHasColimits : HasColimits (DividedPowerRing.{u})

declarations.name: DividedPowers.Extends
declarations.doc:
A divided power structure `γ` on `I` extends along `f : A →+* B` if the extended ideal
`I.map f` admits a divided power structure making `f` a divided power morphism.

declarations.name: DividedPowers.existsUnique_extension
declarations.doc:
If a divided power structure extends along a ring homomorphism, the divided power structure
on the extended ideal making that homomorphism a divided power morphism is unique.
declarations.statement:
public lemma existsUnique_extension {A B : Type*} [CommSemiring A] [CommSemiring B]
    {I : Ideal A} (γ : _root_.DividedPowers I) (f : A →+* B)
    (h : Extends γ f) :
    ∃! δ : _root_.DividedPowers (I.map f),
      _root_.DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism γ δ f
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: DividedPowers.DividedPowerRing.dividedPowers_extends_of_map_eq_bot_or_isPrincipal_or_flat
declarations.doc:
Divided powers extend along a ring homomorphism if the mapped ideal is zero, the source
ideal is principal, or the homomorphism is flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem DividedPowerRing.dividedPowers_extends_of_map_eq_bot_or_isPrincipal_or_flat
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) {B : Type v} [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B)
    (h : (A.ideal.map f = ⊥) ∨ A.ideal.IsPrincipal ∨ f.Flat) :
    Extends A.dividedPowers f
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: DividedPowers.DividedPowerRing.isDPMorphism_extendedDividedPowersOfMapEqBotOrIsPrincipalOrFlat
declarations.doc:
The chosen divided powers on the mapped ideal make the original ring homomorphism a divided
power morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    DividedPowerRing.isDPMorphism_extendedDividedPowersOfMapEqBotOrIsPrincipalOrFlat
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) {B : Type v} [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B)
    (h : (A.ideal.map f = ⊥) ∨ A.ideal.IsPrincipal ∨ f.Flat) :
    _root_.DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism A.dividedPowers
      (DividedPowerRing.extendedDividedPowersOfMapEqBotOrIsPrincipalOrFlat A f h) f
declarations.comment: existence

declarations.name: DividedPowers.dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers
declarations.doc:
The canonical divided power structure on the divided power ideal of a finite-variable
divided power polynomial algebra.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers (A : DividedPowerRing.{u})
    (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] : _root_.DividedPowers (dividedPowerPolynomialIdeal A.ideal ι)
declarations.comment: divided power structure

declarations.name: DividedPowers.dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers_dpow_variable
declarations.doc: The canonical divided powers send `xᵢ` to the distinguished monomial `xᵢ^[n]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers_dpow_variable
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] (i : ι) (n : ℕ) :
    (dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A ι).dpow n
        (dividedPowerPolynomialVariable A i) =
      dividedPowerPolynomialVariableMonomial A i n
declarations.comment: value on variables

declarations.name: DividedPowers.dividedPowerPolynomialCoefficient_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
The coefficient map into the divided power polynomial algebra is a morphism of divided
power rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dividedPowerPolynomialCoefficient_isDPMorphism
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (ι : Type w) [Finite ι] :
    _root_.DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism A.dividedPowers
      (dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A ι)
      (algebraMap A (DividedPowerAlgebra A (ι →₀ A)))
declarations.comment: coefficient morphism

declarations.name: DividedPowers.dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers_unique
declarations.doc:
The canonical structure is the unique divided power structure which has the prescribed
values on variables and makes the coefficient map a divided power morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers_unique
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (ι : Type w) [Finite ι]
    (δ : _root_.DividedPowers (dividedPowerPolynomialIdeal A.ideal ι))
    (hvar : ∀ (i : ι) (n : ℕ),
      δ.dpow n (dividedPowerPolynomialVariable A i) =
        dividedPowerPolynomialVariableMonomial A i n)
    (hcoeff : _root_.DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism A.dividedPowers δ
      (algebraMap A (DividedPowerAlgebra A (ι →₀ A)))) :
    δ = dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A ι
declarations.comment: uniqueness

declarations.name: DividedPowers.existsUnique_dPMorphism_from_dividedPowerPolynomial
declarations.doc:
A divided power morphism on coefficients and one element of the target divided power ideal
for each variable extend uniquely to the divided power polynomial algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_dPMorphism_from_dividedPowerPolynomial
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (ι : Type w) [Finite ι]
    (C : DividedPowerRing.{v})
    (f : _root_.DividedPowers.DPMorphism A.dividedPowers C.dividedPowers)
    (k : ι → C.ideal) :
    ∃! φ : _root_.DividedPowers.DPMorphism (dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A ι)
        C.dividedPowers,
      (φ.comp (dividedPowerPolynomialCoefficientDPMorphism A ι) = f ∧
        ∀ i : ι, φ (dividedPowerPolynomialVariable A i) = (k i : C))
declarations.comment: universal property

declarations.name: DividedPowers.finiteStageMap_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc: Transition maps between finite stages preserve the canonical divided powers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteStageMap_isDPMorphism (A : DividedPowerRing.{u})
    {W : Type w} {E F : Finset W} (h : E ⊆ F) :
    _root_.DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism
      (dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A E)
      (dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A F)
      (finiteStageMap A h).toRingHom
declarations.comment: compatible_divided_powers

declarations.name: DividedPowers.setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers
declarations.doc:
The divided powers on the distinguished ideal of the divided power polynomial algebra
on an arbitrary type of variables, induced from all finite-variable subalgebras.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (W : Type w) :
    _root_.DividedPowers (dividedPowerPolynomialIdeal A.ideal W)
declarations.comment: compatible_divided_powers

declarations.name: DividedPowers.finiteStageInclusion_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc: Every finite-stage inclusion preserves divided powers induced on the colimit.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteStageInclusion_isDPMorphism (A : DividedPowerRing.{u})
    {W : Type w} (E : Finset W) :
    _root_.DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism
      (dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A E)
      (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A W)
      (finiteStageInclusion A E).toRingHom
declarations.comment: compatible_divided_powers

declarations.name: DividedPowers.setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers_dpow_variable
declarations.doc: The induced divided powers send a variable to its divided power monomial.
declarations.statement:
public theorem setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers_dpow_variable
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) {W : Type w} (i : W) (n : ℕ) :
    (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A W).dpow n
        (dividedPowerPolynomialVariable A i) =
      dividedPowerPolynomialVariableMonomial A i n
declarations.comment: compatible_divided_powers

declarations.name: DividedPowers.setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialCoefficient_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc: The coefficient map is a morphism of divided power rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialCoefficient_isDPMorphism
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (W : Type w) :
    _root_.DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism A.dividedPowers
      (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A W)
      (algebraMap A (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialAlgebra A W))
declarations.comment: compatible_divided_powers

declarations.name: DividedPowers.setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers_unique
declarations.doc: Compatibility with every finite stage uniquely determines the induced divided powers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers_unique
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (W : Type w)
    (δ : _root_.DividedPowers (dividedPowerPolynomialIdeal A.ideal W))
    (hδ : ∀ E : Finset W,
      _root_.DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (dividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A E) δ
        (finiteStageInclusion A E).toRingHom) :
    δ = setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A W
declarations.comment: compatible_divided_powers

declarations.name: DividedPowers.existsUnique_dPMorphism_from_setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomial
declarations.doc:
The universal property of a divided power polynomial algebra on an arbitrary type
of variables: a coefficient morphism and arbitrary images in the target ideal admit
exactly one extension as a divided power morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_dPMorphism_from_setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomial
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (W : Type w) (C : DividedPowerRing.{v})
    (f : _root_.DividedPowers.DPMorphism A.dividedPowers C.dividedPowers)
    (k : W → C.ideal) :
    ∃! φ : _root_.DividedPowers.DPMorphism
      (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers A W) C.dividedPowers,
      (φ.comp (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialCoefficientDPMorphism A W) = f ∧
        ∀ i : W, φ (dividedPowerPolynomialVariable A i) = (k i : C))
declarations.comment: set_indexed_universal_property

declarations.name: DividedPowers.finiteVariableInclusion
declarations.doc:
The canonical inclusion from the divided power polynomial algebra in `s` variables to
the one in `t` variables.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def finiteVariableInclusion (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    {s t : ℕ} (h : s ≤ t) :
    DividedPowerAlgebra A (Fin s →₀ A) →ₐ[A] DividedPowerAlgebra A (Fin t →₀ A)
declarations.comment: finite_variable_inclusion

declarations.name: DividedPowers.finiteVariableInclusion_variableMonomial
declarations.doc: The inclusion preserves each divided power monomial in an existing variable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finiteVariableInclusion_variableMonomial (A : Type u) [CommRing A]

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerEnvelope
declarations.doc:
The divided power envelope of an ideal containing the extension of the base divided power
ideal. Its fields give the structural divided power morphism and the functorial universal Hom

declarations.comment: the divided power envelope D_{B,gamma}(J) of J in B relative to (A, I, gamma)

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerEnvelope_factorization
declarations.doc:
The divided power envelope `D` of an ideal `J ⊆ B` factors the quotient map of `B` by `J`
as `B ⟶ D ⟶ B ⧸ J` through maps over `A`: the canonical map from `B` carries `J` into the
divided power ideal of `D`, and that ideal is precisely the kernel of the second map, which is
the unique ring map to `B ⧸ J` with those two properties.
declarations.statement:
public lemma dividedPowerEnvelope_factorization (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) {B : Type v}
    [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B) (J : Ideal B) (hJ : A.ideal.map f ≤ J)
    (D : DividedPowerEnvelope A f J hJ) :
    J.map D.algebraMap.toRingHom ≤ D.object.ideal ∧
      ∃ p : D.object.carrier →+* B ⧸ J,
        p.comp D.algebraMap.toRingHom = Ideal.Quotient.mk J ∧
        p.comp D.structureMap.toRingHom = (Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp f ∧
        Function.Surjective p ∧
        RingHom.ker p = D.object.ideal ∧
        ∀ p' : D.object.carrier →+* B ⧸ J,
          p'.comp D.algebraMap.toRingHom = Ideal.Quotient.mk J →
          D.object.ideal ≤ RingHom.ker p' → p' = p

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerEnvelope_quotient
declarations.doc:
For a surjection `B' → B`, the canonical map from the divided power envelope of the
inverse image of `J` to the divided power envelope of `J` is surjective, and its kernel is
generated by the positive divided powers of the original kernel.
declarations.statement:
public lemma dividedPowerEnvelope_quotient
    (A : DividedPowerRing) {B' B : Type u} [CommRing B'] [CommRing B]
    (f' : A →+* B') (f : A →+* B) (phi : B' →+* B)
    (hphi : phi.comp f' = f) (hphi_surjective : Function.Surjective phi)
    (J : Ideal B) (hJ : A.ideal.map f ≤ J)
    (D : DividedPowerEnvelope A f J hJ)
    (D' : DividedPowerEnvelope A f' (J.comap phi) (by
      rw [← Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap, Ideal.map_map, hphi]
      exact hJ)) :
    ∃ q : DividedPowers.DPMorphism D'.object.dividedPowers D.object.dividedPowers,
      q.comp D'.structureMap = D.structureMap ∧
      q.toRingHom.comp D'.algebraMap.toRingHom = D.algebraMap.toRingHom.comp phi ∧
      Function.Surjective q ∧
      D'.object.ideal.map q.toRingHom = D.object.ideal ∧
      RingHom.ker q.toRingHom = dividedPowerKernelIdeal phi D' ∧
      (∀ q' : DividedPowers.DPMorphism D'.object.dividedPowers D.object.dividedPowers,
        q'.comp D'.structureMap = D.structureMap →
        q'.toRingHom.comp D'.algebraMap.toRingHom = D.algebraMap.toRingHom.comp phi →
        q' = q)

declarations.name: Crystalline.surjectiveDividedPowerPolynomialMap
declarations.doc:
The divided power polynomial ring maps onto the envelope of an ideal generated
by the coefficient divided power ideal and the chosen variables.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def surjectiveDividedPowerPolynomialMap
    (B : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (T : Type w)
    (J : Ideal B) (hJ : B.ideal.map (RingHom.id B) ≤ J)
    (f : T → B) (hf : J = B.ideal ⊔ Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (D : DividedPowerEnvelope B (RingHom.id B) J hJ) :
    { ψ : DividedPowers.DPMorphism
        (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers B T)
        D.object.dividedPowers //
      ψ.comp (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialCoefficientDPMorphism B T) =
          D.structureMap ∧
        (∀ t : T, ψ (dividedPowerPolynomialVariable B t) =
          D.algebraMap.toRingHom (f t)) ∧
        Function.Surjective ψ }
declarations.comment: surjection

declarations.name: Crystalline.ker_surjectiveDividedPowerPolynomialMap
declarations.doc:
The kernel of the surjection from the divided power polynomial algebra to the divided
power envelope is generated by variable relations and divided powers of linear relations.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ker_surjectiveDividedPowerPolynomialMap
    (B : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (T : Type w)
    (J : Ideal B) (hJ : B.ideal.map (RingHom.id B) ≤ J)
    (f : T → B) (hf : J = B.ideal ⊔ Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (D : DividedPowerEnvelope B (RingHom.id B) J hJ) :
    RingHom.ker (surjectiveDividedPowerPolynomialMap B T J hJ f hf D).1.toRingHom =
      kernelPresentationIdeal B T f
declarations.comment: kernel

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerEnvelope_baseChange
declarations.doc:
A divided power envelope commutes with base change when the base change is flat modulo the
base divided power ideal and its first Tor with that quotient vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dividedPowerEnvelope_baseChange [Algebra B B'] (f : A →+* B) (J : Ideal B)
    (hJ : A.ideal.map f ≤ J)
    (D : DividedPowerEnvelope A f J hJ)
    (D' : DividedPowerEnvelope A ((algebraMap B B').comp f)
      (J.map (algebraMap B B'))
      (map_baseIdeal_le_map f (algebraMap B B') J hJ))
    (hflat : Module.Flat (B ⧸ (A.ideal.map f))
      (B' ⧸ ((A.ideal.map f).map (algebraMap B B'))))
    (hTor : IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} B) 1).obj (ModuleCat.of B B')).obj
      (ModuleCat.of B (B ⧸ (A.ideal.map f))))) :
    letI : Algebra B D.object := D.algebraMap.toRingHom.toAlgebra;
    ∃ e : (D.object ⊗[B] B') ≃+* D'.object,
      ∀ x y, e (TensorProduct.tmul B x y) =
        (baseChangeDPMorphism f (algebraMap B B') J hJ D D').toRingHom x *
          D'.algebraMap.toRingHom y

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerEnvelope_baseChange_of_flat_quotient
declarations.doc:
A divided power envelope commutes with a flat extension modulo the divided
power ideals, provided the target ideal is the extension of the source ideal
plus the target divided power ideal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dividedPowerEnvelope_baseChange_of_flat_quotient
    {B B' : DividedPowerRing.{u}}
    (φ : DividedPowers.DPMorphism B.dividedPowers B'.dividedPowers)
    (J : Ideal B) (J' : Ideal B')
    (hJ : B.ideal.map (RingHom.id B) ≤ J)
    (hJ' : B'.ideal.map (RingHom.id B') ≤ J')
    (hJ'_eq : J' = J.map φ.toRingHom ⊔ B'.ideal)
    (hflat : RingHom.Flat (Ideal.quotientMap B'.ideal φ.toRingHom
      (Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mp φ.ideal_comp)))
    (D : DividedPowerEnvelope B (RingHom.id B) J hJ)
    (D' : DividedPowerEnvelope B' (RingHom.id B') J' hJ') :
    letI : Algebra B D.object := D.algebraMap.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra B B' := φ.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    ∃ e : (D.object ⊗[B] B') ≃+* D'.object,
      ∀ x y, e (TensorProduct.tmul B x y) =
        (dividedPowerEnvelopeBaseChangeMap φ J J' hJ hJ'
          (by rw [hJ'_eq]; exact le_sup_left) D D').toRingHom x *
          D'.algebraMap.toRingHom y

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerEnvelope_tensor_equiv_quotient
declarations.doc:
The quotient presentation of a divided power envelope after extension of its
coefficient ring. The formula on pure tensors identifies the displayed equivalence
with the canonical base-change map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dividedPowerEnvelope_tensor_equiv_quotient
    (B : DividedPowerRing.{u}) (T : Type w)
    (J : Ideal B) (hJ : B.ideal.map (RingHom.id B) ≤ J)
    (f : T → B) (hf : J = B.ideal ⊔ Ideal.span (Set.range f))
    (D : DividedPowerEnvelope B (RingHom.id B) J hJ)
    (B' : Type v) [CommRing B'] [Algebra B B'] :
    letI : Algebra B D.object := D.algebraMap.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    let ψ := (surjectiveDividedPowerPolynomialMap B T J hJ f hf D).1
    let F := setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialAlgebra B T
    let F' := setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialAlgebra B' T
    let baseChange : F →+* F' :=
      (DividedPowerAlgebra.map B'
        (Finsupp.mapRange.linearMap (α := T) (Algebra.linearMap B B'))).toRingHom
    let K' : Ideal F' := (RingHom.ker ψ.toRingHom).map baseChange
    ∃ e : (D.object ⊗[B] B') ≃+* (F' ⧸ K'),
      ∀ (p : F) (b' : B'),
        e (TensorProduct.tmul B (ψ p) b') =
          Ideal.Quotient.mk K' (baseChange p * algebraMap B' F' b')

declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_dividedPowers_secondOrderExtension
declarations.doc:
The ideal of a second-order extension has divided powers given by the explicit
second-order formula, and the scalar inclusion is a divided-power morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dividedPowers_secondOrderExtension
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (γ : DividedPowers I)
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (q : M →ₗ[A] M →ₗ[A] N)
    {B : Type x} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (e : B ≃+ A × (M × N))
    (halgebra : ∀ a : A, e (algebraMap A B a) = (a, (0, 0)))
    (hmul : ∀ b b' : B,
      e (b * b') =
        ((e b).1 * (e b').1,
          ((e b).1 • (e b').2.1 + (e b').1 • (e b).2.1,
            (e b).1 • (e b').2.2 + (e b').1 • (e b).2.2 +
              q (e b).2.1 (e b').2.1 + q (e b').2.1 (e b).2.1)))
    (J : Ideal B) (hJ : ∀ b : B, b ∈ J ↔ (e b).1 ∈ I) :
    ∃ δ : DividedPowers J,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (b : B), 2 ≤ n → b ∈ J →
        δ.dpow n b = e.symm
          (γ.dpow n (e b).1,
            (γ.dpow (n - 1) (e b).1 • (e b).2.1,
              γ.dpow (n - 1) (e b).1 • (e b).2.2 +
                γ.dpow (n - 2) (e b).1 • q (e b).2.1 (e b).2.1))) ∧
      DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism γ δ (algebraMap A B)
declarations.comment: the first-order case, at N = 0 and q = 0

declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_dividedPowers_secondOrderExtension
declarations.doc:
The ideal of a second-order extension has divided powers given by the explicit
second-order formula, and the scalar inclusion is a divided-power morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dividedPowers_secondOrderExtension
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (γ : DividedPowers I)
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
    (q : M →ₗ[A] M →ₗ[A] N)
    {B : Type x} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (e : B ≃+ A × (M × N))
    (halgebra : ∀ a : A, e (algebraMap A B a) = (a, (0, 0)))
    (hmul : ∀ b b' : B,
      e (b * b') =
        ((e b).1 * (e b').1,
          ((e b).1 • (e b').2.1 + (e b').1 • (e b).2.1,
            (e b).1 • (e b').2.2 + (e b').1 • (e b).2.2 +
              q (e b).2.1 (e b').2.1 + q (e b').2.1 (e b).2.1)))
    (J : Ideal B) (hJ : ∀ b : B, b ∈ J ↔ (e b).1 ∈ I) :
    ∃ δ : DividedPowers J,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (b : B), 2 ≤ n → b ∈ J →
        δ.dpow n b = e.symm
          (γ.dpow n (e b).1,
            (γ.dpow (n - 1) (e b).1 • (e b).2.1,
              γ.dpow (n - 1) (e b).1 • (e b).2.2 +
                γ.dpow (n - 2) (e b).1 • q (e b).2.1 (e b).2.1))) ∧
      DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism γ δ (algebraMap A B)

      (DividedPowerThickening.{0, 0, 0} (integersAtPrimeSituation p))
