declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_forall_le_levelEnvelope_hom
declarations.doc:
**Every sufficiently high finite-level divided power envelope maps to a given affine divided
power thickening.**  The level above which this holds is the larger of the cutoff of
`Crystalline.levelCrystallineThickening` and the nilpotency exponent of `p` in `B`, and the
exponent enters the construction only through those two facts: that it is a level, and that
`(p)^e` vanishes in `B`.

`Crystalline.exists_levelEnvelope_hom` is this at the cutoff itself.  The uniform form is what
lets the morphism be produced at a level chosen for some other reason — for instance at a level
past the cutoffs of the two halves of [Stacks, Tag 07KG] part (2), where
`Crystalline.levelFamilyIso` identifies this family of levels with the finite levels of the
completed envelope.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_forall_le_levelEnvelope_hom
    (s : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v})
    {P : Type u} [CommRing P] [Algebra s.A P]
    (hP : ∃ (σ : Type u), Nonempty (MvPolynomial σ s.A ≃ₐ[s.A] P))
    (f : P →ₐ[s.A] s.C) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    (B : DividedPowerThickening.{u, v, u} s) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ e, N ≤ e →
      ∃ he : (levelCrystallineThickening s f hf).1 ≤ e,
        Nonempty (((levelCrystallineThickening s f hf).2 e he).1 ⟶ B)
declarations.comment: for every sufficiently large level

declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_levelEnvelope_hom
declarations.doc:
A sufficiently high finite-level divided power envelope maps to any affine
divided power thickening.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_levelEnvelope_hom
    (s : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v})
    {P : Type u} [CommRing P] [Algebra s.A P]
    (hP : ∃ (σ : Type u), Nonempty (MvPolynomial σ s.A ≃ₐ[s.A] P))
    (f : P →ₐ[s.A] s.C) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    (B : DividedPowerThickening.{u, v, u} s) :
    ∃ e : ℕ,
      ∃ he : (levelCrystallineThickening s f hf).1 ≤ e,
        Nonempty (((levelCrystallineThickening s f hf).2 e he).1 ⟶ B)

declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_forall_le_levelThickening_hom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Lemma 60.5.6, Tag 07HP] for the finite levels of the completed divided power
envelope of a polynomial presentation, at every sufficiently large level**: every divided power
thickening `B` of `C/A` receives a morphism from `D̂/(p)^e` for all large `e`.

`Crystalline.exists_levelThickening_hom` is the same statement at the single object
`Crystalline.completedCrystallineThickening s q hq` and for a single level.  Both generalisations
are needed to reach the levels of `...SmallSite.wholeSpaceSystem`, which are the levels of
`Crystalline.tensorPowerEnvelopeThickening` and not of
`Crystalline.completedCrystallineThickening`: the object is arbitrary subject to being a
realisation of the completed envelope of some polynomial presentation, which is what lets the
*other* presentation `Crystalline.tensorPowerPresentation s q 0` be used, and the level is
arbitrary subject to being large, which is what lets it be written in the form
`Crystalline.uniformLevel s + e` the system is indexed by.

The three hypotheses `Crystalline.levelFamilyIso` pins its object down with are three fields of
`Crystalline.CompletedEnvelopeThickening`, read across the two `rfl`s
`Crystalline.completedEnvelopeDPRing_eq` and
`Crystalline.presentationEnvelope_eq_polynomialDividedPowerEnvelope`; so nothing is carried beyond
surjectivity of the presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_forall_le_levelThickening_hom (W : CompletedEnvelopeThickening s q hq)
    (B : DividedPowerThickening.{u, u, u} s) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ e, N ≤ e →
      ∃ h : IsPAdicLevel W.thickening.ring.ideal W.thickening.ring.dividedPowers s.p e,
        Nonempty (levelThickeningObj W.thickening e h ⟶ B)
declarations.comment: for every sufficiently large finite level of the completed envelope

declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_levelThickening_hom
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07HP] for the second family of levels: every divided power thickening of `C/A`
receives a morphism from a finite level `D̂/(p)^e` of the completed envelope.**

This is the statement the hypothesis `hdet` of
`...SmallSite.LevelComparison07JG.faithful_functor_of_isLevel` wants, on the family `hdet` is
stated over: the levels of `...SmallSite.wholeSpaceSystem` are the levels
`Crystalline.levelThickening` of `Crystalline.tensorPowerEnvelopeThickening`, whose ring is
`Crystalline.completedPresentationEnvelope` by `Crystalline.completedEnvelopeDPRing_eq`, and not
the levels `Crystalline.levelCrystallineThickening` that [Stacks, Tag 07HP] produces morphisms out
of.

Two things are composed.  `Crystalline.exists_forall_le_levelEnvelope_hom` gives the morphism out
of the first family at *every* sufficiently large level, so a level can be chosen past the cutoffs
of the two halves of [Stacks, Tag 07KG] part (2) as well; there
`Crystalline.completedLevelFamilyIso` identifies the two families.  The two proofs that the chosen
level is past the cutoff of the first family are proofs of the same proposition, so the two levels
of the first family they name are the same object.

This is stated at the single object `Crystalline.completedCrystallineThickening s f hf`, the
completed envelope of the presentation `f` itself, and at a single level.  Neither restriction can
be lifted here, and both have to be for the levels of `...SmallSite.wholeSpaceSystem`, which are
the levels of `Crystalline.tensorPowerEnvelopeThickening` in degree zero and so belong to a
*different* presentation.  The generalisation on both counts is
`Crystalline.exists_forall_le_levelThickening_hom` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Crystalline/LevelFamilyFinality.lean`, which applies
`Crystalline.levelFamilyIso` at an arbitrary `Crystalline.CompletedEnvelopeThickening` — three of
whose fields are its three pinning hypotheses on the nose — and so needs no comparison of the two
presentations.

This does not by itself discharge `hdet`: that a morphism of crystals is determined by its
restrictions to the levels needs, beyond a morphism `B ⟶ T_e` for every `B`, the crystal
property, which is `...SmallSite.moduleRestrictionSheafMap_eq_of_hom` of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Crystalline/LevelCrystalDeterminacy.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_levelThickening_hom (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    (hP : ∃ σ : Type u, Nonempty (MvPolynomial σ s.A ≃ₐ[s.A] P))
    (B : DividedPowerThickening.{u, u, u} s) :
    ∃ (e : ℕ) (h : IsPAdicLevel ((completedCrystallineThickening s f hf).2.1).ring.ideal
        ((completedCrystallineThickening s f hf).2.1).ring.dividedPowers s.p e),
      Nonempty (levelThickeningObj (completedCrystallineThickening s f hf).2.1 e h ⟶ B)
declarations.comment: for the finite levels of the completed envelope

declarations.name: Crystalline.DividedPowerDerivation
declarations.doc:
A divided power `A`-derivation from a divided power ring `B` into a `B`-module `M`.

It is an additive map satisfying the Leibniz rule, vanishing on the image of `A`, and
sending `δ n x` to `δ (n - 1) x • D x` for every positive `n` and every `x` in the
distinguished ideal.
declarations.statement:
public structure DividedPowerDerivation
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (B : DividedPowerRing.{v}) (f : A →+* B)
    (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
    extends Derivation ℤ B M

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerDifferentialsQuotientEquiv
declarations.doc: The canonical quotient formula for divided power differentials.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def dividedPowerDifferentialsQuotientEquiv
    (K : Ideal B) (hK : DividedPowers.IsSubDPIdeal B.dividedPowers K) :
    let δ' := DividedPowers.Quotient.dividedPowers B.dividedPowers
      (J := K) (by simpa [inf_of_le_left hK.isSubideal] using hK)
    { e :
        (TensorProduct B (B ⧸ K)
          (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) B.dividedPowers) ⧸
          Submodule.span (B ⧸ K)
            (Set.range fun k : K ↦ TensorProduct.tmul B (1 : B ⧸ K)
              (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) B.dividedPowers k)))
          ≃ₗ[B ⧸ K]
          dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) δ' //
      ∀ b : B,
        e (Submodule.Quotient.mk
          (TensorProduct.tmul B (1 : B ⧸ K)
            (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) B.dividedPowers b))) =
          dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) δ' (Ideal.Quotient.mk K b) }
declarations.comment: quotient

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerDifferentialsDividedPowerPolynomialEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The divided power polynomial decomposition of divided power differentials.**  For a divided
power ring `(B, I, δ)` over `A` and the divided power polynomial algebra `P = B⟨x_w : w ∈ W⟩`
with divided power ideal `IP + P₊`, one has
`Ω¹_{P/A,δ'} = (P ⊗_B Ω¹_{B/A,δ}) ⊕ ⨁_w P · d x_w`, the isomorphism being characterized by its
values on the differentials of coefficients and of variables.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def dividedPowerDifferentialsDividedPowerPolynomialEquiv
    {A : Type uA} [CommRing A] (B : DividedPowerRing.{uB}) [Algebra A B] (W : Type uW) :
    { e : dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A)
          (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers B W) ≃ₗ[
        setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialAlgebra B W]
        ((setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialAlgebra B W ⊗[B]
            dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) B.dividedPowers) ×
          (W →₀ setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialAlgebra B W)) //
      (∀ b : B, e (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A)
          (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers B W)
          (algebraMap (B : Type uB) (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialAlgebra B W) b)) =
        (1 ⊗ₜ[B] dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) B.dividedPowers b, 0)) ∧
      (∀ w : W, e (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A)
          (setIndexedDividedPowerPolynomialDividedPowers B W)
          (dividedPowerPolynomialVariable (B : Type uB) w)) = (0, Finsupp.single w 1)) }
declarations.comment: divided_power_polynomial

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerDifferentialsPolynomialEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical polynomial decomposition of divided power differentials,
characterized by the differentials of constants and of the polynomial variable.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def dividedPowerDifferentialsPolynomialEquiv
    (δ' : DividedPowers (B.ideal.map (Polynomial.C : B →+* B[X])))
    (_h : DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism B.dividedPowers δ'
      (Polynomial.C : B →+* B[X])) :
    { e : dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) δ' ≃ₗ[B[X]]
        (TensorProduct B B[X] (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) B.dividedPowers) × B[X]) //
      (∀ b : B, e (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) δ' (Polynomial.C b)) =
        (TensorProduct.tmul B (1 : B[X])
          (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) B.dividedPowers b), 0)) ∧
      e (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) δ' Polynomial.X) = (0, 1) }
declarations.comment: polynomial

declarations.name: Crystalline.Pushout.dividedPowerDifferentialsEquivDiagonalConormal
declarations.doc:
Divided power differentials are canonically the conormal module of the diagonal,
modulo the square of its kernel and divided powers of order at least two.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def dividedPowerDifferentialsEquivDiagonalConormal
    (h : IsPushout f f s₀ s₁) :
    letI : Algebra A B := f.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    {e : dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) B.dividedPowers ≃ₗ[B] diagonalConormal h //
      ∀ b : B,
        e (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) B.dividedPowers b) = diagonalDifference h b}
declarations.comment: canonical identification

declarations.name: Crystalline.DividedPowerThickening.isSubDPIdeal_and_existsUnique_dividedPowerDifferentialsEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07HV.** In Situation 07MD, let `(B, J, δ)` be an object of `CRIS(C/A)`
and let `(B(1), J(1), δ(1))` be its coproduct with itself in `CRIS(C/A)`, with coprojections
`s₀, s₁`.  Denote `K = Ker(B(1) → B)`.  Then `K ∩ J(1) ⊂ J(1)` is preserved by the divided power
structure, and `Ω_{B/A,δ} = K / (K² + (K ∩ J(1))^{[2]})` canonically: there is exactly one
`B`-linear isomorphism carrying `d b` to the class of `s₁ b - s₀ b` for every `b ∈ B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSubDPIdeal_and_existsUnique_dividedPowerDifferentialsEquiv
    (h : IsColimit (BinaryCofan.mk s₀ s₁)) :
    letI : Algebra S.A X.ring := X.fromBase.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    Y.ring.dividedPowers.IsSubDPIdeal (diagonalKernel h ⊓ Y.ring.ideal) ∧
      ∃! e : dividedPowerDifferentials (A := S.A) X.ring.dividedPowers ≃ₗ[X.ring]
          diagonalConormal h,
        ∀ b : X.ring,
          e (dividedPowerDifferential (A := S.A) X.ring.dividedPowers b) =
            diagonalDifference h b
declarations.comment: both parts, for an object of CRIS(C/A) and its self-coproduct in CRIS(C/A)

declarations.name: Crystalline.DividedPowerThickening.diagonalKernel_isSubDPIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07HV, part (1).** Let `(B, J, δ)` be an object of `CRIS(C/A)` and
`(B(1), J(1), δ(1))` its coproduct with itself in `CRIS(C/A)`, with `K = Ker(B(1) → B)`.  Then
`K ∩ J(1) ⊂ J(1)` is preserved by the divided power structure.
declarations.statement:
public theorem diagonalKernel_isSubDPIdeal
    (h : IsColimit (BinaryCofan.mk s₀ s₁)) :
    Y.ring.dividedPowers.IsSubDPIdeal (diagonalKernel h ⊓ Y.ring.ideal)
declarations.comment: part (1) in CRIS(C/A): K ∩ J(1) is preserved by the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerEnvelopeDifferentialsEquiv
declarations.doc:
The divided power differentials of a divided power envelope are canonically the
base change of the ordinary Kähler differentials of the original algebra.  The
displayed equation identifies the canonical equivalence on universal differentials.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def dividedPowerEnvelopeDifferentialsEquiv
    (A : DividedPowerRing.{u}) {B : Type u} [CommRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (J : Ideal B) (hJ : A.ideal.map f ≤ J)
    (E : DividedPowerEnvelope A f J hJ) :
    letI : Algebra A B := f.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra B E.object := E.algebraMap.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra A E.object := E.structureMap.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    { e : dividedPowerDifferentials
          (A := A) E.object.dividedPowers ≃ₗ[E.object]
          TensorProduct B E.object (KaehlerDifferential A B) //
      ∀ b : B,
        e (dividedPowerDifferential
            (A := A) E.object.dividedPowers (E.algebraMap.toRingHom b)) =
          (1 : E.object) ⊗ₜ[B] KaehlerDifferential.D A B b }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialFormsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tags 07HX, 0FL5 and 0FLV.** The canonical map
`f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⟶ Ω^n_{X'/S'}` on relative differential forms attached to a commutative square of
schemes: the comparison of Tag 01CI followed by the degree-`n` component of the comparison of
exterior algebras.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def relativeDifferentialFormsMap (hcomm : f ≫ p = p' ≫ g) (n : ℤ) :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj (relativeDifferentialForms p n) ⟶
      relativeDifferentialForms p' n
declarations.comment: the linearized canonical map on differential forms

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamAbelianPushforwardMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07HX.** The canonical map of de Rham complexes
`Ω^•_{X/S} ⟶ f_*Ω^•_{X'/S'}` of a commutative square of schemes, read in abelian sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def deRhamAbelianPushforwardMap (hcomm : f ≫ p = p' ≫ g) :
    SheafOfModules.deRhamAbelianComplex (deRhamAlgebras p)
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras p)) ⟶
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.LerayLowDegree.abelianPushforward.{u, u}
          f.base).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        (SheafOfModules.deRhamAbelianComplex (deRhamAlgebras p')
          (SheafOfModules.deRhamDifferential (deRhamAlgebras p')))
declarations.comment: the canonical map of complexes `Ω^•_{X/S} ⟶ f_*Ω^•_{X'/S'}`

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamPullback.deRhamPullbackChain
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07HX.** The canonical morphism of complexes

`ρ : f^{-1}Ω^•_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω^•_{X/S}`

of `(f∘g)^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules on `X`, adjoint to the canonical map
`Ω^•_{Y/S} ⟶ (relativeBase f g)_*Ω^•_{X/S}` of Tag 07HX read in `g^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def deRhamPullbackChain :
    ((_root_.pullback (relativeBase f g)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        (Scheme.Hom.deRhamComplex g) ⟶
      Scheme.Hom.deRhamComplex (f ≫ g)
declarations.comment: the canonical map `f⁻¹Ω^•_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω^•_{X/S}` of a morphism of schemes over `S`, read in complexes of `(f∘g)^{-1}𝒪_S`-modules. The companion map `Ω^•_{X/S} ⟶ f_*Ω^•_{X'/S'}`, in abelian sheaves, is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.deRhamAbelianPushforwardMap`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.homEquiv_relativeDifferentialFormsMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07HX.** The canonical map `f^*Ω^n_{X/S} ⟶ Ω^n_{X'/S'}` on relative
differential forms is the adjoint transpose of the degree-`n` component of the canonical
homomorphism of sheaves of graded algebras `⋀ Ω_{X/S} ⟶ f_*(⋀ Ω_{X'/S'})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homEquiv_relativeDifferentialFormsMap (hcomm : f ≫ p = p' ≫ g) (n : ℤ) :
    (modulePullbackPushforwardAdjunction f.toLRSHom.toShHom).homEquiv
        (relativeDifferentialForms p n) (relativeDifferentialForms p' n)
        (relativeDifferentialFormsMap f p p' g hcomm n) =
      (deRhamFormsPushforwardHom f p p' g hcomm).app n
declarations.comment: the linearized canonical map on forms is the transpose of the graded homomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.DeRhamPullback.deRhamPullbackChain_f
declarations.doc:
**The degreewise factorization of the de Rham pullback map.** The degree-`n` component of
`ρ : f^{-1}Ω^•_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω^•_{X/S}` is the comparison `f^{-1}Ω^n_{Y/S} ⟶ f^*Ω^n_{Y/S}` followed
by the `𝒪_X`-linear canonical map `f^*Ω^n_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω^n_{X/S}` on relative differential forms,
with coefficients restricted along `(f∘g)^{-1}𝒪_S ⟶ 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem deRhamPullbackChain_f (n : ℕ) :
    (deRhamPullbackChain f g).f n =
      relativeInverseImageToPullback f g (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialForms g (n : ℤ)) ≫
        (_root_.pushforward (toInverseImageBase (f ≫ g))).map
          (Scheme.Hom.relativeDifferentialFormsMap f g (f ≫ g) (𝟙 S)
            ((Category.comp_id (f ≫ g)).symm) (n : ℤ))
declarations.comment: the degree-n component of the canonical map f⁻¹Ω^•_{Y/S} ⟶ Ω^•_{X/S}

declarations.name: exists_unique_quotient_deRhamDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07HY.** Let `S` be the de Rham complex of `B` over `A` and let
`π : Ω[B⁄A] → Ω` be a surjection of `B`-modules whose kernel is generated by elements `ω` with
`π ω = 0` and `(⋀^2 π) (d ω) = 0`.  Then there is exactly one family of `A`-linear maps
`Ω^p = ⋀[B]^p Ω → Ω^{p+1}` making the squares `d ∘ (⋀^p π) = (⋀^{p+1} π) ∘ d_{B/A}` commute;
it obeys the same rule `d (f₀ · d f₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d f_p) = d f₀ ∧ ⋯ ∧ d f_p` on generators, with
`d f = π (d_{B/A} f)`, and it is again a complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_unique_quotient_deRhamDifferential
    (S : SourceDeRham A B)
    {Ω : Type u} [AddCommGroup Ω] [Module B Ω] (π : Ω[B⁄A] →ₗ[B] Ω)
    (hπ : Function.Surjective π)
    (hgen : S.GenerationHypothesis π) :
    ∃ dΩ : (∀ p, TgtA A B Ω p →ₗ[A] TgtA A B Ω (p + 1)),
      S.Commutes π dΩ ∧
      SatisfiesRule π dΩ ∧
      (∀ dΩ' : (∀ p, TgtA A B Ω p →ₗ[A] TgtA A B Ω (p + 1)), S.Commutes π dΩ' → dΩ' = dΩ) ∧
      (∀ p, (dΩ (p + 1)).comp (dΩ p) = 0)

The module `Ωⁱ_{B/A,δ}`, the `i`-th exterior power of the module of divided

    DividedPowerDeRhamComplex (A := A) hJ

declarations.doc: The generator formula uniquely determines the divided power de Rham complex.

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerDifferentials_lift
declarations.doc:
The quotient of Kähler differentials by the divided power relations represents
divided-power-compatible `A`-derivations.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dividedPowerDifferentials_lift
    {M : Type w} [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
    (D : DividedPowerDerivation A B (algebraMap A B) M) :
    ∃! lift :
        dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) B.dividedPowers →ₗ[B] M,
      ∀ b : B,
        lift (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) B.dividedPowers b) = D b
declarations.comment: the universal divided power derivation

declarations.name: Crystalline.dividedPowerDifferentials_generationHypothesis
declarations.doc:
The quotient projection satisfies the generation hypothesis for descending the de Rham
differential to divided power differential forms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dividedPowerDifferentials_generationHypothesis
    (S : SourceDeRham A B) :
    S.GenerationHypothesis
      (dividedPowerDifferentialRelations (A := A) B.dividedPowers).mkQ
declarations.comment: descent of the de Rham differential

declarations.name: Crystalline.Connection
declarations.doc:
An additive connection on a `B`-module `M` relative to a map from the Kähler
differentials of `B` over `A` to a `B`-module `Ω`.
declarations.statement:
public structure Connection
    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    {Omega : Type*} [AddCommGroup Omega] [Module B Omega]
    (pi : Ω[B⁄A] →ₗ[B] Omega)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
declarations.comment: connection

declarations.name: Crystalline.extendedConnection
declarations.doc:
A connection extends to the tensor products with all exterior powers of `Omega`. On a pure
tensor its value is the wedge of the connection term with the form, plus the coefficient tensored
with the descended de Rham differential of the form.

`S` is not de Rham data: `Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.sourceDeRham` constructs the de Rham
complex of `B` over `A` ([Stacks, Tag 0FKF]) and
`Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.SourceDeRham.eq_sourceDeRham` proves it is the only term of
`SourceDeRham A B`, so `S` names that complex; its square-zero property is derived from the
defining rule on generators by `Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.comp_eq_zero_of_gen`.  The
quotient `π : Ω[B⁄A] → Omega` with `hπ` and `hgen` is the setting [Stacks, Tag 07I0] itself
fixes, by reference to [Stacks, Tag 07HY].
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def extendedConnection
    (S : SourceDeRham A B) (π : Ω[B⁄A] →ₗ[B] Omega)
    (hπ : Function.Surjective π) (hgen : S.GenerationHypothesis π)
    (nabla : Connection A B π M) : ExtendedConnection S π nabla
declarations.comment: extended_connection. The extension of a connection to M ⊗ ⋀^p Omega in every degree, with the displayed formula on pure tensors. The de Rham differentials of B over A are constructed, in Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.sourceDeRham, and SourceDeRham.eq_sourceDeRham proves that term is the only one of SourceDeRham A B, so the binder S names the de Rham complex of 0FKF; its complex property d ∘ d = 0 follows from the defining rule on generators by comp_eq_zero_of_gen. The binders π, hπ, hgen are the quotient of the differentials that the tag itself fixes, by reference to 07HY

declarations.name: Crystalline.Connection.IsIntegrable
declarations.doc:
A connection is integrable if its composite with its canonical extension from one-forms to
two-forms is zero.

As in `Crystalline.extendedConnection`, `S` is not de Rham data: it can only be
`Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.sourceDeRham A B`, the de Rham complex of [Stacks, Tag 0FKF],
by `Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.SourceDeRham.eq_sourceDeRham`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def IsIntegrable
    (S : SourceDeRham A B) (pi : Ω[B⁄A] →ₗ[B] Omega)
    (hpi : Function.Surjective pi) (hgen : S.GenerationHypothesis pi)
    (nabla : Connection A B pi M) : Prop
declarations.comment: integrable_connection. Vanishing of the composite M → M ⊗ Ω^1 → M ⊗ Ω^2 of a connection with its own degree-one extension. As for extended_connection, the de Rham differentials are constructed in Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.sourceDeRham and SourceDeRham.eq_sourceDeRham proves the binder S admits that term alone

declarations.name: Crystalline.extendedConnection_comp_self_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The consecutive extended differentials of an integrable connection compose to zero, so an
integrable connection makes `M ⊗_B Ω^•` a complex.

`S` is not de Rham data: it can only be `Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.sourceDeRham A B`, the
de Rham complex of [Stacks, Tag 0FKF], by
`Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.SourceDeRham.eq_sourceDeRham`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem extendedConnection_comp_self_eq_zero
    (S : SourceDeRham A B) (pi : Ω[B⁄A] →ₗ[B] Omega)
    (hpi : Function.Surjective pi) (hgen : S.GenerationHypothesis pi)
    (nabla : Connection A B pi M)
    (hintegrable : Connection.IsIntegrable S pi hpi hgen nabla) (p : ℕ) :
    ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap (p + 1)).comp
      ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap p) = 0
declarations.comment: connection_de_rham_complex. The last clause of the tag: for an integrable connection the extended differentials compose to zero, so M ⊗ Ω^• is a complex. The de Rham differentials of B over A are constructed in Stacks.DeRham.DifferentialDescent.sourceDeRham and SourceDeRham.eq_sourceDeRham proves the binder S admits that term alone

A divided power structure on a sheaf of ideals: every ideal of sections has divided powers,

declarations.name: Crystalline.DividedPowerScheme

A scheme equipped with a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals and a divided power structure on

declarations.name: Crystalline.DividedPowerScheme.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of divided power schemes. On each open subset of the target, the induced map on
sections is a homomorphism of divided power rings. In particular, it maps the target ideal into
the source ideal.
declarations.statement: public structure Hom (X Y : DividedPowerScheme.{u})
declarations.comment: morphisms of divided power schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.SchemeThickening
declarations.doc:
**A divided power thickening of schemes.**  A thickening `immersion : source ⟶ target.scheme`
whose defining ideal is, on every affine open, the divided power ideal of `target`.
declarations.statement: structure SchemeThickening

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.topology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  The big crystalline site of `X` over `(S, I, γ)`: the category
`CRIS(X/S)` with the Zariski topology, the topology generated by the Zariski covering families of
divided power thickenings.
declarations.statement: abbrev topology (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) : GrothendieckTopology (Thickening S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening
declarations.doc:
An object of the big crystalline category `CRIS(X/S)`: a divided power thickening `U ↪ T`
over `S`, together with a map `U ⟶ X` over `S`.
declarations.statement: structure Thickening (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.Hom
declarations.doc:
A morphism of `CRIS(X/S)`: a map of the underlying thickenings over the divided power base
which is compatible with the maps to `X`.
declarations.statement: structure Hom (A B : Thickening S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.instCategory
declarations.doc:
Divided power thickenings of `X` relative to `S` form the big crystalline category
`CRIS(X/S)`.
declarations.statement: instance instCategory : Category.{u} (Thickening S)
declarations.comment: the category CRIS(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.forget
declarations.doc:
The forgetful functor `CRIS(X/S) ⥤ Sch/X`, sending a divided power thickening `U ↪ T` with
its map `U ⟶ X` to the scheme `U` over `X`.
declarations.statement: def forget (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) : Thickening S ⥤ Over S.X

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.free
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07I8.** A scheme over `X`, viewed as the divided power thickening
`(U, U, ∅)` of `X` relative to `S`.  This is a one-sided inverse of the forgetful functor, and its
left adjoint.
declarations.statement: def free : Over S.X ⥤ Thickening S

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.hasNonemptyFiniteLimits_thickening
declarations.doc:
The big crystalline category `CRIS(X/S)` has all nonempty finite limits, in particular
products of pairs and fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNonemptyFiniteLimits_thickening (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    HasNonemptyFiniteLimits (Thickening S)
declarations.comment: clause (1): CRIS(X/S) has all nonempty finite limits, in particular products of pairs and fibre products

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.instHasPullbacksThickening
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07I9, part of the first assertion.** The big crystalline category
`CRIS(X/S)` has fibre products: the fibre product of the ambient divided power schemes,
[Stacks, Tag 07ME], is the ambient divided power scheme of the fibre product, and its closed
fibre is the fibre product of the thickened schemes.

This is the fibre product half of the first assertion of [Stacks, Tag 07I9], proved directly from
the envelope rather than deduced from binary products.  Clause (1) in full is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.hasNonemptyFiniteLimits_thickening` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Crystalline/BigSite/BinaryProductInstance.lean`.
declarations.statement:
instance instHasPullbacksThickening (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    HasPullbacks (Thickening S)
declarations.comment: part of clause (1): fibre products, built directly from the envelope of 07ME

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.forget_preservesLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07I9, second assertion.** The forgetful functor `CRIS(X/S) ⥤ Sch/X`
preserves every limit that exists, being a right adjoint.
declarations.statement: instance forget_preservesLimits : PreservesLimits (forget S)
declarations.comment: the functor (07I7) commutes with limits

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.isPullback_targetHom_of_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IA.** Let a fibre square of divided power thickenings of `X`
relative to `(S, I, γ)` have vertices `(U₃, T₃, δ₃) ⟶ (U₂, T₂, δ₂)` and
`(U₁, T₁, δ₁) ⟶ (U, T, δ)`.  If `T₂ ⟶ T` is flat and `U₂ = T₂ ×_T U`, then `T₃ = T₁ ×_T T₂` as
schemes, with the projections of the original square.  Divided powers extend uniquely along a
flat ring map, so the ordinary fibre product of ambient schemes already carries the divided power
thickening computing the fibre product in `CRIS(X/S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.isPullback_targetHom_of_flat
    (f : B ⟶ A) (g : C ⟶ A) (i : D ⟶ B) (j : D ⟶ C)
    (h : IsPullback i j f g)
    (hf : Flat f.targetHom.hom)
    (hB : IsPullback B.thickening.immersion f.sourceHom
      f.targetHom.hom A.thickening.immersion) :
    IsPullback i.targetHom.hom j.targetHom.hom
      f.targetHom.hom g.targetHom.hom

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.IsSyntomicCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  A syntomic covering family of divided power thickenings of
`X/S`: every `Uᵢ` is `U ×_T Tᵢ` and `{Tᵢ ⟶ T}` is a syntomic covering of schemes.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSyntomicCovering {B : Thickening S} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} B) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1), syntomic coverings

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.IsCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  A family of morphisms `{(Uᵢ, Tᵢ, δᵢ) ⟶ (U, T, δ)}` of divided
power thickenings of `X/S` is a covering for a precoverage `K` of schemes when every `Uᵢ` is
`U ×_T Tᵢ` and the family `{Tᵢ ⟶ T}` is a covering for `K`.
declarations.statement:
def IsCovering (K : Precoverage Scheme.{u}) {B : Thickening S}
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} B) : Prop

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.IsZariskiCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  A Zariski covering family of divided power thickenings of
`X/S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsZariskiCovering {B : Thickening S} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} B) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1), Zariski coverings

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.IsEtaleCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  An étale covering family of divided power thickenings of
`X/S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsEtaleCovering {B : Thickening S} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} B) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1), étale coverings

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.IsSmoothCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  A smooth covering family of divided power thickenings of
`X/S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsSmoothCovering {B : Thickening S} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} B) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1), smooth coverings

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.IsFppfCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  An fppf covering family of divided power thickenings of
`X/S`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsFppfCovering {B : Thickening S} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} B) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1), fppf coverings

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.topology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  The big crystalline site of `X` over `(S, I, γ)`: the category
`CRIS(X/S)` with the Zariski topology, the topology generated by the Zariski covering families of
divided power thickenings.
declarations.statement: abbrev topology (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) : GrothendieckTopology (Thickening S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.topos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IB.**  The crystalline topos `(X/S)_CRIS`, the sheaves of sets on the
big crystalline site.
declarations.statement: abbrev topos (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.changeBase
declarations.doc:
**Change of divided power base.**  A divided power thickening of `X` relative to `(S, I, γ)`
is one of `Y` relative to `(S', I', γ')`, with structure maps `T ⟶ S ⟶ S'` and `U ⟶ X ⟶ Y`.  The
underlying thickening and the maps between thickenings are unchanged.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def changeBase (S S' : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) (f : S.S ⟶ S'.S)
    (g : S.X ⟶ S'.X)
    (h : S.toClosedFiber ≫ DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberMap f = g ≫ S'.toClosedFiber) :
    Thickening S ⥤ Thickening S'
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.changeBase_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
Change of divided power base is cocontinuous for the big
crystalline Zariski topologies.
declarations.statement:
instance changeBase_isCocontinuous :
    (changeBase S S' f g h).IsCocontinuous (topology S) (topology S')
declarations.comment: cocontinuity

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.changeBaseMorphism
declarations.doc:
The morphism of crystalline topoi
`(X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (Y/S')_CRIS` induced by change of divided power base: its pushforward is the sheaf
pushforward along the cocontinuous functor `changeBase`, and its inverse image is the sheaf
pullback, which is left exact.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def changeBaseMorphism (S S' : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) (f : S.S ⟶ S'.S)
    (g : S.X ⟶ S'.X)
    (h : S.toClosedFiber ≫ DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberMap f = g ≫ S'.toClosedFiber) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (topos S) (topos S')
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.changeBase_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IC.**  Change of divided power base is continuous for the big
crystalline Zariski topologies.  It suffices to check the Zariski covering families; such a
family maps to the family of the same thickenings over the image of the base, which is again
Zariski covering because being Cartesian and covering the ambient scheme do not involve the
structure maps to the divided power base and to `X`.  The sheaf condition then transfers because
change of base turns compatible families into compatible families.
declarations.statement:
instance changeBase_isContinuous :
    (changeBase S S' f g h).IsContinuous (topology S) (topology S')
declarations.comment: continuity

declarations.name: Crystalline.FCrystalSituation.frobeniusChangeBase
declarations.doc:
**The Frobenius endofunctor of the big crystalline category of `X/S`.**  Change of divided
power base along `Spec(σ)` and the absolute Frobenius of `X`.
declarations.comment: the functor, for the Frobenius of a Frobenius-crystal situation

declarations.name: Crystalline.FCrystalSituation.crystallineFrobenius
declarations.doc:
**The Frobenius morphism `(F_X)_cris : (X/S)_cris ⟶ (X/S)_cris` of crystalline topoi.**  It
is the morphism of topoi induced by change of divided power base along `Spec(σ)` and the absolute
Frobenius of `X`.
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi, for the Frobenius of a Frobenius-crystal situation

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.zariskiComparisonRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The comparison with the Zariski site
`U_{X/S} : (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ Sh((Sch/X)_Zar)` as a morphism of ringed topoi -- the left vertical arrow
of the diagram of the remark.  Its structure map is the unit of the adjunction between the
inverse image and the direct image of sheaves of commutative rings, whose inverse-image form is
the identity.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zariskiComparisonRinged (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    RingedToposHom (crystallineZariskiRingedTopos S) (zariskiOverRingedTopos S.X)
declarations.comment: the comparison as a morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.forget_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ID.**  The forgetful functor `CRIS(X/S) ⥤ Sch/X` is cocontinuous for
the Zariski topologies.  A Zariski covering of the thickened scheme `U` of an object `(U, T, δ)`
is, up to refinement by its members' images, the family of opens of `T` matching the images of its
members: the immersion `U ↪ T` is a thickening, hence a homeomorphism on points, and restricting
`(U, T, δ)` to those opens of `T` is a Zariski covering family of `CRIS(X/S)` whose image under
the forgetful functor refines the given one.
declarations.statement:
instance forget_isCocontinuous (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    (forget S).IsCocontinuous (topology S) (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S.X)
declarations.comment: cocontinuity of the forgetful functor

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.zariskiComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ID.**  The comparison morphism of topoi
`U_{X/S} : (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ Sh((Sch/X)_Zar)` from the big crystalline topos of `X/S` to the big
Zariski topos of `X`, induced by the cocontinuous forgetful functor `CRIS(X/S) ⥤ Sch/X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zariskiComparison (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (topos S) (Sheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S.X) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zariskiOverStructureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The structure sheaf `𝒪` of the big Zariski site `(Sch/Z)_Zar`,** the sheaf of commutative
rings sending a scheme `T` over `Z` to `Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zariskiOverStructureSheaf (Z : Scheme.{u}) :
    Sheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over Z) CommRingCat.{u + 1}
declarations.comment: the structure sheaf of the big Zariski topoi of the diagram

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zariskiOverRingedTopos
declarations.doc:
**The big Zariski topos of a scheme as a ringed topos,** [Stacks, Tag 07IE]: the site
`(Sch/Z)_Zar` together with its structure sheaf `T ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def zariskiOverRingedTopos (Z : Scheme.{u}) : RingedTopos.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
declarations.comment: the big Zariski topoi of the diagram, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zariskiOverRingedMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The morphism of *ringed* big Zariski topoi
`Sh((Sch/X)_Zar) ⟶ Sh((Sch/Y)_Zar)` induced by a morphism of schemes `X ⟶ Y`: the underlying
morphism of topoi is `AlgebraicGeometry.zariskiOverMorphism`, and the structure map is the
adjunct of the identification of the inverse image of `T ↦ Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` with itself.  These are
the bottom and diagonal arrows `f_big` and `Sh((Sch/S₀)_Zar) ⟶ Sh((Sch/S)_Zar)` of the diagram
of the remark.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zariskiOverRingedMorphism :
    RingedToposHom (zariskiOverRingedTopos X) (zariskiOverRingedTopos Y)
declarations.comment: the big Zariski arrows of the diagram, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.crystallineZariskiRingedTopos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The big crystalline topos `(X/S)_CRIS` as a ringed topos: the
site `CRIS(X/S)` together with the inverse image `U_{X/S}⁻¹𝒪` of the structure sheaf of the big
Zariski site of `X`.  Since the inverse image of the morphism of topoi attached to a cocontinuous
functor is restriction along that functor, this structure sheaf is
`(U, T, δ) ↦ Γ(U, 𝒪_U)`, the sheaf `\underline{𝐆_a}` of [Stacks, Tag 07IN].
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev crystallineZariskiRingedTopos (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    RingedTopos.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
declarations.comment: the big crystalline topoi of the diagram, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.zariskiComparisonRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The comparison with the Zariski site
`U_{X/S} : (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ Sh((Sch/X)_Zar)` as a morphism of ringed topoi -- the left vertical arrow
of the diagram of the remark.  Its structure map is the unit of the adjunction between the
inverse image and the direct image of sheaves of commutative rings, whose inverse-image form is
the identity.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zariskiComparisonRinged (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    RingedToposHom (crystallineZariskiRingedTopos S) (zariskiOverRingedTopos S.X)
declarations.comment: the crystalline-to-Zariski comparisons of the diagram, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.structureMorphismRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The structure morphism of the big crystalline site
`(X/S)_CRIS ⟶ Sh((Sch/S)_Zar)` as a morphism of *ringed* topoi: the comparison `U_{X/S}`
followed by the big Zariski morphism along `X ⟶ S`.  This is the lower route through the diagram
of the remark, which is what defines the structure morphism whether or not `p` is locally
nilpotent on the closed fibre.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureMorphismRinged (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    RingedToposHom (crystallineZariskiRingedTopos S) (zariskiOverRingedTopos S.S.scheme)
declarations.comment: the structure morphism, as a morphism of ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberZariskiRingedTopos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The crystalline topos `(S₀/S)_CRIS` of the closed fibre as a
ringed topos: the upper right corner of the diagram of the remark, available because `p` is
locally nilpotent on `S₀`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev closedFiberZariskiRingedTopos : RingedTopos.{u, u + 1, u + 1}
declarations.comment: the crystalline topos of the closed fibre, as a ringed topos

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberZariskiComparisonRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The comparison `U_{S₀/S} : (S₀/S)_CRIS ⟶ Sh((Sch/S₀)_Zar)` as
a morphism of ringed topoi: the right vertical arrow of the diagram.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def closedFiberZariskiComparisonRinged :
    RingedToposHom (closedFiberZariskiRingedTopos S hp)
      (zariskiOverRingedTopos (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S))
declarations.comment: the right vertical arrow of the diagram, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberRingedMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The top arrow `f_CRIS : (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (S₀/S)_CRIS` of the
diagram as a morphism of ringed topoi, for `f : X ⟶ S₀` the structure morphism.  Its structure
map is invertible, being the identification of the two routes to the big Zariski topos of
`S₀`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def closedFiberRingedMorphism :
    RingedToposHom (crystallineZariskiRingedTopos S) (closedFiberZariskiRingedTopos S hp)
declarations.comment: the top arrow of the diagram, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberStructureMorphismRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The structure morphism of the big crystalline site read along
the upper route of the diagram: `f_CRIS`, then `U_{S₀/S}`, then the big Zariski morphism along
`S₀ ⟶ S`.  This is the composition the remark takes as the definition of the structure morphism
when `p` is locally nilpotent on the closed fibre.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def closedFiberStructureMorphismRinged :
    RingedToposHom (crystallineZariskiRingedTopos S) (zariskiOverRingedTopos S.S.scheme)
declarations.comment: the structure morphism through the closed fibre, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.comparisonSquareRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The square of the diagram commutes as a diagram of *ringed*
topoi: `U_{S₀/S} ∘ f_CRIS` and `f_big ∘ U_{X/S}` are 2-isomorphic as morphisms of ringed topoi,
the underlying 2-isomorphism of topoi being
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.comparisonSquare`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def comparisonSquareRinged :
    RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (RingedToposHom.comp (X := crystallineZariskiRingedTopos S)
        (Y := zariskiOverRingedTopos S.X)
        (Z := zariskiOverRingedTopos (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S))
        (zariskiOverRingedMorphism S.toClosedFiber) (zariskiComparisonRinged S))
      (RingedToposHom.comp (X := crystallineZariskiRingedTopos S)
        (Y := closedFiberZariskiRingedTopos S hp)
        (Z := zariskiOverRingedTopos (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S))
        (closedFiberZariskiComparisonRinged S hp) (closedFiberRingedMorphism S hp))
declarations.comment: the square of the diagram, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.zariskiStructureTriangleRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The lower triangle of the diagram commutes as a diagram of
*ringed* topoi: the big Zariski morphisms along `X ⟶ S₀` and `S₀ ⟶ S` compose, as morphisms of
ringed topoi, to the one along `X ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zariskiStructureTriangleRinged :
    RingedToposHom.TwoIso.{u, u + 1, u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (RingedToposHom.comp
        (X := zariskiOverRingedTopos S.X)
        (Y := zariskiOverRingedTopos (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S))
        (Z := zariskiOverRingedTopos S.S.scheme)
        (zariskiOverRingedMorphism (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberι S.S))
        (zariskiOverRingedMorphism S.toClosedFiber))
      (zariskiOverRingedMorphism (sourceToBase S))
declarations.comment: the big Zariski triangle of the diagram, as ringed topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberStructureTriangleRinged
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The diagram of *ringed* topoi commutes: the structure
morphism of the big crystalline site read along the upper route -- `f_CRIS`, then `U_{S₀/S}`,
then the big Zariski morphism along `S₀ ⟶ S` -- is 2-isomorphic, as a morphism of ringed topoi,
to the one read along the lower route, which is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.structureMorphismRinged`.  This is the assertion of the
remark, pasted out of the square and the big Zariski triangle.
declarations.comment:
the commutativity of the diagram of ringed topoi: the two routes from (X/S)_CRIS
  to the big Zariski topos of S agree

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.structureFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The functor `CRIS(X/S) ⥤ Sch/S`, `(U, T, δ)/S ↦ U/S`: forget
the ambient divided power thickening and read the resulting scheme over `X` as a scheme over
`S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureFunctor (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    Thickening S ⥤ Over S.S.scheme
declarations.comment: the functor (U, T, δ)/S ↦ U/S

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.structureFunctor_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The functor `(U, T, δ)/S ↦ U/S` is cocontinuous, being the
composite of the cocontinuous forgetful functor with `Over.map` along `X ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
instance structureFunctor_isCocontinuous (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    (structureFunctor S).IsCocontinuous (topology S)
      (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S.S.scheme)
declarations.comment: cocontinuity of (U, T, δ)/S ↦ U/S

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.structureMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The structure morphism
`(X/S)_CRIS ⟶ Sh((Sch/S)_Zar)` of the big crystalline site, the morphism of topoi attached to the
cocontinuous functor `(U, T, δ)/S ↦ U/S`.  It is defined whether or not `p` is locally nilpotent
on the closed fibre `S₀ = V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureMorphism (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (topos S)
      (Sheaf (Scheme.zariskiTopology.over S.S.scheme) (Type (u + 1)))
declarations.comment: the structure morphism

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.changeBaseZariskiSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  Change of divided power base and the crystalline-to-Zariski
comparisons form a commutative square: the composite
`(X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (Y/S')_CRIS ⟶ Sh((Sch/Y)_Zar)` is isomorphic to
`(X/S)_CRIS ⟶ Sh((Sch/X)_Zar) ⟶ Sh((Sch/Y)_Zar)`, both being the morphism of topoi attached to
the cocontinuous functor `(U, T, δ) ↦ U/Y`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def changeBaseZariskiSquare (S S' : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
    (f : S.S ⟶ S'.S) (g : S.X ⟶ S'.X)
    (h : S.toClosedFiber ≫ DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberMap f = g ≫ S'.toClosedFiber) :
    ((zariskiOverMorphism g).comp (zariskiComparison S)).pushforward ≅
      ((zariskiComparison S').comp (changeBaseMorphism S S' f g h)).pushforward
declarations.comment: the crystalline-Zariski square, as topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The closed fibre `S₀ = V(I)` of a divided power scheme on which
`p` is locally nilpotent is itself a global crystalline situation over `(S, I, γ)`, with the
identity as its structure morphism to the closed fibre.  In particular the big crystalline site
`CRIS(S₀/S)` is available.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev closedFiberSituation (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
    (hp : ∀ x : DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S,
      IsNilpotent (S.p : (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}
declarations.comment: the crystalline situation on the closed fibre

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The morphism of crystalline topoi
`f_CRIS : (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (S₀/S)_CRIS` attached to the structure morphism `f : X ⟶ S₀`, obtained from
change of divided power base along the identity of `(S, I, γ)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def closedFiberMorphism (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
    (hp : ∀ x : DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S,
      IsNilpotent (S.p : (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (topos S) (topos (closedFiberSituation S hp))
declarations.comment: the crystalline arrow of the diagram

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.comparisonSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The square of the diagram: `U_{S₀/S} ∘ f_CRIS` is isomorphic to
`f_big ∘ U_{X/S}`, for `f : X ⟶ S₀` the structure morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def comparisonSquare (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
    (hp : ∀ x : DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S,
      IsNilpotent (S.p : (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ((zariskiOverMorphism S.toClosedFiber).comp (zariskiComparison S)).pushforward ≅
      ((zariskiComparison (closedFiberSituation S hp)).comp
        (closedFiberMorphism S hp)).pushforward
declarations.comment: the square of the diagram, as topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.zariskiStructureTriangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The lower triangle of the diagram: the big Zariski morphisms
along `X ⟶ S₀` and `S₀ ⟶ S` compose to the one along `X ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def zariskiStructureTriangle (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    ((zariskiOverMorphism (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberι S.S)).comp
        (zariskiOverMorphism S.toClosedFiber)).pushforward ≅
      (zariskiOverMorphism (sourceToBase S)).pushforward
declarations.comment: the big Zariski triangle of the diagram, as topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.structureTriangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The structure morphism is the composite of the
crystalline-to-Zariski comparison `U_{X/S}` with the big Zariski morphism along `X ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def structureTriangle (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    ((zariskiOverMorphism (sourceToBase S)).comp (zariskiComparison S)).pushforward ≅
      (structureMorphism S).pushforward
declarations.comment: the structure morphism through the big Zariski topos of X, as topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberStructureTriangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IE.**  The structure morphism of the big crystalline site is the route
through `(S₀/S)_CRIS` and the big Zariski topos of `S₀`, which is the composition the remark takes
as the definition of the structure morphism when `p` is locally nilpotent on `S₀`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def closedFiberStructureTriangle (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
    (hp : ∀ x : DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S,
      IsNilpotent (S.p : (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ((zariskiOverMorphism (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberι S.S)).comp
        ((zariskiComparison (closedFiberSituation S hp)).comp
          (closedFiberMorphism S hp))).pushforward ≅
      (structureMorphism S).pushforward
declarations.comment: the structure morphism through the crystalline topos of the closed fibre, as topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.IsCrystalline
declarations.doc:
The property that cuts out the small crystalline category: the structure map `U ⟶ X` of a
divided power thickening `(U, T, δ)` of `X` relative to `(S, I, γ)` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCrystalline : ObjectProperty (Thickening S)
declarations.comment: (1), the condition on the objects

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening
declarations.doc:
The small crystalline category `Cris(X/S, I, γ)`, abbreviated `Cris(X/S)`: the full
subcategory of the big crystalline category `CRIS(X/S)` on the divided power thickenings
`(U, T, δ)` for which `U ⟶ X` is an open immersion.
declarations.statement: abbrev CrystallineThickening (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
declarations.comment: (1), the full subcategory Cris(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.IsZariskiCovering
declarations.doc:
A Zariski covering family of the small crystalline category: a family of morphisms of
`Cris(X/S)` which is a Zariski covering family of the big crystalline category `CRIS(X/S)`, that
is, whose squares are Cartesian and whose ambient divided power schemes form a Zariski covering.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsZariskiCovering {B : CrystallineThickening S} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} B) : Prop
declarations.comment: (1), the Zariski coverings

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallTopology
declarations.doc:
The small crystalline site of `X` over `(S, I, γ)`: the full subcategory `Cris(X/S)` of
`CRIS(X/S)` on the thickenings `(U, T, δ)` with `U ⟶ X` an open immersion, endowed with the
Zariski topology, the topology generated by the Zariski covering families.
declarations.statement:
abbrev smallTopology (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    GrothendieckTopology (CrystallineThickening S)
declarations.comment: (1), the small crystalline site

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallTopos
declarations.doc:
The crystalline topos `(X/S)_cris`, the topos of sheaves of sets on the small crystalline
site.
declarations.statement: abbrev smallTopos (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
declarations.comment: (2), the crystalline topos

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallForget
declarations.doc:
The forgetful functor `Cris(X/S) ⥤ X_Zar`, `(U, T, δ) ↦ U`, from the small crystalline site
to the small Zariski site: it keeps the scheme `U` with its open immersion into `X`.
declarations.statement:
def smallForget (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    CrystallineThickening S ⥤ ZariskiOpen S

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallFree
declarations.doc:
The functor `X_Zar ⥤ Cris(X/S)` sending an open `U ⟶ X` to the object `(U, U, ∅)` of the
small crystalline site: the scheme `U` thickened by itself, the ambient scheme carrying the zero
divided power ideal.
declarations.statement:
def smallFree (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    ZariskiOpen S ⥤ CrystallineThickening S
declarations.comment: the functor

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallFreeForgetAdjunction
declarations.doc:
The functor `smallFree`, `U ↦ (U, U, ∅)`, is left adjoint to the forgetful functor
`smallForget`: a morphism `(U, U, ∅) ⟶ (V, T, δ)` of the small crystalline site is exactly a
morphism `U ⟶ V` of the small Zariski site.
declarations.statement:
def smallFreeForgetAdjunction (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    smallFree S ⊣ smallForget S
declarations.comment: left adjoint

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.ι_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ.**  The inclusion `Cris(X/S) ⥤ CRIS(X/S)` is cocontinuous for the
Zariski topologies of the two crystalline sites.
declarations.statement:
instance ι_isCocontinuous :
    (ι S).IsCocontinuous (smallTopology S) (topology S)
declarations.comment: the inclusion is cocontinuous

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.ι_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ.**  The inclusion `Cris(X/S) ⥤ CRIS(X/S)` is continuous for the
Zariski topologies of the two crystalline sites: the restriction of a sheaf on the big crystalline
site is a sheaf on the small one.  It suffices to check the Zariski covering families of the small
site; such a family is one of the big site, and the sheaf condition transfers because a family of
sections compatible over the vertices lying in `Cris(X/S)` is compatible over all vertices.
declarations.statement:
instance ι_isContinuous :
    (ι S).IsContinuous (smallTopology S) (topology S)
declarations.comment: the inclusion is continuous

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.smallToBigMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ.**  The morphism of topoi
`i : (X/S)_cris ⟶ (X/S)_CRIS` induced by the inclusion `Cris(X/S) ⥤ CRIS(X/S)`: its direct
image `i_*` is the sheaf pushforward along the cocontinuous inclusion and its inverse image
`i^{-1}` is the sheaf pullback `𝒢 ↦ (ι^p 𝒢)^#`, which is left exact.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToBigMorphism (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (smallTopos S) (topos S)
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi i induced by the inclusion

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.inverseImageIsoRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ.**  The inverse image `i^{-1}` of the inclusion morphism of topoi
is plain restriction of a sheaf on the big crystalline site to the small one: the sheafification
in `i^{-1} = (ι^p\ )^#` is unnecessary because the inclusion is both continuous and cocontinuous.
Restriction is the direct image `π_*` of the retraction, so this is the formula
`π_* = i^{-1}` of the tag.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def inverseImageIsoRestriction
    (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    (smallToBigMorphism S).inverseImage ≅
      (ι S).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1)) (smallTopology S) (topology S)
declarations.comment: π_* = i^{-1}: the inverse image of i is restriction

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.lowerShriekRestrictionIsoId
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ.**  The composite `π ∘ i` is the identity, on inverse images: the
unit `𝟭 ⟶ i_! ⋙ i^{-1}` of the lower shriek adjunction is an isomorphism, the inclusion being
continuous, cocontinuous and fully faithful.  Since `π^{-1} = i_!` and `π_* = i^{-1}`, this is the
inverse image of the composite `(X/S)_cris ⟶ (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (X/S)_cris`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lowerShriekRestrictionIsoId (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    𝟭 (smallTopos S) ≅
      Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (ι S) (Type (u + 1))
          (smallTopology S) (topology S) ⋙
        (ι S).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1)) (smallTopology S) (topology S)
declarations.comment: the composite π ∘ i is the identity, on inverse images

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.preservesFiniteLimits_lowerShriekAb
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ, clause (6), at abelian coefficients: the lower shriek `i_!` along
the inclusion `Cris(X/S) ⥤ CRIS(X/S)` is exact on sheaves of abelian groups.**

Unlike the set-valued statement `preservesFiniteLimits_lowerShriek`, this needs no covering
argument: the final object of a category of abelian sheaves is the zero object and `i_!`, being a
left adjoint between additive categories, preserves it.  What remains is
[Stacks, Tag 00X4] for the shapes of [Stacks, Tag 00X6], namely
`Stacks.Sites.LowerShriek.gShriek_preservesFiniteLimits`, whose hypotheses are that `Cris(X/S)`
have fibre products and equalizers which the inclusion preserves — the four theorems above, all
instances of [Stacks, Tag 07I9].
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_lowerShriekAb :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (ι S)
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (smallTopology S) (topology S))
declarations.comment: clause (6) at abelian coefficients: i_! is exact on sheaves of abelian groups, with no covering argument needed

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.coversTop_ι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ, clause (6), the covering step.**  The representable sheaves of the
objects of `Cris(X/S)` cover the final sheaf of `(X/S)_CRIS`: every object of `CRIS(X/S)` has a
Zariski covering each member of which admits a morphism to an object of `Cris(X/S)`.

This is the step the source omits in general.  Cover the thickened scheme of `A` by the affine
opens `W` supplied by `exists_affine_neighbourhood_toX`; the restriction of `A` to `W` has
thickened scheme `W` and its part of `U` maps into an affine open `V` of `X`, hence affinely,
so `exists_crystalline_hom_of_affine` applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem coversTop_ι (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    (topology S).CoversTop (ι S).obj
declarations.comment: clause (6), the covering step: the representables of Cris(X/S) cover the final sheaf of (X/S)_CRIS, which the source omits in general

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.preservesFiniteLimits_lowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ, clause (6): the lower shriek `i_!` along the inclusion
`Cris(X/S) ⥤ CRIS(X/S)` is exact.**

Lower shriek is right exact, being a left adjoint, and preserves fibre products because the index
category of the pointwise left Kan extension along `i` is filtered.  What remains is the final
sheaf, and that is `coversTop_ι`: the representables of `Cris(X/S)` cover it.  Both halves are
`Stacks.Sites.LowerShriek.sheafPullback_preservesFiniteLimits_of_coversTop`.

What makes that index category filtered is products of pairs in `CRIS(X/S)`, the first half of
[Stacks, Tag 07I9], which [Stacks, Tag 07IJ] cites; it is the global instance
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.instHasBinaryProductsThickening`, and the Stacks proof of
this clause invokes products of `Cris(X/S)` for the same reason.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_lowerShriek (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (ι S)
      (Type (u + 1)) (smallTopology S) (topology S))
declarations.comment: clause (6): i_! is exact, whose covering step -- the part the source omits in general -- is coversTop_ι

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.moduleLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ, at module coefficients: the lower shriek
`i_! : Mod(𝒪_{X/S} on Cris(X/S)) ⥤ Mod(𝒪_{X/S} on CRIS(X/S))`** along the inclusion of the small
crystalline site into the big one.

It is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.lowerShriek` ([Stacks, Tag 0797]) for the inclusion: a sheaf of
modules on `Cris(X/S)` is pushed forward as a presheaf of modules along `i.op` and the result is
sheafified for the big crystalline topology.  The inclusion is continuous and cocontinuous by
`...SmallSite.instIsContinuousι` and `...SmallSite.instIsCocontinuousι` of
`SmallSite/BigComparison.lean`, both unconditional, and the sheafification the construction needs
is of `AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}`-valued presheaves on the big site, which is
`...SmallSite.instHasSheafifyBigAddCommGrpCat`; see the module docstring, which corrects the
record that this was unavailable.
declarations.statement: def moduleLowerShriek : ModuleSheaf S ⥤ BigModuleSheaf S
declarations.comment: the lower shriek i_! at module coefficients

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.moduleLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ, at module coefficients: `i_! ⊣ i^{-1}`.**  The module-level lower
shriek is left adjoint to the restriction `...SmallSite.crisRestrictModules` of modules from
`CRIS(X/S)` to `Cris(X/S)`.
declarations.statement: def moduleLowerShriekAdjunction : moduleLowerShriek S ⊣ crisRestrictModules.{u + 1} S
declarations.comment: i_! is left adjoint to i^{-1} on sheaves of modules

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isIso_moduleLowerShriekAdjunction_unit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ: the formula `i^{-1}i_! = id`, at module coefficients.**  The unit
of `i_! ⊣ i^{-1}` on sheaves of modules is an isomorphism.

The inclusion `...CrystallineThickening.ι` is fully faithful, continuous and cocontinuous, and
the comparison of structure sheaves is the identity, so this is
`SheafOfModules.isIso_unit_of_isIso_coefficient`: in the adjoint triple `i_! ⊣ i^{-1} ⊣ i_*` the
unit of the left-hand adjunction is invertible exactly when the counit of the right-hand one is,
and the latter is full faithfulness of the direct image of modules along a fully faithful functor
of sites.  No model of `i_!` enters that argument, so this holds of the one built above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_moduleLowerShriekAdjunction_unit :
    IsIso (moduleLowerShriekAdjunction S).unit
declarations.comment: i^{-1} i_! = id on sheaves of modules

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.ιCreatesLimitOfNonempty
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ, first assertion.**  The inclusion `Cris(X/S) ⥤ CRIS(X/S)` creates
the limit of every nonempty finite diagram of divided power thickenings of `X` whose maps to `X`
are open immersions: the limit of the diagram in `CRIS(X/S)` exists by clause (1) of
[Stacks, Tag 07I9] and its vertex again has open immersion to `X`, the forgetful functor to
`Sch/X` commuting with limits and a finite nonempty limit of opens of `X` being an open of `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ιCreatesLimitOfNonempty (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
    (J : Type) [SmallCategory J] [FinCategory J] [Nonempty J]
    (F : J ⥤ CrystallineThickening S) :
    CreatesLimit F (ι S)
declarations.comment: the inclusion commutes with finite nonempty limits

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.hasNonemptyFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ, first assertion.**  The small crystalline category `Cris(X/S)` has
all finite nonempty limits.  They are created by the inclusion from the finite nonempty limits of
`CRIS(X/S)`, which exist by clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 07I9].
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNonemptyFiniteLimits (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    _root_.HasNonemptyFiniteLimits (CrystallineThickening S)
declarations.comment: nonempty finite limits in Cris(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.ι_preservesNonemptyFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IJ, first assertion.**  The inclusion `Cris(X/S) ⥤ CRIS(X/S)` commutes
with finite nonempty limits.  Every nonempty finite shape is one of which `CRIS(X/S)` has limits,
by clause (1) of [Stacks, Tag 07I9], and the inclusion creates those.
declarations.statement:
theorem ι_preservesNonemptyFiniteLimits (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u})
    (J : Type) [SmallCategory J] [FinCategory J] [Nonempty J] :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape J (ι S)
declarations.comment: the inclusion commutes with finite nonempty limits

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.retractionMorphism
declarations.doc:
The retraction `π : (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (X/S)_cris` as a morphism of topoi: its direct image is
`i^{-1}`, restriction of a sheaf on the big crystalline site to the small one, and its inverse
image is the lower shriek `i_!`, the two being adjoint.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def retractionMorphism (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (topos S) (smallTopos S)
declarations.comment: the retraction π as a morphism of topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.retractionPushforwardIsoInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**`π_* = i^{-1}`**: the direct image of the retraction `π : (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (X/S)_cris` is
isomorphic to the inverse image of the inclusion morphism of topoi
`i : (X/S)_cris ⟶ (X/S)_CRIS`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def retractionPushforwardIsoInverseImage (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    (retractionMorphism S).pushforward ≅ (smallToBigMorphism S).inverseImage
declarations.comment: π_* = i^{-1}, relating the direct image of π to the inverse image of i

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.retractionMorphism_comp_smallToBigMorphism_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**The composite `π ∘ i` is the identity, on inverse images**: the inverse image of the
composite `(X/S)_cris ⟶ (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (X/S)_cris` is isomorphic to the identity functor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def retractionMorphism_comp_smallToBigMorphism_inverseImage
    (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) : 𝟭 (smallTopos S) ≅
      ((retractionMorphism S).comp (smallToBigMorphism S)).inverseImage
declarations.comment: the composite π ∘ i is the identity: its inverse image is the identity functor

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.CrystallineThickening.retractionMorphism_comp_smallToBigMorphism_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**The composite `π ∘ i` is the identity, on direct images**: the direct image of the
composite `(X/S)_cris ⟶ (X/S)_CRIS ⟶ (X/S)_cris` is isomorphic to the identity functor, by the
counit of `i^{-1} ⊣ i_*`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def retractionMorphism_comp_smallToBigMorphism_pushforward
    (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    ((retractionMorphism S).comp (smallToBigMorphism S)).pushforward ≅ 𝟭 (smallTopos S)
declarations.comment: the composite π ∘ i is the identity: its direct image is the identity functor

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.crisMorphism
declarations.doc:
The morphism of small crystalline topoi `f_cris : (X/S)_cris ⟶ (Y/S')_cris` attached to a
morphism of divided power bases `S ⟶ S'` and a compatible morphism `X ⟶ Y` of schemes over their
closed fibres: the composite `π_Y ∘ f_CRIS ∘ i_X` of the inclusion morphism of topoi for `X/S`,
change of divided power base on the big crystalline topoi, and the retraction for `Y/S'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def crisMorphism (S S' : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) (f : S.S ⟶ S'.S)
    (g : S.X ⟶ S'.X)
    (h : S.toClosedFiber ≫ DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberMap f = g ≫ S'.toClosedFiber) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (smallTopos S) (smallTopos S')
declarations.comment: f_cris = π_Y ∘ f_CRIS ∘ i_X

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.forgetToOpens_preservesBinaryProducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IL.**  The forgetful functor `Cris(X/S) ⥤ X_Zar` of
[Stacks, Tag 07IH] commutes with products.
declarations.statement:
instance forgetToOpens_preservesBinaryProducts (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) (forgetToOpens S)
declarations.comment: the functor (07IH) commutes with products

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.forgetToOpens_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IL.**  The forgetful functor `Cris(X/S) ⥤ X_Zar` of
[Stacks, Tag 07IH] commutes with fibred products.
declarations.statement:
instance forgetToOpens_preservesPullbacks (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan (forgetToOpens S)
declarations.comment: the functor (07IH) commutes with fibred products

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.forgetToOpens_zariskiCovering_functorPushforward_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IL.**  The forgetful functor `Cris(X/S) ⥤ X_Zar` of
[Stacks, Tag 07IH] is continuous: the image of a Zariski covering family of the small crystalline
site is a covering of the small Zariski site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem forgetToOpens_zariskiCovering_functorPushforward_mem
    (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) {A : CrystallineThickening S}
    (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} A) (hE : CrystallineThickening.IsZariskiCovering E) :
    E.sieve₀.functorPushforward (forgetToOpens S) ∈
      Opens.grothendieckTopology S.X.carrier ((forgetToOpens S).obj A)
declarations.comment: the functor (07IH) is continuous: it carries covering families to coverings

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.forgetToOpens_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IL.**  The forgetful functor `Cris(X/S) ⥤ X_Zar` of
[Stacks, Tag 07IH] is cocontinuous.  A covering sieve of the open `U` of `X` underlying an object
`(U, T, δ)` of `Cris(X/S)` gives, for every point of `T`, an open of `X` in the sieve containing
the image of that point; the preimages in `U` of those opens match opens of `T`, because the
immersion `U ↪ T` is a thickening and therefore a homeomorphism on points, and the restrictions of
`(U, T, δ)` to them form a Zariski covering family of `Cris(X/S)` each of whose members lands in
the sieve.
declarations.statement:
instance forgetToOpens_isCocontinuous (S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}) :
    (forgetToOpens S).IsCocontinuous (smallTopology S)
      (Opens.grothendieckTopology S.X.carrier)
declarations.comment: the functor (07IH) is cocontinuous

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.zariskiToposMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IL.**  The morphism of topoi
`u_{X/S} : (X/S)_cris ⟶ Sh(X_Zar)` relating the small crystalline topos of `X/S` with the small
Zariski topos of `X`, induced by the cocontinuous forgetful functor `Cris(X/S) ⥤ X_Zar` of
[Stacks, Tag 07IH].  Its pushforward is the sheaf pushforward along that functor and its inverse
image the sheaf pullback, which is left exact.
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi u_{X/S} : (X/S)_cris ⟶ Sh(X_Zar)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.structureToposMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IM.**  The structure morphism
`τ_{X/S} : (X/S)_cris ⟶ Sh(S_Zar)`: the comparison `u_{X/S}` of [Stacks, Tag 07IL] followed by the
small Zariski morphism along the structure morphism `X ⟶ S`.  This is the lower route of the
remark's diagram, so it is defined whether or not `p` is locally nilpotent on the closed fibre
`S₀ = V(I)`.
declarations.comment:
the structure morphism τ_{X/S} : (X/S)_cris ⟶ Sh(S_Zar), taken along the lower
  route of the diagram, so defined whether or not p is locally nilpotent on S₀

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberCrisMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IM.**  The top arrow
`f_cris : (X/S)_cris ⟶ (S₀/S)_cris` of the diagram, for `f : X ⟶ S₀` the structure morphism of `X`
over `S`.  Local nilpotence of `p` on the closed fibre `S₀ = V(I)` is the standing assumption the
remark makes before it draws the diagram, and it is what makes `S₀` a global crystalline situation
over `(S, I, γ)`, [Stacks, Tag 07IE], hence what the small crystalline site `Cris(S₀/S)` and its
topos are built from; the arrow is then the one of [Stacks, Tag 07IK] for change of divided power
base along the identity of `(S, I, γ)`, whose left exactness of `i_!` for `S₀/S` makes the
retraction `π_{S₀}` of [Stacks, Tag 07IJ] a morphism of topoi.
declarations.statement:
def closedFiberCrisMorphism
    (hlocnil : ∀ x : DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S,
      IsNilpotent (S.p : (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiber S.S).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    MorphismOfTopoi (smallTopos S) (smallTopos (closedFiberSituation S hlocnil))
declarations.comment:
the top arrow f_cris : (X/S)_cris ⟶ (S₀/S)_cris of the diagram, together with the
  site Cris(S₀/S) it lands in, for p locally nilpotent on S₀ = V(I), which is the remark's own
  standing condition on this arrow

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallZariskiStructureTriangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IM.**  The trailing arrow of the diagram: the small Zariski morphism
`f_small : Sh(X_Zar) ⟶ Sh(S₀, Zar)` along the structure morphism `f : X ⟶ S₀`, followed by the
small Zariski morphism `Sh(S₀, Zar) ⟶ Sh(S_Zar)` along the closed immersion `S₀ ⟶ S`, is the small
Zariski morphism along `X ⟶ S`.
declarations.statement:
def smallZariskiStructureTriangle :
    ((opensMapMorphismOfTopoi (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberι S.S).base).comp
