        (opensMapMorphismOfTopoi S.toClosedFiber.base)).pushforward ≅
      (opensMapMorphismOfTopoi (sourceToBase S).base).pushforward
declarations.comment:
the trailing arrow of the diagram: the small Zariski morphisms along X ⟶ S₀ and
  S₀ ⟶ S compose to the one along X ⟶ S, as an invertible 2-morphism of topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.structureToposMorphism_isoLowerRoute
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IM.**  The structure morphism
`τ_{X/S} : (X/S)_cris ⟶ Sh(S_Zar)` is the lower route of the diagram: the comparison `u_{X/S}` of
[Stacks, Tag 07IL], then the small Zariski morphism along `X ⟶ S₀`, then the small Zariski
morphism along `S₀ ⟶ S`.  This is the route the remark takes as the definition of `τ_{X/S}`, and
it does not assume `p` locally nilpotent on `S₀`.
declarations.statement:
def structureToposMorphism_isoLowerRoute :
    ((opensMapMorphismOfTopoi (DividedPowerScheme.closedFiberι S.S).base).comp
        ((opensMapMorphismOfTopoi S.toClosedFiber.base).comp
          (zariskiToposMorphism S))).pushforward ≅
      (structureToposMorphism S).pushforward
declarations.comment:
the structure morphism τ_{X/S} is the lower route of the diagram, u_{X/S} followed
  by f_small and then by the trailing arrow, as an invertible 2-morphism of topoi,
  with no hypothesis on p.  The diagram's upper square u_{S₀/S} ∘ f_cris ≅ f_small ∘ u_{X/S} is a separate
  clause of the remark and is registered separately, on
  Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberCrisUpperSquare of SmallSite/UpperSquare.lean

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.closedFiberCrisUpperSquare
declarations.doc:
**The upper square of the diagram of [Stacks, Tag 07IM].**  For `f : X ⟶ S₀` the structure
morphism of `X` over `S`, the direct image of `u_{S₀/S} ∘ f_cris` is isomorphic to that of
`f_small ∘ u_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
def closedFiberCrisUpperSquare :
    ((zariskiToposMorphism (closedFiberSituation S hlocnil)).comp
        (closedFiberCrisMorphism S hlocnil)).pushforward ≅
      ((opensMapMorphismOfTopoi S.toClosedFiber.base).comp
        (zariskiToposMorphism S)).pushforward
declarations.comment: the upper square of the diagram: u_{S₀/S} ∘ f_cris is isomorphic to f_small ∘ u_{X/S}, for f : X ⟶ S₀ the structure morphism

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.restrictionFMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IP.**  The `f`-map from the restriction of a presheaf to the ambient
scheme of the target of a morphism `f` of `CRIS(X/S)` to its restriction to the ambient scheme of
the source: over an open `W` of the target it is the presheaf applied to the restriction of `f`
over `W`.
declarations.statement:
def restrictionFMap {A B : Thickening S} (g : A ⟶ B) :
    restriction F B ⟶ g.targetHom.hom.base _* restriction F A
declarations.comment: the f-map assembled from the restriction mappings

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.comparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IP.**  The comparison morphism `c_f : f⁻¹F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` of a morphism
`f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` of `CRIS(X/S)`, obtained from the `f`-map `F_{T'} ⟶ f_* F_T` by the
adjunction between inverse and direct image.
declarations.statement:
def comparison [HasColimits 𝒜] {A B : Thickening S} (g : A ⟶ B) :
    (TopCat.Presheaf.pullback 𝒜 g.targetHom.hom.base).obj (restriction F B) ⟶ restriction F A
declarations.comment: the comparison map on the big crystalline site, for presheaves

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.isIso_comparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison morphism of an open immersion of `CRIS(X/S)` is an isomorphism.**  For a
Cartesian morphism `f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` which is an open immersion on ambient schemes,
the restriction `F_T` is the restriction of `F_{T'}` to the open `T` of `T'`, so the comparison
morphism `c_f : f⁻¹F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_comparison [HasColimits 𝒜] {A B : Thickening S} (g : A ⟶ B)
    [IsOpenImmersion g.targetHom.hom] (hg : IsCartesian g) : IsIso (comparison F g)
declarations.comment: the comparison map is an isomorphism for an open immersion

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.CohomologyRestriction.restrictionFMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IP.**  The `f`-map from the restriction of a presheaf on `Cris(X/S)` to
the ambient scheme of the target of a morphism `f` of `Cris(X/S)` to its restriction to the ambient
scheme of the source: over an open `W` of the target it is the presheaf applied to the restriction
of `f` over `W`.
declarations.statement:
def restrictionFMap {A B : CrystallineThickening S} (g : A ⟶ B) :
    restriction F B ⟶ g.hom.targetHom.hom.base _* restriction F A
declarations.comment: the f-map on the small crystalline site, for presheaves

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.moduleComparisonSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IQ.**  The comparison map `c_f : f^* F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` of a morphism
`f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` of `CRIS(X/S)` and a sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules `F`, a map of
sheaves of `𝒪_T`-modules obtained from the `f`-map `F_{T'} ⟶ f_* F_T` by the adjunction between
pullback and pushforward of *sheaves* of modules.  The pullback is the sheafification of the
pullback of presheaves of modules, so this map is in general not the comparison map
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.moduleComparison` of the underlying presheaves
of modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def moduleComparisonSheaf (g : A ⟶ B) :
    (SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (ringRestrictionSheafFMap g)).obj
        (moduleRestrictionSheaf M B) ⟶ moduleRestrictionSheaf M A
declarations.comment: the comparison map for modules on the big crystalline site, for sheaves

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.isIso_moduleComparisonSheaf_of_isCartesian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IQ.**  The comparison map of sheaves of modules of a Cartesian open
immersion of `CRIS(X/S)` is an isomorphism: the restriction `F_T` is then the restriction of
`F_{T'}` to the open `T` of `T'` already at the level of presheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_moduleComparisonSheaf_of_isCartesian (g : A ⟶ B)
    [IsOpenImmersion g.targetHom.hom] (hg : IsCartesian g) :
    IsIso (moduleComparisonSheaf M g)
declarations.comment: the comparison map for sheaves of modules is an isomorphism for an open immersion

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.moduleComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IQ.**  The comparison morphism `c_f : f^* M_{T'} ⟶ M_T` of a morphism
`f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` of `CRIS(X/S)` and a presheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules `M`, a map of
`𝒪_T`-modules obtained from the `f`-map `M_{T'} ⟶ f_* M_T` by the adjunction between pullback and
pushforward of presheaves of modules along the `f`-map of the structure sheaf.
declarations.comment: the comparison map for modules on the big crystalline site, for presheaves

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.isIso_moduleComparison
declarations.doc:
**The comparison morphism of an open immersion of `CRIS(X/S)` for presheaves of modules is an
isomorphism.**  For a Cartesian morphism `f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` which is an open immersion
on ambient schemes, the restriction `M_T` is the restriction of `M_{T'}` to the open `T` of `T'`,
so the comparison morphism `c_f : f^* M_{T'} ⟶ M_T` is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_moduleComparison (M : PresheafOfModules.{u} (crisRing S)) (g : A ⟶ B)
    [IsOpenImmersion g.targetHom.hom] (hg : IsCartesian g) : IsIso (moduleComparison M g)
declarations.comment: the comparison map for modules is an isomorphism for an open immersion

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.CohomologyRestriction.moduleComparisonSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IQ.**  The comparison map `c_f : f^* F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` of a morphism
`f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` of `Cris(X/S)` and a sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules `F` on
`Cris(X/S)`, a map of sheaves of `𝒪_T`-modules obtained from the `f`-map `F_{T'} ⟶ f_* F_T` by the
adjunction between pullback and pushforward of *sheaves* of modules.  The pullback is the
sheafification of the pullback of presheaves of modules, so this map is in general not the
comparison map
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.CohomologyRestriction.moduleComparison` of the
underlying presheaves of modules.
declarations.comment: the comparison map for modules on the small crystalline site, for sheaves

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.IsLocallyQuasiCoherent
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the big crystalline site is *locally quasi-coherent* when
for every object `(U, T, δ)` the restriction `F_T` is a quasi-coherent `𝒪_T`-module.
declarations.statement: def IsLocallyQuasiCoherent (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf S)) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1): locally quasi-coherent, on the big site CRIS(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.IsLocallyQuasiCoherent
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the small crystalline site is *locally quasi-coherent* when
for every object `(U, T, δ)` of `Cris(X/S)` the restriction `F_T` is a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_T`-module. The restriction is the pushforward of `F` along the restrictions of the object to
the opens of its ambient scheme, lifted to `Cris(X/S)`; it is a module over the restriction of the
structure sheaf of the big crystalline site to the ambient scheme of the underlying object.
declarations.statement: def IsLocallyQuasiCoherent (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (1): locally quasi-coherent, on the small site Cris(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.IsSheafCrystal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IS.**  A sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the big crystalline site is a
*crystal in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules* when for every morphism `f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` of the site
the comparison map `c_f : f^* F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` of *sheaves* of `𝒪_T`-modules is an isomorphism.

This is the sheaf-level reading of the condition, the pullback being the pullback of sheaves of
modules, that is, the sheafification of the pullback of presheaves of modules.  It is the reading
the source intends and it is weaker than the presheaf-level condition
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.IsCrystal`; see the correction described in the module
documentation.
declarations.statement:
def IsSheafCrystal {S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}}
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf S)) : Prop
declarations.comment:
part (3): crystal in modules on the big site CRIS(X/S), with the comparison maps
  of sheaves of modules

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.IsSheafCrystal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IS, part (3) for `𝒞 = Cris(X/S)`.**  A sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on
the small crystalline site is a *crystal in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules* when for every morphism
`f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` of `Cris(X/S)` the comparison map `c_f : f^* F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` of
*sheaves* of `𝒪_T`-modules is an isomorphism.

This is the sheaf-level reading of the condition, the pullback being the pullback of sheaves of
modules, that is, the sheafification of the pullback of presheaves of modules.  It is the reading
the source intends and it is weaker than the condition read with the comparison maps of presheaves
of modules.  The same clause for the big crystalline site is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.IsSheafCrystal`.
declarations.statement:
def IsSheafCrystal {S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}}
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (3): crystal in modules on the small site Cris(X/S), with the comparison maps of sheaves

registrations.name: SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
registrations.comment: part (2): quasi-coherent, on either crystalline site

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isSheafCrystal_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IT, the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(b): a quasi-coherent sheaf of
`𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the big crystalline site is a crystal in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules.**

For a morphism `f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` the comparison map `c_f : f^* F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` of
sheaves of `𝒪_T`-modules is an isomorphism.  This is the source's argument, with its opening
reduction "it suffices to prove (a) and (b) Zariski locally" carried out: quasi-coherence gives,
around every point of `T'`, an open `V` on whose restriction `(U' ∩ V, V, δ'|_V)` the module has a
global presentation, the restrictions of `f` over those opens cover `T`, and over each of them the
source's computation applies on the localised site `CRIS(X/S)/(U' ∩ V, V, δ'|_V)`, by
`Thickening.isIso_moduleComparisonSheaf_of_hasGlobalPresentation_target`.
The comparison maps of the structure morphisms of the two restrictions are isomorphisms, those
morphisms being Cartesian open immersions, so the `f`-map cocycle
(`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.Thickening.fmapComp_comp`) transfers bijectivity of the
`f`-map composition to the direct images from the members of the cover, and invertibility of
`c_f` follows because it is Zariski-local on `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafCrystal_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf S)) (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsSheafCrystal M
declarations.comment:
the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(b) on the big site CRIS(X/S): a quasi-coherent sheaf of
  𝒪_{X/S}-modules is a crystal in 𝒪_{X/S}-modules, the crystal condition being read with the
  comparison maps of sheaves of modules.  The same implication on the small site Cris(X/S), and
  the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(a) on each of the two sites, carry this tag separately.  The converse
  (2) ⇒ (1) is a separate statement

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isLocallyQuasiCoherent_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IT, the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(a): a quasi-coherent sheaf of
`𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the big crystalline site is locally quasi-coherent.**

Quasi-coherence gives, around every point of the ambient scheme `T` of every object `(U, T, δ)`,
an open `V` on whose restriction `(U ∩ V, V, δ|_V)` the module has a global presentation
(`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.exists_hasGlobalPresentation_restrictOpen`, which is
cocontinuity of the restriction functor).  Intersecting `V` with a given open `W` of `T` makes
those opens into an open cover of `W`, and each presentation restricts to one of `F_T` on the
Zariski site localised at `V ⊓ W` by
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.hasGlobalPresentation_moduleRestrictionSheaf_over`; that
is quasi-coherence of `F_T` over `W`.

This is one of the two halves of the implication (1) ⇒ (2) of the tag, on this site; the other
half, that a quasi-coherent module is a crystal, is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isSheafCrystal_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Crystalline.CrystalsModules.QuasicoherentCrystal`.  The same
implication for `𝒞 = Cris(X/S)`, the other site the tag is stated for, is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isLocallyQuasiCoherent_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`
of `StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Crystalline.SmallSite.QuasicoherentImpliesLocal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiCoherent_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf S)) (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsLocallyQuasiCoherent M
declarations.comment:
the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(a) on the big site CRIS(X/S): quasi-coherent implies
  locally quasi-coherent.  The same implication on the small site Cris(X/S), and the other half
  (1) ⇒ (2)(b) that a quasi-coherent module is a crystal, on each of the two sites, carry this tag
  separately.  The converse (2) ⇒ (1) is a separate statement

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isLocallyQuasiCoherent
declarations.doc:
**The implication (2) ⇒ (1) of [Stacks, Tag 07IT] on the big crystalline site `CRIS(X/S)`: a
locally quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules which is a crystal in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules is
quasi-coherent on the site.**

Quasi-coherence is Zariski-local on the ambient scheme of each object
(`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_forall_isAffine`), so it is
enough to present `F` globally on the localisation of `CRIS(X/S)` at an object whose ambient scheme
is affine, which is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.hasGlobalPresentation_over_of_isAffine`.

The crystal condition is read at sheaf level, as
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.IsSheafCrystal`; that is the reading under which the tag
holds, and the two hypotheses are exactly the source's conditions (a) and (b).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isLocallyQuasiCoherent
    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf S)} (hlqc : IsLocallyQuasiCoherent M)
    (hcrys : IsSheafCrystal M) : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment:
the implication (2) ⇒ (1) on the big site CRIS(X/S): a sheaf of 𝒪_{X/S}-modules
  whose restrictions F_T are all quasi-coherent and which is a crystal in 𝒪_{X/S}-modules is
  quasi-coherent on the site

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07IT] on the big crystalline site `CRIS(X/S)`:** a sheaf of
`𝒪_{X/S}`-modules is quasi-coherent on the site if and only if all its restrictions `F_T` are
quasi-coherent `𝒪_T`-modules and it is a crystal in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules.

The two halves of the forward implication are
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isLocallyQuasiCoherent_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite` and
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isSheafCrystal_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`; the converse is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isLocallyQuasiCoherent`.  The
crystal condition is read at sheaf level, which is the reading under which the tag holds; see the
module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf S)) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔ IsLocallyQuasiCoherent M ∧ IsSheafCrystal M
declarations.comment:
the equivalence on the big site CRIS(X/S), with the crystal condition read with the
  comparison maps of sheaves of modules

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isSheafCrystal_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IT, the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(b): a quasi-coherent sheaf of
`𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the small crystalline site is a crystal in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules.**

For a morphism `f : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U', T', δ')` of `Cris(X/S)` the comparison map
`c_f : f^* F_{T'} ⟶ F_T` of sheaves of `𝒪_T`-modules is an isomorphism.  This is the source's
argument, with its opening reduction "it suffices to prove (a) and (b) Zariski locally" carried
out: quasi-coherence gives, around every point of `T'`, an open `V` on whose restriction
`(U' ∩ V, V, δ'|_V)` the module has a global presentation
(`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.exists_hasGlobalPresentation_restrictOpen`), the
restrictions of `f` over those opens cover `T`, and over each of them the source's computation
applies on the localised site `Cris(X/S)/(U' ∩ V, V, δ'|_V)`, by
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.CohomologyRestriction`
`.isIso_moduleComparisonSheaf_of_hasGlobalPresentation_target`.  The comparison maps of the
structure morphisms of the two restrictions are isomorphisms, those morphisms being Cartesian open
immersions, so the `f`-map cocycle
(`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.CohomologyRestriction.fmapComp_comp`) transfers
bijectivity of the `f`-map composition to the direct images from the members of the cover, and
invertibility of `c_f` follows because it is Zariski-local on `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheafCrystal_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)) (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsSheafCrystal M
declarations.comment:
the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(b) on the small site Cris(X/S): a quasi-coherent sheaf of
  𝒪_{X/S}-modules is a crystal in 𝒪_{X/S}-modules, the crystal condition being read with the
  comparison maps of sheaves of modules.  The same implication on the big site CRIS(X/S), and the
  implication (1) ⇒ (2)(a) on each of the two sites, carry this tag separately.  The converse
  (2) ⇒ (1) is a separate statement

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isLocallyQuasiCoherent_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IT for `𝒞 = Cris(X/S)`, the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(a): a quasi-coherent
sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the small crystalline site is locally quasi-coherent.**

Quasi-coherence gives, around every point of the ambient scheme `T` of every object `(U, T, δ)` of
`Cris(X/S)`, an open `V` on whose restriction `(U ∩ V, V, δ|_V)` the module has a global
presentation (`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite`
`.exists_hasGlobalPresentation_restrictOpen`, which is cocontinuity of the restriction functor).
Intersecting `V` with a given open `W` of `T` makes those opens into an open cover of `W`, and each
presentation restricts to one of `F_T` on the Zariski site localised at `V ⊓ W` by
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite`
`.hasGlobalPresentation_moduleRestrictionSheaf_over`; that is quasi-coherence of `F_T` over `W`.

This is one of the two halves of the implication (1) ⇒ (2) of the tag; the other half, that a
quasi-coherent module is a crystal, is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isSheafCrystal_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Crystalline.SmallSite.QuasicoherentCrystal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyQuasiCoherent_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)) (hM : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsLocallyQuasiCoherent M
declarations.comment:
the implication (1) ⇒ (2)(a) on the small site Cris(X/S): quasi-coherent implies
  locally quasi-coherent.  The same implication on the big site CRIS(X/S), and the other half
  (1) ⇒ (2)(b) that a quasi-coherent module is a crystal, on each of the two sites, carry this tag
  separately.  The converse (2) ⇒ (1) is a separate statement

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isLocallyQuasiCoherent
declarations.doc:
**The implication (2) ⇒ (1) of [Stacks, Tag 07IT] on the small crystalline site `Cris(X/S)`: a
locally quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules which is a crystal in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules is
quasi-coherent on the site.**

Quasi-coherence is Zariski-local on the ambient scheme of each object
(`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_forall_isAffine`), so
it is enough to present `F` globally on the localisation of `Cris(X/S)` at an object whose ambient
scheme is affine, which is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.hasGlobalPresentation_over_of_isAffine`.

The crystal condition is read at sheaf level, as
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.IsSheafCrystal`; that is the reading under which
the tag holds, and the two hypotheses are exactly the source's conditions (a) and (b).
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isLocallyQuasiCoherent
    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)} (hlqc : IsLocallyQuasiCoherent M)
    (hcrys : IsSheafCrystal M) : M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment:
the implication (2) ⇒ (1) on the small site Cris(X/S): a sheaf of 𝒪_{X/S}-modules
  whose restrictions F_T are all quasi-coherent and which is a crystal in 𝒪_{X/S}-modules is
  quasi-coherent on the site

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07IT] on the small crystalline site `Cris(X/S)`:** a sheaf of
`𝒪_{X/S}`-modules is quasi-coherent on the site if and only if all its restrictions `F_T` are
quasi-coherent `𝒪_T`-modules and it is a crystal in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules.

The two halves of the forward implication are
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isLocallyQuasiCoherent_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`
and `Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isSheafCrystal_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`; the
converse is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isQuasicoherentOnSite_of_isLocallyQuasiCoherent`.
The crystal condition is read at sheaf level, which is the reading under which the tag holds; see
the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_iff (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)) :
    M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ↔ IsLocallyQuasiCoherent M ∧ IsSheafCrystal M
declarations.comment:
the equivalence on the small site Cris(X/S), with the crystal condition read with
  the comparison maps of sheaves of modules

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeQuasicoherentCrystal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IU.**  A *crystal in finite locally free modules* on the small
crystalline site: a sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `Cris(X/S)` which is a crystal in quasi-coherent
modules — that is, quasi-coherent, condition (1) of [Stacks, Tag 07IT] — and is finite locally
free.  [Stacks, Tag 07IS] states the conditions for `CRIS(X/S)` and for `Cris(X/S)` alike, and
both predicates used here are the general ones for a sheaf of modules on a site, so this differs
from the condition on the big site only in the site it is read on.
declarations.statement:
structure IsFiniteLocallyFreeQuasicoherentCrystal {S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}}
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)) : Prop
declarations.comment:
crystals in finite locally free modules on the small site Cris(X/S), with the
  crystal in quasi-coherent modules taken as condition (1) of Stacks 07IT

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.IsFiniteLocallyFreeQuasicoherentCrystal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IU.**  A *crystal in finite locally free modules* on the big
crystalline site: a sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `CRIS(X/S)` which is a crystal in quasi-coherent
modules — that is, quasi-coherent, condition (1) of [Stacks, Tag 07IT] — and is finite locally
free, every object of the site having a covering on whose members the restricted module is a
finite free module over the restricted structure sheaf.

This is the big-site form of the condition [Stacks, Tag 07N3] builds its F-crystal on, so it is
stated here, upstream of `Crystalline.FCrystal`; the small-site form of the same condition and
what either form gives through [Stacks, Tag 07IT] are in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Crystalline.CrystalsModules.FiniteLocallyFreeCrystal`.
declarations.statement:
structure IsFiniteLocallyFreeQuasicoherentCrystal {S : GlobalCrystallineSituation.{u}}
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf S)) : Prop
declarations.comment:
crystals in finite locally free modules on the big site CRIS(X/S), with the crystal
  in quasi-coherent modules taken as condition (1) of Stacks 07IT

registrations.name: SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite
registrations.comment:
a crystal in quasi-coherent modules on either crystalline site is a
  quasi-coherent sheaf of modules, condition (1) of Stacks 07IT

declarations.name: Crystalline.dpDifferentialsSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf of divided power differentials** `Ω_{T/Y,δ}` of a divided power scheme `T` over a
scheme `Y`: the sheaf of `𝒪_T`-modules associated with the presheaf of divided power
differentials.
declarations.statement: def dpDifferentialsSheaf : T.scheme.Modules
declarations.comment:
the sheaf Ω_{T/Y,δ} of divided power differentials of a divided power
  scheme over a scheme

declarations.name: Crystalline.universalDPSchemeDerivation_isUniversal
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of the sheaf of divided power differentials.**  Every divided power
derivation of `𝒪_T` over `Y` into a sheaf of `𝒪_T`-modules factors uniquely through the universal
one.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalDPSchemeDerivation_isUniversal :
    (universalDPSchemeDerivation T Y f).IsUniversal
declarations.comment: the universal divided power derivation d_{T/Y,δ} and its universal property

declarations.name: Crystalline.existsUnique_siteDPDesc
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of `d_{ℬ/𝒜,δ}`** ([Stacks, Tag 07IW]).  Every divided power
`𝒜`-derivation of `ℬ` into a sheaf of `ℬ`-modules factors through the universal divided power
derivation by a unique map of sheaves of modules.  The site and the base `𝒜` are arbitrary: `𝒜`
is a presheaf of commutative rings, so that `𝒜 = f⁻¹𝒪'` for a morphism of ringed topoi may be
used in its presheaf form, and the modules live in any universe `max u w` in which the site
admits sheafification.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_siteDPDesc (F : SheafOfModules.{max u w} (ringSheaf B))
    (D : PresheafOfModulesOfCommRing.Derivation' F.val φ) (hD : IsSiteDPDerivation φ δ D) :
    ∃! f : siteDPDifferentials.{w} φ δ ⟶ F,
      (siteDPUniversalDerivation.{w} φ δ).postcomp f.val = D
declarations.comment: the universal divided power 𝒜-derivation d_{ℬ/𝒜,δ} : ℬ → Ω_{ℬ/𝒜,δ} on a site

declarations.name: Crystalline.universalDerivation_postcomp_siteDPQuotient
declarations.doc:
**`d_{ℬ/𝒜,δ}` is the composite `ℬ ⟶ Ω_{ℬ/𝒜} ⟶ Ω_{ℬ/𝒜,δ}`** of the universal derivation
of [Stacks, Tag 04BL] with `Crystalline.siteDPQuotient`.
declarations.statement:
theorem universalDerivation_postcomp_siteDPQuotient :
    (universalDerivation A B φ).postcomp (siteDPQuotient φ δ).val =
      siteDPUniversalDerivation.{u} φ.hom δ.toPresheafDividedPowers
declarations.comment: d_{ℬ/𝒜,δ} is the composite of d_{ℬ/𝒜} : ℬ → Ω_{ℬ/𝒜} with Ω_{ℬ/𝒜} → Ω_{ℬ/𝒜,δ}

declarations.name: Crystalline.siteDPQuotient_relation
declarations.doc:
**The map `Ω_{ℬ/𝒜} ⟶ Ω_{ℬ/𝒜,δ}` kills the local sections
`d_{ℬ/𝒜}(δ_n x) - δ_{n-1}(x) d_{ℬ/𝒜}(x)`.**
declarations.statement:
theorem siteDPQuotient_relation (U : Cᵒᵖ) (n : ℕ) (x : B.obj.obj U)
    (hx : x ∈ sectionIdeal B I U) :
    ((siteDPQuotient φ δ).val.app U).hom (siteDPRelation φ δ U n x) = 0
declarations.comment: Ω_{ℬ/𝒜} → Ω_{ℬ/𝒜,δ} kills the sections d(δ_n x) - δ_{n-1}(x) d(x)

declarations.name: Crystalline.existsUnique_siteDPQuotient_desc
declarations.doc:
**`Ω_{ℬ/𝒜,δ}` is the quotient of `Ω_{ℬ/𝒜}` by the submodule generated by the local sections
`d_{ℬ/𝒜}(δ_n x) - δ_{n-1}(x) d_{ℬ/𝒜}(x)`.**  Every map of sheaves of `ℬ`-modules out of
`Ω_{ℬ/𝒜}` killing those sections factors uniquely through `Ω_{ℬ/𝒜} ⟶ Ω_{ℬ/𝒜,δ}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_siteDPQuotient_desc (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (ringSheaf B))
    (g : moduleOfDifferentials A B φ ⟶ F)
    (hg : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (n : ℕ) (x : B.obj.obj U), x ∈ sectionIdeal B I U →
      (g.val.app U).hom (siteDPRelation φ δ U n x) = 0) :
    ∃! h : siteDPDifferentials.{u} φ.hom δ.toPresheafDividedPowers ⟶ F,
      siteDPQuotient φ δ ≫ h = g
declarations.comment:
Ω_{ℬ/𝒜} → Ω_{ℬ/𝒜,δ} is the quotient by the submodule generated by the sections
  d(δ_n x) - δ_{n-1}(x) d(x)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.existsUnique_crisDesc
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of `d_{X/S}`** ([Stacks, Tag 07IW]).  Every `S`-derivation of
`𝒪_{X/S}` into a sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `Cris(X/S)`, that is every derivation killing the
sections pulled back from the opens of `S` and obeying the divided power chain rule on `𝒥_{X/S}`
([Stacks, Tag 07IX]), factors through `d_{X/S}` by a unique map of sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_crisDesc (F : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} (crisStructureRingSheaf S))
    (D : PresheafOfModulesOfCommRing.Derivation' (M := F.val) (crisBaseMap S))
    (hD : IsSiteDPDerivation.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u} (M := F.val) (crisBaseMap S)
      (crisDividedPowers S) D) :
    ∃! f : crisDifferentials S ⟶ F, (crisUniversalDerivation S).postcomp f.val = D
declarations.comment:
Ω_{X/S} and the universal divided power derivation d_{X/S} : 𝒪_{X/S} → Ω_{X/S} on
  Cris(X/S), from the construction on a site applied to (X/S)_cris → Sh(S_Zar)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.SDerivation
declarations.doc:
**An `S`-derivation on the small crystalline site** ([Stacks, Tag 07IX]).  For a presheaf `F`
of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `Cris(X/S)`, a map of presheaves of abelian groups `𝒪_{X/S} → F` such
that for every object `(U, T, δ)` and *every* open `V ⊆ S` through which `T → S` factors, the map
`Γ(T, 𝒪_T) → F(U, T, δ)` is a divided power `Γ(V, 𝒪_V)`-derivation.  For `F` the underlying
presheaf `ℱ.val` of a sheaf `ℱ` of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules this is the definition of the source.
declarations.statement: structure SDerivation (F : PresheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S).obj)
declarations.comment: S-derivation O_{X/S} → F into a sheaf F of O_{X/S}-modules on Cris(X/S), as SDerivation S F.val

declarations.name: Crystalline.affineSectionsEquiv
declarations.doc:
For an affine open `W` of a divided power scheme `T` lying over an affine open `V` of the base
`Y`, the sections of the sheaf `Ω_{T/Y,δ}` of divided power differentials over `W` are the module
`Ω¹_{Γ(W,𝒪_T)/Γ(V,𝒪_Y),δ}` of divided power differentials of the corresponding rings.
declarations.comment: clause (2): the sections over an affine open

declarations.name: Crystalline.dpDifferentialsSheaf_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf of divided power differentials is quasi-coherent**, being the quotient of the
quasi-coherent sheaf of relative differentials by a subsheaf which, over an affine open, is the
image of a free module.
declarations.statement:
instance dpDifferentialsSheaf_isQuasicoherent :
    (dpDifferentialsSheaf T Y f).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of the sheaf of divided power differentials

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.crysDifferentialsSheafRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IZ, the module identification.**  For an object `(U, T, δ)` of
`Cris(X/S)` the restriction `(Ω_{X/S})_T` of the sheaf of crystalline differentials to `T_Zar` is
the sheaf `Ω_{T/S,δ}` of divided power differentials of `T` over `S`, as sheaves of
`𝒪_T`-modules.
declarations.comment: (Ω_{X/S})_T = Ω_{T/S,δ}, as sheaves of 𝒪_T-modules on T_Zar

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.crysDifferentialsSheafRestrictionIso_hom_app_d
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07IZ, the derivations.**  Under the identification
`Ω_{T/S,δ} ≅ (Ω_{X/S})_T` of `crysDifferentialsSheafRestrictionIso`, the universal divided power
derivation `d_{T/S,δ}` is the restriction `d_{X/S}|_T` of the universal derivation of `Ω_{X/S}`:
for an open `W` of `T` and a section `b` of `𝒪_T` over `W`, the section `d_{T/S,δ} b` of
`Ω_{T/S,δ}` over `W` corresponds to `d_{X/S} b` over the restricted object `(U ∩ W, W, δ|_W)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem crysDifferentialsSheafRestrictionIso_hom_app_d (A : CrystallineThickening S)
    (W : A.obj.thickening.target.scheme.Opens) (b : Γ(A.obj.thickening.target.scheme, W)) :
    (crysDifferentialsSheafRestrictionIso A).hom.val.app (op W)
        ((universalDPSchemeDerivation A.obj.thickening.target S.S.scheme
          A.obj.toBase.hom).app W b) =
      crysSheafD S (A.restrictOpen W) (openTopRes W b)
declarations.comment: d_{X/S}|_T = d_{T/S,δ}

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.affineCrysFormsSheafOneEquiv
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07J0]: the sections of the sheaf `Ω_{X/S}` over an affine object.**  For an
object `(U, T, δ)` of `Cris(X/S)` with `T` affine whose structure morphism factors through an
affine open `V ⊆ S`, the sections over `(U, T, δ)` of the sheaf `Ω_{X/S}` — the sheaf
`crysFormsSheaf S 1` associated with `⋀¹ Ω_{X/S} = Ω_{X/S}` — are the divided power differentials
`Ω_{Γ(T, 𝒪_T)/Γ(V, 𝒪_V), δ}`, as modules over `Γ(T, 𝒪_T)` (the sections of `𝒪_{X/S}` there).

It is the inverse of the sheafification map on those sections
(`bijective_toCrysFormsSheaf_app_of_isAffine`), followed by `⋀¹ M = M` and the presheaf-level
identification `Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.affineCrysDifferentialsIso`.
declarations.statement:
def affineCrysFormsSheafOneEquiv [IsAffine A.obj.thickening.target.scheme]
    {V : S.S.scheme.Opens}
    (h : (⊤ : A.obj.thickening.target.scheme.Opens) ≤ A.obj.toBase.hom ⁻¹ᵁ V)
    (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    (crysFormsSheaf S 1).val.obj (op A) ≃ₗ[crysFormRing S A] affineCrysDifferentialsObj S A.obj h
declarations.comment: Γ((U, T, δ), Ω_{X/S}) = Ω_{Γ(T, 𝒪_T)/Γ(V, 𝒪_V), δ} for the sheaf Ω_{X/S} (crysFormsSheaf S 1, the sheaf associated with ⋀¹ of the crystalline differentials) on an affine object of Cris(X/S) mapping into an affine open V ⊆ S

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isClosedImmersion_smallSelfProductAmbientDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07J1.**  The ambient diagonal `Δ : T ⟶ T(1)` of a self-product taken in
`Cris(X/S)` is a closed immersion.  It is surjective on stalks because it is a section of either
coprojection, and a closed embedding because it is a homeomorphism on spaces: that is `U(1) = U`
read through the immersions of the two thickenings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_smallSelfProductAmbientDiagonal
    (h : IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk pr₀ pr₁)) :
    IsClosedImmersion (smallSelfProductAmbientDiagonal h).hom
declarations.comment: the diagonal Δ : T ⟶ T(1) is a closed immersion

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.ker_ideal_smallSelfProductAmbientDiagonal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07J1.**  On an affine open of `T(1)` the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
of the closed immersion `Δ` is the diagonal ideal.  This is what reconciles the presentation of
`K` used here and in `SelfProductDiagonal.lean` — the kernel of `Δ` on sections over each open —
with the source's, the quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of the closed immersion `Δ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ker_ideal_smallSelfProductAmbientDiagonal (h : IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk pr₀ pr₁))
    (W : D.obj.thickening.target.scheme.affineOpens) :
    (smallSelfProductAmbientDiagonal h).hom.ker.ideal W =
      smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal h (W : D.obj.thickening.target.scheme.Opens)
declarations.comment: K is the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf of the closed immersion Δ, on affine opens

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallSelfProductConormalSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf of `𝒪_T`-modules `K/K^{[2]}`**: the sheaf associated with the conormal presheaf
`V ↦ K/K^{[2]}` over `p₀⁻¹V ⊓ p₁⁻¹V`.  The diagonal is a homeomorphism `T ≅ T(1)` on spaces, so
this is the quotient of the ideal sheaf `K` of `Δ` by its divided square, read on `T`, with
`𝒪_T`-module structure through `Δ`.
declarations.statement:
def smallSelfProductConormalSheaf (h : IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk pr₀ pr₁)) :
    SheafOfModules.{u} B.obj.thickening.target.scheme.ringCatSheaf
declarations.comment: the sheaf of 𝒪_T-modules K/K^{[2]} of the second assertion, the sheaf associated with the conormal modules over the opens p₀⁻¹V ⊓ p₁⁻¹V of T(1)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.restrictedCrysDifferentialsSheafIsoConormalSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07J1, second assertion.**  For a self-product
`(U(1), T(1), δ(1))` of an object `(U, T, δ)` of `Cris(X/S)`, with `K` the ideal of the diagonal
`Δ : T ⟶ T(1)`, the sheaf of `𝒪_T`-modules `(Ω_{X/S})_T` is isomorphic to `K/K^{[2]}`.  The
isomorphism is the sheafification of the comparison morphism, which sends `d f` to the class of
`p₁^♯ f - p₀^♯ f` (`smallSelfProductConormalComparison_d`).
declarations.statement:
def restrictedCrysDifferentialsSheafIsoConormalSheaf (h : IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk pr₀ pr₁)) :
    restrictedCrysDifferentialsSheaf S B.obj ≅ smallSelfProductConormalSheaf h
declarations.comment: second assertion: (Ω_{X/S})_T ≅ K/K^{[2]} as sheaves of 𝒪_T-modules, d f ↦ [p₁^♯ f - p₀^♯ f]; the first assertion is smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal_le and smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal_isSubDPIdeal

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal_le
declarations.doc:
For a self-product `(U(1), T(1), δ(1))` of an object `(U, T, δ)` of `Cris(X/S)` with itself,
the diagonal ideal `K` of `Δ : T ⟶ T(1)` is contained in the divided power ideal `J_{T(1)}` on
every open of `T(1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal_le (h : IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk pr₀ pr₁))
    (W : D.obj.thickening.target.scheme.Opens) :
    smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal h W ≤ D.obj.thickening.target.ideal.obj (op W)
declarations.comment: K ⊆ J_{T(1)}; sections over each open, K the kernel of Δ on sections

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal_isSubDPIdeal
declarations.doc:
For a self-product `(U(1), T(1), δ(1))` of an object `(U, T, δ)` of `Cris(X/S)` with itself,
the diagonal ideal `K` of `Δ : T ⟶ T(1)` is preserved by the divided structure on `J_{T(1)}` on
every open of `T(1)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal_isSubDPIdeal (h : IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk pr₀ pr₁))
    (W : D.obj.thickening.target.scheme.Opens) :
    (D.obj.thickening.target.dividedPowers.dividedPowers (op W)).IsSubDPIdeal
      (smallSelfProductDiagonalIdeal h W)
declarations.comment: K is preserved by the divided structure on J_{T(1)}; sections over each open

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningHom
declarations.doc:
**The functoriality datum of the first-order universal thickening of [Stacks, Tag 07J2].**
For a morphism `g : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U₁, T₁, δ₁)` of `CRIS(X/S)`, the induced morphism
`(U, T', δ') ⟶ (U₁, T₁', δ₁')` of the site together with its two commutation relations, which
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Crystalline/UniversalThickeningFunctorial.lean` constructs as
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteMap`,
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteMap_comp_P₀` and
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteMap_comp_P₁`.

This is the input [Stacks, Tag 07J6] uses to turn its family of connections into a morphism of
abelian sheaves on the site.
declarations.statement: def firstOrderThickeningHom {A B : Thickening S} (g : A ⟶ B) : FirstOrderThickeningHom g
declarations.comment: the functoriality datum of the first-order thickening, in the shape in which the naturality clause of 07J6 consumes it

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSchemeMap
declarations.doc: **The morphism of schemes `T_A' ⟶ T_B'` between the first-order universal thickenings.**
declarations.comment: the morphism T' ⟶ T₁' of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningMapApp_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**The map on sections of the first-order thickenings is a homomorphism of divided power
rings.**  It carries `J'_B = J_B ⊕ Ω_B` into `J'_A = J_A ⊕ Ω_A` because the ambient morphism does
so on the first summand, and it commutes with `δ'` because the ambient morphism commutes with
`δ` and the map on differentials is semilinear.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningMapApp_isDPMorphism (g : A ⟶ B)
    (U : B.thickening.target.scheme.Opens) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism
      (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers B.thickening.target S.S.scheme B.toBase.hom (op U))
      (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers A.thickening.target S.S.scheme A.toBase.hom
        (op (ambientHom g ⁻¹ᵁ U)))
      (firstOrderThickeningMapApp g (op U)).hom
declarations.comment: the map T' ⟶ T₁' is compatible with the divided powers δ'

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningDPMap
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of divided power schemes `(T_A', J_A', δ_A') ⟶ (T_B', J_B', δ_B')`** between
the first-order universal thickenings.
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningDPMap (g : A ⟶ B) :
    firstOrderThickeningDPScheme S A ⟶ firstOrderThickeningDPScheme S B
declarations.comment: the morphism T' ⟶ T₁' of divided power schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSchemeMap_comp_projHom
declarations.doc:
**The map of first-order thickenings commutes with the first projection**, both sides
carrying `(b, ω)` to `gh^# b`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningSchemeMap_comp_projHom (g : A ⟶ B) :
    firstOrderThickeningSchemeMap g ≫
        firstOrderThickeningProjHom B.thickening.target S.S.scheme B.toBase.hom =
      firstOrderThickeningProjHom A.thickening.target S.S.scheme A.toBase.hom ≫ ambientHom g
declarations.comment: the map T' ⟶ T₁' commutes with p₀, for schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSchemeMap_comp_P₁Hom
declarations.doc:
**The map of first-order thickenings commutes with the second projection.**  This is the
computation `dg ∘ d_B = d_A ∘ gh^#`: one side carries `b` to `(gh^# b, dg (d_B b))` and the
other to `(gh^# b, d_A (gh^# b))`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningSchemeMap_comp_P₁Hom (g : A ⟶ B) :
    firstOrderThickeningSchemeMap g ≫
        firstOrderThickeningP₁Hom B.thickening.target S.S.scheme B.toBase.hom =
      firstOrderThickeningP₁Hom A.thickening.target S.S.scheme A.toBase.hom ≫ ambientHom g
declarations.comment: the map T' ⟶ T₁' commutes with p₁, for schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteMap
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of `CRIS(X/S)` between the first-order universal thickenings** induced by a
morphism `g` of `CRIS(X/S)`: the functoriality datum of [Stacks, Tag 07J2].
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningSiteMap (g : A ⟶ B) :
    firstOrderThickeningObject S A ⟶ firstOrderThickeningObject S B
declarations.comment: the functoriality (U, T, δ) ↦ (U, T', δ') of the first-order thickening

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteMap_comp_P₀
declarations.doc:
**The functoriality datum commutes with the first projection**, the left relation of
[Stacks, Tag 07J2].
declarations.comment: the functoriality datum commutes with p₀, in CRIS(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteMap_comp_P₁
declarations.doc:
**The functoriality datum commutes with the second projection**, the right relation of
[Stacks, Tag 07J2].
declarations.comment: the functoriality datum commutes with p₁, in CRIS(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The structure sheaf of the first-order universal thickening** `T'` of a divided power
scheme `T` over `Y`: the square-zero extension `𝒪_T ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ}` of the structure sheaf of `T`
by its sheaf of divided power differentials.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningSheaf : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} ↑T.scheme
declarations.comment: the structure sheaf of the first-order thickening

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningIdeal
declarations.doc:
**The ideal `J' = J ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ}`** of the sections of `𝒪_{T'}` over an open: the sections
whose component in `𝒪_T` lies in the divided power ideal of `T`.
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningIdeal (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    Ideal ↑((firstOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f).obj W)
declarations.comment: the extended ideal J' = J ⊕ Ω

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers
declarations.doc:
**The divided power structure `δ'` on the ideal `J' = J ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ}`**, given in degree
`k + 1` by `(g, ω) ↦ (δ_{k+1} g, δ_k g · ω)` and in degree zero by `1`.
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers (firstOrderThickeningIdeal T Y f W)
declarations.comment: the divided power structure on J'

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickening_mul_eq_zero
declarations.doc: **The sheaf of divided power differentials is an ideal of square zero in `𝒪_{T'}`.**
declarations.comment: the differentials are an ideal of square zero

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickening_restriction_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Every restriction map of `𝒪_{T'}` is compatible with the divided powers of `J'`**, so the
rings of sections of `𝒪_{T'}` with the ideals `J'` and the structures `δ'` form a presheaf of
divided power rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickening_restriction_isDPMorphism
    {W W' : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ} (i : W ⟶ W') :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W')
      (((firstOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f).map i).hom)
declarations.comment: the divided powers on J' are compatible with restriction

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningP₀
declarations.doc: **The first of the two maps `𝒪_T → 𝒪_{T'}`**, the inclusion `g ↦ (g, 0)`.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningP₀ : T.scheme.sheaf.obj ⟶ firstOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f
declarations.comment: the map p₀

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningP₁
declarations.doc:
**The second of the two maps `𝒪_T → 𝒪_{T'}`**, the inclusion shifted by the universal
divided power derivation: `g ↦ (g, d_{T/Y,δ} g)`.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningP₁ : T.scheme.sheaf.obj ⟶ firstOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f
declarations.comment: the map p₁

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningProj
declarations.doc: **The projection `𝒪_{T'} → 𝒪_T`**, forgetting the differential component.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningProj : firstOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f ⟶ T.scheme.sheaf.obj
declarations.comment: the quotient map

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningP₀_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc: **`p₀` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J` and `J'`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningP₀_isDPMorphism (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W)
      (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (((firstOrderThickeningP₀ T Y f).app W).hom)
declarations.comment: p₀ is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningP₁_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**`p₁` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J` and `J'`**, because the
universal divided power derivation obeys the divided power chain rule.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningP₁_isDPMorphism (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W)
      (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (((firstOrderThickeningP₁ T Y f).app W).hom)
declarations.comment: p₁ is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningProj_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**The projection `𝒪_{T'} → 𝒪_T` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J'`
and `J`.**
declarations.comment: the quotient map is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningP₁_sub_P₀
declarations.doc:
**The difference of the two maps `𝒪_T → 𝒪_{T'}` is the universal divided power derivation**,
followed by the inclusion of `Ω_{T/Y,δ}` as the square-zero summand.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningP₁_sub_P₀ (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ)
    (a : ↑(T.scheme.sheaf.obj.obj W)) :
    ((firstOrderThickeningP₁ T Y f).app W).hom a - ((firstOrderThickeningP₀ T Y f).app W).hom a =
      sqZeroExtMk 0 (sheafApp T Y f W.unop a)
declarations.comment: p₁ - p₀ is the universal derivation

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningKernelEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The ideal of the first-order thickening `T → T'` is the sheaf of divided power
differentials**: the kernel of `𝒪_{T'} → 𝒪_T` over an open is canonically `Ω_{T/Y,δ}`.
declarations.comment: the ideal of the thickening is the differentials

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickening_ker_sq
declarations.doc:
**`T → T'` is a first-order thickening**: the ideal of the projection `𝒪_{T'} → 𝒪_T` has
square zero on every open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickening_ker_sq (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    RingHom.ker (((firstOrderThickeningProj T Y f).app W).hom) ^ 2 = ⊥
declarations.comment: T → T' is a first-order thickening

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningScheme
declarations.doc:
**The first-order universal thickening `T'` as a scheme.**  The topological space of `T`
equipped with the structure sheaf `𝒪_{T'} = 𝒪_T ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ}`; it is a scheme because it is
isomorphic, as a locally ringed space, to the realization of the square-zero extension.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningScheme : Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: the first-order thickening T' as a scheme

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningι
declarations.doc:
**The immersion `i : T ⟶ T'`**, whose map on sections is the projection
`𝒪_{T'} ⟶ 𝒪_T`.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningι : T.scheme ⟶ firstOrderThickeningScheme T Y f
declarations.comment: the immersion i : T ⟶ T' of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningProjHom
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `p₀ : T' ⟶ T`**, induced by the inclusion `g ↦ (g, 0)` of structure
sheaves.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningProjHom : firstOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ T.scheme
declarations.comment: the morphism p₀ : T' ⟶ T of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningP₁Hom
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `p₁ : T' ⟶ T`**, induced by the derivation-shifted inclusion
`g ↦ (g, d_{T/Y,δ} g)` of structure sheaves.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningP₁Hom : firstOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ T.scheme
declarations.comment: the morphism p₁ : T' ⟶ T of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningι_comp_projHom
declarations.doc: **`p₀` retracts the immersion `i`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningι_comp_projHom :
    firstOrderThickeningι T Y f ≫ firstOrderThickeningProjHom T Y f = 𝟙 T.scheme
declarations.comment: the diagram relation p₀ ∘ i = id, for schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningι_comp_P₁Hom
declarations.doc: **`p₁` retracts the immersion `i`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningι_comp_P₁Hom :
    firstOrderThickeningι T Y f ≫ firstOrderThickeningP₁Hom T Y f = 𝟙 T.scheme
declarations.comment: the diagram relation p₁ ∘ i = id, for schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningι_isFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**The immersion `T ⟶ T'` is a first-order thickening of schemes**: its ideal sheaf has
square zero, because the kernel of `𝒪_{T'} ⟶ 𝒪_T` over every open is the square-zero summand
`Ω_{T/Y,δ}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningι_isFirstOrderThickening :
    Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening (firstOrderThickeningι T Y f)
declarations.comment: i : T ⟶ T' is a first-order thickening of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningιKernelEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The ideal sheaf of `i : T ⟶ T'` is `Ω_{T/Y,δ}`**: over every open, the kernel of the map
on sections of `i` is canonically the module of divided power differentials.
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningιKernelEquiv
    (W : (Opens ↑(firstOrderThickeningScheme T Y f))ᵒᵖ) :
    ↑((dpDifferentialsModules T Y f).obj (firstOrderThickeningOpen T Y f W)) ≃+
      RingHom.ker (((firstOrderThickeningι T Y f).c.app W).hom)
declarations.comment: the ideal sheaf of i is the sheaf of divided power differentials

declarations.name: Crystalline.firstOrderThickeningP₁Hom_comp_base
declarations.doc:
**`p₀` and `p₁` are morphisms over the base `Y`, and they agree there**: their difference is
the universal divided power derivation, which kills every section pulled back from `Y`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningP₁Hom_comp_base :
    firstOrderThickeningP₁Hom T Y f ≫ f = firstOrderThickeningProjHom T Y f ≫ f
declarations.comment: p₀ and p₁ agree over the base

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningIdealSheaf
declarations.doc: **The extended ideal `J' = J ⊕ Ω_{T/S,δ}` as a sheaf of ideals on `T'`.**
declarations.comment: the ideal J' as a sheaf of ideals on T'

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningIdealSheaf_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**The extended ideal `J'` is quasi-coherent**, being the ideal sheaf of the closed immersion
`U ⟶ T'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningIdealSheaf_isQuasicoherent :
    (firstOrderThickeningIdealSheaf S A).toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the ideal J' is quasi-coherent

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningDPScheme
declarations.doc:
**The divided power scheme `(T', J', δ')`.**  The scheme `T'`, the quasi-coherent ideal
`J' = J ⊕ Ω_{T/S,δ}` and the divided power structure `δ'` of [Stacks, Tag 07J2].
declarations.statement: public abbrev firstOrderThickeningDPScheme : DividedPowerScheme.{u}
declarations.comment: T' with the ideal J' and the divided powers δ' is a divided power scheme

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningProjDP
declarations.doc: **`p₀ : T' ⟶ T` is a morphism of divided power schemes.**
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningProjDP :
    firstOrderThickeningDPScheme S A ⟶ A.thickening.target
declarations.comment: p₀ is a morphism of divided power schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningP₁DP
declarations.doc: **`p₁ : T' ⟶ T` is a morphism of divided power schemes.**
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningP₁DP :
    firstOrderThickeningDPScheme S A ⟶ A.thickening.target
declarations.comment: p₁ is a morphism of divided power schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningιDP
declarations.doc: **`i : T ⟶ T'` is a morphism of divided power schemes.**
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningιDP :
    A.thickening.target ⟶ firstOrderThickeningDPScheme S A
declarations.comment: i is a morphism of divided power schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSchemeThickening
declarations.doc:
**The divided power thickening `U ⟶ T'`**: a thickening of schemes whose defining ideal is
the divided power ideal `J'`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev firstOrderThickeningSchemeThickening : SchemeThickening.{u}
declarations.comment: U ⟶ T' is a divided power thickening

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningObject
declarations.doc:
**`(U, T', δ')` is an object of `CRIS(X/S)`.**  This is the assertion of [Stacks, Tag 07J2]
that the first-order universal thickening of an object of the crystalline category is again an
object of it: `T'` with the ideal `J' = J ⊕ Ω_{T/S,δ}` and the divided powers `δ'` is a divided
power scheme, `U ⟶ T'` is a divided power thickening, and `T' ⟶ S` is `p₀` followed by the
structure morphism of `T`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev firstOrderThickeningObject : Thickening S
declarations.comment: (U, T', δ') is an object of CRIS(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteι
declarations.doc: **The morphism `i : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U, T', δ')` of `CRIS(X/S)`.**
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningSiteι : A ⟶ firstOrderThickeningObject S A
declarations.comment: the morphism i of CRIS(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteP₀
declarations.doc: **The morphism `p₀ : (U, T', δ') ⟶ (U, T, δ)` of `CRIS(X/S)`.**
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningSiteP₀ : firstOrderThickeningObject S A ⟶ A
declarations.comment: the morphism p₀ of CRIS(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteP₁
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `p₁ : (U, T', δ') ⟶ (U, T, δ)` of `CRIS(X/S)`.**  It is a morphism over the
divided power base because `p₁` and `p₀` agree after composing with the structure morphism of
`T`, the universal divided power derivation killing every section pulled back from `S`.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningSiteP₁ : firstOrderThickeningObject S A ⟶ A
declarations.comment: the morphism p₁ of CRIS(X/S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteι_comp_P₀
declarations.doc:
**`p₀ ∘ i = id` in `CRIS(X/S)`**, the left relation of the diagram of
[Stacks, Tag 07J2].
declarations.statement:
public theorem firstOrderThickeningSiteι_comp_P₀ :
    firstOrderThickeningSiteι S A ≫ firstOrderThickeningSiteP₀ S A = 𝟙 A

**`p₁ ∘ i = id` in `CRIS(X/S)`**, the right relation of the diagram of

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteι_isFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**`i : (U, T, δ) ⟶ (U, T', δ')` is a first-order thickening whose ideal sheaf is
`Ω_{T/S,δ}`**, which is the restriction `(Ω_{X/S})_T` of the crystalline differentials by
[Stacks, Tag 07IZ].
declarations.comment: i is a first-order thickening with ideal sheaf Ω_{T/S,δ}

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningSiteKernelEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The ideal sheaf of `i : T ⟶ T'` is `(Ω_{X/S})_T`**, the restriction of the crystalline
differentials to the ambient scheme of the object — which is the spelling in which
[Stacks, Tag 07J2] states it.  Over every open the kernel of the map on sections of `i` is the
sheaf `Ω_{T/S,δ}` of divided power differentials, and [Stacks, Tag 07IZ] identifies that sheaf
with `(Ω_{X/S})_T`.
declarations.statement:
public def firstOrderThickeningSiteKernelEquiv
    (W : (Opens ↑(firstOrderThickeningScheme A.thickening.target S.S.scheme
      A.toBase.hom))ᵒᵖ) :
    ↑((restrictedCrysDifferentialsSheaf S A).val.obj
        (firstOrderThickeningOpen A.thickening.target S.S.scheme A.toBase.hom W)) ≃+
      RingHom.ker (((firstOrderThickeningι A.thickening.target S.S.scheme
        A.toBase.hom).c.app W).hom)
declarations.comment: the ideal sheaf of i is the restriction of Ω_{X/S} to T

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.firstOrderThickeningCrysObject

states it.
declarations.statement: public def firstOrderThickeningCrysObject : CrystallineThickening S
declarations.comment: (U, T', δ') is an object of Cris(X/S)
