declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.secondOrderThickeningSiteData
declarations.doc:
**The second-order universal thickening of [Stacks, Tag 07J3] as an object of `CRIS(X/S)`,
with the morphism `q₁₂` and the two relations the integrability argument consumes.**  Every field
is a declaration of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Crystalline/SecondOrderThickeningScheme.lean`: the object is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.secondOrderThickeningObject`, the morphisms are
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₁₂`,
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₁` and
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₂`, and the two relations are
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₁₂_comp_P₀` and
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₁₂_comp_P₁`.
declarations.statement: def secondOrderThickeningSiteData (A : Thickening S) : SecondOrderThickeningSiteData A
declarations.comment: the second-order thickening as an object of CRIS(X/S) together with q₁₂ and the two relations q₁ = q₁₂ ∘ p₀, q₂ = q₁₂ ∘ p₁, in the shape in which the integrability argument of 07J6 consumes them

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**The structure sheaf of the second-order universal thickening** `T''` of a divided power
scheme `T` over `Y`: the presheaf of commutative rings
`𝒪_T ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ} ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ} ⊕ Ω²_{T/Y,δ}` whose multiplication is corrected in the last
coordinate by the exterior product of the two middle coordinates.  All four summands are
sheaves.
declarations.statement: public def secondOrderThickeningPresheaf : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}
declarations.comment: the structure sheaf of the second-order thickening

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The structure sheaf of the second-order universal thickening**, as a sheaf: all four
summands `𝒪_T`, `Ω_{T/Y,δ}`, `Ω_{T/Y,δ}` and `Ω²_{T/Y,δ}` are sheaves, so the second-order
extension satisfies the sheaf condition.
declarations.statement: public def secondOrderThickeningSheaf : TopCat.Sheaf CommRingCat.{u} ↑T.scheme
declarations.comment: the structure sheaf of the second-order thickening is a sheaf

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickening_mul
declarations.doc: **The multiplication of `𝒪_{T''}` in coordinates.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickening_mul (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ)
    (x y : SecondOrderExt (dpWedge T Y f) W) :
    (secondOrderExtFst (x * y) = secondOrderExtFst x * secondOrderExtFst y ∧
      secondOrderExtLeft (x * y) =
        secondOrderExtFst x • secondOrderExtLeft y +
          secondOrderExtFst y • secondOrderExtLeft x) ∧
    secondOrderExtRight (x * y) =
        secondOrderExtFst x • secondOrderExtRight y +
          secondOrderExtFst y • secondOrderExtRight x ∧
      secondOrderExtTop (x * y) =
        secondOrderExtFst x • secondOrderExtTop y + secondOrderExtFst y • secondOrderExtTop x +
          (dpWedge T Y f).app W (secondOrderExtLeft x) (secondOrderExtRight y) +
          (dpWedge T Y f).app W (secondOrderExtLeft y) (secondOrderExtRight x)
declarations.comment: the multiplication of the second-order thickening

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningIdeal
declarations.doc:
**The ideal `J''` of the second-order universal thickening**: the inverse image of the
divided power ideal of `T` under the projection `𝒪_{T''} → 𝒪_T`.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningIdeal (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    Ideal (SecondOrderExt (dpWedge T Y f) W)
declarations.comment: the ideal J'' of the second-order thickening

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers
declarations.doc:
**The divided power structure `δ''` on the ideal `J''`** of the second-order universal
thickening.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers (secondOrderThickeningIdeal T Y f W)
declarations.comment: the divided power structure on J''

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers_dpow_add_two
declarations.doc:
**The displayed formula for `δ''`**:
`δ''_{k+2}(f, ω₁, ω₂, η) = (δ_{k+2} f, δ_{k+1} f · ω₁, δ_{k+1} f · ω₂,
δ_{k+1} f · η + δ_k f · ω₁ ∧ ω₂)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers_dpow_add_two (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) (k : ℕ)
    {x : SecondOrderExt (dpWedge T Y f) W} (hx : x ∈ secondOrderThickeningIdeal T Y f W) :
    (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W).dpow (k + 2) x =
      secondOrderExtMk
        ((T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W).dpow (k + 2) (secondOrderExtFst x))
        ((T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W).dpow (k + 1) (secondOrderExtFst x) •
          secondOrderExtLeft x)
        ((T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W).dpow (k + 1) (secondOrderExtFst x) •
          secondOrderExtRight x)
        ((T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W).dpow (k + 1) (secondOrderExtFst x) •
            secondOrderExtTop x +
          (T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W).dpow k (secondOrderExtFst x) •
            (dpWedge T Y f).app W (secondOrderExtLeft x) (secondOrderExtRight x))
declarations.comment: the divided power formula on J''

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickening_restriction_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**Every restriction map of `𝒪_{T''}` is compatible with the divided powers of `J''`**, so the
rings of sections of `𝒪_{T''}` with the ideals `J''` and the structures `δ''` form a presheaf of
divided power rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickening_restriction_isDPMorphism
    {W W' : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ} (i : W ⟶ W') :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W')
      (secondOrderExtRingHom (dpWedge T Y f) i)
declarations.comment: the divided powers on J'' are compatible with restriction

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀
declarations.doc: **The first of the three maps `𝒪_T → 𝒪_{T''}`**, `f ↦ (f, 0, 0, 0)`.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₀ :
    T.scheme.sheaf.obj ⟶ secondOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f
declarations.comment: the map q₀

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₁
declarations.doc: **The second of the three maps `𝒪_T → 𝒪_{T''}`**, `f ↦ (f, d f, 0, 0)`.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₁ :
    T.scheme.sheaf.obj ⟶ secondOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f
declarations.comment: the map q₁

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₂
declarations.doc:
**The third of the three maps `𝒪_T → 𝒪_{T''}`**, `f ↦ (f, d f, d f, 0)`.  It is
multiplicative because the exterior product is antisymmetric.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₂ :
    T.scheme.sheaf.obj ⟶ secondOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f
declarations.comment: the map q₂

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀₁
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₀₁ :
    firstOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f ⟶ secondOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f
declarations.comment: the map q₀₁

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀₂
declarations.doc:
**The map `q₀₂ : 𝒪_{T'} → 𝒪_{T''}`**, `(f, ω) ↦ (f, ω, ω, 0)`.  It is multiplicative
because the exterior product is antisymmetric.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₀₂ :
    firstOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f ⟶ secondOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f
declarations.comment: the map q₀₂

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc: **`q₀` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J` and `J''`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningQ₀_isDPMorphism (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W)
      (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (((secondOrderThickeningQ₀ T Y f).app W).hom)
declarations.comment: q₀ is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₁_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**`q₁` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J` and `J''`**, because the
universal divided power derivation obeys the divided power chain rule and the exterior product of
a differential with zero vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningQ₁_isDPMorphism (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W)
      (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (((secondOrderThickeningQ₁ T Y f).app W).hom)
declarations.comment: q₁ is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₂_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**`q₂` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J` and `J''`**, because the
universal divided power derivation obeys the divided power chain rule and the exterior product of
a differential with itself vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningQ₂_isDPMorphism (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (T.dividedPowers.dividedPowers W)
      (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (((secondOrderThickeningQ₂ T Y f).app W).hom)
declarations.comment: q₂ is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀₁_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc: **`q₀₁` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J'` and `J''`.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningQ₀₁_isDPMorphism (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (((secondOrderThickeningQ₀₁ T Y f).app W).hom)
declarations.comment: q₀₁ is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀₂_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**`q₀₂` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J'` and `J''`**, because the
exterior product of a differential with itself vanishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningQ₀₂_isDPMorphism (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (((secondOrderThickeningQ₀₂ T Y f).app W).hom)
declarations.comment: q₀₂ is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀_eq_Q₀₁_comp_P₀
declarations.doc: **`q₀ = q₀₁ ∘ p₀`.**
declarations.comment: q₀ = q₀₁ ∘ p₀

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₁_eq_Q₀₁_comp_P₁
declarations.doc: **`q₁ = q₀₁ ∘ p₁`.**
declarations.comment: q₁ = q₀₁ ∘ p₁

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀_eq_Q₀₂_comp_P₀
declarations.doc: **`q₀ = q₀₂ ∘ p₀`.**
declarations.comment: q₀ = q₀₂ ∘ p₀

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₂_eq_Q₀₂_comp_P₁
declarations.doc: **`q₂ = q₀₂ ∘ p₁`.**
declarations.comment: q₂ = q₀₂ ∘ p₁

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₁₂
declarations.doc:
**The map `q₁₂ : 𝒪_{T'} → 𝒪_{T''}`**, `(f, ω) ↦ (f, d f, ω, d ω)`.  It is multiplicative
because the de Rham differential obeys the Leibniz rule
`d (f η + g ω) = f (d η) + g (d ω) + (d f) ∧ η + (d g) ∧ ω`, which is exactly the correction term
of the second-order multiplication.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₁₂ :
    firstOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f ⟶ secondOrderThickeningPresheaf T Y f
declarations.comment: the map q₁₂

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₁₂_isDPMorphism
declarations.doc:
**`q₁₂` is compatible with the divided power structures on `J'` and `J''`**, because the
universal divided power derivation obeys the divided power chain rule and the de Rham
differential obeys its divided power Leibniz rule
`d (δ_{k+1}(f) ω) = δ_{k+1}(f) (d ω) + δ_k(f) ((d f) ∧ ω)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningQ₁₂_isDPMorphism (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    DividedPowers.IsDPMorphism (firstOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (secondOrderThickeningDividedPowers T Y f W)
      (((secondOrderThickeningQ₁₂ T Y f).app W).hom)
declarations.comment: q₁₂ is compatible with the divided powers

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₁_eq_Q₁₂_comp_P₀
declarations.doc:
**`q₁ = q₁₂ ∘ p₀`**, the two-form coordinate because the de Rham differential of the zero
differential vanishes.
declarations.comment: q₁ = q₁₂ ∘ p₀

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₂_eq_Q₁₂_comp_P₁
declarations.doc:
**`q₂ = q₁₂ ∘ p₁`**, the two-form coordinate because the de Rham differential kills every
exact differential.
declarations.comment: q₂ = q₁₂ ∘ p₁

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickening_ker_cube
declarations.doc:
**`T → T''` is a second-order thickening**: the ideal of the projection `𝒪_{T''} → 𝒪_T` has
vanishing cube on every open.  Its square lies in the top summand, and the top summand
annihilates it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickening_ker_cube (W : (Opens ↑T.scheme)ᵒᵖ) :
    RingHom.ker (secondOrderExtFstHom (dpWedge T Y f) W) ^ 3 = ⊥
declarations.comment: T → T'' is a second-order thickening of sheaves of rings

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningScheme
declarations.doc:
**The second-order universal thickening `T''` as a scheme.**  The topological space of `T`
equipped with the structure sheaf
`𝒪_{T''} = 𝒪_T ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ} ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ} ⊕ Ω²_{T/Y,δ}`; it is a scheme because it is isomorphic,
as a locally ringed space, to the realization of the square-zero extension of `𝒪_{T'}` by
`K`.
declarations.statement: public def secondOrderThickeningScheme : Scheme.{u}
declarations.comment: the second-order thickening T'' as a scheme

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningι
declarations.doc:
**The immersion `j : T' ⟶ T''`**, whose map on sections is the projection
`𝒪_{T''} ⟶ 𝒪_{T'}`.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningι :
    firstOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ secondOrderThickeningScheme T Y f
declarations.comment: the immersion T' ⟶ T'' of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningιT
declarations.doc:
**The immersion `T ⟶ T''`**: the immersion `T ⟶ T'` followed by `T' ⟶ T''`.  Its map on
sections is `Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningFstProj`, the projection `𝒪_{T''} ⟶ 𝒪_T`.
declarations.statement: public def secondOrderThickeningιT : T.scheme ⟶ secondOrderThickeningScheme T Y f
declarations.comment: the immersion T ⟶ T'' of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀₁Hom
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `q₀₁ : T'' ⟶ T'`**, induced by the map `(g, ω) ↦ (g, ω, 0, 0)` of structure
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₀₁Hom :
    secondOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ firstOrderThickeningScheme T Y f
declarations.comment: the morphism q₀₁ : T'' ⟶ T' of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀₂Hom
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `q₀₂ : T'' ⟶ T'`**, induced by the map `(g, ω) ↦ (g, ω, ω, 0)` of structure
sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₀₂Hom :
    secondOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ firstOrderThickeningScheme T Y f
declarations.comment: the morphism q₀₂ : T'' ⟶ T' of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₁₂Hom
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `q₁₂ : T'' ⟶ T'`**, induced by the map
`(g, ω) ↦ (g, d g, ω, d ω)` of structure sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public def secondOrderThickeningQ₁₂Hom :
    secondOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ firstOrderThickeningScheme T Y f
declarations.comment: the morphism q₁₂ : T'' ⟶ T' of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀Hom
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `q₀ : T'' ⟶ T`**, the composite of `q₀₁` with `p₀`; on sections this is the
relation `q₀ = q₀₁ ∘ p₀` of [Stacks, Tag 07J3].
declarations.statement: public def secondOrderThickeningQ₀Hom : secondOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ T.scheme
declarations.comment: the morphism q₀ : T'' ⟶ T of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₁Hom
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `q₁ : T'' ⟶ T`**, the composite of `q₀₁` with `p₁`; on sections this is the
relation `q₁ = q₀₁ ∘ p₁`.
declarations.statement: public def secondOrderThickeningQ₁Hom : secondOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ T.scheme
declarations.comment: the morphism q₁ : T'' ⟶ T of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₂Hom
declarations.doc:
**The morphism `q₂ : T'' ⟶ T`**, the composite of `q₁₂` with `p₁`; on sections this is the
relation `q₂ = q₁₂ ∘ p₁`.
declarations.statement: public def secondOrderThickeningQ₂Hom : secondOrderThickeningScheme T Y f ⟶ T.scheme
declarations.comment: the morphism q₂ : T'' ⟶ T of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningQ₀Hom_eq_Q₀₁_comp_P₀

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningι_isFirstOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**`T' ⟶ T''` is a first-order thickening of schemes**: its ideal sheaf has square zero,
because the kernel of `𝒪_{T''} ⟶ 𝒪_{T'}` over every open is the square-zero ideal
`K = 0 ⊕ 0 ⊕ Ω_{T/Y,δ} ⊕ Ω²_{T/Y,δ}`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningι_isFirstOrderThickening :
    Stacks.Thickenings.IsFirstOrderThickening (secondOrderThickeningι T Y f)
declarations.comment: T' ⟶ T'' is a first-order thickening of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.secondOrderThickeningιT_isNthOrderThickening
declarations.doc:
**`T → T''` is a second-order thickening of schemes**, which is the description of `T''` in
[Stacks, Tag 07J3].  The ideal sheaf of `T ⟶ T''` is the kernel of `𝒪_{T''} ⟶ 𝒪_T`, whose cube
vanishes on every open by `Crystalline.secondOrderThickening_ker_cube`.

The order is *not* obtained by composing the two first-order thickenings `T ⟶ T'` and
`T' ⟶ T''`: a composite of two first-order thickenings is in general only of order three — for
`Z = Spec k[x]/(x⁴)`, the closed subschemes cut out by `(x²)` and by `(x)` give first-order
thickenings whose composite has `(x)³ ≠ 0` — and what makes the order here two is the explicit
vanishing of the cube in the sheaf-level computation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem secondOrderThickeningιT_isNthOrderThickening :
    Stacks.Thickenings.IsNthOrderThickening 2 (secondOrderThickeningιT T Y f)
declarations.comment: T → T'' is a second-order thickening of schemes

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.crysSheafRingMap_q₀₁_add_q₁₂_diffSection
declarations.doc:
**The first formula of [Stacks, Remark 60.14.5, Tag 07J3] on sections over an object.**  On a
section `ω` of the square-zero summand `Ω_{T/S,δ}` of `𝒪_{T'}` the three maps out of `𝒪_{T'}` of
the remark satisfy

`q₀₁^* ω + q₁₂^* ω = q₀₂^* ω + d ω`,

the two-form `d ω` being read in `𝒪_{T''}` through the top summand.  Indeed
`q₀₁ (0, ω) = (0, ω, 0, 0)`, `q₁₂ (0, ω) = (0, 0, ω, d ω)` and `q₀₂ (0, ω) = (0, ω, ω, 0)`.  This
is the identity `q₀₁^* ω + q₁₂^* ω - q₀₂^* ω = d ω` that the proof of [Stacks, Tag 07J6] reads off
the remark.
declarations.statement:
theorem crysSheafRingMap_q₀₁_add_q₁₂_diffSection (A : Thickening S)
    (ω : crysDiffSections A) :
    crysSheafRingMap (secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₀₁ S A)
          (firstOrderThickeningDiffSection A ω) +
        crysSheafRingMap (secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₁₂ S A)
          (firstOrderThickeningDiffSection A ω) =
      crysSheafRingMap (secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₀₂ S A)
          (firstOrderThickeningDiffSection A ω) +
        secondOrderTopSection A (crysDeRham A ω)
declarations.comment: the first formula of the remark on the sections over an object: on a section of the square-zero summand of 𝒪_{T'}, q₀₁ + q₁₂ = q₀₂ + d, the two-form d ω being read through the top summand Ω² of 𝒪_{T''}

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.crysSheafRingMap_q₁₂_mul_q₀₁_diffSection
declarations.doc:
**The second formula of [Stacks, Remark 60.14.5, Tag 07J3] on sections over an object.**  The
product in `𝒪_{T''}` of a section of the square-zero summand of `𝒪_{T'}` read through `q₁₂` with
one read through `q₀₁` is their exterior product, in the other order:

`q₁₂^* ω · q₀₁^* ω' = ω' ∧ ω`.
declarations.statement:
theorem crysSheafRingMap_q₁₂_mul_q₀₁_diffSection (A : Thickening S)
    (ω ω' : crysDiffSections A) :
    crysSheafRingMap (secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₁₂ S A)
          (firstOrderThickeningDiffSection A ω) *
        crysSheafRingMap (secondOrderThickeningSiteQ₀₁ S A)
          (firstOrderThickeningDiffSection A ω') =
      secondOrderTopSection A (crysWedgeSections A ω' ω)
declarations.comment: the second formula of the remark on the sections over an object: the product in 𝒪_{T''} of a differential read through q₁₂ with one read through q₀₁ is their exterior product in the other order, read through the top summand Ω²

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.crysDeRhamNatSheafComplex
declarations.doc:
**The de Rham complex `𝒪_{X/S} → Ω¹_{X/S} → Ω²_{X/S} → ⋯` of abelian sheaves on the small
crystalline site `Cris(X/S)`**, at the coefficient universe `u + 1`: the termwise sheafification
of the de Rham complex of abelian presheaves `crysDeRhamCochainComplex`, whose differentials are
the de Rham differentials of [Stacks, Tag 07HY] built from the universal `S`-derivation `d_{X/S}`.
Its degree-`i` term is the sheaf `Ω^i_{X/S} = ∧^i_{𝒪_{X/S}} Ω_{X/S}` (`crysFormsSheaf`), by
`crysDeRhamNatSheafComplexXIso`, and its degree-zero term is `𝒪_{X/S}`, by
`crysDeRhamNatSheafComplexXZeroIso`.
declarations.statement:
def crysDeRhamNatSheafComplex :
    CochainComplex (Sheaf (smallTopology S) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) ℕ
declarations.comment: the de Rham complex 𝒪_{X/S} → Ω¹_{X/S} → Ω²_{X/S} → ⋯ of abelian sheaves on Cris(X/S); its terms are the sheaves Ω^i_{X/S} = crysFormsSheaf S i (crysDeRhamNatSheafComplexXIso), its degree-zero term is 𝒪_{X/S} (crysDeRhamNatSheafComplexXZeroIso), and its differential is the unique map of sheaves extending the de Rham differential of local sections (toCrysFormsSheafULift_comp_crysDeRhamNatSheafDifferential, crysDeRhamNatSheafDifferential_unique)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.crysFormsSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules `Ω^j_{X/S}` on the small crystalline site**, the sheaf
associated with the presheaf `Ω^j_{X/S} = ⋀^j Ω_{X/S}` (`toCrysFormsSheaf`), with its sections in
`Type u`.  It is the shrinking of the sheafification `crysFormsSheafULift` taken at the module
universe `u + 1`, whose sections are `u`-small (`small_crysFormsSheafULift_obj`).

This is the sheaf `Ω^j_{X/S} = ∧^j_{𝒪_{X/S}} Ω_{X/S}` of [Stacks, Tag 07J4]: by [Stacks, Tag 01CG]
the exterior power of a sheaf of modules is the sheafification of the sectionwise exterior power,
and the sheaf `Ω_{X/S}` is the sheafification of the presheaf of crystalline differentials, whose
sectionwise exterior power has the same sheafification.  The de Rham complex of sheaves built on
it is `crysDeRhamNatSheafComplex` of `SmallSite/DeRhamComplexSheaf.lean`.
declarations.statement: def crysFormsSheaf (j : ℕ) : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)
declarations.comment: Ω^j_{X/S} = ∧^j_{𝒪_{X/S}} Ω_{X/S}, the sheaf of 𝒪_{X/S}-modules on Cris(X/S): the sheafification of the sectionwise exterior power (Tag 01CG); toCrysFormsSheaf is the canonical map from the presheaf of forms, locally injective and locally surjective

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.crystalConnectionCris
declarations.doc:
**The canonical connection of a crystal, as a morphism of abelian sheaves
`∇ : F ⟶ F ⊗_{𝒪_{X/S}} Ω_{X/S}` on `Cris(X/S)`.**  On the ambient scheme `T` of every object it
is the connection `p₁^* s - p₀^* s`, read through `(F ⊗ Ω_{X/S})_T = F_T ⊗ Ω_{T/S,δ}`
(`crystalConnectionCrisApp_restrict`).
declarations.statement: def crystalConnectionCris : abelianSheaf F ⟶ tensorDifferentialFormsSheaf F 1
declarations.comment: the canonical connection ∇ : F ⟶ F ⊗_{𝒪_{X/S}} Ω_{X/S} of a crystal F on Cris(X/S), a morphism of abelian sheaves: on every T it is p₁^* s - p₀^* s on the first-order thickening T' of 07J2, read through (F ⊗ Ω_{X/S})_T = F_T ⊗ Ω_{T/S,δ}

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.crystalConnectionCris_isIntegrableConnection
declarations.doc:
**A crystal `F` in `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `Cris(X/S)` comes equipped with a canonical integrable
connection.**  The connection is
`∇ = crystalConnectionCris : F ⟶ F ⊗_{𝒪_{X/S}} Ω_{X/S}`, a morphism of abelian sheaves on
`Cris(X/S)`, and

1. (**it is a connection**) `∇(f s) = f ∇(s) + s ⊗ d f` for every object `A` and all sections `f`
   of `𝒪_{X/S}` and `s` of `F` over `A`;
2. (**it is the canonical one**) on the ambient scheme `T` of every object, `∇(s)` is
   `p₁^* s - p₀^* s` on the first-order thickening `T'` of [Stacks, Tag 07J2], read in
   `F_T ⊗ Ω_{T/S,δ} ⊂ F_{T'}`;
3. the exterior product by a one-form is `(x ⊗ η) ∧ ω = x ⊗ (η ∧ ω)` on local pure tensors, and
   the extension `crystalExtensionCris : F ⊗ Ω_{X/S} ⟶ F ⊗ Ω²_{X/S}` is given by the rule
   `∇(s ⊗ ω) = ∇(s) ∧ ω + s ⊗ d ω` of [Stacks, Tag 07I0] and [Stacks, Section 60.15, Tag 07J5];
4. (**it is integrable**) `∇ ∘ ∇ = 0 : F ⟶ F ⊗ Ω²_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem crystalConnectionCris_isIntegrableConnection (hF : IsSheafCrystal F) :
    ((∀ (A : CrystallineThickening S) (f : crysFormRing S A) (s : F.val.obj (op A)),
        (show tensorFormsModSec F 1 A from
          (crystalConnectionCris hF).hom.app (op A) (ULift.up (f • s))) =
          f • (show tensorFormsModSec F 1 A from
            (crystalConnectionCris hF).hom.app (op A) (ULift.up s)) +
          (show tensorFormsModSec F 1 A from
            (CategoryTheory.toSheafify (smallTopology S) (tensorDifferentialFormsPresheaf F 1)).app
              (op A) (ULift.up (formsTmul F s (formsD A f))))) ∧
      ∀ (A : CrystallineThickening S) (s : (abelianSheaf F).obj.obj (op A)),
        (firstOrderTensorInclusion F A).val.app (op ⊤)
            ((tensorFormsAmbientIsoOne A).hom.app (op ⊤)
              ((tensorDifferentialFormsSheaf F 1).obj.map (A.restrictOpenHom ⊤).op
                ((crystalConnectionCris hF).hom.app (op A) s))).down =
          crystalConnectionRaw F A ⊤ (F.val.map (A.restrictOpenHom ⊤).op s.down)) ∧
    ((∀ (A : CrystallineThickening S) (ω : (crysDifferentialForms S 1).obj (op A))
          (x : F.val.obj (op A)) (η : (crysDifferentialForms S 1).obj (op A)),
        crystalWedgeCrisApp F A ω
            ((CategoryTheory.toSheafify (smallTopology S) (tensorDifferentialFormsPresheaf F 1)).app
              (op A) (ULift.up (formsTmul F x η))) =
          (CategoryTheory.toSheafify (smallTopology S) (tensorDifferentialFormsPresheaf F 2)).app
            (op A) (ULift.up (formsTmul F x (formsWedgeOne η ω)))) ∧
      (∀ (A : CrystallineThickening S) (s : F.val.obj (op A))
          (ω : (crysDifferentialForms S 1).obj (op A)),
        (crystalExtensionCris hF).hom.app (op A)
            ((CategoryTheory.toSheafify (smallTopology S) (tensorDifferentialFormsPresheaf F 1)).app
              (op A) (ULift.up (formsTmul F s ω))) =
          crystalWedgeCrisApp F A ω ((crystalConnectionCris hF).hom.app (op A) (ULift.up s)) +
            (show (tensorDifferentialFormsSheaf F 2).obj.obj (op A) from
              (CategoryTheory.toSheafify (smallTopology S)
                (tensorDifferentialFormsPresheaf F 2)).app
                  (op A) (ULift.up (formsTmul F s (formsDeRham A ω))))) ∧
      crystalConnectionCris hF ≫ crystalExtensionCris hF = 0)
declarations.comment: a crystal F on Cris(X/S) has a canonical integrable connection: ∇ = crystalConnectionCris : F ⟶ F ⊗ Ω_{X/S}, a morphism of abelian sheaves, satisfies the Leibniz rule, is p₁^* s - p₀^* s on every T, its extension F ⊗ Ω ⟶ F ⊗ Ω² obeys ∇(s ⊗ ω) = ∇(s) ∧ ω + s ⊗ d ω, and ∇ ∘ ∇ = 0

declarations.doc:
The `p`-adically completed divided power envelope of the kernel of a
surjective polynomial presentation of `C` over `A`.

declarations.name: Crystalline.pAdicCompletedDividedPowerDifferentials
declarations.doc:

declarations.name: Crystalline.pAdicCompletedDividedPowerDifferentialsEquivLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07J9, the first identification.** `Ω_D = lim_e Ω_{D_e/A, γ̄}`: the completed module
of divided power differentials is the inverse limit of the modules of divided power
differentials of the finite levels `D_e`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def pAdicCompletedDividedPowerDifferentialsEquivLimit
    (s : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v}) {ι : Type w}
    (f : MvPolynomial ι s.A →ₐ[s.A] s.C) :
    pAdicCompletedDividedPowerDifferentials s f ≃+
      ((limit (QuotientDifferentialsSystem.functor (A := s.A)
          (polynomialDividedPowerEnvelopeRing s f).ideal
          (polynomialDividedPowerEnvelopeRing s f).dividedPowers s.p
          (presentationDifferentialsCompletionComparison s f).quotientSystem) :
        AddCommGrpCat) : Type (max u w))
declarations.comment: the inverse limit over the finite levels

declarations.name: Crystalline.pAdicCompletedDividedPowerDifferentialsEquivCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07J9, the second identification.** `Ω_D = lim_e Ω_{D/A, γ̄}/p^eΩ_{D/A, γ̄}`: the
completed module of divided power differentials is also the `p`-adic completion of the module
of divided power differentials of the completed envelope `D` itself.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def pAdicCompletedDividedPowerDifferentialsEquivCompletion
    (s : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v}) {ι : Type w}
    (f : MvPolynomial ι s.A →ₐ[s.A] s.C) :
    pAdicCompletedDividedPowerDifferentials s f ≃+
      AdicCompletion
        (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal
          (A := AdicCompletion
            (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := polynomialDividedPowerEnvelopeRing s f) s.p)
            (polynomialDividedPowerEnvelopeRing s f)) s.p)
        (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := s.A)
          (DividedPowers.completedDividedPowers (polynomialDividedPowerEnvelopeRing s f).ideal
            (polynomialDividedPowerEnvelopeRing s f).dividedPowers s.p
            (polynomialDividedPowerEnvelope_prime_nilpotent s f)).1)
declarations.comment: the p-adic completion of the differentials of the completed envelope

declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_dividedPowerDifferentialsCompletionEquiv
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a ring map, let `(J, δ)` be a divided power structure on `B`, let `p` be
prime, let `A` be a `ℤ_(p)`-algebra and let `p` be nilpotent in `B / J`.  Then
`lim_e Ω_{B_e/A, δ̄} = lim_e Ω_{B/A, δ} / pᵉ Ω_{B/A, δ}
  = lim_e Ω_{B^∧/A, δ^∧} / pᵉ Ω_{B^∧/A, δ^∧}`.

The conclusion is written out here, with no reference to
`Crystalline.DifferentialsCompletionComparison`.  Beyond a level `N`, each `pᵉ B` lies in `J` and
is stable under the divided powers of `δ` (`level`), so `B_e = B / pᵉ B` carries divided powers
`δ̄` and the modules `Ω_{B_e/A, δ̄} = Crystalline.quotientDifferentials ..` form an inverse system
whose transition maps are those induced on universal differentials (`transition`, and the first
conjunct).  The second and third limits are Mathlib's `AdicCompletion`s of `Ω_{B/A, δ}` and of
`Ω_{B^∧/A, δ^∧}`; `fromOriginal` and `fromCompletion` identify every level of their towers of
quotients with that system, compatibly with all three families of transition maps, which is the
first equality in the strong form of an isomorphism of inverse systems.  `limitEquiv` is the
isomorphism of the second limit with the third that results, and the last conjunct says its
component at each level `N + e` is `fromOriginal` followed by the inverse of `fromCompletion`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_dividedPowerDifferentialsCompletionEquiv
    [Fact p.Prime] [Algebra (DividedPowers.IntegersAtPrime p) A]
    (hp : IsNilpotent (Ideal.Quotient.mk J (p : B))) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ)
      (level : ∀ e, N ≤ e → (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p ^ e ≤ J) ∧
        delta.IsSubDPIdeal (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p ^ e))
      (transition : ∀ e e' : ℕ, e ≤ e' →
        quotientDifferentials (A := A) J delta p (N + e')
            (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e')).1 (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e')).2 →+
          quotientDifferentials (A := A) J delta p (N + e)
            (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).1 (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).2)
      (fromOriginal : ∀ e : ℕ, differentialsModPow (A := A) J delta p (N + e) ≃ₗ[B]
        quotientDifferentials (A := A) J delta p (N + e)
          (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).1 (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).2)
      (fromCompletion : ∀ e : ℕ,
        completedDifferentialsModPow (A := A) J delta p hp (N + e) ≃+
          quotientDifferentials (A := A) J delta p (N + e)
            (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).1 (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).2)
      (limitEquiv : AdicCompletion (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p)
            (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) delta) ≃+
          AdicCompletion
            (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal
              (A := AdicCompletion (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p) B) p)
            (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A)
              (DividedPowers.completedDividedPowers J delta p hp).1)),
      (∀ (e e' : ℕ) (h : e ≤ e') (b : B),
          transition e e' h
              (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A)
                (DividedPowers.quotientDividedPowers J delta p (N + e')
                  (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e')).1 (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e')).2)
                (Ideal.Quotient.mk (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p ^ (N + e')) b)) =
            dividedPowerDifferential (A := A)
              (DividedPowers.quotientDividedPowers J delta p (N + e)
                (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).1 (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).2)
              (Ideal.Quotient.mk (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p ^ (N + e)) b)) ∧
      (∀ (e : ℕ) (b : B),
          fromOriginal e
              (Submodule.Quotient.mk (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A) delta b)) =
            dividedPowerDifferential (A := A)
              (DividedPowers.quotientDividedPowers J delta p (N + e)
                (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).1 (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).2)
              (Ideal.Quotient.mk (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p ^ (N + e)) b)) ∧
      (∀ (e e' : ℕ) (h : e ≤ e')
          (omega : differentialsModPow (A := A) J delta p (N + e')),
          transition e e' h (fromOriginal e' omega) =
            fromOriginal e
              (AdicCompletion.transitionMap (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p)
                (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) delta)
                (Nat.add_le_add_left h N) omega)) ∧
      (∀ (e : ℕ) (b : AdicCompletion (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p) B),
          fromCompletion e
              (Submodule.Quotient.mk
                (dividedPowerDifferential (A := A)
                  (DividedPowers.completedDividedPowers J delta p hp).1 b)) =
            dividedPowerDifferential (A := A)
              (DividedPowers.quotientDividedPowers J delta p (N + e)
                (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).1 (level _ (Nat.le_add_right N e)).2)
              (AdicCompletion.evalₐ (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p) (N + e) b)) ∧
      (∀ (e : ℕ) (b : AdicCompletion (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p) B)
          (omega : completedDifferentialsModPow (A := A) J delta p hp (N + e)),
          fromCompletion e (b • omega) =
            AdicCompletion.evalₐ (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p) (N + e) b •
              fromCompletion e omega) ∧
      (∀ (e e' : ℕ) (h : e ≤ e')
          (omega : completedDifferentialsModPow (A := A) J delta p hp (N + e')),
          transition e e' h (fromCompletion e' omega) =
            fromCompletion e
              (AdicCompletion.transitionMap
                (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal
                  (A := AdicCompletion (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p) B) p)
                (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A)
                  (DividedPowers.completedDividedPowers J delta p hp).1)
                (Nat.add_le_add_left h N) omega)) ∧
      (∀ (e : ℕ) (omega : AdicCompletion (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p)
            (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) delta)),
          fromCompletion e
              (AdicCompletion.eval
                (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal
                  (A := AdicCompletion (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p) B) p)
                (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A)
                  (DividedPowers.completedDividedPowers J delta p hp).1)
                (N + e) (limitEquiv omega)) =
            fromOriginal e
              (AdicCompletion.eval (DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := B) p)
                (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) delta) (N + e) omega))
declarations.comment: the identification of the inverse limits that defines Ω_D, the case B = D

declarations.name: Crystalline.completedDividedPowerDifferential
declarations.doc:
The universal divided power derivation of the completed envelope, characterized
on the dense image of the original envelope.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def completedDividedPowerDifferential
    (s : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v}) {ι : Type w}
    (f : MvPolynomial ι s.A →ₐ[s.A] s.C) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    let env := polynomialDividedPowerEnvelope s f
    let E := env.object
    letI : Algebra s.A E := env.structureMap.toRingHom.toAlgebra
    let P := DividedPowers.pAdicIdeal (A := E) s.p
    let Ω := AdicCompletion P (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := s.A) E.dividedPowers)
    Σ' hp : IsNilpotent (Ideal.Quotient.mk E.ideal (s.p : E)),
      let D := DividedPowerRing.of
        (pAdicCompletedDividedPowerEnvelope s f hf)
        (DividedPowers.completionIdeal E.ideal s.p hp)
        (DividedPowers.completedDividedPowers E.ideal E.dividedPowers s.p hp).1
      letI : Algebra s.A D :=
        ((algebraMap E D).comp env.structureMap.toRingHom).toAlgebra
      { d : DividedPowerDerivation s.A D (algebraMap s.A D) Ω //
        ∀ b : E, d (algebraMap E D b) =
          AdicCompletion.of P (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := s.A) E.dividedPowers)
            (dividedPowerDifferential (A := s.A) E.dividedPowers b) }

declarations.name: Crystalline.instIsAdicCompleteCompletedDividedPowerRing

This is item (07JB) of [Stacks, Lemma 60.17.3, Tag 07JG] for the module `M = D` over itself, the
case of the coefficient sheaf `𝒪_{X/S}`.  Mathlib's `AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete_self` proves

`Crystalline.pAdicIdeal_map_ringHom` identifies that extension with the ideal `(p) ⊆ D`; the
finite generation it asks of `(p) ⊆ B` is `Submodule.fg_span_singleton`.
declarations.comment: item (07JB) for the module `M = D` over the completed divided power ring itself

`∇ m = ∑ θ_i m ⬝ d x_i`, for every `m` only finitely many pairs `(i, k)` with `k ≥ 1` satisfy

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.pairTensorLevel_crystalPairFunctor_nabla
declarations.doc:
**The connection `∇` of the pair attached to a crystal is obtained by evaluating the canonical
connection of [Stacks, Tag 07J6] on the finite thickenings.**  For a crystal `ℱ` in quasi-coherent
`𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `Cris(X/S)`, an element `m` of `M = lim_e Γ((X, T_e, δ̄), ℱ)` and a level
`e`, the image of `∇(m) ∈ M ⊗̂_D Ω_D` in `Γ(T_e, Ω_{T_e/S,δ̄}) ⊗_{Γ(T_e, 𝒪)} Γ(T_e, ℱ)` is the
canonical connection of `ℱ` on the sections over `(X, T_e, δ̄)`, applied to the image of `m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pairTensorLevel_crystalPairFunctor_nabla (Fc : QuasiCoherentCrystal S) (e : ℕ)
    (m : wholeSpaceSections hp Fc ⦋0⦌) :
    pairTensorLevel hp Fc e (((crystalPairFunctor hp).obj Fc).nabla m) =
      AffineConnection.connection (bijective_crysExtensionSectionsMap_levelObj hp Fc e)
        (pairComponent hp Fc e m)
declarations.comment: for any surjective polynomial presentation g : A[x_i : i ∈ ι] → C, supplied as the WholeSpacePresentation instance (the default instance is the tautological one): the connection of the pair attached to a crystal is the canonical connection of 07J6 evaluated on the finite thickenings (X, T_e, δ̄): its image at each level e is the 07J6 connection of the crystal over T_e applied to the image of m

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.firstOrderTensorInclusion_crystalConnection_crystalPairFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The connection `∇` of the pair attached to a crystal is obtained by evaluating the
sheaf-level canonical connection of [Stacks, Tag 07J6] on the finite thickenings.**  For a crystal
`ℱ` in quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `Cris(X/S)`, an element `m` of
`M = lim_e Γ((X, T_e, δ̄), ℱ)` and a level `e`, the canonical connection
`∇ : ℱ_{T_e} ⟶ ℱ_{T_e} ⊗ Ω_{T_e/S,δ̄}` of `...SmallSite.crystalConnection`, applied to the image
of `m` over the whole of `T_e` and read in the sections of `ℱ` over the first-order thickening
`T'_e` through the canonical morphism `ℱ_{T_e} ⊗ Ω ⟶ p₀_* ℱ_{T'_e}`, is the image of `∇(m)` at
the level `e` read there through the canonical map `ω ⊗ s ↦ ω · p₀^* s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem firstOrderTensorInclusion_crystalConnection_crystalPairFunctor
    (Fc : QuasiCoherentCrystal S) (e : ℕ) (m : wholeSpaceSections hp Fc ⦋0⦌) :
    (firstOrderTensorInclusion Fc.obj (levelObj hp 0 e)).val.app (op ⊤)
        ((crystalConnection (levelObj hp 0 e) Fc.property.2).hom.app (op ⊤)
          (crysSiteRestrict Fc.obj ((levelObj hp 0 e).restrictOpenHom ⊤)
            (show Fc.obj.val.obj (op (levelObj hp 0 e)) from pairComponent hp Fc e m))) =
      crysSiteRestrict Fc.obj
        ((firstOrderThickeningCrysObject S (levelObj hp 0 e)).restrictOpenHom ⊤)
        (AffineConnection.diffAction Fc.obj (levelObj hp 0 e)
          (pairTensorLevel hp Fc e (((crystalPairFunctor hp).obj Fc).nabla m)))
declarations.comment: for any surjective polynomial presentation g : A[x_i : i ∈ ι] → C, supplied as the WholeSpacePresentation instance (the default instance is the tautological one): the connection of the pair attached to a crystal is the sheaf-level canonical connection of 07J6 evaluated on the finite thickenings (X, T_e, δ̄), level by level

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.crystalPairFunctor
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Lemma 60.17.3, Tag 07JG]: the functor**

`{crystals in quasi-coherent 𝒪_{X/S}-modules on Cris(X/S)} ⟶ {pairs (M, ∇) satisfying (07JB),
(07JC), (07JD) and (07JE)}`,

in the situation of [Stacks, Section 60.17, Tag 07J7]: `X = Spec(C)`, `S = Spec(A)` affine with
`p` nilpotent on `C`, `P = A[x_i : i ∈ ι] → C` any surjective polynomial presentation (the
instance `...SmallSite.WholeSpacePresentation S hp` the system of thickenings is built from; by
default `A[x_c : c ∈ C] → C`), `D` the `p`-adically completed divided power envelope (07J8),
`Ω_D` its completed module of divided power differentials (07J9) and `d : D → Ω_D` (07JA).  It
sends a crystal `ℱ` to `M = lim_e Γ((X, T_e, δ̄), ℱ)` with the connection read off the crystal's
Taylor expansion over `D(1)`, and a morphism of crystals to the induced map of the limits.  That
this connection is the canonical connection of [Stacks, Tag 07J6] evaluated on the finite
thickenings `(X, T_e, δ̄)` is `...SmallSite.pairTensorLevel_crystalPairFunctor_nabla` and
`...SmallSite.firstOrderTensorInclusion_crystalConnection_crystalPairFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
def crystalPairFunctor :
    QuasiCoherentCrystal S ⥤ Pair.{u, u, u, u} S.p (pairRing hp) (pairForms hp) (pairDx hp)
      (derivationFun ((affineSituation S hp).A : Type u) (pairRing hp) _ (pairForms hp)
        (pairDerivation hp))
declarations.comment: the functor from the crystals in quasi-coherent O_{X/S}-modules on Cris(X/S) to the pairs (M, ∇) satisfying (07JB), (07JC), (07JD) and (07JE), for any surjective polynomial presentation g : P = A[x_i : i ∈ ι] → C, supplied as the WholeSpacePresentation instance (the default instance is the tautological one): M = lim_e Γ(T_e, F), ∇ read off the Taylor expansion of the crystal over D(1); that ∇ is the 07J6 connection evaluated on the T_e is pairTensorLevel_crystalPairFunctor_nabla

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.crystalPairFunctor_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Proposition 60.17.4, Tag 07JH]: the functor of [Stacks, Lemma 60.17.3, Tag 07JG]**

`{crystals in quasi-coherent 𝒪_{X/S}-modules on Cris(X/S)} ⟶ {pairs (M, ∇) satisfying (07JB),
(07JC), (07JD) and (07JE)}`

**is an equivalence of categories.**  This is the functor `...SmallSite.crystalPairFunctor` of
the tag 07JG, in the situation of [Stacks, Section 60.17, Tag 07J7]: `X = Spec(C)`,
`S = Spec(A)` affine with `p` nilpotent on `C`, any surjective polynomial presentation
`P = A[x_i : i ∈ ι] → C` (the instance `...SmallSite.WholeSpacePresentation S hp` the system of
thickenings is built from; by default the tautological `A[x_c : c ∈ C] → C`), `D`
the `p`-adically completed divided power envelope and `Ω_D` its completed module of divided power
differentials.  It sends `ℱ` to `M = lim_e Γ((X, T_e, δ̄), ℱ)` with its specified canonical
crystalline connection: the canonical connection of [Stacks, Tag 07J6] evaluated on the finite
thickenings `(X, T_e, δ̄)`, which is
`...SmallSite.pairTensorLevel_crystalPairFunctor_nabla`.
declarations.statement: theorem crystalPairFunctor_isEquivalence : (crystalPairFunctor hp).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: for any surjective polynomial presentation g : P = A[x_i : i ∈ ι] → C, supplied as the WholeSpacePresentation instance (the default instance is the tautological one): the functor of 07JG, from the crystals in quasi-coherent O_{X/S}-modules on Cris(X/S) to the pairs (M, ∇) over D satisfying (07JB), (07JC), (07JD) and (07JE), with its connection the canonical connection of 07J6 evaluated on the finite thickenings (pairTensorLevel_crystalPairFunctor_nabla), is an equivalence of categories

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.vanishing07JJ_abelianSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be a locally quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the small crystalline site
`Cris(X/S)` of a global crystalline situation. Then for every object `(U, T, δ)` of `Cris(X/S)`
whose ambient divided power scheme `T` is affine, and every `p > 0`, the cohomology of the
localized site vanishes:

`H^p(Cris(X/S)/(U, T, δ), F) = 0`.

The statement is about the abelian sheaf `SmallSite.abelianSheaf F` of the coefficient universe
`u + 1`, which is the universe in which the cohomology of `Cris(X/S)` and of its localizations
exists; the modules of `F` itself live in `Type u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem vanishing07JJ_abelianSheaf (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S))
    (hF : IsLocallyQuasiCoherent F) : Vanishing07JJ S (abelianSheaf F)
declarations.comment: the case of the objects (U, T, δ) whose ambient divided power scheme T is affine, in the packaged form SmallSite.Vanishing07JJ that the consumers of the tag in this library use, and for the abelian sheaf SmallSite.abelianSheaf F of the coefficient universe u + 1 attached to a locally quasi-coherent module F. The source's remaining case of U affine is reduced to this one in isZero_overCohomology_abelianSheaf_of_isAffine, which states both

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.isZero_overCohomology_abelianSheaf_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
Let `F` be a locally quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the small crystalline site
`Cris(X/S)` of a global crystalline situation. Then for every object `(U, T, δ)` of `Cris(X/S)`
with `T` **or** `U` affine, and every `p > 0`, the cohomology of the localized site vanishes:

`H^p(Cris(X/S)/(U, T, δ), F) = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_overCohomology_abelianSheaf_of_isAffine
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S)) (hF : IsLocallyQuasiCoherent F)
    (A : CrystallineThickening S)
    (hA : IsAffine A.obj.thickening.target.scheme ∨ IsAffine A.obj.thickening.source)
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero ((overCohomologyFunctor S A p).obj ((restrictToOver S A).obj (abelianSheaf F)))
declarations.comment: both cases of the hypothesis: the objects (U, T, δ) with T or U affine, for the abelian sheaf SmallSite.abelianSheaf F of the coefficient universe u + 1 attached to a locally quasi-coherent module F

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.chaoticCohomologyComparisonIso
declarations.doc:
In Situation [Stacks, Tag 07MF] with `X` and `S` affine, let
`𝒞 ⊆ Cris(X/S)` be the full subcategory of divided power thickenings `(X, T, δ)` of the whole of
`X` with the chaotic topology of [Stacks, Tag 07GE].  Then for every locally quasi-coherent sheaf
`F` of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `Cris(X/S)` and every degree `j`,

`H^j(𝒞, F|_𝒞) ≅ H^j(Cris(X/S), F)`.

Both sides are read on the abelian sheaf `SmallSite.abelianSheaf F` of the coefficient universe
`u + 1`.
declarations.statement:
def chaoticCohomologyComparisonIso (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf S))
    (hF : IsLocallyQuasiCoherent F) (j : ℕ) :
    (chaoticCohomologyFunctor S j).obj ((restrictToWhole S).obj (abelianSheaf F)) ≅
      (cohomologyFunctor S j).obj (abelianSheaf F)
declarations.comment: for the abelian sheaf SmallSite.abelianSheaf F of the coefficient universe u + 1 attached to a locally quasi-coherent sheaf F of 𝒪_{X/S}-modules, which is the generality in which the input [Stacks, Tag 07JJ] holds

declarations.name: Crystalline.completedCrystallineToposMorphism
declarations.doc:
The morphism of topoi induced by the canonical functor from crystalline
thickenings to completed crystalline thickenings.
declarations.statement:
public def completedCrystallineToposMorphism
    (S : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v}) :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology (CrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} S)ᵒᵖ)
        (Type (max u v (w + 1))))
      (Sheaf (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology (CompletedCrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} S)ᵒᵖ)
        (Type (max u v (w + 1))))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi

declarations.name: Crystalline.abelianSheafPushforwardIsoDirectImage
declarations.doc:
The natural isomorphism identifying the abelian-sheaf pushforward induced by the
crystalline site functor with the right Kan extension used to compute its derived
functors. It comes from the uniqueness of right adjoints, and is an isomorphism of
functors, not merely an objectwise comparison.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def abelianSheafPushforwardIsoDirectImage
    (S : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v}) :
    abelianSheafPushforward S ⋙
        (completedAbelianSheafEquivalence.{u, v, w} S).functor ≅
      (abelianSheafEquivalence.{u, v, w} S).functor ⋙ abelianDirectImage S
declarations.comment: identification of the abelian direct image

declarations.name: Crystalline.abelianSheafPushforwardForgetIsoPushforward
declarations.doc:
The natural isomorphism exhibiting the abelian-sheaf direct image, on underlying
sets, as the direct image of the same morphism of topoi. It comes from the uniqueness
of right adjoints, and is natural in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def abelianSheafPushforwardForgetIsoPushforward
    (S : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v}) :
    abelianSheafPushforward S ⋙
        sheafForget
          (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology (CompletedCrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} S)ᵒᵖ) ≅
      sheafForget
          (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology (CrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} S)ᵒᵖ) ⋙
        (completedCrystallineToposMorphism S).pushforward
declarations.comment: compatibility with the geometric morphism

declarations.name: Crystalline.abelianDirectImageObjObjIsoLimitFiniteLevelSections
declarations.doc:
**The direct image of [Stacks, Tag 07JL], computed.** For an abelian presheaf `F` on the
ordinary affine crystalline category and a finite-level system `T` for a completed thickening
`X`, the value at `X` of the direct image of `F` is the inverse limit of the sections of `F` on
the finite-level quotients of `X`:
`g_*(F)(X) ≅ lim_e F(X/(p)^(N + e))`.

The direct image is the right Kan extension along `crystallineToCompleted`, whose value at `X`
is the limit over the structured-arrow category, and the finite-level diagram is initial there
by `Crystalline.finiteLevel_initial`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def abelianDirectImageObjObjIsoLimitFiniteLevelSections
    {S : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v}}
    (F : CrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} S ⥤ Ab.{max u v (w + 1)})
    {X : CompletedCrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} S} (T : FiniteLevelSystem X) :
    ((abelianDirectImage S).obj F).obj X ≅ limit (finiteLevelSections T F)
declarations.comment: the direct image computed as the limit over the finite levels

declarations.name: Crystalline.abelianSheafPushforwardObjObjIsoLimitFiniteLevelSections
declarations.doc:
**The sections of the direct image of [Stacks, Tag 07JL].** The value at a completed
thickening `X` of the direct image of an abelian sheaf `F` on the ordinary affine crystalline
site is the inverse limit of the sections of `F` on the finite-level quotients of `X`.

This is `Crystalline.abelianDirectImageObjObjIsoLimitFiniteLevelSections` transported along
`Crystalline.abelianSheafPushforwardIsoDirectImage`, so that it speaks about the
site-theoretic pushforward rather than the right Kan extension.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def abelianSheafPushforwardObjObjIsoLimitFiniteLevelSections
    (S : AffineCrystallineSituation.{u, v})
    (F : Sheaf (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology (CrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} S)ᵒᵖ)
      Ab.{max u v (w + 1)})
    {X : CompletedCrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} S} (T : FiniteLevelSystem X) :
    ((completedAbelianSheafEquivalence.{u, v, w} S).functor.obj
        ((abelianSheafPushforward S).obj F)).obj X ≅
      limit (finiteLevelSections T
        ((abelianSheafEquivalence.{u, v, w} S).functor.obj F))
declarations.comment: the sections of the direct image as the limit over the finite levels

declarations.name: Crystalline.rightDerivedPushforwardSectionsIsoRightDerivedLimit
declarations.doc:
For an abelian sheaf `𝓖` on `𝒞 = (Cris(C/A))ᵒᵖ`, a completed thickening `B` and every degree
`p`, the sections over `B` of the `p`-th higher direct image of `𝓖` along the morphism of topoi
`g : Sh(𝒞) ⟶ Sh(𝒞^∧)` are the `p`-th derived inverse limit of the sections of `𝓖` on the finite
levels of `B`:

`R ᵖ g_* 𝓖 (B) ≅ R ᵖ lim_e 𝓖(B/(p)^{N + e})`.
declarations.statement:
def rightDerivedPushforwardSectionsIsoRightDerivedLimit
    (𝓖 : Sheaf (littleChaoticTopology.{u, v, w} s) Ab.{max u v (w + 1)})
    (B : CompletedCrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} s) (p : ℕ) :
    ((completedAbelianSheafEquivalence.{u, v, w} s).functor.obj
        (((abelianSheafPushforward.{u, v, w} s).rightDerived p).obj 𝓖)).obj B ≅
      ((lim : Rlim.InvSystemAb.{max u v (w + 1)} ⥤ Ab.{max u v (w + 1)}).rightDerived p).obj
        (finiteLevelSections (uniformLevelSystem B)
          ((abelianSheafEquivalence.{u, v, w} s).functor.obj 𝓖))
declarations.comment: the higher direct images as the derived limits over the finite levels

declarations.name: Crystalline.rightDerivedOnePushforwardSectionsIsoRightDerivedOneLimit
declarations.doc:
`R ¹ g_* 𝓖 (B) ≅ R ¹ lim_e 𝓖(B_e)`: for an abelian sheaf `𝓖` on `𝒞 = (Cris(C/A))ᵒᵖ` and a
completed thickening `B`, the sections over `B` of the first higher direct image of `𝓖` along the
morphism of topoi `g : Sh(𝒞) ⟶ Sh(𝒞^∧)` are the first derived inverse limit of the inverse system
`e ↦ 𝓖(B/(p)^{N + e})` of sections on the finite levels of `B`.
declarations.statement:
def rightDerivedOnePushforwardSectionsIsoRightDerivedOneLimit
    (𝓖 : Sheaf (littleChaoticTopology.{u, v, w} s) Ab.{max u v (w + 1)})
    (B : CompletedCrystallineThickening.{u, v, w} s) :
    ((completedAbelianSheafEquivalence.{u, v, w} s).functor.obj
        (((abelianSheafPushforward.{u, v, w} s).rightDerived 1).obj 𝓖)).obj B ≅
      ((lim : Rlim.InvSystemAb.{max u v (w + 1)} ⥤ Ab.{max u v (w + 1)}).rightDerived 1).obj
        (finiteLevelSections (uniformLevelSystem B)
          ((abelianSheafEquivalence.{u, v, w} s).functor.obj 𝓖))
declarations.comment: the first higher direct image as the first derived limit over the finite levels

declarations.name: Crystalline.isZero_rightDerived_abelianSheafPushforward_of_two_le
declarations.doc:
`R ᵖ g_* 𝓖 = 0` for every `p ≥ 2` and every abelian sheaf `𝓖` on `𝒞 = (Cris(C/A))ᵒᵖ`, where
`g_*` is the direct image `Crystalline.abelianSheafPushforward` of the morphism of topoi
`g : Sh(𝒞) ⟶ Sh(𝒞^∧)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_abelianSheafPushforward_of_two_le
    (𝓖 : Sheaf (littleChaoticTopology.{u, v, w} s) Ab.{max u v (w + 1)})
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 2 ≤ p) :
    IsZero (((abelianSheafPushforward.{u, v, w} s).rightDerived p).obj 𝓖)
declarations.comment: the vanishing of the higher direct images in degrees at least two

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.derivedGlobalSectionsIsoPowerCechComplexExtend
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07JM.** Let `𝒞` carry the chaotic topology, let `X` be an object of
`𝒞` to which every object of `𝒞` admits a morphism, and let `𝒞` have products of pairs. For every
abelian sheaf `𝓕` on `𝒞` the total cohomology `RΓ(𝒞, 𝓕)` is represented by the complex
`𝓕(X) → 𝓕(X × X) → 𝓕(X × X × X) → ⋯` associated to the cosimplicial abelian group
`[n] ↦ 𝓕(X^{n + 1})`.

This is the comparison itself, an isomorphism of complexes of abelian groups between
`RΓ(𝒞, 𝓕)` and that complex placed in the nonnegative degrees. An isomorphism of complexes is
sent to an isomorphism of `D(Ab)` by the localisation functor, which is
`Stacks.Cohomology.derivedGlobalSectionsQIsoPowerCechComplexExtend`, and to the isomorphism of
cohomology groups in each degree, which is
`Stacks.Cohomology.sheafHAddEquivPowerCechComplexHomology`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.derivedGlobalSectionsQIsoPowerCechComplexExtend
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07JM**, in the derived category of abelian groups: on the chaotic site
with a covering object `X` and products of pairs, `RΓ(𝒞, 𝓕)` and the complex
`𝓕(X) → 𝓕(X × X) → 𝓕(X × X × X) → ⋯` become isomorphic in `D(Ab)`.

This is `Stacks.Cohomology.derivedGlobalSectionsIsoPowerCechComplexExtend` read through the
localisation functor `CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.Q`. The instance
`HasDerivedCategory.{w} AddCommGrpCat.{u}` only chooses a model of `D(Ab)` with morphisms in a
given universe; one always exists, by `CategoryTheory.HasDerivedCategory.standard`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsQIsoPowerCechComplexExtend
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} AddCommGrpCat.{u}] :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj (chaoticDerivedGlobalSections X hX F) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((powerCechComplex F.obj X).extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.sheafHAddEquivPowerCechComplexHomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07JM** in degree `n`: the cohomology `H^n(𝒞, 𝓕)` of the chaotic site
is the degree-`n` cohomology of the complex `𝓕(X) → 𝓕(X × X) → 𝓕(X × X × X) → ⋯`.

This is `H^n` of `Stacks.Cohomology.derivedGlobalSectionsIsoPowerCechComplexExtend`, the
cohomology of `RΓ(𝒞, 𝓕)` being `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H` by
`CategoryTheory.ProjectiveResolution.extAddEquivCohomologyClass`. It is the map whose existence
`Stacks.Cohomology.nonempty_addEquiv_sheafH_homology_powerCechComplex` asserts.
declarations.statement:
def sheafHAddEquivPowerCechComplexHomology
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology C) AddCommGrpCat.{u})] (n : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H F n ≃+ (powerCechComplex F.obj X).homology n

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.functorHObjIsoPowerCechComplexHomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07JM** in degree `n`, as an isomorphism of objects of
`AddCommGrpCat`: the value at `𝓕` of Mathlib's cohomology functor `CategoryTheory.Sheaf.functorH`
of the chaotic site is the degree-`n` cohomology of the complex
`𝓕(X) → 𝓕(X × X) → 𝓕(X × X × X) → ⋯`.

This is `Stacks.Cohomology.sheafHAddEquivPowerCechComplexHomology` read as a morphism of the
category `AddCommGrpCat`, which is the form in which an isomorphism of cohomology groups is
stated elsewhere in the library.
declarations.statement:
def functorHObjIsoPowerCechComplexHomology
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology C) AddCommGrpCat.{u})] (n : ℕ) :
    (Sheaf.functorH (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology C) n).obj F ≅
      (powerCechComplex F.obj X).homology n

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.nonempty_addEquiv_sheafH_homology_powerCechComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07JM.** Let `𝒞` carry the chaotic topology, let `X` be an object of
`𝒞` to which every object of `𝒞` admits a morphism, and let the nonempty finite powers
`X^{n + 1}` of `X` exist in `𝒞`. For every abelian sheaf `𝓕` on `𝒞` the total cohomology
`RΓ(𝒞, 𝓕)` is represented by the complex `𝓕(X) → 𝓕(X × X) → 𝓕(X × X × X) → ⋯` associated to the
cosimplicial abelian group `[n] ↦ 𝓕(X^{n + 1})`: in every degree the cohomology of the site
agrees with the cohomology of that complex.

The source asks `𝒞` to have products of pairs; the hypothesis here is the weaker one that the
proof uses, and the source's implies it by `Stacks.Cohomology.hasProduct_fin_succ`.

The comparison itself is `Stacks.Cohomology.addEquivSheafHHomologyPowerCechComplex`; this is
that `def` read as an existence statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_addEquiv_sheafH_homology_powerCechComplex
    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (⊥ : GrothendieckTopology C) AddCommGrpCat.{u})] (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (Sheaf.H F n ≃+ (powerCechComplex F.obj X).homology n)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.wholeSpaceSystemDerivedIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Proposition 60.20.1, Tag 07JN]: the complex `M(0) → M(1) → M(2) → ⋯` computes
`RΓ(Cris(X/S), F)`**, as an isomorphism in the bounded below derived category `D⁺(Ab)`:

`M(•) ≅ RΓ(Cris(X/S), F)`,

for a sheaf `F` of `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on `Cris(X/S)`, over an affine situation (`X` and `S`
affine, `p` nilpotent on `Γ(X, ⊤)`), satisfying the two hypotheses of the tag:

1. `F` is locally quasi-coherent, and
2. for every morphism of `Cris(X/S)` whose map of ambient schemes is a closed immersion, the
   comparison map `c_f` is locally surjective.

Here `M(n) = lim_e Γ((X, T(n)_e, δ(n)), F)` for the system `(X, T(n)_e, δ(n))` of the proof
(`...SmallSite.wholeSpaceSystem`, built from the presentation of the
`...SmallSite.WholeSpacePresentation` instance), the complex being extended by zero to `ℤ`, and
`RΓ(Cris(X/S), -)` is `...SmallSite.derivedGlobalSections`, the right derived functor of global
sections.  The isomorphism is the canonical comparison of the proof: the Čech zigzag
`M(•) ⟶ Tot(lim_e I^•(T(•)_e)) ⟵ Γ(Cris(X/S), I^•)` through the Čech double complex of an
injective resolution `I^•` of `F` (`...SmallSite.wholeSpaceSystemDerivedIsoOfAbelian_hom`).
Hypothesis (1) gives the vanishing of [Stacks, Tag 07JJ] at the objects of the system, and (1) and
(2) the surjectivity of the restrictions along its towers; these are what make both arrows of the
zigzag quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
def wholeSpaceSystemDerivedIso :
    DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.obj
        (Stacks.Cohomology.extendPlusObj
          (sectionsComplex (wholeSpaceSystem S hp) (abelianSheaf F).obj)) ≅
      (derivedGlobalSections S).obj (abelianSheaf F)
declarations.comment: the complex M(0) → M(1) → M(2) → ⋯ of the system (X, T(n)_e, δ(n)) computes RΓ(Cris(X/S), F): an isomorphism M(•) ≅ RΓ(Cris(X/S), F) in D⁺(Ab), the Čech comparison through an injective resolution, for F locally quasi-coherent with c_f locally surjective along closed immersions, X and S affine

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.hasKernels_iAdicallyCompleteModuleCat

**Stacks 07JR.** If `I` is a finitely generated ideal of `R`, then the category of
`I`-adically complete `R`-modules has cokernels.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasCokernels_iAdicallyCompleteModuleCat
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG) :
    HasCokernels (IAdicallyCompleteModuleCat.{v} R I)
declarations.comment: cokernels

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.not_abelian_iAdicallyCompleteModuleCat_of_principal
declarations.doc:
If `R` is a Noetherian ring without zero divisors which is complete for a principal ideal
`I = (π)` whose generator is neither zero nor a unit, and `E : Type v` is an `R`-module with a
linear equivalence `E ≃ₗ[R] R`, then the category of `I`-adically complete `R`-modules in
`Type v` is not abelian.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_abelian_iAdicallyCompleteModuleCat_of_principal
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [NoZeroDivisors R]
    (I : Ideal R) (hR : IsAdicComplete I R) (π : R) (hIspan : I = Ideal.span {π})
    (hπ : π ≠ 0) (hπnonunit : ¬ IsUnit π)
    (E : Type v) [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] (eER : E ≃ₗ[R] R) :
    ¬ Nonempty (Abelian (IAdicallyCompleteModuleCat.{v} R I))
declarations.comment: not_abelian, for a named ring and a named principal ideal
