declarations.name: Crystalline.PthRootExtension.exists_homotopyInverse_completedPthRootExtension_situation
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Lemma 60.25.3, Tag 07N1].**

In Situation 07MD (`s`), let `P = A[x_i] → C` be a surjective polynomial presentation (`f`, `hf`),
let `D` be the `p`-adic completion of the divided power envelope `D_{P,γ}(ker f)` with its divided
powers `γ̄` (07J8, [Stacks, Tag 07KG]), and let `Ω^q_D` be the `p`-adic completion of the divided
power forms of `D` over `A` (07J9, in its second form `Ω_D = lim_e Ω_{D/A,γ̄}/p^e`).  Let `λ ∈ D`,
let `D'` be the `p`-adic completion of `D[z]⟨ξ⟩/(ξ - (z^p - λ))` with the divided powers of
[Stacks, Tag 07KD], and let `Ω^q_{D'}` be the `p`-adic completion of the divided power forms of
`D'` over `A`.  Let `M` be a `D`-module with a connection `∇ : M → M ⊗̂_D Ω_D` (07JC), integrable
(07JD) in the sense of [Stacks, Remark 60.6.1, Tag 07I0]: the composite `M → M ⊗̂ Ω¹ → M ⊗̂ Ω²`
vanishes.  Then:

* `M ⊗^∧_D Ω^•_D` and `M ⊗^∧_D Ω^•_{D'}` are complexes;
* the canonical map `c_M^• : M ⊗^∧_D Ω^•_D → M ⊗^∧_D Ω^•_{D'}` of (07PY) is a map of complexes;
* there is a map of complexes `e_M^•` in the opposite direction with `e_M^• ∘ c_M^• = p`, so that
  `e_M^• ∘ c_M^•` is homotopic to `p` (by the zero homotopy), and a homotopy `h` with
  `h d = p - c_M^• ∘ e_M^•` in degree `0` and `d h + h d = p - c_M^• ∘ e_M^•` in positive degrees,
  so that `c_M^• ∘ e_M^•` is homotopic to `p`; moreover `h ∘ c_M^• = 0`.

The hypotheses (07JB), completeness of `M`, and (07JE), quasi-nilpotence of `∇`, are not needed
and are not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homotopyInverse_completedPthRootExtension_situation
    (lam : (𝒟 : Type u)) (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (𝒟 : Type u) M]
    (nabla : CompletedConnection s.p (𝒟 : Type u)
      (completedDividedPowerForms s.p (s.A : Type u) (𝒟).dividedPowers 1)
      (completedDividedPowerDifferentialOnRing s.p (s.A : Type u) (𝒟).dividedPowers) M)
    (hint : IsCompletedIntegrable s.p (s.A : Type u) (𝒟 : Type u) (𝒟).dividedPowers M nabla) :
    CompletedDeRham.IsSquareZero s.p (𝒟 : Type u) (completedDividedPowerForms s.p (s.A : Type u)
        (𝒟).dividedPowers)
        (completedDividedPowerWedgeOnRing s.p (s.A : Type u) (𝒟).dividedPowers)
        (completedDividedPowerDeRham s.p (s.A : Type u) (𝒟).dividedPowers) M nabla
        (isGradedLeibniz_completedDividedPowerOnRing s.p (s.A : Type u) (𝒟).dividedPowers) ∧
      CompletedDeRham.IsSquareZero s.p (completedPrimeRingSelf 𝒟 s.p lam)
        (completedDividedPowerForms s.p (s.A : Type u)
          (completedPrimeDividedPowers 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf)))
        (completedDividedPowerWedgeOnRing s.p (s.A : Type u)
          (completedPrimeDividedPowers 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf)))
        (completedDividedPowerDeRham s.p (s.A : Type u)
          (completedPrimeDividedPowers 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf)))
        (genuineCarrier 𝒟 s.p lam M)
        (genuineCompletedConnection (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
            (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M nabla)
        (isGradedLeibniz_completedDividedPowerOnRing s.p (s.A : Type u) _) ∧
      (∀ q : ℕ, (genuineCompletedDifferential (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out :
          s.p.Prime).ne_zero
          (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M nabla
          q).comp (genuineCompletedComparison (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out :
              s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M q) =
        (genuineCompletedComparison (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
            (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M (q + 1)).comp
          (baseCompletedDifferential (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p M nabla q)) ∧
      ∃ (e : ∀ q : ℕ, genuineCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
          (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M q →+
          baseCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p M q)
        (h : ∀ q : ℕ, genuineCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
            (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M (q + 1) →+
          genuineCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M q),
        (∀ (q : ℕ) (y : genuineCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
            (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M q),
          e (q + 1) (genuineCompletedDifferential (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out :
              s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M
            nabla q y) = baseCompletedDifferential (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p M nabla q (e q y)) ∧
        (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : baseCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p M q),
          e q (genuineCompletedComparison (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M q x) =
            s.p • x) ∧
        (∀ y : genuineCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
            (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M 0,
          h 0 (genuineCompletedDifferential (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M nabla 0
            y) = s.p • y - genuineCompletedComparison (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out :
                s.p.Prime).ne_zero
                (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M 0
              (e 0 y)) ∧
        (∀ (q : ℕ) (y : genuineCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
            (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M
            (q + 1)),
          genuineCompletedDifferential (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M nabla q
              (h q y) +
            h (q + 1) (genuineCompletedDifferential (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out :
                s.p.Prime).ne_zero
                (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M
              nabla (q + 1) y) =
            s.p • y - genuineCompletedComparison (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out :
                s.p.Prime).ne_zero
                (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M
              (q + 1) (e (q + 1) y)) ∧
        (∀ (q : ℕ) (x : baseCompletedTerm (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p M (q + 1)),
          h q (genuineCompletedComparison (s.A : Type u) 𝒟 s.p lam (Fact.out : s.p.Prime).ne_zero
              (completedEnvelopeOfPresentation_prime_nilpotent s f hf) M (q + 1)
            x) = 0)
declarations.comment: in Situation 07MD with D the completed divided power envelope of 07J8 and the completed forms of 07J9; for every completed connection integrable in the sense of 07I0

declarations.name: Crystalline.FCrystalSituation
declarations.doc:
A global crystalline situation over an affine divided power base, with the distinguished
prime in its divided power ideal and a divided power endomorphism of the base ring lifting the
absolute Frobenius modulo that prime.

See [Stacks Project, Tag 07N2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07N2).
declarations.statement: public structure FCrystalSituation

declarations.name: Crystalline.SmallFCrystal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07N3.**  An *F-crystal on `X/S` relative to `σ`*: a crystal `E` in
finite locally free `𝒪_{X/S}`-modules on the small crystalline site `Cris(X/S)` together with a map
`F_E : (F_X)_cris^* E ⟶ E`.

The crystal in finite locally free modules is the notion of [Stacks, Tag 07IU] on `Cris(X/S)`,
`...SmallSite.ModuleSheaf.IsFiniteLocallyFreeQuasicoherentCrystal`:
quasi-coherence, condition (1) of [Stacks, Tag 07IT], together with finite local freeness.  The
pullback `(F_X)_cris^*` is `Crystalline.FCrystalSituation.smallFrobeniusModulePullback`, the
pullback of modules along `(F_X)_cris = π_X ∘ (F_X)_CRIS ∘ i_X` of [Stacks, Tag 07IK].
declarations.statement: structure SmallFCrystal (T : FCrystalSituation.{u})
declarations.comment: F-crystal

declarations.name: Crystalline.SmallFCrystal.Nondegenerate
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07N3.**  An F-crystal is *nondegenerate* when there are an integer
`i ≥ 0` and a map `V : E ⟶ (F_X)_cris^* E` with `V ∘ F_E = p ^ i`, the composite being taken
diagrammatically as `F_E ≫ V`, an endomorphism of `(F_X)_cris^* E`, and the scalar `p ^ i` acting
through the `ℕ`-action on morphisms.
declarations.statement: def SmallFCrystal.Nondegenerate {T : FCrystalSituation.{u}} (E : SmallFCrystal T) : Prop
declarations.comment: nondegenerate

declarations.name: Matrix.det_mul_det_and_two_sided_of_mul_eq_pow_smul_one
declarations.doc:
**The matrix computation of [Stacks, Tag 07N4].**  Let `R` be a commutative ring, `r` an
integer and `K, L` two `r × r` matrices over `R` with `K L = pⁱ 1`.  Then:

* `det(K) det(L) = p ^ (r i)`;
* the adjugate `L'` of `L` satisfies `L' L = L L' = det(L) 1`;
* `K' = p ^ (r i) K` satisfies `K' L = p ^ j 1` and `L K' = p ^ j 1`, where `j = r i + i`.

The second-sided identity `L K' = p ^ j 1` is the content: it is obtained, as in the source, from
the adjugate and the determinant identity.  The element `p` is arbitrary, and `r ≥ 1` is not
needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem det_mul_det_and_two_sided_of_mul_eq_pow_smul_one {r : ℕ}
    {K L : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) R} {p : R} {i : ℕ}
    (h : K * L = p ^ i • (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) R)) :
    K.det * L.det = p ^ (r * i) ∧
      (L.adjugate * L = L.det • (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) R) ∧
        L * L.adjugate = L.det • (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) R)) ∧
      (p ^ (r * i) • K) * L = p ^ (r * i + i) • (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) R) ∧
      L * (p ^ (r * i) • K) = p ^ (r * i + i) • (1 : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) R)
declarations.comment: the matrix computation: for r × r matrices K, L over a ring R with K L = p ^ i 1, det(K) det(L) = p ^ (r i), the adjugate L' of L satisfies L' L = L L' = det(L) 1, and K' = p ^ (r i) K satisfies K' L = p ^ j 1 and L K' = p ^ j 1 for j = r i + i

declarations.name: Crystalline.FCrystal.nsmul_two_sided_of_rankLE
declarations.doc:
**The last sentence of [Stacks, Tag 07N4].**  Let `(E, F_E)` be an `F`-crystal whose rank is
bounded by `rmax`, and let `V` be as in [Stacks, Tag 07N3], `F_E ≫ V = p ^ i • 𝟙`, that is
`V ∘ F_E = p ^ i • id`.  Setting `V' = p ^ N • V` with `N ≥ rmax * i` gives both
`V' ∘ F_E = p ^ (N + i) • id` and `F_E ∘ V' = p ^ (N + i) • id`; in diagrammatic order these are
`F_E ≫ V' = p ^ (N + i) • 𝟙` and `V' ≫ F_E = p ^ (N + i) • 𝟙`.
declarations.statement:
theorem FCrystal.nsmul_two_sided_of_rankLE
    (hE : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLE
      (crystallineRingedSite T.global) E.crystal rmax)
    {V : E.crystal ⟶ T.frobeniusModulePullback.obj E.crystal}
    (hV : E.frobenius ≫ V = (T.global.p ^ i) • 𝟙 (T.frobeniusModulePullback.obj E.crystal))
    (hN : rmax * i ≤ N) :
    E.frobenius ≫ ((T.global.p ^ N) • V) =
        (T.global.p ^ (N + i)) • 𝟙 (T.frobeniusModulePullback.obj E.crystal) ∧
      ((T.global.p ^ N) • V) ≫ E.frobenius = (T.global.p ^ (N + i)) • 𝟙 E.crystal
declarations.comment: for an F-crystal (E, F) whose rank is bounded by rmax and V as in Definition 07N3 with V ∘ F = p ^ i id, the map V' = p ^ N V with N ≥ rmax * i satisfies V' ∘ F = p ^ (N + i) id and F ∘ V' = p ^ (N + i) id

declarations.name: Crystalline.FCrystal.nondegenerate_conditions_of_rankLE
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07N4]: for an `F`-crystal of bounded rank, both conditions follow from
nondegeneracy.**  Let `(E, F)` be an `F`-crystal as in [Stacks, Tag 07N3] whose rank is bounded
by `rmax`.  If `E` is nondegenerate, that is `V ∘ F = p ^ i • id` for some `i ≥ 0` and some
`V : E ⟶ (F_X)_cris^* E`, then

* there are `n` and `V'` with `V' ∘ F = p ^ n • id` and `F ∘ V' = p ^ n • id`, the condition
  often assumed in the literature, and
* there is an integer `j ≥ 0` such that `Ker(F)` and `Coker(F)` are killed by `p ^ j`, the
  condition needed for [Stacks, Tag 07N5].

The kernel and the cokernel are described by their universal properties: every map into
`(F_X)_cris^* E` which `F` sends to zero, and every map out of `E` which kills the image of `F`,
is killed by `p ^ j`.
declarations.statement:
theorem FCrystal.nondegenerate_conditions_of_rankLE
    (hE : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLE
      (crystallineRingedSite T.global) E.crystal rmax) (hnd : E.Nondegenerate) :
    (∃ (n : ℕ) (V' : E.crystal ⟶ T.frobeniusModulePullback.obj E.crystal),
        E.frobenius ≫ V' = (T.global.p ^ n) • 𝟙 (T.frobeniusModulePullback.obj E.crystal) ∧
          V' ≫ E.frobenius = (T.global.p ^ n) • 𝟙 E.crystal) ∧
      ∃ j : ℕ,
        (∀ (Q : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf T.global))
          (q : Q ⟶ T.frobeniusModulePullback.obj E.crystal),
          q ≫ E.frobenius = 0 → (T.global.p ^ j) • q = 0) ∧
        (∀ (Q : SheafOfModules.{u} (crystallineStructureSheaf T.global))
          (q : E.crystal ⟶ Q), E.frobenius ≫ q = 0 → (T.global.p ^ j) • q = 0)
declarations.comment: if the rank of E is bounded, both conditions follow from the nondegeneracy condition of Definition 07N3: there is V' with V' ∘ F = p ^ n id and F ∘ V' = p ^ n id, and there is j ≥ 0 such that Ker(F) and Coker(F) are killed by p ^ j

declarations.name: Crystalline.FCrystal.exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLE_of_compactSpace
declarations.doc:
If `X` is quasi-compact, there is an integer `rmax` such that every object of `CRIS(X/S)` has a
covering on each member of which `E` is a direct sum of at most `rmax` copies of `𝒪_{X/S}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem FCrystal.exists_isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLE_of_compactSpace [CompactSpace T.global.X] :
    ∃ rmax : ℕ, AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRankLE
      (crystallineRingedSite T.global) E.crystal rmax
declarations.comment: the rank of E is bounded if X is quasi-compact

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.statement07N5
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07N5].**  In Situation [Stacks, Tag 07N2] let `(E, F_E)` be a nondegenerate
`F`-crystal.  Assume `A` is a `p`-adically complete Noetherian ring and that `X → S₀` is proper
smooth.  Then the canonical map

`F_E ∘ (F_X)^*_cris : RΓ(Cris(X/S), E) ⊗^L_{A, σ} A ⟶ RΓ(Cris(X/S), E)`

becomes an isomorphism after inverting `p`.

The conclusion is `...SmallSite.Statement07N5` at `...SmallSite.frobeniusMap07N5Canonical`, the
canonical `F_E ∘ (F_X)^*_cris`, and its standing hypotheses — `A` Noetherian, `A` `p`-adically
complete, `X ⟶ S₀` proper, `X ⟶ S₀` smooth, `E` an `F`-crystal, `E` nondegenerate — are the
tag's own.

The proof is the source's.  The map of the theorem is the composite of the three arrows
(`frobeniusMap07N5Canonical_eq_comp`).  Arrow 1 is an isomorphism
(`...SmallSite.isIso_baseChangeArrow07QC`, from [Stacks, Tag 07MU] and [Stacks, Tag 07MY]);
arrow 2 is an isogeny (`becomesIsoAfterInvertingPrime_relativeFrobeniusArrow07N6`, from
[Stacks, Tag 07QB]), so arrows 1 and 2 together are an isogeny
(`becomesIsoAfterInvertingPrime_baseChangeArrow07QC_comp`); arrow 3 is an isogeny by
nondegeneracy (`...SmallSite.becomesIsoAfterInvertingPrime_frobeniusCohomologyMap`,
[Stacks, Tag 07N4], with the rank bound `exists_hasBoundedCommonLocalRank_of_isProper`); and the
three combine by `...SmallSite.becomesIsoAfterInvertingPrime_iff_of_factors`.
declarations.statement: theorem statement07N5 : Statement07N5 T (frobeniusMap07N5Canonical T)
declarations.comment: the theorem: for a nondegenerate F-crystal over a p-adically complete Noetherian A with X -> S_0 proper smooth, the canonical map F_E o (F_X)_cris^* on RGamma(Cris(X/S), E) becomes an isomorphism after inverting p

declarations.name: Module.IsRelation
declarations.doc:
`IsRelation f x` says that the coefficients `f` give a relation among the elements
`x` of an `R`-module, i.e. `∑ i, f i • x i = 0`.
declarations.statement:
def IsRelation {R : Type*} [Semiring R] {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → R) (x : ι → M) : Prop

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.nonempty_algEquiv_pi_primesOver
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, `S` a finite `R`-algebra and `p` a prime of `R`. Let `Rₚ` be the
local ring of `R` at `p` and, for each of the (finitely many) primes `q` of `S` lying over `p`, let
`S_q` be the local ring of `S` at `q`. Then the base change of `S` along the completion `Rₚ^∧` of
`Rₚ` at its maximal ideal is, as an `S`-algebra, the product of the completions `S_q^∧` of the
`S_q` at their maximal ideals: `Rₚ^∧ ⊗[R] S = S_{q₁}^∧ × ⋯ × S_{q_m}^∧`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem AdicCompletion.nonempty_algEquiv_pi_primesOver
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Module.Finite R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime]
    (Rp : Type*) [CommRing Rp] [Algebra R Rp] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rp p] [IsLocalRing Rp]
    (Sq : p.primesOver S → Type*) [∀ q, CommRing (Sq q)] [∀ q, Algebra S (Sq q)]
    [∀ q, IsLocalization.AtPrime (Sq q) q.1] [∀ q, IsLocalRing (Sq q)] :
    Nonempty (S ⊗[R] AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal Rp) Rp ≃ₐ[S]
      ∀ q, AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Sq q)) (Sq q))
declarations.comment: The source's middle term `(S_p)^∧` is Mathlib's `AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian` over `Rₚ`; the two outer terms are identified here. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: exists_subalgebra_finite_inj_aeval_pow_smul_mem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NA** (Noether normalization over a domain). Let `R` be a domain and let `S` be an
`R`-algebra of finite type with `R → S` injective. Then there are an integer `d`, an `R`-subalgebra
`S'` of `S`, elements `y_1, …, y_d ∈ S'` and a nonzero `f ∈ R` such that the `R`-algebra map
`R[Y_1, …, Y_d] → S'`, `Y_i ↦ y_i`, is injective and makes `S'` a finite module over
`R[Y_1, …, Y_d]`, and such that every element of `S` lies in `S'` after multiplication by a power
of `f`; the last condition says precisely that `S'_f ≅ S_f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_subalgebra_finite_inj_aeval_pow_smul_mem (R S : Type*) [CommRing R]
    [IsDomain R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [FaithfulSMul R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] :
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (S' : Subalgebra R S) (y : Fin d → S') (f : R), f ≠ 0 ∧
      Function.Injective (MvPolynomial.aeval y : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R →ₐ[R] S') ∧
      (MvPolynomial.aeval y : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R →ₐ[R] S').Finite ∧
      ∀ x : S, ∃ n : ℕ, f ^ n • x ∈ S'
declarations.comment:
The chain `R → R[y_1, …, y_d] → S' → S` is realized with `S'` a `Subalgebra R S` and
the middle map `MvPolynomial.aeval y`; `S'_f ≅ S_f` is stated in the elementary form
`∀ x : S, ∃ n, f ^ n • x ∈ S'`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.exists_isIdempotentElem_nonempty_algEquiv_prod_quotient
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a Noetherian ring, let `S` be an `R`-algebra of finite type, and
let `q` be a prime of `S` lying over `p ⊂ R` at which `R → S` is quasi-finite. Let `Rₚ` and `S_q`
be the local rings of `R` at `p` and of `S` at `q`. Then the base change of `S` along the
completion `Rₚ^∧` of `Rₚ` at its maximal ideal is, as an `S`-algebra, the product of the
completion `S_q^∧` of `S_q` at its maximal ideal with a complementary factor cut out by an
idempotent: `Rₚ^∧ ⊗[R] S = S_q^∧ × B` for some `Rₚ^∧`-algebra `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem AdicCompletion.exists_isIdempotentElem_nonempty_algEquiv_prod_quotient
    {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [Algebra.FiniteType R S] (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
    [q.LiesOver p] [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R q]
    (Rp : Type*) [CommRing Rp] [Algebra R Rp] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Rp p] [IsLocalRing Rp]
    (Sq : Type*) [CommRing Sq] [Algebra S Sq] [IsLocalization.AtPrime Sq q] [IsLocalRing Sq] :
    ∃ e : S ⊗[R] AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal Rp) Rp, IsIdempotentElem e ∧
      Nonempty (S ⊗[R] AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal Rp) Rp ≃ₐ[S]
        AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal Sq) Sq ×
          ((S ⊗[R] AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal Rp) Rp) ⧸ Ideal.span {e}))
declarations.comment: The source's `B` is named here as the explicit factor `(S ⊗[R] Rₚ^∧) ⧸ (e)` of an idempotent `e`, which is what makes it an `Rₚ^∧`-algebra. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.smoothAt_bot_iff_isSeparableExtension
declarations.doc:
**Smoothness at the generic point is separability of the fraction field extension**
(Stacks 07ND). Let `R → S` be a finite type map of domains, let `K` and `L` be the fraction fields
of `R` and `S`, and let `L` be a `K`-algebra compatibly with both towers — which forces `R → S` to
be injective. Then `R → S` is smooth at `𝔮 = (0)` in the sense of Definition 00TB — some nonzero
`g ∈ S` has `S_g` smooth over `R` — if and only if `L/K` is separable.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.smoothAt_bot_iff_isSeparableExtension (R S K L : Type*)
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Field K] [Field L] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    [Algebra S L] [IsFractionRing S L] [Algebra R L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsScalarTower R S L] [IsScalarTower R K L] :
    Algebra.SmoothAt R S (⊥ : Ideal S) ↔ Algebra.IsSeparableExtension K L
declarations.comment:
Smoothness at `(0)` is Definition 00TB, `Algebra.SmoothAt R S (⊥ : Ideal S)`: some
`g ∉ (0)` with `Localization.Away g` smooth (so of finite presentation) over `R`, not Mathlib's
`Algebra.IsSmoothAt`, which is only formal smoothness of `S_{(0)}`; the formal-smoothness form is
`Algebra.isSmoothAt_bot_iff_isSeparableExtension`, and the passage to 00TB uses generic finite
presentation (00FG). Separability of the possibly transcendental extension `L/K` is
`Algebra.IsSeparableExtension`, Definition 030O (2), not `Algebra.IsSeparable`. The fraction fields
are abstract, pinned by `IsFractionRing`, and the source's injectivity of `R → S` is implied by
the compatible `K`-algebra structure on `L` rather than assumed. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: exists_isFiniteFree_residueField_equiv
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 07NE (Lemma 10.159.3). Given a commutative ring `R`, a prime `p`, and a finite
field extension `L / κ(p)`, there exist a commutative ring `S` and a finite free ring map
`φ : R →+* S` such that, with `q := pS = Ideal.map φ p`:
* `q` is prime;
* `q` lies over `p` (`p = q.comap φ`);
* the induced residue field extension `κ(q) / κ(p)` is `κ(p)`-isomorphic to `L / κ(p)`, i.e.
  there is a ring isomorphism `Φ : κ(q) ≃+* L` whose composite with the induced map
  `κ(p) → κ(q)` equals the structure map `κ(p) → L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiniteFree_residueField_equiv.{u, v}
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (p : Ideal R) [hp : p.IsPrime]
    (L : Type v) [Field L] [Algebra (ResidueFieldAtPrime R p) L]
    [Module.Finite (ResidueFieldAtPrime R p) L] :
    ∃ (S : Type u) (_ : CommRing S) (φ : R →+* S),
      IsFiniteFree φ ∧
      ∃ (_ : (Ideal.map φ p).IsPrime) (hpq : p = (Ideal.map φ p).comap φ),
        ∃ (Φ : ResidueFieldAtPrime S (Ideal.map φ p) ≃+* L),
          (Φ.toRingHom.comp (inducedResidueMap φ p (Ideal.map φ p) hpq) :
            ResidueFieldAtPrime R p →+* L) = algebraMap (ResidueFieldAtPrime R p) L

declarations.name: Algebra.isRegularRing_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Regularity ascends along smooth maps of rings** (Stacks Tag 07NF). Let `R → S` be a smooth
ring map. If `R` is a regular ring, then `S` is a regular ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.isRegularRing_of_smooth (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra.Smooth R S] [IsRegularRing R] : IsRegularRing S
declarations.comment: The ring map is an `Algebra R S` instance and smoothness of it is Mathlib's `Algebra.Smooth R S` (equivalently `(algebraMap R S).Smooth`, by `RingHom.smooth_algebraMap`), as in the companion statements 033B and 033C; regularity is Mathlib's `IsRegularRing`, Definition 00OD verbatim, which already contains Noetherianness, so the source's standing convention that a regular ring is Noetherian is carried by the predicate on both sides. Mathlib has the polynomial case and transport along ring equivalences, but no ascent along a smooth map. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: IsRegularRing.of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Regularity descends along a faithfully flat ring map** (Stacks 07NG). Let `R → S` be a ring
map. If it is faithfully flat and `S` is a regular ring, then `R` is a regular ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsRegularRing.of_faithfullyFlat {R : Type u} (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    [Algebra R S] [Module.FaithfullyFlat R S] [IsRegularRing S] : IsRegularRing R
declarations.comment: The source's "regular ring" is Mathlib's class `IsRegularRing` (Definition 00OD), which already includes Noetherianness, so the Noetherianness of `R` that the source derives from Lemma 033E is part of the conclusion; the ring map `R → S` is an `Algebra R S` instance and its faithful flatness is `Module.FaithfullyFlat R S`, equal to `(algebraMap R S).FaithfullyFlat` by `RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular.of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
**Geometric regularity descends through faithfully flat maps of algebras.**
Let `k` be a field and let `A → B` be a faithfully flat map of `k`-algebras. If `B` is
geometrically regular over `k`, then so is `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsGeometricallyRegular.of_faithfullyFlat {k : Type u} {A : Type v} (B : Type w)
    [Field k] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsScalarTower k A B] [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B] [IsGeometricallyRegular k B] :
    IsGeometricallyRegular k A
declarations.comment: The source's faithfully flat `k`-algebra map `A → B` is `Algebra A B` with `IsScalarTower k A B` and `Module.FaithfullyFlat A B`, the latter being `(algebraMap A B).FaithfullyFlat` by `RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff`; geometric regularity is `Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular` (Definition 0382), which already implies the Noetherianness the source assumes. Named after the sibling 07NG, `IsRegularRing.of_faithfullyFlat`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic
declarations.doc:
`φ : R →+* S` is *formally smooth for the `n`-adic topology*, where `n` is an
ideal of `S`: for every square-zero ideal `J` of a ring `A`, every ring map
`f : R → A`, and every ring map `ψ : S → A ⧸ J` making the square commute and
with `ψ` killing some power of `n` (some `k ≥ 1` with `n ^ k ≤ ker ψ`), there
exists a lift `g : S → A` with
`(Ideal.Quotient.mk J) ∘ g = ψ` and `g ∘ φ = f`.
declarations.statement:
def FormallySmoothNAdic {R : Type v} {S : Type w} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (φ : R →+* S) (n : Ideal S) : Prop

declarations.name: RingHom.FormallySmoothTop.exists_continuous_lift_of_isAdic
declarations.doc:
A formally smooth homomorphism lifts continuously through a closed quotient of an adic
complete ring, provided a positive power of the quotient ideal lies in an ideal of definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_continuous_lift_of_isAdic
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {A : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R] [IsLinearTopology R R]
    [CommRing S] [TopologicalSpace S] [IsTopologicalRing S] [IsLinearTopology S S]
    [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    (f : R →+* S) (n : Ideal S) (hn : IsAdic n)
    (hf : RingHom.FormallySmoothTop.{w} f)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : IsAdic I) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (J : Ideal A) (hJ : IsClosed (J : Set A))
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (hJI : J ^ t ≤ I)
    (g : R →+* A) (hg : Continuous g)
    (ψ : S →+* A ⧸ J) (hψ : Continuous ψ)
    (hcomm : ψ.comp f = (Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp g) :
    ∃ φ : S →+* A, Continuous φ ∧ φ.comp f = g ∧
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp φ = ψ

declarations.name: exists_continuous_lift_of_isFormallySmooth_of_isAdic
declarations.doc:
A formally smooth homomorphism for the `n`-adic topology lifts continuously through a closed
quotient of an adic ring when a positive power of the quotient ideal lies in an ideal of
definition.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_continuous_lift_of_isFormallySmooth_of_isAdic
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {A : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [IsTopologicalRing R] [IsLinearTopology R R]
    [CommRing S] [TopologicalSpace S] [IsTopologicalRing S] [IsLinearTopology S S]
    [CommRing A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    (f : R →+* S) (n : Ideal S) (hn : IsAdic n)
    (hf : IsFormallySmooth.{w} f)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : IsAdic I) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (J : Ideal A) (hJ : IsClosed (J : Set A))
    (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (hJI : J ^ t ≤ I)
    (g : R →+* A) (hg : Continuous g)
    (ψ : S →+* A ⧸ J) (hψ : Continuous ψ)
    (hcomm : ψ.comp f = (Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp g) :
    ∃ φ : S →+* A, Continuous φ ∧ φ.comp f = g ∧
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp φ = ψ

declarations.name: isFormallySmooth_mvPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NL.** Formal power series rings over a characteristic-zero field,
over a field of characteristic `p`, and over a Cohen ring are formally smooth
over `ℚ`, `𝔽_p`, and `ℤ`, respectively, for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isFormallySmooth_mvPowerSeries.{u} (n p : ℕ)
    (K L Λ : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] [Field L] [Fact p.Prime] [CharP L p]
    [CommRing Λ] [IsDomain Λ] [IsCohenRing Λ] :
    letI : Algebra (ZMod p) L := ZMod.algebra L p
    @IsFormallySmooth.{u} ℚ (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K) inferInstance
        (⊥ : Ideal ℚ).adicTopology (⊥ : Ideal ℚ).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
        (Ideal.isLinearTopology ⊥) inferInstance
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K)).adicTopology
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K)).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
        (Ideal.isLinearTopology _) (algebraMap ℚ (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K)) ∧
      @IsFormallySmooth.{u} (ZMod p) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) L) inferInstance
          (⊥ : Ideal (ZMod p)).adicTopology
          (⊥ : Ideal (ZMod p)).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
          (Ideal.isLinearTopology ⊥) inferInstance
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) L)).adicTopology
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) L)).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
          (Ideal.isLinearTopology _) (algebraMap (ZMod p) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) L)) ∧
        @IsFormallySmooth.{u} ℤ (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) inferInstance
          (⊥ : Ideal ℤ).adicTopology (⊥ : Ideal ℤ).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
          (Ideal.isLinearTopology ⊥) inferInstance
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)).adicTopology
          (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
          (Ideal.isLinearTopology _) (algebraMap ℤ (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ))

declarations.name: main_theorem_one
declarations.doc:
**Statement (1).** If `y_1, ..., y_n` is a regular system of parameters of
`A = K[[x_1, ..., x_n]]`, then the canonical substitution map
`K[[Y_1, ..., Y_n]] → A`, `Y_i ↦ y_i`, is an isomorphism.

The canonical map is `MvPowerSeries.substAlgHom (hasSubst_of_mem_maximalIdeal y)`: the
substitution `X i ↦ y i`, which is defined precisely because each `y i` lies in `m_A` and
hence has zero constant coefficient, and which is the unique continuous `K`-algebra map
sending `X i` to `y i`. The conclusion states that *this* map sends `X i` to `y i` and is
bijective — i.e. is an isomorphism of `K`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_one (K : Type*) [Field K] (n : ℕ)
    (y : Fin n → maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K)) (hy : IsRegularSystemOfParameters y) :
    (∀ i,
        (MvPowerSeries.substAlgHom (hasSubst_of_mem_maximalIdeal y) :
            MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K →ₐ[K] MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K)
          (MvPowerSeries.X i) = (y i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K)) ∧
      Function.Bijective
        ((MvPowerSeries.substAlgHom (hasSubst_of_mem_maximalIdeal y) :
          MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K →ₐ[K] MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K))

declarations.name: main_theorem_two
declarations.doc:
**Statement (2).** If `z_1, ..., z_r` form part of a regular system of parameters for
`A = K[[x_1, ..., x_n]]`, then `r <= n` and `A/(z_1, ..., z_r)` is isomorphic (as a
`K`-algebra) to the power series ring `K[[Y_1, ..., Y_{n-r}]]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_two (K : Type*) [Field K] (n r : ℕ)
    (z : Fin r → maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K))
    (hz : FormsPartOfRegularSystemOfParameters z) :
    r ≤ n ∧
      Nonempty
        ((MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K ⧸
            Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i => (z i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) K)))) ≃ₐ[K]
          MvPowerSeries (Fin (n - r)) K)

declarations.name: main_theorem_three
declarations.doc:
**Statement (3).** Let `Lambda` be a Cohen ring with uniformizer the prime number
`pr`, and let `B = Lambda[[x_1, ..., x_n]]`. If `p, y_1, ..., y_n` is a regular system of
parameters of `B` (where `p = pr` viewed in `B` via the coefficient inclusion), then the
canonical `Lambda`-algebra homomorphism `Lambda[[Y_1, ..., Y_n]] -> B` sending `Y_i` to
`y_i` — `cohenSubstAlgHom`, the `m_Λ`-adic translation followed by substitution of the
normalized family — is an isomorphism: it sends `X i` to `y i` and it is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_three (Λ : Type*) [CommRing Λ] [IsDomain Λ] [IsDiscreteValuationRing Λ]
    (hΛ : IsCohenRing Λ) (n : ℕ) (pr : ℕ) (hunif : maximalIdeal Λ = Ideal.span {(pr : Λ)})
    (p : maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ))
    (hp : (p : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) = algebraMap Λ (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) (pr : Λ))
    (y : Fin n → maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ))
    (hrsp : IsRegularSystemOfParameters (Fin.cons p y)) :
    (∀ i, cohenSubstAlgHom hΛ y (MvPowerSeries.X i) = (y i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)) ∧
      Function.Bijective (cohenSubstAlgHom hΛ y)

declarations.name: main_theorem_four
declarations.doc:
**Statement (4).** Let `Lambda` be a Cohen ring with uniformizer the prime number
`pr`, and let `B = Lambda[[x_1, ..., x_n]]`. If `p, z_1, ..., z_r` form part of a regular
system of parameters for `B` (the length-`(r+1)` sequence `p, z_1, ..., z_r`, with `p`
the uniformizer viewed in `B`), then `r <= n` and `B/(z_1, ..., z_r)` is isomorphic (as a
`Lambda`-algebra) to the power series ring `Lambda[[Y_1, ..., Y_{n-r}]]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem_four (Λ : Type*) [CommRing Λ] [IsDomain Λ] [IsDiscreteValuationRing Λ]
    (hΛ : IsCohenRing Λ) (n r : ℕ) (pr : ℕ) (hunif : maximalIdeal Λ = Ideal.span {(pr : Λ)})
    (p : maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ))
    (hp : (p : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) = algebraMap Λ (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ) (pr : Λ))
    (z : Fin r → maximalIdeal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ))
    (hz : FormsPartOfRegularSystemOfParameters (Fin.cons p z)) :
    r ≤ n ∧
      Nonempty
        ((MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ ⧸
            Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i => (z i : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) Λ)))) ≃ₐ[Λ]
          MvPowerSeries (Fin (n - r)) Λ)

declarations.name: exists_powerSeries_presentation_of_isLocalHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NN.** A local homomorphism `A → B` of Noetherian complete local rings admits
a commutative presentation by surjections from power series rings `R` and `S`. According to the
residue characteristic, these are power series rings over fields or over Cohen rings. The map
`R → S` carries a regular system of parameters to part of one, is flat, and has regular closed
fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_powerSeries_presentation_of_isLocalHom
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] :
    ∃ (R S : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsRegularLocalRing R)
      (_ : IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R)
      (_ : CommRing S) (_ : IsRegularLocalRing S)
      (_ : IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S) S)
      (g : R →+* S) (qA : R →+* A) (qB : S →+* B),
      Function.Surjective qA ∧ Function.Surjective qB ∧
      IsLocalHom g ∧ IsLocalHom qA ∧ IsLocalHom qB ∧
      f.comp qA = qB.comp g ∧
      (∃ (xs : List R) (ys : List S) (zs : List S),
        Ideal.ofList xs = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ∧
        xs.length = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank ∧
        Ideal.ofList ys = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S ∧
        ys.length = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S).spanFinrank ∧
        ys = xs.map g ++ zs ∧
        (ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) = 0 →
          ∃ (nR nS : ℕ) (kR kS : Type (max u v)) (_ : Field kR) (_ : Field kS),
            Nonempty (R ≃+* MvPowerSeries (Fin nR) kR) ∧
            Nonempty (S ≃+* MvPowerSeries (Fin nS) kS)) ∧
        (∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) = p →
          ∃ (nR nS : ℕ) (ΛR ΛS : Type (max u v))
            (_ : CommRing ΛR) (_ : IsDomain ΛR) (_ : IsCohenRing ΛR)
            (_ : CommRing ΛS) (_ : IsDomain ΛS) (_ : IsCohenRing ΛS),
            Nonempty (R ≃+* MvPowerSeries (Fin nR) ΛR) ∧
            Nonempty (S ≃+* MvPowerSeries (Fin nS) ΛS) ∧
            IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ΛR = Ideal.span {(p : ΛR)} ∧
            IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal ΛS = Ideal.span {(p : ΛS)} ∧
            ∃ xs', xs = (p : R) :: xs')) ∧
      letI : Algebra R S := g.toAlgebra
      Module.Flat R S ∧
        IsRegularLocalRing (S ⧸ Ideal.map g (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))

declarations.name: flat_of_isFormallySmooth_maximalIdeal_adic
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NP.** A formally smooth local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, for the
maximal-ideal-adic topologies on source and target, is flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_of_isFormallySmooth_maximalIdeal_adic.{v, w}
    {A : Type v} {B : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    (hf : RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max v w} f (maximalIdeal B)) :
    letI : Algebra A B := f.toAlgebra
    Module.Flat A B

declarations.name: RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.of_flat_of_specialFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NQ, (2) ⟹ (3).** A flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings whose
special fibre is adically formally smooth over the residue field of the source is itself formally
smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem FormallySmoothNAdic.of_flat_of_specialFibre
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Module.Flat A B]
    (hbar : FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v}
      (algebraMap (ResidueField A) (ResidueField A ⊗[A] B))
      (maximalIdeal (ResidueField A ⊗[A] B))) :
    FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal B)

declarations.name: flat_geometricallyRegular_specialFiber_formallySmooth_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `f : A → B` be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings, let
`k` be the residue field of `A`, and let `B̄ = k ⊗[A] B` be the special
fibre. The following are equivalent:

1. `f` is flat and `B̄` is geometrically regular over `k`;
2. `f` is flat and `k → B̄` is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic
   topology;
3. `f` is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic topology on `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem flat_geometricallyRegular_specialFiber_formallySmooth_tfae
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] :
    letI : Algebra A B := f.toAlgebra
    let k := ResidueField A
    let Bbar := k ⊗[A] B
    List.TFAE [
      Module.Flat A B ∧ Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k Bbar,
      Module.Flat A B ∧
        RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v}
          (algebraMap k Bbar) (maximalIdeal Bbar),
      RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} f (maximalIdeal B)]

declarations.name: exists_completeLocal_formallySmooth_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NR.** Let `A` be a Noetherian complete local ring and let `B` be a
Noetherian complete local algebra over the residue field of `A`. If `B` is formally smooth for
its maximal-ideal-adic topology, then it is the special fibre of a Noetherian complete local
ring `C` that is adically formally smooth over `A` via a local homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_completeLocal_formallySmooth_lift
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A) A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal B) B]
    [Algebra (ResidueField A) B]
    (hB : RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v}
      (algebraMap (ResidueField A) B) (maximalIdeal B)) :
    ∃ (C : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : IsNoetherianRing C)
      (_ : IsLocalRing C) (_ : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal C) C)
      (f : A →+* C) (_ : IsLocalHom f),
      RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} f (maximalIdeal C) ∧
        letI : Algebra A C := f.toAlgebra
        Nonempty ((ResidueField A ⊗[A] C) ≃ₐ[ResidueField A] B)

declarations.name: exists_completeLocal_formallySmooth_lift_with_baseChange
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NS.** Consider local homomorphisms `A → A' → B` of Noetherian complete local
rings such that `A → A'` induces an isomorphism on residue fields. If the special fibre of `B`
over `A'` is formally smooth, then it is induced by an adically formally smooth Noetherian
complete local `A`-algebra `C` mapping locally to `B`.

The completed base change of `C` to `A'` is again Noetherian, complete, local, and flat over
`A'`, and its induced map to `B` is surjective. Moreover, `C → B` is surjective when `A → A'`
is, finite when `A → A'` is finite, and the completed base-change map is an isomorphism when
`A' → B` is flat.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_completeLocal_formallySmooth_lift_with_baseChange
    {A : Type u} {A' : Type v} {B : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A) A]
    [CommRing A'] [IsNoetherianRing A'] [IsLocalRing A']
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A') A']
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal B) B]
    (f : A →+* A') [IsLocalHom f]
    (g : A' →+* B) [IsLocalHom g]
    (hf : Function.Bijective (ResidueField.map f))
    (hB : letI : Algebra A' B := g.toAlgebra
      RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v w}
        (algebraMap (ResidueField A') (ResidueField A' ⊗[A'] B))
        (maximalIdeal (ResidueField A' ⊗[A'] B))) :
    ∃ (C : Type (max u v w)) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : IsNoetherianRing C)
      (_ : IsLocalRing C) (_ : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal C) C)
      (a : A →+* C) (_ : IsLocalHom a)
      (c : C →+* B) (_ : IsLocalHom c),
      c.comp a = g.comp f ∧
      RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v w} a (maximalIdeal C) ∧
      (letI : Algebra A A' := f.toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra A' B := g.toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra A C := a.toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra (ResidueField A) (ResidueField A') := (ResidueField.map f).toAlgebra
       ∃ e : (ResidueField A ⊗[A] C) ≃ₐ[ResidueField A]
           (ResidueField A' ⊗[A'] B),
         (∀ x : ResidueField A,
           e (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := A) (S := ResidueField A)
             (A := ResidueField A) (B := C) x) =
             Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := A') (S := ResidueField A')
               (A := ResidueField A') (B := B) (ResidueField.map f x)) ∧
         (∀ y : C,
           e (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := A)
             (A := ResidueField A) (B := C) y) =
           Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := A')
             (A := ResidueField A') (B := B) (c y))) ∧
      (letI : Algebra A A' := f.toAlgebra
       letI : Algebra A C := a.toAlgebra
       let T := C ⊗[A] A'
       let iA' : A' →+* T :=
         (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := A) (A := C) (B := A')).toRingHom
       let J : Ideal T := (maximalIdeal A').map iA'
       let D := AdicCompletion J T
       ∃ (t : T →+* B) (q : D →+* B)
         (_ : IsNoetherianRing D) (_ : IsLocalRing D),
         t.comp (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := A) (S := A)
           (A := C) (B := A')).toRingHom = c ∧
         t.comp iA' = g ∧
         q.comp (algebraMap T D) = t ∧
         IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal D) D ∧
         ((algebraMap T D).comp iA').Flat ∧
         Function.Surjective q ∧
         (Function.Surjective f → Function.Surjective c) ∧
         (f.Finite → c.Finite) ∧
         (g.Flat → Function.Bijective q))

declarations.name: isRegularRingHom_of_comp_of_flat_of_surjectiveOnSpec
declarations.doc:
If a composite ring homomorphism is regular and the second homomorphism is flat and
surjective on prime spectra, then the first homomorphism is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRingHom_of_comp_of_flat_of_surjectiveOnSpec
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w}
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C)
    (hgf : IsRegularRingHom (g.comp f))
    (hgflat : g.Flat)
    (hgsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap g)) :
    IsRegularRingHom f

declarations.name: AdicCompletion.noetherian_completeLocal_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
The completion of a Noetherian local ring `(A, 𝔪)` is a Noetherian local ring with maximal
ideal `𝔪 A^∧`, complete with respect to it, and faithfully flat over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem noetherian_completeLocal_faithfullyFlat (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [IsLocalRing A] :
    IsNoetherianRing (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) ∧
      IsLocalRing (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) ∧
      maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) =
        (maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A)) ∧
      IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A))
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A) ∧
      Module.FaithfullyFlat A (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A)
declarations.comment: the completion of a Noetherian local ring

declarations.name: ringKrullDim_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NV.** A Noetherian local ring and its completion at the maximal ideal have the
same Krull dimension.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ringKrullDim_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    ringKrullDim A = ringKrullDim (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A)

declarations.name: depth_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NW.** A Noetherian local ring and its completion at the maximal ideal have the
same depth.
declarations.statement:
public theorem depth_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    Module.depth A (maximalIdeal A) A =
      Module.depth (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A)
        (maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A))
        (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A)

declarations.name: isMaximalCohenMacaulay_iff_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NX.** A Noetherian local ring is Cohen–Macaulay if and only if its completion at
the maximal ideal is Cohen–Macaulay.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isMaximalCohenMacaulay_iff_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay A A ↔
      Module.IsMaximalCohenMacaulay (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)
        (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)

declarations.name: isRegularLocalRing_iff_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NY.** A Noetherian local ring is regular if and only if its completion at the
maximal ideal is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularLocalRing_iff_adicCompletion_maximalIdeal {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A] :
    IsRegularLocalRing A ↔
      IsRegularLocalRing (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A)

declarations.name: reducedness_and_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07NZ.** For a Noetherian local ring `A`, a reduced completion forces `A` to be
reduced. The converse fails, even for a Noetherian local domain. If `A` is Nagata, then `A` is
reduced if and only if its completion is reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem reducedness_and_adicCompletion (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsNoetherianRing A] :
    (IsAnalyticallyUnramified A → IsReduced A) ∧
      (∃ (B : Type v) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : IsLocalRing B) (_ : IsNoetherianRing B)
        (_ : IsDomain B), ¬ IsAnalyticallyUnramified B) ∧
      (IsNagataRing A → (IsReduced A ↔ IsAnalyticallyUnramified A))

declarations.name: exists_pBasis_extending
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07P2** (extension to p-basis).
Every `p`-independent family `{x_i}` over `k` extends to a `p`-basis: there is a subset `S ⊆ K`
containing the range of `x` whose inclusion `S → K` is a `p`-basis of `K` over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pBasis_extending
    {I : Type*} (x : I → K) (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p]
    (hx : PIndependent k x p) :
    ∃ S : Set K, Set.range x ⊆ S ∧ PBasis k (Subtype.val : S → K) p
declarations.comment: extension to p-basis

declarations.name: exists_pBasis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07P2** (existence of p-basis).
There is a subset of `K` that is a `p`-basis of `K` over `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pBasis (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p] :
    ∃ S : Set K, PBasis k (Subtype.val : S → K) p
declarations.comment: existence of p-basis

declarations.name: pIndependent_iff_linearIndependent_differentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07P2** ((1)<=>(2)).
For a family `x : I → K`, the elements `{x_i}` are `p`-independent over `k` if and only if the
differentials `{d x_i}` are `K`-linearly independent in `Ω_{K/k}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pIndependent_iff_linearIndependent_differentials
    {I : Type*} (x : I → K) (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p] :
    PIndependent k x p ↔
      LinearIndependent K (fun i => (KaehlerDifferential.D k K) (x i))

declarations.name: pBasis_iff_basis_differentials
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07P2** ((a)<=>(b)).
For a family `x : I → K`, the elements `{x_i}` form a `p`-basis of `K` over `k` if and only if the
differentials `{d x_i}` form a `K`-basis of `Ω_{K/k}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem pBasis_iff_basis_differentials
    {I : Type*} (x : I → K) (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p] :
    PBasis k x p ↔
      (LinearIndependent K (fun i => (KaehlerDifferential.D k K) (x i)) ∧
        ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span K
          (Set.range (fun i => (KaehlerDifferential.D k K) (x i))))

declarations.name: intersection_subfields_07P3
declarations.doc:
Let `K/k` be a field extension and `{K_α}_{α ∈ A}` a nonempty directed family of
intermediate fields with intersection `k`. Then for every `n` and every `K`-subspace
`V ⊆ K^{⊕n}`, `V` meets `k^{⊕n}` nontrivially iff `V` meets every `K_α^{⊕n}` nontrivially.

Here:
* `hinf : ⨅ α, Kα α = ⊥` encodes the condition `k = ⋂_α K_α` (the intermediate
  field `⊥` is the copy of `k` in `K`);
* `hdir : ∀ α α', ∃ α'', Kα α'' ≤ Kα α ⊓ Kα α'` encodes downward directedness of the family;
* the condition `k ⊆ K_α` is automatic from `Kα α : IntermediateField k K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem intersection_subfields_07P3 {A : Type*} [Nonempty A]
    (Kα : A → IntermediateField k K)
    (hinf : ⨅ α, Kα α = ⊥)
    (hdir : ∀ α α', ∃ α'', Kα α'' ≤ Kα α ⊓ Kα α')
    (n : ℕ) (V : Submodule K (Fin n → K)) :
    NonzeroSubset ((V : Set (Fin n → K)) ∩ coordSubset n (⊥ : IntermediateField k K)) ↔
    ∀ α, NonzeroSubset ((V : Set (Fin n → K)) ∩ coordSubset n (Kα α))

declarations.name: iInf_ker_kaehlerDifferentialMap_eq_bot_and_frobeniusFieldRange_eq_iInf
declarations.doc:
Let `Kα` be a downward-directed family of subfields of a field `K` of characteristic
`p`, each containing the `p`-th powers, and suppose their intersection is exactly the subfield
of `p`-th powers. Then the kernels of the canonical maps from `Ω[K/(ZMod p)]` to
`Ω[K/(Kα α)]` have trivial intersection. Moreover, after any finite extension `L / K`,
the intersection of the composita `L^p Kα` is `L^p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem iInf_ker_kaehlerDifferentialMap_eq_bot_and_frobeniusFieldRange_eq_iInf
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {K : Type u} [Field K] [CharP K p] [Algebra (ZMod p) K]
    {A : Type v} (Kα : A → IntermediateField (ZMod p) K)
    (hpow : ∀ α, (frobenius K p).fieldRange ≤ (Kα α).toSubfield)
    (hiInf : (frobenius K p).fieldRange = ⨅ α, (Kα α).toSubfield)
    (hdir : ∀ α α', ∃ α'', Kα α'' ≤ Kα α ⊓ Kα α') :
    (⨅ α, LinearMap.ker (KaehlerDifferential.map (ZMod p) (Kα α) K K)) = ⊥ ∧
      ∀ (L : Type w) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L],
        letI : CharP L p :=
          charP_of_injective_algebraMap (algebraMap K L).injective p
        (frobenius L p).fieldRange =
          ⨅ α, (frobenius L p).fieldRange ⊔ (Kα α).toSubfield.map (algebraMap K L)

declarations.name: fractionFields_powerSeries_polynomial_subrings
declarations.doc:
Let `x` be a p-basis of a field `k` of characteristic `p`. Inside
`A = k[[X₁, ..., Xₙ]][Y₁, ..., Yₘ]`, let `AJ` be obtained by taking coefficients in the
subfield generated by `k^p` and the `x i` for `i ∉ J`, and replacing every `X` and `Y` by
its p-th power. The fraction fields of the `AJ` form a downward-directed family whose
intersection is the p-th-power subfield and each `AJ ⊆ A` is finite.
declarations.statement:
public theorem fractionFields_powerSeries_polynomial_subrings
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {k : Type u} [Field k] [CharP k p]
    [Algebra (ZMod p) k] {I : Type v} (x : I → k)
    (hx : _root_.PBasis (ZMod p) x p) (n m : ℕ) :
    let kJ : Finset I → Subfield k := fun J =>
      (frobenius k p).fieldRange ⊔ Subfield.closure (x '' {i | i ∉ J})
    let A := MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k)
    letI : IsDomain A := NoZeroDivisors.to_isDomain A
    letI : CharP A p :=
      charP_of_injective_algebraMap (algebraMap k A).injective p
    let K := FractionRing A
    letI : CharP K p :=
      charP_of_injective_algebraMap (IsFractionRing.injective A K) p
    let toA : (J : Finset I) →
        MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) ↥(kJ J)) →+* A := fun J =>
      MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom
        ((MvPolynomial.C : MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k →+* A).comp
          ((MvPowerSeries.expand p (Nat.Prime.ne_zero Fact.out)).toRingHom.comp
            (MvPowerSeries.map (kJ J).subtype)))
        (fun i => MvPolynomial.X i ^ p)
    let AJ : Finset I → Subring A := fun J => RingHom.range (toA J)
    let KJ : Finset I → IntermediateField (ZMod p) K := fun J =>
      IntermediateField.adjoin (ZMod p) ((algebraMap A K) '' (AJ J : Set A))
    (∀ J, (frobenius K p).fieldRange ≤ (KJ J).toSubfield) ∧
      (frobenius K p).fieldRange = ⨅ J, (KJ J).toSubfield ∧
      (∀ J J', ∃ J'', KJ J'' ≤ KJ J ⊓ KJ J') ∧
      ∀ J, Module.Finite (AJ J) A

declarations.name: IsJ0
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07P7 (1).** A commutative ring is J-0 if its regular locus contains a nonempty
open subset.
declarations.statement: public def IsJ0 (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: IsJ1
declarations.doc: **Stacks 07P7 (2).** A commutative ring is J-1 if its regular locus is open.
declarations.statement: public def IsJ1 (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: IsJ2
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07P7 (3).** A commutative ring is J-2 if every finite type algebra over it is
J-1.
declarations.statement: public def IsJ2 (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: isJ1_iff_zeroLocus_inter_regularLocus_contains_nonempty_open
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07P8.** A Noetherian ring is J-1 if and only if, for every point `p` of
its regular locus, `V(p)` intersected with the regular locus contains a nonempty open subset
of `V(p)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJ1_iff_zeroLocus_inter_regularLocus_contains_nonempty_open
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsJ1 R ↔
      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
        IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) →
          ∃ U : Set (PrimeSpectrum R), IsOpen U ∧
            (U ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus p.asIdeal).Nonempty ∧
            U ∩ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus p.asIdeal ⊆
              PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus p.asIdeal ∩
                {x | IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime x.asIdeal)}

declarations.name: isJ1_of_forall_quotient_isJ0
declarations.doc: **Stacks 07P9.** A Noetherian ring is J-1 if its quotient by every prime ideal is J-0.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJ1_of_forall_quotient_isJ0 (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, IsJ0 (R ⧸ p.asIdeal)) :
    IsJ1 R

declarations.name: isJ0_of_injective_finiteType
declarations.doc:
If an injective finite type map sends a Noetherian domain into a J-0 domain, then the
source is J-0.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJ0_of_injective_finiteType
    (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsDomain R] [IsDomain S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (hinj : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S)) (hS : IsJ0 S) :
    IsJ0 R

declarations.name: isJ0_of_finiteType_injective_of_isSeparable_fractionRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07PB.** Let `R → S` be an injective finite type map of domains. If `R` is
Noetherian and J-0 and the induced extension of fraction fields is separable, then `S` is J-0.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJ0_of_finiteType_injective_of_isSeparable_fractionRing
    (R S : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [CommRing S] [IsDomain S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (hR : IsJ0 R) (hRS : Function.Injective (algebraMap R S))
    (hsep :
      letI : FaithfulSMul R S := (faithfulSMul_iff_algebraMap_injective R S).mpr hRS
      letI : Algebra (FractionRing R) (FractionRing S) :=
        FractionRing.liftAlgebra R (FractionRing S)
      Algebra.IsSeparableExtension (FractionRing R) (FractionRing S)) :
    IsJ0 S

declarations.name: isJ2_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07PC.** For a Noetherian ring `R`, the following are equivalent: `R` is J-2;
every finite type domain algebra over `R` is J-0; every finite algebra over `R` is J-1; and
every finite purely inseparable extension of a residue field of `R` is the fraction field of a
finite J-0 domain algebra over `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJ2_tfae (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    List.TFAE
      [ IsJ2 R,
        ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [IsDomain S],
          IsJ0 S,
        ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S],
          IsJ1 S,
        ∀ (p : PrimeSpectrum R) (L : Type u) [Field L]
          [Algebra p.asIdeal.ResidueField L] [Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField L]
          [IsPurelyInseparable p.asIdeal.ResidueField L],
          letI : Algebra R L :=
            ((algebraMap p.asIdeal.ResidueField L).comp
              (algebraMap R p.asIdeal.ResidueField)).toAlgebra
          ∃ R' : Subalgebra R L,
            Module.Finite R R' ∧ IsJ0 R' ∧ IsFractionRing R' L ]

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivationExtension.locDeriv
declarations.doc: The derivation of the localization `L` extending `D` along `R → L`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def locDeriv : Derivation ℤ L L
declarations.comment: (2): the extension itself

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivationExtension.locDeriv_extendsAlong
declarations.doc: `locDeriv D S L` extends `D` along the canonical map `R → L`.
declarations.statement: lemma locDeriv_extendsAlong : ExtendsAlong (algebraMap R L) D (locDeriv D S L)
declarations.comment: (2): the extension property of `locDeriv`

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivationExtension.locDeriv_unique
declarations.doc: `locDeriv D S L` is the only derivation of `L` extending `D` along `R → L`.
declarations.statement:
lemma locDeriv_unique (Dloc : Derivation ℤ L L)
    (hDloc : ExtendsAlong (algebraMap R L) D Dloc) : Dloc = locDeriv D S L
declarations.comment: (2): uniqueness of `locDeriv`

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivationExtension.exists_derivation_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
A derivation `D` on a ring `R` extends, along the canonical map `R → AdicCompletion I R`, to a
derivation of the `I`-adic completion of `R`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivation_adicCompletion
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (D : Derivation ℤ R R) (I : Ideal R) :
    ∃ Dcompl : Derivation ℤ (AdicCompletion I R) (AdicCompletion I R),
      ExtendsAlong (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion I R)) D Dcompl

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivationExtension.exists_derivation_clear_denominators
declarations.doc:
Let `R'` be a finite type `R`-algebra and let `g ∈ R` be an element whose image in `R'` is a
nonzerodivisor, such that the induced map `f : R_g → R'_g` between the localizations at the powers
of `g` is bijective. Then for some `N : ℕ` the derivation `g ^ N • D` extends, along
`R → R'`, to a derivation of `R'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivation_clear_denominators
    {R R' : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [Algebra R R']
    [Algebra.FiniteType R R']
    (D : Derivation ℤ R R) (g : R)
    (Rg : Type*) [CommRing Rg] [Algebra R Rg]
    [IsLocalization (Submonoid.powers g) Rg]
    (R'g : Type*) [CommRing R'g] [Algebra R' R'g]
    [IsLocalization (Submonoid.powers ((algebraMap R R') g)) R'g]
    (f : Rg →+* R'g)
    (hf_comm : f.comp (algebraMap R Rg) = (algebraMap R' R'g).comp (algebraMap R R'))
    (hf_iso : Function.Bijective f)
    (hg_nzd : (algebraMap R R') g ∈ nonZeroDivisors R') :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (Δ : Derivation ℤ R' R'),
      ExtendsAlong (algebraMap R R') (g ^ N • D) Δ

declarations.name: isRegularRing_quotient_span_singleton_of_isUnit_derivation
declarations.doc:
The Jacobian criterion for hypersurfaces: if some derivation sends `f` to a
unit modulo `(f)`, then the quotient of a regular ring by `(f)` is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRing_quotient_span_singleton_of_isUnit_derivation
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsRegularRing R] (f : R) (D : Derivation ℤ R R)
    (hD : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {f}) (D f))) :
    IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})

declarations.name: isRegularRing_quotient_polynomial_sub_C_of_isUnit_derivation
declarations.doc:
If a derivation of a regular ring sends `f` to a unit, then the quotient of
the polynomial ring by `p(X) - f` is regular for every integer polynomial `p`.
In particular, this applies to `p = X ^ n` for every positive integer `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRing_quotient_polynomial_sub_C_of_isUnit_derivation
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsRegularRing R] (f : R) (D : Derivation ℤ R R)
    (hD : IsUnit (D f)) (p : Polynomial ℤ) :
    IsRegularRing
      (Polynomial R ⧸ Ideal.span
        {p.map (algebraMap ℤ R) - Polynomial.C f})

declarations.name: exists_derivation_apply_ne_zero_of_not_pow_fractionRing
declarations.doc:
If a domain `B` of prime characteristic is of finite type over a Noetherian complete local
ring, then every element of `B` that is not a p-th power in its fraction field is detected by an
ordinary derivation of `B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_derivation_apply_ne_zero_of_not_pow_fractionRing
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] {R B K : Type*}
    [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [CharP B p] [Algebra R B] [Algebra.FiniteType R B]
    [Field K] [Algebra B K] [IsFractionRing B K]
    (f : B) (hf : ¬ ∃ x : K, algebraMap B K f = x ^ p) :
    ∃ D : Derivation ℤ B B, D f ≠ 0

declarations.name: isJ0_of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07PI.** A Noetherian local domain complete for its maximal-ideal-adic topology is
J-0.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJ0_of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R] : IsJ0 R

declarations.name: isJ2_of_standard_classes_and_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07PJ.** Fields, Noetherian complete local rings, the integers, one-dimensional
Noetherian local rings, one-dimensional Nagata rings, and characteristic-zero Dedekind domains
are J-2; moreover, every finite type algebra over a J-2 ring is J-2.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJ2_of_standard_classes_and_finiteType :
    (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K], IsJ2 K) ∧
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
      [IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R], IsJ2 R) ∧
    IsJ2 ℤ ∧
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R],
      ringKrullDim R = 1 → IsJ2 R) ∧
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R],
      IsNagataRing R → ringKrullDim R = 1 → IsJ2 R) ∧
    (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R] [CharZero R],
      IsJ2 R) ∧
    (∀ (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
      [Algebra.FiniteType R S], IsJ2 R → IsJ2 S)

declarations.name: exists_derivation_extension_of_formallySmoothNAdic
declarations.doc:
A derivation of a Noetherian local ring extends across a local homomorphism to a complete
Noetherian local ring that is formally smooth for its maximal-ideal-adic topology.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_derivation_extension_of_formallySmoothNAdic.{u, v}
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f]
    [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) B]
    (hfs : RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v, u, v} f (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B))
    (D : Derivation ℤ A A) :
    ∃ D' : Derivation ℤ B B, ∀ a : A, D' (f a) = f (D a)

declarations.name: isRegularRingHom_flat_geometricallyRegular_specialFiber_formallySmooth_tfae
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRingHom_flat_geometricallyRegular_specialFiber_formallySmooth_tfae
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v}
    [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A) A]
    [CommRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal B) B]
    (f : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom f] :
    letI : Algebra A B := f.toAlgebra
    let k := ResidueField A
    let Bbar := k ⊗[A] B
    List.TFAE [
      IsRegularRingHom f,
      Module.Flat A B ∧ Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular k Bbar,
      Module.Flat A B ∧
        RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v}
          (algebraMap k Bbar) (maximalIdeal Bbar),
      RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} f (maximalIdeal B)]

declarations.name: isGRing_iff_quotientCompletion_isGeometricallyRegular
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian ring is a G-ring if and only if every completed localization of a prime
quotient, after base change to the residue field of the smaller prime, is geometrically regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGRing_iff_quotientCompletion_isGeometricallyRegular
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsGRing R ↔
      ∀ (p q : PrimeSpectrum R) (_hqp : q.asIdeal ≤ p.asIdeal),
        let Q := R ⧸ q.asIdeal
        let S := Localization
          (Submonoid.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal) p.asIdeal.primeCompl)
        @Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular q.asIdeal.ResidueField
          (AdicCompletion
              ((p.asIdeal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk q.asIdeal)).map (algebraMap Q S)) S ⊗[Q]
            q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
          inferInstance inferInstance Algebra.TensorProduct.rightAlgebra

declarations.name: quasiFinite_preserves_geometricallyRegular_formalFibers_and_isGRing
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a finite-type map of Noetherian rings and let `q' ⊆ p'` be primes of
`S` at which the map is quasi-finite at `p'`. Geometric regularity ascends from the corresponding
formal fibre over `R` to that over `S`; it therefore ascends for every formal fibre of the local
rings at the two primes. If the map is quasi-finite everywhere, it also carries the G-ring
property from `R` to `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiFinite_preserves_geometricallyRegular_formalFibers_and_isGRing
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    (q' p' : Ideal S) [q'.IsPrime] [p'.IsPrime] (hq'p' : q' ≤ p')
    [Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt R p'] :
    ((let T := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')))
          (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')) ⊗[R] (Ideal.under R q').ResidueField
      letI : Algebra (Ideal.under R q').ResidueField T :=
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := R)).toRingHom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular (Ideal.under R q').ResidueField T) →
      (let T := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p'))
          (Localization.AtPrime p') ⊗[S] q'.ResidueField
      letI : Algebra q'.ResidueField T :=
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := S)).toRingHom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular q'.ResidueField T)) ∧
    ((∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')),
        let T := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')))
            (Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')) ⊗[Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')]
          q.asIdeal.ResidueField
        letI : Algebra q.asIdeal.ResidueField T :=
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : q.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₐ[
            Localization.AtPrime (Ideal.under R p')] T).toRingHom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular q.asIdeal.ResidueField T) →
      ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.AtPrime p'),
        let T := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p'))
            (Localization.AtPrime p') ⊗[Localization.AtPrime p'] q.asIdeal.ResidueField
        letI : Algebra q.asIdeal.ResidueField T :=
          (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight :
            q.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₐ[Localization.AtPrime p'] T).toRingHom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular q.asIdeal.ResidueField T) ∧
    (Algebra.QuasiFinite R S → IsGRing R → IsGRing S)

declarations.name: isGRing_iff_finiteFree_formalFibers_isRegularRing
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian ring is a G-ring if and only if every formal fibre of every finite free algebra
over it is a regular ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGRing_iff_finiteFree_formalFibers_isRegularRing (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsGRing R ↔
      ∀ (S : Type (max u v)) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Module.Finite R S]
          [Module.Free R S],
        ∀ (q p : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime] [p.IsPrime], q ≤ p →
          IsRegularRing
            (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p))
                (Localization.AtPrime p) ⊗[S] q.ResidueField)

declarations.name: isGeometricallyRegular_formalFiber_mvPolynomial_mvPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
If `A` is a polynomial ring in `m` variables over the formal power-series
ring in `n` variables over a field `k` of prime characteristic, then the generic formal fibre of
the completion of `A` at any prime ideal is geometrically regular over the fraction field of
`A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    isGeometricallyRegular_formalFiber_mvPolynomial_mvPowerSeries
    {p m n : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) (A : Type v) (K : Type w) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (_ : A ≃ₐ[k] MvPolynomial (Fin m) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) k))
    [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (q : Ideal A) [q.IsPrime] :
    let T := AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
        (Localization.AtPrime q) ⊗[A] K
    letI : Algebra K T :=
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : K →ₐ[A] T).toRingHom.toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular K T

declarations.name: isGRing_of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal
declarations.doc: A Noetherian local ring complete for its maximal-ideal-adic topology is a G-ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGRing_of_isPrecomplete_maximalIdeal
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [IsPrecomplete (maximalIdeal R) R] : IsGRing R

declarations.name: isGRing_iff_isRegularRingHom_adicCompletion_at_maximal
declarations.doc:
A Noetherian ring is a G-ring if and only if the completion map of its localization at every
maximal ideal is regular.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGRing_iff_isRegularRingHom_adicCompletion_at_maximal
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    IsGRing R ↔
      ∀ (m : Ideal R) [m.IsMaximal],
        IsRegularRingHom
          (algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime m)
            (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime m))
              (Localization.AtPrime m)))

declarations.name: isGeometricallyRegular_formalFiber_polynomial
declarations.doc:
The formal fibre at a nonzero prime `r` contained in a maximal ideal `q` of
`A[X]`, where `q` lies over the maximal ideal of the Noetherian complete local
domain `A` and `r` lies over zero, is geometrically regular over `κ(r)` when
the fraction field of `A` has prime characteristic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyRegular_formalFiber_polynomial
    (p : ℕ) (_hp : p.Prime)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsLocalRing A]
    [IsPrecomplete (maximalIdeal A) A] [CharP (FractionRing A) p]
    (q r : Ideal (Polynomial A)) [q.IsMaximal] [r.IsPrime]
    (hq : q.comap Polynomial.C = maximalIdeal A)
    (_hr0 : r ≠ ⊥) (_hrq : r ≤ q) (hrA : r.comap Polynomial.C = ⊥) :
    Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular r.ResidueField
      (r.ResidueField ⊗[Polynomial A]
        AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime q))
          (Localization.AtPrime q))

declarations.name: isGRing_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc: An algebra essentially of finite type over a G-ring is a G-ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGRing_of_essFiniteType
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType R S] (hR : IsGRing R) :
    IsGRing S

declarations.name: isGRing_basic_examples
declarations.doc:
Fields, Noetherian complete local rings, the integers, and Dedekind domains
whose fraction fields have characteristic zero are G-rings. Moreover, a finite-type algebra over
any G-ring is a G-ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGRing_basic_examples :
    (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K], IsGRing K) ∧
      (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
        [IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R], IsGRing R) ∧
      IsGRing ℤ ∧
      (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R] [CharZero (FractionRing R)],
        IsGRing R) ∧
      (∀ (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
        [Algebra.FiniteType R S], IsGRing R → IsGRing S)

declarations.name: Crystalline.baseChange_isIntegrable
declarations.doc: An integrable connection remains integrable after the compatible base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem baseChange_isIntegrable
    (hintegrable : Connection.IsIntegrable S pi hpi hgen nabla) :
    Connection.IsIntegrable S' pi' hpi' hgen'
      (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)
declarations.comment: integrability after base change

declarations.name: Crystalline.existsUnique_baseChangeDeRhamMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical degreewise map from a connection's de Rham complex to that of its base
change is uniquely specified by its value on wedges of one-forms, and commutes with the
extended differentials.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_baseChangeDeRhamMap
    (_hintegrable : Connection.IsIntegrable S pi hpi hgen nabla) :
    ∃! c : ∀ p : ℕ,
      RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)) →ₗ[A]
        RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega')),
      (∀ (p : ℕ) (m : M) (omega : Fin p → Omega),
        c p (m ⊗ₜ[B] exteriorPower.ιMulti B p omega) =
          (1 ⊗ₜ[B] m) ⊗ₜ[B'] exteriorPower.ιMulti B' p (psi ∘ omega)) ∧
      (∀ (p : ℕ) (x : M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)),
        c (p + 1) ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap p x) =
          (extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
            (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap p (c p x))
declarations.comment: canonical map of complexes
