declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_homotopyInverse_baseChangeDeRhamMap_baseLinear
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07Q7 (Lemma 60.25.1).** In the situation of Section 60.25 — a commutative square
`B → B'` over `A → A'`, quotients `Ω_{B/A} → Ω` and `Ω_{B'/A'} → Ω'` to which the de Rham
differential descends, a compatible `ψ : Ω → Ω'`, a `B`-module `M` with integrable connection
`∇`, the canonical map of complexes `c_M^•` of equation 07PY, and data `a ∈ B`, `z ∈ B'`,
`θ : B' → B'` satisfying assumptions (1)–(7) — there exists a map of complexes

`e_M^• : M ⊗_B (Ω')^• ⟶ M ⊗_B Ω^•`

such that `c_M^• ∘ e_M^•` and `e_M^• ∘ c_M^•` are homotopic to multiplication by `a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopyInverse_baseChangeDeRhamMap_baseLinear
    (S : SourceDeRham A B) (S' : SourceDeRham A' B')
    (pi : Ω[B⁄A] →ₗ[B] Omega) (pi' : Ω[B'⁄A'] →ₗ[B'] Omega')
    (hpi : Function.Surjective pi) (hgen : S.GenerationHypothesis pi)
    (hpi' : Function.Surjective pi') (hgen' : S'.GenerationHypothesis pi')
    (psi : Omega →ₛₗ[algebraMap B B'] Omega')
    (hpsi : ∀ b : B, psi (pi (KaehlerDifferential.D A B b)) =
      pi' (KaehlerDifferential.D A' B' (algebraMap B B' b)))
    (nabla : Connection A B pi M)
    (hintegrable : Connection.IsIntegrable S pi hpi hgen nabla)
    (c : ∀ p : ℕ,
      RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)) →ₗ[A]
        RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega')))
    (hc_wedge : ∀ (p : ℕ) (m : M) (omega : Fin p → Omega),
      c p (m ⊗ₜ[B] exteriorPower.ιMulti B p omega) =
        (1 ⊗ₜ[B] m) ⊗ₜ[B'] exteriorPower.ιMulti B' p (psi ∘ omega))
    (hc_comm : ∀ (p : ℕ) (x : M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)),
      c (p + 1)
          ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap p x) =
        (extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
          (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap p (c p x))
    (a : B) (z : B') (theta : B' →ₗ[B] B')
    (dec : DzDecomposition pi' psi z)
    (hd_a_eq_zero : SourceDeRham.targetD pi a = 0)
    (hpartialZ_theta : ∀ f : B', dec.partialZ (theta f) = a • f)
    (huniv :
      Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.LocalizationCriteria.UniversallyInjective.{max u w}
        (Algebra.linearMap B B'))
    (hepsilon : ∀ f : B',
      a • f - theta (dec.partialZ f) ∈ Set.range (algebraMap B B'))
    (hepsilonPrime : ∀ f : B',
      TensorProduct.map theta (LinearMap.id (R := B) (M := Omega)) (dec.dOne f) -
          dec.dOne (theta f) ∈
        LinearMap.range (TensorProduct.mk B B' Omega 1)) :
    ∃ e : ∀ p : ℕ,
      RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega')) →ₗ[A]
        RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)),
      (∀ (p : ℕ) (x : RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega'))),
          e (p + 1)
              ((extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
                (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap
                p x) =
            (extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap
              p (e p x)) ∧
        (∀ (p : ℕ) (b : B) (y : RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega'))),
            e p (RestrictScalars.lsmul A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega'))
                (algebraMap B B' b) y) =
              RestrictScalars.lsmul A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)) b (e p y)) ∧
        (∃ h : ∀ p : ℕ,
            RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega')) →ₗ[A]
              RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega')),
          (∀ x : RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^0 Omega')),
              h 0 ((extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
                (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap
                0 x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^0 Omega'))
                    (algebraMap B B' a) x -
                  c 0 (e 0 x)) ∧
            (∀ (p : ℕ)
                (x : RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega'))),
              (show RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega')) from
                (extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
                  (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap
                    p (h p x)) +
                  h (p + 1)
                    ((extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
                      (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap
                      (p + 1) x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega'))
                    (algebraMap B B' a) x -
                  c (p + 1) (e (p + 1) x)) ∧
            (∀ (p : ℕ) (b : B)
                (y : RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega'))),
              h p (RestrictScalars.lsmul A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega'))
                  (algebraMap B B' b) y) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega'))
                  (algebraMap B B' b) (h p y))) ∧
        (∃ k : ∀ p : ℕ,
            RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^(p + 1) Omega)) →ₗ[A]
              RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)),
          (∀ x : RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^0 Omega)),
              k 0 ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap
                0 x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^0 Omega)) a x - e 0 (c 0 x)) ∧
            (∀ (p : ℕ) (x : RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^(p + 1) Omega))),
              (extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap
                  p (k p x) +
                k (p + 1)
                  ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap
                    (p + 1) x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^(p + 1) Omega)) a x -
                  e (p + 1) (c (p + 1) x)) ∧
            (∀ (p : ℕ) (b : B) (x : RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^(p + 1) Omega))),
              k p (RestrictScalars.lsmul A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^(p + 1) Omega)) b x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)) b (k p x)))
declarations.comment: with the B-linearity of the reverse map e and of the homotopy h, which the p-adically completed form of Tag 07N1 needs

declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_homotopyInverse_baseChangeDeRhamMap
declarations.doc:
Let `c_M^• : M ⊗_B Ω^• ⟶ (M ⊗_B B') ⊗_{B'} (Ω')^•` be the base change map of de Rham
complexes of a `B`-module `M` with integrable connection `∇`. Given `a ∈ B` with `d(a) = 0`, a
decomposition `Ω' = (B' ⊗_B Ω) ⊕ B' dz`, and a `B`-linear `θ : B' → B'` with `∂_z ∘ θ = a`,
`a f - θ(∂_z(f)) ∈ B` and `(θ ⊗ 1)(d₁(f)) - d₁(θ(f)) ∈ Ω` for all `f ∈ B'`, and with `B → B'`
universally injective, there is a map of complexes
`e_M^• : (M ⊗_B B') ⊗_{B'} (Ω')^• ⟶ M ⊗_B Ω^•` such that `c_M^• ∘ e_M^•` and `e_M^• ∘ c_M^•`
are both homotopic to multiplication by `a`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopyInverse_baseChangeDeRhamMap
    (S : SourceDeRham A B) (S' : SourceDeRham A' B')
    (pi : Ω[B⁄A] →ₗ[B] Omega) (pi' : Ω[B'⁄A'] →ₗ[B'] Omega')
    (hpi : Function.Surjective pi) (hgen : S.GenerationHypothesis pi)
    (hpi' : Function.Surjective pi') (hgen' : S'.GenerationHypothesis pi')
    (psi : Omega →ₛₗ[algebraMap B B'] Omega')
    (hpsi : ∀ b : B, psi (pi (KaehlerDifferential.D A B b)) =
      pi' (KaehlerDifferential.D A' B' (algebraMap B B' b)))
    (nabla : Connection A B pi M)
    (hintegrable : Connection.IsIntegrable S pi hpi hgen nabla)
    (c : ∀ p : ℕ,
      RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)) →ₗ[A]
        RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega')))
    (hc_wedge : ∀ (p : ℕ) (m : M) (omega : Fin p → Omega),
      c p (m ⊗ₜ[B] exteriorPower.ιMulti B p omega) =
        (1 ⊗ₜ[B] m) ⊗ₜ[B'] exteriorPower.ιMulti B' p (psi ∘ omega))
    (hc_comm : ∀ (p : ℕ) (x : M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)),
      c (p + 1)
          ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap p x) =
        (extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
          (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap p (c p x))
    (a : B) (z : B') (theta : B' →ₗ[B] B')
    (dec : DzDecomposition pi' psi z)
    (hd_a_eq_zero : SourceDeRham.targetD pi a = 0)
    (hpartialZ_theta : ∀ f : B', dec.partialZ (theta f) = a • f)
    (huniv :
      Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.LocalizationCriteria.UniversallyInjective.{max u w}
        (Algebra.linearMap B B'))
    (hepsilon : ∀ f : B',
      a • f - theta (dec.partialZ f) ∈ Set.range (algebraMap B B'))
    (hepsilonPrime : ∀ f : B',
      TensorProduct.map theta (LinearMap.id (R := B) (M := Omega)) (dec.dOne f) -
          dec.dOne (theta f) ∈
        LinearMap.range (TensorProduct.mk B B' Omega 1)) :
    ∃ e : ∀ p : ℕ,
      RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega')) →ₗ[A]
        RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)),
      (∀ (p : ℕ) (x : RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega'))),
          e (p + 1)
              ((extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
                (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap
                p x) =
            (extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap
              p (e p x)) ∧
        (∃ h : ∀ p : ℕ,
            RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega')) →ₗ[A]
              RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^p Omega')),
          (∀ x : RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^0 Omega')),
              h 0 ((extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
                (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap
                0 x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^0 Omega'))
                    (algebraMap B B' a) x -
                  c 0 (e 0 x)) ∧
            ∀ (p : ℕ)
                (x : RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega'))),
              (show RestrictScalars A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega')) from
                (extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
                  (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap
                    p (h p x)) +
                  h (p + 1)
                    ((extendedConnection S' pi' hpi' hgen'
                      (Connection.baseChange psi nabla hpsi)).toLinearMap
                      (p + 1) x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B' ((B' ⊗[B] M) ⊗[B'] (⋀[B']^(p + 1) Omega'))
                    (algebraMap B B' a) x -
                  c (p + 1) (e (p + 1) x)) ∧
        (∃ k : ∀ p : ℕ,
            RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^(p + 1) Omega)) →ₗ[A]
              RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^p Omega)),
          (∀ x : RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^0 Omega)),
              k 0 ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap
                0 x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^0 Omega)) a x - e 0 (c 0 x)) ∧
            ∀ (p : ℕ) (x : RestrictScalars A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^(p + 1) Omega))),
              (extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap
                  p (k p x) +
                k (p + 1)
                  ((extendedConnection S pi hpi hgen nabla).toLinearMap
                    (p + 1) x) =
                RestrictScalars.lsmul A B (M ⊗[B] (⋀[B]^(p + 1) Omega)) a x -
                  e (p + 1) (c (p + 1) x))

declarations.name: Crystalline.oneVariableTheta_apply
declarations.doc:
**The operator `θ` of Example 07Q8.**  It raises the divided power degree of the variable by
one in every term of the divided power monomial expansion: `θ(∑ bₘ z^[m]) = ∑ bₘ z^[m+1]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem oneVariableTheta_apply (f : oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B) :
    oneVariableTheta B f =
      ((oneVariableMonomialBasis B).repr f).sum fun m b =>
        b • (oneVariableDividedPowers B).dpow (m + 1) (oneVariableVariable B)
declarations.comment: the operator θ

declarations.name: Crystalline.oneVariable_sub_theta_partialZ
declarations.doc:
**Assumption (6) of Section 60.25 at `a = 1`, in sharp form.**  The difference
`f - θ(∂_z(f))` is the constant term `f(0)` of `f`, the image under `B → B⟨z⟩` of the
augmentation of `f`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem oneVariable_sub_theta_partialZ (f : oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B) :
    f - oneVariableTheta B (oneVariablePartialZ A B f) =
      algebraMap (B : Type u) (oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B)
        (dividedPowerPolynomialAugmentation (B : Type u) Unit f)

declarations.name: Crystalline.oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial_standingAssumptions
declarations.doc:
**Example 07Q8, the verification of the standing assumptions.**  For a divided power ring
`(B, J, δ)` over `A`, the divided power polynomial ring `B' = B⟨z⟩` with its divided powers on
`J' = B'₊ + JB'`, the quotients `Ω = Ω¹_{B/A,δ}` and `Ω' = Ω¹_{B'/A,δ'}`, the element `a = 1` and
the operator `θ` of `Crystalline.oneVariableTheta` satisfy the seven standing assumptions of
Section 60.25: `d(1) = 0`, the decomposition `Ω' = (B' ⊗_B Ω) ⊕ B' dz`, `B`-linearity of `θ`,
`∂_z ∘ θ = 1`, universal injectivity of `B → B'`, `f - θ(∂_z(f)) ∈ B`, and
`(θ ⊗ 1)(d₁(f)) - d₁(θ(f)) ∈ Ω`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial_standingAssumptions :
    ∃ dec : DzDecomposition (oneVariablePolyProjection A B)
      (dividedPowerPolynomialOneFormComparison A B) (oneVariableVariable B),
      SourceDeRham.targetD (oneVariableBaseProjection A B) (1 : (B : Type u)) = 0 ∧
      (∀ f : oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B,
        dec.partialZ (oneVariableTheta B f) = (1 : (B : Type u)) • f) ∧
      Stacks.UniversalInjectivity.LocalizationCriteria.UniversallyInjective.{v}
        (Algebra.linearMap (B : Type u) (oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B)) ∧
      (∀ f : oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B,
        (1 : (B : Type u)) • f - oneVariableTheta B (dec.partialZ f) ∈
          Set.range (algebraMap (B : Type u) (oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B))) ∧
      (∀ f : oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B,
        TensorProduct.map (oneVariableTheta B)
            (LinearMap.id (R := (B : Type u))
              (M := dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) B.dividedPowers)) (dec.dOne f) -
            dec.dOne (oneVariableTheta B f) ∈
          LinearMap.range (TensorProduct.mk (B : Type u)
            (oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B)
            (dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) B.dividedPowers) 1))
declarations.comment: the seven standing assumptions for B⟨z⟩ at a = 1

declarations.name: Crystalline.exists_homotopyEquiv_oneVariableDeRhamComparison
declarations.doc:
**Example 07Q8, the conclusion.**  Let `(B, J, δ)` be a divided power ring which is an
`A`-algebra, let `B⟨z⟩` be the divided power polynomial ring on one divided power variable, and
let `M` carry an integrable connection `∇ : M → M ⊗_B Ω¹_{B/A,δ}`.  Then the canonical map of de
Rham complexes `c_M^• : M ⊗_B Ω^*_{B/A,δ} ⟶ M ⊗_B Ω^*_{B⟨z⟩/A,δ'}` is a homotopy equivalence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_homotopyEquiv_oneVariableDeRhamComparison
    (nabla : Connection A (B : Type u) (oneVariableBaseProjection A B) M)
    (hint : Connection.IsIntegrable (oneVariableBaseSource A B) (oneVariableBaseProjection A B)
      (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) (oneVariableBaseGenerationHypothesis A B) nabla)
    (c : ∀ p : ℕ, oneVariableSourceTerm A B M p →ₗ[A] oneVariableTargetTerm A B M p)
    (hc_wedge : ∀ (p : ℕ) (m : M)
        (omega : Fin p → dividedPowerDifferentials (A := A) B.dividedPowers),
      c p (m ⊗ₜ[(B : Type u)] exteriorPower.ιMulti (B : Type u) p omega) =
        ((1 : oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B) ⊗ₜ[(B : Type u)] m) ⊗ₜ[
          oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B]
          exteriorPower.ιMulti (oneVariableDividedPowerPolynomial B) p
            (dividedPowerPolynomialOneFormComparison A B ∘ omega))
    (hc : ∀ (p : ℕ) (x : oneVariableSourceTerm A B M p),
      c (p + 1) ((extendedConnection (oneVariableBaseSource A B)
            (oneVariableBaseProjection A B) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
            (oneVariableBaseGenerationHypothesis A B) nabla).toLinearMap p x) =
        (extendedConnection (oneVariablePolySource A B) (oneVariablePolyProjection A B)
          (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) (oneVariablePolyGenerationHypothesis A B)
          (oneVariableBaseChangeConnection A B nabla)).toLinearMap p (c p x)) :
    ∃ E : HomotopyEquiv (oneVariableSourceDeRhamComplex A B nabla hint)
        (oneVariableTargetDeRhamComplex A B nabla hint),
      E.hom = oneVariableDeRhamComparison A B nabla hint c hc
declarations.comment: Lemma 07Q7 at a = 1 for B⟨z⟩

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.annihilation07Q9_of_isIteratedAlphaPCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Lemma 60.26.3, Tag 07Q9.**  Let `p = T.p` be the prime of the global
crystalline situation `T`, whose divided power scheme `(S, 𝓘, γ)` lies over `ℤ_(p)`.  Let
`f : X' ⟶ X` be an iterated `α_p`-cover (`hf`) of schemes over `S₀ = V(𝓘)` — `X'` lies over
`S₀` through `f`, which is the situation `overSituation T f` — of constant degree `q` (`hq`).
Let `ℱ` be a crystal in quasi-coherent sheaves on `Cris(X/S)` (`hF`) and `ℱ' = f_cris^*ℱ`
(`crisModuleInverseImage` of `ℱ`).  Then in every distinguished triangle

`Ru_{X/S, *}ℱ ⟶ f_*Ru_{X'/S, *}ℱ' ⟶ E ⟶ Ru_{X/S, *}ℱ[1]`

on the canonical map `moduleComparison07Q9` (in the derived category of abelian sheaves on `X`;
`f_*` is the derived direct image of the Zariski topoi, which is `f_*` since `f` is a
homeomorphism), the object `E` has every cohomology sheaf annihilated by `q` (`Annihilation07Q9`).

The hypothesis `p ∈ 𝓘` of the source is not needed: the argument only uses that `p` is nilpotent
on `X`, which every global crystalline situation carries.
declarations.statement:
theorem annihilation07Q9_of_isIteratedAlphaPCover
    {q : ℕ} (hf : IsIteratedAlphaPCover T.p f) (hq : HasConstantDegree f q)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf T)) (hF : IsQuasiCoherentCrystal T F) :
    Annihilation07Q9 T q
      (moduleComparison07Q9 (overSituation T f) T (𝟙 T.S) f (overSituation_compat T f)
        ((moduleULift T).obj F))
declarations.comment: for an iterated α_p-cover f : X' → X over S_0 of constant degree q and a crystal in quasi-coherent modules F on Cris(X/S), with F' = f_cris^* F, the cone E of Ru_{X/S,*}F → f_* Ru_{X'/S,*}F' has all cohomology sheaves annihilated by q

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.annihilated_ker_coker_crisModuleCohomologyMap_of_isIteratedAlphaPCover
declarations.doc:
Let `p` be a prime and `(S, I, γ)` a divided power scheme over `ℤ_(p)` (the prime, the
`ℤ_(p)`-structure of the base and the local nilpotence of `p` on `X` are part of the situation
`T`), `S₀ = V(I)`.  Let `f : X' ⟶ X` be an iterated `α_p`-cover of
schemes over `S₀` of constant degree `q`, `ℱ` a crystal in quasi-coherent modules on `Cris(X/S)`
and `ℱ' = f_cris^*ℱ`.  Then the kernel and the cokernel of

`f^* : H^i(Cris(X/S), ℱ) ⟶ H^i(Cris(X'/S), ℱ')`

are annihilated by `q^{i + 1}`: every class killed by `f^*` is killed by `q^{i + 1}`, and
`q^{i + 1}` times every class of `H^i(Cris(X'/S), ℱ')` lies in the image of `f^*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem annihilated_ker_coker_crisModuleCohomologyMap_of_isIteratedAlphaPCover
    (q : ℕ) (hf : IsIteratedAlphaPCover T.p f) (hq : HasConstantDegree f q)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf T)) (hF : IsQuasiCoherentCrystal T F)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Sheaf (smallTopology (overSituation T f)) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Sheaf (smallTopology T) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (Sheaf (opensTopology (overSituation T f)) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (Sheaf (opensTopology T) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}] (i : ℕ) :
    (∀ x, crisModuleCohomologyMap (overSituation T f) T (𝟙 T.S) f (overSituation_compat T f)
        ((moduleULift T).obj F) i x = 0 → ((q : ℤ) ^ (i + 1)) • x = 0) ∧
      ∀ y, ∃ x, ((q : ℤ) ^ (i + 1)) • y =
        crisModuleCohomologyMap (overSituation T f) T (𝟙 T.S) f (overSituation_compat T f)
          ((moduleULift T).obj F) i x
declarations.comment: f^* : H^i(Cris(X/S), F) → H^i(Cris(X'/S), F') has kernel and cokernel annihilated by q^(i+1)

declarations.name: Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.SmallSite.relativeFrobeniusToTwist_isIteratedAlphaPCover_cohomologyBound
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Lemma 60.26.5, Tag 07QB].**  In the global crystalline situation `X/S` of
[Stacks, Tag 07MF] with `p` in the divided power ideal `I`, let `S₀ = V(I)`,
`X^{(1)} = X ×_{S₀, F_{S₀}} S₀` and `F_{X/S₀} : X ⟶ X^{(1)}` the relative Frobenius, and assume
that `X ⟶ S₀` is smooth of relative dimension `d`.  Then

* `F_{X/S₀}` is an iterated `α_p`-cover of degree `p ^ d`, and
* for every crystal in quasi-coherent modules `𝒢` on `Cris(X^{(1)}/S)` and every `i`, the map
  `F_{X/S₀}^* : H^i(Cris(X^{(1)}/S), 𝒢) ⟶ H^i(Cris(X/S), F_{X/S₀, cris}^*𝒢)` has kernel and
  cokernel annihilated by `p^{d(i + 1)}`.

The first assertion is
`Crystalline.GlobalCrystallineSituation.isIteratedAlphaPCoverOfDegree_relativeFrobeniusToTwist`.
The second is [Stacks, Lemma 60.26.4, Tag 07QA]
(`...SmallSite.annihilated_ker_coker_crisModuleCohomologyMap_of_isIteratedAlphaPCover`) applied to
`f = F_{X/S₀}` and `q = p ^ d`, whose two hypotheses on `f` are the first assertion, read on `X/S`
by `zsmul_id_kernel_cokernel_crisModuleCohomologyMap_relativeFrobeniusToTwist_of`.  The map is
`...SmallSite.crisModuleCohomologyMap` for the morphism `F_{X/S₀}` of situations over the
identity of `S`, and `F_{X/S₀, cris}^*` is the pullback `...SmallSite.crisModuleInverseImage` of
`𝒪`-modules; `𝒢` enters through `...SmallSite.moduleULift`, at the module universe of the
cohomology of `Cris(X^{(1)}/S)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeFrobeniusToTwist_isIteratedAlphaPCover_cohomologyBound (d : ℕ)
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d T.toClosedFiber] :
    (IsIteratedAlphaPCover T.p (T.relativeFrobeniusToTwist hp) ∧
        HasConstantDegree (T.relativeFrobeniusToTwist hp) (T.p ^ d)) ∧
      ∀ (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf (T.frobeniusTwistSituation hp))),
        IsQuasiCoherentCrystal (T.frobeniusTwistSituation hp) G → ∀ i : ℕ,
          ((T.p : ℤ) ^ (d * (i + 1))) • 𝟙 (kernel (crisModuleCohomologyMap T
              (T.frobeniusTwistSituation hp) (𝟙 T.S) (T.relativeFrobeniusToTwist hp)
              (T.toClosedFiber_comp_closedFiberMap_id hp)
              ((moduleULift (T.frobeniusTwistSituation hp)).obj G) i)) = 0 ∧
            ((T.p : ℤ) ^ (d * (i + 1))) • 𝟙 (cokernel (crisModuleCohomologyMap T
              (T.frobeniusTwistSituation hp) (𝟙 T.S) (T.relativeFrobeniusToTwist hp)
              (T.toClosedFiber_comp_closedFiberMap_id hp)
              ((moduleULift (T.frobeniusTwistSituation hp)).obj G) i)) = 0
declarations.comment: for the global crystalline situation with p in I and X -> S_0 smooth of relative dimension d: F_{X/S_0} : X -> X^{(1)} is an iterated alpha_p-cover of degree p ^ d, and for every crystal in quasi-coherent modules G on Cris(X^{(1)}/S) and every i the map F_{X/S_0}^* : H^i(Cris(X^{(1)}/S), G) -> H^i(Cris(X/S), F_{X/S_0,cris}^* G) has kernel and cokernel annihilated by p^{d(i+1)}

declarations.name: Algebra.FormallyUnramified.directLimit
declarations.doc:
**Concrete `Ring.DirectLimit` form.** Equip the direct limit
`Ring.DirectLimit S φ` of a directed system of `R`-algebras with its canonical
`R`-algebra structure `directLimitAlgebra φ`. If every `S i` is formally unramified
over `R`, then so is the direct limit. (No extra compatibility hypothesis is needed:
the canonical maps `Ring.DirectLimit.of … i` are automatically `R`-algebra
homomorphisms, cf. `Ring.DirectLimit.of_commutes`.)
declarations.statement:
theorem Algebra.FormallyUnramified.directLimit
    [DirectedSystem S (fun i j h => (φ i j h : S i → S j))]
    (hunram : ∀ i, Algebra.FormallyUnramified R (S i)) :
    letI := directLimitAlgebra φ
    Algebra.FormallyUnramified R (Ring.DirectLimit S (fun i j h => (φ i j h : S i → S j)))

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular.of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Geometric regularity ascends along smooth maps of algebras.** Let `k` be a field and let
`A → B` be a smooth map of `k`-algebras. If `A` is geometrically regular over `k`, then so is
`B`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsGeometricallyRegular.of_smooth {k : Type u} (A : Type v) {B : Type w}
    [Field k] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsScalarTower k A B] [Algebra.Smooth A B] [IsGeometricallyRegular k A] :
    IsGeometricallyRegular k B
declarations.comment: The source's smooth `k`-algebra map `A → B` is `Algebra A B` with `IsScalarTower k A B` and `Algebra.Smooth A B`, the latter being `(algebraMap A B).Smooth` by `RingHom.smooth_algebraMap` and being Definition 00T2; geometric regularity is `Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular` (Definition 0382), which already implies the Noetherianness Definition 0382 assumes. Named after the sibling 07NH, `IsGeometricallyRegular.of_faithfullyFlat`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular.of_directed_of_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, `A` a `k`-algebra, and let `t : ι → Subfield k` be a nonempty directed
family of subfields of `k` with `⨆ i, t i = ⊤`, that is, `k = colim (t i)`. If `A` is
geometrically regular over every `t i`, then `A` is geometrically regular over `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsGeometricallyRegular.of_directed_of_iSup_eq_top {k : Type u} {A : Type v}
    {ι : Type w} [Nonempty ι] [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (t : ι → Subfield k)
    (dir : Directed (· ≤ ·) t) (htop : ⨆ i, t i = ⊤)
    [∀ i, IsGeometricallyRegular (t i) A] :
    IsGeometricallyRegular k A
declarations.comment: The source's `k = colim k_i` over subfields is a directed family `t : ι → Subfield k` with `⨆ i, t i = ⊤`, equivalently (`Subfield.mem_iSup_of_directed`) every element of `k` lying in some `t i`; `Nonempty ι` is necessary, since for `ι` empty and `k` a prime field the supremum is `⊤` and the hypothesis vacuous. `A` is a `t i`-algebra by restriction of scalars along `t i ↪ k` (`IsScalarTower ↥(t i) k A`), and geometric regularity is `Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular` (Definition 0382), which already implies the Noetherianness Definition 0382 assumes. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: Algebra.isGeometricallyRegular_iff_tower_top_of_isSeparable
declarations.doc:
Let `k'/k` be a separable algebraic field extension and let `A` be a `k'`-algebra, viewed as a
`k`-algebra by restriction of scalars. Then `A` is geometrically regular over `k` if and only if
it is geometrically regular over `k'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGeometricallyRegular_iff_tower_top_of_isSeparable (k : Type u) (k' : Type v)
    (A : Type w) [Field k] [Field k'] [CommRing A] [Algebra k k'] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k' A]
    [IsScalarTower k k' A] [Algebra.IsSeparable k k'] :
    IsGeometricallyRegular k A ↔ IsGeometricallyRegular k' A
declarations.comment: The source's separable algebraic extension `k'/k` is `Algebra.IsSeparable k k'`, which already contains algebraicity (`Algebra.IsSeparable.isAlgebraic`); no finiteness is assumed, the reduction to the finite case being internal to the proof (Lemma 07QG). `A` being an algebra over `k'` and over `k` at once is `IsScalarTower k k' A`, which pins the `k`-structure to be the restriction of the `k'`-structure. Geometric regularity is `Algebra.IsGeometricallyRegular` (Definition 0382), which already implies the Noetherianness Definition 0382 assumes. Named after Mathlib's `Algebra.isSeparable_tower_top_of_isSeparable`, `tower_top` naming the right-hand side. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isRegularRingHom_comp
declarations.doc:
The composite of two regular ring homomorphisms is regular if all its fibres are
Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isRegularRingHom_comp
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} {C : Type w} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    (f : A →+* B) (g : B →+* C)
    (hf : IsRegularRingHom f) (hg : IsRegularRingHom g)
    (hNoetherian : ∀ (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime],
      let : Algebra A C := (g.comp f).toAlgebra
      IsNoetherianRing (p.Fiber C)) :
    IsRegularRingHom (g.comp f)

declarations.name: isReduced_of_isRegularRingHom
declarations.doc:
If `f : R →+* S` is regular, `R` and `S` are Noetherian, and `R` is
reduced, then `S` is reduced.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isReduced_of_isRegularRingHom {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hf : IsRegularRingHom f) [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [IsReduced R] : IsReduced S

declarations.name: henselization_faithfullyFlat_and_quotient_basis
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07QM.** Let `Rh` and `Rsh` be respectively a henselization and a strict
henselization of a local ring `R`, with residue field of `Rsh` identified with a separable
closure `κsep` of the residue field of `R`. Then `R → Rh → Rsh` is faithfully flat, the maximal
ideals are generated by those below them, reduction modulo every power of the maximal ideal is
unchanged by henselization, and the corresponding reduction of `Rsh` has a basis obtained by
reducing one fixed family of elements of `Rsh`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem henselization_faithfullyFlat_and_quotient_basis.{u, v, w, t}
    {R : Type u} {Rh : Type w} {Rsh : Type t} {κsep : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh] [HenselianLocalRing Rh]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap R Rh)]
    [CommRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh] [Algebra Rh Rsh]
    [IsScalarTower R Rh Rsh] [HenselianLocalRing Rsh]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Rh Rsh)]
    [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep] [IsSepClosed (ResidueField Rsh)]
    (hRh_ind : (CommAlgCat.etale.{w} R).ind.{w} (CommAlgCat.of R Rh))
    (hRh_res : Function.Bijective (ResidueField.map (algebraMap R Rh)))
    (hRsh_ind : (CommAlgCat.etale.{t} R).ind.{t} (CommAlgCat.of R Rsh))
    (_hRsh_res : ∃ e : κsep ≃+* ResidueField Rsh, ∀ x : R,
      e (algebraMap (ResidueField R) κsep (residue R x)) =
        residue Rsh (algebraMap R Rsh x)) :
    Module.FaithfullyFlat R Rh ∧
      Module.FaithfullyFlat Rh Rsh ∧
      (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R Rh) = maximalIdeal Rh ∧
      (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R Rsh) = maximalIdeal Rsh ∧
      (maximalIdeal Rh).map (algebraMap Rh Rsh) = maximalIdeal Rsh ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Bijective
        (Ideal.quotientMap ((maximalIdeal R ^ n).map (algebraMap R Rh))
          (algebraMap R Rh) Ideal.le_comap_map)) ∧
      ∃ (ι : Type t) (x : ι → Rsh), ∀ n : ℕ,
        letI : Algebra (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ n)
            (Rsh ⧸ (maximalIdeal R ^ n).map (algebraMap R Rsh)) :=
          Ideal.Quotient.algebraQuotientOfLEComap Ideal.le_comap_map
        ∃ b : Module.Basis ι (R ⧸ maximalIdeal R ^ n)
            (Rsh ⧸ (maximalIdeal R ^ n).map (algebraMap R Rsh)),
          ∀ i, b i = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (x i)
declarations.comment:
The identification `_hRsh_res` of `ResidueField Rsh` with `κsep` is carried, for
faithfulness to the source statement, but is not needed by the proof: the basis comes from
ind-étaleness of `R → Rsh` together with `[IsSepClosed (ResidueField Rsh)]`. Hence the leading
underscore on that binder.

declarations.name: henselization_formallyEtale_and_isFormallySmooth
declarations.doc:
The maps from a local ring to its henselization, from its henselization to its strict
henselization, and from the original ring to its strict henselization are formally étale. With
the discrete topology on each source, they are formally smooth for the adic topology defined by
the maximal ideal of the corresponding target.
declarations.statement:
public theorem henselization_formallyEtale_and_isFormallySmooth
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh] [Algebra Rh Rsh]
    [IsScalarTower R Rh Rsh]
    (κsep : Type v)
    [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    [IsHenselization R κsep Rsh]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap Rh Rsh)] :
    Algebra.FormallyEtale R Rh ∧
      Algebra.FormallyEtale Rh Rsh ∧
      Algebra.FormallyEtale R Rsh ∧
      (letI : TopologicalSpace R := ⊥
       letI : DiscreteTopology R := ⟨rfl⟩
       letI := (maximalIdeal Rh).adicTopology
       letI : IsTopologicalRing Rh := (maximalIdeal Rh).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
       letI : IsLinearTopology Rh Rh := (maximalIdeal Rh).isLinearTopology
       IsFormallySmooth (algebraMap R Rh)) ∧
      (letI : TopologicalSpace Rh := ⊥
       letI : DiscreteTopology Rh := ⟨rfl⟩
       letI := (maximalIdeal Rsh).adicTopology
       letI : IsTopologicalRing Rsh := (maximalIdeal Rsh).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
       letI : IsLinearTopology Rsh Rsh := (maximalIdeal Rsh).isLinearTopology
       IsFormallySmooth (algebraMap Rh Rsh)) ∧
      (letI : TopologicalSpace R := ⊥
       letI : DiscreteTopology R := ⟨rfl⟩
       letI := (maximalIdeal Rsh).adicTopology
       letI : IsTopologicalRing Rsh := (maximalIdeal Rsh).ringFilterBasis.isTopologicalRing
       letI : IsLinearTopology Rsh Rsh := (maximalIdeal Rsh).isLinearTopology
       IsFormallySmooth (algebraMap R Rsh))

declarations.name: RingHom.Etale.ringKrullDim_localization_atPrime_eq
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 07QP. For an étale ring map `f : A →+* B`, if `q` is a prime of `B` lying over the
prime `p` of `A`, then the Krull dimensions of the localizations `A_p` and `B_q` agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.Etale.ringKrullDim_localization_atPrime_eq {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    {f : A →+* B} (hf : f.Etale) (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime]
    (hlo : p = q.comap f) :
    ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p) = ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime q)

declarations.name: henselization_fibres_equiv_pi_residueFields
declarations.doc:
Let `Rh` and `Rsh` be respectively a henselization and a strict henselization of a
Noetherian local ring `R`. Over every prime `p` of `R`, their fibres are finite products of the
residue fields at exactly the primes lying over `p`, and all the corresponding residue-field
extensions are separable algebraic.
declarations.statement:
public theorem henselization_fibres_equiv_pi_residueFields
    (R Rh Rsh : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    (κsep : Type v) [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsHenselization R κsep Rsh]
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    (∃ (t : ℕ) (q : Fin t → Ideal Rh) (hq : ∀ i, (q i).IsPrime)
        (hlo : ∀ i, (q i).LiesOver p),
      (letI : ∀ i, (q i).IsPrime := hq
       letI : ∀ i, Algebra p.ResidueField (q i).ResidueField := fun i ↦
         (Ideal.ResidueField.map p (q i) (algebraMap R Rh) (hlo i).over).toAlgebra
       Nonempty
         (TensorProduct R p.ResidueField Rh ≃ₐ[p.ResidueField]
           (∀ i, (q i).ResidueField)) ∧
       (∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField (q i).ResidueField) ∧
       (∀ i, Algebra.IsAlgebraic p.ResidueField (q i).ResidueField)) ∧
      Function.Injective q ∧
      (∀ q' : Ideal Rh, ∀ _ : q'.IsPrime, q'.LiesOver p ↔ ∃ i, q i = q')) ∧
    (∃ (s : ℕ) (r : Fin s → Ideal Rsh) (hr : ∀ i, (r i).IsPrime)
        (hlo : ∀ i, (r i).LiesOver p),
      (letI : ∀ i, (r i).IsPrime := hr
       letI : ∀ i, Algebra p.ResidueField (r i).ResidueField := fun i ↦
         (Ideal.ResidueField.map p (r i) (algebraMap R Rsh) (hlo i).over).toAlgebra
       Nonempty
         (TensorProduct R p.ResidueField Rsh ≃ₐ[p.ResidueField]
           (∀ i, (r i).ResidueField)) ∧
       (∀ i, Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField (r i).ResidueField) ∧
       (∀ i, Algebra.IsAlgebraic p.ResidueField (r i).ResidueField)) ∧
      Function.Injective r ∧
      (∀ r' : Ideal Rsh, ∀ _ : r'.IsPrime, r'.LiesOver p ↔ ∃ i, r i = r'))

declarations.name: isGRing_henselization_and_strictHenselization
declarations.doc: The henselization and strict henselization of a local G-ring are G-rings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isGRing_henselization_and_strictHenselization
    (R : Type u) (Rh : Type w) (Rsh : Type x)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
    [CommRing Rh] [IsLocalRing Rh] [Algebra R Rh]
    [CommRing Rsh] [IsLocalRing Rsh] [Algebra R Rsh]
    (κsep : Type v) [Field κsep] [Algebra (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsSepClosure (ResidueField R) κsep]
    [IsHenselization R (ResidueField R) Rh]
    [IsHenselization R κsep Rsh]
    (hR : IsGRing R) :
    IsGRing Rh ∧ IsGRing Rsh

declarations.name: IsQuasiExcellent
declarations.doc: A commutative ring is quasi-excellent if it is Noetherian, a G-ring, and J-2.
declarations.statement: public def IsQuasiExcellent (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: IsExcellent
declarations.doc: A commutative ring is excellent if it is quasi-excellent and universally catenary.
declarations.statement: public def IsExcellent (R : Type u) [CommRing R] : Prop

declarations.name: isQuasiExcellent_and_isExcellent_of_essFiniteType
declarations.doc:
An algebra essentially of finite type over a quasi-excellent ring is quasi-excellent, and
an algebra essentially of finite type over an excellent ring is excellent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasiExcellent_and_isExcellent_of_essFiniteType
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [Algebra.EssFiniteType R S] :
    (IsQuasiExcellent R → IsQuasiExcellent S) ∧
      (IsExcellent R → IsExcellent S)

declarations.name: isNagataRing_of_isQuasiExcellent
declarations.doc: **Stacks 07QV.** A quasi-excellent commutative ring is a Nagata ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isNagataRing_of_isQuasiExcellent {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    (hR : IsQuasiExcellent R) : IsNagataRing R

declarations.name: isExcellent_of_standard_classes_and_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07QW.** Fields, Noetherian complete local rings, the integers, and Dedekind domains
whose fraction fields have characteristic zero are excellent; moreover, every finite-type
algebra over an excellent ring is excellent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isExcellent_of_standard_classes_and_finiteType :
    (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K], IsExcellent K) ∧
      (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R]
        [IsPrecomplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R], IsExcellent R) ∧
      IsExcellent ℤ ∧
      (∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R] [CharZero (FractionRing R)],
        IsExcellent R) ∧
      (∀ (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
        [Algebra.FiniteType R S], IsExcellent R → IsExcellent S)

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_approximate_solution_of_henselian_isGRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07QY (the approximation property for G-rings).** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a henselian local
G-ring. A system of polynomial equations over `R` with a solution in the `𝔪`-adic completion
`R^∧` has, for every `N`, a solution in `R` congruent to the given one modulo `𝔪 ^ N R^∧`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_approximate_solution_of_henselian_isGRing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HenselianLocalRing R] (hG : IsGRing R)
    {m n : ℕ} (f : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
    (a : Fin n → AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)
    (ha : ∀ j, MvPolynomial.aeval a (f j) = 0) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ b : Fin n → R,
      (∀ i, a i - algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R) (b i) ∈
        ((maximalIdeal R) ^ N).map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R))) ∧
      ∀ j, MvPolynomial.aeval b (f j) = 0
declarations.comment:
the full conclusion for a henselian local G-ring -- general `m`, `n` and
every `N`, including `N = 0` -- with `𝔪^N R^∧` as the extension of `𝔪^N` to
`AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R`, and with NO carried hypotheses. All three of the source's
cited inputs are formalized and used: Popescu's Theorem 07GC, reached from the G-ring hypothesis
through Lemma 0AH2; and 07M7 and 04GG, which are consumed inside Lemma 0AH5 applied
to the henselian pair `(R, 𝔪)`. Nothing else is assumed.

declarations.name: Stacks.Smoothing.exists_localEtaleSolution_of_isGRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07QZ (the approximation property for G-rings).** Let `(R, 𝔪)` be a Noetherian local
G-ring. A system of polynomial equations over `R` with a solution in the `𝔪`-adic completion
`R^∧` has, for every `N`, a solution in an étale extension `R → R'` at a maximal ideal `𝔪'` over
`𝔪` with `κ(𝔪) = κ(𝔪')`, congruent to the given solution modulo `(𝔪')^N R^∧`.

The G-ring hypothesis is the source's, and it enters where the source puts it: through Popescu's
Theorem 07GC and Lemma 0AH2, which is
`Stacks.Smoothing.isIndSmoothAdicCompletion_of_isGRing`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_localEtaleSolution_of_isGRing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (hG : IsGRing R)
    {m n : ℕ} (f : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (N : ℕ)
    (a : Fin n → AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)
    (ha : ∀ j, MvPolynomial.aeval a (f j) = 0) :
    ∃ s : StacksDraft.ArtinApproximation.LocalEtaleSolution R f N a,
      s.prime.IsMaximal ∧
        ∃ ι : s.carrier →ₐ[R] AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R,
          (∀ x : s.carrier,
              x ∈ s.prime ↔ ι x ∈ maximalIdeal (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)) ∧
            (∀ i, a i - ι (s.sol i) ∈
              (s.prime ^ N).map (ι : s.carrier →+* AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R)) ∧
            ∀ i, a i - ι (s.sol i) ∈
              (maximalIdeal R ^ N).map (algebraMap R (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R))
declarations.comment: the conclusion for a Noetherian local G-ring, with NO hypothesis beyond the source's own: the appeal to Popescu's Theorem 07GC that the source makes here runs through Lemma 0AH2 and `indSmooth_of_isRegularRingMap`, which is proved. The instance `IsNoetherianRing R` is redundant, being the first component of `IsGRing` (Tag 07GH); it is present because the statement names the maximal ideal of `R^∧`, which is only known to be local once `R` is known to be Noetherian. Every part of the source's conclusion is here: the étale `R → R'`, the ideal `𝔪'` lying over `𝔪`, its MAXIMALITY, the residue field equality `κ(𝔪) = κ(𝔪')`, the solution `b` in `R'`, and the congruence `a_i - b_i ∈ (𝔪')^N R^∧` read along the embedding `R' ⊂ R^∧` — which is local at `𝔪'`, as in the source's `R ⊂ R'_{𝔪'} ⊂ R^h ⊂ R^∧`. Two further conclusions are added: the same congruence modulo the smaller `𝔪^N R^∧`, and the congruence of Lemma 0CAR in `(R'_{𝔪'})^∧`, which is the `approx` field of `LocalEtaleSolution`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isJ2_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07R4.** For a locally Noetherian scheme, the J-2 condition is
equivalent to holding on the members of an open covering, to the section ring of every affine
open being J-2, and to that ring-theoretic condition holding on one affine open covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isJ2_tfae (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsLocallyNoetherian X] :
    List.TFAE [
      IsJ2 X,
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens),
        (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, IsJ2 (U i).toScheme,
      ∀ U : X.affineOpens, _root_.IsJ2 Γ(X, U.1),
      ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.affineOpens),
        (⨆ i, (U i).1) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, _root_.IsJ2 Γ(X, (U i).1)]
declarations.comment: equivalent conditions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.regular_tfae
declarations.doc: The five characterizations of a regular morphism with locally Noetherian fibres.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.Hom.regular_tfae {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (h : ∀ y : Y, IsLocallyNoetherian (f.fiber y)) :
    List.TFAE [
      Scheme.Hom.IsRegular f,
      Flat f ∧ ∀ y : Y,
        IsGeometricallyRegular (f.fiberToSpecResidueField y),
      ∀ (U : X.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen U) (V : Y.Opens) (_ : IsAffineOpen V)
        (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V),
        IsRegularRingHom (f.appLE V U hUV).hom,
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → Y.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            ∀ i, Scheme.Hom.IsRegular
              (f.resLE (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → Y.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ V j),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i,
                let hUV : U i ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V j := (le_iSup U i).trans hU.le
                IsRegularRingHom (f.appLE (V j) (U i) hUV).hom]

declarations.name: surjective_of_surjective_mod_locallyNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 07RD.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, `I ⊆ R` a locally
nilpotent ideal, and `f : S →ₐ[R] S'` an `R`-algebra map such that the induced
map `S → S'/IS'` is surjective and `S'` is of finite type over `R`. Then `f`
is surjective.

The proof is the Stacks 07RD argument, reorganized to avoid
the `R₀` reduction by observing that the finitely many nilpotent coefficients
generate a nilpotent ideal directly via Tag 00IM with `J = ⊥`.

Let `P := MvPolynomial ι R` for a `Fintype ι`. Since `S'` is finite type over
`R`, choose a *surjective* `R`-algebra hom `φ : P →ₐ[R] S'` (generators
`xⱼ := φ (X j)`).

`hsurj` says `π ∘ f` is surjective, where `π = Ideal.Quotient.mk (IS')`. Hence
for each `j` there is `sⱼ ∈ S` with `π (xⱼ) = π (f sⱼ)`, i.e.
`xⱼ - f sⱼ ∈ IS' = Ideal.map (algebraMap R S') I`.

An element of `IS'` is a finite sum `Σ_k (algebraMap aₖ)·bₖ` with `aₖ ∈ I`,
`bₖ ∈ S'`. Lift each `bₖ` through `φ` to `βₖ ∈ P`, and set
`h j := Σ_k (C aₖ) · βₖ ∈ P`, so that `φ (h j) = xⱼ - f sⱼ`. Define
`g j := X j - h j`, whence `φ (g j) = xⱼ - (xⱼ - f sⱼ) = f sⱼ ∈ range f`.

Let `𝔫 ⊆ R` be the ideal generated by the finite set `{aₖ}` of coefficients
used above. Each `aₖ ∈ I` is nilpotent (`hI`), so `𝔫 ≤ (⊥ : Ideal R).radical`
(the nilradical); and `𝔫` is finitely generated. By Tag 00IM
(`Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg`) there is `N` with `𝔫 ^ N ≤ ⊥`, i.e.
`𝔫 ^ N = ⊥`: `𝔫` is nilpotent. Put `𝔐 := Ideal.map C 𝔫 ⊆ P`; then
`𝔐 ^ N ≤ Ideal.map C (𝔫 ^ N) = ⊥`, so `𝔐` is nilpotent, and each `h j ∈ 𝔐`
(it is a combination of `C aₖ` with `aₖ ∈ 𝔫`).

By `aeval_sub_nilpotent_surjective`, `σ := aeval g : P →ₐ[R] P` is surjective.
Therefore the `R`-subalgebra of `P` generated by `{g j}` is `⊤` (it contains
`σ.range = ⊤`, and `Algebra.adjoin R {g j} = σ.range`). Applying `φ`:
`S' = φ '' P = φ '' (adjoin R {g j}) = Algebra.adjoin R {φ (g j)}
     = Algebra.adjoin R {f sⱼ} ≤ (f.range : Subalgebra R S')`,
since each `f sⱼ ∈ f.range` and `f.range` is an `R`-subalgebra. Hence
`f.range = ⊤`, i.e. `f` is surjective. ∎
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_of_surjective_mod_locallyNilpotent
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.IsLocallyNilpotent)
    (f : S →ₐ[R] S')
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective
      ((Ideal.Quotient.mk (extendedIdeal I S')).comp f.toRingHom))
    (hft : Algebra.FiniteType R S') :
    Function.Surjective f

declarations.name: AlgHom.bijective_of_bijective_quotientMapₐ_of_le_nilradical
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07RE**. Let `I ⊆ R` be an ideal all of whose elements are nilpotent, let `S` be of
finite type over `R` and let `S'` be of finite presentation and flat over `R`. If an `R`-algebra
map `f : S →ₐ[R] S'` induces a bijection `S/IS → S'/IS'`, then `f` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem AlgHom.bijective_of_bijective_quotientMapₐ_of_le_nilradical
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] {S' : Type w} [CommRing S']
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R S'] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R S']
    [Module.Flat R S'] (I : Ideal R) (hI : I ≤ nilradical R) (f : S →ₐ[R] S')
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMapₐ (I.map (algebraMap R S')) f
          (Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap.mpr fun x hx ↦
            show f (algebraMap R S x) ∈ I.map (algebraMap R S') from
              f.commutes x ▸ Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ hx) :
        S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S) →ₐ[R] S' ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S'))) :
    Function.Bijective f
declarations.comment:
That `I` consists of nilpotents is spelled `I ≤ nilradical R`, the source's
`S/IS → S'/IS'` is `Ideal.quotientMapₐ` applied to `f`, and finite type, finite presentation and
flatness are instance arguments.

declarations.name: Stacks.DirectLimit.FiniteDescent.finite_baseChange_of_colimit_finite
declarations.doc:
Let `L` be the directed colimit of a directed system of `R`-algebras `(A i)`, and let
`φ : B →ₐ[R] C` be a map of `R`-algebras of finite type. If the base change
`id_L ⊗ φ : L ⊗_R B → L ⊗_R C` is a finite ring map, then there is an index `i` such that the
base change `id_{A i} ⊗ φ : A i ⊗_R B → A i ⊗_R C` is a finite ring map.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_baseChange_of_colimit_finite
    {A : ι → Type*} [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (A i)]
    {f : ∀ ⦃i j⦄, i ≤ j → A i →ₐ[R] A j}
    {L : Type*} [CommRing L] [Algebra R L]
    {g : ∀ i, A i →ₐ[R] L}
    (φ : B →ₐ[R] C)
    (hcolim : IsDirectedColimit A f L g)
    (hfin_type : φ.FiniteType)
    (hfin : (baseChange L φ).toRingHom.Finite) :
    ∃ i : ι, (baseChange (A i) φ).toRingHom.Finite

declarations.name: surjective_baseChange_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
Let `A = colim_i Aᵢ` be a directed colimit of `A₀`-algebras, and let `C₀` be an
`A₀`-algebra that is of finite type over the `A₀`-algebra `B₀` (via the structure map
`φ₀ : B₀ → C₀`). If the base change `id_A ⊗ φ₀ : A ⊗_{A₀} B₀ → A ⊗_{A₀} C₀` is
surjective, then there is some index `i` for which the base change
`id_{Aᵢ} ⊗ φ₀ : Aᵢ ⊗_{A₀} B₀ → Aᵢ ⊗_{A₀} C₀` is already surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_baseChange_of_colimit
    (hcolim : IsRingColimit A₀ Aᵢ f A g)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (baseChangeColim A₀ A B₀ C₀))
    (hft : Algebra.FiniteType B₀ C₀) :
    ∃ i : I, Function.Surjective (baseChange A₀ Aᵢ B₀ C₀ i)

declarations.name: RingHom.Etale.exists_baseChange_etale_of_colimitPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Étale spreads out in a filtered colimit of base rings.** Let `A` be the colimit of a
filtered diagram of `R`-algebras `Aᵢ`, computed on underlying sets, and let `φ : B →ₐ[R] C` be of
finite presentation. If the base change `1 ⊗ φ : A ⊗[R] B → A ⊗[R] C` is étale, then
`1 ⊗ φ : Aᵢ ⊗[R] B → Aᵢ ⊗[R] C` is étale for some `i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_baseChange_etale_of_colimitPresentation
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {J : Type w} [Category.{t} J] [IsFiltered J]
    {A : CommAlgCat.{v} R} (pres : ColimitPresentation J A)
    [PreservesColimit (pres.diag ⋙ forget₂ (CommAlgCat R) CommRingCat) (forget CommRingCat)]
    {B C : Type*} [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R C] (φ : B →ₐ[R] C)
    (hφ : φ.toRingHom.FinitePresentation)
    (hA : (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id R ↥A) φ).toRingHom.Etale) :
    ∃ i : J, (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id R ↥(pres.diag.obj i)) φ).toRingHom.Etale
declarations.comment:
The source's `A_0` is the base ring `R` and its index set restricted to `i ≥ 0`,
which is cofinal, is the diagram; `A = colim A_i` is `Limits.ColimitPresentation J A` in
`CommAlgCat R` over an arbitrary filtered `J`, together with the `PreservesColimit` instance
saying the colimit is computed on underlying sets, and the base change of `φ` is Mathlib's
`Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id R _) φ`. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiProjective_of_isProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07RL over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base. A projective morphism
is quasi-projective.** This is the forward half of clause (1) of Tag 0BCL, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_iff_isQuasiProjective_and_isProper` proves over such a base.
declarations.comment: over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base, the forward half of clause (1) of Tag 0BCL; the source states the tag over an arbitrary base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.isQuasiProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07RL. A projective morphism is quasi-projective.** Properness supplies
the finite-type half, and the `f`-very ample module of
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.exists_isRelativelyVeryAmple` is `f`-ample by [Stacks, Tag 01VN],
`f` being quasi-compact. No hypothesis on the base is used, which is how the source states the
tag.

It is also **clause (5) of [Stacks, Tag 0B43]**, which the source proves by citing Tag 07RL:
membership of `X` in the category `QP_S` of that tag is
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective X.hom`, so "if `X ⟶ S` is projective then `X ∈ QP_S`" is
this statement. Tag 0B43's hypothesis that `S` carries an ample invertible sheaf is not needed
for it and is not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsProjective.isQuasiProjective {f : X ⟶ S} (hf : IsProjective f) :
    IsQuasiProjective f

declarations.name: Stacks.QuasiProjectiveCompactification.exists_isOpenImmersion_isProjective_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07RM].** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a quasi-projective morphism with `S` quasi-compact
and quasi-separated. Then `f` factors as `X ⟶ X' ⟶ S` where `X ⟶ X'` is an open immersion and
`X' ⟶ S` is projective, in the sense of clause (1) of Definition 01W8.

Half 1 of the source's proof is
`Stacks.QuasiProjectiveCompactification.immersionIntoProjective_isProjective`; half 2, the
factorisation of a quasi-compact immersion through the closure of its image, is
`Stacks.QuasiProjectiveCompactification.exists_isOpenImmersion_isProjective`, whose two conditions
on the projectivity predicate are discharged by `AlgebraicGeometry.IsProjective.isSeparated` and
`Stacks.QuasiProjectiveCompactification.isProjective_comp_of_isClosedImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_isProjective_of_qcqs {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (hf : AlgebraicGeometry.IsQuasiProjective f) :
    ∃ (X' : Scheme.{u}) (j : X ⟶ X') (p : X' ⟶ S),
      IsOpenImmersion j ∧ IsProjective p ∧ j ≫ p = f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeApproximationOfIsLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07RN**, as data: the extended system itself.
It is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteTypeApproximation` together with the choice of a witness,
so it is noncomputable; the construction is propositional throughout, every stage of it being
chosen from an existential statement.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def finiteTypeApproximationOfIsLimit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : Iᵒᵈ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵈ} (v : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map v)]
    [∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (terminal.from (D.obj i))]
    [∀ i, QuasiCompact (terminal.from (D.obj i))]
    (S : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (U : S.Opens)
    [CompactSpace (U : Scheme.{u})]
    (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵈ).obj (U : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ D)
    (hp : IsLimit (Cone.mk (U : Scheme.{u}) p)) :
    Scheme.FiniteTypeApproximation D S U p

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etale_pullback_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07RP.** If a locally finitely presented morphism at one stage of a cofiltered
inverse system becomes étale over the limit, then it is étale at some later stage.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etale_pullback_of_isLimit
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I]
    (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f₀.left]
    [Etale ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ i : Over i₀, Etale ((Over.pullback (D.map i.hom)).map f₀).left
