`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isAffineSpace_system_obj_of_mk_lt`.
declarations.statement:
theorem DescentSituation.exists_isAffineSpace_system_obj {B : BigFppfSite.{u}} {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {hS : B.Contains S} {hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})} {I : Type v} [Preorder I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (D : DescentSituation B S hS hZ I)
    (hI : Cardinal.lift.{u} #I < Cardinal.lift.{v} B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hX : IsAffineSpace B S hS D.limitCone.pt) :
    ∃ i, D.base ≤ i ∧ IsAffineSpace B S hS (D.system.obj (op i))
declarations.comment: Correction: the index set is taken smaller than the cofinality of the site's size cutoff, the form the convention of Section 70.2 takes in this size model; without it the statement is false here (a system of projective lines over fields of sizes cofinal in the cutoff has empty, hence affine, limit)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasAffineStageDescent_of_chartsBounded
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 084R, if the limit `X` of the inverse system is an affine algebraic
space then `X_i` is an affine algebraic space for some `i` beyond the distinguished index, the
charts of the system being bounded in the sense of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ChartsBounded`.

The size restriction cannot be dropped: `Stacks.Refute07SQ.not_statement07SQ` exhibits a descent
situation over an index as large as the cutoff whose limit is the empty algebraic space, which is
affine, and none of whose stages is affine.
declarations.statement: theorem hasAffineStageDescent_of_chartsBounded : HasAffineStageDescent B S hS hZ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isAffineSpace_system_obj_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07SQ.** In the situation of Stacks 084R, over an arbitrary base scheme, if the limit
`X` of the inverse system is an affine algebraic space then so is some stage `X_i` with `i` at or
beyond the distinguished index.

The only hypothesis beyond Situation 084R is the chapter's standing convention of Section 70.2
(tag 07SD), that every ring considered has its spectrum in the big fppf site; for this system it
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits`: for every stage, every affine
scheme-valued point of it and the base changes to that point of the later stages, the limit of
those affine schemes — the spectrum of the colimit of their rings — lies in the site. Nothing is
asked of the index. The convention is used three times: to make the limit of the affine charts
of the system an object of the site (Stacks 07SF), to make the ring of global functions of the
limit the filtered colimit of those of the stages (Stacks 07SI for the structure sheaf), and in
Stacks 084S.

It cannot be dropped. Index the stages by the finite subsets of a field `F` of cardinality at
least the cutoff of the site, the stage at a subset being the punctured affine plane over the
subring of `F` it generates: a directed system of quasi-compact separated schemes with affine
transition morphisms, none of them affine. A nonempty object of the site has too small a ring of
functions to receive `F`, so the limit of the system in the site is empty, hence affine. See
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.not_forall_exists_isAffineSpace_system_obj`; that the
system violates the convention is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.SiteConventionCounterexample.not_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits`.

Affineness of an algebraic space is the absolute notion, taken over the terminal scheme, so the
whole descent is read there: the relocalization along `S ⟶ Spec ℤ` carries the descent situation
over `S` to one over the terminal scheme, which is where the identification of an affine
algebraic space with the spectrum of its global functions is available, and the convention
survives that passage,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.siteContainsBaseChangeLimits_viewOverIntegers`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineSpace_system_obj_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
    (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.system)
    (hX : IsAffineSpace B S hS D.limitCone.pt) :
    ∃ i, D.base ≤ i ∧ IsAffineSpace B S hS (D.system.obj (op i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isRepresentable_system_obj
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 084R over a scheme `S` — a directed inverse system of quasi-compact
and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition morphisms, together with a
chosen limit `X` — if `X` is a scheme then some stage `X_i` is a scheme. The index set may live in
any universe; its cardinality is asked to be below the cofinality of the site's size cutoff.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRepresentable_system_obj {I : Type v} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : DescentSituation B S hS hZ I)
    (hI : Cardinal.lift.{u} #I < Cardinal.lift.{v} B.cutoff.ord.cof)
    (hX : D.limitCone.pt.IsRepresentable) :
    ∃ i, (D.system.obj (op i)).IsRepresentable
declarations.comment: Correction: the index set is taken smaller than the cofinality of the site's size cutoff, the form the convention of Section 70.2 takes in this size model; without it the statement is false here (base changes of a non locally separated space to fields of sizes cofinal in the cutoff have empty limit, a scheme, and no stage a scheme)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_isRepresentable_system_obj_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits
declarations.doc:
In the situation of Stacks 084R — a directed inverse system of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic spaces over `S` with affine transition morphisms, together with a chosen
limit `X`, under the convention of Section 70.2 (tag 07SD) that the rings the chapter forms have
their spectra in the big fppf site — if `X` is a scheme then there is a stage `X_i` which is a
scheme. Nothing is asked of the index set beyond directedness.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isRepresentable_system_obj_of_siteContainsBaseChangeLimits {I : Type u}
    [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (D : DescentSituation B S hS hZ I) (hconv : SiteContainsBaseChangeLimits B S hS D.system)
    (hX : D.limitCone.pt.IsRepresentable) :
    ∃ i, (D.system.obj (op i)).IsRepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_finiteFiltration_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space has a finite filtration
by open subspaces such that every reduced stratum has a quasi-compact
separated scheme as an étale neighborhood, isomorphic above the stratum.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finiteFiltration_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hqc : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hqs : AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : ℕ → Subfunctor X),
      0 < n ∧
      U 0 = ⊤ ∧
      U n = (⊥ : Subfunctor X).sheafify
        (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ∧
      (∀ p ≤ n, AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsOpenSubspace B S hS (U p)) ∧
      (∀ p < n, U (p + 1) ≤ U p) ∧
      ∃ (T : (p : Fin n) → Subfunctor (U p.val).toFunctor)
        (V : Fin n → AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS)
        (f : ∀ p : Fin n, yoneda.obj (V p) ⟶ (U p.val).toFunctor),
        ∀ p : Fin n,
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsClosedSubspace B S hS (T p)) ∧
          (Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS (T p).toFunctor
            ((T p).ι ≫ (U p.val).ι)) =
              Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS (U p.val).toFunctor
                (U p.val).ι) \
              Set.range (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pointsMap B S hS (U (p.val + 1)).toFunctor
                (U (p.val + 1)).ι)) ∧
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Space.HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS (T p).toFunctor
            (fun Y : Scheme.{u} => IsReduced Y)) ∧
          CompactSpace ((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (V p)) ∧
          Scheme.IsSeparated ((AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (V p)) ∧
          (MorphismProperty.inverseImage
            (@Surjective.{u} : MorphismProperty Scheme.{u})
            (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS)).presheaf (f p) ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsEtale B S hS (f p) ∧
          IsIso (pullback.fst (T p).ι (f p))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasNoetherianApproximation_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
declarations.doc:
Absolute Noetherian approximation. Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
space over `Spec ℤ`, the terminal scheme `⊤_ Scheme`, on the big fppf site `B`. Then there are a
directed set `I` and an inverse system `(X_i)` of algebraic spaces over `I` such that
(1) the transition morphisms are affine, (2) each `X_i` is quasi-separated and of finite type
over `ℤ`, and (3) `X = lim X_i`, the limit being taken in presheaves on the site.

The hypotheses are exactly those of the source, and nothing further is assumed: `X` is written
as a limit by the descending induction over the strata of Stacks 07ST, through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasConventionalNoetherianApproximation_of_etaleAtlas`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasNoetherianApproximation_of_isQuasiCompactSpace
    {X : (BigFppfOver B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ X)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ X)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ hZ X) :
    HasNoetherianApproximation B (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) hZ hZ X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_gluedRelationSource_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07SV.** The displayed square of the proof of absolute Noetherian
approximation, in the form in which the proof establishes it.

The data: a morphism `v : V ⟶ V'`, open subschemes `j : W ⟶ V` and `j' : W' ⟶ V'` with `W`
the inverse image of `W'`, that is with `hj` cartesian; objects `Q`, `Q'` with sections `d`,
`d'` of projections `p`, `p'` — in the application `Q = W ×_U W`, `Q' = W' ×_{U'} W'`,
`p` and `p'` are the first projections and `d`, `d'` the diagonals — such that `Q` is the base
change of `Q'` along `k`, that is with `hQ` cartesian; and the relations `R`, `R'` obtained by
glueing `V` to `Q` along `W` and `V'` to `Q'` along `W'`, with source maps `s`, `s'` which are
the identity on the chart `V`, resp. `V'`, and `p`, resp. `p'`, followed by the open immersion
on the other chart. Then for the morphism `r : R ⟶ R'` induced by `v` and `q` the square

```
R  --r-->  R'
|          |
s          s'
v          v
V  --v-->  V'
```

is cartesian. Nothing is assumed about the base over which `Q` and `Q'` are fibre products,
so this applies verbatim when that base is an algebraic space, as it is in the source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_gluedRelationSource_of_isPullback
    {v : V ⟶ V'} {k : W ⟶ W'} {j : W ⟶ V} {j' : W' ⟶ V'} [IsOpenImmersion j']
    {p : Q ⟶ W} {p' : Q' ⟶ W'} {d : W ⟶ Q} {d' : W' ⟶ Q'} [IsOpenImmersion d']
    {q : Q ⟶ Q'} (hj : IsPullback k j j' v) (hQ : IsPullback q p p' k)
    (hd : d ≫ p = 𝟙 W) (hdq : d ≫ q = k ≫ d')
    {a : V ⟶ R} {b : Q ⟶ R} {a' : V' ⟶ R'} {b' : Q' ⟶ R'}
    (hR : IsPushout j d a b) (hR' : IsPushout j' d' a' b')
    {s : R ⟶ V} (hsa : a ≫ s = 𝟙 V) (hsb : b ≫ s = p ≫ j)
    {s' : R' ⟶ V'} (hsa' : a' ≫ s' = 𝟙 V') (hsb' : b' ≫ s' = p' ≫ j')
    {r : R ⟶ R'} (hra : a ≫ r = v ≫ a') (hrb : b ≫ r = q ≫ b') :
    IsPullback r s s' v
declarations.comment: the displayed square is cartesian, for any base-changed fibre square over W

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_gluedRelationSource
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07SV.** The displayed square of the proof of absolute Noetherian
approximation, written out for the construction the source performs. Let `w' : W' ⟶ U'` be
étale, let `u : U ⟶ U'` be arbitrary, and let `W = W' ×_{U'} U`. Let `j' : W' ⟶ V'` and
`j : W ⟶ V` be open immersions with `W` the inverse image of `W'`, that is with `hj`
cartesian. Let `R` be obtained by glueing `V` to `W ×_U W` along the diagonal copy of `W`,
and `R'` likewise at the primed stage, and let `s`, `s'` be the source maps: the identity on
the chart `V`, resp. `V'`, and the first projection on the chart `W ×_U W`, resp.
`W' ×_{U'} W'`. If `r : R ⟶ R'` is the morphism induced by `v` on the glueings, then the
square formed by `r`, `s`, `s'` and `v` is cartesian.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_gluedRelationSource {u : U ⟶ U'} {v : V ⟶ V'} {w' : W' ⟶ U'} [Etale w']
    {j' : W' ⟶ V'} [IsOpenImmersion j'] {j : pullback w' u ⟶ V}
    (hj : IsPullback (pullback.fst w' u) j j' v)
    {a : V ⟶ R} {b : pullback (pullback.snd w' u) (pullback.snd w' u) ⟶ R}
    {a' : V' ⟶ R'} {b' : pullback w' w' ⟶ R'}
    (hR : IsPushout j (pullback.diagonal (pullback.snd w' u)) a b)
    (hR' : IsPushout j' (pullback.diagonal w') a' b')
    {s : R ⟶ V} (hsa : a ≫ s = 𝟙 V)
    (hsb : b ≫ s = pullback.fst (pullback.snd w' u) (pullback.snd w' u) ≫ j)
    {s' : R' ⟶ V'} (hsa' : a' ≫ s' = 𝟙 V') (hsb' : b' ≫ s' = pullback.fst w' w' ≫ j')
    {r : R ⟶ R'} (hra : a ≫ r = v ≫ a')
    (hrb : b ≫ r = etaleRelationTransition w' u ≫ b') :
    IsPullback r s s' v
declarations.comment: the displayed square for R_i glued from V_i and W_i x_{U_i} W_i is cartesian

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isColimit_algebraicSpaces_of_scheme
declarations.doc:
Under descent of separated étale families and preservation of the scheme
colimit by étale base change, the colimit is also a colimit of algebraic spaces.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isColimit_algebraicSpaces_of_scheme
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I]
    (D : I ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (c : Cocone D)
    (_hColimit : IsColimit ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).mapCocone c))
    (hCover : ∀ x : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj c.pt,
      ∃ (i : I) (y : (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj (D.obj i)),
        (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (c.ι.app i) y = x)
    (hEtaleColimit :
      ∀ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (v : U ⟶ c.pt),
        Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map v) →
        ∀ (E : I ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : E ⟶ D)
          (q : E ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj U),
          (∀ i, IsPullback (p.app i) (q.app i) (c.ι.app i) v) →
          IsColimit ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).mapCocone
            ({ pt := U, ι := q } : Cocone E)))
    (hEtaleDescent :
      ∀ (E : I ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : E ⟶ D),
        (∀ i, Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p.app i))) →
        (∀ i, _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated
          ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map (p.app i))) →
        (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j),
          IsPullback (E.map f) (p.app i) (p.app j) (D.map f)) →
        ∃ (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (v : U ⟶ c.pt)
          (q : E ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj U),
          Etale ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map v) ∧
          (∀ i, IsPullback (p.app i) (q.app i) (c.ι.app i) v)) :
    ∀ (F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u),
      IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F →
      ∀ (a : ∀ i : I, yoneda.obj (D.obj i) ⟶ F),
        (∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), yoneda.map (D.map f) ≫ a j = a i) →
        ∃! b : yoneda.obj c.pt ⟶ F,
          ∀ i, yoneda.map (c.ι.app i) ≫ b = a i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPushout_algebraicSpaces_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07SY.** The pushout `Y' = Y ⨿_X X'` of a thickening `X ⟶ X'` and an affine morphism
`X ⟶ Y` of schemes over `S` is also a pushout in the category of algebraic spaces over `S`. The
étale clause of Stacks 07RX enters through `Stacks.Pushout.etale_gluingFunctor_obj_iff` and
Stacks 06AD through `Stacks.Thickenings.forall_isAffine_of_isThickening`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPushout_algebraicSpaces_of_isThickening_of_isAffineHom
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {X X' Y Y' : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (i : X ⟶ X') (f : X ⟶ Y) (a : X' ⟶ Y') (b : Y ⟶ Y')
    (hi : IsThickening ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map i))
    [IsAffineHom ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f)]
    (hPushout : IsPushout ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map i)
      ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map f)
      ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map a)
      ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map b)) :
    IsPushout
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (yoneda.map i) :
        (⟨yoneda.obj X, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS X⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
        (⟨yoneda.obj X', isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS X'⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (yoneda.map f) :
        (⟨yoneda.obj X, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS X⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
        (⟨yoneda.obj Y, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS Y⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (yoneda.map a) :
        (⟨yoneda.obj X', isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS X'⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
        (⟨yoneda.obj Y', isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS Y'⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
      (ObjectProperty.homMk (yoneda.map b) :
        (⟨yoneda.obj Y, isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS Y⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶
        (⟨yoneda.obj Y', isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS Y'⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.factorizationEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The category `𝒞_Λ` is equivalent to the opposite of the category of factorizations
`Spec k ⟶ Spec A ⟶ S` of the given point by the spectrum of an Artinian local ring with
residue field identified with `k`.**
declarations.statement:
public def factorizationEquivalence :
    ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, u, u} Λ k ≌ (ArtinianLocalFactorization S k x)ᵒᵖ
declarations.comment: the category 𝒞_Λ is equivalent to the opposite of the category of factorizations Spec k ⟶ Spec A ⟶ S of the point, with A Artinian local and its residue field identified with k

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.artinianLocalAlgCatEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The category `𝒞_Λ` does not depend, up to canonical equivalence, on the choice of the
affine open `Spec Λ ⊂ S` through which the point factors.** Both are equivalent to the
opposite of the category of factorizations of the point, which refers only to the point.
declarations.statement:
public def artinianLocalAlgCatEquiv :
    ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, u, u} Λ k ≌ ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, u, u} Λ' k
declarations.comment: the category 𝒞_Λ is independent, up to canonical equivalence, of the choice of the affine open Spec Λ ⊂ S the point factors through

registrations.name: Deformation.Artin.predeformationCategory
registrations.comment: the construction of the category 𝓕_{𝓧,k,x₀} of deformations of x₀, its objects and its reversed morphisms, together with its projection to 𝒞_Λ

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.ArtinianLocalFactorization
declarations.doc:
A factorization `Spec(k) ⟶ Spec(A) ⟶ S` of a finite-type field-valued point
of a locally Noetherian scheme, where `A` is an Artinian local ring and the first arrow
identifies `k` with its residue field.
declarations.statement:
public structure ArtinianLocalFactorization (S : Scheme.{u}) (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (x : Spec (CommRingCat.of k) ⟶ S) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType x]
    [QuasiCompact x]

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.predeformationCategory
declarations.doc: The predeformation category `𝓕_{𝓧,k,x₀}` and its canonical functor to `𝒞_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def predeformationCategory :
    PredeformationConstruction iΛ q x₀ hx₀

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.predeformationCategory_isPredeformationCategory
declarations.doc:
The canonical deformation category of a point of a fibred category is a
predeformation category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem predeformationCategory_isPredeformationCategory
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    let C := Deformation.Artin.predeformationCategory iΛ
      (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) x₀ hx₀
    letI : Category C.carrier := C.category
    Deformation.IsPredeformationCategory C.projection

declarations.name: ann_extension_eq_ann_baseChange_elem
declarations.doc:
For a flat ring map `φ : R → S` and any `m` in an `R`-module `M`, the extension of the
annihilator `Ann_R(m)` to `S` equals the `S`-annihilator of the base-changed element
`1 ⊗ m ∈ S ⊗_R M`: `Ann_R(m) S = Ann_S(1 ⊗ m)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ann_extension_eq_ann_baseChange_elem [Module.Flat R S] (m : M) :
    Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (Ideal.torsionOf R M m)
      = Ideal.torsionOf S (S ⊗[R] M) ((1 : S) ⊗ₜ[R] m)

declarations.name: ann_extension_eq_ann_baseChange_module
declarations.doc:
For a flat ring map `φ : R → S` and a finite `R`-module `M`, the extension of the
annihilator `Ann_R(M)` to `S` equals the `S`-annihilator of the base change `S ⊗_R M`:
`Ann_R(M) S = Ann_S(S ⊗_R M)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ann_extension_eq_ann_baseChange_module [Module.Flat R S] [Module.Finite R M] :
    Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (Module.annihilator R M)
      = Module.annihilator S (S ⊗[R] M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport_pullback
declarations.doc:
The scheme-theoretic inverse image of the scheme-theoretic support of a finite type
quasi-coherent module along a flat morphism is the scheme-theoretic support of its pullback.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_pullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) [Flat f]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [F.IsFiniteType] :
    schemeTheoreticSupport ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F) =
      (schemeTheoreticSupport F).comap f

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.SchemeColimits.higherDirectImage_preservesFilteredColimits
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes, its `p`-th higher direct
image functor on sheaves of abelian groups preserves all filtered colimits.
declarations.statement:
instance higherDirectImage_preservesFilteredColimits
    {X S : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact f] [AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiSeparated f] (p : ℕ) :
    PreservesFilteredColimits
      ((TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward AddCommGrpCat.{u} f.base).rightDerived p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Simplicial.Descent.cartesianObjectsOverEquivalenceDescentData
declarations.doc:
Cartesian simplicial objects over `X` are equivalent to descent data consisting of an
object over `X₀` and a normalized transition isomorphism satisfying the cocycle condition.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cartesianObjectsOverEquivalenceDescentData (X : SimplicialObject C) :
    ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun Y : Over X ↦ Y.hom.Equifibered) ≌
      DescentDatum X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_normalizationScheme_iso_pullback_of_smooth
declarations.doc:
**Normalization and smooth morphisms.** Let `φ : X ⟶ Y` be a smooth morphism of schemes and
assume every quasi-compact open of `Y` has finitely many irreducible components. Then the same is
true for `X`, and there is a unique isomorphism `X^ν ≅ X ×_Y Y^ν` over `X`, where `X^ν` and `Y^ν`
are the normalizations of `X` and `Y`.

Existence is the cartesian square `AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_normalizationSchemeMap_of_smooth`;
uniqueness holds because the only endomorphism of `X^ν` over `X` is the identity, by the universal
property `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.existsUnique_lift_normalization`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_normalizationScheme_iso_pullback_of_smooth {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (φ : X ⟶ Y)
    [Smooth φ] (hY : ∀ U : Y.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set Y) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite) :
    ∃ hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite,
      ∃! e : X.normalizationScheme hX ≅ pullback φ (Y.normalization hY),
        e.hom ≫ pullback.fst φ (Y.normalization hY) = X.normalization hX

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsModuleFiberTransitionIso
declarations.doc:
**The cartesian condition of Stacks 07TF for sheaves of modules**, expressed through the
2-morphism of this file: a sheaf of `O`-modules on the total site of a simplicial site is
cartesian when every canonical transition `f_φ^*F_m ⟶ F_n` between its component restrictions,
namely `moduleFiberTransition`, is an isomorphism.

This is part (2) of the source definition; parts (1), (3) and (4) are
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianSheaf`, `.IsCartesianAbSheaf` and the
derived-category conditions. The same condition stated through the transition of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Simplicial.ComponentRingedTopos.ModuleTransition` is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianModule`.
declarations.comment: part (2), for the module fibre transition of the component 2-morphism

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianDerivedModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TF (4).** An object `K` of the derived category of `O`-modules on the total site
is *cartesian* when the derived transition `Lf_φ^* K_m ⟶ K_n` of its restrictions along every
simplex map `φ : [m] ⟶ [n]` is an isomorphism.

Parts (1), (2) and (3) of the source definition are
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianSheaf` and `.IsCartesianAbSheaf`,
`.IsModuleFiberTransitionIso`, and `.IsCartesianDerived'`.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCartesianDerivedModule (K : DerivedCategory (S.totalRingedTopos O).Modules) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (4), cartesian objects of D(O): the derived transitions Lf_phi^* K_m -> K_n are isomorphisms

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TF (2).** A sheaf of `O`-modules on the total site of a simplicial-site situation
is *cartesian* if every canonical transition `f_φ^*ℱₘ ⟶ ℱₙ` between its restrictions to the
components is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCartesianModule (O : Sheaf S.totalTopology CommRingCat.{u})
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (S.totalRingSheaf O)) : Prop
declarations.comment: cartesian modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.IsCartesianModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TF (2) for the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme.** A sheaf of
`𝒪_X`-modules on the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme `X` is *cartesian* when every
transition `(X φ)^* F_m ⟶ F_n` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: public def IsCartesianModule (X : SimplicialObject Scheme.{u}) (F : Modules X) : Prop
declarations.comment: part (2), for the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme (the site of 09VL, which this development does not carry as a term of Situation 09WE), with the component modules of `ZariskiModulePushforward` and the transition of 09WF constructed here

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TF.** A sheaf of sets on the total site of a simplicial site is *cartesian* if
every canonical transition `f_φ⁻¹ Fₘ ⟶ Fₙ` between its components is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCartesianSheaf (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u})
    (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology (Type u)) : Prop
declarations.comment: cartesian sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianAbSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TF.** A sheaf of abelian groups on the total site of a simplicial site is
*cartesian* if the canonical transitions of its underlying sheaf of sets are isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsCartesianAbSheaf (S : SimplicialSiteSituation.{u})
    (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) : Prop
declarations.comment: cartesian sheaves of abelian groups

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianDerived'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TF.** An object of the derived category of abelian sheaves on the total site of a
simplicial site is *cartesian* if the canonical transition along every simplex map is an
isomorphism.

The derived categories are the standard ones and the transition is `derivedComponentTransition`;
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianDerived` states the condition for an arbitrary
choice of derived categories.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCartesianDerived' (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) : Prop
declarations.comment: cartesian objects of the derived category

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianDerived
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TF (3).** An object of the derived category of abelian sheaves on the total site
is cartesian when the canonical transition along every simplex map is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsCartesianDerived (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) : Prop
declarations.comment: cartesian_derived_sheaf

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianDerivedModule_iff_faces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TG (4).** An object of the derived category of `O`-modules on the total site of
a simplicial site is cartesian if and only if the derived transition along every face map is an
isomorphism.

The simplex maps whose derived transition is invertible form a multiplicative class: the
identity law is `isIso_derivedComponentModuleTransition_id` and the composition law is the
cocycle condition `derivedComponentModuleTransition_comp` of Stacks 0D9P together with
Stacks 0D6D. Every arrow of the simplex category is a composite of faces and degeneracies, and
`SimplexCategory.δ_comp_σ_self` exhibits each degeneracy as the second factor of a composite
that is an identity, so no separate hypothesis on the degeneracies is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianDerivedModule_iff_faces
    (K : DerivedCategory (S.totalRingedTopos O).Modules) :
    S.IsCartesianDerivedModule O K ↔
      ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)),
        IsIso ((S.derivedComponentModuleTransition O (SimplexCategory.δ i)).app K)
declarations.comment: face criterion for objects of D(O)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isCartesianModule_iff_faces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TG (3) for the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme.** A sheaf of
`𝒪_X`-modules on the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme is cartesian if and only if the
transition `(d^{k+1}_i)^* F_k ⟶ F_{k+1}` along every face map is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCartesianModule_iff_faces (X : SimplicialObject Scheme.{u}) (F : Modules X) :
    IsCartesianModule X F ↔
      ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)),
        IsIso (componentModuleTransition X (SimplexCategory.δ i).op F)
declarations.comment: part (3), the criterion for sheaves of MODULES, for the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme (the site of 09VL, which this development does not carry as a term of Situation 09WE) with the cartesian condition of `ZariskiCartesianModule`. Parts (1) and (2) of the source, for sheaves of sets and for objects of the derived category of the total site, and part (4), for the derived pullbacks, are not covered here; parts (1) and (2) for a simplicial-site situation are `CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianSheaf_iff_faces` and `isCartesianAbSheaf_iff_faces`

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianDerived_iff_faces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TG (2).** An object of the derived category of abelian sheaves on the total site
of a simplicial site is cartesian if and only if the canonical derived transition along every
face map is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianDerived_iff_faces (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) :
    S.IsCartesianDerived K ↔
      ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)),
        IsIso ((derivedTransition S (SimplexCategory.δ i)).app K)
declarations.comment: face criterion for objects of D(C_total)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianSheaf_iff_faces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TG.** A sheaf of sets on the total site of a simplicial site is cartesian if and
only if the canonical transition along every face map is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianSheaf_iff_faces (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology (Type u)) :
    IsCartesianSheaf S F ↔
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)),
        IsIso ((fiberTransition S (SimplexCategory.δ i)).app F)
declarations.comment: face criterion for sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianAbSheaf_iff_faces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TG.** A sheaf of abelian groups on the total site of a simplicial site is
cartesian if and only if the canonical transition along every face map is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianAbSheaf_iff_faces (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) :
    IsCartesianAbSheaf S F ↔
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)),
        IsIso ((abelianFiberTransition S (SimplexCategory.δ i)).app F)
declarations.comment: face criterion for sheaves of abelian groups

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isCartesianModule_iff_faces
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TG (3).** A sheaf of `O`-modules on the total site of a simplicial site is
cartesian if and only if the canonical transition along every face map is an isomorphism.

The simplex maps whose transition is invertible form a multiplicative class, the identity and
composition laws being the unit and cocycle laws `fiberTransitionModules_id` and
`fiberTransitionModules_comp` of Stacks 09WF for modules. Every arrow of the simplex category is
a composite of faces and degeneracies, and `SimplexCategory.δ_comp_σ_self` exhibits each
degeneracy as the second factor of a composite that is an identity, so no separate hypothesis on
the degeneracies is needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCartesianModule_iff_faces (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (S.totalRingSheaf O)) :
    IsCartesianModule S O M ↔
      ∀ (k : ℕ) (i : Fin (k + 2)),
        IsIso (S.fiberTransitionModules O (SimplexCategory.δ i) M)
declarations.comment: face criterion for sheaves of modules

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cartesianModuleSheafEquivCartesianModulePair
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TH.** Let `S` be a simplicial-site situation and `O` a sheaf of commutative rings on
its total site. The category of cartesian sheaves of `O`-modules is equivalent to the category of
pairs `(ℱ, α)`, where `ℱ` is an `O₀`-module and `α : f_{δ¹₁}^*ℱ ≅ f_{δ¹₀}^*ℱ` is an isomorphism
of `O₁`-modules such that `f_{δ²₁}^*α = f_{δ²₀}^*α ∘ f_{δ²₂}^*α` as `O₂`-module maps. The functor
of the equivalence takes a cartesian module to its degree-zero restriction and the comparison of
its two transitions to degree one.
declarations.statement:
def cartesianModuleSheafEquivCartesianModulePair :
    S.CartesianModuleSheaf O ≌ CartesianModulePair S O

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
Let `f : V ⟶ U` be a morphism of simplicial schemes and let `F` be a quasi-coherent module on
`U_Zar`. Then the pullback `f^*F` is a quasi-coherent module on `V_Zar`.
declarations.comment: for a quasi-coherent module, which is the hypothesis the source states; proved through the localization 04J0 of a morphism of ringed sites at an object, in the form asking only that every object of the source site admit an arrow into the image of the functor, applied on the equi-universe model of the total Zariski site, and not through 0D7M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback_of_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TI for a globally presented module.** For a morphism of simplicial schemes
`f : V ⟶ U` and a sheaf of `𝒪_U`-modules on `U_Zar` admitting a global presentation, the
pullback `f^*F` is a quasi-coherent sheaf of `𝒪_V`-modules on `V_Zar`.
declarations.comment: for a module admitting a GLOBAL presentation on the total Zariski site, a strengthening of the source's hypothesis that it be quasi-coherent, i.e. presented only locally. The source's statement is proved in full at `AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePullback`, through the localization 04J0 of a morphism of ringed sites at an object on the equi-universe model of the total Zariski site; this is the direct specialization of 03DO, which needs no localization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isQuasicoherent_componentModule_modulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TJ for the components of the pushforward.** Let `f : V ⟶ U` be a morphism of
simplicial schemes and `G` a sheaf of `𝒪_V`-modules on the total Zariski site. If `f_n` is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated and the degree-`n` component `G_n` is a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_{V_n}`-module, then the degree-`n` component `(f_*G)_n` of the pushforward is a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_{U_n}`-module.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherent_componentModule_modulePushforward (f : V ⟶ U)
    (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) [QuasiCompact (f.app n)] [QuasiSeparated (f.app n)]
    (G : Modules V) [((componentModule V n).obj G).IsQuasicoherent] :
    ((componentModule U n).obj ((modulePushforward f).obj G)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the quasi-coherence of the COMPONENTS of the pushforward only: `(f_*G)_n` is a quasi-coherent module on `U_n` as soon as `f_n` is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `G_n` is quasi-coherent. This is the source's identification `F_n = f_{n,*}G_n` (09VP, here `componentModulePushforwardIso`) together with 01LC, and it needs neither the cartesian hypothesis on `f` nor the flatness of the face maps of `U`. What is NOT proved is that `f_*G` is quasi-coherent on the total Zariski site: the source gets that from 0D7M, of which this development has only the right-hand side (`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.IsCartesianWithQuasicoherentComponents`, neither direction of the equivalence), and the other half of that right-hand side -- that `f_*G` is cartesian, which is where 02KH and the flatness of the face maps enter -- cannot even be stated here, the development carrying no cartesian-module predicate for the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TJ.** Let `f : V ⟶ U` be a cartesian morphism of simplicial schemes, assume that
the face maps `d^n_j` of `U` are flat and that the components `f_n : V_n ⟶ U_n` are quasi-compact
and quasi-separated. Then for a quasi-coherent module `G` on the total Zariski site of `V` the
direct image `f_*G` is a quasi-coherent module on the total Zariski site of `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward (f : V ⟶ U)
    (hcart : NatTrans.Equifibered f)
    (hflat : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : Fin (k + 2)), Flat (U.δ j))
    (hqc : ∀ k : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, QuasiCompact (f.app k))
    (hqs : ∀ k : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparated (f.app k))
    (G : Modules V) (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePushforward f).obj G).IsQuasicoherentOnSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.quasicoherentModulePullbackAdjPushforward'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TK.** Let `f : V ⟶ U` be a cartesian morphism of simplicial schemes such that
every face map of `U` is flat and every component `f_n : V_n ⟶ U_n` is quasi-compact and
quasi-separated. Then the pullback `f^*` and the pushforward `f_*` are an adjoint pair between
the category of quasi-coherent modules on `U_Zar` and the category of quasi-coherent modules on
`V_Zar`.

Quasi-coherence of the pullback is Stacks 07TI and of the pushforward is Stacks 07TJ;
adjointness itself is the adjunction of Stacks 03D7 on all sheaves of modules, restricted along
the two full subcategory inclusions.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def quasicoherentModulePullbackAdjPushforward' (f : V ⟶ U)
    (hcart : NatTrans.Equifibered f)
    (hflat : ∀ (k : ℕ) (j : Fin (k + 2)), Flat (U.δ j))
    (hqc : ∀ k : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, QuasiCompact (f.app k))
    (hqs : ∀ k : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparated (f.app k)) :
    quasicoherentModulePullback f ⊣ quasicoherentModulePushforward' f hcart hflat hqc hqs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackToSimplicialSchemeComponentIso
declarations.doc:
**The pullback is computed degreewise**: the component in degree `n` of the pullback of a
quasi-coherent `O_S`-module `M` to the total Zariski site of `(X/S)_•` is the pullback of `M`
along the structure morphism `(X/S)_n ⟶ S`, naturally in `M`.
declarations.comment: the functor is pullback: its component in degree n is the pullback along the structure morphism (X/S)_n ⟶ S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_pullbackToSimplicialScheme_of_section
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes with a section `σ`, and let `(X/S)_•` be the
simplicial scheme of Stacks 024A. Then pullback is an equivalence between the quasi-coherent
`O_S`-modules and the quasi-coherent modules on the total Zariski site `((X/S)_•)_Zar`. The
pullback functor is `AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackToSimplicialScheme`; its component in degree `n`
is the pullback along `(X/S)_n ⟶ S`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackToSimplicialSchemeComponentIso`).
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_pullbackToSimplicialScheme_of_section (σ : S ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 S) :
    (pullbackToSimplicialScheme f).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEquivalence_pullbackToSimplicialScheme_of_fpqcLocalSection
declarations.doc:
Pullback is an equivalence between the quasi-coherent `O_S`-modules and the quasi-coherent
modules on `((X/S)_•)_Zar` already when `f` has a section only fpqc locally on `S`: there is an
fpqc covering `{p_i : T_i ⟶ S}` and morphisms `s_i : T_i ⟶ X` with `s_i ≫ f = p_i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_pullbackToSimplicialScheme_of_fpqcLocalSection {I : Type*}
    {T : I → Scheme.{u}} (p : ∀ i, T i ⟶ S)
    (hp : Presieve.ofArrows T p ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.{u} S)
    (s : ∀ i, T i ⟶ X) (hs : ∀ i, s i ≫ f = p i) :
    (pullbackToSimplicialScheme f).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the footnote: it is enough that f have a section fpqc locally on S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasicoherentDescentEquivalenceOfSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TL, in its descent-data form.** For a morphism of schemes `f : X ⟶ S` with a
section, pullback is an equivalence between the category of quasi-coherent `O_S`-modules and the
category of quasi-coherent descent data for `{f}`, i.e. the quasi-coherent modules on the
simplicial scheme `(X/S)_•` of Stacks 024A.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentDescentEquivalenceOfSection
    (f : X ⟶ S) (σ : S ⟶ X) (hσ : σ ≫ f = 𝟙 S) :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ≌
      QuasicoherentDescentData (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{0} f).f
declarations.comment: the equivalence, with its target in descent-data form: the quasi-coherent descent data for {f}, not yet identified with QCoh(((X/S)_bullet)_Zar); that identification is the cited 07TJ together with 07TH, and 07TJ is absent here

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.quasicoherentDescentEquivalenceOfFpqcLocalSection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TL in the stronger form of its footnote, in the descent-data form.** If `f` admits
a section after an fpqc covering of `S`, pullback is an equivalence between the quasi-coherent
`O_S`-modules and the quasi-coherent descent data for `{f}`, i.e. the quasi-coherent modules on
the simplicial scheme `(X/S)_•` of Stacks 024A.
declarations.statement:
def quasicoherentDescentEquivalenceOfFpqcLocalSection
    (f : X ⟶ S) {I : Type v} {T : I → Scheme.{u}} (p : ∀ i, T i ⟶ S)
    (hp : Presieve.ofArrows T p ∈ Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.{u} S)
    (s : ∀ i, T i ⟶ X) (hs : ∀ i, s i ≫ f = p i) :
    (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent S.ringCatSheaf).FullSubcategory ≌
      QuasicoherentDescentData (PreZeroHypercover.singleton.{0} f).f
declarations.comment: the footnote's stronger form, f having a section only fpqc locally on S; target in descent-data form as above, its identification with QCoh(((X/S)_bullet)_Zar) being the cited 07TJ together with 07TH, and 07TJ is absent here

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.groupoidSimplicialScheme
declarations.doc: **Stacks 07TN.** The simplicial scheme associated to a groupoid scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def groupoidSimplicialScheme {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (G : GroupoidScheme S) : GroupoidSimplicialScheme G

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.quasicoherentModuleEquivQuasicoherentOnTotalSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TP.**  Let `S` be a scheme, `(U,R,s,t,c)` a groupoid scheme over `S` and `X` the
simplicial scheme of Stacks 07TN.  The category of quasi-coherent modules on `(U,R,s,t,c)` in
the sense of Stacks 03LI is equivalent to the category of quasi-coherent modules on `X_{Zar}`.

The equivalence is the composite of three steps.  Quasi-coherent modules on the total Zariski
site are the pairs `(ℱ, α)` of Stacks 07TH with quasi-coherent degree-zero module, by Stacks 07TH
and Stacks 0D7M; such pairs are the groupoid descent data of `(U,R,s,t,c)`, because in degrees
`≤ 2` the nerve is `U`, `R` and `R ×_{s,U,t} R` with faces the source, the target, the two
projections and the composition law; and groupoid descent data are the quasi-coherent modules of
Stacks 03LI, which is `descentDataEquivQuasicoherentModule`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def quasicoherentModuleEquivQuasicoherentOnTotalSite :
    QuasicoherentModule G ≌ QuasicoherentZariskiModule (groupoidSimplicialScheme G).toSchemes
declarations.comment: The normalization `e^*α = id` of Stacks 03LI, which the source's proof passes over, is proved here: it is automatic for an invertible descent morphism satisfying the cocycle condition.

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.groupoidCechNerveTarget
declarations.doc:
The canonical cartesian map from the Čech nerve of the source of a groupoid scheme to its
nerve.

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.isQuasicoherent_pushforwardSource_pullbackTarget
declarations.doc:
**The first assertion of Tag 07TR.**  For a groupoid scheme whose source map is
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the module `s_* t^* 𝒢` is quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherent_pushforwardSource_pullbackTarget
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [QuasiSeparated G.source.left]
    (𝒢 : G.objects.left.Modules) [𝒢.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward G.source.left).obj
      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).obj 𝒢)).IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: the quasi-coherence of `s_* t^* 𝒢`

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.coinductionAlpha
declarations.doc:
**The canonical isomorphism `α` of Tag 07TR.**  For a groupoid scheme `(U, R, s, t, c)` with
`s` and `t` flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated and a quasi-coherent module `𝒢` on `U`, this
is the canonical isomorphism `t^* s_* t^* 𝒢 ≅ s^* s_* t^* 𝒢`.  It is the composite of the two
flat base-change isomorphisms of the squares of the composition diagram with the identification
of `pr_0^* t^* 𝒢` and `c^* t^* 𝒢`.

This does not include the cocycle condition and the normalization along the identity section,
which are what make `(s_* t^* 𝒢, α)` a quasi-coherent module on the groupoid scheme.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coinductionAlpha [Flat G.source.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [QuasiSeparated G.source.left]
    (𝒢 : G.objects.left.Modules) [𝒢.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward G.source.left).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).obj 𝒢)) ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback G.source.left).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward G.source.left).obj
          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).obj 𝒢))
declarations.comment: the construction of the canonical isomorphism `α`; not the cocycle and identity conditions making `(s_* t^* 𝒢, α)` a module on the groupoid, and not the functor to `QCoh(U, R, s, t, c)` nor its right adjointness to the forgetful functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.coinductionAlpha_naturality
declarations.doc:
The canonical isomorphism `α` is natural in `𝒢`, which is the sense in which the
construction `𝒢 ↦ (s_* t^* 𝒢, α)` is canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem coinductionAlpha_naturality [Flat G.source.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [QuasiSeparated G.source.left]
    {𝒢 𝒢' : G.objects.left.Modules} [𝒢.IsQuasicoherent] [𝒢'.IsQuasicoherent]
    (φ : 𝒢 ⟶ 𝒢') :
    (coinductionAlpha G 𝒢).hom ≫
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback G.source.left).map
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward G.source.left).map
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).map φ)) =
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).map
          ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward G.source.left).map
            ((Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).map φ)) ≫
        (coinductionAlpha G 𝒢').hom
declarations.comment: the naturality of `α` in `𝒢`

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.coinductionAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Coinduction is right adjoint to forgetting a groupoid descent datum.**  This is the
adjunction of Tag 07TR.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def coinductionAdjunction : quasicoherentForget G ⊣ coinduction G
declarations.comment: the right adjointness of the coinduction functor to the forgetful functor

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.cocycle_coinductionAlpha
declarations.doc:
**The cocycle condition for the coinduction descent isomorphism.**  On the scheme of
composable arrows, applying `α` to the two arrows in succession agrees with applying it to their
composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem cocycle_coinductionAlpha
    [Flat G.source.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [QuasiSeparated G.source.left]
    (𝒢 : G.objects.left.Modules) [𝒢.IsQuasicoherent] :
    successiveDescent G (coinductionAlpha G 𝒢).hom =
      reindexHom G.comp.left (coinductionAlpha G 𝒢).hom
declarations.comment: the cocycle condition for `α`, the first of the two conditions making `(s_* t^* 𝒢, α)` a quasi-coherent module on the groupoid scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.identity_coinductionAlpha
declarations.doc:
**The normalization of the coinduction descent isomorphism along the identity section.**
Pulling `α` back along the identity section gives the identity of `s_* t^* 𝒢`.  With
`cocycle_coinductionAlpha` this exhibits `(s_* t^* 𝒢, α)` as a quasi-coherent module on the
groupoid scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem identity_coinductionAlpha
    [Flat G.source.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [QuasiSeparated G.source.left]
    (𝒢 : G.objects.left.Modules) [𝒢.IsQuasicoherent] :
    identityDescent G (coinductionAlpha G 𝒢).hom =
      𝟙 ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward G.source.left).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback G.target.left).obj 𝒢))
declarations.comment: the normalization of `α` along the identity section, the second of the two conditions making `(s_* t^* 𝒢, α)` a quasi-coherent module on the groupoid scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCoherent_pullback_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07TT.** For a flat, surjective, quasi-compact and quasi-separated
morphism `f : Y ⟶ X` of locally Noetherian schemes, a quasi-coherent module `F` on `X` and a
coherent submodule `G` of `f^*F`, the fibre product of the unit `F ⟶ f_* f^* F` with the
pushforward of the inclusion is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_pullback_pushforward {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [Flat f] [Surjective f]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (G : Y.Modules) [G.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsCoherent]
    (φ : G ⟶ (Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj F) [Mono φ] :
    (pullback ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f).unit.app F)
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).map φ)).IsCoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_filtered_diagram_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07TU.**  Let `(U, R, s, t, c)` be a groupoid scheme over `S` with `U`
and `R` Noetherian and with `s` and `t` flat, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.  Then every
quasi-coherent module `(ℱ, β)` on the groupoid scheme is the colimit of a filtered diagram of
quasi-coherent modules on the groupoid scheme whose underlying modules on `U` are coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_filtered_diagram_of_isCoherent
    [IsNoetherian G.objects.left] [IsNoetherian G.arrows.left]
    [Flat G.source.left] [Flat G.target.left]
    [QuasiCompact G.source.left] [QuasiCompact G.target.left]
    [QuasiSeparated G.source.left] [QuasiSeparated G.target.left]
    (M : QuasicoherentModule G) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (inst : SmallCategory I),
      let _ := inst
      ∃ (_ : IsFiltered I) (D : I ⥤ QuasicoherentModule G)
        (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj M),
        (∀ i, (D.obj i).module.IsCoherent) ∧
          Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk M φ))
declarations.comment: every quasi-coherent module on the groupoid scheme is the colimit of a filtered diagram of quasi-coherent modules on the groupoid scheme with coherent underlying modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GroupoidScheme.exists_filtered_diagram_of_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07TV.** A quasi-coherent module on an affine groupoid scheme whose
arrow ring is free over its object ring via the source map is a filtered colimit of
finite-type groupoid modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_filtered_diagram_of_isFiniteType
    {S : Scheme.{u}} (G : GroupoidScheme S)
    [IsAffine G.objects.left] [IsAffine G.arrows.left]
    (hfree : letI : Algebra Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤) :=
      G.source.left.appTop.hom.toAlgebra
      Module.Free Γ(G.objects.left, ⊤) Γ(G.arrows.left, ⊤))
    (M : QuasicoherentModule G) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (inst : SmallCategory I),
      let _ := inst
      ∃ (_ : IsFiltered I)
        (D : I ⥤ QuasicoherentModule G)
        (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj M),
        (∀ i, (D.obj i).module.IsFiniteType) ∧
          Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk M φ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquiv_of_isAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
For an algebraic space `X` over `S` with a surjective étale chart `φ : U ⟶ X`, the invariant
locally closed subschemes of `U` correspond bijectively to the locally closed subspaces of `X`,
and the bijection is characterised by pullback along `φ`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquiv` with its hypothesis
`hdesc` supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquiv_of_isAlgebraicSpace
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) :
    {e : InvariantLocallyClosedSubscheme B S hS hs ≃
      LocallyClosedQuotientSubspace B S hS (X := X) //
      ∀ Z, ((e Z).1.preimage φ) = subschemePoints B S hS Z.1}
declarations.comment: canonical bijection

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closed_iff_of_isAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
The subspace of `X` corresponding to an invariant subscheme of the chart is closed exactly when
that subscheme is closed in the chart.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.closed_iff` with its hypothesis `hdesc` supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closed_iff_of_isAlgebraicSpace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (Z : InvariantLocallyClosedSubscheme B S hS hs) :
    IsClosedSubspace B S hS
        ((invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquiv_of_isAlgebraicSpace B S hS hs he hX).1 Z).1 ↔
      _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion Z.1.arrow
declarations.comment: closedness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.open_iff_of_isAlgebraicSpace
declarations.doc:
The subspace of `X` corresponding to an invariant subscheme of the chart is open exactly when
that subscheme is open in the chart.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.open_iff` with its hypothesis `hdesc` supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem open_iff_of_isAlgebraicSpace (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (Z : InvariantLocallyClosedSubscheme B S hS hs) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS
        ((invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquiv_of_isAlgebraicSpace B S hS hs he hX).1 Z).1 ↔
      _root_.AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion Z.1.arrow
declarations.comment: openness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Presentation.invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquivOfExtendsRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TW**, the canonical bijection, with invariance of the subschemes of the
presenting scheme taken in the groupoid sense of Stacks 03BC part (4) against any groupoid
scheme extending the presenting relation.

Effective descent of immersions along the surjective étale morphisms of the site, which is
Stacks 02W8 in the form Stacks 03I2 consumes, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isEffectiveDescentAlongSurjectiveEtale_isImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def Presentation.invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquivOfExtendsRelation
    (P : Presentation B S hS X hX) {G : GroupoidScheme S}
    (hG : ExtendsRelation (prod.lift ((Over.post B.inclusion).map P.target)
      ((Over.post B.inclusion).map P.source)) G)
    (hobj : G.objects.left = (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj P.U) :
    {e : {Z : Subobject ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj P.U) //
            AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion Z.arrow ∧
              IsInvariantMonomorphism G (Z.arrow ≫ eqToHom hobj.symm)} ≃
          LocallyClosedQuotientSubspace B S hS (X := X) //
      ∀ Z, ((e Z).1.preimage P.toSpace) = subschemePoints B S hS Z.1}
declarations.comment: the canonical bijection, with invariance taken in the groupoid sense

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Presentation.closed_iff_of_extendsRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TW**, closedness, with invariance taken in the groupoid sense: the subspace of
the presented algebraic space corresponding to an invariant subscheme of the presenting scheme
is closed exactly when that subscheme is closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem Presentation.closed_iff_of_extendsRelation
    (P : Presentation B S hS X hX) {G : GroupoidScheme S}
    (hG : ExtendsRelation (prod.lift ((Over.post B.inclusion).map P.target)
      ((Over.post B.inclusion).map P.source)) G)
    (hobj : G.objects.left = (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj P.U)
    (Z : {Z : Subobject ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj P.U) //
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion Z.arrow ∧
        IsInvariantMonomorphism G (Z.arrow ≫ eqToHom hobj.symm)}) :
    IsClosedSubspace B S hS
        ((P.invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquivOfExtendsRelation B S hS hG hobj).1 Z).1 ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion Z.1.arrow
declarations.comment: closedness, with invariance taken in the groupoid sense

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.Presentation.open_iff_of_extendsRelation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TW**, openness, with invariance taken in the groupoid sense: the subspace of
the presented algebraic space corresponding to an invariant subscheme of the presenting scheme
is open exactly when that subscheme is open.
declarations.statement:
theorem Presentation.open_iff_of_extendsRelation
    (P : Presentation B S hS X hX) {G : GroupoidScheme S}
    (hG : ExtendsRelation (prod.lift ((Over.post B.inclusion).map P.target)
      ((Over.post B.inclusion).map P.source)) G)
    (hobj : G.objects.left = (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj P.U)
    (Z : {Z : Subobject ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj P.U) //
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion Z.arrow ∧
        IsInvariantMonomorphism G (Z.arrow ≫ eqToHom hobj.symm)}) :
    IsOpenSubspace B S hS
        ((P.invariantLocallyClosedSubschemeEquivOfExtendsRelation B S hS hG hobj).1 Z).1 ↔
      AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion Z.1.arrow
declarations.comment: openness, with invariance taken in the groupoid sense

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supp_restrictToChart_eq_preimage_supportOfSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TY.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module and let `φ : U ⟶ X` be an étale morphism from a scheme, that is, an object of the
small étale site of `X`.  Then the support of `φ^* F` as a module on the *scheme* `U` is the
inverse image under `|φ|` of the support of `F`:
`Supp(φ^* F) = |φ|^{-1}(Supp(F))`.

The proof is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supp_restrictToChart_eq_preimage_supportOfSheaf` with its
comparison `(φ^* F)_u ⊗_{𝒪_{U, u}} 𝒪_{X, x̄} ≅ F_{x̄}` supplied by Stacks 05VP,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_chartStalkTensorComparison`, which holds because `F` is
quasi-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem supp_restrictToChart_eq_preimage_supportOfSheaf_of_isQuasicoherent
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (U : SmallEtale B S hS X.1)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    SheafOfModules.supp (restrictToChart B S hS X.2 F U) =
      (fun u => pointsMap B S hS (yoneda.obj ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1).obj U))
          U.obj.hom
          ((pointsEquivScheme B S hS ((SmallEtale.toOver B S hS X.1).obj U)).symm u)) ⁻¹'
        supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F)
declarations.comment: the support of a quasi-coherent module pulled back along an étale chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nontrivial_geometricModuleStalk_iff_nontrivial_residueFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TZ, part (2), second equivalence.** Let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of
finite type on an algebraic space `X` over `S` and let `x̄` be a geometric point of `X`.  Then

`F_{x̄} ≠ 0 ↔ F_{x̄} ⊗_{𝒪_{X, x̄}} κ(x̄) ≠ 0`.

This is Nakayama's lemma.  The stalk is a finite module over the étale local ring by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.module_finite_geometricModuleStalk`, and the residue map is a local
homomorphism of local rings, so base change along it keeps a nonzero finite module nonzero
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nontrivial_extendScalars_of_isLocalHom`); the converse direction
needs no hypotheses at all
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nontrivial_of_nontrivial_extendScalars`).
declarations.statement:
theorem nontrivial_geometricModuleStalk_iff_nontrivial_residueFibre (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) :
    Nontrivial ↥(geometricModuleStalk B S hS X x F) ↔
      letI := isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 X.2 x
      Nontrivial ↥(geometricModuleResidueFibre B S hS X x F)
declarations.comment: part (2), second equivalence: the stalk at a geometric point is nonzero iff the fibre over the residue field is nonzero

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_modulePullback_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TZ, part (3).** Let `g : X' ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and
let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type.  Then the support of the pullback
`g^* F` of Stacks 03LU is the inverse image of the support of `F`:

`Supp(g^* F) = |g|^{-1}(Supp(F))`.

The pullback is again of finite type by Stacks 03DO,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_modulePullback`, which is the other clause of this
part of the tag.

At a geometric point `ȳ` of `X'` the stalk of the pullback is the base change
`(g^* F)_{ȳ} ≅ 𝒪_{X', ȳ} ⊗_{𝒪_{X, g ∘ ȳ}} F_{g ∘ ȳ}` of the stalk of `F` at the image
geometric point, by `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.geometricModuleStalkPullbackIso`.  One inclusion
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nontrivial_of_nontrivial_extendScalars`, which needs no
hypotheses.  The other is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nontrivial_extendScalars_of_isLocalHom`: the
stalk of `F` is a finite module over the étale local ring, the homomorphism of étale local
rings of Stacks 04NG is local, and the image geometric point detects the support because `F` is
quasi-coherent (the first equivalence of part (2)).
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_modulePullback_eq (g : X' ⟶ X) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS X'.1
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj F)) =
      pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom ⁻¹'
        supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F)
declarations.comment: part (3): the stalk of a pullback at a geometric point, and the equality of supports

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_supportOfSheaf_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TZ, part (1).** The support of an `𝒪_X`-module of finite type on an algebraic
space `X` is closed in the point set of `X`.

Outside the support pick a geometric point over the given point; its stalk vanishes, so there
is an étale chart carrying only the zero section of the module.  The image of the point set of
that chart is open, because an étale chart is open on points by clause (3) of Stacks 03BX, it
contains the given point, and it misses the support: a geometric point of `X` over a point of
the image lifts to the chart by Stacks 05VN, so the chart is a neighbourhood of it and its
stalk vanishes too.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_supportOfSheaf_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (F : Modules.{u, m} B S hS X hX) [SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F] :
    IsClosed (supportOfSheaf B S hS X ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F))
declarations.comment: support_closed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite_isFiniteTypeOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TZ.** Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `F` be a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module of finite type.  Then

1. the support of `F` is closed;
2. for a geometric point `x̄` of `X` lying over a point `x`,
   `x ∈ Supp(F) ↔ F_{x̄} ≠ 0` and `F_{x̄} ≠ 0 ↔ F_{x̄} ⊗_{𝒪_{X, x̄}} κ(x̄) ≠ 0`;
3. for every morphism `g : X' ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` the pullback `g^* F` of
   Stacks 03LU is again of finite type and `Supp(g^* F) = |g|^{-1}(Supp(F))`.

Clause (1) is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_supportOfSheaf_of_isFiniteTypeOnSite`, which
does not use quasi-coherence.  The two equivalences of clause (2) are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_supportOfSheaf_iff_nontrivial_geometricModuleStalk_of_liesOver`
and `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nontrivial_geometricModuleStalk_iff_nontrivial_residueFibre`.  The
two conclusions of clause (3) are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_modulePullback` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_modulePullback_eq`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite_isFiniteTypeOnSite
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hqc : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) :
    IsClosed (supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F)) ∧
      (∀ (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) (pt : points B S hS X.1), x.LiesOver pt →
        (pt ∈ supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F) ↔
            Nontrivial (geometricModuleStalk B S hS X x F)) ∧
          (Nontrivial (geometricModuleStalk B S hS X x F) ↔
            letI := isLocalRing_etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 X.2 x
            Nontrivial (geometricModuleResidueFibre B S hS X x F))) ∧
      ∀ (X' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (g : X' ⟶ X),
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj F) ∧
          supportOfSheaf B S hS X'.1
              ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj ((modulePullback B S hS g).obj F)) =
            pointsMap B S hS X'.1 g.hom ⁻¹'
              supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.mem_supportOfSheaf_iff_nontrivial_geometricModuleStalk_of_liesOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07TZ, part (2), first equivalence.** Let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module on an
algebraic space `X` and let `x̄` be a geometric point lying over a point `x` of `X`.  Then

`x ∈ Supp(F) ↔ F_{x̄} ≠ 0`.

The support of Stacks 04KA is defined by nonvanishing of the stalk at some geometric point over
`x`; the content here is that for a quasi-coherent module every geometric point over `x`
detects the support, so the equivalence holds at the given `x̄`.

Pick a small étale neighbourhood of `x̄`.  Nonvanishing of `F_{x̄}` is membership of the chart
point in the support of the chart restriction, and that support is the inverse image of the
support of `F` by Stacks 07TY; the chart point maps to the image of `x̄`, which is `x`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_supportOfSheaf_iff_nontrivial_geometricModuleStalk_of_liesOver
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] (x : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1)
    (pt : points B S hS X.1) (hx : x.LiesOver pt) :
    pt ∈ supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F) ↔
      Nontrivial (geometricModuleStalk B S hS X x F)
declarations.comment: part (2), first equivalence: the support against the stalk at a geometric point

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_eq_range_pointsMap_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**The support of a finite type `𝒪_X`-module is the set of points of its scheme-theoretic
support.**

The point set of a closed subspace is the zero locus of its defining ideal sheaf, and the ideal
sheaf cutting out the scheme-theoretic support is the annihilator ideal of `F`; so the claim is
that the support of `F` is the zero locus of its annihilator ideal sheaf.  One inclusion needs
only that the unit function lies in the annihilator ideal wherever that ideal is the whole of
`𝒪_X`, so `F` vanishes on every chart over such a chart and its support misses the image.  The
other is where finite type enters: off the support every geometric stalk of `F` vanishes, and
for a module of finite type that produces a small étale neighbourhood over which `F` has no
nonzero sections at all, hence a chart whose image contains the point and on which the
annihilator ideal is everything.

That the scheme-theoretic support is a closed subspace cut out by the annihilator ideal sheaf
is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedSubspace_schemeTheoreticSupport`, which quasi-
coherence and finite type supply.

This is part (4) of [Stacks, Tag 07U0] for the module on the ambient space.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_eq_range_pointsMap_schemeTheoreticSupport
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F) =
      Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F).toFunctor
        (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F).ι)
declarations.comment: part (4): the support of F is the point set of its scheme-theoretic support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U0, existence.**  A finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F` is the direct
image of a quasi-coherent module on its scheme-theoretic support, which is a closed subspace
of `X`.

That the scheme-theoretic support is a closed subspace, and that the ideal cutting it out is
the annihilator ideal of `F`, are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isClosedSubspace_schemeTheoreticSupport`; so that ideal
annihilates `F`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentEssImagePushforward_of_isClosedImmersion` turns that
into the module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hft : PresheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).J F.val) :
    ∃ (hZ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F))
      (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS
        (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).1
        (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).2),
      G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧ Nonempty ((modulePushforward B S hS
        (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
          ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)).obj G ≅ F)
declarations.comment: existence of the quasi-coherent module on the scheme-theoretic support

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U0, minimality.**  The scheme-theoretic support of `F` is contained in every
closed subspace of `X` from which `F` is a direct image.

The ideal cutting out such a closed subspace annihilates `F` by the first half of Stacks 04CJ
part (3), so that subspace is a member of the family being intersected.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_le (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).1
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).2)
    (e : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj G ≅ F) :
    schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F ≤ Z.1
declarations.comment: minimality: the scheme-theoretic support is contained in every closed subspace from which F is a direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.module_on_closedSubspace_unique
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U0, part (2).**  A module on a closed subspace of `X` whose direct image is `F`
is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the chosen identifications of the direct
images with `F`.

This is full faithfulness of the direct image along a closed immersion, Stacks 04CJ part (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem module_on_closedSubspace_unique (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (G H : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).1
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).2)
    (eG : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj G ≅ F)
    (eH : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj H ≅ F) :
    ∃! φ : G ≅ H,
      (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).map φ.hom ≫ eH.hom =
        eG.hom
declarations.comment: part (2): uniqueness up to unique isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteTypeOnSite_module_on_closedSubspace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U0, part (3).**  A module on a closed subspace of `X` whose direct image is a
module of finite type is itself of finite type.

By Stacks 04CJ part (2) it is isomorphic to the inverse image of `F`, which is of finite type by
Stacks 03DO, and finite type passes along an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeOnSite_module_on_closedSubspace (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).1
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).2)
    (e : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj G ≅ F) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite G
declarations.comment: part (3): the module on the closed subspace is of finite type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport_isSmallest_and_properties
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_isSmallest_and_properties (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) :
    ∃ hZ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F),
      -- existence of a quasi-coherent module on `Z` whose direct image is `F`
      (∃ G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).1
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).2,
        G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧ Nonempty ((modulePushforward B S hS
          (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
            ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)).obj G ≅ F)) ∧
      -- minimality
      (∀ (Z' : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
        (G' : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z').1
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z').2),
        ((modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z')).obj G' ≅ F) →
          schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F ≤ Z'.1) ∧
      -- part (1)
      (∀ A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1,
        letI : (chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F A).IsQuasicoherent :=
          isQuasicoherent_chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F hF A
        letI : (chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F A).IsFiniteType :=
          Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeFiniteType.isFiniteType_of_forall_moduleFinite_sections
            (chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F A)
            (moduleFinite_sections_chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F hF hFft A)
        Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport (chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F A) =
          idealSheafDataOfChart B S hS X
            (definingIdealSheaf B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)
            (definingIdealSheaf_isCartesianOnAffineCharts B S hS X
              ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩) A) ∧
      -- part (2)
      (∀ (G H : Modules.{u, u} B S hS
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).1
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).2)
        (eG : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
          ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)).obj G ≅ F)
        (eH : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
          ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)).obj H ≅ F),
        ∃! φ : G ≅ H, (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
          ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)).map φ.hom ≫ eH.hom = eG.hom) ∧
      -- part (3)
      (∀ (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).1
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).2),
        ((modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
          ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)).obj G ≅ F) →
          SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite G) ∧
      -- part (4)
      supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F) =
          Set.range (pointsMap B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F).toFunctor
            (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F).ι) ∧
      (∀ (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).1
          (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).2),
        ((modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
          ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)).obj G ≅ F) →
          supportOfSheaf B S hS
            (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).1
            ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj G) = Set.univ)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport_chartRestrictionSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U0, part (1), with the support of the restriction taken in the sense of
schemes.**  Let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `Z ⊆ X` be its
scheme-theoretic support and let `A` be an étale scheme chart of `X` — a scheme `U` with an
étale morphism to `X`.  Then the scheme-theoretic support of Stacks 05JV of the restriction of
`F` to `U` is the sheaf of ideals that `Z` cuts out on `U`, that is, `Z ×_X U`.

Over an affine open `V` of `U` both sides are the annihilator of the sections of `F` over the
