étale chart `V` cuts out: the left-hand side by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.annihilator_sections_chartRestrictionSheaf` and the right-hand side
because the ideal cutting out the scheme-theoretic support is the annihilator ideal sheaf of
`F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_chartRestrictionSheaf (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (hZ : Z.1 = schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F)
    (A : SmallEtale B S hS X.1) :
    letI : (chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F A).IsQuasicoherent :=
      isQuasicoherent_chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F hF A
    letI : (chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F A).IsFiniteType :=
      Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.TopDegreeFiniteType.isFiniteType_of_forall_moduleFinite_sections
        (chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F A)
        (moduleFinite_sections_chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F hF hFft A)
    Scheme.Modules.schemeTheoreticSupport (chartRestrictionSheaf B S hS X F A) =
      idealSheafDataOfChart B S hS X (definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z)
        (definingIdealSheaf_isCartesianOnAffineCharts B S hS X Z) A
declarations.comment: part (1): on a scheme U étale over X the scheme-theoretic support of the restriction of F, in the sense of schemes, is the sheaf of ideals that the scheme-theoretic support of F cuts out on U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport_modulePullback_schemeSpace_of_isEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U0, part (1).**  Let `F` be a finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module with
scheme-theoretic support `Z ⊆ X`, let `U` be a scheme over `S` and let `φ : U → X` be an étale
morphism.  Then the fibre product `Z ×_X U` is the scheme-theoretic support of `φ^*F`.

An étale morphism of algebraic spaces is flat (Stacks 0467,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFlat_of_isEtale`), so this is Stacks 089C,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport_modulePullback`, at `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem schemeTheoreticSupport_modulePullback_schemeSpace_of_isEtale
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hft : PresheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).J F.val)
    (U : BigFppfOver B S hS) (φ : schemeSpace U ⟶ X) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) :
    schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS (schemeSpace U) ((modulePullback B S hS φ).obj F) =
      (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F).preimage φ.hom
declarations.comment: part (1): on a scheme étale over X the scheme-theoretic support of the inverse image of F is the inverse image of the scheme-theoretic support of F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport_eq_univ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U0, part (4), for the module on the scheme-theoretic support.**  Let `F` be a
finite type quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `Z ⊆ X` be its scheme-theoretic support and let
`G` be an `𝒪_Z`-module whose direct image along the inclusion is `F`.  Then the support of `G`
is all of `|Z|`.

`G` is of finite type by part (3), so the support of its direct image is the image of its
support under the injective map on points of a closed immersion; that direct image is `F`,
whose support is `|Z|` by the other half of part (4),
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.supportOfSheaf_eq_range_pointsMap_schemeTheoreticSupport`.
declarations.statement:
theorem supportOfSheaf_module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport_eq_univ
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (hFft : SheafOfModules.IsFiniteTypeOnSite F) (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1)
    (hZeq : Z.1 = schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).1
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).2)
    (e : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj G ≅ F) :
    supportOfSheaf B S hS (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X Z).1
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj G) = Set.univ
declarations.comment: part (4): the module on the scheme-theoretic support has support all of it

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U1.** The *scheme theoretic support* of a finite type quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `F`: the intersection of the closed subspaces of `X` whose defining ideal
annihilates `F`.

By `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTheoreticSupport_eq_of_definingIdealSheaf_eq` this is the
closed subspace cut out by the annihilator ideal sheaf of `F`, which for a quasi-coherent `F` of
finite type is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals; so the intersection is itself a closed subspace
and it is the smallest member of the family, which is the content of Stacks 07U0.
declarations.statement: def schemeTheoreticSupport (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) : Subfunctor X.1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isAffineHom_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc: A closed immersion of algebraic spaces is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_of_isClosedImmersion
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hf : IsClosedImmersion B S hS f) :
    IsAffineHom B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_normalizationLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (3).** Let `f : F ⟶ G` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`
carrying every point of codimension zero to a point of codimension zero, and let `ν : F^ν ⟶ F`
and `μ : G^ν ⟶ G` be normalizations. Then there is a unique morphism `f^ν : F^ν ⟶ G^ν` with
`μ ∘ f^ν = f ∘ ν`.

This is the universal property of the normalization of `G`, part (4) of Stacks 0BB4, applied to
the composite `F^ν ⟶ F ⟶ G`. Its two hypotheses on that composite are normality of `F^ν`, which
is part (1) of Stacks 0BB4, and preservation of codimension-zero points, which holds for `ν` by
part (3) of Stacks 0BB4 and for `f` by assumption.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_normalizationLift {G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (D : NormalizationData B S hS F) (D' : NormalizationData B S hS G)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hgeneric : ∀ x : points B S hS F, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
      localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS F f x) = 0) :
    ∃! g : D.space ⟶ D'.space, g ≫ D'.hom = D.hom ≫ f
declarations.comment: part (3), for arbitrary normalization data of the two spaces: the unique lift of a morphism preserving codimension-zero points

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isIso_pullbackLift_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (4).** Let `f : F ⟶ G` be a smooth — in particular an étale — morphism
of algebraic spaces over `S` with `G` satisfying the equivalent conditions of Stacks 0BB1, and
let `ν : F^ν ⟶ F` and `μ : G^ν ⟶ G` be normalizations. Then `F` satisfies the equivalent
conditions of Stacks 0BB1 and `f` carries points of codimension zero to points of codimension
zero — these are the hypotheses of part (3) — and the morphism `f^ν` of part (3) induces an
isomorphism `F^ν ⟶ F ×_G G^ν`.

The two hypotheses of part (3) are Stacks 0GMD and Stacks 0GMC for the flat, locally
finite-type morphism `f`.

For the isomorphism, `F ×_G G^ν` is terminal among normal algebraic spaces over `F` preserving
codimension zero in the same way `F^ν` is, and the comparison morphisms are therefore mutually
inverse. That `F ×_G G^ν` is such an object is read off one chart:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.exists_chart_pullback_snd_of_isSmooth` exhibits a
surjective étale scheme chart of `F` over which `pullback.snd μ f` is the normalization of the
chart, which makes `F ×_G G^ν` normal — the chart of it so produced has a normal scheme — and
makes `pullback.snd μ f` preserve codimension zero, codimension zero being tested on that
chart. The universal property of `F^ν`, part (4) of Stacks 0BB4, then supplies the morphism
`F ×_G G^ν ⟶ F^ν` over `F`; its two composites with the canonical `F^ν ⟶ F ×_G G^ν` are
identities by the uniqueness halves of that property for `F` and for `G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullbackLift_of_isSmooth {G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (D : NormalizationData B S hS F) (D' : NormalizationData B S hS G)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    {f : F ⟶ G} (hf : IsSmooth B S hS f)
    (hGfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS G) :
    HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F ∧
      (∀ x : points B S hS F, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS F f x) = 0) ∧
      ∀ (g : D.space ⟶ D'.space) (hg : g ≫ D'.hom = D.hom ≫ f),
        IsIso (pullback.lift g D.hom hg)
declarations.comment: part (4), for a smooth morphism and arbitrary normalization data of the two spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.exists_iso_yoneda_normalizationScheme
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an object of the big fppf site of `S` every
quasi-compact open of whose underlying scheme has finitely many irreducible components, and let
`D` be normalization data for the algebraic space it represents. Then `D.space` is represented
by an object `Xν` of the site whose underlying scheme is the normalization scheme of the
underlying scheme of `X`, and under that identification `D.hom` is the normalization
morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_yoneda_normalizationScheme {X : BigFppfOver B S hS}
    (D : NormalizationData B S hS (yoneda.obj X))
    (hX : ∀ V : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X).Opens,
      IsCompact (V : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X)) →
        (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) :
    ∃ (Xν : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : Xν ⟶ X)
      (e : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Xν) ≅
        Scheme.normalizationScheme ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) hX)
      (φ : D.space ≅ yoneda.obj Xν),
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p =
          e.hom ≫ Scheme.normalization ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) hX ∧
        φ.hom ≫ yoneda.map p = D.hom
declarations.comment: part (2): the normalization of a scheme as an algebraic space

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isNormal_and_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (1).** Let `F` be an algebraic space over `S` equipped with
normalization data. Then the normalization of `F` is a normal algebraic space over `S` and the
normalization morphism is integral.

The two halves are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isNormal` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isIntegralHom`. The hypotheses of Stacks 0BB1 are
carried by the chart field of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData`, which produces for
every surjective étale scheme chart the finiteness of the sets of irreducible components of its
quasi-compact opens.
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isNormal_and_isIntegralHom_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (1).** Let `F` be an algebraic space over `S` satisfying the equivalent
conditions of Tag 0BB1. Then its normalization `F^ν` is a normal algebraic space and the
normalization morphism `ν_F : F^ν ⟶ F` is integral.
declarations.statement:
theorem isNormal_and_isIntegralHom_normalization {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F) :
    Space.IsNormal B S hS (normalizationPresheaf B S hS hF hfin) ∧
      Space.IsIntegralHom B S hS (normalization B S hS hF hfin)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_iso_yoneda_normalizationScheme_normalization
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (2).** Let `X` be an object of the big fppf site of `S` every
quasi-compact open of whose underlying scheme has finitely many irreducible components, so that
the algebraic space `X` represents satisfies the conditions of Tag 0BB1. Then the normalization
`X^ν` of that algebraic space is represented by an object `Xν` of the site whose underlying
scheme is the normalization scheme of the underlying scheme of `X`, and under that
identification `ν_X` is the normalization morphism of Tag 035E.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_yoneda_normalizationScheme_normalization (X : BigFppfOver B S hS)
    (hX : ∀ V : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X).Opens,
      IsCompact (V : Set ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X)) →
        (irreducibleComponents V).Finite) :
    ∃ (Xν : BigFppfOver B S hS) (p : Xν ⟶ X)
      (e : ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj Xν) ≅
        Scheme.normalizationScheme ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) hX)
      (φ : normalizationPresheaf B S hS (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS X)
        (hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_yoneda B S hS X hX) ≅ yoneda.obj Xν),
      (BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).map p =
          e.hom ≫ Scheme.normalization ((BigFppfOver.toScheme B S hS).obj X) hX ∧
        φ.hom ≫ yoneda.map p = normalization B S hS (isAlgebraicSpace_yoneda B S hS X)
          (hasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents_yoneda B S hS X hX)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsUnique_comp_normalization_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (3).** Let `f : F ⟶ G` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` both
satisfying the equivalent conditions of Tag 0BB1, such that every point of codimension zero of
`F` maps to a point of codimension zero of `G`. Then there is a unique morphism
`f^ν : F^ν ⟶ G^ν` with `ν_G ∘ f^ν = f ∘ ν_F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_comp_normalization_eq {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hFfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (hGfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS G)
    (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hgeneric : ∀ x : points B S hS F, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
      localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS F f x) = 0) :
    ∃! g : normalizationPresheaf B S hS hF hFfin ⟶ normalizationPresheaf B S hS hG hGfin,
      g ≫ normalization B S hS hG hGfin = normalization B S hS hF hFfin ≫ f
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_pullbackLift_normalization_of_isEtale_or_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (4).** Let `f : F ⟶ G` be an étale or a smooth morphism of algebraic
spaces over `S` with `G` satisfying the equivalent conditions of Tag 0BB1. Then the hypotheses of
part (3) hold — `F` satisfies the conditions of Tag 0BB1 too, and `f` carries points of
codimension zero to points of codimension zero — and the morphism `f^ν : F^ν ⟶ G^ν` of part (3)
induces an isomorphism `F^ν ⟶ F ×_G G^ν`.

The third conjunct is the existence and uniqueness of `f^ν`, part (3) at the hypotheses just
established, and the fourth is the isomorphism `(f^ν, ν_F) : F^ν ⟶ F ×_G G^ν`.

The condition of Tag 0BB1 on `F` is stated as an existential because the normalization `F^ν`
is only defined given it; by proof irrelevance the witness does not matter. The isomorphism is
asserted for every `g` with `ν_G ∘ g = f ∘ ν_F`, and by the third conjunct there is exactly one
such `g`, namely `f^ν`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_pullbackLift_normalization_of_isEtale_or_isSmooth
    {F G : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (hGfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS G) {f : F ⟶ G}
    (hf : IsEtale B S hS f ∨ IsSmooth B S hS f) :
    ∃ hFfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F,
      (∀ x : points B S hS F, localRingDimension B S hS x = 0 →
        localRingDimension B S hS (pointsMap B S hS F f x) = 0) ∧
      (∃! g : normalizationPresheaf B S hS hF hFfin ⟶ normalizationPresheaf B S hS hG hGfin,
        g ≫ normalization B S hS hG hGfin = normalization B S hS hF hFfin ≫ f) ∧
      ∀ (g : normalizationPresheaf B S hS hF hFfin ⟶ normalizationPresheaf B S hS hG hGfin)
        (hg : g ≫ normalization B S hS hG hGfin = normalization B S hS hF hFfin ≫ f),
        IsIso (pullback.lift g (normalization B S hS hF hFfin) hg)
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_normalizationData_isNormal_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, the construction together with part (1), at the hypotheses of the tag.** Let
`F` be an algebraic space over `S` satisfying condition (2) of Tag 0BB1: every quasi-compact
open of every étale scheme chart of `F` has finitely many irreducible components. Then there
*is* normalization data for `F` — an algebraic space `F^ν` over `S` together with a morphism
`ν_F : F^ν ⟶ F` whose base change along every surjective étale scheme chart of `F` is the
normalization of that chart — with `F^ν` normal and `ν_F` integral.

Nothing is assumed beyond the two hypotheses the tag itself carries: no normalization data is
given, `F` is not assumed representable, and no bound on sizes is imposed. The datum is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_normalizationData`, which forms `F^ν` as the quotient of a
normalized étale presentation, and the two properties are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isNormal_and_isIntegralHom`.

The other three parts of the tag are stated for an arbitrary
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData` and so are unconditional as they stand; what this
statement adds to them is that their hypothesis is always satisfiable. Part (2), the
identification of the normalization of a representable algebraic space with the normalization
scheme of the representing scheme, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.exists_iso_yoneda_normalizationScheme`. Part (3), the
unique lift of a morphism carrying points of codimension zero to points of codimension zero, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.existsUnique_normalizationLift`. Part (4), the
identification of the normalization of the source of a smooth — in particular an étale —
morphism with the base change of the normalization of the target, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isIso_pullbackLift_of_isSmooth`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_normalizationData_isNormal_isIntegralHom (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F) :
    ∃ D : NormalizationData B S hS F,
      Space.IsNormal B S hS D.space ∧ Space.IsIntegralHom B S hS D.hom
declarations.comment: the construction and part (1) at the hypotheses of the tag: an algebraic space satisfying condition (2) of Tag 0BB1 has normalization data, its normalization is normal, and its normalization morphism is integral

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isPullback_hom_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (4), for a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces: the normalization square
is cartesian.** Let `φ : F ⟶ G` be a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces over `S`, let `D` be
normalization data for `G` and `D'` normalization data for `F`. Then there is a morphism
`F^ν ⟶ G^ν` over `φ` exhibiting `F^ν` as the fibre product `F ×_G G^ν`.

The morphism `F^ν ⟶ G^ν` and its inverse comparison `F ×_G G^ν ⟶ F^ν` both come from the
universal property of the normalization, Stacks 0BB4 part (4): `F^ν` is normal, and so is
`F ×_G G^ν`, being smooth over the normal space `G^ν`; the relevant morphisms carry codimension
zero to codimension zero because flat morphisms do (Stacks 0GMC), because the normalization
morphisms do (Stacks 0BB4 part (3)), and because the projection `F ×_G G^ν ⟶ F` does
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.localRingDimension_pullback_snd_eq_zero`). The two
composites are identities by the uniqueness half of the same universal property.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPullback_hom_of_isSmooth (D : NormalizationData B S hS G)
    (D' : NormalizationData B S hS F) (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G)
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (φ : F ⟶ G) (hφ : IsSmooth B S hS φ) :
    ∃ m : D'.space ⟶ D.space, IsPullback m D'.hom D.hom φ
declarations.comment: part (4) for a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces, with given normalizations

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.exists_isPullback_hom_of_isSmooth
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U4, part (4), for a smooth morphism, with the normalization of the source
produced.** Only normalization data for the target is given: the source satisfies the condition
of Stacks 0BB1 because the target does and the morphism is flat and locally of finite type
(Stacks 0GMD), so it has normalization data by Stacks 07U4, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.NormalizationData.isPullback_hom_of_isSmooth` applies to it.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPullback_hom_of_isSmooth (D : NormalizationData B S hS G)
    (hG : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS G) (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F) (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hφ : IsSmooth B S hS φ) (hGfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS G) :
    ∃ (D' : NormalizationData B S hS F) (m : D'.space ⟶ D.space),
      IsPullback m D'.hom D.hom φ
declarations.comment: part (4) for a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_normalizationData
declarations.doc:
**Tag 07U4, the existence of the normalization.** An algebraic space over `S` every
quasi-compact open of every étale scheme chart of which has finitely many irreducible
components — condition (2) of Tag 0BB1 — has normalization data: an algebraic space `F^ν` over
`S` with a morphism `F^ν ⟶ F` whose base change along every surjective étale scheme chart of
`F` is the normalization of that chart.

The datum is glued along a surjective étale chart `w : h_U ⟶ F`: the normalizations of the
charts along `R = U ×_F U` form an étale equivalence relation, the quotient sheaf is an
algebraic space by Tag 02WW, and the chart condition is checked at `w` by a computation with
the kernel pair of the quotient map and at every other chart by descent along the refinement.
No representability and no bound on sizes is assumed.

The four numbered parts of Tag 07U4 are not proved here; they are the subject of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.Normal`,
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.NormalizationIntegral` and
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.NormalizationEtaleChart`, which assume the datum this
theorem produces.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_normalizationData {F : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hF : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS F)
    (hfin : HasLocallyFiniteIrreducibleComponents B S hS F) :
    Nonempty (NormalizationData B S hS F)
declarations.comment: the existence of the normalization

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosed_singleton_class_of_isAlgebraic_residueField
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` above every point of which every étale
chart of `X` by an affine scheme has a finite fibre, which is condition `(α)` of Stacks 03JX —
in particular a decent one. Let `p` be a field-valued point of `X`
with field of definition `k`, so a commutative diagram `Spec k ⟶ X ⟶ S`. If the image point
`s` of `Spec k ⟶ S` is a closed point of `S` and the residue field extension `κ(s) ⟶ k` is
algebraic, then the image of `Spec k ⟶ X` is a closed point of `|X|`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosed_singleton_class_of_isAlgebraic_residueField
    {X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hdecent : HasFiniteChartFibersAtEveryPoint B S hS X)
    (p : FieldValuedPoint B S hS X)
    (hclosed : IsClosed ({(S.SpecToEquivOfField p.carrier p.toBase).1} : Set S))
    (halg : letI := (S.SpecToEquivOfField p.carrier p.toBase).2.hom.toAlgebra
      Algebra.IsAlgebraic
        (S.residueField (S.SpecToEquivOfField p.carrier p.toBase).1) p.carrier) :
    IsClosed ({p.class B S hS X} : Set (points B S hS X))
declarations.comment: with decency read as condition (alpha) of Stacks 03JX

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_smallEtaleAbelianPushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U6.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S`. For every degree `p` and every filtered diagram `F` of abelian
sheaves on the small étale site of `X`, the canonical map from the colimit of the degree-`p`
higher direct images to the degree-`p` higher direct image of the colimit is an isomorphism:
`R^p f_* (colim F_i) = colim R^p f_* F_i`.

The direct image is the direct image of abelian sheaves along the morphism of small étale topoi
of Stacks 03G2, part (3). It is transported, along the comparison equivalence of Stacks 03G1 at
abelian coefficients, to the direct image along the base-change morphism of *sites* of
Stacks 03G2, part (1), where the statement is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_spacesPushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimit_post_rightDerived_smallEtaleAbelianPushforward
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS f.hom) (hqs : IsQuasiSeparated B S hS f.hom)
    (p : ℕ) {I : Type w} [SmallCategory I] [IsFiltered I]
    [HasColimitsOfShape I Ab.{u + 1}]
    (F : I ⥤ Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.obj) Ab.{u + 1}) :
    IsIso (colimit.post F
      ((abelianPushforward (SmallEtale.topology B S hS X.obj)
        (smallToposMorphism B S hS f)).rightDerived p))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.preservesColimitsOfShape_coyoneda_of_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let `G` be
an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation and let `λ ↦ F_λ` be a filtered system of `𝒪_X`-modules.
Then

`colim_λ Hom_X(G, F_λ) = Hom_X(G, colim_λ F_λ)`,

here in the form that `Hom_X(G, -)` preserves colimits of the given filtered shape, which says
exactly that the canonical comparison map out of any such colimit is a bijection. The module
universe is the universe `u` of the schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_coyoneda_of_isFinitePresentation
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS F) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ F)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) [G.IsFinitePresentation]
    (K : Type u) [Category.{u} K] [IsFiltered K] :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape K (coyoneda.obj (Opposite.op G))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_modulePushforward_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U8, `f_*F ≅ Rf_*F`.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of algebraic spaces
over `S` and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then the canonical map from the direct
image `f_*F`, placed in degree zero, to the derived direct image `Rf_*F` is an isomorphism: the
unit of the right derived functor `Rf_*` of `f_*` on bounded below derived categories is
invertible at `F[0]`.

Equivalently `R^p f_*F = 0` for `p > 0`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_isAffineHom` (Stacks 073H, the
reduction of the source to Stacks 02KG through Equation 69.3.0.1); the two are equivalent for the
left exact functor `f_*` by part (2) of Stacks 015C. No model of the derived categories is
fixed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit_app_modulePushforward_isAffineHom
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS Y.1 Y.2)]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsIso ((modulePushforward B S hS f).rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnith.app
      ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.singleFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) 0).obj F))
declarations.comment: f_*F ≅ Rf_*F: the canonical map from the direct image to the derived direct image is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U8, the quasi-coherence of the direct image.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine
morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `F` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module. Then the
direct image `f_*F` is quasi-coherent.

The hypothesis `h` is the same statement for a target represented by a scheme of the site.
Everything else is the reduction of the source: quasi-coherence is chartwise by Stacks 03LZ,
the restriction of `f_*F` to a chart is the direct image along the base change of `f` by
Stacks 03LX, and a base change of an affine morphism is affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_isAffineHom
    (h : SchemeTargetAffinePushforwardQuasicoherent B S hS)
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of the direct image, reduced chartwise to the case of a target represented by a scheme of the site, which is the hypothesis h

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07U8, the quasi-coherence of the direct image, with no hypothesis.**  Let
`f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `F` be a quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module. Then the direct image `f_*F` is quasi-coherent.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_of_isAffineHom` with its
hypothesis supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.schemeTargetAffinePushforwardQuasicoherent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasicoherentOnSite_modulePushforward_isAffineHom {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj F).IsQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.comment: quasi-coherence of the direct image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_moduleBaseChangeMap_app_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Affine base change for the direct image of a quasi-coherent module** (the base change
clause of Stacks 07U8; Stacks 02KG for schemes).  For a cartesian square of algebraic spaces
whose right morphism `f` is affine, the base change map `g^*f_*F ⟶ f'_*(g')^*F` is an
isomorphism at every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `F`.  The bottom morphism `g` is
arbitrary.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_moduleBaseChangeMap_app_of_isAffineHom (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    IsIso ((moduleBaseChangeMap f g f' g' sq.w).app F)
declarations.comment: base change: g^*f_*F = f'_*(g')^*F for f affine and F quasi-coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCoherent
declarations.doc:
A coherent module on an algebraic space is a quasi-coherent module which is coherent on its
small étale ringed site.

The predicate is on all modules rather than only on the quasi-coherent ones, so that it
applies directly to kernels, cokernels and extensions formed in the ambient category of
modules.  It does not need the locally Noetherian assumption; that assumption enters the
characterizations of Stacks 07UB and the closure results of Stacks 07UC.
declarations.statement:
class IsCoherent (M : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF) : Prop
    extends SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite M, SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_iff_forall_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UB, conditions (1) and (4).**  A module on an algebraic space is coherent if and
only if its restriction to the slice at every étale chart is coherent there.

The restriction is restriction to the slice of the small étale site at the chart; see the
implementation notes.  The module universe is the universe of the structure rings, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_iff_isCoherentOnSite` pins.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_iff_forall_over (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF M ↔
      ∀ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).C,
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
          (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).over U).O)) (M.over U)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_iff_exists_surjective_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UB, conditions (1) and (5).**  A module on an algebraic space is coherent if and
only if there is an étale chart whose structure morphism is surjective on points and whose
slice restriction is coherent.

The forward implication uses that an algebraic space has such a chart at all, namely its
atlas: `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_surjective_smallEtale_chart`.  The restriction is
restriction to the slice of the small étale site at the chart; see the implementation notes.
The module universe is the universe of the structure rings, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_iff_isCoherentOnSite` pins.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_iff_exists_surjective_over (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF M ↔
      ∃ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).C, IsSurjective B S hS U.1.hom ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
          (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).over U).O)) (M.over U)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.forall_over_iff_exists_surjective_over
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UB, conditions (4) and (5).**  The slice restriction of a module on an algebraic
space is coherent at *every* étale chart if and only if it is coherent at *one* étale chart
whose structure morphism is surjective on points.

This is the adjacent equivalence at the bottom of the chain of Stacks 07UB, stated without
reference to its condition (1).  Unlike the two equivalences with condition (1) it is at a free
module universe: both implications pass through coherence of the module on the whole small
étale ringed site, and only the identification of that with condition (1) needs the universe
fixed.  The restriction is restriction to the slice of the small étale site at the chart; see
the implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_over_iff_exists_surjective_over (M : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF) :
    (∀ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).C,
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
          (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).over U).O)) (M.over U)) ↔
      ∃ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).C, IsSurjective B S hS U.1.hom ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite
          (R := (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).over U).O)) (M.over U)
declarations.comment: conditions (4) and (5)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_iff_isFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.doc:
A module on a locally Noetherian algebraic space is coherent if and only if it is an
`𝒪_F`-module of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_iff_isFinitePresentationOnSite
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF M ↔ M.IsFinitePresentationOnSite
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_structureSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UB, the structure sheaf.**  The structure sheaf of a locally Noetherian
algebraic space is a coherent `𝒪_F`-module.

Quasi-coherence is `SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite_unit` and finite type is
`PresheafOfModules.isFiniteType_unit`, neither of which needs the hypothesis; the relations
clause is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isFiniteType_relations_unit`, applied to the covering
by Noetherian affine charts of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_covering_through_noetherianAffine`.
declarations.statement:
instance isCoherent_structureSheaf
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))] :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF
      (SheafOfModules.unit (ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O))
declarations.comment: structure sheaf

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_iff_isQuasicoherentOnSite_and_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UB, conditions (1) and (2).**  A module on a locally Noetherian algebraic space
is coherent if and only if it is quasi-coherent and of finite type.

The base change property of the sections over the affine charts, which the conditional form in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.CoherentNoetherian` carries, is Descent, Proposition
03DX (2) and follows from quasi-coherence, which is a hypothesis in the direction that needs
it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_iff_isQuasicoherentOnSite_and_isFiniteType
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF M ↔
      (M.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧
        PresheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).J M.val)
declarations.comment: conditions (1) and (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_of_fact_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UB, finite locally free modules.**  A finite locally free module on a locally
Noetherian algebraic space is coherent, as an instance.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_of_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite` with finite local
freeness supplied by instance search through `Fact`, which is how the predicate — an `abbrev`
and not a class — can be an instance hypothesis.  The same wrapping is used by the locally
Noetherian hypothesis of `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_structureSheaf`.
declarations.statement:
instance isCoherent_of_fact_isFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    (M : Modules.{u, m} B S hS F hF)
    [Fact (SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite M)] :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF M
declarations.comment: finite locally free modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_of_isInvertible_instance
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UB, invertible modules.**  An invertible module on a locally Noetherian algebraic
space is coherent, as an instance.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_of_isInvertible` with invertibility taken as an
instance-implicit binder, discharged from the local context.
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible` is a class, which is what lets the hypothesis be written
that way; it does not mean instance search *finds* invertibility, and on this site it finds it
for nothing at all, the structure sheaf included —
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isInvertible_unit` does not apply here, its
`CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.WEqualsLocallyBijective` hypothesis not being synthesized
for the topology as the small étale ringed site spells it.  That is also what makes the instance
free: the branch it adds to the search for `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCoherent` closes on the
invertibility subgoal unless the caller has already put invertibility in its context, which is
the only situation the instance is for.
declarations.statement:
instance isCoherent_of_isInvertible_instance
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    [Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (structurePresheaf B S hS F)
      ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS F hF).O)).property M] :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF M
declarations.comment: invertible modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_kernel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07UC].** The kernel of a map of coherent modules on an algebraic space is
coherent.

The kernel of a map of coherent sheaves of modules on an arbitrary site is coherent, by
Stacks 01BY (3); quasi-coherence of the kernel is then free at this module universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_kernel {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (hM : IsCoherent B S hS F hF M)
    (hN : IsCoherent B S hS F hF N) (φ : M ⟶ N) : IsCoherent B S hS F hF (kernel φ)
declarations.comment: kernel

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07UC].** The cokernel of a map of coherent modules on an algebraic space is
coherent.

The cokernel of a map of coherent sheaves of modules on an arbitrary site is coherent, by
Stacks 01BY (3); quasi-coherence of the cokernel is then free at this module universe.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_cokernel {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (hM : IsCoherent B S hS F hF M)
    (hN : IsCoherent B S hS F hF N) (φ : M ⟶ N) : IsCoherent B S hS F hF (cokernel φ)
declarations.comment: cokernel

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_X₂_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07UC].** An extension of coherent modules on an algebraic space is coherent:
the middle term of a short exact sequence of `𝒪_F`-modules whose outer terms are coherent is
coherent.

An extension is represented by a short exact complex of `𝒪_F`-modules, so the statement
quantifies over all extensions of the third term by the first rather than over a choice of one.
The content is Stacks 01BY (4) on the small étale ringed site of `F`; quasi-coherence of the
middle term is free at this module universe.
declarations.comment: extensions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.nonempty_abelian_coherentModules
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07UC].** The category `Coh(𝒪_F)` of coherent modules on an algebraic space is
abelian.

The abelian structure is the one a full subcategory of an abelian category closed under kernels,
cokernels and finite coproducts carries, assembled by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coherentModules_abelian_of_closure`; the kernel and cokernel closure
properties are Stacks 01BY (3) on the small étale ringed site and the coproduct one comes from
the extension result above.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_abelian_coherentModules :
    Nonempty (Abelian (CoherentModules.{u, u} B S hS F hF))
declarations.comment: abelian category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_of_mono_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**The submodule clause of Stacks 07UD on the small étale ringed site.**  A quasi-coherent
submodule of a module coherent on the small étale ringed site of a locally Noetherian algebraic
space is itself coherent on that site.

The submodule is of finite type by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteType_of_mono_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, and a submodule of finite
type of a coherent module is coherent by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_of_mono_of_isFiniteType`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_of_mono_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (ι : N ⟶ M) [Mono ι]
    (hN : N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hM : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite M) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite N
declarations.comment: a quasi-coherent submodule of a coherent module is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_of_mono_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**The submodule clause of Stacks 07UD.**  A quasi-coherent submodule of a coherent module on a
locally Noetherian algebraic space is coherent, for the predicate
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCoherent` of Stacks 07UA.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_of_mono_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (ι : N ⟶ M) [Mono ι]
    (hN : N.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hM : IsCoherent B S hS F hF M) :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF N
declarations.comment: a quasi-coherent submodule of a coherent module is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_of_epi_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**The quotient clause of Stacks 07UD on the small étale ringed site.**  A quasi-coherent
quotient module of a module coherent on the small étale ringed site of a locally Noetherian
algebraic space is itself coherent on that site.  The quotient is given by an epimorphism
`p : M ⟶ Q` of `𝒪_F`-modules.

The kernel of `p` is a quasi-coherent submodule of `M`, being cartesian on affine charts by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCartesianOnAffineCharts_kernel`, so it is of finite type by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiniteType_of_mono_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`, and a quotient of a
coherent module by a submodule of finite type is coherent by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherentOnSite_of_epi_of_isFiniteType_kernel`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherentOnSite_of_epi_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    {M Q : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (p : M ⟶ Q) [Epi p]
    (hQ : Q.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hM : SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite M) :
    SheafOfModules.IsCoherentOnSite Q
declarations.comment: a quasi-coherent quotient module of a coherent module is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_of_epi_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
declarations.doc:
**The quotient clause of Stacks 07UD.**  A quasi-coherent quotient module of a coherent module
on a locally Noetherian algebraic space is coherent, for the predicate
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsCoherent` of Stacks 07UA.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_of_epi_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite
    [Fact (HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS F (fun V : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian V))]
    {M Q : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF} (p : M ⟶ Q) [Epi p]
    (hQ : Q.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (hM : IsCoherent B S hS F hF M) :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF Q
declarations.comment: a quasi-coherent quotient module of a coherent module is coherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_smallEtaleInternalHomSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UE, the sheaf-hom clause.**  The internal Hom `𝓗om_{𝒪_F}(M, N)` of two coherent
`𝒪_F`-modules on an algebraic space is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_smallEtaleInternalHomSmall (M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    [IsCoherent B S hS F hF M] [IsCoherent B S hS F hF N] :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF (smallEtaleInternalHomSmall B S hS F hF M N)
declarations.comment: internal Hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_tensorModule_and_smallEtaleInternalHomSmall
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UE.**  Let `F` be an algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `M`, `N` be
coherent `𝒪_F`-modules.  Then `M ⊗_{𝒪_F} N` and `𝓗om_{𝒪_F}(M, N)` are coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_tensorModule_and_smallEtaleInternalHomSmall
    (M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    [IsCoherent B S hS F hF M] [IsCoherent B S hS F hF N] :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF (tensorModule B S hS F hF M N) ∧
      IsCoherent B S hS F hF (smallEtaleInternalHomSmall B S hS F hF M N)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_tensorModule
declarations.doc:
The tensor product `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.tensorModule` of two coherent `𝒪_F`-modules on an
algebraic space is coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_tensorModule (M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    [IsCoherent B S hS F hF M] [IsCoherent B S hS F hF N] :
    IsCoherent B S hS F hF (tensorModule B S hS F hF M N)
declarations.comment: tensor product

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpen_isZero_restrictToOpenPoints_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UF, part (1).**  A coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose stalk at a geometric point `x̄`
vanishes vanishes on an open subspace of `X` containing the image of `x̄`.

The locally Noetherian hypothesis of the cited statement is not used: the support of a module of
finite type is closed by Stacks 07TZ on any algebraic space, so the statement here is a strict
generalisation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpen_isZero_restrictToOpenPoints_of_isCoherent (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M]
    (x : points B S hS X.1) (p : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) (hp : p.LiesOver x)
    (hstalk : Subsingleton (stalkSet p (M.val.presheaf ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat.{u}))) :
    ∃ (W : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hW : IsOpen W), x ∈ W ∧
      IsZero ((restrictToOpenPoints.{u, u} B S hS X W hW).obj M)
declarations.comment: part (1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpen_mono_restrictToOpenPoints_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UF, part (2).**  A morphism of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules injective on the stalk at a
geometric point `x̄` is a monomorphism after restriction to an open subspace of `X` containing
the image of `x̄`.

The kernel is coherent on the small étale site, hence of finite type, and its stalk at `x̄`
vanishes; part (1) applies to it, and étale restriction is left exact.  The locally Noetherian
hypothesis of the cited statement is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpen_mono_restrictToOpenPoints_map (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2} [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M]
    [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 N] (φ : M ⟶ N)
    (x : points B S hS X.1) (p : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) (hp : p.LiesOver x)
    (hinj : Function.Injective (moduleStalkSetMap B S hS X p φ)) :
    ∃ (W : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hW : IsOpen W), x ∈ W ∧
      Mono ((restrictToOpenPoints.{u, u} B S hS X W hW).map φ)
declarations.comment: part (2)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpen_epi_restrictToOpenPoints_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UF, part (3).**  A morphism of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules surjective on the stalk at
a geometric point `x̄` is an epimorphism after restriction to an open subspace of `X` containing
the image of `x̄`.

The cokernel is coherent on the small étale site, hence of finite type, and its stalk at `x̄`
vanishes; part (1) applies to it, and étale restriction is right exact.  The locally Noetherian
hypothesis of the cited statement is not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpen_epi_restrictToOpenPoints_map (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2} [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M]
    [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 N] (φ : M ⟶ N)
    (x : points B S hS X.1) (p : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) (hp : p.LiesOver x)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (moduleStalkSetMap B S hS X p φ)) :
    ∃ (W : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hW : IsOpen W), x ∈ W ∧
      Epi ((restrictToOpenPoints.{u, u} B S hS X W hW).map φ)
declarations.comment: part (3)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isOpen_isIso_restrictToOpenPoints_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UF, part (4).**  A morphism of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules bijective on the stalk at a
geometric point `x̄` becomes an isomorphism after restriction to an open subspace of `X`
containing the image of `x̄`.

Kernel and cokernel are both of finite type with vanishing stalk at `x̄`, so both vanish on the
complement of the union of their two closed supports; there the restriction is both a
monomorphism and an epimorphism.  The locally Noetherian hypothesis of the cited statement is
not used.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isOpen_isIso_restrictToOpenPoints_map (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2} [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M]
    [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 N] (φ : M ⟶ N)
    (x : points B S hS X.1) (p : GeometricPoint B S hS X.1) (hp : p.LiesOver x)
    (hbij : Function.Bijective (moduleStalkSetMap B S hS X p φ)) :
    ∃ (W : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hW : IsOpen W), x ∈ W ∧
      IsIso ((restrictToOpenPoints.{u, u} B S hS X W hW).map φ)
declarations.comment: part (4)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UG.**  Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`, let `F` be a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `i : Z → X` be the scheme-theoretic support of `F` and let `G` be
the quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module with `i_*G ≅ F`.  Then `G` is a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module.

Here the witness `hZ` that the support is a closed subspace is an argument; it is a
proposition that always holds, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedSubspace_schemeTheoreticSupport_of_isCoherent`, and the form
with no such argument is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_module_on_coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_module_on_schemeTheoreticSupport
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F]
    (hZ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F))
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).1
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).2)
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (e : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
      ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩)).obj G ≅ F) :
    IsCoherent B S hS
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).1
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X ⟨schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F, hZ⟩).2 G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_module_on_coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UG.**  Let `X` be a locally Noetherian algebraic space over `S`, let `F` be a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module, let `i : Z → X` be the scheme-theoretic support of `F` and let `G` be
the quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module with `i_*G ≅ F`.  Then `G` is a coherent `𝒪_Z`-module.

The scheme-theoretic support is read as the closed subspace
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport`, so no witness of closedness is
assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_module_on_coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport
    (hX : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F]
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X (coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F)).1
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X (coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F)).2)
    (hG : G.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (e : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubspaceInclusion B S hS X
      (coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F))).obj G ≅ F) :
    IsCoherent B S hS
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X (coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F)).1
      (closedSubspaceToSpace B S hS X (coherentSchemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F)).2 G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_rightDerived_and_isCoherent_modulePushforward_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UH.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of algebraic spaces over `S` with `Y`
locally Noetherian, and let `𝓕` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Then `R^p f_*𝓕 = 0` for every
`p > 0`, and `f_*𝓕` is a coherent `𝒪_Y`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_and_isCoherent_modulePushforward_of_isFinite
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hG : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 G) :
    (have := hasInjectiveResolutions_modules B S hS X.1 X.2
      ∀ p : ℕ, 0 < p → IsZero (((modulePushforward B S hS f).rightDerived p).obj G)) ∧
      IsCoherent B S hS Y.1 Y.2 ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj G)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isFinite_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**The vanishing half of Stacks 07UH.**  For a finite morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic
spaces over `S`, a coherent `𝒪_X`-module `𝓕` and `p > 0`, the higher direct image vanishes:
`R^p f_* 𝓕 = 0`.

A finite morphism is affine, `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IsFinite.isAffineHom`, and a coherent
module is quasi-coherent, so this is Stacks 073H,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isQuasicoherentOnSite`.

`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isFinite` is the same
statement with the affine case carried as the hypothesis `hchart` and with `𝓕` only required to
be a module; that hypothesis is now discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartwiseIsZeroHigherDirectImage_of_isAffineHom`, which asks for `𝓕`
quasi-coherent and `p > 0` — exactly what the source assumes here.

The source also assumes `Y` locally Noetherian; that is used by the coherence half of the tag,
not by this one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isFinite_of_isCoherent
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    (G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hG : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 G) (p : ℕ)
    (hp : 0 < p) :
    have := hasInjectiveResolutions_modules B S hS X.1 X.2
    IsZero (((modulePushforward B S hS f).rightDerived p).obj G)
declarations.comment: vanishing of the higher direct images, with nothing carried

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_modulePushforward_of_isFinite'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UH, coherence of the direct image.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of
algebraic spaces over `S` with `Y` locally Noetherian, and let `𝓕` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module.
Then `f_*𝓕` is a coherent `𝒪_Y`-module.

A finite morphism is affine, hence representable
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.relativelyRepresentable_of_isAffineHom`), and proper by Stacks 04NZ
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFinite_iff_isAffineHom_and_isProper`), so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_modulePushforward_of_isProper`.  The vanishing assertion of
Stacks 07UH is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isFinite_of_isCoherent`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCoherent_modulePushforward_of_isFinite' (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsFinite B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS Y.1 (fun T : Scheme.{u} ↦ IsLocallyNoetherian T))
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hM : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M) :
    IsCoherent B S hS Y.1 Y.2 ((modulePushforward B S hS f).obj M)
declarations.comment: coherence of the direct image

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isZero_rightDerived_modulePushforward_of_isFinite_of_isQuasicoherent
registrations.comment: vanishing of the higher direct images R^p f_* F, p > 0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_eventually_constant_quasicoherentSubobjects
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UJ.** The ascending chain condition holds for the quasi-coherent submodules of a
coherent module on a Noetherian algebraic space: an ascending sequence of quasi-coherent subobjects
of a coherent `𝒪_F`-module is eventually constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_eventually_constant_quasicoherentSubobjects
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F)
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF) (hM : IsCoherent B S hS F hF M)
    (G : ℕ → Subobject M)
    (hG : ∀ n, SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite (G n : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF))
    (hmono : Monotone G) :
    ∃ n, ∀ k, n ≤ k → G k = G n

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_idealPowSmul_eq_bot_iff_supportOfSheaf_subset_idealZeroLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UK.** Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S`, let `F` be a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module and let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_X` be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, cutting out the
closed subspace `Z ⊆ X`.  Then `ℐⁿ F = 0` for some `n ≥ 0` if and only if the support of `F` is
contained in `Z`, set theoretically.

The closed subspace enters only through its point set `|V(ℐ)|`, which is what the set-theoretic
containment refers to.  For the forward implication no finiteness is needed: over a chart on
which `ℐ` is the whole structure sheaf, and over every chart below it, `F` has no sections at
all, so the support misses the image of that chart.  The converse is the substantial half: on a
surjective affine chart with Noetherian ring of sections, which a Noetherian algebraic space has,
the sections of `F` form a finite module annihilated by a power of each section of `ℐ`, hence by
a power of `ℐ(U)` because the ring is Noetherian; and quasi-coherence carries that single
annihilation to every chart.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_idealPowSmul_eq_bot_iff_supportOfSheaf_subset_idealZeroLocus
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1)
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hM : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M)
    (I : (SheafOfModules.unit (structureRingSheaf B S hS X)).Submodule)
    (hI : I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    (∃ n : ℕ, Stacks.Sites.idealSmul (M := M)
        (Stacks.Sites.idealPow (O := (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O) I n) ⊤ = ⊥) ↔
      supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj M) ⊆
        idealZeroLocus B S hS X I

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_idealPowSmul_inf_eq
declarations.doc:
Artin-Rees for a quasi-coherent submodule `G` of a coherent module `M` and a quasi-coherent
sheaf of ideals `I` on a Noetherian algebraic space: there is a `c ≥ 0` with
`I ⁿ⁻ᶜ (I ᶜ M ⊓ G) = I ⁿ M ⊓ G` for every `n ≥ c`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_idealPowSmul_inf_eq (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ F) (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS F hF)
    (hM : IsCoherent B S hS F hF M) (G : M.Submodule)
    (hG : G.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) (I : IdealSheaves B S hS F hF)
    (hI : I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, c ≤ n →
      Stacks.Sites.idealPowSmul I (n - c) (idealPowSubmodule I c M ⊓ G)
        = idealPowSubmodule I n M ⊓ G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalMapToHomRestrict_bijective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07UM], first display.**  For a Noetherian algebraic space `X` over `S`, a
quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ` with open complement `U = X ∖ V(ℐ)`, a coherent `𝒪_X`-module
`𝒢` and a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, the canonical map

`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℐⁿ 𝒢, ℱ) ⟶ Hom_{𝒪_U}(𝒢|_U, ℱ|_U)`

is bijective.

Injectivity is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalMapToHomRestrict_injective`: a morphism
`φ : ℐⁿ𝒢 ⟶ ℱ` vanishing on `U` has coherent image supported in `V(ℐ)`, so some power of `ℐ`
annihilates that image and `φ` dies on a deeper step of the filtration.  Surjectivity is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalMapToHomRestrict_surjective`: a morphism `𝒢|_U ⟶ ℱ|_U` is
transported to a surjective Noetherian affine chart, extended there by the first display of
[Stacks, Tag 01YB] on the chart's scheme, made compatible on the kernel pair by raising the
exponent of the ideal, and glued.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToHomRestrict_bijective (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1) (hI : I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (G F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hG : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 G)
    [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    Function.Bijective (canonicalMapToHomRestrict B S hS X I G F)
declarations.comment: first display

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalMapToSections_bijective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07UM], the "in particular" display.**  For a Noetherian algebraic space `X`
over `S`, a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `ℐ` with open complement `U = X ∖ V(ℐ)` and a
quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module `ℱ`, the canonical map

`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℐⁿ, ℱ) ⟶ Γ(U, ℱ|_U)`

is bijective.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.canonicalMapToHomRestrict_bijective` at `𝒢 = 𝒪_X`, which is
legitimate because the structure sheaf of a Noetherian algebraic space is coherent
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCoherent_structureSheaf`, the structure-sheaf clause of
[Stacks, Tag 07UB]), composed with the bijection `SheafOfModules.unitHomEquiv` identifying the
morphisms `𝒪_U ⟶ ℱ|_U` with the sections of `ℱ|_U`.  Noetherian implies the étale-local
Noetherian property that the coherence of the structure sheaf asks for, which is `hN.2.2`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalMapToSections_bijective (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ X.1) (hI : I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) [F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    Function.Bijective (canonicalMapToSections B S hS X I F)
declarations.comment: the in particular display

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealPowHomRestrict
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of the first display of [Stacks, Tag 07UM], term by term.**  A morphism
`φ : ℐⁿ G ⟶ F` restricts along an étale morphism `j : Y ⟶ X` whose image misses `V(ℐ)` to a
morphism `G|_Y ⟶ F|_Y`, the source being read through the isomorphism `ℐⁿ G|_Y ≅ G|_Y` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_etaleModulePullback_idealPowModuleι`.

These maps agree along the transition maps of the direct system, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealPowHomRestrict_homOfLE`, so together they are a single map out of
`colim_n Hom_{𝒪_X}(ℐⁿ G, F)`.  The bijectivity asserted by the tag is not proved; see the
section "What is not proved" of the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def idealPowHomRestrict {Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (hj : IsEtale B S hS j.hom) (I : IdealSheaves B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (hjU : Set.range (pointsMap B S hS Y.1 j.hom) ⊆ idealUnitLocus B S hS X I)
    (n : ℕ) {M N : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2} (φ : idealPowModule I n M ⟶ N) :
    (etaleModulePullback B S hS j hj).obj M ⟶ (etaleModulePullback B S hS j hj).obj N
declarations.comment: the canonical map of the first display, term by term

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_shortExact_coherent_supportOfSheaf_subset
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UP.** Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S` and let `F` be a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose support is the union `Z ∪ Z'` of two closed subsets of `|X|`.  Then
there is a short exact sequence `0 → 𝒢' → F → 𝒢 → 0` of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules with `𝒢'`
supported in `Z'` and `𝒢` supported in `Z`.

The sequence produced is the canonical one: `𝒢'` is the subsheaf of sections of `F` supported
in `Z'` and `𝒢` is the quotient of `F` by it.  Quasi-coherence of `𝒢'` is part (3) of
Stacks 0859, whose hypotheses hold because the complement of `Z'` is an open subspace of `X`
and its inclusion is quasi-compact, `X` being Noetherian; `𝒢'` is then coherent by Stacks 07UD
and `𝒢` by Stacks 07UC.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_coherent_supportOfSheaf_subset
    (hTop : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (hN : IsNoetherian B S hS hTop X.1)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F)
    (Z Z' : Set (points B S hS X.1)) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (hZ' : IsClosed Z')
    (hsupp : supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 (moduleAddSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2 F) = Z ∪ Z') :
    ∃ (G' G : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (i : G' ⟶ F) (p : F ⟶ G) (w : i ≫ p = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk i p w).ShortExact ∧ IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 G' ∧
        IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 G ∧
        supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 (moduleAddSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2 G') ⊆ Z' ∧
        supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 (moduleAddSheaf B S hS X.1 X.2 G) ⊆ Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mono_modulePushforward_idealSum_of_schemeTheoreticSupport
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07UQ].**  Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let `ℱ` be a
coherent `𝒪_X`-module whose scheme-theoretic support `i : Z → X` is reduced with `|Z|`
irreducible.  Then there are an integer `r > 0`, a nonzero quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
`ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Z` and an injective map of coherent modules `i_*(ℐ^{⊕ r}) → ℱ` whose cokernel is
supported on a proper closed subspace of `Z`, namely on the image of a closed `T ⊊ |Z|`.

The scheme-theoretic support is a closed subspace (it is part of the conclusion), `ℱ = i_*𝒢` for
a quasi-coherent `𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢` by [Stacks, Tag 07U0], `𝒢` is coherent by
[Stacks, Tag 07UG], and its support is all of `|Z|` because the support of `ℱ` is the image of
`|Z|` and `i` is injective on points.  The case `Z = X`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_mono_biproduct_idealSheaf_cokernel_support_subset`, applies to
`𝒢` on the Noetherian space `Z`; the direct image is exact, so it keeps the injection and
carries the cokernel to the cokernel, whose support is then in the image of `T`.  The source
`i_*(ℐ^{⊕ r})` is quasi-coherent, the direct image along a closed immersion preserving
quasi-coherence, and it is a submodule of the coherent `ℱ`, hence coherent by
[Stacks, Tag 07UD].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mono_modulePushforward_idealSum_of_schemeTheoreticSupport
    (noeth : IsNoetherian B S hS hZt X.1) (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (coh : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F)
    (redIrr : IsReducedIrreducible B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F)) :
    ∃ hZ : IsClosedSubspace B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F),
      ∃ (r : ℕ) (I : (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
          (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS
          (closedSubfunctorSpace B S hS hZ).1 (closedSubfunctorSpace B S hS hZ).2).O))).Submodule),
        I.toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherentOnSite ∧ 0 < r ∧ I ≠ ⊥ ∧
        IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 ((modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubfunctorι B S hS hZ)).obj
          (⨁ fun _ : Fin r => I.toSheafOfModules)) ∧
        ∃ φ : (modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubfunctorι B S hS hZ)).obj
            (⨁ fun _ : Fin r => I.toSheafOfModules) ⟶ F, Mono φ ∧
          ∃ (Q : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (q : F ⟶ Q) (w : φ ≫ q = 0),
            Nonempty (IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ q w)) ∧
            ∃ T : Set (points B S hS (schemeTheoreticSupport B S hS X F).toFunctor),
              IsClosed T ∧ T ≠ Set.univ ∧
              supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1 ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj Q) ⊆
                pointsMap B S hS _ (closedSubfunctorι B S hS hZ).hom '' T

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasIdealDevissage_of_isCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07UR.**  Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S`
and let `F` be a coherent `𝒪_X`-module.  Then `F` carries a filtration

`0 = F₀ ⊆ F₁ ⊆ … ⊆ F_m = F`

by coherent submodules such that for each `j` there are a reduced closed subspace `Z_j ⊆ X`
with `|Z_j|` irreducible and a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals `I_j ⊆ 𝒪_{Z_j}` with
`F_j / F_{j-1} ≅ (Z_j → X)_* I_j`.

The filtration is produced as a structure by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasTagFiltration_of_isCoherent` and read in this existential form by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasIdealDevissage_of_hasTagFiltration`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasIdealDevissage_of_isCoherent (terminal : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (noeth : IsNoetherian B S hS terminal X.1)
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (coh : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M) :
    HasIdealDevissage B S hS X M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.property_of_ideal_pushforward_and_extensions
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over `S` and let `P` be a property of `𝒪_X`-modules
such that

1. for a short exact sequence `0 → F₁ → F → F₂ → 0` of coherent modules, if `F₁` and `F₂` have
   `P` then so does `F`;
2. for every reduced closed subspace `i : Z → X` with `|Z|` irreducible and every quasi-coherent
   sheaf of ideals `I ⊆ 𝒪_Z`, `P` holds for `i_*I`.

Suppose moreover that `X` has a point or that `P` holds for every zero module.  Then `P` holds
for every coherent module on `X`.

Without the alternative the statement fails when `|X|` is empty
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isNoetherian_not_forall_property`).
declarations.statement:
theorem property_of_ideal_pushforward_and_extensions (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (noetherian : IsNoetherian B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (P : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 → Prop)
    (nonempty_or_zero : Nonempty (points B S hS X.1) ∨
      ∀ M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2, IsZero M → P M)
    (extensions : ClosedUnderCoherentExtensions B S hS X P)
    (idealPushforward : ∀ (Z : Subfunctor X.1) (closed : IsClosedSubspace B S hS Z),
      IsReducedIrreducible B S hS Z →
      ∀ I : QuasicoherentIdeals B S hS (closedSubfunctorSpace B S hS closed),
        P ((modulePushforward B S hS (closedSubfunctorι B S hS closed)).obj
          I.1.toSheafOfModules))
    (M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (coherent : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 M) : P M

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.property_of_isCoherent_of_hasGenericSubsheaves
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07UT.**  Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S` and
let `P` be a property of coherent `𝒪_X`-modules such that

1. for a short exact sequence `0 → F₁ → F → F₂ → 0` of coherent modules, if `F₁` and `F₂` have
   `P` then so does `F`;
2. if `P` holds for `F^{⊕ r}` for some `r ≥ 1`, then it holds for `F`;
3. for every reduced closed subspace `i : Z → X` with `|Z|` irreducible there is a coherent
   `𝒪_Z`-module `𝒢` with `Supp(𝒢) = Z` such that for every nonzero quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals
   `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪_Z` there is a quasi-coherent `𝒢' ⊆ ℐ𝒢` with `Supp(𝒢/𝒢')` a proper closed subset of `|Z|`
   and `P(i_*𝒢')`

and such that `P` holds for the zero module.  Then `P` holds for every coherent `𝒪_X`-module.

The source does not list the zero module among its hypotheses, and its conclusion fails without
it: the property "is nonzero" satisfies (1), (2) and (3) — in (3) take `𝒢 = 𝒪_Z` and `𝒢' = ℐ𝒪_Z`
— and does not hold for the zero module.  The source's proof runs over the nonempty supports
only.

The proof is the source's Noetherian induction on the support of `F`, run over the closed
subsets of `|X|`, a Noetherian topological space by Stacks 04ZF.  A module with empty support is
zero; a reducible support is split by Stacks 07UP and (1) concludes; an irreducible support is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.property_of_isIrreducible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_of_isCoherent_of_hasGenericSubsheaves
    (noeth : IsNoetherian B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (zero : ∀ M : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2, IsZero M → P M)
    (extension : ClosedUnderCoherentExtensions B S hS X P)
    (ofSum : ∀ F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2, IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F →
      ∀ r : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → P (⨁ fun _ : Fin r => F) → P F)
    (generic : HasGenericSubsheaves B S hS X P)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (coherent : IsCoherent B S hS X.1 X.2 F) : P F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFiltered_and_nonempty_isColimit_coherentSubobjectCocone
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian algebraic space over a scheme `S`.  Every quasi-coherent
`𝒪_X`-module `F` is the filtered colimit of its coherent submodules: the coherent submodules of `F`
form a filtered category, and the cocone of their inclusions into `F` is a colimit cocone.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiltered_and_nonempty_isColimit_coherentSubobjectCocone
    (terminal_mem : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (noetherian : IsNoetherian B S hS terminal_mem X)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) [hFq : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite] :
    IsFiltered (CoherentSubobject B S hS X hX F) ∧
      Nonempty (IsColimit (coherentSubobjectCocone B S hS X hX F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFiltered_isColimit_isFinitePresentation_of_isAffineHom_of_isNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UW.**  Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be an affine morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme
`S` with `Y` Noetherian.  Then every quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module is a filtered colimit of
`𝒪_X`-modules of finite presentation.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isFilteredColimit_isFinitePresentation_of_isAffineHom` with its
five inputs proved: the Noetherian case
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isFiltered_isColimit_isFinitePresentation_of_isNoetherian`),
Stacks 07U8 for the direct image, Stacks 03GA and 03DO (7) for the pullback, the surjectivity of
the counit (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_modulePullbackAdjunction_counit_app_of_isAffineHom`) and
the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `X`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiCompactSpace_and_isAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated_of_isAffineHom`).

The index category is the category of triples `(i, j, α)` that the source's proof constructs,
whose objects carry a morphism of `𝒪_X`-modules, and so lives in `Type (u + 1)` with Hom-types in
`Type u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isFiltered_isColimit_isFinitePresentation_of_isAffineHom_of_isNoetherian
    {X Y : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : IsAffineHom B S hS f.hom)
    (hY : IsNoetherian B S hS hZ Y.1)
    (F : Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherentOnSite) :
    ∃ (K : Type (u + 1)) (inst : Category.{u} K),
      let _ := inst
      ∃ (_ : IsFiltered K) (D : K ⥤ Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
        (φ : D ⟶ (Functor.const K).obj F),
        (∀ k, (D.obj k).IsFinitePresentation) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk F φ))
declarations.comment: for an affine morphism f : X ⟶ Y of algebraic spaces over S with Y Noetherian, every quasi-coherent 𝒪_X-module is a filtered colimit of finitely presented 𝒪_X-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CohomologyVanishingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UY.** A quasi-compact, quasi-separated algebraic space `X` over a scheme `S`
every one of whose quasi-coherent modules has vanishing first cohomology.
declarations.statement: structure CohomologyVanishingSituation

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CohomologyVanishingSituation.isIso_unit_tensorSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UZ, first assertion: `p_*(M ⊗_A 𝒪_X) = M~`.**  In Situation 07UY, for every
`A`-module `M`, the unit `M~ ⟶ p_*p^*M~ = p_*(M ⊗_A 𝒪_X)` of the adjunction `p^* ⊣ p_*` of
Stacks 03LU is an isomorphism.

`p` is an isomorphism (`…CohomologyVanishingSituation.isIso_toSpecA`), so `p^*` is fully faithful
and the unit is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_unit_tensorSheaf :
    IsIso ((modulePullbackAdjunction T.site (⊤_ Scheme.{u}) T.containsTerminal T.toSpecA).unit.app
      (T.tildeModule M))
declarations.comment: first assertion: p_*(M ⊗_A 𝒪_X) = M~, the unit M~ ⟶ p_*p^*M~ of the adjunction p^* ⊣ p_* being an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CohomologyVanishingSituation.globalSectionsTensorLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07UZ, second assertion: `Γ(X, M ⊗_A 𝒪_X) = M`.**  In Situation 07UY, for every
`A`-module `M`, the global sections of `M ⊗_A 𝒪_X = p^*M~` are `M`, as `A`-modules, the global
sections being a module over `A = Γ(X, 𝒪_X)`.

It is `M = Γ(Spec A, M~) = Γ(Spec A, p_*p^*M~) = Γ(X, p^*M~)`, the middle step being the first
assertion `…CohomologyVanishingSituation.isIso_unit_tensorSheaf` and the last Stacks 0732.
declarations.statement:
def globalSectionsTensorLinearEquiv :
    M ≃ₗ[T.globalFunctions]
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars T.globalFunctionsOverIntegersEquiv.toRingHom).obj
        (T.spaceSections M)
declarations.comment: second assertion: Γ(X, M ⊗_A 𝒪_X) = M, as A-modules

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.CohomologyVanishingSituation.isZero_rightDerived_one_globalSectionsFunctor_of_isAffineHom
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of Stacks 07V0.** In the situation of Stacks 07UY, let `f : X' ⟶ X` be an affine
morphism of algebraic spaces and let `𝓕'` be a quasi-coherent `𝒪_{X'}`-module.  Then
`H¹(X', 𝓕') = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_one_globalSectionsFunctor_of_isAffineHom
    {X' : AlgebraicSpaces T.site T.base T.containsBase} (f : X' ⟶ T.space)
