**The change of deformation base.** If the lifting property defining versality holds with
the local ring of `S` at `s` as deformation base, it holds with any `Λ` whose spectrum maps to
`S` compatibly with the chosen residue point.

Every Artinian local `Λ`-algebra occurring in a lifting problem has its residue point at the
chosen point of `S` — for the target because the lifting property already imposes that of the
arrow `a`, read through `Deformation.Artin.schemeMap_over`, and for the source because the
surjection is `Λ`-linear and respects the residue identifications — so each is canonically an
`𝒪_{S,s}`-algebra (`Deformation.Artin.stalkObj`), the surjection between them is a morphism of
`𝒞_{𝒪_{S,s}}` with the same underlying ring map (`Deformation.Artin.stalkHom`), and the two
presentations of each base over `S` agree
(`Deformation.Artin.specMap_stalkAlgebra_comp_fromSpecStalk`).

Nothing is asked of `iΛ`: not that it be an open immersion, nor even a monomorphism. The
factorization through the local ring is produced at the level of schemes, so `𝒪_{S,s}` is never
identified with a localization of `Λ`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem liftsAtResiduePoint_changeBase
    (hstalk : LiftsAtResiduePoint (Λ := S.presheaf.stalk s) (k := k) (alg := algStalk)
      (S.fromSpecStalk s) q U x hx κ) :
    LiftsAtResiduePoint (Λ := Λ) (k := k) iΛ q U x hx κ
declarations.comment: the lifting property over the local ring of S transfers to the affine open

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.liftsAtResiduePoint_base_of_isVersalAt
declarations.doc:
**Versality at a point, read with an arbitrary affine deformation base.** If `x` is versal
at `u₀` then the lifting property holds with *any* `Spec Λ ⟶ S` as deformation base, at the
canonical residue-field point of `u₀`.

`Deformation.Artin.IsVersalAt` is literally the lifting property with the local ring of `S` at
the image of `u₀` as base (`Deformation.Artin.isVersalAt_iff_liftsAtResiduePoint`), and
`Deformation.Artin.liftsAtResiduePoint_changeBase` moves the base; the one compatibility it
asks of the residue point is that it factor through that local ring, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Spec_stalkClosedPointTo_fromSpecStalk`.

This is the form the degree `-1` half of the direction `(1) ⇒ (2)` of [Stacks, Tag 07YM]
consumes: the small extension it tests versality against is built from `Λ`-algebras, `Λ` being
the ring of the affine open the family maps into, and the objects of `𝒞_{𝒪_{S,s}}` are not
available to it. Nothing is asked of `iΛ` — in particular not that it be an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem liftsAtResiduePoint_base_of_isVersalAt
    (hversal : IsVersalAt U q u₀ x hx) :
    LiftsAtResiduePoint (Λ := Λ) (k := U.left.residueField u₀) iΛ q U x hx
      (U.left.fromSpecResidueField u₀)
declarations.comment: versality gives the lifting property over any affine deformation base

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.naiveVersalityCriterion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YM.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme, let `𝒳` be a category fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S` satisfying (RS\*), let `U = Spec A` be affine of finite
type over `S` mapping into an affine open `Spec Λ ⊆ S`, let `x` be an object of `𝒳` over `U`,
and let `ξ : E ⟶ NL_{A/Λ}` be a morphism of `D⁻(A)` such that

1. for every deformation situation `(x, A' → A)` the object `x` lifts to `Spec A'` exactly
   when `E ⟶ NL_{A/Λ} ⟶ NL_{A/A'}` is zero, and
2. there is an isomorphism of functors `T_x(−) ⟶ Ext⁰_A(E, −)` carrying the canonical element
   to `E ⟶ NL_{A/Λ} ⟶ Ω_{A/Λ}`.

Let `u₀ ∈ U` be a finite type point with residue field `k`. Then `x` is versal at `u₀` as soon
as `ξ` induces a surjection `H^{-1}(E ⊗ᴸ_A k) ⟶ H^{-1}(NL_{A/Λ} ⊗ᴸ_A k)` and an injection
`H^0(E ⊗ᴸ_A k) ⟶ H^0(NL_{A/Λ} ⊗ᴸ_A k)`; and conversely, if `u₀` is a closed point at which `x`
is versal, then `ξ` induces such a surjection and such an injection.

Both directions are stated at once, as the predicate
`Deformation.Artin.NaiveVersalityCriterion` which [Stacks, Tag 07YN] and [Stacks, Tag 07YU]
consume as a hypothesis.
declarations.statement: public theorem naiveVersalityCriterion : NaiveVersalityCriterion hp hRS P hΩ E ξ

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.tangentEquiv_canonicalTangentMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YM, hypothesis (ii) in use.** Under the functorial isomorphism
`T_x(-) ≅ Ext⁰_A(E, -)` of hypothesis (ii), the map on tangent spaces of Stacks 07YC sends a
tangent vector `θ : Ω_{A/Λ} →ₗ[A] k` to `ξ` followed by the augmentation
`Deformation.Artin.naiveCotangentToDifferentials` followed by `θ`.

This is the naturality of the isomorphism at the morphism of site modules attached to `θ`,
together with its prescribed value at the canonical element:
`Deformation.Artin.canonicalTangentMap` is by definition the image of the canonical element
under that morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tangentEquiv_canonicalTangentMap (θ : Ω[A⁄Λ] →ₗ[A] k) :
    tangentEquiv (⟨ModuleCat.of A k, hk⟩ : SiteModule A B)
        (canonicalTangentMap Λ A k B S hS toS hA p x hx hp hRS hΩ hk baseMap
          baseFactorization θ) =
      ξ ≫ naiveCotangentToDifferentials Λ A ≫
        (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).map (ModuleCat.ofHom θ)
declarations.comment: the map on tangent spaces factors through the augmentation

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.length_ker_eq_one_of_linearEquiv_residueField
declarations.doc:
**The length-one hypothesis of
`Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.isSmallExtension_powQuotientMap`.** The kernel of the
thickening of [Stacks, Tag 07YL] has length one over `A'`: it is a copy of the residue field
at a maximal ideal of `A`, hence a simple `A`-module
(`Deformation.Artin.isSimpleModule_residueField`), and the `A'`-submodules of it are its
`A`-submodules because the two actions agree through the surjection `A' → A`
(`isSimpleModule_iff_isSimpleModule_of_algebraMap_surjective`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem length_ker_eq_one_of_linearEquiv_residueField
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsMaximal]
    (e : RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A) ≃ₗ[A] p.ResidueField) :
    Module.length A' (RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A)) = 1
declarations.comment: the kernel `I` of `A' → A` has length one over `A'`

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.mul_ker_eq_bot_of_linearEquiv_residueField
declarations.doc:
**The Artin–Rees input of [Stacks, Tag 07YM].** An ideal of `A'` carried by the surjection
`A' → A` into the kernel of `A ⟶ κ(𝔭)` annihilates the kernel `I` of that surjection: the two
actions on `I` agree, and `I` is a copy of `κ(𝔭)`, on which `𝔭` acts by zero.

Applied with `q = Ker(A' ⟶ κ(𝔭))` this is the hypothesis `𝔭' · I = 0` of
`Deformation.Artin.exists_pow_inf_eq_bot_of_mul_eq_bot`, which produces the exponent `n > 1`
with `(𝔭') ^ n ⊓ I = 0`. Only primality of `𝔭` is used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem mul_ker_eq_bot_of_linearEquiv_residueField
    (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (e : RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A) ≃ₗ[A] p.ResidueField)
    (q : Ideal A')
    (hq : ∀ a' ∈ q, algebraMap A' A a' ∈ RingHom.ker (algebraMap A p.ResidueField)) :
    q * RingHom.ker (algebraMap A' A) = ⊥
declarations.comment: 𝔭' annihilates the kernel I of A' → A

declarations.name: Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.powQuotientObj
declarations.doc:
The object `R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` of `𝒞_Λ`, for `𝔭 = Ker ε` the augmentation ideal of a surjective
augmentation of a Noetherian `Λ`-algebra and `n ≠ 0`. The algebra `R` itself is not asked to
be local or Artinian.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def powQuotientObj [IsNoetherianRing R] (ε : R →ₐ[Λ] k)
    (hε : Function.Surjective ε) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : ArtinianLocalAlgCat.{u, v, w} Λ k
declarations.comment: the object `A/𝔭 ^ n` of `𝒞_Λ` at a closed point

declarations.name: Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.maximalIdeal_pow_powQuotientObj_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th power of the maximal ideal of `R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` vanishes. This is the hypothesis
`𝔪_{B'} ^ n = 0` of
`Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.not_isEssentialSurjection_of_lift_powQuotient`, read at the
object `Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.powQuotientObj` of `𝒞_Λ` rather than at the bare
quotient ring; it is `IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_quotient_pow_pow_eq_bot`, the augmentation
ideal being maximal.
declarations.comment: the maximal ideal of the object `A'/(𝔭') ^ n` of `𝒞_Λ` has vanishing power

declarations.name: Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.ker_powQuotientMapAlgHom
declarations.doc:
**The kernel computation of [Stacks, Tag 07YM].** For `φ : R' ↠ R` surjective, the kernel
of `R' ⧸ (𝔭') ^ n ⟶ R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` is the image of `Ker φ`.

The preimage of `𝔭 ^ n` under `φ` is `(𝔭') ^ n + Ker φ`, because `𝔭 ^ n` is the image of
`(𝔭') ^ n`; passing to `R' ⧸ (𝔭') ^ n` kills the first summand.
declarations.statement:
public theorem ker_powQuotientMapAlgHom {ε' : R' →ₐ[Λ] k} {ε : R →ₐ[Λ] k} {φ : R' →ₐ[Λ] R}
    (hφ : ε.comp φ = ε') (n : ℕ) (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ) :
    RingHom.ker (powQuotientMapAlgHom hφ n).toRingHom =
      (RingHom.ker φ.toRingHom).map
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk (RingHom.ker ε'.toRingHom ^ n))
declarations.comment: the kernel of `A'/(𝔭') ^ n ⟶ A/𝔭 ^ n` is the image of `I = Ker(A' → A)`

declarations.name: Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.powQuotientMap
declarations.doc:
The morphism `R' ⧸ (𝔭') ^ n ⟶ R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` of `𝒞_Λ` induced by a map of augmented
Noetherian algebras.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def powQuotientMap [IsNoetherianRing R'] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {ε' : R' →ₐ[Λ] k} {ε : R →ₐ[Λ] k} {φ : R' →ₐ[Λ] R} (hφ : ε.comp φ = ε')
    (hε' : Function.Surjective ε') (hε : Function.Surjective ε) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] :
    powQuotientObj ε' hε' n ⟶ powQuotientObj ε hε n
declarations.comment: the morphism `A'/(𝔭') ^ n ⟶ A/𝔭 ^ n` of `𝒞_Λ`

declarations.name: Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.isSmallExtension_powQuotientMap
declarations.doc:
**The small extension of [Stacks, Tag 07YM].** Let `φ : R' ↠ R` be a surjection of
augmented Noetherian `Λ`-algebras whose kernel `I` has length one over `R'`, and suppose
`(𝔭') ^ n ⊓ I = 0`. Then `R' ⧸ (𝔭') ^ n ⟶ R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` is a small extension of Artinian local
rings.

The kernel is the image of `I` by `ker_powQuotientMapAlgHom`, and `(𝔭') ^ n ⊓ I = 0` makes
that image a copy of `I`, hence again of length one. In the source `I` is a one-dimensional
`k`-vector space and the hypothesis `(𝔭') ^ n ⊓ I = 0` is the conclusion of the Artin–Rees
step `Deformation.Artin.exists_pow_inf_eq_bot_of_mul_eq_bot`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSmallExtension_powQuotientMap [IsNoetherianRing R'] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {ε' : R' →ₐ[Λ] k} {ε : R →ₐ[Λ] k} {φ : R' →ₐ[Λ] R} (hφ : ε.comp φ = ε')
    (hε' : Function.Surjective ε') (hε : Function.Surjective ε)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hinf : RingHom.ker ε'.toRingHom ^ n ⊓ RingHom.ker φ.toRingHom = ⊥)
    (hlen : Module.length R' (RingHom.ker φ.toRingHom) = 1) :
    InfinitesimalLifting.IsSmallExtension
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (powQuotientMap hφ hε' hε n).hom.toRingHom)
declarations.comment: `A'/(𝔭') ^ n ⟶ A/𝔭 ^ n` is a small extension

declarations.name: Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.exists_section_of_lift_powQuotient
declarations.doc:
**The section of [Stacks, Tag 07YM].** If the quotient map `R → R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` lifts through a
morphism `f : C ⟶ R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` of `𝒞_Λ` whose source has `𝔪_C ^ n = 0`, then `f` has a section
in `𝒞_Λ`.

The lift factors through `R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` by `IsLocalRing.exists_isLocalHom_comp_mk_pow`, and the
factorization is a morphism of `𝒞_Λ`: it is a `Λ`-algebra map because `σ` is, it is local by
that lemma, and it respects the identifications of the residue fields because `f` does.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_section_of_lift_powQuotient
    (hn : maximalIdeal (C : Type v) ^ n = ⊥) :
    ∃ s : powQuotientObj ε hε n ⟶ C, s ≫ f = 𝟙 (powQuotientObj ε hε n)
declarations.comment: the lift factors through A/𝔭 ^ n, giving a section of the small extension

declarations.name: Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.not_isEssentialSurjection_of_lift_powQuotient
declarations.doc:
**The contradiction of [Stacks, Tag 07YM].** A small extension `f : C ⟶ R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` of
`𝒞_Λ` whose source has `𝔪_C ^ n = 0` and through which the quotient map `R → R ⧸ 𝔭 ^ n` lifts
is not an essential surjection: the lift produces a section
(`Deformation.ArtinianLocalAlgCat.exists_section_of_lift_powQuotient`), and a small extension
with a section is not essential (`Deformation.not_isEssentialSurjection_iff_exists_section`).
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_isEssentialSurjection_of_lift_powQuotient
    (hn : maximalIdeal (C : Type v) ^ n = ⊥)
    (hf : InfinitesimalLifting.IsSmallExtension (CommRingCat.ofHom f.hom.toRingHom)) :
    ¬ IsEssentialSurjection f
declarations.comment: a lift of A through A'/(𝔭') ^ n contradicts essential surjectivity

declarations.name: isLocalRing_quotient_pow_of_isMaximal
declarations.doc:
For a maximal ideal `p` of a ring that need not be local and `n ≠ 0`, the ring `R ⧸ p ^ n`
is local.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isLocalRing_quotient_pow_of_isMaximal (p : Ideal R) [p.IsMaximal] {n : ℕ}
    (hn : n ≠ 0) : IsLocalRing (R ⧸ p ^ n)
declarations.comment: the local half of `A/𝔭 ^ n`, for `𝔭` the prime of a closed point

declarations.name: isArtinianRing_quotient_pow_of_isMaximal
declarations.doc:
For a maximal ideal `p` of a Noetherian ring that need not be local and `n ≠ 0`, the ring
`R ⧸ p ^ n` is Artinian.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isArtinianRing_quotient_pow_of_isMaximal [IsNoetherianRing R] (p : Ideal R)
    [p.IsMaximal] {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) : IsArtinianRing (R ⧸ p ^ n)
declarations.comment: the Artinian half of `A/𝔭 ^ n`, for `𝔭` the prime of a closed point

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_quotient_pow
declarations.doc:
For a maximal ideal `p` and `n ≠ 0`, the maximal ideal of `R ⧸ p ^ n` is the image of
`p`.
declarations.comment: the maximal ideal of `A/𝔭 ^ n`, for `𝔭` the prime of a closed point

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_quotient_pow_pow_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
For a maximal ideal `p` and `n ≠ 0`, the `n`-th power of the maximal ideal of `R ⧸ p ^ n`
vanishes: that maximal ideal is the image of `p`, so its `n`-th power is the image of `p ^ n`,
which is the ideal being quotiented out.

This is the hypothesis `𝔪_{B'} ^ n = 0` under which a lift of `R` through a morphism onto
`R ⧸ p ^ n` factors (`IsLocalRing.exists_isLocalHom_comp_mk_pow`), and in [Stacks, Tag 07YM]
it is the sentence "since the maximal ideal of `B'` has `n`th power equal to zero". The ring
`R` is not asked to be local.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal_quotient_pow_pow_eq_bot (p : Ideal R) [p.IsMaximal]
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (R ⧸ p ^ n) ^ n = ⊥
declarations.comment: the maximal ideal of `A'/(𝔭') ^ n` has vanishing `n`-th power

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_isLocalHom_comp_mk_pow
declarations.doc:
**The local factorization of [Stacks, Tag 07YM].** A ring map `σ : R → S` into a local
ring whose maximal ideal satisfies `𝔪_S ^ n = 0` factors through `R ⧸ p ^ n` for every ideal
`p` whose image under `σ` lies in `𝔪_S`, and the factorization is a local homomorphism as soon
as `p` is maximal and `n ≠ 0`.

The ring `R` is not asked to be local: in the source `σ` goes from the finite-type algebra `A`
to an Artinian local ring `B'` and `p` is the prime of the closed point, so the hypothesis
`p.map σ ≤ 𝔪_S` — rather than `IsLocalHom σ` — is what is available. Maximality of `p` and
`n ≠ 0` are used only to make `R ⧸ p ^ n` a local ring, hence only for the `IsLocalHom`
half; the factorization itself is `Ideal.Quotient.lift` applied to
`Ideal.pow_le_ker_of_map_le` and holds for an arbitrary ideal `p` and arbitrary `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.exists_isLocalHom_comp_mk_pow [IsLocalRing S] (f : R →+* S)
    (p : Ideal R) [p.IsMaximal] {n : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (hp : p.map f ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S)
    (hn : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal S ^ n = ⊥) :
    ∃ F : R ⧸ p ^ n →+* S, IsLocalHom F ∧ F.comp (Ideal.Quotient.mk (p ^ n)) = f
declarations.comment: σ : A → B' with 𝔪_{B'} ^ n = 0 factors through A/𝔭 ^ n

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.isOpenVersalityAt_of_naiveObstructionAt
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YN**, with the versality criterion of Stacks 07YM discharged rather than assumed.

`Deformation.Artin.exists_isOpen_isVersalAt_of_naiveObstructionAt` takes that criterion as a
hypothesis, and must: it lives in a module this one imports, while the criterion is proved here,
so it cannot apply it without a cycle. This is the same statement with the hypothesis supplied by
`Deformation.Artin.naiveVersalityCriterion`, so the tag sits on a declaration that grants
nothing.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenVersalityAt_of_naiveObstructionAt
    (data : NaiveObstructionAt hp hRS P hΩ E ξ)
    (hFinite : ∀ n : ℤ,
      Module.Finite P.ring ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} P.ring) n).obj E))
    (u₀ : Spec (.of P.ring)) (hu₀ : IsClosed ({u₀} : Set (Spec (.of P.ring))))
    (hversal : IsVersalAt (Over.mk P.obj.alg.toScheme) (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u₀ P.point
      P.overScheme_eq) :
    ∃ V : Set (Spec (.of P.ring)), IsOpen V ∧ u₀ ∈ V ∧
      ∀ u ∈ V, IsFiniteTypePoint u →
        IsVersalAt (Over.mk P.obj.alg.toScheme) (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u P.point
          P.overScheme_eq

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.NaiveObstructionTheory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YP.** A naive obstruction theory for a category fibred in groupoids `𝒳` over
the big fppf site of `S` satisfying (RS*), relative to a fixed affine chart `Spec Λ ⊆ S`: a
complex `E_x ∈ D⁻(A)` with a map `ξ_x : E_x ⟶ NL_{A/Λ}` for every object `x` of `𝒳` over
`Spec A`, identifications of `Inf_x` and `T_x` with `Ext^{-1}_A(E_x, −)` and
`Ext^0_A(E_x, −)`, and a functoriality map `E_x ⟶ E_y` for every ring map `A ⟶ B`, subject to
the five conditions of the source.
declarations.statement:
public structure NaiveObstructionTheory (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids)
    (hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp) (c : AffineChart S)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.NaiveObstructionTheory.functoriality_homology_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YT.** Let `𝒳` be fibred in groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`, satisfying
(RS*) and endowed with a naive obstruction theory. Let `A ⟶ B` be a ring map in the site, let
`y = x|_{Spec B}` be the restriction of an object `x` of `𝒳` over `Spec A`, and let `k` be a
`B`-algebra which is a field whose two module structures occur in the site. Then the
functoriality map `E_x ⟶ E_y` induces bijections
`H^i(E_x ⊗ᴸ_A k) ⟶ H^i(E_y ⊗ᴸ_B k)` for `i = 0` and `i = 1`.

Nothing about the comparison is assumed. The first step of the source proof is the (RS*)
identification of the lifts of `x` over `A[k]` with the lifts of `y` over `B[k]`, on
isomorphism classes by `Deformation.Artin.bijective_squareZeroLiftBaseChangeMap` and on the
automorphisms of the trivial lift by
`Deformation.Artin.bijective_of_isInfinitesimalAutomorphismBaseChange`; through clauses (2)
and (iii) of Stacks 07YP these give bijectivity on `Ext^0` and on `Ext^{-1}`, and the duality
of Stacks 07YK turns that into the conclusion in degrees `0` and `1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem NaiveObstructionTheory.functoriality_homology_bijective
    {hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids} {hRS : SatisfiesRSStar B S hS p hp} {c : AffineChart S}
    (N : NaiveObstructionTheory B S hS p hp hRS c) (P Q : ChartedObject B S hS p c)
    (hom : AffineObject.Hom P.obj Q.obj) [Algebra P.ring Q.ring]
    [IsScalarTower c.ring P.ring Q.ring] (halg : algebraMap P.ring Q.ring = hom.alg.ringMap)
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (g : Q.ring →+* k)
    (hM : IsSiteModule P.ring B
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (g.comp (algebraMap P.ring Q.ring))).obj
        (ModuleCat.of k (ULift.{u} k))))
    (hN : IsSiteModule Q.ring B
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars g).obj (ModuleCat.of k (ULift.{u} k)))) :
    Function.Bijective (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) 0).map
        (naiveObstructionFieldBaseChangeMap N P Q hom halg g)).hom) ∧
      Function.Bijective (((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} k) 1).map
        (naiveObstructionFieldBaseChangeMap N P Q hom halg g)).hom)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.isOpenVersality_of_naiveObstructionTheory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YU.** Let `S` be a locally Noetherian scheme and `𝒳` a category fibred in
groupoids over the big fppf site of `S`. Assume that `𝒳` satisfies (RS*) and that `𝒳` has a
naive obstruction theory, and assume the proviso of the source: the complexes `E_x` of
Stacks 07YP have finitely generated cohomology groups for the pairs `(A, x)` with `A` of finite
type over `S`. Then openness of versality holds for `𝒳`: if `U` is a scheme locally of finite
type over `S`, `x` an object of `𝒳` over `U` and `u₀` a finite type point of `U` at which `x`
is versal, then there is an open neighbourhood of `u₀` at every finite type point of which `x`
is versal.

The conclusion is the body of `Deformation.Artin.IsOpenVersality`, written out; see the
implementation notes of this file for why the predicate itself cannot be used.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenVersality_of_naiveObstructionTheory [IsLocallyNoetherian S]
    (N : ∀ c : AffineChart S, NaiveObstructionTheory B S hS p hp hRS c)
    (hFinite : ∀ (c : AffineChart S) (Q : ChartedObject B S hS p c),
      Algebra.FiniteType c.ring Q.ring → ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite Q.ring
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Q.ring) n).obj ((N c).complex Q).obj))
    (U : Over S) (hUft : LocallyOfFiniteType U.hom) (x : X)
    (hx : (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion).obj x = U) (u₀ : U.left)
    (hu₀ : IsFiniteTypePoint u₀)
    (hversal : IsVersalAt U (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u₀ x hx) :
    ∃ V : U.left.Opens, u₀ ∈ V.1 ∧
      ∀ u ∈ V.1, IsFiniteTypePoint u →
        IsVersalAt U (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u x hx

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.SectionsObstructionModel.exists_finiteProjectiveModel_obstructionSpace
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07YW], the obstruction spaces.** Let `Λ` be Noetherian, let
`g : W ⟶ Spec Λ` be proper and let `𝓕` be a coherent `𝒪_W`-module flat over `Λ`. Then there is a
finite complex `N` of finite projective `Λ`-modules such that, for every `Λ`-algebra `A`, every
cartesian square exhibiting `W_A` as the base change of `W`, and every `A`-module `M`,

`𝒪_x(M) = H¹(W_A, 𝓕_A ⊗_A M) ≅ H¹((N ⊗_Λ A) ⊗_A M)`,

the obstruction space of the obstruction theory of [Stacks, Tag 07YH] at `M`. In degree `i` the
right-hand complex is `M ⊗_Λ Nⁱ` by
`Deformation.Artin.SectionsPerfectComplex.tensorComplexXLinearEquiv`, so the right-hand side is
the source's `H¹(N ⊗_Λ M)`.

Composed with
`Deformation.Artin.SectionsPerfectComplex.nonempty_derivedCohomology_two_iso_homology_one` this
is the source's reformulation `𝒪_x(M) = H²(K ⊗^𝐋_A M)` with `K = (N ⊗_Λ A)[-1]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteProjectiveModel_obstructionSpace {Λ : Type u} [CommRing Λ]
    {W : Scheme.{u}} (g : W ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of Λ)) (F : W.Modules)
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [IsProper g] [F.IsCoherent]
    (hflat : IsFlatOver g.toLRSHom.toShHom F) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} Λ) ℤ) (a b : ℤ),
      N.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ N.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite Λ (N.X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective Λ (N.X i)) ∧
        ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (φ : Λ →+* A) {W' : Scheme.{u}}
          {g' : W' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)} {p : W' ⟶ W}
          (_hsq : IsPullback p g' g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)))
          (M : ModuleCat.{u} A),
          Nonempty ((obstructionFunctor g' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback p).obj F)).obj M ≅
            ((tensorComplex M).obj (extendScalarsComplex φ N)).homology 1)
declarations.comment: the obstruction spaces of the example of Tag 07YH are 𝒪_x(M) = H¹(N ⊗_Λ M)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.SectionsObstructionModel.exists_finiteProjectiveModel_homology_iso_obstruction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07YW], the complex `N`.** Let `Λ` be Noetherian, let `g : W ⟶ Spec Λ` be
proper and let `𝓕` be a coherent `𝒪_W`-module flat over `Λ`. Then there is a finite complex `N`
of finite projective `Λ`-modules which universally computes the cohomology of `𝓕` — for every
base change `φ : Λ → Λ'`, `Hⁱ(W_{Λ'}, 𝓕_{Λ'}) ≅ Hⁱ(N ⊗_Λ Λ')` — and, writing
`K = (N ⊗_Λ A)[-1]` for a `Λ`-algebra `A`, the degree-one cohomology of `N ⊗_Λ M` is the
degree-two cohomology of `K ⊗^𝐋_A M` for every `A`-module `M`.

This is `Deformation.Artin.SectionsPerfectComplex.exists_finiteProjectiveModel_obstruction`
without its binder `_haffineBase`, the affine-base case of [Stacks, Tag 02O5], which that proof
never uses: [Stacks, Tag 07VL]
(`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperFlatGlobalSections.exists_finiteProjectiveModel_homology_iso`)
is unconditional.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteProjectiveModel_homology_iso_obstruction {Λ : Type u} [CommRing Λ]
    {W : Scheme.{u}} (g : W ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of Λ)) (F : W.Modules)
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [IsProper g] [F.IsCoherent]
    (hflat : IsFlatOver g.toLRSHom.toShHom F) :
    ∃ (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} Λ) ℤ) (a b : ℤ),
      N.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ N.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite Λ (N.X i)) ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective Λ (N.X i)) ∧
        (∀ {Λ' : Type u} [CommRing Λ'] (φ : Λ →+* Λ') {W' : Scheme.{u}}
          {g' : W' ⟶ Spec (.of Λ')} {p : W' ⟶ W}
          (_hsq : IsPullback p g' g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) (i : ℤ),
          Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} Λ') i).obj
              (derivedGlobalSectionsOverBase g' ((Scheme.Modules.pullback p).obj F)) ≅
            (extendScalarsComplex φ N).homology i)) ∧
        ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (φ : Λ →+* A) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A),
          Nonempty ((Deformation.Artin.derivedCohomology A
                (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
                  (Deformation.Artin.SectionsPerfectComplex.shiftedBaseChange φ N)) 2).obj M ≅
            ((tensorComplex M).obj (extendScalarsComplex φ N)).homology 1)
declarations.comment: there exists a finite complex N of finite projective Λ-modules which universally computes the cohomology of 𝓕

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.SectionsPerfectComplex.nonempty_derivedCohomology_two_iso_homology_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07YW], the degree shift.** With `K = (N ⊗_Λ A)[-1]` for a bounded above
complex `N` of flat `Λ`-modules, the degree-one cohomology of `N ⊗_Λ M` — the obstruction module
of [Stacks, Tag 07YH] in the form the source reaches through [Stacks, Tag 07VL] — is the
degree-two cohomology of `K ⊗^𝐋_A M`:

`H¹((N ⊗_Λ A) ⊗_A M) ≅ H²(K ⊗^𝐋_A M)`.

In degree `i` the left-hand complex is `M ⊗_Λ Nⁱ` by `tensorComplexXLinearEquiv`, so the
left-hand side is the source's `H¹(N ⊗_Λ M)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem nonempty_derivedCohomology_two_iso_homology_one {Λ : Type u} [CommRing Λ]
    (φ : Λ →+* A) (N : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} Λ) ℤ) (b : ℤ) [N.IsStrictlyLE b]
    (hN : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Flat Λ (N.X i)) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) :
    Nonempty ((Deformation.Artin.derivedCohomology A
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (shiftedBaseChange φ N)) 2).obj M ≅
      ((tensorComplex M).obj
        (Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProperFlatGlobalSections.extendScalarsComplex φ N)).homology
          1)
declarations.comment: the reformulation 𝒪(M) = H²(K ⊗^𝐋_A M) with K = (N ⊗_Λ A)[-1], from the description 𝒪(M) = H¹(N ⊗_Λ M)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.DualDeformationSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YX.** A dual deformation situation: a complex `K` of `A`-modules whose first
derived-tensor cohomology is the tangent functor of `x`, together with obstruction elements
in its second derived-tensor cohomology which are functorial in the deformation situation and
vanish exactly when `x` lifts.
declarations.statement:
public structure DualDeformationSituation (A Λ : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing Λ]
    [Algebra Λ A] (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (toS : Spec (.of A) ⟶ S) (hA : B.Contains (Spec (.of A)))
    (X : Type v) [Category.{w} X] (p : X ⥤ BigFppfOver B S hS)

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.exists_obstructionEvaluation_eq_obstruction
declarations.doc:
There is a class `ξ` in `H¹(K ⊗ᴸ NL_{A/Λ})` such that every square-zero thickening
`D : A' → A` of the situation `sit` admits a ring map `Λ → A'` compatible with `sit.affineOpen`
and with `Λ → A`, along which the evaluation `obstructionEvaluation` of `ξ` is the obstruction
element `sit.obstruction A' D`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_obstructionEvaluation_eq_obstruction :
    ∃ ξ : (derivedTensorCohomology A sit.K 1).obj (derivedNaiveCotangentComplex Λ A),
      ∀ (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] (D : SquareZeroThickening A B S hS toS hA A'),
        ∃ f : Λ →+* A',
          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom f) ≫ sit.affineOpen = B.inclusion.map D.toS' ∧
          ∃ hf : D.q.comp f = algebraMap Λ A,
          letI : Algebra Λ A' := f.toAlgebra
          letI : Algebra A' A := D.q.toAlgebra
          letI : IsScalarTower Λ A' A :=
            IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun r =>
              (congrArg (fun g : Λ →+* A => g r) hf).symm
          obstructionEvaluation Λ A' A sit.K D.squareZeroSurjection.1
              D.squareZeroSurjection.2 ξ = sit.obstruction A' D
declarations.comment: clause (1) alone, and WITHOUT the boundary condition (iv): a single class ξ on NL_{A/Λ} whose canonical evaluation `obstructionEvaluation` at every deformation situation is that situation's obstruction element. The whole tag — clause (1) together with clause (2), that ξ's image in H¹(K ⊗ᴸ Ω_{A/Λ}) is the canonical element of the tangent functor — is `Deformation.Artin.exists_isCotangentObstructionClass`, which assumes (iv) and whose conclusion is `Deformation.Artin.IsCotangentObstructionClass`, the full conjunction. This theorem is kept beside it because clause (1) needs no hypothesis: the class it produces is adjusted there by an element of H¹(K ⊗ᴸ Ω_{P/Λ} ⊗_P A) to achieve clause (2), an adjustment clause (1) cannot see because `mor₁ ≫ mor₂ = 0`.

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.exists_isCotangentObstructionClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YY.** A dual deformation situation satisfying the boundary condition (iv) has a
cotangent obstruction class: a single class `ξ` on `NL_{A/Λ}` whose evaluation at every
square-zero thickening is that thickening's obstruction element, and whose image in
`H¹(K ⊗ᴸ Ω_{A/Λ})` is the canonical element of the tangent functor.

The class of clause (1), built at a chosen presentation, need not satisfy clause (2); it is
corrected by an element of `H¹(K ⊗ᴸ Ω_{P/Λ} ⊗_P A)` supplied by
`Deformation.Artin.exists_correction_of_boundaryCondition`, and the correction is invisible to
clause (1) because the inclusion of the degree-zero term of `NL(α)` followed by the projection
onto the conormal module is zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isCotangentObstructionClass
    (hiv : DualNotion.ObstructionBoundaryCondition Λ A B S hS toS hA X p sit) :
    ∃ ξ, IsCotangentObstructionClass Λ A B S hS toS hA X p sit ξ

declarations.name: Deformation.Artin.DualNotion.exists_isOpen_isVersalAt_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07YZ.** In Situation 07YX assume that (iv) of Lemma 07YY holds and that `K` is a
perfect object of `D(A)`. In this case, if `x` is versal at a closed point `u₀ ∈ U = Spec A`
then there exists an open neighbourhood `u₀ ∈ U' ⊆ U` such that `x` is versal at every finite
type point of `U'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpen_isVersalAt_of_isPerfect
    (hboundary : ObstructionBoundaryCondition Λ A B S hS toS hA X p sit)
    (hperfect : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect sit.K)
    (u₀ : Spec (.of A)) (hu₀ : IsClosed ({u₀} : Set (Spec (.of A))))
    (hversal : IsVersalAt (Over.mk toS) (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u₀ sit.x
      (versalityBase Λ A B S hS toS hA X p sit)) :
    ∃ V : Set (Spec (.of A)), IsOpen V ∧ u₀ ∈ V ∧
      ∀ u ∈ V, IsFiniteTypePoint u →
        IsVersalAt (Over.mk toS) (p ⋙ Over.post B.inclusion) u sit.x
          (versalityBase Λ A B S hS toS hA X p sit)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.ObjectwiseLimitPreserving.exists_isStackInGroupoids_isLimitPreservingOnObjects_not_isLimitPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07Z1.** Let `S` be a nonempty scheme. There exists a stack in groupoids
`p : 𝒳 ⥤ (Sch/S)_fppf` such that `p` is limit preserving on objects (Stacks 06CU), but `𝒳`
is not limit preserving (Stacks 07XL). The stack is the stack of torsors under a countable
product of copies of a nonzero injective abelian sheaf, a stack in groupoids by Stacks 04UM.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isStackInGroupoids_isLimitPreservingOnObjects_not_isLimitPreserving
    (B : AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    [Nonempty S] :
    ∃ 𝒳 : CatFiberedInGroupoids.{u, u, u + 1, u + 1}
        (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver B S hS),
      𝒳.val.p.IsStackInGroupoids.{u + 1}
          (AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.topology B S hS) ∧
        AlgebraicGeometry.BigFppfOver.IsLimitPreservingOnObjects.{u, v, w, u, u + 1} B S hS 𝒳
          (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.terminalCFG B S hS)
          (Bicategory.InducedBicategory.mkHom
            (AlgebraicGeometry.Stack.toTerminalCFG B S hS 𝒳)) ∧
        ¬ Deformation.Artin.IsLimitPreserving.{u, v, w, u + 1, u} B S hS 𝒳

declarations.name: homogeneousLocalization_away_finiteType
declarations.doc:
**Tag 07Z2, part 1.**
Let `S` be a graded `R`-algebra of finite type over `R`, and let `f ∈ S_d` be
homogeneous with `d ≥ 1`.  Then the degree-`0` localization `S_(f)` is of finite
type over `R` (a finitely generated `R`-algebra).
declarations.statement:
theorem homogeneousLocalization_away_finiteType (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) [Algebra.FiniteType R S] :
    Algebra.FiniteType R (SLoc 𝒜 f)

declarations.name: moduleLocalization_away_finite
declarations.doc:
**Tag 07Z2, part 2.**
Under the same hypotheses, if moreover `M` is a finite (finitely generated)
graded `S`-module — with grading `ℳ` satisfying `M = ⨁_n ℳ n`
(`DirectSum.Decomposition ℳ`) and the compatibility `𝒜 i · ℳ j ⊆ ℳ (i + j)`
(`SetLike.GradedSMul 𝒜 ℳ`) — then the degree-`0` localization `M_(f)` is a
finite `S_(f)`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem moduleLocalization_away_finite (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (hd : 1 ≤ d) [Algebra.FiniteType R S]
    [Module.Finite S M] : Module.Finite (SLoc 𝒜 f) (MLoc 𝒜 ℳ f d)

declarations.name: blowup_image_a_mem_nonZeroDivisors
declarations.doc: The image of `a` in `R[I/a]` is a nonzerodivisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem blowup_image_a_mem_nonZeroDivisors {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (a : R)
    (ha : a ∈ I) :
    haveI : Fact (a ∈ I) := ⟨ha⟩
    (algebraMap R (Blowup I a)) a ∈ nonZeroDivisors (Blowup I a)

declarations.name: blowup_idealMap_eq_span
declarations.doc:
The ideal of `R[I/a]` generated by the image of `I` equals the principal ideal generated by
the image of `a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem blowup_idealMap_eq_span {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (a : R) (ha : a ∈ I) :
    haveI : Fact (a ∈ I) := ⟨ha⟩
    Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Blowup I a)) I
      = Ideal.span {(algebraMap R (Blowup I a)) a}

declarations.name: blowup_localization_away_bijective
declarations.doc:
The map `R_a → (R[I/a])_a` induced by the structure map `R → R[I/a]` on localizations at the
powers of `a` is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem blowup_localization_away_bijective {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (a : R)
    (ha : a ∈ I) :
    haveI : Fact (a ∈ I) := ⟨ha⟩
    Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMap (Blowup.of : R →+* Blowup I a) a)

declarations.name: generates_algebra_iff_generates_irrelevant
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 07Z4: for a family `(f i)` of homogeneous elements of strictly
positive degree in a graded ring `A` with grading `𝒜` (the `GradedRing 𝒜`
hypothesis, together with the explicit `DirectSum.Decomposition 𝒜`, encodes the
direct-sum decomposition `A = ⨁_d 𝒜 d`), the family generates `A` as an algebra
over the degree-zero subring `𝒜 0` if and only if it generates the irrelevant
ideal `S₊` as an ideal of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem generates_algebra_iff_generates_irrelevant
    {I : Type*} (f : I → A) (d : I → ℕ)
    (hd : ∀ i, 0 < d i) (hf : ∀ i, f i ∈ 𝒜 (d i)) :
    Algebra.adjoin ↥(𝒜 0) (Set.range f) = ⊤ ↔
    Ideal.span (Set.range f) = (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal

declarations.name: minorIdeal_succ_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07Z7** (part 1).
For every `r ≥ 0`, `I_{r+1}(A) ⊆ I_r(A)`; equivalently
`I_0(A) ⊇ I_1(A) ⊇ I_2(A) ⊇ ⋯`.

declarations.name: minorIdeal_fromRows_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07Z7** (part 2).
If `B = fromRows A C` consists of the `n` rows of `A` followed by `n'` extra rows `C`, then
`I_{r+n'}(B) ⊆ I_r(A)` for every `r ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: minorIdeal_mul_le
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07Z7** (part 3).
For a square matrix `C` and the product `C * A`,
`I_r(C * A) ⊆ I_r(A)` for every `r ≥ 0`.

declarations.name: minorIdeal_fromBlocks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07Z7** (part 4).
For the block diagonal matrix `diag(A₁, A₂) = fromBlocks A₁ 0 0 A₂`,
`I_r(diag(A₁, A₂)) = ∑_{r₁ + r₂ = r} I_{r₁}(A₁) · I_{r₂}(A₂)`, where the sum runs over all pairs
`(r₁, r₂)` of natural numbers with `r₁ + r₂ = r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem minorIdeal_fromBlocks {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {l₁ o₁ l₂ o₂ : Type*}
    (A₁ : Matrix l₁ o₁ R) (A₂ : Matrix l₂ o₂ R) (r : ℕ) :
    minorIdeal (Matrix.fromBlocks A₁ 0 0 A₂) r =
      ∑ p ∈ Finset.antidiagonal r, minorIdeal A₁ p.1 * minorIdeal A₂ p.2

declarations.name: Stacks.Fitting.fittingIdeal_monotone
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 07Z7.** The Fitting ideals of a finite module increase.
declarations.comment: (1), for Fitting ideals

declarations.name: minorIdeal_eq_of_quotientLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07Z8.** The ideal generated by the `(n - k) × (n - k)` minors of a presentation
matrix of a finite module is independent of the presentation: if `A` has `n` rows, `B` has `m`
rows, and the cokernels of the two column maps are isomorphic `R`-modules, then
`I_{n-k}(A) = I_{m-k}(B)`. This is what makes `fittingIdeal` well defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem minorIdeal_eq_of_quotientLinearEquiv {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {n m : ℕ} {J K : Type*}
    (A : Matrix (Fin n) J R) (B : Matrix (Fin m) K R) (k : ℕ)
    (h : ((Fin n → R) ⧸ Submodule.span R
        (Set.range (fun j : J => fun i : Fin n => A i j))) ≃ₗ[R]
      ((Fin m → R) ⧸ Submodule.span R
        (Set.range (fun j : K => fun i : Fin m => B i j)))) :
    minorIdeal A (n - k) = minorIdeal B (m - k)

declarations.name: fittingIdeal
declarations.doc:
The `k`th Fitting ideal of a finite module. For negative indices, in particular `-1`, it is
the zero ideal. For nonnegative indices it is generated by the minors of a finite free
presentation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fittingIdeal {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {M : Type*}
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] (k : ℤ) : Ideal R

declarations.name: fittingIdeal_eq_minorIdeal_of_presentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07Z9.** The Fitting ideal agrees with the minor ideal of any finite free
presentation of the module, not only the presentation chosen in the definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_eq_minorIdeal_of_presentation {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    {n : ℕ} {J : Type*} (A : Matrix (Fin n) J R) (k : ℕ)
    (e : ((Fin n → R) ⧸ Submodule.span R
      (Set.range (fun j : J => fun i : Fin n => A i j))) ≃ₗ[R] M) :
    fittingIdeal (M := M) (k : ℤ) = minorIdeal A (n - k)

declarations.name: fittingIdeal_basic_properties
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZA.** Basic properties of the Fitting ideals of a finite module: generation in
bounded degree, compatibility with direct sums and scalar extension, finite generation for
finitely presented modules, monotonicity under quotients, the annihilator and support
descriptions in degree zero, and the computation for a quotient of the ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_basic_properties {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M] :
    (∀ n : ℕ, (∃ f : Fin n → M, Submodule.span R (Set.range f) = ⊤) →
      fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (n : ℤ) = ⊤) ∧
    (∀ (M' : Type w) [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M'] [Module.Finite R M'],
      fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M × M') 0 =
          fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) 0 * fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M') 0 ∧
      ∀ l : ℕ, fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M × M') (l : ℤ) =
        ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (l + 1),
          fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ) *
            fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M') ((l - k : ℕ) : ℤ)) ∧
    (∀ (S : Type x) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] (k : ℕ),
      fittingIdeal (R := S) (M := TensorProduct R S M) (k : ℤ) =
        Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) (fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ))) ∧
    (Module.FinitePresentation R M →
      ∀ k : ℕ, (fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ)).FG) ∧
    (∀ (M' : Type w) [AddCommGroup M'] [Module R M']
      (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (k : ℕ) (hf : Function.Surjective f),
        letI := Module.Finite.of_surjective f hf
        fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ) ≤
          fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M') (k : ℤ)) ∧
    (fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) 0 ≤ Module.annihilator R M) ∧
    (PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus ((fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) 0 : Ideal R) : Set R) =
      Module.support R M) ∧
    (∀ I : Ideal R, fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := R ⧸ I) 0 = I)

declarations.name: fittingIdeal_fin_eq_bot_or_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZB.** The Fitting ideal of a finite free module is zero below its rank and the
unit ideal from its rank onward.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_fin_eq_bot_or_top {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (k : ℤ) :
    fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := Fin n → R) k =
      if k < n then ⊥ else ⊤

declarations.name: fittingIdeal_local_generation_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `M` be a finite module over a commutative ring `R`, let `k` be a natural
number, and let `p` be a prime ideal of `R`. The following are equivalent: the `k`th Fitting ideal
of `M` is not contained in `p`; the fibre of `M` at `p` has dimension at most `k`; the
localization of `M` at `p` is generated by `k` elements; and this generation property holds on
some principal neighbourhood of `p`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fittingIdeal_local_generation_tfae
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] (k : ℕ) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] :
    [
      ¬ fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (k : ℤ) ≤ p,
      Module.finrank p.ResidueField (p.ResidueField ⊗[R] M) ≤ k,
      ∃ g : Fin k → LocalizedModule.AtPrime p M,
        Submodule.span (Localization.AtPrime p) (Set.range g) = ⊤,
      ∃ f : R, f ∉ p ∧ ∃ g : Fin k → LocalizedModule.Away f M,
        Submodule.span (Localization.Away f) (Set.range g) = ⊤
    ].TFAE

declarations.name: finiteLocallyFreeOfRank_fittingIdeal_tfae
declarations.doc:
A finite module is finite locally free of rank `r` if and only if its
`(r - 1)`st Fitting ideal is zero and its `r`th Fitting ideal is the unit ideal; equivalently, all
Fitting ideals below `r` are zero and all those from `r` onward are the unit ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem finiteLocallyFreeOfRank_fittingIdeal_tfae
    {R : Type u} {M : Type v} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R M] (r : ℕ) :
    [
      Module.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank R M r,
      fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) ((r : ℤ) - 1) = ⊥ ∧
        fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) (r : ℤ) = ⊤,
      (∀ k : ℤ, k < r → fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) k = ⊥) ∧
        (∀ k : ℤ, (r : ℤ) ≤ k → fittingIdeal (R := R) (M := M) k = ⊤)
    ].TFAE

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjChain.mapDomain_eq_top_of_eventually_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZE (1)**: a graded homomorphism bijective in all large degrees is defined on all
of `Proj ℬ`. Only surjectivity is used, so this is Stacks 01N1's first assertion.
declarations.comment: part (1), the domain is all of Proj B

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjChain.isIso_projMapData_hom_of_eventually_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZE (2)** on Tag 01MY's bundle: the underlying morphism of
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistCompare.projMapData` is an isomorphism. This is the form the
statements of the chain quantify over, and it is the previous result unchanged, since the bundle's
morphism is `mapHom` by definition.
declarations.comment: part (2), the projective-spectrum morphism is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjChain.isIso_projMapData_twistMap_of_eventually_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZE (3)**: a graded homomorphism bijective in all large degrees makes Tag 01MY's
comparison map on the `n`-th twist an isomorphism, for every `n : ℤ`.

The map is an epimorphism by Stacks 01N0, and a monomorphism because its adjoint form is
injective on sections and the unit of the adjunction is an isomorphism by assertion (2).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isIso_projMapData_twistMap_of_eventually_bijective (ψ : 𝒜 →+*ᵍ ℬ)
    (hψ : ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop, Function.Bijective (GradedRingHom.gradedAddHom ψ d))
    (n : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((ProjTwistCompare.projMapData 𝒜 ℬ ψ).twistMap n)
declarations.comment: part (3), the maps on twists are isomorphisms

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.relativeProjMapTriple
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme, let `A` and `B` be quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebras, set
`p : X = Proj_S(A) ⟶ S` and `q : Y = Proj_S(B) ⟶ S`, and let `ψ : A ⟶ B` be a homomorphism of
graded `𝒪_S`-algebras. There is a canonical open `U(ψ) ⊆ Y`, a canonical morphism of schemes
`r_ψ : U(ψ) ⟶ X` over `S`, and a map of `ℤ`-graded `𝒪_{U(ψ)}`-algebras

`θ = θ_ψ : r_ψ^*(⨁_{d ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_X(d)) ⟶ ⨁_{d ∈ ℤ} 𝒪_{U(ψ)}(d)`,

and the triple `(U(ψ), r_ψ, θ)` is characterised by the property that for every affine open
`W ⊆ S` the triple `(U(ψ) ∩ q⁻¹W, r_ψ|_{U(ψ) ∩ q⁻¹W}, θ|_{U(ψ) ∩ q⁻¹W})` is the triple attached
to `ψ : A(W) ⟶ B(W)`, via the identifications `p⁻¹W = Proj(A(W))` and `q⁻¹W = Proj(B(W))`.

The triple is `ψ.relativeMapDomain`, `relativeMapHom ψ` and `relativeTwistAlgebraHom ψ`, and the
seven conjuncts are, in order:

1. `r_ψ` is a morphism over `S`.
2. The inverse image of `U(ψ)` under the chart over an affine open `W` of the base is the open
   `mapDomain` of `ψ_W` in `Proj(B(W))`.
3. Under the canonical identification of `U(ψ) ∩ q⁻¹W` with `U(ψ_W)`, the restriction of `r_ψ` is
   the morphism `mapHom` of `ψ_W` followed by the chart of `X` over `W`.
4. In every degree `n`, the restriction of the `n`-th component of `θ` to the piece over `W` is
   `relativeTwistChart ψ n W`, the comparison map for `ψ_W` conjugated by the chart
   identifications.
5., 6., 7. Each of the three is determined by its affine-local description.
declarations.statement:
public theorem relativeProjMapTriple :
    (relativeMapHom ψ ≫ (relativeProj A).toBase =
        ψ.relativeMapDomain.ι ≫ (relativeProj B).toBase) ∧
      (∀ (V : S.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V),
        (relativeProj B).chart V hV ⁻¹ᵁ ψ.relativeMapDomain =
          mapDomain (A.grading V) (B.grading V) (ψ.sectionHom V)) ∧
      (∀ U : AffineOpen S,
        (chartPieceIso ψ U).hom ≫
            (relativeProj B).scheme.homOfLE
                (inf_le_left : ψ.relativeMapDomain ⊓ ((relativeProj B).toBase ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) ≤ _) ≫
              relativeMapHom ψ =
          mapHom (A.grading U.1) (B.grading U.1) (ψ.sectionHom U.1) ≫
            (relativeProj A).chart U.1 U.2) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (U : S.affineOpens),
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pieceIncl ψ U)).map ((relativeTwistAlgebraHom ψ).app n) =
          relativeTwistChart ψ n U) ∧
      (∀ W : (relativeProj B).scheme.Opens,
        (∀ (V : S.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V),
            (relativeProj B).chart V hV ⁻¹ᵁ W =
              mapDomain (A.grading V) (B.grading V) (ψ.sectionHom V)) →
          W = ψ.relativeMapDomain) ∧
      (∀ r : ψ.relativeMapDomain.toScheme ⟶ (relativeProj A).scheme,
        (∀ U : AffineOpen S,
            (((relativeProj B).chart U.1 U.2).isoImage
                  (mapDomain (A.grading U.1) (B.grading U.1) (ψ.sectionHom U.1))).hom ≫
                (relativeProj B).scheme.homOfLE (chartImage_le ψ U) ≫ r =
              mapHom (A.grading U.1) (B.grading U.1) (ψ.sectionHom U.1) ≫
                (relativeProj A).chart U.1 U.2) →
          r = relativeMapHom ψ) ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ)
          (θ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback (relativeMapHom ψ)).obj (relativeTwist A n) ⟶
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback ψ.relativeMapDomain.ι).obj (relativeTwist B n)),
        (∀ U : S.affineOpens,
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback (pieceIncl ψ U)).map θ = relativeTwistChart ψ n U) →
          θ = (relativeTwistAlgebraHom ψ).app n)
declarations.comment: the tag in one statement: the open U(ψ) of Proj_S(B), the morphism r_ψ : U(ψ) ⟶ Proj_S(A) over S, and θ as a map of ℤ-graded 𝒪_{U(ψ)}-algebras, together with the characterisation of all three over every affine open of the base by the triple Lemma 01MY attaches to the induced homomorphism of graded rings of sections, and the uniqueness of each

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwistStatement.relativeMapDomain_mapHom_twistMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07ZH].** Let `S` be a scheme, let `A`, `B` and `C` be quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_S`-algebras and let `φ : A ⟶ B` and `ψ : B ⟶ C` be homomorphisms between them. Then the open,
the morphism and the maps on twists that Tag 07ZG attaches to the composite `ψ ∘ φ` are
determined by those of `φ` and of `ψ`.

The three conjuncts are, in order:

1. `U(ψ ∘ φ) = r_ψ^{-1}(U(φ))`: the open attached to the composite is the inverse image under
  `r_ψ` of the open attached to the inner factor, read inside `Proj_S(C)` as the image of that
  inverse image under the inclusion of `U(ψ)`. (This is the intended reading of a source
  statement that is type-incorrect as printed; see the implementation notes above.)
2. `r_{ψ ∘ φ} = r_φ ∘ r_ψ|_{U(ψ ∘ φ)}`: the morphism attached to the composite is the
  restriction `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.relativeMapHomRestrict` of `r_ψ` to
  `U(ψ ∘ φ)`, followed by the morphism attached to the inner factor.
3. `θ_ψ ∘ r_ψ^*θ_φ = θ_{ψ ∘ φ}`: for every `n` the `n`-th map on twists of the composite is the
  inverse image along that same restriction of the `n`-th map on twists of `φ`, followed by the
  inverse image along the inclusion of `U(ψ ∘ φ)` into `U(ψ)` of the `n`-th map on twists of
  `ψ`. The isomorphisms of inverse-image functors that identify the source and the target of the
  two sides are the ones named by conjuncts 1 and 2 and by
  `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.relativeMapHomRestrict_comp_ι`.

Each conjunct is the corresponding component declaration:
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjMapComp.relativeMapDomain_comp`,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.relativeMapHomRestrict_comp_relativeMapHom` and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.relativeTwistMap_comp`. The source states the tag for
arbitrary `A`, `B`, `C`, `φ` and `ψ`, and those are the only binders here.
declarations.statement:
theorem relativeMapDomain_mapHom_twistMap_comp :
    (ψ.comp φ).relativeMapDomain =
        ψ.relativeMapDomain.ι ''ᵁ (relativeMapHom ψ ⁻¹ᵁ φ.relativeMapDomain) ∧
      relativeMapHomRestrict φ ψ ≫ relativeMapHom φ = relativeMapHom (ψ.comp φ) ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ,
        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr
              (relativeMapHomRestrict_comp_relativeMapHom φ ψ)).inv.app
            (relativeTwist A n) ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (relativeMapHomRestrict φ ψ)
              (relativeMapHom φ)).inv.app (relativeTwist A n) ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback (relativeMapHomRestrict φ ψ)).map
              (relativeTwistMap φ n) ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp (relativeMapHomRestrict φ ψ)
              φ.relativeMapDomain.ι).hom.app (relativeTwist B n) ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr
              (relativeMapHomRestrict_comp_ι φ ψ)).hom.app (relativeTwist B n) ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp
              ((relativeProj C).scheme.homOfLE (relativeMapDomain_comp_le φ ψ))
              (relativeMapHom ψ)).inv.app (relativeTwist B n) ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullback ((relativeProj C).scheme.homOfLE
              (relativeMapDomain_comp_le φ ψ))).map (relativeTwistMap ψ n) ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp
              ((relativeProj C).scheme.homOfLE (relativeMapDomain_comp_le φ ψ))
              ψ.relativeMapDomain.ι).hom.app (relativeTwist C n) ≫
            (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr (Scheme.homOfLE_ι (relativeProj C).scheme
              (relativeMapDomain_comp_le φ ψ))).hom.app (relativeTwist C n) =
          relativeTwistMap (ψ.comp φ) n
declarations.comment:
the tag's three assertions in one statement: the domain of the composite is the
inverse image of the inner factor's domain along `r_ψ`, the morphism of the composite is the
restriction of `r_ψ` followed by `r_φ`, and the maps on twists compose. The first conjunct is
the intended reading `U(psi.comp phi) = r_psi^{-1}(U(phi))` of a source statement printed as
`U(psi.comp phi) = r_phi^{-1}(U(psi))`, which is TYPE-INCORRECT -- `r_phi` is defined on
`U(phi)` in `Proj_S(B)` and so accepts opens of `Proj_S(A)`, whereas `U(psi)` is an open of
`Proj_S(C)`, the two names having been interchanged; the deviation is documented in the module
docstring

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwistCounterexample.exists_epi_not_isIso_relativeTwistMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07ZI] (3), second half.** The maps `θ_n : r_ψ^* 𝒪_X(n) ⟶ 𝒪_Y(n)` of Tag 07ZG
are not isomorphisms in general, even if `A → B` is surjective: there are a scheme `S`,
quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebras `A` and `B` and a homomorphism `ψ : A ⟶ B` such that every
`ψ_n : A_n ⟶ B_n` is an epimorphism (so the hypothesis of Tag 07ZI holds in every degree), every
`θ_n` is an epimorphism, as the first half of assertion (3) says, and `θ_1` is not an
isomorphism.

The witness is `S = Spec R` for `R = ULift ℤ`, `A = R[x, y]/(x²)` with `deg x = 1`, `deg y = 2`,
`B = A/(x)` and `ψ` the quotient map:
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistCompare.NotIsoExample.epi_sheafHom_app`,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.epi_relativeTwistMap_of_eventually_epi` and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjTwistCompare.NotIsoExample.not_isIso_relativeTwistMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_not_isIso_relativeTwistMap :
    ∃ (S : Scheme.{u}) (A B : SheafGradedAlgebra S) (ψ : SheafGradedAlgebraHom A B),
      (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (ψ.app n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Epi (relativeTwistMap ψ n)) ∧
        ¬ IsIso (relativeTwistMap ψ ((1 : ℕ) : ℤ))
declarations.comment:
(3), second half: the maps θ are surjective but not isomorphisms in general, even
if A → B is surjective — a map ψ of quasi-coherent graded algebras surjective in every degree with
θ₁ not an isomorphism (A = R[x,y]/(x²), deg x = 1, deg y = 2, B = A/(x), on Spec R)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwistStatement.domain_closedImmersion_twistEpi_of_eventually_epi
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07ZI].** Let `S` be a scheme, let `A` and `B` be quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_S`-algebras and let `ψ : A ⟶ B` be a homomorphism between them. If `A_d → B_d` is surjective
for all sufficiently large `d`, then `U(ψ) = Y`, the morphism `r_ψ : U(ψ) ⟶ X` of Tag 07ZG is a
closed immersion, and every map `θ_n : r_ψ^* 𝒪_X(n) ⟶ 𝒪_Y(n)|_{U(ψ)}` is an epimorphism.

The three conjuncts are, in order:

1. The open of `Y = Proj_S(B)` on which `ψ` induces a morphism is all of `Y`.
2. That morphism is a closed immersion.
3. For every `n : ℤ` the comparison map on the `n`-th twist is an epimorphism.

Each is the corresponding component declaration:
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjMapDomain.relativeMapDomain_eq_top_of_eventually_epi`,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjMapDomain.isClosedImmersion_relativeMapHom_of_eventually_epi`
and `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.epi_relativeTwistMap_of_eventually_epi`. The only
hypothesis is the source's, degreewise surjectivity in all large degrees.

The source's assertion (3) adds that the maps `θ_n` are not isomorphisms in general, even if
`A → B` is surjective. That is an existence statement, not a consequence of the hypothesis, and is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwistCounterexample.exists_epi_not_isIso_relativeTwistMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem domain_closedImmersion_twistEpi_of_eventually_epi
    (hsurj : ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop, Epi (ψ.app (d : ℤ))) :
    ψ.relativeMapDomain = ⊤ ∧
      IsClosedImmersion (relativeMapHom ψ) ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, Epi (relativeTwistMap ψ n)
declarations.comment:
the tag's three assertions in one statement: under degreewise surjectivity in all
large degrees the domain of definition is all of `Proj_S(B)`, the induced morphism `r_ψ` is a
closed immersion, and every comparison map `θ_n` on twists is an epimorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwistStatement.domain_isIso_twistIsIso_of_eventually_isIso
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07ZJ].** Let `S` be a scheme, let `A` and `B` be quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_S`-algebras and let `ψ : A ⟶ B` be a homomorphism between them. If `A_d → B_d` is an
isomorphism for all sufficiently large `d`, then `U(ψ) = Y`, the morphism `r_ψ : U(ψ) ⟶ X` of
Tag 07ZG is an isomorphism, and every map `θ_n : r_ψ^* 𝒪_X(n) ⟶ 𝒪_Y(n)|_{U(ψ)}` is an
isomorphism.

The three conjuncts are, in order:

1. The open of `Y = Proj_S(B)` on which `ψ` induces a morphism is all of `Y`.
2. That morphism is an isomorphism.
3. For every `n : ℤ` the comparison map on the `n`-th twist is an isomorphism.

Each is the corresponding component declaration:
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjMapDomain.relativeMapDomain_eq_top_of_eventually_isIso`,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjMapDomain.isIso_relativeMapHom_of_eventually_isIso` and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.isIso_relativeTwistMap_of_eventually_isIso`. The only
hypothesis is the source's, degreewise invertibility in all large degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem domain_isIso_twistIsIso_of_eventually_isIso
    (hbij : ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop, IsIso (ψ.app (d : ℤ))) :
    ψ.relativeMapDomain = ⊤ ∧
      IsIso (relativeMapHom ψ) ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, IsIso (relativeTwistMap ψ n)
declarations.comment:
the tag's three assertions in one statement: under degreewise invertibility in all
large degrees the domain of definition is all of `Proj_S(B)`, the induced morphism `r_ψ` is an
isomorphism, and every comparison map `θ_n` on twists is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwistStatement.domain_closedImmersion_twistIsIso_of_generatedInDegreeOne
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 07ZK].** Let `S` be a scheme, let `A` and `B` be quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_S`-algebras and let `ψ : A ⟶ B` be a homomorphism between them. If `A_d → B_d` is surjective
for all sufficiently large `d` and `A` is generated by `A_1` over `A_0`, then `U(ψ) = Y`, the
morphism `r_ψ : U(ψ) ⟶ X` of Tag 07ZG is a closed immersion, and every map
`θ_n : r_ψ^* 𝒪_X(n) ⟶ 𝒪_Y(n)|_{U(ψ)}` is an isomorphism.

The three conjuncts are, in order:

1. The open of `Y = Proj_S(B)` on which `ψ` induces a morphism is all of `Y`.
2. That morphism is a closed immersion.
3. For every `n : ℤ` the comparison map on the `n`-th twist is an isomorphism.

The first two are the two component declarations of Tag 07ZI,
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjMapDomain.relativeMapDomain_eq_top_of_eventually_epi` and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjMapDomain.isClosedImmersion_relativeMapHom_of_eventually_epi`,
which need only the surjectivity hypothesis; the third is
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag07ZGTwist.isIso_relativeTwistMap_of_generatedInDegreeOne`, which
uses both. Generation in degree one is read over the affine opens of the base, which is where the
graded algebras have graded rings of sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem domain_closedImmersion_twistIsIso_of_generatedInDegreeOne
    (hsurj : ∀ᶠ d : ℕ in atTop, Epi (ψ.app (d : ℤ)))
    (hgen : ∀ U : S.Opens, IsAffineOpen U → A.IsGeneratedInDegreeOneAt U) :
    ψ.relativeMapDomain = ⊤ ∧
      IsClosedImmersion (relativeMapHom ψ) ∧
      ∀ n : ℤ, IsIso (relativeTwistMap ψ n)
declarations.comment:
the tag's three assertions in one statement: under degreewise surjectivity in all
large degrees and generation in degree one the domain of definition is all of `Proj_S(B)`, the
induced morphism `r_ψ` is a closed immersion, and every comparison map `θ_n` on twists is an
isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isRetrocompact_iff_forall_affineOpens
declarations.doc:
**A subset of a scheme is retrocompact exactly when its intersection with every affine open
is quasi-compact.**
declarations.statement:
theorem isRetrocompact_iff_forall_affineOpens (E : Set X) :
    IsRetrocompact E ↔ ∀ W : X.affineOpens, IsCompact (E ∩ (W : Set X))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.pushforward_annihilatorSubsheaf_range_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ZN.** Pushing forward the annihilator of the extended ideal gives
the annihilator of the original ideal, as subobjects of the pushed-forward module.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforward_annihilatorSubsheaf_range_eq
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (I : Y.Modules)
    (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf) [Mono i]
    (F : X.Modules) (U : Y.Opens) :
    Set.range (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).map
      (annihilatorSubsheaf
        (extendedIdealSheaf f I i) F
        (extendedIdealSheafι f I i)).ι).app U) =
    Set.range (((annihilatorSubsheaf I
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F) i).ι).val.app (op U))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.supportedSectionsSubmodule_isQuasicoherent
declarations.doc:
The subsheaf of sections supported on a closed subset with retrocompact complement is
quasicoherent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem supportedSectionsSubmodule_isQuasicoherent {X : Scheme.{u}} (Z : Set X)
    (hZ : IsClosed Z) (hZc : IsRetrocompact Zᶜ) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] :
    (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.supportedSectionsSubmodule Z
      F).toSheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent
declarations.comment: supported_sections_is_quasicoherent

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_supportedSectionsSubmodule_iff_exists_pow_le_annihilator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZP, the torsion description of the supported sections.** Let `Z` be a subset of
a scheme `X`, let `U` be an affine open and let `I ⊆ 𝒪_X(U)` be a finitely generated ideal
whose zero locus meets `U` in `Z`. A section of a quasi-coherent `𝒪_X`-module over `U` has all
its germs outside `Z` equal to zero exactly when some power of `I` annihilates it.

Such an `I` exists for every closed `Z` with retrocompact complement, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fg_ideal_zeroLocus_eq_inter`; so the two together are the tag's
description of the sections of the supported-section subsheaf over an affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_supportedSectionsSubmodule_iff_exists_pow_le_annihilator {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (Z : Set X) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    {I : Ideal Γ(X, U)} (hIfg : I.FG)
    (hI : Z ∩ (U : Set X) = X.zeroLocus (U := U) (I : Set Γ(X, U)) ∩ (U : Set X))
    (s : Γ(F, U)) :
    s ∈ (supportedSectionsSubmodule Z F).toSubmodule.obj (op U) ↔
      ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ a ∈ I ^ n, a • s = 0
declarations.comment: the supported sections over an affine open are the ideal-power torsion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_fg_ideal_zeroLocus_eq_inter
declarations.doc:
On an affine open of a scheme, a closed subset with retrocompact complement is the
zero locus of a finitely generated ideal of the ring of sections.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_fg_ideal_zeroLocus_eq_inter (X : Scheme.{u}) (Z : Set X)
    (hZ : IsClosed Z) (hZc : IsRetrocompact Zᶜ) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    ∃ I : Ideal Γ(X, U), I.FG ∧
      Z ∩ (U : Set X) = X.zeroLocus (U := U) I ∩ (U : Set X)
declarations.comment: finite_ideal_for_closed_subset_on_affine

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_supportedSectionsSubmodule_zeroLocus_span_singleton_iff
declarations.doc:
**The sections supported on a principal zero locus are the torsion for the powers of its
generator.** A global section of a quasi-coherent module on `Spec R` has all its germs outside
`V(a)` zero exactly when some power of `a` kills it.

This is the affine-open description of [Stacks, Tag 07ZP] at the ideal `(a)`, which is finitely
generated; the passage from a power of the ideal to a power of the element is
`Ideal.span_singleton_pow`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma mem_supportedSectionsSubmodule_zeroLocus_span_singleton_iff
    (F : (Spec R).Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (a : R) (s : Γ(F, ⊤)) :
    s ∈ (supportedSectionsSubmodule (principalZeroLocus R a) F).toSubmodule.obj (op ⊤) ↔
      ∃ n : ℕ, a ^ n • s = 0
declarations.comment: the sections supported on V(a) are the a-power torsion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.range_pushforward_supportedSectionsSubmodule_eq
declarations.doc:
The pushforward of the subsheaf supported over `Z` is the subsheaf of
the pushforward supported on `Z`, as subobjects of the pushforward sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_pushforward_supportedSectionsSubmodule_eq
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (Z : Set Y) (hZ : IsClosed Z) (F : X.Modules) (U : Y.Opens) :
    Set.range (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).map
      (supportedSectionsSubmodule (f.base ⁻¹' Z) F).ι).app U) =
      Set.range (((supportedSectionsSubmodule Z
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj F)).ι).val.app (op U))

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag01VMRelativeVeryAmple.isClosedImmersion_canonicalSymProjHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 07ZR: the morphism `Proj_S(𝒜) ⟶ 𝐏(𝒜_1)` is a closed immersion**, for `𝒜`
generated by `𝒜_1` over `𝒜_0`, with no hypothesis on the graded-algebra map because the map is
the canonical one.
declarations.statement: theorem isClosedImmersion_canonicalSymProjHom : IsClosedImmersion (canonicalSymProjHom A hgen)
declarations.comment: the morphism X -> P(A_1) associated to the canonical map Sym(A_1) -> A is a closed immersion

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag07ZRVeryAmple.isInvertibleModule_twistOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 07ZR: `𝒪_X(1)` is an invertible `𝒪_X`-module**, for `X = Proj_S(A)` the relative
homogeneous spectrum of a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra generated by `A_1` over `A_0`.

This is Stacks Tag 01O4 in a single degree: `𝒪_X(1)` is the absolute twist `𝒪(1)` on each affine
chart of `X`, and the graded ring of sections over each affine open of the base is generated by
its degree-one part, which trivializes that twist near every point.
declarations.statement:
theorem isInvertibleModule_twistOne (A : SheafGradedAlgebra S)
    (hgen : ProjRepresentsF1.IsGeneratedInDegreeOne A) :
    IsInvertibleModule (relativeProj A).scheme (twistOne A)
declarations.comment: O_X(1) is invertible

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag07ZRVeryAmple.twistOneIsoPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 07ZR: the closed immersion `X ⟶ 𝐏(A_1)` pulls `𝒪_{𝐏(A_1)}(1)` back to
`𝒪_X(1)`.** The closed immersion is `Stacks.Tag01VMRelativeVeryAmple.canonicalSymProjHom`, the
morphism of Stacks Tag 07ZG attached to the canonical map `Sym(A_1) ⟶ A` read on all of `X`, and
the isomorphism is the inverse of the map `θ_1` of Tag 07ZG, which is an isomorphism by Stacks
Tag 07ZK (3).
declarations.statement:
def twistOneIsoPullback :
    twistOne A ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (canonicalSymProjHom A hgen)).obj
        (Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.twistOne (A.piece 1))
declarations.comment: the closed immersion X -> P(A_1) pulls back O_{P(A_1)}(1) to O_X(1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Tag07ZRVeryAmple.isRelativelyVeryAmple_twistOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 07ZR: `𝒪_X(1)` is very ample relative to `X ⟶ S`**, for `X = Proj_S(A)` the
relative homogeneous spectrum of a quasi-coherent graded `𝒪_S`-algebra generated by `A_1` over
`A_0`.

Relative very ampleness is Stacks Tag 01VM,
`Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple`: the quasi-coherent module on the base is `A_1`,
the immersion over the base is the closed immersion
`Stacks.Tag01VMRelativeVeryAmple.canonicalSymProjHom` attached to the canonical map
`Sym(A_1) ⟶ A`, and the identification of `𝒪_X(1)` with its pullback of `𝒪_{𝐏(A_1)}(1)` is
`Stacks.Tag07ZRVeryAmple.twistOneIsoPullback`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRelativelyVeryAmple_twistOne :
    have := isInvertibleModule_twistOne A hgen
    Stacks.Tag01VMVeryAmple.IsRelativelyVeryAmple (relativeProj A).toBase (twistOne A)
declarations.comment: O_X(1) is relatively very ample on X/S

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_relativeProj_toBase_and_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Example 07ZS.** Let `S` be a scheme and `𝒜` a quasi-coherent graded
`𝒪_S`-algebra generated by `𝒜_1` over `𝒜_0`, with `𝒜_1` of finite type over `𝒪_S`, and let
`X = Proj_S(𝒜)`. Then `X ⟶ S` is projective (Tag 01W8), and the morphism
`X ⟶ 𝐏(𝒜_1) = Proj_S(Sym(𝒜_1))` associated to the canonical graded `𝒪_S`-algebra map
`Sym(𝒜_1) ⟶ 𝒜` is a closed immersion over `S`.

The three conjuncts are, in order: projectivity of the projection of `Proj_S(𝒜)`; the closed
immersion `Stacks.Tag01VMRelativeVeryAmple.canonicalSymProjHom`, which is Tag 07ZK (2) for the
canonical map; and its compatibility with the projections to `S`. The first is Tag 0B3U,
`AlgebraicGeometry.isProjective_relativeProj_toBase`, which is proved from the other two.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProjective_relativeProj_toBase_and_isClosedImmersion {S : Scheme.{u}}
    (A : SheafGradedAlgebra.{u} S)
    (hgen : Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.ProjRepresentsF1.IsGeneratedInDegreeOne A)
    (hfin : (A.piece 1).IsFiniteType) :
    IsProjective (relativeProj A).toBase ∧
      IsClosedImmersion (Stacks.Tag01VMRelativeVeryAmple.canonicalSymProjHom A hgen) ∧
      Stacks.Tag01VMRelativeVeryAmple.canonicalSymProjHom A hgen ≫
          (Stacks.SymGraded.schemeProjectiveBundle (A.piece 1)
            (Stacks.SymGraded.isQuasicoherentPieces_of_isQuasicoherent (A.piece 1))).toBase =
        (relativeProj A).toBase

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isAffineHom_ι_of_forall_support_inter_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ZT.** Support-only form: if every point of `X` has an affine open
neighbourhood `V` on which the support of the ideal sheaf `I` is the zero locus of a single
section `a`, then the inclusion into `X` of any open `W` presenting the complement of that
support is an affine morphism. The hypothesis asks nothing about the ideal `I.ideal V` beyond
its radical, so it applies to ideal sheaves that are only locally principal up to radicals.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_ι_of_forall_support_inter_eq
    (hI : ∀ x : X, ∃ (V : X.affineOpens) (_ : x ∈ (V.1 : Set X)) (a : Γ(X, V.1)),
      (I.support : Set X) ∩ (V.1 : Set X) = X.zeroLocus {a} ∩ (V.1 : Set X))
    {W : X.Opens} (hW : (W : Set X) = (I.support : Set X)ᶜ) :
    IsAffineHom (Scheme.Opens.ι W)
declarations.comment:
the complement is affine over the base already when the support is locally a
zero locus of one section

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isAffineHom_ι_compl_support_of_isLocallyPrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ZT.** Let `X` be a scheme and let `Z ⊆ X` be a locally principal
closed subscheme, cut out by the ideal sheaf `I`. Then the inclusion of the open complement
`X \ Z` into `X` is an affine morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_ι_compl_support_of_isLocallyPrincipal (hI : IsLocallyPrincipal I) :
    IsAffineHom (Scheme.Opens.ι I.support.compl)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isAffineHom_compl_of_isLocallyPrincipal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ZT.**  The open complement of a locally principal closed subscheme
is affine over the ambient scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_compl_of_isLocallyPrincipal (hI : IsLocallyPrincipal I) :
    IsAffineHom (Scheme.Opens.ι I.support.compl)

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_compl_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ZU (scheme-theoretic density).**  The complement of an effective
Cartier divisor is scheme-theoretically dense in the ambient scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSchemeTheoreticallyDense_compl_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
    (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I) :
    Scheme.Opens.IsSchemeTheoreticallyDense I.support.compl
declarations.comment: scheme-theoretic density

declarations.name: Stacks.Divisors.isAffineHom_compl_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ZU (affineness).**  The complement of an effective Cartier divisor
is affine over the ambient scheme: an effective Cartier divisor is locally principal, so Tag
07ZT applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineHom_compl_of_isEffectiveCartierDivisor (hI : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I) :
    IsAffineHom (Scheme.Opens.ι I.support.compl)
declarations.comment: affineness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_left_of_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ZV.**  If the product of the ideal sheaves of two closed subschemes
of a scheme cuts out an effective Cartier divisor, then the first subscheme is an effective
Cartier divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_left_of_mul (I J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hIJ : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (I * J)) : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor I
declarations.comment: effectivity of the first summand

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isEffectiveCartierDivisor_right_of_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 07ZV.**  If the product of the ideal sheaves of two closed subschemes
of a scheme cuts out an effective Cartier divisor, then the second subscheme is an effective
Cartier divisor.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEffectiveCartierDivisor_right_of_mul (I J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hIJ : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor (I * J)) : IsEffectiveCartierDivisor J
declarations.comment: effectivity of the second summand

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.quasiCompact_relativeProj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZX.** The structure morphism of the relative homogeneous spectrum of a
quasi-coherent graded algebra is quasi-compact as soon as the algebra is of finite type over its
degree-zero part, or generated by its degree-one piece, or has locally nilpotent positive part
modulo a finite type quasi-coherent degree-zero submodule.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiCompact_relativeProj
    (h : IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero s ∨ IsFinitelyGeneratedInDegreeOne s ∨
      HasNilpotentPositiveQuotient s) :
    QuasiCompact (relativeProjToBase s)

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFiniteType.locallyOfFiniteType_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZY, first assertion.** The structure morphism of the relative homogeneous spectrum
of a finite type quasi-coherent graded algebra is locally of finite type.
declarations.statement:
public theorem locallyOfFiniteType_toBase (hA : IsFiniteType A) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (relativeProj A).toBase
declarations.comment: relative_proj_finite_type

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFiniteType.quasiCompact_toBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZY, first assertion.** The structure morphism of the relative homogeneous spectrum
of a finite type quasi-coherent graded algebra is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
public theorem quasiCompact_toBase (hA : IsFiniteType A) :
    QuasiCompact (relativeProj A).toBase
declarations.comment: relative_proj_finite_type

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RelativeProjFiniteType.isFiniteType_relativeProjTwist
declarations.doc:
Every twist `𝒪_X(t)` on the relative projective spectrum `X = Proj_S(A)` of a finite type
quasi-coherent graded algebra is a finite-type module sheaf. The twists are the homogeneous pieces
of the twist datum `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.GluedTwistAlgebra.twistDataOfGradedAlgebra` of `A`.
declarations.comment: relative_proj_twist_finite_type

declarations.name: Stacks.RelativeProj.Situation.universallyClosed_relativeProjToBase_of_isIntegralInDegreeZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 07ZZ.** If the degree-zero part of the graded algebra of a relative `Proj`
situation is integral over the structure sheaf and the graded algebra is of finite type over its
degree-zero part, then the structure morphism of the relative homogeneous spectrum is
universally closed.
declarations.statement:
theorem universallyClosed_relativeProjToBase_of_isIntegralInDegreeZero
    (hint : s.IsIntegralInDegreeZero)
    (hft : s.IsFiniteTypeOverDegreeZero) :
    UniversallyClosed (relativeProjToBase s)
